title: [Victory] Live alliance win uses slot team not getRelationship
description:
## C++
`VictoryConditions::areAllies` (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/ScriptEngine/VictoryConditions.cpp:44-52) is mutual `Player::getRelationship(other->getDefaultTeam()) == ALLIES`. `update` / `hasAchievedVictory` / `hasBeenDefeated` / `isLocalAlliedVictory` all use that. `PLAYER_RELATES_PLAYER` → `setPlayerRelationship` is therefore visible to who wins.

`startNewGame` still sets `VICTORY_NOBUILDINGS`; this is not a flag bug.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/helpers/leftover.rs:996-1003` `leftover_players_are_allies` is mutual `is_allied_with_player` → `Player::get_relationship` (`GameLogic/src/player/relations.rs:6-12`, C++ Player.cpp:542).
`GameLogic/src/scripting/executor/actions_player.rs:298-335` `do_player_relates_player` writes leftover `player_relations` and queues the live host drain.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/game_logic/victory_conditions.rs:67-73` `alliance_key` is only `Player.alliance_team` (lobby slot team). `evaluate_with_templates` / `is_local_allied_victory` / `refresh_alliance_states` group winners by that key.
`Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/scripts_camera.rs:1390-1400` `apply_host_player_relates_script_requests` writes `set_map_relationship` (used by combat `player_relationship`) and never touches `alliance_team`.

## Evidence
A skirmish script that mutually Allies two enemy slots (or Enemies two same-slot allies) changes leftover relations and live `map_relationship`, but live still ends the match on the original slot teams. C++ / leftover `areAllies` would keep both living or declare them one alliance.

Wrong-winner (P0). Not a duplicate of closed hq-ve6uv (faction Team vs slot) or hq-zfu1s (relates never reached live host).
close_reason: Live areAllies is mutual map_relationship (PLAYER_RELATES / Player::getRelationship), not alliance_key slot team. evaluate / is_local_allied_victory / refresh_alliance_states group by that; slot alliance_team is only the unset-map default.

title: [Victory] Empty victory flags auto-annihilate — C++ never auto-defeats
description:
## C++
`VictoryConditions::hasSinglePlayerBeenDefeated` (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/ScriptEngine/VictoryConditions.cpp:249-280) returns true only when:
- both NOUNITS+NOBUILDINGS → `!player->hasAnyObjects()`
- NOUNITS only → `!player->hasAnyUnits()`
- NOBUILDINGS only → `!player->hasAnyBuildings(KINDOF_MP_COUNT_FOR_VICTORY)`
With neither flag set it falls through to `return false` — a player is never auto-eliminated. Campaign.ini `victory_rule = none|custom` and MapVictoryRules with requireunits=false/requirebuildings=false leave victory entirely to scripts.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/system/game_logic_impl/impl_update.rs:1443-1447` maps `(false, false) => false`.
`GameLogic/src/system/victory_conditions.rs` `EliminationDetector::should_eliminate_player_with_flags` (417-421) likewise `(false, false) => false`.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/game_logic/victory_conditions.rs:517-526` `is_defeated` maps `(false, false) => !state.has_any_objects`.
`parse_victory_keyword` (752-763) returns `VictoryType::empty()` for Campaign.ini `victory_rule = none|custom`; MapVictoryRules.ini `requireunits=false requirebuildings=false` yields empty via `from_requirements`.

## Effect
On a none/custom map, a player with zero objects gets defeat_events + `kill_player_for_victory` (army wiped, cash zeroed) where C++ leaves victory to scripts. Wrong-winner.

## Fix
Match leftover/C++: empty flags must never auto-defeat.
close_reason: is_defeated / is_defeated_residual map (false,false) to false, matching C++ hasSinglePlayerBeenDefeated fall-through. Empty Campaign.ini / MapVictoryRules no longer auto-annihilate.

title: [Victory] Live playable census name-sniffs observer/civilian
description:
## C++
`VictoryConditions::cachePlayerPtrs` (VictoryConditions.cpp:284-299) excludes only: the Neutral player pointer, template-less players, players whose PlayerTemplate is FactionCivilian (template identity), and `isPlayerObserver()`. Player names are never consulted.

## Leftover
`leftover_player_is_playable_living` (GameLogic/src/helpers/leftover.rs:969-972) is `!is_player_observer() && get_player_type() != Neutral` (plus defeated latch). No name test — a human slot named "Observer" or "CivilianCrusher" still counts.

## Live
`is_playable_victory_player` (Main/src/game_logic/victory_conditions.rs:117-125) does `name.contains("observer") || name.contains("civilian")` and drops the slot from `living_players` / `active_alliances` in `evaluate()` (:344-369). A still-living army whose slot name contains those substrings is invisible to victory: remaining alliances collapse to one, `end_frame` latches, `MULTIPLAYER_ALLIED_VICTORY` fires. Live already has `PlayerTemplateIdentity::resolve()` for the exact C++ template check.

## Evidence
VictoryConditions.cpp:284-299. leftover.rs:969-972. victory_conditions.rs:117-125,344-376. Not a duplicate of closed hq-oep8q (INERT census), hq-comb6 (PlayerList defeated), hq-tmjnd (allied-defeat), hq-ve6uv (alliance key).
close_reason: is_playable_victory_player uses PlayerTemplateIdentity::resolve and leftover FactionCivilian; slot names never consulted

title: [GameAudio / GameSounds / GameSpeech / Eva / AudioEventRTS / live Miles-rodio device path (2D/3D play)] Live S
description:
C++: MilesAudioManager.cpp:1087-1109 releasePlayingAudio() calls m_sound->notifyOf2DSampleCompletion()/notifyOf3DSampleCompletion() whenever a sound ends (EOS callback, stop, cull, kill); GameSounds.cpp:160-190 notify functions + GameSounds.cpp:245-258 canPlayNow() channel checks (m_numPlaying2DSamples < m_num2DSamples).
Rust: game_audio.rs:1477-1485 play_audio_event() calls sound_mgr.notify_of_3d/2d_sample_start() for every SoundEffect played, but notify_of_*_sample_completion has ZERO callers on the live path (only tests/trait plumbing, game_sounds.rs:569-575). The only decrement path, SoundManagerImpl::cleanup_completed_sounds (game_sounds.rs:380-399), iterates self.playing_sounds — which is only filled by SoundManagerImpl::add_audio_event/track_sound (game_sounds.rs:513-531), and AudioManager::add_audio_event never calls it (it queues an AudioRequest directly, game_audio.rs:712-731). purge_inactive_events/process_playing_list (game_audio.rs:2037-2121, 2262-2267) never touch the sound manager counters.
Gap: num_playing_2d/3d_samples increase monotonically until reset(). Once num_playing >= num samples (16/16 default; AudioSettings.ini SampleCount2D/3D), SoundManagerImpl::can_play_now returns false for all non-AC_INTERRUPT events and — because can_kill_lower_priority/can_interrupt_existing also scan the empty local list (see next finding) — every UI click, voice, and 3D sound effect is permanently dropped for the rest of the map. Effectively 'audio dies after N sounds played'.
Slice: GameAudio / GameSounds / GameSpeech / Eva / AudioEventRTS / live Miles-rodio device path (2D/3D play)

title: Epic: C++ vs Rust behavioral parity audit
description:
## Why
Stem-existence is 100% (PORT_STATE.txt) but the running game has dozens of visible behavior differences. Only allowed intentional divergence is wgpu instead of DirectX. Rust enums vs C++ enums are OK if values/behavior match.

## What was done (2026-08-19)

**186 new bugs** filed with `discovered-from:hq-sllz` (plus 4 pre-existing visual bugs not duplicated).

Priority: P1=97 (player-visible gameplay/render/UI), P2=67, P3=7, P4=15 (GameNetwork + online menus, deferred).

title: gpui-status never written: --hyphen flags never construct RuntimeHostBridge
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### hq-status-zero-root-cause (high)
gpui-status never written: hub launched with --hyphen flags the parser stores as 'runtime-host' keys, so RuntimeHostBridge is never constructed (silent None) and zero status writes ever run

C++: Retail C++ accepts only exact single-dash tokens: WinMain.cpp:892-920 tokenizes lpCmdLine via nextParam and matches whole tokens with stricmp, e.g. WinMain.cpp:903 `if (stricmp(token,"-win")==0) ApplicationIsWindowed=true;`. A GNU-style `--runtime-host=windowed` token has no C++ parsing path at all.

Rust: hub describe windowed-generals (failed exit=1 uptime=2m15s, matching brief pid 81341 / ~2m15s): `generals --runtime-host=windowed --windowed ... --gpui-control=/tmp/generals_windowed_control.txt --gpui-status=/tmp/generals_windowed_status.txt --gpui-frame=/tmp/generals_windowed_frame.png`. command_line.rs:338 `let option_name = arg.trim_start_matches('-');` strips dashes but the equals-split at :341-345 keeps the inner hyphen, inserting options key `"runtime-host"`/`"gpui-status"` (generic insert at :112). get_option_value (command_line.rs:531-534) lowercases only — no hyphen→underscore normalization. Consumers use underscore keys: option_takes_value list command_line.rs:397-402 (`runtime_host|gpui_control|gpui_status|gpui_frame`); RuntimeHostBridge::is_runtime_host_requested runtime.rs:218-222 and from_command_line runtime.rs:226-231 (`args.get_option_value("gpui_control")?` etc.). Resu

Fix: Launch with the underscore single-dash form the code and the smoke harness use — exactly executable_smoke.rs:967-978: `-runtime_host=windowed -windowed -gpui_control=… -gpui_status=… -gpui_frame=…`. Durable fix: in CommandLineArgs::parse_option (command_line.rs:343,348) normalize the option name via name.replace('-', "_") (or match both spellings like the existing `"smoke-test"|"smoketest"` alias at command_line.rs:~285), and make RuntimeHostBridge::from_command_line log a warning when `runtime_

### hq-status-write-not-frame-gated (medium)
Answer to the gating question: the status write is NOT gated on a frame that never happens — publish_booting runs synchronously before the event loop, so the hang cannot explain 0 bytes; only bridge-never-constructed can

C++: C++ GameEngine::execute main loop (GameEngine.cpp, m_maxFPS limit ~:856) always returns control to the OS pump each frame; there is no file-status publish in C++ to compare, so the relevant C++ fact is that the WinMain pump (WinMain.cpp:965+) keeps running while frames render — a hung frame would still leave earlier-published observable state.

Rust: run_loop.rs:66-69: `RuntimeHostBridge::from_command_line(...)` then `bridge.publish_booting()` execute synchronously BEFORE `event_loop.run(...)` (run_loop.rs:~88) — not frame-gated. run_loop.rs:322-326 publishes again via publish_booting_from_winit_query immediately after window creation. Per-frame publish_runtime sits at the END of drive_frame (run_loop.rs:282-285) → publish_status → unconditional `let _ = fs::write(&self.status_path, payload)` (runtime.rs, end of publish_status). Therefore a mid-frame hang (macOS 'not responding' = winit closure stuck inside engine.update/render) would freeze updates but leave the LAST payload on disk — proven by the earlier 16:07 run where the same file held `state=Menu ui_screen=Some(MainMenu) fps=30 frame=8374` (session transcript findearthmap_art.jsonl line 287). A 0-byte file requires zero publishes ever — consistent only with bridge None.

Fix: No engine fix needed for the 0 bytes itself; for diagnosis, publish_booting could include the parsed runtime_host/gpui option spellings so a misconfigured launch is visible as state=Booting with an args-mismatch field.
close_reason: Hyphen --runtime-host/--gpui-status aliases construct RuntimeHostBridge. test_hyphen_runtime_host_aliases_resolve + hyphen_runtime_host_flags_construct_bridge pass.

title: Unbounded waypoint chain walks hang Menu after ScriptEngine first update
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### hang-01 (high)
Hang frame identified: everything after 'ScriptEngine first update' runs in ONE unbounded-duration logic frame; update_shell_with_budget(dt,1) bounds frame COUNT not TIME — C++ GAME_SHELL ticks bounded subsystems on the main loop

C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/System/GameLogic.cpp:3600-3602 — TheScriptEngine->UPDATE() runs inline in GameLogic::update on the main logic loop; every pass there (scripts, terrain, modules, AI, partition, destroy list) is bounded per frame, and camera waypoint setup is capped at 25 (W3DView.cpp:2835, W3DView.h:28), so GAME_SHELL never blocks the UI.

Rust: Log fires at the START of crate ScriptEngine::update_active (GameLogic/src/scripting/engine/update.rs:41-52). Same-frame remainder: execute_side_scripts over 10 sides x 82 scripts (update.rs:124-243), team-factory update, sequential progression, then Main's SECOND walker mission_scripts.update (Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/scripts_camera.rs:361-373), the drain block (scripts_camera.rs:423-660), then terrain/water-edge/process_commands/sleepy Movement->host pathfinding (Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/step.rs:131-260). Entry camera_drain.rs:291-293 host_update_shell_with_budget(dt,1) -> step.rs:54-104: the budget limits fixed steps per present, NOT the duration of one update_simulation. shell.rs:1819-1823 already documents a prior minutes-long single step ('pathfinding/scripts + ASSET_MANAGER'). No info log exists between the first-update log and the next warns ('Slow mission script u

Fix: Add per-phase timing/watchdog logging inside evaluate_and_execute_scripts and update_simulation phases so a hung shell frame names its phase; optionally a frame-time abort guard. Do not implement per assignment.

### hang-02 (high)
ScriptCameraPathMove::new walks waypoint link[0] chain with NO bound — infinite loop + unbounded Vec on cyclic/bi-directional paths; C++ caps at MAX_WAYPOINTS=25

C++: W3DView.cpp:2835 'while (pWay && m_mcwpInfo.numWaypoints < MAX_WAYPOINTS)' with W3DView.h:28 'enum {MAX_WAYPOINTS=25};' — chain walk hard-capped. C++ builds the same cyclic graph incl. bi-directional reverse links (TerrainLogic.cpp:1374-1384).

Rust: Main/src/game_logic/game_logic/script_camera.rs:201-208 — 'while let Some(next_id) = current.get_link(0) { ... points.push(...); current = next; }' with no cap or visited-set; reverse links created at GameLogic/src/terrain.rs:2306-2329 (add_waypoint_link). MAP DATA (I RefPack-decoded ShellMapMD.map via a JS port of script_loader.rs decompress_refpack_stream): 139 waypoints, 114 links, 34 waypoints start CYCLIC link[0] chains (Car_Path 17-ring, Chinook_Path 4-ring, Hover_Path1/2, Commanche_Patrol). NOT the observed shell hang: ShellMapMD has ZERO MOVE_CAMERA_ALONG_WAYPOINT_PATH actions (rawType 17 count 0; camera uses rawType 14 MoveCameraTo, bounded) — but any map whose scripts use that action into a cyclic chain hangs forever while C++ stops at 25.

Fix: Port the C++ bound: stop at 25 waypoints or track visited ids; keep partial-chain semantics on dangling links. Do not implement per assignment.

### hang-03 (high)
UnitAIUpdate FollowWaypointPath chain walk unbounded except a >1-link break — cyclic 1-link rings (ShellMapMD Car_Path) loop forever; C++ caps unit waypoint queue at 16

C++: AIUpdate.h:681-683 'enum { MAX_WAYPOINTS = 16 }; Coord3D m_waypointQueue[MAX_WAYPOINTS]' + AIUpdate.cpp:1141 'if (m_waypointCount < MAX_WAYPOINTS)' — unit waypoint queues length-capped.

Rust: GameLogic/src/object/unit/ai_commands.rs:1341-1351 — builds 'chain' via 'while let Some(node) = current { chain.push(...); if node.get_num_links() > 1 { break; } current = node.get_link(0)... }'. Decoded ShellMapMD: Car_Path/Chinook_Path/Hover rings have exactly ONE outgoing link per node -> walk never terminates, 'chain' grows unboundedly. Issued by do_team_follow_waypoints (executor/actions_victory_team.rs:376-421) / do_named_follow_waypoints (actions_named.rs:90-136); the shell patrol scripts target exactly these rings ('Chinooks Patrol' rawType 36 Chinook_Path, 'Hover Patrol' rawType 56 Hover_Path1, 'Spawn Trucks And Attack' rawType 113 Van_Path). Currently no-op on the live host (empty OBJECT_REGISTRY dual-world) but a latent deterministic hang once crate objects/teams are populated.

Fix: Cap the walk at 16 (AIUpdate MAX_WAYPOINTS) or break on revisit. Do not implement per assignment.
close_reason: TerrainLogic::walk_link0_chain visited-set + WAYPOINT_PATH_LIMIT=1024. ScriptCameraPathMove and UnitAI fallback use it. Cyclic Car_Path cannot unbounded-grow.

title: Sync W3D+texture loads on render thread; no negative cache; beachball
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### hang-1 (critical)
CONFIRMED: Live render path performs synchronous W3D loads on the main (render) thread, re-attempted every frame for missing models — render-thread sync-load hang is real

C++: C++ never loads geometry during the frame draw: (1) all condition-state models are preloaded at map load behind the loading screen — W3DModelDraw.cpp:1099 W3DModelDrawModuleData::preloadAssets → :363 ModelConditionInfo::preloadAssets → W3DDisplay.cpp:3195-3207 W3DDisplay::preloadModelAssets → Load_3D_Assets("name.w3d"), and W3DAssetManager.cpp:966-999 Load_3D_Assets early-returns 'this file has already been loaded' from a loaded-files hash so a miss is attempted once per file, never per frame; (2) render objects are persistent per drawable condition state (W3DModelDraw.cpp:3010 m_renderObject = Create_Render_Obj(...) once on state change), the per-frame draw never re-resolves; (3) textures stream on a dedicated background thread — textureloader.cpp:181-205 LoaderThreadClass _TextureLoadThread ('Texture loader thread', priority -4) with _ForegroundQueue/_BackgroundQueue, main thread only 

Rust: run_loop.rs:79-203: winit event_loop.run closure → drive_frame → engine.render() executes on the macOS main thread; blocking it starves AppKit → beachball. Inside render(): input.rs:1377-1382 computes deferred budget and allow_sync_model_loads; pipeline_execute.rs:161-179 collect_render_items → pipeline_collect.rs:919-1093 ensure_render_model_loaded runs INLINE in the frame: locks the global asset manager, calls sync load_w3d_model (manager.rs:2009-2084; block_in_place/block_on when multithread runtime), and on failure falls to resolve_mesh_for_model_key (mesh_asset_resolve.rs:1240-1330) which re-locks the manager and probes up to 4 candidate keys, then try_load_w3d_from_filesystem → find_filesystem_w3d. RenderModelLoadResult::Failed is never cached anywhere (pipeline_collect.rs:624-637 just counts it) and render items are rebuilt statelessly every frame — so every missing model is re-at

Fix: Mirror C++ structure: preload all condition-state models at map/shell load (W3DDisplay::preloadModelAssets analog) with a per-file attempted-once cache, cache negative results (pipeline-level failed-key set mirroring C++ LoadedFiles + HAnimManager.Is_Missing), and make render-time resolution cache-only (fail to no-draw like C++ NULL robj) instead of sync I/O per item per frame.

### hang-2 (critical)
Residual filesystem W3D walk has NO negative cache: ~700-1000 stat'd candidate paths rebuilt and re-stat'd per missing model per frame (the actual per-frame wall)

C++: W3DAssetManager.cpp:966-999: Load_3D_Assets checks the loaded-files hash first and returns TRUE ('this file has already been loaded') — a failed or successful file load is never re-read; assetmgr.cpp:906-908 HAnimManager.Is_Missing(name) skips repeat on-demand loads of known-missing animations; C++ has no per-frame filesystem directory probing at all — asset paths are resolved through the mounted BIG archives and the loaded-files hash.

Rust: mesh_asset_resolve.rs:51-60 W3D_SEARCH_ROOT_RESIDUALS has 9 entries; :919-946 w3d_filename_variants produces ~12 case/casing variants per key; :955-1002 filesystem_w3d_candidates joins ~28 roots (cwd + 9 residuals + 4 cwd-relative + 5 manifest-relative + 9 manifest-../../../ residuals) × filenames × {root, Art/W3D, art/w3d} ≈ 700-1000 PathBufs with a dedup HashSet, and find_filesystem_w3d (:1022-1026) stat's each via is_file(). try_load_w3d_from_filesystem (:1134-1155) is reached from resolve_mesh_for_model_key on EVERY load attempt for a missing model. The AssetManager negative cache missing_model_keys (manager.rs:2025-2033) only guards the archive probe inside load_w3d_model — nothing guards this walk. For a 271-missing-model scene this is ~200k-270k stats + equivalent allocations per frame on the render thread.

Fix: Add a process-wide negative cache keyed by canonical model key that gates resolve_mesh_for_model_key entirely (record on first Missing result, like manager.rs missing_model_keys but covering the residual path), and/or build the root list once as a static — C++ parity is one attempted lookup per file identity, not per frame.

### hang-3 (critical)
Startup deferral budget is bypassed: RenderBridge drain hardcodes allow_sync_model_loads=true, and any non-Menu state (or missing startup anchor) sets budget=0 → unbounded sync loads for ALL items every frame

C++: C++ has no per-frame load budget because it has no per-frame loading — preloadAssets (W3DModelDraw.cpp:1099) covers every drawable's condition states at map load once, and Create_Render_Obj results persist in m_renderObject (W3DModelDraw.cpp:3010). On-demand loading (assetmgr.cpp:728) exists but the persistent-robj design means it fires on state change, not per frame.

Rust: shell.rs:767-791 startup_deferred_model_load_budget returns 0 whenever current_state != Menu or startup_frame is None → input.rs:1382 allow_sync_model_loads = (budget == 0) is then TRUE and pipeline_execute.rs:146-155 sets deferred_model_load_budget = usize::MAX — every render item sync-loads per frame (also triggers prewarm_startup_models, pipeline_execute.rs:127-137). Worse, even inside Menu the GameClient drawable path bypasses the budget entirely: pipeline_execute.rs:210-216 calls drain_render_bridge_submissions, and pipeline_collect.rs:1301-1309 calls ensure_render_model_loaded(graphics_system, model_name, model_name, TRUE, budget) with hardcoded allow_sync=true — every bridge submission (shell-map scenery drawables) gets an uncapped sync load attempt every frame. This is the unbounded 271-model wall behind the brief's 'deferred_loads=4/4 then hang' (the 4/frame budget only throttle

Fix: Pass allow_sync_model_loads through to drain_render_bridge_submissions instead of hardcoded true; treat non-Menu transitions as 'preloaded or fail-closed', not 'sync-load everything per frame' — i.e., invert the default so render-time loads are cache-hit-only and misses defer to a load queue.

### hang-4 (high)
Texture loads also block the render thread: prime_texture_raw_blocking uses block_in_place+block_on inline, forward pass streams up to 64 blocking primes per frame (forward=233ms contributor)

C++: textureloader.cpp:194-205: dedicated background LoaderThreadClass ('Texture loader thread') performs task->Load() I/O off-thread (:936-962 Thread_Function pops _BackgroundQueue, pushes finished tasks to _ForegroundQueue); main thread TextureLoader::Update (:812-837) only applies completed tasks; failures Apply_Missing_Texture() once (:892-910). W3DDisplay::preloadTextureAssets (W3DDisplay.cpp:3210-3221) funnels through Get_Texture which queues rather than blocks.

Rust: manager.rs:1162-1175 prime_texture_raw_blocking wraps the async archive read in tokio::task::block_in_place + Handle::block_on — called from the render thread. forward_render.rs:526-527 calls stream_pending_textures(texture_stream_budget()) at the start of every ForwardPass::render — budget is 64 when >256 pending (forward_materials.rs:597-611), each iteration doing lock + create_texture_from_cached_assets + blocking prime + decode. forward_render.rs:426-510 prewarm_textures_blocking primes ALL requested textures inline (and drains the queue with budget clamped 64-2048) in a single frame. Textures ARE negatively cached (textures.rs:442-447 cache_missing_fallback → known_missing_textures), so this is bounded unlike the model path — but the synchronous archive reads + DDS/TGA decode on the main thread explain the persistent forward=233ms in the brief.

Fix: Port the C++ split: a background texture-load worker (file read + decode off-thread) with the render thread only uploading finished wgpu textures from a drained queue per frame (the existing pending_texture_stream machinery is already the right shape — remove the blocking prime from the render thread).
close_reason: Menu startup_deferred_model_load_budget never returns 0 (missing startup_frame used to flip allow_sync=true). missing_model_keys negative cache on W3D miss.

title: 271 ShellMapMD models missing: ZH .big files are a delta over base Generals
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### W3D-271-ROOT-CAUSE (high)
271 model_missing root cause: the repo ships only the 17 Zero Hour .big files, which are a DELTA over the base Generals install — every pristine base-game mesh (all trees PT*, civilian props CB*/PM*/CV*, faction units AVPaladin/NVMIG/AVLeopard/UIRGrd_SKN, buildings ABPWRPLANT/NBPwrPlant...) exists in no mounted archive. This is an asset-availability problem, not a path-resolution bug.

C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/Win32Device/Common/Win32BIGFileSystem.cpp:31-49 `init()`: `loadBigFilesFromDirectory("", "*.big")` for the ZH run dir, THEN reads base Generals `InstallPath` from the registry and `loadBigFilesFromDirectory(installPath, "*.big")` — retail C++ always mounts the BASE game archives (W3D.big, Textures.big) that carry the shared meshes. ZH-only archives carry just ZH-new/updated art (verified: AVHUMMER.W3D, NVMIGN.W3D, AVTOMAHAWK_MD.W3D exist; pristine AVPaladin/NVMIG/AVTomahawk do not).

Rust: Parsed all 17 BIGs in windows_game/Command & Conquer Generals Zero Hour/ with a BIG index parser: `avpaladin`, `nvmig`, `avtomahawk`, `abpwrplant`, `ptdogwod01`, `ptxpine03`, `uirgrd_skn`, `pmcluster`, `cbquonset1` etc. are in NONE of them (only _d/_md/_n damaged/night/MD variants and .tga/.dds textures exist). Rust already knows: GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/assets/archive.rs:192-218 `warn_if_base_archives_missing` logs 'Base Generals archives not loaded (missing: Textures.big, W3D.big)... Zero Hour models may reference textures unavailable in ZH-only archives'. `add_default_search_paths` (archive.rs:46-160) does probe base-install dir names ('Command & Conquer Generals', .../Data, combined layouts, home-sibling scans) — no such install exists in this repo, so nothing mounts. w3d_load_fallback_keys is intentionally empty (mesh_asset_resolve.rs:~530) so no damaged/MD substitution is made.

Fix: Obtain a base Generals install's W3D.big + Textures.big and place them in windows_game/Command & Conquer Generals Zero Hour/ (or point GENERALS_BASE_INSTALL_PATH / GENERALS_ASSETS_DIR at a base install). No code change needed for resolution; the mount order already mirrors C++ (Common/src/common/system/archive_file_system.rs:55-63 loads *.big from every search root).

### hang-271-models-missing (high)
Only 7 render items survived collection (model_missing=271): the ShellMapMD world's objects have no resolvable W3D models, so just 2 roofs + scraps draw

C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DDisplay.cpp:1875-1876 `// draw all views of the world; drawViews();` — every Drawable's draw modules render each frame; models are loaded through W3DAssetManager at drawable creation (W3DAssetManager.cpp) with retail .BIG archives mounted, so the shell map's full object set (buildings, props, trees) renders. There is no per-frame budget/skip path that silently drops ~97% of world objects.

Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/graphics/render_pipeline/pipeline_collect.rs:624-639 `RenderModelLoadResult::Failed => ... model_missing += 1` (also :223, :265, :707 empty-mesh, :738); SkippedByBudget is a separate counter (:616-623), so the live log's model_missing=271 with render_items=7 means 271 objects genuinely failed model resolution/loading, not just budget deferral. Budgets are also tight: startup prewarm caps at 48 (sync) / 12 (async) candidates (pipeline_prewarm.rs prewarm_startup_models `prewarm_limit`), per-frame deferred loads budgeted (pipeline_execute.rs:146-155; live log 0/16 → 4/4 after apply). The 7 surviving items are the "two arched roofs"; the 271 failures are [INFERENCE] unresolved W3D art names against the mounted asset set (not inspected at runtime), consistent with the skybox TGA set also being unresolvable (hang-no-skybox).

Fix: Capture debug_last_missing_model_samples (pipeline_collect.rs:625-638 caps at 16 names) for one live frame and check each name against the mounted .BIG/loose-asset index — the fix is asset-mount/name-resolution coverage (and prewarm seeded from the actual shell-map object list, not a 48-entry cap), not a renderer change.

### W3D-SHELLMAP-EMPTY-WORLD (high)
Yes — this is (the dominant cause of) the empty world: ShellMapMD places 771 objects; 342 are roads/waypoints/scorch decals, 12 ambients and 3 CINE props are skip-listed, and of the remaining 414 model-bearing placements, 334 (81%) reference meshes absent from every mounted BIG. Only 19 templates / 80 placements can actually render.

C++: Retail C++ renders this map fully because the same 334 placements resolve into base-game W3D.big meshes mounted from the registry install path (Win32BIGFileSystem.cpp:37-49).

Rust: Decompressed MapsZH.big:Maps/ShellMapMD/ShellMapMD.map (EAR\0+RefPack, 86,345→1,116,150 bytes CkMp) with a port of script_loader.rs's decoder and counted ObjectsList v3: 771 placements / 108 templates. Cross-checked each template's INI model (135 INI files parsed from extracted INIZH) against the union of all 17 BIGs: missing = 71 templates / 334 spawnable placements, incl. ALL trees (TreeSpruce03×10→PTXPine03, TreeDogwood2×33→PTDogwod02, TreeFir02×28→PTXFIR02, TreeMaple1×23→PTMaple01, ...), rocks, fences (ChainLinkFence×36→PMWallChn2), docks, drums, and even pristine faction units (AVPaladin, NVMIG, ABPWRPLANT, AVComanche, AVTomahawk). Available (ZH-delta art only): TreePalm1×28 (PTPalm01), GLATrap×16 (NBWall), RocksG*, AVHUMMER×4, ZH-new units (Lazr_Crusader/ChinaTankECM/Helix), etc. The observed 271 sits between the distinct-missing (71) and placement-weighted (334) bounds — it is the

Fix: Treat 271 as a symptom metric, not a bug to chase: with base-game archives mounted it collapses toward zero. Optionally add a boot log summarizing 'map X: N placements dropped for unavailable meshes' so the empty-world cause is visible without debug samples.
close_reason: Cannot ship missing base Generals .big files. Fail-soft: reskin ModelName lookup + negative cache + Menu never unbounded-sync. Remaining: retail base assets still required for 271 meshes.

title: Terrain pass clears backbuffer to peach fog; scene skips C++ black clear
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### hang-peach-clear (critical)
Terrain pass clears the whole backbuffer to map fog color [0.9,0.71,0.6]; main scene pass then skips its black clear — the screen's base color is peach, not black

C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DDisplay.cpp:1640 W3DDisplay::draw; :1859 `WW3D::Begin_Render( true, true, Vector3( 0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f ), TheWaterTransparency->m_minWaterOpacity )` — every frame clears BLACK, then :1876 drawViews() paints skybox+terrain over it. Signature GeneralsMD/Code/Libraries/Source/WWVegas/WW3D2/ww3d.cpp:708 `WW3D::Begin_Render(bool clear,bool clearz,const Vector3 & color,...)`, default color Vector3(0,0,0) (ww3d.h:115). No C++ path ever clears to a lighting/fog color (also :1585 Vector3(0,0,0)).

Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/graphics/render_pipeline/pipeline_minimap.rs:73-97 `terrain_clear_color()` returns `fog_color.or(ambient_color).or(sun_color)` as the clear color (fog first → ShellMapMD lighting [0.9,0.71,0.6] = the observed peach). pipeline_prewarm.rs:335-437 `update_and_enqueue_terrain_pass` enqueues a pre-scene render pass labeled "main terrain pass" whose color attachment is `load: wgpu::LoadOp::Clear(clear_color)` (:397, :412) — it is the FIRST pass to touch the backbuffer each frame (called every execute frame, pipeline_execute.rs:283-285). Libraries/Source/WWVegas/WW3D2/crates/ww3d-renderer-3d/src/rendering/wgpu_main_renderer.rs:413-428: when `had_pre_scene_callbacks` the main scene `render_frame` gets `None` instead of `Some(clear_color)`, i.e. LoadOp::Load — the engine's own black clear (config default Vec4(0,0,0,1), :41) is suppressed exactly when terrain exists. Net

Fix: Make the terrain pass clear opaque black to match W3DDisplay::draw:1859 (or better, leave the terrain pass on LoadOp::Load and let the engine's Begin_Render-equivalent clear black once per frame, restoring the C++ clear-then-draw order). The GENERALS_DEBUG_CLEAR_COLOR env override at pipeline_minimap.rs:74 shows the color was chosen for debugging, not C++ parity. Fog color belongs in the terrain fragment fog blend, never in a clear.
close_reason: terrain_clear_color is wgpu::Color::BLACK matching W3DDisplay.cpp:1859 Begin_Render black clear. Fog no longer paints the backbuffer.

title: Menu→Menu after shell apply destroys MainMenu WND (root_windows=0)
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### HM-1 (high)
Menu→Menu re-transition tears down the shell; C++ never tears down MainMenu when GAME_SHELL finishes

C++: GameLogic.cpp:2195-2203 `if(m_gameMode == GAME_SHELL){ if(TheShell->getScreenCount()==0) TheShell->push("Menus/MainMenu.wnd"); else if(TheShell->top()){TheShell->top()->hide(FALSE); TheShell->top()->bringForward();} HideControlBar(); }` — no hideShell, no MainMenuShutdown. hideShell is explicitly guarded OFF for shell games: GameLogicDispatch.cpp:316-317 `if(!TheGameLogic->isInShellGame()) TheShell->hideShell();`; GameLogic.cpp:2209 `// TheShell->hideShell();` commented out.

Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/cnc_game_engine/input.rs:906-909 — exit arm `GameState::Menu => { debug!("Exiting Menu state"); self.hide_shell_menu(); }` runs even when new_state==Menu. Trigger chain: boot starts Loading with worker (boot.rs:337-341); slow worker (≥8s @ ≥18%, shell.rs:2001-2018) releases Loading→Menu #1 (camera_drain.rs:452-461) which pushes MainMenu.wnd + MainMenuInit; worker later completes → host_finalize_startup_map_load logs 'Loaded startup shell map' (shell.rs:1891) → fallback_to_menu → transition_to_state(Menu) (shell.rs:1946) = Menu→Menu with full teardown.

Fix: In host_transition_to_state, skip the Menu exit-arm teardown when new_state == Menu (mirror GameLogic.cpp:2195-2203: push-if-empty / unhide+bringForward / HideControlBar only). Alternative C++-faithful restore: re-enter an already-hidden stack top through Shell::showShell(true) so run_init (MainMenuInit) re-runs.

### HM-2 (high)
Exact teardown chain that blanks the menu: hideShell(immediate) → MainMenuShutdown → layout.hide(true) on ALL windows

C++: MainMenu.cpp:337-347 static shutdownComplete: `isShuttingDown = FALSE; layout->hide(TRUE); TheShell->shutdownComplete(layout);` — C++ WindowLayout::hide (WindowLayout.cpp:56-73) iterates m_windowList which holds ROOT windows only (WindowLayout.cpp:206-210 load adds only info.windows; MainMenu.wnd has one root MainMenuParent), so hideShell hides one root and children inherit invisibility through the hierarchy.

Rust: input.rs:908 → shell.rs:429-441 hide_shell_menu → base.rs:2593-2611 Shell::hide_shell (clear_background=true; run_shutdown(&mut immediate_pop=true); IME detach; is_shell_active=false) → main_menu.rs:814-853 MainMenuShutdown popImmediate branch → main_menu.rs:2101-2110 finish_shutdown_complete: `layout.hide(true)` + is_shutting_down=false (TheShell->shutdownComplete omitted) → layout.rs:65-75 ManagerWindowLayout::hide queues manager.hide_window(win,true) for EVERY window (Rust layout list includes children — layout_load.rs adds recursively) → hierarchy.rs:284-292 hide_window + window_hiding (hierarchy.rs:366-408: keyboard_focus=None, mouse_capture released, modal popped). base.rs:258-261 sets BasicWindowLayout.state=Destroying. Layout is NOT popped — screen_count stays 1.

Fix: Either drop the exit-arm hide entirely for Menu→Menu (preferred, HM-1), or restore via showShell(true) re-init. Structural: make ManagerWindowLayout::hide touch root windows only (C++ layout membership) so per-child HIDDEN state survives.

### HM-3 (high)
Re-enter restores window bits but NOT what MainMenuInit owns — hybrid of two C++ paths, matches neither

C++: Every C++ path that does hideShell re-enters via showShell(TRUE): Shell.h:112 `void showShell( Bool runInit = TRUE );` → Shell.cpp:385-420 `if(runInit){ top()->runInit(NULL); }`; callers PopupSaveLoad.cpp:398, FileTransfer.cpp:257, GameClient.cpp:555 (after intro). MainMenuInit restores focus: MainMenu.cpp:650-651 `layout->bringForward(); TheWindowManager->winSetFocus(parentMainMenu);`, fade cadence and dropdown resets.

Rust: shell.rs:391-394 `else if let Some(top) = shell.top() { top.hide(false); top.bring_forward(); }` — only clears HIDDEN bits + reorders. MainMenuInit (main_menu.rs:591+) never re-runs: no winSetFocus(parentMainMenu) equivalent, no justEntered fade cadence, no dropdown reset, no init-hide-pack reapplication. Consequences: (a) keyboard focus/mouse capture destroyed by window_hiding during teardown and never restored; (b) menu_world_frames_rendered is NOT reset by the real transition (only the test harness resets it, types.rs:220), so the one-shot first-run reveal at input.rs:1201 (`== 45` exact match, reveal_main_menu_first_input_like_cpp → winHide(FALSE) DROPDOWN_MAIN) cannot re-fire — if the worker finalize landed around/before frame 45 (menu frames stall 220ms-1.4s per the WND overlay rebuild), MapBorder2 (parent of ALL menu buttons — main_menu.rs tests 3983-4098 place ButtonSinglePlayer/

Fix: Re-enter through run_init (showShell(true) semantics) whenever the shell was torn down, or eliminate the teardown (HM-1). Reset menu_world_frames_rendered (or re-arm the reveal) on Menu enter.

### wnd-f1 (critical)
Rust GameClient::reset destroys ALL WND windows via WindowManagerSubsystem::reset — C++ GameClient::reset never touches the window manager (no TheWindowManager->reset() caller exists in retail)

C++: GameClient.cpp:426-457 GameClient::reset() resets drawables, TheDisplay, TerrainVisual, RayEffects, VideoPlayer, Eva, SnowManager ONLY — window manager untouched. Grep of entire GeneralsMD/Code for 'TheWindowManager->reset' returns ZERO callers. Window destruction in retail happens only via Shell::doPop→WindowLayout::destroyWindows (Shell.cpp:609-645), Shell::reset, or ~GameWindowManager. MainMenuShutdown (MainMenu.cpp:658-690) never destroys windows: it latches isShuttingDown, cancels patch check, reverse-animates, then shutdownComplete hides the layout. So shell MainMenu.wnd windows survive every game start/load in C++.

Rust: core/game_client/impl_init.rs:142-181 GameClient::reset() → self.subsystem_manager.reset_all() → core/game_client/subsystem.rs:69-74 resets window_manager → core/subsystems.rs:1241-1251 WindowManagerSubsystem::reset → gui/window_manager/mod.rs:341-357 WindowManager::reset → destroy_all_windows() (create_destroy.rs:143-157 drains root_windows, immediately destroys) + layouts.clear() + transitions.reset(). Live triggers of Common GameEngine::reset → game_client.reset(): Common/src/system/SaveGame/game_state.rs:663-666 (every save-game load) and gui/callbacks/popup_save_load.rs:1010-1020 (WND save/load popup load-failure path: engine.reset() then queue_shell_show(true)). This wipes MainMenu.wnd (and every shell layout) from the WM.

Fix: Match C++: remove the window_manager reset from GameClient::reset()/reset_all() (C++ GameClient::reset resets display/terrain/ray/video/eva/snow only). If a WM clear is ever needed, it must be paired with Shell stack teardown + re-push like C++ Shell::reset + startNewGame GAME_SHELL push (GameLogic.cpp:2195-2203).

### wnd-f2 (critical)
After windows are destroyed, the Shell stack's stale BasicWindowLayout never recreates them — ensure_layout() short-circuits on the surviving Rc; hide(false)/bring_forward/run_init all no-op, leaving draw_all permanently empty

C++: C++ WindowLayout is destroyed together with its windows: Shell::doPop (Shell.cpp:609-645) unlinks AND deletes the layout object; any later shell screen comes from a fresh winCreateLayout + load(.wnd) in doPush (Shell.cpp:583-607). There is no state where a live Shell stack entry references destroyed windows. GameLogic::startNewGame GAME_SHELL branch (GameLogic.cpp:2195-2203) re-pushes 'Menus/MainMenu.wnd' when screenCount==0, else re-shows the intact top.

Rust: gui/shell/base.rs:211-224 BasicWindowLayout::ensure_layout returns early when self.layout is Some — it never re-runs create_layout_with_windows even after WindowManager::reset cleared the WM registry and destroy_window_immediate (window_manager/create_destroy.rs:209-260) marked every window DESTROYED, removed it from root_windows/window_by_id AND from the owning layout's own list (lines 248-254). So the still-on-stack BasicWindowLayout("Menus/MainMenu.wnd") holds layout=Some(empty Rc): run_init runs MainMenuInit callbacks whose find_window_by_name lookups all fail, hide(false)/bring_forward iterate an empty window list. Main's show_shell_menu (cnc_game_engine/shell.rs:389-393) sees get_screen_count()==1 → else-branch top.hide(false)+bring_forward() → nothing recreated; draw_all iterates root_windows (gui/window_manager/draw.rs:40-46) which is empty.

Fix: Either (a) prevent the destroy (wnd-f1 fix), or (b) make ensure_layout() detect the destroyed state (WM layouts registry no longer contains this layout after reset cleared it) and re-create via create_layout_with_windows, mirroring C++ where the layout object dies with its windows.

### wnd-f4 (medium)
Live Menu re-entry never re-runs MainMenuInit: Main show_shell_menu's stack-non-empty branch only hide(false)+bring_forward, while C++ Shell::showShell(TRUE) re-runs layout->runInit → MainMenuInit (dropdown re-hide, scheme reload, focus)

C++: Shell.cpp:385-446 Shell::showShell(runInit=TRUE): 'layout->runInit(NULL)' re-executes MainMenuInit (MainMenu.cpp:429-653): re-hides dropDownWindows[1..] (all dropdowns incl. DROPDOWN_MAIN/MapBorder2 that contains SOLO PLAY), initialHide(), showSelectiveButtons(SHOW_NONE), layout->hide(FALSE) (line ~579), loadScheme("MainMenu"), bringForward(), winSetFocus(parentMainMenu). WindowLayout::hide (WindowLayout.cpp:56-73) sets winHide on every window and latches m_hidden; runInit is inline in WindowLayout.h:93. GameLogic.cpp:2199-2203 uses the hide(FALSE)+bringForward variant only for the in-game→shell branch — both C++ entry points exist.

Rust: Rust Shell::show_shell(run_init=true) (base.rs:2551-2577) faithfully ports showShell incl. run_init on the top layout, but the live Menu-state entry path never calls it: input.rs:931-956 transition_to_state(Menu) → self.show_shell_menu() (cnc_game_engine/shell.rs:364-426), which does Shell init + show_shell_map(true) + {count==0 → push | else top.hide(false)+top.bring_forward()} — no run_init. After hide_shell (shell.rs:436; base.rs:2593-2610 runs shutdown → finish_shutdown_complete → layout.hide(true) on ALL windows incl. dropdowns), re-entry just unhides everything: stale dropdown/not_shown/just_entered state, no scheme reload, no focus — and combined with wnd-f1/f2 the unhide is a no-op on destroyed windows.

Fix: Route the stack-non-empty branch through Shell::show_shell(true) (run_init) instead of the inline hide/bring_forward pair, matching C++ showShell(TRUE); keep the count==0 push behavior (show_main_menu_after_shell_game_start, base.rs:2580-2590) for the empty-stack branch.

### wnd-f5 (medium)
Observable symptom chain answering 'is draw_all empty': flush_ui_to_frame sees root_windows=0 → zero draw commands → UI render pass skipped → 3D shell-map terrain with no SOLO PLAY/buttons; the 45-frame fallback reveal cannot heal destroyed windows

C++: C++ ordering is correct and always repaints: W3DDisplay.cpp:1863-1867 draws the 3D scene, then TheInGameUI->draw() — which ends with TheWindowManager->winRepaint() (W3DInGameUI.cpp:415) — before End_Render. winRepaint (GameWindowManager.cpp:1309-1340) walks the intact window list in BELOW/normal/ABOVE tail-to-head passes every frame; retail never reaches a shell-active state with destroyed windows.

Rust: Render order parity confirmed (not the bug): Main/src/graphics/render_pipeline/forward_render.rs:670-672 enqueues flush_ui_to_frame as a post-frame callback after the scene; ui_render_pass.rs:147-190 reads root_window_count, calls draw_all, and on had_draw_commands==0 logs 'flush_ui_to_frame: zero draw commands (root_windows=N) — gadget draws queued nothing', ends the frame and returns Ok — no UI render pass at all. draw_all (gui/window_manager/draw.rs:40-77) iterates root_windows only (correct winRepaint port incl. hidden-subtree suppression). After wnd-f1/f2 destruction root_windows is permanently 0. Main's mitigation — input.rs:1198-1203 'staring at terrain with no chrome, reveal after ~1.5s' → reveal_main_menu_first_input_like_cpp → reveal_hidden_main_menu (main_menu.rs:650-662) — only flips not_shown and unhides MapBorder2 via find_window_by_name, which returns None for destroyed wi

Fix: Fix the root causes (wnd-f1/f2/f3) rather than the symptom. Diagnostic aid: the existing 'zero draw commands (root_windows=N)' log plus the Shell top-filename residual (dispatch.rs:793-797) lets a smoke test assert root_windows>0 whenever GameState::Menu has a non-empty shell stack.
close_reason: Menu->Menu skips hide_shell_menu. WindowManagerSubsystem::reset is a no-op like C++ GameClient::reset. ButtonSinglePlayer survives reset test.

title: [SpecialPower] leftover can_do_special_power unused — live invents location click for no-target leftover powers
description:
## C++
ActionManager::canDoSpecialPower (ActionManager.cpp:1820-1907) is the no-target gate. After module/ready, SPECIAL_REMOTE_CHARGES / SPECIAL_CIA_INTELLIGENCE / SPECIAL_COMMUNICATIONS_DOWNLOAD / SPECIAL_DETONATE_DIRTY_NUKE / SPECIAL_CHANGE_BATTLE_PLANS / SPECIAL_LAUNCH_BAIKONUR_ROCKET return TRUE; location/object-only types return FALSE. CommandXlat.cpp:1080-1098 issues MSG_DO_SPECIAL_POWER when the button has neither COMMAND_OPTION_NEED_OBJECT_TARGET nor NEED_TARGET_POS. ControlBarCommandProcessing.cpp:829-836 fires GUI_COMMAND_SPECIAL_POWER immediately as MSG_DO_SPECIAL_POWER (no map click).

## Leftover
TheActionManager::can_do_special_power (action_manager.rs:834-902) matches that switch. command_button.rs:437-443 is_valid_to_use_on routes no-option buttons through leftover can_do_special_power. leftover can_do_special_power_at_location is FALSE for CIA / CommunicationsDownload / DetonateDirtyNuke / ChangeBattlePlans / RemoteCharges (special_power_at_location_ok `_ => false`).

## Live
Main never calls leftover can_do_special_power. special_power_pending_options (ui_commands.rs:2546-2562) defaults those leftover no-target types to NEED_POS. DoSpecialPower button arming (ui_commands.rs:2259-2312) always arms PendingMapCommand::SpecialPower. execute_special_power then leftover_can_do_special_power_at_location (command_executor/special_power.rs:286-300) rejects empty-ground CIA/CommunicationsDownload/DetonateDirtyNuke/RemoteCharges. leftover_can_do_special_power_at_object allows them (`!location_target_only`). PowerTarget::None is never issued from the command bar.

## Player-visible
CIA Intelligence / Communications Download / Detonate Dirty Nuke / Remote Charges (detonate) need a map click. Empty ground is leftover-illegal. Button-only leftover/C++ fire never runs. Clicking a unit can fire leftover no-target powers.
close_reason: Live leftover-calls ActionManager::can_do_special_power / special_power_is_no_target for leftover no-target powers (CIA/CommunicationsDownload/DetonateDirtyNuke/RemoteCharges/BattlePlan/Baikonur). Named buttons fire immediately with PowerTarget::None; pending options no longer invent NEED_POS; empty-ground Location stays leftover-illegal; leftover no-target unit clicks are leftover at_object false.

title: [ScriptCond] Live UNIT_HEALTH injects current max as InitialHealth
description:
## C++
`ScriptConditions::evaluateUnitHealth` (ScriptConditions.cpp:924-934) is `(curHealth*100 + initialHealth/2)/initialHealth` where `initialHealth = BodyModule::getInitialHealth()`. ActiveBody stores `m_initialHealth` from INI `InitialHealth` (often != `MaxHealth`). `setInitialHealth(percent)` only changes current HP; `setMaxHealth` overwrites both max and initial.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/object/body/active_body.rs` keeps `initial_health` separate from `max_health` (`get_initial_health` 2079-2083). Leftover `eval_unit_health` (executor/eval_named.rs:863-868) on the empty-registry live path uses host snapshot `obj.initial_health` with the C++ formula. `HostScriptQueryObject.initial_health` is that C++ InitialHealth field.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/scripts_camera.rs:527` injects `initial_health: obj.health.maximum.max(obj.max_health).max(1.0)` — current max, not leftover/C++ InitialHealth. Live spawn (`object/construct.rs`) seeds both current and max from `template.max_health` only. Map `objectInitialHealth` (`world_save.rs:170-175`) scales current HP and never stores a separate initial.

## Evidence
A unit with INI InitialHealth 80 / MaxHealth 100 at full authored start: C++/leftover percent = 100; live inject denominator 100 with current 80 → ~80%. After map objectInitialHealth=50 with InitialHealth==MaxHealth both agree; the INI mismatch and post-upgrade/veterancy cases do not.

## Player-visible
Campaign/skirmish UNIT_HEALTH scripts fire at the wrong HP percent whenever authored InitialHealth != live current max.

Not a duplicate of closed hq-rjnou (leftover eval formula, now leftover-right).
close_reason: Live UNIT_HEALTH injects leftover/C++ InitialHealth (not current max). Object stores initial_health from leftover ActiveBody INI; setMaxHealth overwrites it; setInitialHealth/objectInitialHealth only scales current HP.

title: [HUD] Live never feeds leftover idle-worker ButtonIdleWorker enable
description:
C++ path + behavior:
Player.cpp addOwnedObject / idle-dozer bookkeeping calls InGameUI::addIdleWorker. IdleWorker.cpp update enables ControlBar.wnd:ButtonIdleWorker when the local idle-dozer count is > 0 (and input is enabled). The button stays disabled with zero idle workers.

Leftover path + behavior:
gamelogic::player::Player::add_owned_object (GameLogic/src/player/core.rs) posts TheInGameUI::add_idle_worker for idle dozers. IdleWorkerCallbacks::refresh_idle_workers_from_logic drains take_idle_worker_events and update_idle_worker_button enables ControlBar.wnd:ButtonIdleWorker when worker_count > 0 (GameClient/src/gui/callbacks/ingame_callbacks.rs). Matches C++.

Live path + behavior:
Main GameLogic owns host dozers. Code/Main never calls leftover add_idle_worker / never posts leftover idle-worker additions from host idle dozers (no matches under Main/). Leftover PlayerList + OBJECT_REGISTRY stay empty on the live host, so leftover events never fire. ButtonIdleWorker stays disabled even when the host has idle dozers.

Evidence:
- C++ InGameUI addIdleWorker + IdleWorker button enable
- leftover Player::add_owned_object → TheInGameUI::add_idle_worker
- leftover IdleWorkerCallbacks::update_idle_worker_button
- live Main: zero add_idle_worker / TheInGameUI::add_idle_worker / idle_worker_additions calls
- not a duplicate of closed hq-9x2 (that was click-to-select bridging, not count/enable)

title: [Guard] HijackGuard inner scan skips canHijackVehicle aircraft/drone gates
description:
## C++
`AIGuardMachine::lookForInnerTarget` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/AI/AIGuard.cpp:221-230`) for `isHijackGuard()` installs `PartitionFilterPossibleToHijack` + `ALLOW_ENEMIES`. That filter is `ActionManager::canHijackVehicle` (`ActionManager.cpp:829-887`): live, unshrouded, Enemies, KINDOF_VEHICLE, not KINDOF_AIRCRAFT, not KINDOF_DRONE, and a HijackedVehicleCrateCollide `wouldLikeToCollideWith`. Closest legal vehicle wins.

## Leftover (right)
`scan_guard_inner_target` (`GameLogic/src/ai/guard.rs:188-197`) uses `relationship_to == Enemies` then `TheActionManager::can_hijack_vehicle` (`action_manager.rs:1350-1392`), which ports the same aircraft/drone/shroud/collide gates.

## Live (wrong)
`scan_guard_inner_target` (`Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/support_states.rs:453-459`) for `hijack_guard` only checks `rel == Enemies`, `KindOf::Vehicle`, and `!is_hijacked`. No aircraft reject, no drone reject, no shroud, no HijackedVehicleCrateCollide. CommandButtonHunt `hunt_enter_action_ok` already rejects aircraft/drone; Guard HijackGuard does not.

A Guard-ordered Hijacker therefore acquires the closest Comanche/drone (KINDOF_VEHICLE) as nemesis and walks off the legal tank. Enter-hunt is already gated; Guard scan is not.

## Evidence
Not hq-h8azg (HijackGuard unused — closed; scan now runs). Not hq-wtvdj (EnterGuard canEnterObject). Not hq-3uwdw (hijack *action* ImmuneToCapture/drone/boat — the click/collide path, not Guard inner scan).
close_reason: Live HijackGuard inner scan now uses ActionManager::canHijackVehicle gates: shroud, Vehicle, not Aircraft, not Drone, HijackedVehicleCrateCollide wouldLikeToCollideWith (hijack_target_rejected).

title: [Hunt] findClosestEnemy/guard ignore undetected-defector getRelationship
description:
## C++
`Object::getRelationship` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Object.cpp:1548-1568`):
- `getIsUndetectedDefector()` → `NEUTRAL` so the defector's AI does not auto-acquire and give away position
- `that->getIsUndetectedDefector()` → `ALLIES` so teammates treat the flashing defector as their own

`AI::findClosestEnemy` (`AI.cpp:579-622`) always runs `PartitionFilterLiveMapEnemies`, which requires `getRelationship == ENEMIES`. Guard `lookForInnerTarget` (`AIGuard.cpp:209`) uses `PartitionFilterRelationship ALLOW_ENEMIES` on the same `getRelationship`. Hunt and Guard therefore skip the defector and the defector skips hunting during the undetected window (defector crate / hijack / conversion).

## Leftover (right)
`Object::relationship_to` (`GameLogic/src/object/object_queries.rs:69-82`) applies the same two overrides before `Team::get_relationship`. Leftover hunt (`ai/states/hunt.rs` → `find_closest_enemy`) and leftover guard (`ai/guard.rs:190,211` `relationship_to`) inherit them.

## Live (wrong)
`GameLogic::object_relationship` / `object_relationship_from_owners` (`Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/object_queries.rs:450-525`) never consults `Object::is_undetected_defector`. Hunt `find_closest_enemy` (`world_tick/mood.rs:190-194`) uses that when both objects have owners. Guard `scan_guard_inner_target` (`world_objects/support_states.rs:446-468`) uses `host_guard_leftover_relationship` → the same owner map.

After a team flip, live hunt/guard treat the new owner as Enemies immediately: the defector auto-hunts old teammates (gives away position) and old teammates auto-hunt the flashing defector.

## Evidence
Not hq-kb4sr (converted units keep orders / skip radar-voice-kickout). Not hq-nde4y (Neutral civilians on Guard). Not stealthed-undetected beads (hq-29qjk / hq-am2jn).
close_reason: Live object_relationship, host_guard_leftover_relationship, and find_closest_enemy apply C++ Object::getRelationship undetected-defector overrides (self Neutral, that Allies).

title: [Phys/Bounce] Live motion-step bounce overwrites leftover 0-or-PI roll
description:
C++: `PhysicsBehavior::handleBounce` (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:505-512) on `vz < 0` rights with `setAngles(yaw, 0, zvec.Z>0 ? 0 : PI)` so inverted wrecks stay inverted (roll=PI). `testStunnedUnitForDestruction` then still sees a flip.

Leftover: `physics_bounce.rs:48-58` ports that 0-or-PI roll from `up_z`. Live even has the leftover helper `right_physics_pitch_keep_flip` (`physics_motion.rs:582-598`) and `compute_ground_bounce_force` calls it (`:709-712`).

Live motion-step then overwrites it: `tick_physics_motion_step` (`physics_motion.rs:885-894`) after applying bounce force calls `right_physics_pitch_roll`, which rebuilds yaw-only (`setAngles(yaw,0,0)`). `handle_shock_ground_bounce` (`:958`) does the same. Leftover 0-or-PI righting never survives the live Euler.

Evidence: leftover `object/behavior/physics_bounce.rs:48-58`, C++ PhysicsUpdate.cpp:505-512, live `object/physics_motion.rs:573-580, 885-894, 956-958`.

Player-visible: tossed / stunned vehicles that land inverted are slammed upright on the bounce, so leftover stun-kill-on-flip and inverted wreck poses never stick.
close_reason: Live bounce keeps leftover 0-or-PI roll through motion-step and shock bounce so stun-kill sees flip; parachute building bounce already walks contained_by to outermost chute.

title: [Locomotor] Live FACE leftover handleBehaviorZ unused — pose-Y then double Z
description:
C++: `Locomotor::locoUpdate_moveTowardsAngle` (Locomotor.cpp:847-896). If `getMinSpeed() > 0`, it projects a point along the goal heading and calls `locoUpdate_moveTowardsPosition` once (appearance mover + one `handleBehaviorZ` with real terrain). Else rotate + one `handleBehaviorZ`. Never a second Z pass.

Leftover: `maintain.rs:53-93` `loco_update_move_towards_angle` matches that: minSpeed delegates to leftover `move_towards` (single `handle_behavior_z_for` via leftover `get_surface_ht_at_pt`).

Live: `Object::loco_update_move_towards_angle` (`object/physics.rs:623-653`) applies a homemade rotate + `apply_forward_speed_force`, then calls `handle_behavior_z(p.y)` / `handle_behavior_z(us.y)` using the object's own altitude as surface. `world_tick/movement.rs:345-349` then always calls `apply_live_handle_behavior_z(obj, surface_y, None)` again. Leftover single-pass terrain Z is unused.

Evidence: leftover `locomotor/core_impl/maintain.rs:53-93`, leftover `behavior_z.rs:121-179`, live `object/physics.rs:623-653`, live `world_tick/movement.rs:342-349`.

Player-visible: script / NeedToFace / idle FACE on hover and wings applies lift twice and the first pass aims at `preferredHeight + currentY`, so Comanche/Raptor FACE climbs off the authored hover/cruise band instead of leftover-holding height.
close_reason: Live FACE leftover-marches leftover-terrain Z once: loco_update_move_towards_angle is XY-only; movement.rs apply_live_handle_behavior_z uses leftover_surface_ht. No pose-Y then double lift.

title: [Locomotor] Live march ignores leftover CloseEnoughDist3D
description:
C++: `AIUpdateInterface::getLocomotorDistanceToGoal` (AIUpdate.cpp:2448-2456) uses 3D center-to-goal when `m_curLocomotor->isCloseEnoughDist3D()` or `KINDOF_PROJECTILE`. `LocomotorTemplate::m_isCloseEnoughDist3D` is parsed from `CloseEnoughDist3D` and stamped onto `IS_CLOSE_ENOUGH_DIST_3D` (Locomotor.cpp:473, 640). That 3D remaining-path feeds approach-brake and arrival so diving missiles keep flying until they are actually at the last node, not merely above its XY.

Leftover: `ini_bridge.rs` copies `is_close_enough_dist_3d`. `Locomotor` sets `FLAG_CLOSE_ENOUGH_3D`. `ai_loco.rs:857-858` and leftover `path_following.rs` measure 3D length when the flag or projectile is set.

Live: `HostLocomotorBinding` / `apply_host_locomotor_binding` never bind the flag. `world_tick/movement.rs` waypoint-advance and `reached_target` always use 2D `horiz()`. `raise_on_path_dist_to_goal` only special-cases projectiles to skip the 2× IS_BRAKING latch, still using 2D distance.

Evidence: leftover `GameLogic/src/object/unit/ai_loco.rs:857`, leftover `locomotor/ini_bridge.rs:162`, live `locomotor_bootstrap.rs:276-281` (no 3D field), live `world_tick/movement.rs:442-446, 923`.

Player-visible: SCUD / neutron / other CloseEnoughDist3D or projectile locos treat “over the target” as arrived while still high, so they cut throttle / plant / detonate in the air instead of diving the last vertical stretch.
close_reason: Live march leftover-uses CloseEnoughDist3D: on_path_dist seeds leftover get_locomotor_distance_to_goal 3D to last node so diving missiles keep flying until actually at the node.

title: [PlaceEvent] Sneak-attack construction drops placement facing
description:
## C++
`PlaceEventTranslator.cpp:214-232` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/MessageStream/PlaceEventTranslator.cpp`): when the builder `ProductionUpdateInterface::getSpecialPowerConstructionCommandButton()` is set (sneak-attack construct), LMB confirm appends `MSG_DO_SPECIAL_POWER_AT_LOCATION` with special-power template ID, world, **placement angle**, options, and source object. `OCLSpecialPower::doSpecialPowerAtLocation` (`OCLSpecialPower.cpp:167-185`) forwards that angle into `ObjectCreationList::create(...)`, so the spawned tunnel faces the click-drag heading.

## Leftover (right)
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/message_stream/place_event_translator.rs` `handle_place_click` emits `GameMessageType::DoSpecialPowerAtLocation(pending.power_id, world, angle, 0, pending.options, source)` using `TheInGameUI::get_placement_angle()`. `command_router.rs` appends the real. `GameLogic` `handler_special.rs` reads arg 2 as angle and calls `do_special_power_at_location(&pos, angle, ...)`. Leftover `Object::do_special_power_at_location` / `OclSpecialPower` forward the angle (hq-9qp8 closed).

title: [Weapon] leftover RATIONALIZE getAttackRange/isContactWeapon unused — live peels raw range + #else FUDGE
description:

The `#else` `ATTACK_RANGE_FUDGE=1.05` branch is not compiled.

## Leftover (RIGHT)
`GameLogic/src/weapon/template.rs`:
- `get_attack_range` / `get_minimum_attack_range` apply the same −¼ cell undersize.
- `is_contact_weapon` uses `(attack_range - 2.5) < 10`.

`Main/src/game_logic/thing.rs` `weapon_from_store` copies `wt.attack_range` / `wt.minimum_attack_range` raw — never calls leftover `get_attack_range` / `get_minimum_attack_range`.

close_reason: Live peels leftover RATIONALIZE getAttackRange/getMinimumAttackRange/isContactWeapon. weapon_from_store uses leftover get_attack_range/get_minimum_attack_range (−¼ cell). is_contact_weapon_range uses (authored-2.5)<10 not #else FUDGE 1.05. host_is_contact_weapon_name peels leftover is_contact_weapon. description:

title: [Cam] ROLLING_AVERAGE persists onto next path
description:
C++ W3DView::cameraModRollingAverage (W3DView.cpp:2740-2746) writes m_mcwpInfo.rollingAverageFrames, but W3DView::setupWaypointPath (W3DView.cpp:2865) hard-resets rollingAverageFrames=1 at the start of every new path (moveCameraTo, moveCameraAlongWaypointPath, resetCamera). An idle CAMERA_MOD_SET_ROLLING_AVERAGE is never observable on a later path; it only smooths a path already in flight (moveAlongWaypointPath avgFactor, W3DView.cpp:3126).

Leftover View::camera_mod_rolling_average (GameClient/src/display/view.rs:2607-2611) applies only to an existing camera_path and drops the request when idle. CameraPath::new initializes rolling_average_frames:1 (cinematic_camera.rs:426). No pending arm.

Live GameLogic::apply_script_camera_mod_rolling_average (Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/scripts_camera.rs:5793-5803) stores script_camera_pending_rolling_average_frames when no path is active, and start_camera_path_move (scripts_camera.rs:5505-5507) applies those frames to the NEXT path. Test camera_mod_rolling_average_arms_for_next_camera_path encodes the wrong behavior.

Observable: script issues CAMERA_MOD_SET_ROLLING_AVERAGE(N) while idle, then later MOVE_CAMERA_ALONG_WAYPOINT_PATH — C++/leftover path runs unsmoothed (rolling=1); live path runs with N-frame lagged focus.
close_reason: Idle CAMERA_MOD_SET_ROLLING_AVERAGE no longer arms the next path; apply only to in-flight script_camera_path (C++ setupWaypointPath reset / leftover drop).

title: [Physics] Live onCollide immobile test uses !can_move not KINDOF_IMMOBILE
description:
## C++
`PhysicsBehavior::onCollide` (`PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1221-1222`) uses `other->isKindOf(KINDOF_IMMOBILE)` only. Dead, EMP-disabled, deployed, docked, or garrisoned mobiles stay mobile: `processCollision` (usually no stiffness bounce). Immobile mass cheat is 999999; crash/stiffness path is buildings/trees/props.

## Leftover
`physics_collide.rs:144` `other_immobile = other.is_kind_of(KindOf::Immobile)`. Same KindOf gate as C++.

## Live
`GameLogic::try_physics_collide` (`world_tick/physics.rs:242-246`) and `apply_immobile_collide_bounce` (`:602-606`) classify other as immobile via:
`KindOf::Structure || KindOf::Structure /* immobile residual */ || !can_move()`.
`Object::can_move` (`object/orders.rs:5-19`) is not C++ `isMobile`: it also requires `is_alive`, `!deployed`, `!is_disabled()`, `!flailing`, and not Docked/Garrisoned.

So a tank hitting a dead wreck, EMP'd Humvee, deployed Tomahawk, or garrisoned infantry takes the building stiffness/crash path. C++/leftover keep those as mobile-mobile `processCollision`. Live has `KindOf::Immobile` (used in crash evaluate) but the pair-loop immobile test never reads it.

## Evidence
Leftover-right / live-wrong. Not a closed dup of hq-exasi (living AI bounce off real immobile), hq-yunv0 (stiffness zeros vel), hq-owowd (dead wrecks skip collide).
close_reason: Live try_physics_collide, apply_immobile_collide_bounce, and evaluate_vehicle_crash_into now classify other as immobile via KindOf::Immobile only (C++ PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1221-1222 / leftover physics_collide.rs:144). Dead, EMP, deployed, docked, or garrisoned mobiles stay processCollision. Test: collide_immobile_is_kindof_immobile_not_can_move.

title: [Locomotor] Live FACE is one-frame yaw not ANGLE-goal locoUpdate
description:
## C++
`AIFaceState` (`AIStates.cpp:7403-7455`) sets `m_canTurnInPlace = curLoco->getMinSpeed()==0`. Each update until `|relAngle| < ~2°`:
- turn-in-place → `setLocomotorGoalOrientation` (`AIUpdate.cpp:2228-2230` calls `locoUpdate_moveTowardsAngle`)
- else (Wings/Thrust minSpeed>0) → `setLocomotorGoalPositionExplicit` so the unit flies a curve toward the face point.

`locoUpdate_moveTowardsAngle` (`Locomotor.cpp:847-896`): stun return; if minSpeed>0 invent a point `2*minSpeed` along the heading and `locoUpdate_moveTowardsPosition`; else rotate + `handleBehaviorZ`.

## Leftover
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/states/face.rs` `face_towards`: same `min_speed==0` gate, ANGLE vs POSITION_EXPLICIT, persist until 0.035 rad.
`AIUpdateInterface::do_locomotor` `LocoGoalType::Angle` → `loco_update_move_towards_angle` (`maintain.rs:48-86`).

## Live
`GameLogic::private_face_position` / `private_face_object` (`world_tick/physics.rs:758-791`) call `Object::face_position` (`object/rtb.rs:740-746`) once: `rotate_towards_position` and return true.
- No persist-until-faced Face state (script FACE turns one `maxTurnRate` slice).
- No `canTurnInPlace` (jets spin in place instead of flying toward the point).
- `loco_update_move_towards_angle` exists (`object/physics.rs:623-654`) but is only called from a unit test, never from Face/script FACE.

## Evidence
Leftover-right / live-wrong. Not a closed dup of hq-rpufb (FACE leftover-only, closed when host started moving), hq-2zqa (snap-rotate, closed after `rotate_towards_position`), hq-ixce (Face xfer).
close_reason: Live FACE persists as ANGLE-goal locoUpdate (minSpeed==0) or POSITION_EXPLICIT (jets); not one-frame yaw.

title: [Hunt] findClosestEnemy ranks by center not FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_2D
description:
## C++
`AI::findClosestEnemy` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/AI/AI.cpp:651-681`) ranks with `FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_2D`:
- no AttackPriorityInfo: `getClosestObject(..., FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_2D, filters)`
- with priority: `iterateObjectsInRange(..., FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_2D, ...)` then `getDistanceSquared(..., FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_2D)` for the priority-distance modifier.
Bounding-sphere 2D is center XY minus both objects' bounding-circle radii (0 if hulls overlap). Hunt (`AIHuntState::update`) and mood acquire (`getNextMoodTarget`) both call this.

## Leftover
`AI::find_closest_enemy` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/mod.rs:1787-1791`) uses `ThePartitionManager::get_distance_squared(..., FROM_BOUNDING_SPHERE_2D)`. Helper `object_queries.rs:583-591` subtracts both bounding-circle radii, matching C++.

## Live
`GameLogic::find_closest_enemy` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/mood.rs:223-226`) ranks with raw center-to-center XZ:
```
let dx = opos.x - me_pos.x;
let dz = opos.z - me_pos.z;
let dist = (dx * dx + dz * dz).sqrt();
```
No radius subtract. Hunt (`ai_authority.rs` Patrolling) and mood (`get_next_mood_target`) both use this.

## Evidence
Hunt/mood closest-first among mixed sizes picks the nearer *center*, not the nearer hull. A large building 200wu center / 50wu radius is 150wu bounding-sphere; infantry 180wu center / 5wu radius is 175wu. C++/leftover attack the building first; live attacks the infantry. Not hq-ta2g (leftover crate partition, closed), hq-cwobf (attack *range*), or hq-q7tog (guard FROM_CENTER_2D).
close_reason: Live find_closest_enemy now ranks (and applies the priority-distance modifier) with leftover FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_2D via Object::distance_to_object: center XZ minus both bounding-circle radii, 0 if hulls overlap. Hunt and mood acquire both call this. Mixed-size case: building 200/r50 (hull 145) beats infantry 180/r5 (hull 170).

title: [Weapon] chooseBest lock unused — live combat select falls through temp lock
description:
## C++
`WeaponSet::chooseBestWeaponForTarget` (WeaponSet.cpp:782-783): `if (isCurWeaponLocked()) return TRUE` — current slot stays locked until someone unlocks. FireCurrentWeapon then fires that slot; a reloading FireWeapon/flashbang/snipe waits, it does not auto-choose PRIMARY.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/weapon/weapon_set.rs:683-685` same early return. Leftover fire uses `current_weapon`.

## Live (wrong)
`GameLogic::choose_best_weapon_for_target` (`world_tick/physics.rs:849-850`) does honor lock.

The live combat tick does not. `update_combat` (`world_tick/combat.rs:275-276`) calls `select_combat_weapon_slot`, which (`object/weapons.rs:485-499`) returns the locked slot only when ready+in-range; `LockedTemporarily` "may fall through if clip empty / not ready" into PreferMostDamage auto-choose.

Ranger FireWeapon flashbang / Jarmen snipe / MD laser (LOCKED_TEMPORARILY) mid-reload therefore fires PRIMARY instead of waiting on the locked slot.

## Evidence
Leftover crate is RIGHT. Live should leftover-apply the lock early-return in `select_combat_weapon_slot` (the path `update_combat` actually fires) instead of re-choosing while the temp lock is held.
close_reason: select_combat_weapon_slot leftover-applies choose_best_locked_slot; update_combat FireCurrentWeapon-waits on locked unready slot instead of PreferMostDamage PRIMARY.

title: [Weapon] chooseBest ground attack never leftover-resets PRIMARY
description:
## C++
`WeaponSet::chooseBestWeaponForTarget` (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/WeaponSet.cpp:782-790) returns immediately if `isCurWeaponLocked()`. Otherwise `victim == NULL` (attack-ground / no object) sets `m_curWeapon = PRIMARY_WEAPON` and returns TRUE. Comment: lock is checked first for attack-ground powers; otherwise only Primary attacks the ground.

AIAttackState re-runs chooseBest every frame, so an unlocked unit that just auto-chose SECONDARY (Humvee TOW, Ranger flashbang vs infantry) force-attacking ground fires PRIMARY.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/weapon/weapon_set.rs:683-691` ports both arms: lock → Ok(true); `target_obj == 0` → `current_weapon = Primary`, Ok(true).

## Live (wrong)
`GameLogic::choose_best_weapon_for_target` (`Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/physics.rs:845-856`) honors lock, then on `victim_id == None` only returns `has any slot` and never `set_active_weapon_slot(0)`. No live caller passes `None` anyway.

`unit_command_attack_ground` (`world_scripts/unit_commands.rs:661-689`) never resets the slot.

Ground fire (`world_tick/combat.rs:2397-2413`) uses lock or `active_weapon_slot`. Comment says "Normal ground fire stays primary" but a leftover PreferMostDamage object-attack leaves `active_weapon_slot == 1`, so force-attack-ground keeps TOW/flashbang.

## Evidence
Unlocked Humvee that just shot a tank with TOW, then force-attacks ground: C++/leftover PRIMARY gun; live fires SECONDARY at the point.
close_reason: chooseBest no-victim, unit_command_attack_ground, and ground fire leftover-reset PRIMARY unless locked.

title: [ScriptCond] Live PLAYER_ALL_DESTROYED census counts KINDOF_INERT
description:
## C++
`Team::hasAnyObjects` (`Team.cpp:1751-1776`) skips effectively-dead, destroyed, `KINDOF_PROJECTILE`, `KINDOF_INERT` (radiation fields stay living so ambulances can attack them), and `KINDOF_MINE`. `Player::hasAnyObjects` is the team-prototype walk of that filter. `ScriptConditions::evaluateAllDestroyed` (`ScriptConditions.cpp:207-208`) is `!pPlayer->hasAnyObjects()`.

## Leftover
`Player::has_any_objects` (`GameLogic/src/player/objects.rs:16-20`) and `Team::has_any_objects` (`Common/src/common/rts/team.rs:1330-1343`) skip Projectile, Inert, and Mine — matches C++. Leftover `host_team_has_any_live_objects` (`scripting/conditions/helpers.rs:386-398`) also skips `kind_inert` for TEAM_DESTROYED. `eval_player_all_destroyed` (`executor/eval_basic.rs:607-611`) and `eval_lifecycle` treat injected `HostScriptPlayerCensus.has_any_objects` as C++ `Player::hasAnyObjects`.

## Live
`merge_host_player_census_into_snapshot` (`Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/scripts_camera.rs:751-760`) sets `census.has_any_objects` when the object is not dead and not Projectile/Mine/SmallMissile/BallisticMissile. It never skips `KINDOF_INERT`, even though the same inject already computes `kind_inert` via `leftover_host_template_is_inert` for every `HostScriptQueryObject`. A player whose only remaining objects are radiation fields / other INERT keepalives therefore fails `PLAYER_ALL_DESTROYED` on the live host.

## Evidence
Live `scripts_camera.rs:751-760` vs leftover `objects.rs:16-20` and `helpers.rs:395-397`. Not a duplicate of closed `hq-oep8q` (Victory `counts_as_any_object`, already fixed) or `hq-p46mc` (empty census always-true).
close_reason: Live merge_host_player_census_into_snapshot now leftover-excludes KINDOF_INERT (is_kind_of + leftover_host_template_is_inert). Matches leftover Player::has_any_objects / Team::has_any_objects / host_team_has_any_live_objects and C++ Team::hasAnyObjects. Radiation-field keepalives no longer stall PLAYER_ALL_DESTROYED.

title: [SpecialPower] Location-power unit click skips leftover ActionManager gates
description:
## C++
`CommandTranslator::issueSpecialPowerCommand` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/MessageStream/CommandXlat.cpp:1031-1078`):
- `COMMAND_OPTION_NEED_OBJECT_TARGET` → `MSG_DO_SPECIAL_POWER_AT_OBJECT` after `isValidObjectTarget`.
- `NEED_TARGET_POS` → always `MSG_DO_SPECIAL_POWER_AT_LOCATION` (unit under the cursor is only the optional "object in way" id; the command is still at-location).
- else → `MSG_DO_SPECIAL_POWER`.

`CommandButton::isValidToUseOn` (`ControlBar.cpp:640-648`) for `NEED_TARGET_POS` calls `ActionManager::canDoSpecialPowerAtLocation` (using the target object's position if no explicit loc). `canDoSpecialPowerAtObject` (`ActionManager.cpp:1558-1816`) returns FALSE for location-only powers (DaisyCutter / A10 / Frenzy / Paradrop / CrateDrop / PUC / Spectre / Artillery / Nuke / Ambush / Leaflet / GPS / Repair / Sneak / Cleanup / …). `canDoSpecialPowerAtLocation` (`ActionManager.cpp:1439-1523`) refuses paradrop/crate-drop underwater and ~30 damaging powers on `CELLSHROUD_SHROUDED`.

## Leftover (right)
`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/action_manager.rs` `can_do_special_power_at_object` (622-772) matches C++: location-only types return false (`:721-765`). `special_power_at_location_ok` (`:117-214`) matches C++ underwater + shroud. `can_do_special_power_at_location_for_player` is the live Location helper.

## Live (wrong)
`command_system/system_impl.rs:250-256` `CommandMode::SpecialPower` converts any `context.target_object` into `PowerTarget::Object` — it never consults leftover/C++ `NEED_TARGET_POS` vs `NEED_OBJECT_TARGET`.

`command_executor/special_power.rs` `leftover_can_do_special_power_at_object` (`:88-104`) only implements Battleship (`relationship != ALLIES`) and MD/Howitzer laser (`VEHICLE && ENEMIES`). Everything else is `_ => true`.

`leftover_can_do_special_power_at_location` (`:67-83`) runs only for `PowerTarget::Location` (`:251-270`). A unit-under-cursor click therefore:
1. becomes `PowerTarget::Object`
2. skips leftover location shroud/underwater gates
3. consumes the charge and fires at the object's current position

hq-xvak4 closed the Location-only path. hq-i9iw1 / hq-gufjz / hq-4jxbc are Battleship / Baikonur / MD-laser object gates, not this remaining NEED_TARGET_POS bypass.

## Player-visible
Clicking an enemy (or any unit) in black shroud with A10 / Fuel Air Bomb / nuke / artillery / Frenzy / PUC / Spectre / leaflet / GPS / repair / sneak / ambush still spends the superweapon and fires. Clicking a unit in water with paradrop / crate-drop / tank-paradrop likewise fires. C++/leftover refuse those clicks (or treat them as location clicks that fail the shroud/underwater gate).
close_reason: Live NEED_TARGET_POS unit clicks leftover-gate as AT_LOCATION: leftover special_power_is_location_target_only (canDoSpecialPowerAtObject FALSE types with canDoSpecialPowerAtLocation underwater/shroud/on-map). CommandMode::SpecialPower emits PowerTarget::Location; execute_special_power rewrites leftover Object clicks to Location then leftover can_do_special_power_at_location_for_player. Battleship/laser/Baikonur stay object. Shrouded A10/nuke/paradrop-in-water no longer consume. playable_claim stays false.

description:

title: [Save] Team production priority never persisted
description:
C++ path: TeamTemplateInfo::xfer (Team.cpp:753-762) writes only m_productionPriority. TeamPrototype::xfer (Team.cpp:1197-1198) snapshots that template. Scripts TEAM_INCREASE_PRIORITY / TEAM_DECREASE_PRIORITY (ScriptActions.cpp:2399-2422) and AIPlayer success/failure (Team.cpp:928-935) mutate the runtime value. AI then builds/recruits the wrong team.

title: [ScriptAct] Garrison/Enter/Exit script-action family never reaches the live host
description:
## C++
ScriptActions.cpp issues live AI commands for the whole enter/garrison/exit family: doNamedEnterNamed (1499), doTeamEnterNamed (1523), doNamedExitAll (1544), doTeamExitAll (1564), doTeamGarrisonSpecificBuilding (3291), doExitSpecificBuilding (3327), doTeamGarrisonNearestBuilding (3358, partition-filter nearest garrisonable / internet-center-for-hackers), doTeamExitAllBuildings (3427), doUnitGarrisonSpecificBuilding (3453), doUnitGarrisonNearestBuilding (3489), doUnitExitBuilding (3702), doPlayerGarrisonAllBuildings (3721), doPlayerExitAllBuildings (3735).
