Faithful ports in the executor, all operating on the leftover world: actions_named.rs do_named_enter_named:40, do_named_exit_all:57, do_named_garrison_specific_building:513, do_named_garrison_nearest_building:584, do_named_exit_building; actions_team_relations.rs do_team_enter_named:379, do_team_exit_all:403, do_team_garrison_specific_building:483, do_team_exit_all_buildings:555; actions_garrison.rs do_team_garrison_nearest_building:12; actions_player.rs do_player_garrison_all_buildings:426, do_player_exit_all_buildings:467; actions_skirmish.rs do_exit_specific_building:935. None of them call any request_host_*; executor/mod.rs defines no HostScript*Enter/Garrison/Exit request variant at all.

## Live (wrong)
Main runs the leftover ScriptEngine (engine.update in scripts_camera.rs:4148) and dispatches these actions through the leftover executor, but leftover OBJECT_REGISTRY is empty on the player path (dual_world_registry_unavailable == OBJECT_REGISTRY.is_empty, Wave 249-445 empty-gate residuals), leftover TeamFactory/Player object lists carry no live objects, so every tracker/registry lookup fails and each action silently returns Success. No take_host/apply_host drain exists for any of them (grep of Main for HostScript*(Garrison|Enter|Exit) and apply_host_*(garrison|enter|exit) is empty). Contrast: TEAM_LOAD_TRANSPORTS got request_host_script_load_transports (hq-45m90) and do_named_follow_waypoints in the same file queues request_host_script_follow_waypoints — this family was left out.

## Evidence
Not covered by closed hq-og17 (that added leftover ai/group.rs group_enter/dock/exit/evacuate methods, not the script-action drain), hq-45m90 (load transports), hq-iwgts/hq-2x44y (transport unload placement), or the team entered/exited trigger-condition bead. Title search Garrison/EnterNamed/ExitAll/ExitBuilding/Evacuate shows no bead for this family.

close_reason: Leftover do_named/team/player enter/garrison/exit now request_host_script_garrison_enter when OBJECT_REGISTRY is empty; live apply_host_garrison_enter_exit_script_requests drains into leaveGroup+NORMAL+aiEnter/Evacuate/Exit (nearest-building fill + player garrison/ungarrison). Tests: garrison_enter_exit_queues_round_trip, live_named_enter_and_exit_all_drain_ai_enter_evacuate, live_team_garrison_specific_building_drains_ai_enter.

title: [Physics] Fall-damage threshold drops leftover gravity factor — tosses never splat
description:

## Leftover (right)

## Player-visible
Battle-Bus/shockwave tosses from 40-200 units never splat.
close_reason: Live leftover-parses MinFallHeightForDamage via leftover PhysicsBehaviorModuleData (or height_to_speed with leftover_loco_gravity). Default/compare is leftover ~2.385 not sqrt(80); apply_shock_fall_damage remaps stored g=1 default so 40-200wu tosses splat.

title: [Save] SearchAndDestroy Strategy Center stealth detector never persisted
description:
## C++
`StealthDetectorUpdate::xfer` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/StealthDetectorUpdate.cpp:420-434`) xfers version + UpdateModule base + `m_enabled` (line 432). title: [Save] AI BuildList object binding never persisted
description:
## C++
`BuildListInfo::xfer` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Map/SidesList.cpp:990-1023`) writes `m_objectID`, `m_objectTimestamp`, `m_underConstruction`, gatherer IDs, `m_automaticallyBuild`, and `m_priorityBuild` (v2 also `m_currentGatherers`). `Player::xfer` (`Player.cpp:4124-4176`) snapshots every pad.

`AIPlayer::processBaseBuilding` / `AISkirmishPlayer`:
- `objectID != INVALID_ID` means the pad already owns a live building or scaffold — skip starting a second one; `aiResumeConstruction` continues the same scaffold.
- `objectID == INVALID_ID && timestamp > 0` is the rebuild-delay clock (already filed as hq-05vhe).
- `m_priorityBuild` is the script `BUILD_SPECIFIC_BUILDING` stamp; automatic pads never start via `canMakeUnit(dozer, NULL)`.

After load the AI must still know which pad owns which object, whether that object is mid-construction, and whether a script stamped priority.

## Leftover (right)
`Player::xfer` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/rts/player.rs:4146-4363`) already writes the same table: `object_id`, `object_timestamp`, `under_construction`, gatherers, `automatically_build`, `priority`.

## Live (wrong)
`AIPlayerQueuePersist` AITQ v4 (`Main/src/save_load/snapshot/ai_player_queue_persist.rs`) only stores `building_rebuild_counts` (hq-49v5x) and `building_destroyed_at_times` (hq-05vhe). `AIPlayer::apply_queue_persist` (`Main/src/ai.rs:613-630`) comments explicitly: write remaining spend / rebuild-delay clock only; **do not rebind pad object_id or under-construction**.

`restore_players_from_save` rebuilds `AIPlayer` via `add_ai_player` → `initialize` → `setup_base_layout` (all pads `object_id=None`, `is_built=false`, `is_priority=false`). `retain_queue_object_ids` never touches `building_queue`. `rebind_after_world_reset` / `on_game_loaded` **clears** `object_id` and `is_built`. There is no post-load scan that rebinds pads to restored world objects by template/position.

## Player-visible
1. Mid-construction AI buildings: `resume_interrupted_construction` cannot find the scaffold (`object_id` lost). Underpowered AI then starts a **second** power plant because `power_under_construction` is only detected via `building.object_id`.
2. Already-built pads: `select_priority_or_power_build` sees `object_id=None` and `is_built=false`. Automatic pads still skip, but power pads (`automatic_build || is_under_powered`) and any `is_priority` stamp start **duplicate** construction next to the restored building.
3. Scripted `BUILD_SPECIFIC_BUILDING` stamps (`is_priority`) are not in AITQ, so after load the AI forgets the requested pad.

hq-49v5x / hq-05vhe closed only remaining rebuilds and the delay clock. hq-05vhe close reason: "restore writes that clock only (not object_id/under_construction)".
close_reason: AITQ v5 persists BuildList object_id, is_built, and is_priority; apply_queue_persist rebinds pads after layout rebuild; retain drops stale IDs

title: [Physics] Live Y Euler applies leftover lift without leftover gravity
description:
## C++
`PhysicsUpdate.cpp:626-630` always `applyGravitationalForces` unless `DISABLED_HELD`. `Locomotor::calcLiftToUseAtPt` (`Locomotor.cpp:2022-2110`) returns `desiredAccel - gravity` so lift + gravity nets the desired climb/hold.

## Leftover (right)
`physics_update.rs:839-840` always `apply_gravity` unless HELD. `locomotor/core_impl` `calc_lift_to_use_at_pt` subtracts leftover gravity the same way.

## Live (wrong)
Two host Y-up paths break the pairing:
1. `world_tick/physics.rs:1001-1008` `apply_live_handle_behavior_z` does `vel.y += lift_a; pos.y += vel.y` and never adds leftover gravity. At preferred height leftover lift is `-gravity` (~+0.0711/frame), so hover/wings climb instead of holding.
2. `object/physics_motion.rs:776-786` `tick_physics_motion_step` skips `apply_gravitational_forces` *and* the `physics_accel.y` integrate for `flying_loco_aircraft` (airborne_target aircraft that are not falling/shocked). C++ has no aircraft exception.

Player-visible: helicopters/jets drift up while hovering or circling; aircraft that lose lift do not fall.

## Evidence
Not a rehash of closed `hq-8vhks` (no gravity at all) — gravity was added, then flying was excepted and the leftover lift integrate still omits gravity. Deduped all beads including closed; no flying-skip / lift-without-gravity issue remains open.
close_reason: apply_live_handle_behavior_z now applyGravitationalForces + integrate lift so leftover calcLiftToUseAtPt (desired-gravity) holds hover. tick_physics_motion_step applies gravity for dead/disabled/non-Z-motive aircraft (C++ has no flying skip); living Z-motive already Euler'd lift+gravity on the host march path.

title: [Locomotor] Live blockedBy drops leftover near-goal, path-priority, and reverse skip
description:
## C++
`AIUpdate.cpp:1272-1376` `blockedBy`:
- within one pathfind cell of the goal cell → not blocked
- `isMovingBackwards` → not blocked
- stacked in the same cell → `hasHigherPathPriority` (dozer > vehicle > infantry, then heading, then lower ObjectId)
- off-angle closing pair → higher-priority unit yields (`hasHigherPathPriority` → FALSE)

title: [Dozer] Idle never resumes a parked REPAIR task
description:
## C++
`DozerPrimaryStateMachine` idleConditions (`DozerAIUpdate.cpp:1258-1281`) are `isBuildMostImportant` → BUILD, `isRepairMostImportant` → REPAIR, `isFortifyMostImportant` → FORTIFY. `isRepairMostImportant` (`:1326-1350`) is AI idle && `getMostRecentCommand()==REPAIR`. `newTask` (`:1955-1963`) cancels only a pending task of the *same* type, so a BUILD while Repairing (or REPAIR while Building) parks the other slot. When the dozer goes idle, the primary machine immediately resumes the most-recent pending task of either kind.

## Leftover (right)
`dozer_ai_update.rs:1046-1085` `update()`: when `dozer_task` is none and `current_task==Invalid`, `current_task = get_most_recent_command()` (Build/Repair/Fortify by order_frame), then `spawn_dozer_task_from_current()` resumes that slot.

## Live (wrong)
`command_executor/leftover.rs:1582-1622` `dozer_idle_resume_pending_build` tracks both slots via `dozer_most_recent_pending_task`, then `if is_repair { return false; }` — only BUILD ever resumes from idle. A parked REPAIR (BUILD interrupting Repair, or a failed approach leaving Idle) is pruned-but-never-resumed. The only re-acquire is `update_dozer_bored_repair` after 150 frames, which picks the nearest damaged same-player structure, not the parked player-ordered target.

## Evidence
C++: `isRepairMostImportant` → `DOZER_PRIMARY_REPAIR`.
Leftover: `get_most_recent_command()` includes Repair.
Live: `if is_repair { return false; }`.

Not a refile of closed hq-ylhfz (same-frame BUILD+REPAIR *tie* while both active) or hq-vmy49 (repair mid-build abandoning the scaffold).
close_reason: Idle isRepairMostImportant now resumes parked REPAIR via dozer_idle_resume_pending_build

title: [Dozer] Complete END dock uses current pose not stored ACTION
description:
## C++
`DozerAIUpdate::newTask` (`DozerAIUpdate.cpp:1990-1998`) stores `m_dockPoint[task][END] = ACTION + normalize(ACTION − target) * 5 * PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE_F` at order time. On construction complete (`:627-635`) the dozer `adjustToPossibleDestination` + `aiMoveToPosition` that stored END (fallback current pos only if END missing).

## Leftover (right)
`dozer_ai_update.rs:640-681` `new_task` stores End as ACTION + normalized (ACTION − target) * 5 cells. `handle_build_completion` (`:1034-1041`) moves via `get_dock_point(current_task, DozerDockPoint::End)`.

## Live (wrong)
`dozer_new_task_build` (`command_executor/leftover.rs:1458-1461`) stores only `dozer_dock_action` (ACTION). No END field. `world_tick/production.rs:289-300` completion release calls `dozer_end_dock_position(dozer_pos, bpos)` seeded from the dozer's *current* position (up to `DOZER_MIN_ACTION_TOLERANCE` 70wu off ACTION, and a different axis if the dozer is not on the dock→building line).

## Evidence
C++/leftover: END computed once at newTask from ACTION dock.
Live helper `dozer_end_dock_position` is the right formula but is fed `dozer_pos` not stored ACTION.

Not a refile of closed hq-evalv (that added the back-off move; seed is still current pose, not stored ACTION).
close_reason: Complete END dock seeds dozer_end_dock_position from stored ACTION, fallback current pose

title: [Dozer] Construction rate ignores Handicap BUILDTIME
description:
## C++
`DozerAIUpdate` BUILD (`DozerAIUpdate.cpp:515-518`) sets `framesToBuild = goalObject->getTemplate()->calcTimeToBuild(player)`. `ThingTemplate::calcTimeToBuild` (`ThingTemplate.cpp:1524-1527`) multiplies authored frames by `player->getHandicap()->getHandicap(Handicap::BUILDTIME, this)` (BUILDINGS vs GENERIC) before PlayerTemplate ProductionTimeChange and energy.

## Live (wrong)
`world_tick/production.rs:31-42` authored construction frames use only `player_template_production_time_factor` (ProductionTimeChange). `effective_rate` then applies power. `handicap_build_time_multiplier` exists on Player (`player.rs:1493-1499`) and is used by `modified_build_time_seconds` for the factory *queue* (`drones_and_garrison.rs:2509-2527`), never for dozer/worker pad construction.

## Evidence

Not a refile of closed hq-hvo7u (that closed production-queue `modified_build_time_seconds`; dozer construction never calls it).

title: [LookAt] KEY/SCREENEDGE scroll never mouse-locks
description:
## C++
`LookAtXlat.cpp` `LookAtTranslator::setScrolling` (lines 50-62) is the single entry for all three exclusive scroll types — `SCROLL_KEY` (RAW_KEY, line 187), `SCROLL_RMB` (RMB down, line 206), `SCROLL_SCREENEDGE` (RAW_MOUSE_POSITION edge band, line 290). Every call does `TheInGameUI->setScrolling(TRUE)` + `TheTacticalView->setMouseLock(TRUE)`.

`WindowXlat.cpp:147-172` (Kris Aug-15-2003): while the view is mouse-locked, KEEP every raw message except LMB down/up when `TheInGameUI->isScrolling()`. During keyboard or screen-edge panning, hover/RMB/MMB never reach the window manager and cannot issue orders through the control bar.

## Leftover (right)
`GameClient/src/message_stream/look_at_xlat.rs` `LookAtTranslator::set_scrolling()` — one shared path from Key, Rmb, and ScreenEdge arms. Every type does `TheInGameUI::set_scrolling(true)` + `view.set_mouse_lock(true)`; `stop_scrolling` reverses both (unit test `set_scrolling_locks_mouse_and_stop_restores_prev_cursor`).

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/cnc_game_engine/mouse.rs` `start_rmb_lookat_scroll` is the only place that sets `modes.mouse_locked = true` and `TheInGameUI::set_scrolling(true)`. `update_camera` resolves Key/ScreenEdge via `lookat_resolve_scroll_type` and stores `scroll_type`, but never engages the lock.

`input.rs:400-410` gates WindowXlat-equivalent dispatch on `look_at_host_mouse_locked()`. During arrow-key or edge scroll that flag is false, so hover and RMB/MMB still hit HUD gadgets. C++/leftover keep the window manager suppressed (only LMB passes).

## Evidence
- C++ `LookAtXlat.cpp:50-62,187,206,290` + `WindowXlat.cpp:147-172`
- Leftover `look_at_xlat.rs` `set_scrolling` / `stop_scrolling`
- Live `mouse.rs` `start_rmb_lookat_scroll` (~3966) vs `update_camera` Key/ScreenEdge match (~2247)
- Live `input.rs:403` `look_at_host_mouse_locked()`
- Not a duplicate of closed hq-18sa5 (RMB-only lock), hq-z0n13 (LMB passthrough when already locked), hq-jx12i (setScrolling breaks camera lock)

## Dedup
`bd list --status=all --limit 0 --json`. Closed related: hq-18sa5, hq-z0n13, hq-jx12i, hq-oicfh, hq-m7n9. No open [LookAt]/[Cam] mouse-lock bead for KEY/SCREENEDGE.
close_reason: Live KEY/SCREENEDGE scroll now mouse-locks via shared set_lookat_scroll_mouse_lock (LookAtXlat.cpp:50-76). WindowXlat hover/RMB/MMB stay off HUD; LMB still passes while scrolling.

title: [Locomotor] Wheeled SMALL_TURN recaps speed after approach-brake
description:
## C++
`moveTowardsPositionWheels` (`Locomotor.cpp:1316-1323`) caps `desiredSpeed` to `turnSpeed` when `|relAngle| > PI/20` **before** the approach-brake block (`:1393-1430`).
Once `IS_BRAKING` is latched, `goalSpeed` is overwritten with `actualSpeed-braking` / `-braking/2` / `actualSpeed` and is **not** re-clamped by `turnSpeed`. Treads analog `:1194-1221`. The 15° look-ahead probe (`:1340-1389`) also uses the pre-brake `goalSpeed`.

## Leftover (right)
`move_towards_position_wheels_physics` (`core_impl/move_ground.rs:176-180`) applies the SMALL_TURN cap on `desired_speed` first, then latches/unlatches/donut/curve (`:222-270`). Matches C++ order.

## Live (wrong)
`update_movement` first calls `apply_cpp_approach_brake` (`world_tick/movement.rs:717-723`), which returns the braking goal-speed when latched (`object/physics_motion.rs:1334-1350`), **then** recaps:
```
if delta.abs() > PI/20.0 && speed > turn_speed { speed = turn_speed; }
```
(`movement.rs:769-772`). A braking wheeled/motorcycle unit with >9° heading correction is forced to `maxSpeed/4` instead of `actualSpeed-braking`. The 15° look-ahead (`:793-800`) also sees that post-brake recap.

## Evidence
Truck/Humvee/motorcycle arriving at a waypoint while still turning >9° over-brakes vs C++ and tightens the donut.
close_reason: Wheeled SMALL_TURN now caps desiredSpeed before apply_cpp_approach_brake; IS_BRAKING overwrite is not recapped. 15° look-ahead sees pre-brake speed.

title: [Locomotor] Wings idle maintain Z uses own altitude not terrain
description:
## C++
`Locomotor::locoUpdate_maintainCurrentPosition` (`Locomotor.cpp:2412-2477`) runs appearance maintain then **one** `handleBehaviorZ(obj, physics, m_maintainPos)`.
`maintainCurrentPositionWings` (`:2488-2524`) is 2D circling only.
`handleBehaviorZ` `Z_SURFACE_RELATIVE_HEIGHT` (`:2288-2316`) takes `surfaceHt = getSurfaceHtAtPt(pos.x, pos.y)` (real terrain/water), damps PreferredHeight, then `calcLiftToUseAtPt`. Idle jets hold PreferredHeight above the ground.

## Leftover (right)
`maintain_current_position_wings` is 2D circle only (`core_impl/maintain.rs:216-260`).
`lift_relative_to_layer` uses `get_surface_ht_at_pt` (`behavior_z.rs:151-172`).
`move_dispatch.rs` calls `handle_behavior_z_for` once per frame with that real surface.

## Live (wrong)
Idle Wings: `update_movement` calls `apply_live_handle_behavior_z(obj, surface_y)` (correct terrain) then `loco_maintain_current_position` (`world_tick/movement.rs:970-978`).
Wings early-returns into `maintain_position_wings` (`object/physics.rs:682-685`), which then:
```
let gy = p.y;
let _ = self.handle_behavior_z(gy, Some(maintain.y));
```
(`object/physics.rs:1392-1393`). `handle_behavior_z(SurfaceRelative)` treats `gy` as the surface, so `preferred = PreferredHeight + own_y` every frame — unbounded climb bias. C++/leftover lift off real terrain.

## Evidence
Circling jet with PreferredHeight>0 holding last waypoint climbs instead of riding terrain/water.
close_reason: maintain_position_wings is 2D only. Idle/zero-delta Wings circle then apply_live_handle_behavior_z with leftover getSurfaceHtAtPt, not own altitude.

title: [Production] Live parachute land skips UseSpawnRallyPoint
description:
## C++
`ParachuteContain::onRemoving` (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Contain/ParachuteContain.cpp:493-516): after a non-skirmish rider is released, resolve `rider->getProducerID()` (the chute) then `transport->getProducerID()` (the producing building). If that building's `ExitInterface->useSpawnRallyPoint()` is true, call `exitObjectViaDoor(rider, DOOR_1)` so the rider runs DefaultProductionExitUpdate (UnitCreatePoint + 2-cell natural rally + custom rally). Otherwise `aiIdle`. Flag authored on DefaultProductionExitUpdate (`UseSpawnRallyPoint`).

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/object/contain/parachute_contain.rs:528-568` implements the same chain: skirmish → `ai_hunt`; else producer→transport→building `get_object_exit_interface()`; if `use_spawn_rally_point()` → `exit_object_via_door(rider, Primary)`; else `ai_idle`. `default_production_exit_behavior.rs` parses and exposes the INI flag.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/saboteur_car_bomb.rs:791-806` `apply_parachute_land_ai` only does skirmish → `unit_command_patrol`. Non-skirmish riders get no idle and never consult `ProductionExitMetadata.use_spawn_rally_point` (parsed in `thing.rs:652` / `spawn_templates.rs:2186` but unused on the land path). An airdropped rider from a UseSpawnRallyPoint=Yes producer idles at the LZ instead of walking the factory exit/rally.

## Evidence
C++: `if (exitInterface && exitInterface->useSpawnRallyPoint()) { exitInterface->exitObjectViaDoor(rider, DOOR_1); }`
Leftover: `if exit_guard.use_spawn_rally_point() { exit_guard.exit_object_via_door(...) }`
Live: no `use_spawn_rally_point` consumer under Main except parse + tests.

Not a refile of closed hq-14d7 (that was leftover ungated exit; leftover is now gated correctly).
close_reason: Live apply_parachute_land_ai now 2-hops rider.producer (chute) → chute.producer (building); UseSpawnRallyPoint runs DefaultProductionExit UnitCreatePoint+2-cell natural+custom rally, else aiIdle. put_hijacker_in_airborne_parachute stamps the producer chain.

title: [Select] Live pick drops ALWAYS_SELECTABLE dead objects

`PickDrawableStruct` (`SelectionInfo.cpp:56-59`) also adds `KINDOF_ALWAYS_SELECTABLE` to pick kinds when not force-attacking, so those drawables enter the pick list.
Hover (`SelectionXlat.cpp:434`) posts `MSG_MOUSEOVER_DRAWABLE_HINT` when `!isEffectivelyDead() || isKindOf(KINDOF_ALWAYS_SELECTABLE)`.

## Leftover (right)
`SelectableDrawable::can_select` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/message_stream/selection_xlat.rs:121-124`) matches C++: `if self.is_dead && !self.has_kindof(KINDOF_ALWAYS_SELECTABLE) { return false; }`.
Catalog packing (`:218-219`, `:527-528`) writes AlwaysSelectable into the UI-local kind cache so dead AlwaysSelectable units stay `can_select(false)`.

## Live (wrong)
`UnitControlSystem::presentation_is_selectable` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/unit_control.rs:323-331`) requires `!o.destroyed` with no AlwaysSelectable override, plus Selectable kind / !sold / !unselectable / !masked / not contained.
`pick_object_id_at_world_from_presentation` (`unit_control.rs:373-375`) independently `return None` on `o.destroyed`.
`pick_ray.rs` uses `presentation_is_selectable`.
`CnCGameEngine::is_point_selectable_click_target` / `is_locally_selectable_click_target` (`cnc_game_engine/mouse.rs:1199-1218`) both call `presentation_is_selectable`.
`host_context_pick_profile` (`cnc_game_engine/selection.rs:31-50`) never adds ALWAYS_SELECTABLE (C++ PickDrawableStruct does when !forceAttack).
`presentation_is_squad_live` (`presentation_frame/alive.rs:225-227`) already early-returns AlwaysSelectable — control-group recall only. Click/hover/box pick do not.

Not a refile of closed hq-6kbbu: that bead added KindOf::AlwaysSelectable and fixed `Object::is_selectable`. Live click never consults `Object::is_selectable`.

## Player-visible
Dead UI-feedback / ALWAYS_SELECTABLE rubble cannot be clicked or mouseovered on the live host. Retail and leftover CanSelectDrawable keep them selectable.
close_reason: Live pick keeps ALWAYS_SELECTABLE dead objects: presentation_is_selectable + pick_ray skip + packed always_selectable bool (32-bit KindOf bank full). C++ CanSelectDrawable SelectionXlat.cpp:113 / Object.cpp:3011.

title: [Weapon] Live waypoint-follow slot ignores leftover CapableOfFollowingWaypoints
description:

WeaponSet::findWaypointFollowingCapableWeapon (WeaponSet.cpp:998-1008) walks TERTIARY..PRIMARY and returns the first weapon whose Weapon::isCapableOfFollowingWaypoint() is true. That flag is WeaponTemplate::m_capableOfFollowingWaypoint from Weapon.ini `CapableOfFollowingWaypoints`. Script NAMED_FIRE_WEAPON_FOLLOWING_WAYPOINT_PATH and attack-path fire use that slot. Name substrings are never consulted.

title: [Radar] GLA Command Center invents radar without Radar Van
description:
## C++
Radar is granted only by RadarUpgrade::upgradeImplementation (RadarUpgrade.cpp:104-119) calling Player::addRadar. America CC uses GrantUpgradeCreate Upgrade_AmericaRadar + RadarUpgrade. China CC uses RadarUpgrade TriggeredBy Upgrade_ChinaRadar. GLA radar is GLAVehicleRadarVan GrantUpgradeCreate Upgrade_GLARadar + RadarUpgrade DisableProof. GLACommandCenter has no RadarUpgrade, so a GLA player with only a Command Center has no radar.

## Leftover
GameLogic/src/object/upgrade/radar_upgrade.rs apply_radar_upgrade and GameLogic/src/upgrade/modules/radar.rs upgrade_implementation only add_radar when the RadarUpgrade module is present and applied. ThingFactory/INI attach RadarUpgrade to America/China CC and Radar Van, not GLACommandCenter.

## Live
host_radar.rs:167-173 is_radar_command_center_template returns true for any name containing "commandcenter" or "headquarters", including GLA_CommandCenter / GLACommandCenter. Honesty tests (host_radar.rs:280, 332) assert GLA_CommandCenter is a provider. update_player_radar then sets that player's radar_count from the CC alone, so GLA gets a minimap without a Radar Van.

## Evidence
Retail GLA starts with a Command Center and no radar until a Radar Van is built. Live turns radar on as soon as the GLA CC finishes.
close_reason: Live is_radar_command_center_template no longer matches GLA*CommandCenter. Leftover/INI attach RadarUpgrade only to America/China CC and Radar Van; GLA radar is the van. Honesty + scan + radar-extend now fail-closed for GLA CC.

title: [Radar] EMP/hacked CC still grants radar — live skips Object::onDisabledEdge
description:
## C++
Object::onDisabledEdge (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Object.cpp:3790-3819) walks applied RadarUpgrade modules. On becoming disabled (EMP / HELD / hacked / paralyzed) it calls controller->removeRadar(radarMod->getIsDisableProof()); on re-enable it addRadar. Disable-proof only keeps radar through player brownout (Player::hasRadar + m_disableProofRadarCount). EMP on the van itself still removeRadar(true).

## Leftover
GameLogic/src/object/object_upgrade.rs:278-319 on_disabled_edge matches C++: if an applied RadarUpgrade exists, remove_radar/add_radar(disable_proof). RadarUpgrade::on_delete skips when already disabled so the edge does not double-count.

## Live
Main/src/game_logic/object/install.rs:828-835 on_disabled_edge is a no-op (only comments Overcharge). update_player_radar (world_objects/crates_radar_power.rs:867-911) rebuilds radar_count from is_legal_radar_provider (host_radar.rs:191-207), which only checks alive + constructed + template name — not is_disabled(). An EMP'd America/China CC (or EMP'd Radar Van) still increments radar_count / disable_proof_radar_count, so the minimap stays online.

## Evidence
Lotus/Hacker disable or EMP pulse on the only Command Center must take radar offline until the disable expires. Live keeps it up.
close_reason: Live Object::on_disabled_edge now walks leftover RadarUpgrade (object_upgrade.rs:278-319) and records removeRadar/addRadar. update_player_radar applies those edges then skips is_disabled providers so EMP/hacked CC/van drop radar; disable-proof still only covers player brownout.

title: [Transport] Airborne unload invents KeepContainerVelocityOnExit kick
description:
## C++
`TransportContain::onRemoving` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Contain/TransportContain.cpp:334-350`) copies parent velocity×mass as motive force and applies `ExitPitchRate` **only** when INI `KeepContainerVelocityOnExit` is Yes. Default is FALSE (`TransportContain.cpp: ctor / leftover default`). Independently, `isAboveTerrain()` (`:372-380`) only `setAllowToFall(true)` so the rider can drop; it does not inherit hull cruise speed.

No retail Object INI authors `KeepContainerVelocityOnExit` (grep of the token hits only C++/Rust parsers). Chinook/Helix evacuate therefore drops infantry without a hull-velocity kick.

## Leftover (right)
`transport_contain.rs:737-751` `on_removing` gates the motive-force + `exit_pitch_rate` copy on `self.module_data.keep_container_velocity_on_exit` (default false, parsed from INI). Airborne only sets `set_allow_to_fall(true)` (`:753-756`). Matches C++.

## Live (wrong)
`walk_unit_via_open_contain_exit` (`Main/src/game_logic/world_combat/drones_and_garrison.rs:1597-1602`) whenever `container.is_above_terrain_for_exit()`:
- `unit.allow_to_fall = true` (correct C++ airborne arm)
- **and** `unit.apply_motive_force(hull_vel * mass)` (invented; comment mislabels this as KeepContainerVelocityOnExit)

Live never parses `KeepContainerVelocityOnExit` (`host_env_contain_residual.rs:487-488` is an honesty constant only). Every flying Chinook/Helix Evacuate/Exit therefore slings riders at hull cruise velocity. C++/leftover drop them.

Not hq-a87k (leftover crate used to drop the flag entirely; leftover is now right). Not hq-pj6v9 (ExitStart/End walk).

## Player-visible
Infantry dumped from a flying Combat Chinook/Helix inherit the aircraft's cruise velocity and shoot forward instead of falling at the door.
close_reason: Live walk_unit_via_open_contain_exit no longer invents a hull-velocity kick on airborne unload. KeepContainerVelocityOnExit is stored/parsed (default false); motive force applies only when authored. Airborne independently setAllowToFall.

title: [Team] inherit uses faction proto not named team attitude
description:
C++ path + behavior: Object.cpp:439-448 on create and Object.cpp:857-872 on setTeam. `ai->setAttitude(getTeam()->getPrototype()->getTemplateInfo()->m_initialTeamAttitude)`. The prototype is the object's actual Team instance prototype (map team `AmericaTeamRangers`, default `teamAmerica`, etc.), not the faction enum.

Leftover path + behavior: GameLogic/src/object/object_lifecycle.rs:734-766 `apply_team_ai_profile` reads `self.get_team().get_name()` and `TeamFactory::find_team_prototype(name)`, then `ai.set_attitude` from that prototype's `initial_team_attitude`. Matches C++.

Live path + behavior: Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/teams.rs:491-530 `inherit_team_ai_defaults` maps `Team::USA/China/GLA` to the strings `"USA"`/`"China"`/`"GLA"` and looks up that prototype. Map/script teams are never named `"USA"`. `find_team_prototype("USA")` is typically None so inherit returns without applying attitude. Even when a faction proto exists, Sleep/Aggressive script teams stay Normal. `Object::set_team` / `set_team_and_owner` (visual.rs:49-87) never call inherit at all, so capture/defect also skip C++ setTeam attitude.

Evidence: create_destroy_die.rs:2213-2214 calls inherit after spawn; team_instance_name is already set (create_destroy_die.rs:1193-1195) but unused. Mood matrix Sleep blocks Hunt/Guard/AttackMove; Aggressive converts Move to AttackMove. Scripted teams with teamAggressiveness never get that mood on the live host.

Not a duplicate of hq-7077n (TEAM_SET_ATTITUDE script drain, now closed) or hq-cgb7 (leftover-only missing attack-priority on apply_team_ai_profile).
close_reason: Live inherit_team_ai_defaults looks up team_instance_name (fallback default_host_team_instance_name), never faction USA/America/China/GLA. set_team/set_team_and_owner and merge setTeam apply named proto attitude like leftover apply_team_ai_profile / C++ Object::setTeam.

title: [Save] AI BuildList rebuild-delay timestamp never persisted
description:
## C++
`BuildListInfo::xfer` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Map/SidesList.cpp:990-1023`) writes `m_objectID`, `m_objectTimestamp`, and `m_underConstruction` with the rest of the pad. `Player::xfer` (`Player.cpp:4124-4176`) snapshots every pad.

`AIPlayer::processBaseBuilding` (`AIPlayer.cpp:750-758`) and `AISkirmishPlayer` (`AISkirmishPlayer.cpp:163-176`): when `objectID==INVALID_ID && timestamp>0`, skip rebuild until `timestamp + RebuildDelayTimeSeconds*LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND` (retail 30s). Mid-build pads keep `objectID` so the same scaffold is resumed (`aiResumeConstruction`).

## Leftover (right)
`Player::xfer` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/rts/player.rs:4212-4220`) already writes `object_id`, `timestamp`, and `under_construction`. Leftover `AIPlayer` / `AISkirmishPlayer` (`ai_player/impl_economy.rs:628-638`, `skirmish_player.rs:868-876`) apply the same timestamp delay gate.

## Live (wrong)
`AIBuildingInfo.destroyed_at_time` (`Main/src/ai.rs:265-290`) is the host residual of `m_objectTimestamp`. `process_building_queue` / `sync_build_list_object_status` stamp it on destroy/capture and `rebuild_delay_elapsed` waits `REBUILD_DELAY_SECONDS` (30). `object_id` is the pad→scaffold link.

AITQ v3 (`ai_player_queue_persist.rs` / `capture_queue_persist`) only writes `building_rebuild_counts` (hq-49v5x). It never captures `destroyed_at_time`, `object_id`, or `is_built`/`under_construction`. `rebind_after_world_reset` / `on_game_loaded` (`ai.rs:6718-6764`) then force `object_id=None` and `is_built=false`. Restore therefore always sees `destroyed_at_time=None` → delay elapsed.

## Player-visible
Save after an AI factory/barracks dies: C++ waits 30s before rebuilding. Live starts the rebuild on the first post-load AI tick.

Save mid-construction: C++ keeps the pad bound to the scaffold. Live forgets the link and can queue a second building on the same pad.

## Evidence
C++ `SidesList.cpp:1014-1016` + `AIPlayer.cpp:750-758`. Leftover `player.rs:4212-4220`. Live AITQ `building_rebuild_counts` only; `destroyed_at_time` has zero save_load hits.
close_reason: AITQ v4 persists leftover BuildListInfo.object_timestamp as AIBuildingInfo.destroyed_at_time; restore writes that clock only (not object_id/under_construction). v1-v3 suffixes leave timestamps empty.

title: [Contain] Human Enter never rejects fogged containers
description:
## C++
`ActionManager::canEnterObject` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/RTS/ActionManager.cpp:519-521`) calls `isObjectShroudedForAction` (`:76-102`). After the old `return false` disable was commented out, a human player (`PLAYER_HUMAN`) whose impetus is not `CMD_FROM_SCRIPT` cannot Enter a target whose `getShroudedStatus` is `OBJECTSHROUD_FOGGED` or worse. Applies to garrison, transport, heal, tunnel, and other contain Enter.

## Leftover (right)
`TheActionManager::can_enter_object` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/action_manager.rs:1126-1128`) uses `is_object_shrouded_for_action` (`:42-61`): human player, not `FromScript`, `get_shrouded_status >= Fogged` → reject. Matches C++.

## Live (wrong)
`GameLogic::can_unit_enter_normal_target` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/object_queries.rs:957-1114`) is the host Enter authority used by `command_executor/transport.rs` and `command_executor/validate.rs`. It has no shroud/fog gate. A human Enter on a fogged garrison/transport/heal/tunnel therefore succeeds if other gates pass. Wave 1064 only fail-closes presentation `selection_can_enter_target` (`playable_claim` stays false); host authority still accepts the command.

## Evidence
C++ `isObjectShroudedForAction` enabled (commented `return false` plus commandSource). Leftover ports the same three predicates. Live host Enter never reads object FOW.
close_reason: Live can_unit_enter_normal_target now applies leftover/C++ isObjectShroudedForAction: human player, not FromScript, host shroud >= Fogged rejects garrison/transport/heal/tunnel Enter. Uninitialized shroud and computer players fail-open.

title: [Weapon] Projectileless fire skips leftover delayed damage
description:
## C++
`WeaponTemplate::fireWeaponTemplate` (`Weapon.cpp:998-1075`): when `getProjectileTemplate()==NULL` (and not a projectile detonation), travel time is `v.length() / getWeaponSpeed()`. Lasers still `createLaser` + same-frame `dealDamageInternal`. Non-laser: if `delayInFrames < 1.0` apply `dealDamageInternal` immediately; else `TheWeaponStore->setDelayedDamage` (`Weapon.cpp:1646-1655`) and `WeaponStore::update` (`Weapon.cpp:1589-1598`) later calls `dealDamageInternal` at the stored pos. No flying object, so nothing can collide on the way.

## Leftover (right)
`Weapon::private_fire_weapon` (`weapon_instance.rs:1602-1612`) + `handle_projectileless_flight_damage` (`weapon_instance_combat.rs:38-96`) match: empty `projectile_name` queues `WeaponStore::set_delayed_damage` when `ceil(distance/speed) >= 1`, else `deal_damage_internal` now. `WeaponStore::update` / `process_delayed_damage` (`store.rs:131-148`, `:428-456`) apply the queued shot. Live `world_tick/step.rs:1171-1172` already calls leftover `store.update()`.

## Live (wrong)
`Object::fire_at_ex` (`object/attack.rs:362-421`) always `queue_projectile`. `drain_pending_projectiles` (`combat.rs:1007-1229`) always `fire_projectile_ex` even when `projectile_object_name` is empty. Main has no `set_delayed_damage` caller, so leftover `m_weaponDDI` stays empty. Projectileless finite-speed weapons become dummy CombatSystem projectiles that can collide mid-flight and never use leftover delayed damage.

## Evidence
C++ `Weapon.cpp:998-1075`, `:1589-1598`, `:1646-1655`. Leftover `weapon_instance.rs:1602-1612`, `weapon_instance_combat.rs:38-96`, `store.rs:131-148`. Live `object/attack.rs:362-421`, `combat.rs:1186-1227`, `world_tick/step.rs:1171-1172`. Deduped closed list (no projectileless / setDelayedDamage / delayed-damage bead).
close_reason: Live projectileless fire calls leftover setDelayedDamage; no dummy CombatSystem projectile. Live apply at drain and Phase 14.

title: [Save] AI BuildList remaining rebuilds never persisted
description:
## C++
`Player::xfer` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/RTS/Player.cpp:4124-4176`) snapshots every `BuildListInfo` including remaining `m_numRebuilds`, `m_objectID`, `m_underConstruction`, gatherer IDs, and timestamp. `AIPlayer::processBaseBuilding` / `BuildListInfo::decrementNumRebuilds` spend that remaining count; after load the AI cannot rebuild a pad more times than were left at save.

title: [AssaultTransport] Wounded retrieve and healthy eject teleport
description:
## C++
`AssaultTransportAIUpdate::update` (`AssaultTransportAIUpdate.cpp:260-276`) when a designated target is alive:
- healthy contained members that are not `m_newMember` get `ai->aiExit(transport, CMD_FROM_AI)` so they walk ExitStart/End and fight
- wounded uncontained members get `ai->aiEnter(transport, CMD_FROM_AI)` so they walk back aboard to heal

`retrieveMembers` (`:417-435`) orders every uncontained member `aiEnter` (skip if already `AI_ENTER`). Troop Crawler assault never teleports infantry.

## Leftover (right)
`assault_transport_ai_update.rs` `update` (`:411-428`) issues `AiCommandType::Exit` for healthy contained non-new members and `ai_enter` for wounded uncontained members. `retrieve_members` (`:643-667`) issues `ai_enter` unless already Enter. Matches C++.

## Live
`tick_assault_transport_updates` (`world_tick/crates.rs:1041-1071`):
- healthy eject: `remove_occupant` + `set_position(crawler_pos + (6,0,0))` then `apply_engagement_decision_aware` — no ExitStart/End walk
- wounded retrieve: `add_occupant` + `set_contained_by` + `set_position(crawler_pos)` — instant board

`assault_transport_retrieve_members` (`:1238-1272`) same teleport board (add_occupant + snap to hull). `host_troop_crawler.rs` documents this as "instant enter/exit, no path AI".

## Evidence
C++ `:266` aiExit, `:275` aiEnter, `:431` retrieveMembers aiEnter.
Leftover `:411-428`, `:658-664`.
Live `:1041-1071`, `:1260-1270`.
Closed hq-tk45t / hq-6u2ps / hq-jilpa cover retrieve-on-target-death, giveFinalOrders, and new-member eject, not walk vs teleport. hq-pj6v9 is generic transport Unload/Evacuate, not AssaultTransportAIUpdate.

## Player-visible
During a Troop Crawler assault, wounded Red Guards vanish into the hull and healthy ones pop 6wu out instead of walking ExitStart/End / walking back to board. Retail infantry peel off and return on foot.
close_reason: Live AssaultTransportAIUpdate now issues aiExit ExitStart/End walk for healthy contained members and aiEnter walk for wounded/retrieveMembers; no hull teleport.

title: [Save] Player preorder flag never persisted
description:
## C++
`Player::xfer` v7 (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/RTS/Player.cpp:3993-3997`) writes `m_isPreorder`. ## Leftover (right)

## Live (wrong)
Live `Player.did_preorder` (`game_logic/game_logic/player.rs`) drives `host_preorder_create` / `create_destroy_die.rs` MODELCONDITION_PREORDER. `PlayerRuntimePersist` has no preorder field. `snapshot/restore.rs` constructs every restored player with `did_preorder: false`. `apply_player_to_leftover` never calls leftover `set_preorder`. title: [Save] Team script state never persisted
description:
## C++
`Team::xfer` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/RTS/Team.cpp:2612-2613`) writes `m_state` as an AsciiString after the member-id list. `ScriptActions::doSetTeamState` sets that string; `ScriptConditions::evaluateTeamStateIs` / `evaluateTeamStateIsNot` compare it. Campaign maps use TEAM_SET_STATE then later TEAM_STATE_IS to gate waves, retreats, and objectives.

## Leftover (right)
`Team::xfer` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/rts/team.rs:2513-2515`) already xfers `self.state`. Leftover `do_set_team_state` / `eval_team_state_is` (`scripting/executor/actions_victory_team.rs`, `eval_basic.rs`) read that same field.

## Live (wrong)
`TeamRuntimePersist` (`Main/src/save_load/snapshot/player_team_persist.rs:97-112`) has created/active/see_enemy/waypoint/generic-script/recruitability but no `state`. `capture_team_factory_chunk` never reads `team.get_state()`. `apply_teams_to_leftover` calls `restore_save_script_state(...)` without a state argument, so leftover `Team.state` stays empty after load.

## Player-visible
Save after TEAM_SET_STATE "Attacking". After load TEAM_STATE_IS "Attacking" is false and TEAM_STATE_IS_NOT is true, so campaign scripts re-fire or stall.

## Evidence
C++ Team.cpp:2612-2613; leftover team.rs:2513-2515 + get_state/set_state; live player_team_persist.rs TeamRuntimePersist + restore_save_script_state.
close_reason: TeamRuntimePersist.state captured from leftover get_state. restore_save_script_state now takes state so TEAM_SET_STATE / TEAM_STATE_IS survive load.

title: [Team] isAGoodIdea rejects ready-queue teams C++ still builds
description:
C++ `AIPlayer::isAGoodIdeaToBuildTeam` (AIPlayer.cpp:1471-1508) only walks `iterate_TeamBuildQueue()` and rejects when that prototype is already being built. Ready-queue teams are not a "currently building" veto; `countTeamInstances() >= m_maxInstances` is the only instance cap. A second copy of a maxInstances>1 team can start while the first sits in TeamReadyQueue (idle / 60s force).

Leftover `AIPlayer::is_a_good_idea_to_build_team` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/ai_player/impl_select.rs`) matches C++: production condition, `instances >= max_instances`, then only `team_build_queue` name/handle, then `is_possible_to_build_team(..., true)`.

Live `AIPlayer::is_a_good_idea_to_build_team` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/ai.rs`) also rejects when `team_ready_queue` already has that prototype name. Skirmish AI with maxInstances>1 will not start the next copy until the ready team activates (up to 60s), so the army fields fewer concurrent teams than C++/leftover.

Evidence: C++ 1487-1492 build-queue-only; leftover impl_select.rs:149-164 build-queue-only; live ai.rs:4323-4326 `team_queue || team_ready_queue`.
close_reason: Live is_a_good_idea_to_build_team now matches C++: only TeamBuildQueue vetoes; ready-queue copy is not a currently-building reject.

title: [Locomotor] Live on-path dist never uses hover/aircraft flight-dist
description:

That value is `onPathDistToGoal` for approach-brake and arrival.

## Leftover
`UnitAIUpdate::get_treat_as_aircraft_for_loco_dist_to_goal` + `get_locomotor_distance_to_goal` (GameLogic/src/object/unit/ai_loco.rs:393-416, 818-868) port the same hover / path-extra / flight-dist tests. Matches C++.

title: [Locomotor] Live never sets ALLOW_INVALID_POSITION so taxi/enter/landing get 3x3 shove
description:
## C++
`Locomotor::locoUpdate_moveTowardsPosition` (Locomotor.cpp:968-977) runs `fixInvalidPosition` only when the unit is not AIR and `!getFlag(ALLOW_INVALID_POSITION)`. AI sets the flag for enter/hack (`AIEnterState`), waypoint follow, jet taxi/takeoff/landing (`JetAIUpdate`), Chinook takeoff/landing, Spectre gunship, and deliver-payload re-approach so those poses are not 3x3-shoved off parking/building cells.

## Leftover
`loco_update_move_towards_position` (GameLogic/src/locomotor/core_impl/move_dispatch.rs:41) skips `fix_invalid_position_with` when `allows_invalid_position()`. Leftover AI (`ai_states/enter.rs`, `jet_ai_update.rs`, `chinook_ai_update.rs`, `deliver_payload_ai_update.rs`, `spectre_gunship_update.rs`) sets the flag. Matches C++.

## Live
`update_movement` (Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/movement.rs:397-418) always runs `try_fix_invalid_position_3x3` on non-air invalid cells. Host Object has no `ALLOW_INVALID_POSITION` field or setter. Jet taxi / Chinook landing / enter still get the 3x3 vote shove added by hq-g9idj.

## Evidence
hq-g9idj added the C++ shove; it never added the C++ skip. Player-visible: jets/chinooks/entering infantry get shoved off stall/building cells that leftover/C++ allow.
close_reason: ALLOW_INVALID_POSITION skips 3x3 shove; set on enter/taxi, cleared on exit

title: [Locomotor] AbsoluteHeight live Z is kinematic snap not lift force
description:
## C++
`Locomotor::handleBehaviorZ` (Locomotor.cpp:2288-2317) treats `Z_ABSOLUTE_HEIGHT` the same as `Z_SURFACE_RELATIVE_HEIGHT`: if preferredHeight!=0 or PRECISE_Z_POS, compute damped preferred Z, then `calcLiftToUseAtPt` + `applyMotiveForce` (gravity / maxLift / SpeedLimitZ). Position is not teleported.

## Leftover
`Locomotor::handle_behavior_z_for` (GameLogic/src/locomotor/core_impl/behavior_z.rs:121-130) routes `AbsoluteHeight` through `lift_relative_to_layer` (lift force, no snap). Matches C++.

## Live
`Object::handle_behavior_z` (Main/src/game_logic/object/physics.rs:617-632) for `AbsoluteHeight` does `p.y += delta; set_position` (kinematic snap). `apply_live_handle_behavior_z` (world_tick/physics.rs:997-1012) only Euler-integrates leftover lift for SurfaceRelative / SmoothRelativeToHighestLayer — AbsoluteHeight is excluded.

## Evidence
hq-ygdfb fixed SurfaceRelative only. Leftover wings/thrust factory defaults and any INI `ZAxisBehavior = ABSOLUTE_HEIGHT` locos still pop to preferred height instead of lift-limited climb/dive. Not leftovers-only: live binds `behavior_z` from Common and calls `handle_behavior_z` on the march path.
close_reason: AbsoluteHeight live Z is lift+Euler not kinematic snap

title: [Team] Auto selectTeamToBuild uses invented max-as-required work orders
description:
## C++
`AIPlayer::selectTeamToBuild` (`AIPlayer.cpp:1628-1710`) picks a hi-priority prototype then calls `buildSpecificAITeam(teamProto, false)` (`AIPlayer.cpp` ~1900). That builds work orders from `TeamPrototype` `m_unitsInfo`:
- optional first: `numRequired = maxUnits-minUnits`, `m_required = false` (skipped when count<=0)
- then required: `numRequired = minUnits` (including `minUnits==0`), `m_required = true`
- `createInactiveTeam`, optional `friend_executeAction(productionCondition)` at queue time, append to build queue, `m_teamDelay=0`, arm `m_teamTimer` with wealth mods.

`isPossibleToBuildTeam` (`AIPlayer.cpp:1410-1453`) costs `(min+max)/2 * thingCost` then `cost *= m_teamResourcesToBuild` (`TeamResourcesToStart` in AIData.ini).

## Leftover (right)
`AIPlayer::select_team_to_build` (`GameLogic/src/ai/ai_player/impl_dozer.rs:873-940`) calls `build_specific_ai_team(team_name, false)` (`impl_teams.rs:361-515`) — same optional/required prepend + `create_inactive_team` + queue-time executeActions + `arm_team_timer_after_build`.
`is_possible_to_build_team` (`impl_select.rs:15-113`) uses `(min+max)/2` and leftover `AIData.team_resources_to_build`.

## Live (wrong)
`AIPlayer::select_team_to_build` (`Main/src/ai.rs:4189-4230`) does **not** call leftover `build_specific_ai_team`. It uses `create_team_queue` → `create_work_orders_for_team` (`ai.rs:4891-4996`):
- hardcoded invented compositions (`USA_RangerSquad` → 4 Rangers, `USA_BasicForce`, `China_RedGuardSquad`, `GLA_MassAssault`, …)
- unknown proto names: one **required** order per unit with `count = max_units` (no min/max split, no `minUnits==0` required stub)
Scripted `BUILD_TEAM` already uses leftover-right `build_team_work_orders` (`ai.rs:5033-5058`). Auto-select does not.
`estimate_team_unit_cost` / `can_afford_team_start` (`ai.rs:3009-3033`) cost those wrong counts × hardcoded `TEAM_RESOURCES_TO_START=0.1`, not leftover `(min+max)/2` × AIData `TeamResourcesToStart`.

## Evidence
- C++ `AIPlayer.cpp:1628-1710`, `buildSpecificAITeam` optional/required, `isPossibleToBuildTeam` 1410-1453
- Leftover `impl_dozer.rs:873-940`, `impl_teams.rs:428-456`, `impl_select.rs:52-89`
- Live `ai.rs:4189-4230`, `4891-4996`, `3009-3033`, `5289-5290`
- Player-visible: skirmish AI over-trains (treats max as required), never fields optional extras separately, expires/readies on the wrong census, and starts teams at a different cash threshold than leftover/C++.
close_reason: selectTeamToBuild now uses leftover-right buildSpecificAITeam min/max work orders instead of invented max-as-required compositions

title: [AssaultTransport] Crawler death never giveFinalOrders
description:
## C++
`AssaultTransportAIUpdate::update` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/AIUpdate/AssaultTransportAIUpdate.cpp:131-134`): if the transport `isEffectivelyDead()`, `giveFinalOrders()` then `UPDATE_SLEEP_FOREVER`.
`giveFinalOrders` (`:439-461`) transfers the original order to every living member as `CMD_FROM_PLAYER`: `aiAttackObject` if `m_isAttackObject` and the designated target still exists, else `aiAttackMoveToPosition` if `m_isAttackMove`, then `setAllowedToChase(FALSE)`.

## Leftover
`AssaultTransportAIUpdate::update` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/update/ai_update/assault_transport_ai_update.rs:357-360`) calls `give_final_orders()` when the transport is dead. `give_final_orders` (`:670-709`) issues leftover `ai_attack_object` / `ai_attack_move_to_position` with `CommandSourceType::FromPlayer` and clears chase.

## Live
`tick_assault_transport_updates` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/crates.rs:951-1074`) only walks crawlers that still exist with `assault_transport.active`. Destroying the crawler never runs leftover `give_final_orders`. Dead-crawler members keep whatever leftover AI (or none) they had; they do not inherit the assault attack / attack-move as a player order.

## Player-visible
Killing a Troop Crawler mid-assault drops the squad's attack instead of handing them the original attack / attack-move as if the player issued it.
close_reason: Live tick + destroy giveFinalOrders: dead crawler hands attack/attack-move to members as CMD_FROM_PLAYER.

title: [AssaultTransport] New members eject immediately
description:
## C++
`AssaultTransportAIUpdate::update` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/AIUpdate/AssaultTransportAIUpdate.cpp:220-266`): occupants added after assault starts are flagged `m_newMember[i] = TRUE` (`m_newOccupantsAreNewMembers`). Healthy contained members `aiExit` only when `!m_newMember[i]`. Comment: "New members won't eject out until a new attack order is issued."

title: [Save] AISkirmishPlayer defense-fan cursor never persisted

After load the eight fields stay at ctor 0, so the next `SKIRMISH_BUILD_BASE_DEFENSE_*` / `buildAIBaseDefense` places another turret on the first front/flank slot (or fails the π/3 gate after re-walking from zero) instead of continuing the saved fan.

close_reason: AITQ v2 persists AISkirmishPlayer front/flank defense-fan cursor (8 fields) via capture/apply_queue_persist. v1 suffix still loads with fan at 0.

title: [Save] PLAYER_HUNT units_should_hunt never persisted
description:
C++ `Player::xfer` v6 (`Player.cpp:4509-4514`) writes `m_unitsShouldHunt`. After `PLAYER_HUNT`, newly produced units keep seeking even when the map is momentarily empty (`AIHuntState` only exits to Idle when `!getUnitsShouldHunt()` and there is no victim).

title: [FXDie] Live invents death FX/audio names for templates without authored FXListDie
description:
## C++
FXListDie.cpp onDie (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Die/FXListDie.cpp:44-77) plays only the authored m_defaultDeathFX (INI DeathFX). A template with no FXListDie module - or DeathFX=None - gets nothing from this module; death FX come from SlowDeath phases / CreateObjectDie / CrushDie etc.

Main/src/game_logic/host_fx_list_die.rs fx_list_die_config_for_template (:327-381): when authored_fx_list_die finds no module with DeathFX, name heuristics invent FX + audio: bombtruck/demotruck -> WeaponFX_BombTruckHighExplosiveBombDetonation + "ExplosionBombTruck"; terrorist -> WeaponFX_TerroristDynamitePackDetonation + "ExplosionTerrorist"; scud missile -> "FX_ScudMissileDie" + "ExplosionScud"; nuke missile -> "FX_NukeMissileDie" + "ExplosionNuke"; name contains tank/vehicle/truck -> "FX_VehicleDie" + "VehicleDestroyed"; structures -> "FX_StructureDie" + "BuildingCollapse". object/death.rs fire_fx_list_die (:551-576) queues the invented audio (take_pending_death_fx_audio -> world_tick/ai.rs queue_audio_event) and the invented FX name flows to presentation death_fx_name / dMain/src/gamepts.

## Retail data (INIZH.big, all 135 INI files scanned)
FX_VehicleDie, FX_StructureDie, WeaponFX_TerroristDynamitePackDetonation, FX_ScudMissileDie, FX_NukeMissileDie are NOT authored FXLists (only WeaponFX_BombTruckHighExplosiveBombDetonation is real). ## Player-visible
Vehicles/structures without authored DeathFX emit invented FXList names and queue nonexistent audio events instead of staying silent; the invented pending name can also pre-empt authored SlowDeath phase FX in the death pipeline. playable_claim stays false.
close_reason: fx_list_die_config_for_template now returns only authored DeathFX (plus test inject). Removed bombtruck/terrorist/scud/nuke/tank/structure name heuristics that invented FX_VehicleDie/FX_StructureDie/FX_ScudMissileDie and nonexistent audio. Unauthored templates play nothing; leftover play_death_fx None -> return.

title: [Locomotor] Live march never dispatches Thrust appearance to the 3D thrust mover
description:
## C++
`Locomotor::locoUpdate_moveTowardsPosition` dispatches `LOCO_THRUST` to `moveTowardsPositionThrust` (Locomotor.cpp:1104-1107). `moveTowardsPositionThrust` (Locomotor.cpp:1891-2004):
- `desiredSpeed = clamp(m_minSpeed, desiredSpeed, maxForwardSpeed)`
- goal Z replaced by damped `preferredHeight + getSurfaceHtAtPt` unless PRECISE_Z_POS
- `calcDirectionToApplyThrust` quadratic solve with gravity preload (Locomotor.cpp:175-250)
- thrust clamped to `MaxThrustAngle` cone around nose via tryToRotateVector3D
- orients nose to the **velocity vector** (3x maxTurnRate while OBJECT_STATUS_BRAKING, aim at goal)
- `accelVec = thrustDir*maxAccel - curVel*damping` applied as `applyMotiveForce(mass*accelVec)`

Every Thrust unit (Comanche, Helix, Chinook, MIG on heli locos, missiles bound to locomotors) marches with this 3D model while it has a locomotor goal.

## Leftover (right)
`loco_update_move_towards_position` (`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/locomotor/core_impl/move_dispatch.rs:303-313`) dispatches `LocomotorAppearance::Thrust` to `move_towards_position_thrust_physics` (`core_impl/thrust.rs:104-249`): quadratic thrust dir with `cur_vel.z += loco_gravity()`, maxThrustAngle cone via `try_to_rotate_vector3d`, orient-to-velocity with 3x braking turn, `accel_vec = thrust_dir*max_accel - heading_vel*damping` into `last_motive_accel`. C++-matching per hq-yu9r close.

## Live (wrong)
The production march `GameLogic::update_movement` (`Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/movement.rs:541-835`) has **no Thrust arm**: Climber gets flags/slope, wheeled gets reverse/floor/look-ahead, treads/legs get angleCoeff — Thrust falls into the generic ground march: `desired_angle = atan2` at the flat target, `rotate_towards_position` yaw-only, `target_velocity = heading * speed` accel-blended (movement.rs:791-806). No gravity-aware thrust aim, no MaxThrustAngle cone, no orient-to-velocity (nose points at the goal, not where it flies), no 3x braking turn, no accelVec damping; Z only via `apply_live_handle_behavior_z` lift.

The C++-faithful port `Object::move_towards_thrust` (`Main/src/game_logic/object/physics.rs:1399-1483`, hq-sw06m close) is wired **only** into idle maintain `loco_maintain_current_position` (`physics.rs:691-694`). Its other caller `Object::update_movement` (`object/update.rs:372-374`) is test-only (callers only in `world_tests`). GameWorld movement authority is production-off (`gameworld_shadow/tick/authority.rs:99-103`), so `world_tick/movement.rs` is the live march.

Player-visible: a Comanche/Helix ordered to move or attack-chase flies like a hover car — yaw-at-goal, no banking dive/climb thrust, no velocity alignment; mid-flight it behaves differently from the same unit idle-hovering (which does use the thrust model), so transitions to/from hold are discontinuous.

Not a duplicate: hq-yu9r (closed, fixed the **leftover** thrust mover), hq-sw06m (closed, fixed the **quality** of live `move_towards_thrust` itself; did not wire it into the goal march), hq-2e10h (PRECISE_Z landing stamps).

## Evidence
- C++ Locomotor.cpp:1104-1107, 175-250, 1891-2004
- Leftover `GameEngine/GameLogic/src/locomotor/core_impl/move_dispatch.rs:303-313`, `thrust.rs:104-249`
- Live `Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/movement.rs:541-835` (no Thrust dispatch; generic 791-806), `object/physics.rs:691-694` (maintain-only call), `object/update.rs:372-374` (test-only), `gameworld_shadow/tick/authority.rs:99-103` (host march is live)
close_reason: Live update_movement now dispatches LocomotorAppearance::Thrust to Object::move_towards_thrust (C++ locoUpdate_moveTowardsPosition LOCO_THRUST). Idle maintain already used the 3D mover; goal march no longer uses yaw-at-goal hover-car integration.

title: Tunnel-guard nemesis scan ignores tunnels' current victims
description:
## C++
AITNGuard.cpp AITNGuardMachine::lookForInnerTarget (168-239): after TunnelTracker curNemesis it scans every tunnel and (a) adopts the enemy that tunnel is CURRENTLY ATTACKING - currentTunnel->getAI()->getGoalObject() with relationship ENEMIES - and (b) for damage adopts the attacker only when !info->out.m_noEffect, body->getLastDamageTimestamp() + TheAI->getAiData()->m_guardEnemyScanRate > frame, relationship ENEMIES, and getAbleToAttackSpecificObject(ATTACK_TUNNEL_NETWORK_GUARD, attacker) is POSSIBLE/AFTER_MOVING; on adoption it sets owner->getTeam()->setTeamTargetObject(attacker) and tunnels->updateNemesis(attacker).

## Leftover (matches C++)
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/tn_guard.rs find_tunnel_network_inner_target (~1550-1660): team common-target check, tunnels->getCurNemesis, per-tunnel ai_guard.get_goal_object_id() enemy victim scan, info.output.no_effect skip, window from get_guard_enemy_scan_rate() (AIData), AbleToAttackType::TunnelNetworkGuard gate, team set_team_target_object(attacker_id) + tunnels.update_nemesis.

## Live (wrong)
GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/support_states.rs tick_tunnel_network_nemesis (~7445-7530) derives the shared nemesis ONLY from a tunnel's last_damage_source inside a hardcoded 30-frame window (ts.saturating_add(30)); no per-tunnel attack-victim (goal-object) scan, no no-effect damage skip, no ATTACK_TUNNEL_NETWORK_GUARD able-to-attack gate (any enemy-affiliated damager becomes the pool nemesis even if the guards cannot attack it), and no team common-target write. host_guard_enemy_scan_rate() exists in the same crate (world_tick/teams.rs:236) but is not used here.

## Player-visible
An enemy that walks into tunnel weapon range and gets shot at (never damaging a tunnel itself, or dealing no-effect damage) rallies the GLA tunnel-guard pool in retail; live ignores it, so guards stay inside until a tunnel actually takes damage. An unattackable damager also hijacks the shared nemesis slot, and INI AIData GuardEnemyScanRate overrides are ignored (window hardcoded to 30 frames).

## Not a duplicate
hq-efzff ('GuardTunnelNetwork never runs') was fixed by implementing tick_tunnel_network_nemesis sally/return and hq-70kwp fixed the sally-never-returns leg; neither covers which enemies qualify as nemesis (victim scan, no-effect skip, AIData scan-rate window, able-to-attack gate, team-target propagation).
close_reason: Live tick_tunnel_network_nemesis now matches leftover find_tunnel_network_inner_target / C++ lookForInnerTarget: per-tunnel goal-object (target) victim scan first, last-damage skips non-health-damaging no-effect, window is host_guard_enemy_scan_rate() not hardcoded 30, ATTACK_TUNNEL_NETWORK_GUARD able-to-attack gate when the pool has occupants, set_host_team_common_target + update_nemesis on damage adoption.

title: [AIGroup] groupAttackObject gates members on can_attack
description:
## C++
`AIGroup::groupAttackObjectPrivate` (AIGroup.cpp:2100-2173) near-to-far loop issues `ai->aiAttackObject`/`aiForceAttackObject` to EVERY member with an AIUpdateInterface. Only gates: DISABLED_HELD and `theUnit != victim`. No `isAbleToAttack` gate. Dead-but-present victim still receives orders.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/ai/group.rs:1508-1620` `group_attack_object_private` skips only Held riders; orders every member with AI via `ai_attack_object`/`ai_force_attack_object`.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/command_executor/attack.rs:157-273` `execute_group_attack_object` lines 246-252: `if !u.can_attack() { continue; }` silently drops weaponless members. Lines 166-172 return TargetDestroyed for a dead-but-present victim (C++ proceeds). Same extra `can_attack` gate in `execute_attack_area` (682-684).

## Evidence
Mixed selection (dozer/transport + tanks) right-click attack: C++/leftover queue the attack on non-attackers (they path toward the victim; stunned members resume after stun). Live never orders them. Not hq-x3hzm (passenger fire), hq-oqbaw (attack-move cannot-move), hq-fgy2s (attack-team victims).
close_reason: Live execute_group_attack_object no longer TargetDestroyed on dead-but-present victim; every AI member gets aiAttackObject (unit_command_attack, else set_target). execute_attack_area no longer gates can_attack. Test: group_attack_object_orders_weaponless_and_dead_victim.

title: [AIGroup] Free-move never dissolves formation stamps
description:
## C++
`AIGroup::groupMoveToPosition` free-move loop (AIGroup.cpp:1681) `theUnit->setFormationID(NO_FORMATION_ID)` before `aiMoveToPosition`/`aiFollowPathAppend`, dissolving any stale formation on non-column movers.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/ai/group.rs:676-678` free-move loop `obj.set_formation_id(FormationID::NONE)` for every mover before `compute_individual_destination`.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/command_executor/movement.rs` `execute_move`, `execute_move_to_with_voice`, `execute_force_move` assign goals via `group_move_destinations` and never clear `formation_id`. Only `execute_add_waypoint` calls `unit_command_set_formation(unit_id, 0, ZERO)`.

## Evidence
Stamp 3 units as a formation, add 2 unstamped units, move: C++ clears the stamps (subsequent moves are free/clamped-offset); live keeps fid on the 3, so re-selecting them later takes the formation-offset branch and `compute_ground_path_should_group`'s all-same-fid shortcut can spuriously force group-pathing. Not hq-22ffr (tighten wrongly dissolving formations — opposite direction).
close_reason: Free-move path (execute_move / execute_move_to_with_voice / execute_force_move) calls dissolve_free_move_formation_stamps before dests issue, matching C++ setFormationID(NO_FORMATION_ID). Stamped-formation moves keep fid. Test: free_move_dissolves_mixed_formation_stamps.

title: [AIGroup] Tighten/Scatter drop stunned members via can_move
description:
## C++
`groupTightenToPosition` (AIGroup.cpp:1861), `groupScatter` (1763), free-move bbox (`groupMoveToPosition` :1629) and `getMinMaxAndCenter` (323-363) filter only DISABLED_HELD, KINDOF_IMMOBILE, `getAI()==NULL`. A stunned/subdued/deployed unit still counts toward min/max/center and still receives the order.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/ai/group.rs` tighten (731-734), scatter (890-893), move bbox (637-640): `is_disabled_by_type(Held) || Immobile || no-AI`.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/command_executor/movement.rs` `execute_tighten_to_position` (668), `execute_scatter` (1162), `should_tighten_group_move` bbox (603): `!unit.can_move()`. Host `can_move()` is false while `is_disabled()` or `status.deployed`, so stunned/subdued/deployed members are excluded from the gather bbox and never receive tighten/scatter.

## Evidence
Stun a tank mid-group and click inside the group: C++ tightens/orders it (executes when stun clears); live skips it and computes the scaled bbox from a subset (smaller rect → click can fall outside → tighten never fires). Guard already treats this as AI-interface-only (`group_guard_includes_stunned_member_that_cannot_move`); tighten/scatter/bbox do not. Not hq-iolqu (Guard), hq-oqbaw (attack-move), hq-t4bim (hunt).
close_reason: Tighten/scatter/should_tighten use group_ai_member_receives_move (Held/Immobile/no-AI only). unit_command_tighten_to and unit_command_move_to_moving no longer require can_move; stunned still receive the order. Test: tighten_scatter_include_stunned_members.

title: [AIGroup] Free-move dest clamp uses selection_radius not geometry
description:
## C++
AIGroup::computeIndividualDestination (AIGroup.cpp:470-471) clamps offset length to 6 * obj->getGeometryInfo().getBoundingCircleRadius().

## Leftover (right)
GameLogic/src/ai/group.rs:457 max_length = 6.0 * obj_guard.get_geometry_info().get_bounding_circle_radius().

## Live (wrong)
Main/src/command_executor/movement.rs:359 group_move_destinations gathers obj.selection_radius.max(5.0) and free-move clamp uses that as max_length = 6.0 * radius. Live bounding_circle_radius helper (movement.rs:31-32, documented not the pick/click selection_radius) is used by scatter and add-waypoint but not by the free-move path.

## Evidence
Wide-radius pick units get a far looser spread clamp on live than C++ geometry radius. Not hq-u11dl (that closed scatter selection_radius; this is the groupMoveToPosition free-move clamp site).
close_reason: group_move_destinations free-move clamp uses bounding_circle_radius (geometry) not selection_radius.max(5). Test: free_move_clamp_uses_geometry_not_selection_radius.

title: [Pathfind] adjustToPossibleDestination tier never ported — attack/dozer failures halt instead of walking near
description:
## C++
- Pathfinder::checkForPossible (AIPathfind.cpp:5489-5504): candidate cell accepted when its type is not Impassable/Obstacle/BridgeImpassable AND getEffectiveZone(surfaces, isCrusher, cell->getZone()) == fromZone (terrain-zone fallback when starting in an obstacle).
- Pathfinder::adjustToPossibleDestination (AIPathfind.cpp:5510-5617): if the seed goal cell is same-zone and checkDestination-valid keep it, otherwise 400-cell spiral of try_zone_adjust (same effective zone + checkDestination footprint). Weaker than adjustDestination/checkForAdjust — used where checkForAdjust is too strict.
- Callers: AIUpdateInterface::doPathfind attack failure (AIUpdate.cpp:434-438): m_requestedDestination = victim pos -> adjustToPossibleDestination -> ignoreObstacle(victim) -> computePath. DozerAIUpdate.cpp:633-635 packed-tight dozer goal ("Our goal may be inside a building, if we are packing them in tight, so try adjusting"). AIPlayer.cpp:2370-2373 dozer dispatch. AIUpdate.cpp:1553-1560 move-out-of-way safe positions. Contain exits (OpenContain.cpp:998/1103, GarrisonContain.cpp:1548/1573) are already tracked from the contain slice (hq-jtmgl, hq-6xv03, hq-pj6v9, hq-2x44y).

## Leftover (right)
- GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/pathfind_complete/check_movement.rs: check_for_possible (:462), adjust_to_possible_destination (:512, are_connected zone gate carrying is_crusher), try_zone_adjust — full port, zero live callers.

## Live
- No possible_destination / check_for_possible anywhere in Main. request_object_path (Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/attack.rs:2110-2148) returns false on a null path — no near-victim tier, no ignoreObstacle(victim). assign_unit_attack_path (Main/src/game_logic/world_save.rs:1860-1975) falls back to plain assign_unit_path(unit_id, target_pos, &[]) — no same-zone possible-destination adjust and no victim ignore, so the fallback itself fails when the victim cell/occupancy blocks. walk_unit_via_open_contain_exit (world_combat/drones_and_garrison.rs:1515+) walks ExitEnd/rally raw.

## Player-visible
Attack a target whose in-range firing cells are all blocked (walled yard, stacked defenders): the C++ attacker still walks to a possible same-zone cell near the victim and keeps pressure; the live attacker halts. Dozer dispatched into a packed base: C++ adjusts the goal to a possible cell; live refuses and the dozer stalls.

## Evidence
C++ AIPathfind.cpp:5489-5617; AIUpdate.cpp:434-438, 1553-1560; DozerAIUpdate.cpp:633-635; AIPlayer.cpp:2370-2373. Leftover pathfind_complete/check_movement.rs:462, 512, try_zone_adjust. Live attack.rs request_object_path, world_save.rs assign_unit_attack_path fallback, drones_and_garrison.rs walk_unit_via_open_contain_exit.
close_reason: Live adjustToPossibleDestination: checkForPossible + 400-cell same-zone spiral. Wired find_path_ex retry, assign_unit_attack_path (adjust+ignoreObstacle victim), dozer END dock, AIPlayer bridge-repair go-home.

title: [Hunt] Player attack/move never ends Hunt — unit resumes seek-and-destroy
description:
## C++
`AI_ATTACK_OBJECT` / `AI_MOVE_TO` exit to `AI_IDLE` (AIStates.cpp:686-688, 5754). `AIHuntState::onExit` (7099-7109) destroys the hunt machine and `releaseWeaponLock(LOCKED_TEMPORARILY)` on ANY exit. A subsequent `aiAttackObject`/`aiMoveTo` replaces AI_HUNT at the parent machine; hunt never resumes.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/ai/states/hunt.rs` `classic_on_exit` halts the hunt machine and `release_weapon_lock(LockedTemporarily)` on every exit. Parent transitions to attack/move end Hunt.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/unit_commands.rs` `unit_command_attack` (260-309) and `unit_command_move_to` (189-216) never clear `hunting` (only Stop and Guard do). `world_tick/ai.rs:607-615` flips `hunting && Idle && target-none` back to `Patrolling`, so after the player's ordered attack or move finishes the unit resumes map-wide hunting. Attack also never releases the LockedTemporarily weapon lock.

## Evidence
Player-visible: Hunt then click-attack or move — C++ stays idle after the order; live resumes seek-and-destroy. Flashbang/secondary-locked hunter keeps the locked slot under a player attack order. Not hq-huh1m (guard orders only) or hq-yvq8x (CommandButtonHunt last-command-source gate).
close_reason: Player attack/move ends Hunt: clear hunting + release LOCKED_TEMPORARILY so Idle does not resume Patrolling

title: [Hunt] Hunt scan is lockstep frame%30 not per-unit jitter
description:
## C++
`AIHuntState::onEnter` (AIStates.cpp:7083-7093) sets `m_nextEnemyScanTime = now + GameLogicRandomValue(0, ENEMY_SCAN_RATE)` — comment: so that everyone doesn't scan on the same frame, to avoid spikes. Update (7148-7149) `m_nextEnemyScanTime = now + ENEMY_SCAN_RATE` (`ENEMY_SCAN_RATE = LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND = 30`).

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/ai/states/hunt.rs` `classic_on_enter` jitters `GameLogicRandomValue(0, ENEMY_SCAN_RATE)`; `classic_on_update` `now + ENEMY_SCAN_RATE`. Same in `ai/ai_states/hunt.rs`.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/ai_authority.rs` ~151: `should_scan(30)` is `frame.is_multiple_of(30)`. Every hunting unit runs the O(all-objects) map-wide `find_closest_enemy` on the SAME frames (the spike C++ jitters away). First scan after hunt start waits for the next global 30-boundary instead of a random 0..30.

## Evidence
Not a closed duplicate: cadence beads hq-ylh57 / hq-ew5m are guard-path only.
close_reason: Hunt scan uses per-unit hunt_next_enemy_scan jitter (0..30) then +30, not frame%30

title: [Hunt] FireWeapon CommandButtonHunt re-arms lock every 30 frames
description:
## C++
`CommandButtonHuntUpdate::huntWeapon` (CommandButtonHuntUpdate.cpp ~131-145): every tick — `aiHunt` when idle, `obj->setWeaponLock(weaponSlot, LOCKED_TEMPORARILY)`, return `UPDATE_SLEEP_NONE` (wake EVERY frame). The lock is transiently released elsewhere (`Object::fireCurrentWeapon` releases a temp lock when the locked weapon's clip completes an auto-reload) and re-armed next frame.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/object/update/command_button_hunt_update.rs` `hunt_weapon` — same re-lock + `UpdateSleepTime::None`.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/crates.rs` `tick_command_button_hunt_updates` (~296-380): hunters only processed when `h.due(frame)` and `h.schedule_next(frame)=+30` is applied to ALL modes including FireWeapon, so the slot re-lock runs at most every 30 frames. Combined with live-modeled release in `object/attack.rs:425-433`, a secondary/flashbang hunter can fire its default-slot weapon for up to 29 frames after each clip cycle.

## Evidence
Not hq-t5oyk (that was modes never arming at all; re-arm cadence is uncovered).
close_reason: FireWeapon CommandButtonHunt due every frame (UPDATE_SLEEP_NONE) so temp lock re-arms after clip reload

title: [ControlBar] Sell click sells only the first selected structure
description:
## C++
`ControlBar::processCommandUI` `GUI_COMMAND_SELL` (`ControlBarCommandProcessing.cpp` ~733) appends `MSG_SELL` with no object argument.
`GameLogicDispatch.cpp:1450-1459` — `MSG_SELL` → `currentlySelectedGroup->groupSell(CMD_FROM_PLAYER)` sells every selected structure in the current selection group.

## Leftover (right)
`ControlBar::publish_host_command_if_enabled` (`control_bar_impl/impl_execute.rs`) → `host_command_bridge.rs` `DirectCommand { command_type: Sell, selected_object_ids: context.selected_objects.clone() }` publishes the full leftover WND selection (C++ group scope).

## Live (wrong)

title: GuardRetaliate never escalates INNER to OUTER chase
description:
## C++
AIGuardRetaliate.cpp AIGuardRetaliateMachine constructor (~140-170): AI_GUARD_RETALIATE_INNER transitions success AND failure to AI_GUARD_RETALIATE_OUTER. AIGuardRetaliateInnerState::onEnter leashes at sqr(1.5*stdGuardRange), no timer. AIGuardRetaliateOuterState::onEnter (~360-420) re-attacks the SAME nemesis with m_radiusSqr = sqr(0.67*(adjustedVision + stdGuardRange)) and m_attackGiveUpFrame = frame + m_guardChaseUnitFrames; OuterState::update refreshes the timer while the goal stays within stdGuardRange of center; GuardRetaliateExitConditions also leashes the owner at stdGuardRange. The retaliate chase continues through a timed OUTER phase before GET_CRATE->RETURN.

## Leftover (matches C++)
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/guard_retaliate.rs define_guard_retaliate_states maps GuardRetaliateStateType::Inner success/failure -> Outer; AIGuardRetaliateOuterState::on_enter re-attacks with radius 0.67*(range + std_guard_range) + give-up frame (frame + guard_chase_unit_frames).

## Live (wrong)
GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/teams.rs tick_guard_retaliate_states (~910-1030) stamps scan-acquired victims with guard_chase_phase = 1 (INNER) only (~970/980) and last-attacker victims with GUARD_CHASE_PHASE_RETALIATE; nothing sets phase 2 on the retaliate path (phase 2 comes only from guard-proper begin_guard_chase, world_objects/support_states.rs:3205). guard_retaliate_chase_should_exit (~310-333) implements the phase-2 radius 0.67*(outer+inner) but it is unreachable: when the phase-1 victim leaves the 1.5x inner radius (or the owner leaves the inner leash) the tick clears guard_retaliate_victim and walks home; the timed OUTER continuation never runs. Escalate phase 1 -> 2 (stamp give-up frame) instead of ending, and only end when the OUTER leash/timer trips.

## Player-visible
A unit that retaliates when a friend is shot abandons the chase the moment the attacker steps past 1.5x its guard ring. Retail keeps chasing the same attacker for m_guardChaseUnitFrames (~4s) inside 0.67x(vision+guardRange) before giving up and walking home.

## Not a duplicate
hq-917km added the chase give-up itself (closed); this is the missing INNER->OUTER escalation so live quits at the inner radius without the timed outer phase. hq-vq33x (inner rescan ignores team attackCommonTarget) and hq-6gy4k (return-to-guard after kill) cover different transitions.
close_reason: Live tick_guard_retaliate_states now escalates phase 1 INNER success/failure to phase 2 OUTER (stamp give-up = frame + guardChaseUnitFrames) instead of walking home. OUTER uses 0.67*(vision+stdGuard) and refreshes the timer while the goal stays within stdGuard of center. Matches leftover define_state(Inner, Outer, Outer) / C++ AIGuardRetaliateMachine.

title: [Pathfind] Live zone gates drop crusher zone combiners — crushers refuse fence-divided crossings
description:
## C++
- PathfindZoneManager::getEffectiveZone (AIPathfind.cpp:3118-3141): when crusher, `zone = m_crusherZones[zone]` BEFORE the ground-cliff/water/rubble lookups.
- m_crusherZones is built by the calculateZones equivalency pass: crusherGround (AIPathfind.cpp:1793-1800, CELL_OBSTACLE-with-isObstacleFence <-> CELL_CLEAR) applyZone(..., m_crusherZones, ...) at :2652-2654 and :2688-2690; flattenZones(m_crusherZones, m_hierarchicalZones) at :2748-2749.
- internalFindPath zone gate (AIPathfind.cpp:6532-6550): `Bool isCrusher = obj ? obj->getCrusherLevel() > 0 : false;` zone1/zone2 = getEffectiveZone(surfaces, isCrusher, ...); refuses when effective zones differ (tunneling/ignoreObstacle falls back to terrain zones). checkForPossible/adjustToPossibleDestination (:5494-5495, :5549-5560) and hierarchical enqueue (:7356-7361) are crusher-aware the same way.

## Leftover (right)
- GameEngine/GameLogic/src/path/zone_manager.rs: build_equivalency_tables applies crusher_ground into crusher_zones; get_effective_zone(acceptable_surfaces, crusher, zone) maps crusher_zones first; flatten_zones covers the crusher table.
- GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/pathfind_complete/block_zones.rs: are_connected(start, goal, surfaces, is_crusher) -> get_effective_zone(surfaces, is_crusher, ...); find_path.rs:43-52 zone gate calls are_connected(..., request.is_crusher).

## Live
- Main/src/game_logic/pathfinding.rs get_effective_zone (~:1643) has no crusher parameter and goes straight to cliff/water/rubble; PathfindingGrid only stores ground_water_zones / ground_cliff_zones / ground_rubble_zones (~:215-222) — no crusher combiner is ever built, so fence (is_obstacle_fence) Obstacle zones never merge with adjacent Clear zones.
- find_path_via_crate (~:5570-5577) receives is_crusher but its disconnected-pocket gate calls quick_path_exists_for(from_w, to_w, surfaces) with no crusher; quick_path_exists_for / client_safe_quick_does_path_exist_for and destination_cell_ok zone fallback are likewise crusher-blind.
- Cell-level crusher fence crossing IS wired (hq-epdcu), so the crate A* would cross the fence — the zone pre-gate refuses first.

## Player-visible
Overlord / any crusher-level unit ordered across a fence line that seals off a region: C++ merges fence<->clear zones for crushers via m_crusherZones and paths through (crushing the fence); live zone gate sees two disconnected zones, returns None, and the unit halts at the fence despite being able to crush it. Same refusal hits destination adjust for crushers behind fences.

## Evidence
C++ GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/AI/AIPathfind.cpp:1793-1800, 2652-2690, 2748-2749, 3118-3141, 6532-6550. Leftover GameEngine/GameLogic/src/path/zone_manager.rs (crusher_zones build + get_effective_zone), ai/pathfind_complete/block_zones.rs are_connected, ai/pathfind_complete/find_path.rs:43-52. Live Main/src/game_logic/pathfinding.rs: PathfindingGrid combiner fields ~215-222, get_effective_zone ~1643, build_surface_combiners ~1566, find_path_via_crate pocket gate ~5570-5577, quick_path_exists_for ~1692.
close_reason: Live m_crusherZones built (fence Obstacle↔Clear), getEffectiveZone maps crusher first, find_path_via_crate / destination_cell_ok / client_safe use crusher combiners so crushers cross fence-divided pockets.
