title: [Particle] ParticleSysBone drops bone Z rotation
description:
C++ W3DModelDraw.cpp:2604-2611 recalcBonesForClientParticleSystems does sys->setPosition(&pos) AND sys->rotateLocalTransformZ(rotation) (boneTransform.Get_Z_Rotation) before attachToDrawable so the system is oriented like the bone.

Leftover GameLogic/src/object/draw/w3d_model_draw_impl/draw.rs:607-610 sets position + rotate_particle_system_local_transform_z; lookup_pristine_bone_pose returns (translation, z_rotation). Bridge exposes rotate_particle_system_local_transform_z (particle_manager.rs:1787-1801).

Live Main/src/game_logic/combat_particles.rs:1370-1377 particle_sys_bone_local uses lookup_pristine_bone_translation only. attach_named_to_object_local → attach_particle_system_to_object_local accepts only a Coord3D. Main never calls rotate_particle_system_local_transform_z.

Effect: bone-attached exhausts/stacks/repair/frenzy clouds on rotated bones emit along world axes, not the bone orientation (ORTHO/OUTWARD velocity wrong).
close_reason: ParticleSysBone spawn uses lookup_pristine_bone_pose Z and leftover attach_particle_system_to_object_local_oriented (setPosition, rotateLocalTransformZ, attach). Existing systems are not re-rotated each tick (Rotate_Z is incremental).

title: [Pathfind] Live zone flood merges rubble into ground and treats Impassable as zone 0
description:
## C++
`calculateZones` (`AIPathfind.cpp:2329-2340`) joins cells only when `getType()` is equal, so `CELL_RUBBLE` is its own zone (not Clear). Impassable / BridgeImpassable / Obstacle also get real zone ids. `getEffectiveZone` (`:3157-3162`) joins clear↔rubble only for `GROUND|RUBBLE` locomotors via `m_groundRubbleZones`. `clientSafeQuickDoesPathExist` then compares effective zones.

## Leftover (right)
`block_zones.rs` `flood_fill_type` (`:488-516`) floods by exact cell type (Rubble separate; Impassable gets a real zone). `build_surface_combiners` builds `ground_rubble_zones` via `pair_ground_rubble` (`:668-669, :699-700`). `ZoneManager::get_effective_zone` has a GROUND+RUBBLE branch (`:258-261`). `are_connected` returns true on zone 0 only when zones are genuinely uncalculated (`:179-181`).

## Live (wrong)
`path_zone_flood_kind` (`pathfinding.rs:1413-1421`) maps Rubble into `_ => Some(0)` — the same flood kind as Clear — so rubble fields merge into ground zones. Impassable / Obstacle / BridgeImpassable return `None` and stay zone 0. `build_surface_combiners` / `get_effective_zone` (`:1560-1658`) have water/cliff tables only — no GROUND+RUBBLE. `quick_path_exists_for` (`:1688-1692`) treats `z==0` as uninitialized → **true**.

## Evidence
hq-c88bl closed CELL_RUBBLE stamping. hq-998ki closed missing water/cliff combiners. Remaining: rubble identity + Impassable-as-0. Feeds find_path zone precheck (`:5500`), `destination_cell_ok` (`:3042-3048`), rally (`unit_commands.rs`), and placement (`ui_production.rs`).

## Player-visible
GROUND-only units get "path exists" across/into destroyed-building rubble and map-edge Impassable / under-deck BridgeImpassable cells. Rally and placement skip the no-path warning. C++/leftover refuse unless the locomotor is GROUND+RUBBLE.
close_reason: Live path_zone_flood_kind floods by exact cell type (Rubble != Clear; Impassable/Obstacle/BridgeImpassable get real zones). build_surface_combiners + get_effective_zone join Clear↔Rubble only for GROUND|RUBBLE. stamp_rubble_at_world rebuilds zones after destroy stamps.

title: [Pathfind] Hover/thrust aircraft skip leftover tall-building segment detour
description:
## C++
`Pathfinder::getAircraftPath` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/AI/AIPathfind.cpp:5781-5847`):
- `checkClips` is true only when `getAppearance() == LOCO_WINGS` and gates **only** `circleClipsTallBuilding`.
- The `segmentIntersectsTallBuilding` insertion walk (`limit=20`) runs for **every** aircraft path (hover/thrust included).
- `avoidObject = ai->getBuildingToNotPathAround()` (Chinook combat-drop goal).

## Leftover (right)
`pathfind_complete/line_passable.rs` `get_aircraft_path` (`:390-455`): `circle_clips_tall_building` only when `check_clips`; the segment loop is unconditional with `limit=20` and plumbs `avoid_object` into both helpers.

## Live (wrong)
`PathfindingSystem::find_path_ex_surfaces` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/pathfinding.rs:6941-6957`) sets `check_clips = self.seeker_wings` and gates **both** `circle_clips_tall_building` and `detour_path_around_tall_buildings` on that flag. Hover/thrust (Chinook/Helix) get a two-node straight line. `detour_path_around_tall_buildings` also hardcodes `ignore=None` (`:6750`) and uses a per-segment insert cap of 4 with no overall 20 limit.

## Evidence
hq-8vdsw closed over-clipping (circleClips on ALL aircraft). That fix also hid the segment walk from non-WINGS. Distinct remaining gap: C++/leftover still detour hover/thrust around `KINDOF_AIRCRAFT_PATH_AROUND` buildings.

## Player-visible
Chinooks/Helixes fly through Command Centers and other AIRCRAFT_PATH_AROUND structures instead of inserting the three radial-offset waypoints C++/leftover add.
close_reason: find_path_ex_surfaces: circleClips only when seeker_wings; segmentIntersectsTallBuilding detour (limit=20, avoid=getBuildingToNotPathAround) runs for every aircraft including hover/thrust.

title: [Pathfind] Live patchPath ignores occupancy so stuck units re-path through parked allies
description:
## C++
`Pathfinder::patchPath` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/AI/AIPathfind.cpp:10344-10520`) walks the original path reverse from last→first. Each node runs `checkForMovement` with `considerTransient = blocked`, then relaxes transient outside ±2 cells of the start. Breaks on `!checkForMovement` or `allyFixedCount || enemyFixed` ("Don't patch through cells that are occupied"). Tracks `goalPos` as the still-clear node closest to the unit, A*s to a matching suffix node, splices, then `path->optimize(obj, surfaces, blocked)`.

## Leftover (right)
`pathfind_complete/classify.rs` `patch_path` (`:55-228`) matches: `CheckMovementInfo` with `consider_transient=blocked`, ±2 relaxation, break on `!check_for_movement || ally_fixed_count>0 || enemy_fixed`, closest-goal tracking, suffix-node fallback, splice, `optimize_path`.

## Live (wrong)
`PathfindingSystem::patch_path` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/pathfinding.rs:7000-7046`) reverse-walks with only static `cell_passable_for_layer`. No occupancy, no `blocked`/considerTransient, no closest-goal tracking, no suffix fallback, no post-splice optimize. Called from `world_tick/movement.rs:244-253` when `is_blocked_and_stuck` or `num_frames_blocked>60`.

## Evidence
hq-hsw04 closed "never patchPath" by adding this thinner residual. Occupancy-aware suffix scan is a remaining leftover-right/live-wrong gap.

## Player-visible
A stuck unit whose remaining waypoints sit on parked allies (statically passable cells) is re-patched straight through the occupants and keeps colliding. C++/leftover splice onto nodes past the occupied stretch.
close_reason: patch_path binds the stuck mover, refreshes occupancy, skips allyFixed/enemyFixed suffix nodes with ±2 transient relaxation, closest-goal + suffix fallback, then optimize. movement.rs passes objects+id.

title: [Physics] Stun cliff/water kill has no AIUpdateInterface gate
description:
## C++
`PhysicsBehavior::testStunnedUnitForDestruction` (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1764-1793): after upside-down (`Get_Z_Vector().Z < 0`) and off-map kills, `AIUpdateInterface *aiInt = obj->getAI(); if (!aiInt) return;`. Cliff (`isCliffCell && !hasLocomotorForSurface(CLIFF)`) and water (`isUnderwater && !hasLocomotorForSurface(WATER)`) kills run only for AI-driven units. AI-less debris/props/crates keep tumbling.

## Leftover (right)
`test_stunned_unit_for_destruction` (GameLogic/src/object/behavior/physics_bounce.rs:91-108): `let Some(ai) = obj.get_ai() else { return; }` before cliff (:101-104) and water (:105-108). Matches C++.

## Live (wrong)
`Object::test_stunned_unit_for_destruction` (Main/src/game_logic/object/physics_motion.rs:968-990) has no AI gate. `ensure_locomotor_surfaces` (:953-957) stamps a template-name default (GROUND for anything not aircraft/hover/amphib/ship), then cliff (:983-985) and water (:987-989) always fire. Called on every successful bounce from `tick_physics_motion_step` and `handle_shock_ground_bounce`.

`apply_shock_wave_impulse` (object/physics.rs:96-140) stuns every eligible non-structure/non-projectile body, including AI-less OCL debris. Shockwave-stunned debris/props landing on a cliff or water cell are destroyed on first bounce; C++/leftover leave them alive (they still get upside-down/off-map kills).

Not a duplicate of hq-ugu06 (Object::kill Die pipeline) or hq-7vpd (handleBounce never called the test).

## Evidence
C++ PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1777-1793. Leftover physics_bounce.rs:91-108. Live physics_motion.rs:953-990, object/physics.rs:96-140.
close_reason: Live test_stunned_unit_for_destruction now returns after upside-down/off-map unless leftover thing-factory AIUpdate (or mobile combat fallback) exists, matching C++ getAI() gate so stunned debris/crates keep tumbling on cliff/water.

title: [Save] CHUNK_GameState header campaign side/mission never from CampaignManager
description:
## C++
`GameState::xfer` (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/System/SaveGame/GameState.cpp:1614-1640) refreshes the v2 header on save from `TheCampaignManager`: if a campaign is current, `campaignSide = campaign->m_name` and `missionNumber = getCurrentMissionNumber()` (0-based); otherwise empty string + `CampaignManager::INVALID_MISSION_NUMBER`. `populateSaveGameListbox` shows those fields as the faction/mission columns.

## Leftover (right)
`Common/src/system/SaveGame/game_state.rs:1269-1280` on Save mode calls `notify_get_campaign_snapshot()` and writes that campaign side + mission number, else clears / `INVALID_MISSION_NUMBER`. Score-screen leftover mission-save uses this path.

## Live
`cnc_game_engine/host_authority.rs:1032-1041` `build_save_info` hardcodes `campaign_side = Some(local_team_name)` for every save (including skirmish/LAN) and `mission_number = None`. `save_file.rs:205-211` `write_cpp_game_state_header` then writes that team name + `INVALID_MISSION_NUMBER`. CHUNK_Campaign itself is captured/restored separately (`write_campaign_block` / `capture_campaign_manager_runtime`) — only the list-header metadata is wrong.

## Player-visible
Save-load list (`ui/save_load_menu.rs:666-670`) shows `Faction: <team>` on non-campaign saves (C++ wrote empty) and never `Mission N` for live campaign saves.

## Evidence
C++ GameState.cpp:1614-1640; leftover game_state.rs:1269-1280; live host_authority.rs:1032-1041 and save_file.rs:205-211.
close_reason: CHUNK_GameState v2 header campaign side/mission now from CampaignManager (empty + INVALID when no campaign). Save list no longer invents a faction label on skirmish saves.

title: [Parachute] Empty chute never dies mid-air after losing rider
description:
C++ `ParachuteContain::update` (`ParachuteContain.cpp:411-413`): "If we have lost our passenger for whatever reason, die early. Otherwise we just sit around forever." `if (getContainCount() == 0) getObject()->kill();` — altitude-independent, before the water-slop check.

Leftover `ParachuteContain::update` (`parachute_contain.rs:853-855`) is the same unconditional empty-count kill.

Live `tick_eject_parachute_residual` (`saboteur_car_bomb.rs:573-622`) destroys `AmericaParachute` only in the `is_chute && landed` ground-contact branch (C++ `onCollide(null)` land dump). There is no mid-air `containCount==0` kill. A riderless chute keeps freefalling, stays alive, and remains a `KINDOF_PARACHUTE` AntiParachute target until it hits the ground.

Retail authors the object (`AmericaParachute` via `OCL_EjectPilotViaParachute`, paradrop `PutInContainer`, hijacker airborne eject). Player-visible: shoot the parachuting rider (not the chute) mid-air — C++ empty chute dies immediately; live ghost chute drifts down as a hittable decoy.

Not a duplicate of closed hq-motc / hq-hq5fm / hq-i4xch / hq-fnz14 / hq-cxdch / hq-14d7 (other parachute legs). Wave15 left this unfiled as "narrow"; leftover is right and live is still wrong.
close_reason: Live tick_eject_parachute_residual now matches C++ ParachuteContain::update / leftover parachute_contain.rs:853-855: after occupant sweep, containCount==0 kills AmericaParachute mid-air (altitude-independent, HELD skips). Land dump still releases riders; empty-count kill covers land and rider-loss.

title: [Locomotor] Live lift/SpeedLimitZ bind undoes leftover per-frame units
description:
## C++
`INI::parseAccelerationReal` (INI.cpp:1717-1724) stores Lift/LiftDamaged as dist/sec² ÷ 900 = dist/frame². `INI::parseVelocityReal` (INI.cpp:1710-1716) stores SpeedLimitZ as dist/sec ÷ 30 = dist/frame. `calcLiftToUseAtPt` (Locomotor.cpp:2022-2110) mixes those with `TheGlobalData->m_gravity` (also parseAccelerationReal, retail -64/900). `handleBehaviorZ` applyMotiveForce is per-frame Euler.

## Leftover (right)
Common `ini_locomotor.rs:527-537` stores Lift/LiftDamaged `/900`. `ini_bridge.rs:93-94` copies lift as-is (already per-frame²). `ini_bridge.rs:108-112` applies `parse_velocity_real` (÷30) to SpeedLimitZ. Leftover `calc_lift_to_use_at_pt` (`maintain.rs:552-605`) is all-per-frame², matching C++.

## Live (wrong)
`host_locomotor_binding_from_template` (`locomotor_bootstrap.rs:900-906`):
- `max_lift = t.lift * FPS * FPS` — Common already stored `/900`, so this inflates back to per-sec² and writes that into the per-frame lift channel.
- `speed_limit_z = t.speed_limit_z` — Common stores raw dist/sec; leftover bridge ÷30 is never applied.

`Object::calc_lift_to_use_at_pt` (`object/physics.rs:1019-1063`) then mixes:
- `max_lift` (per-sec², ~900× too large)
- `leftover_loco_gravity()` (`physics.rs:122, 1768-1785` = retail -64/900 per-frame²)
- `speed_limit_z` (per-sec compared as if per-frame)

`apply_surface_relative_lift` (`physics.rs:654-657`) applyMotiveForce + the Z Euler (`world_tick/physics.rs`) are dt-less per-frame. Every INI-bound hover/wings aircraft has ~900× lift vs gravity and a 30× SpeedLimitZ cap miss. Tests that set `max_lift = 5.0` by hand do not catch the bind.

Not a duplicate of hq-rqv8 (leftover Common converters; leftover GameLogic bridge is already right) or hq-ygdfb/hq-ryf26/hq-2e10h (lift *path*, not unit scale).

## Evidence
C++ INI.cpp:1710-1724, Locomotor.cpp:428-437, 2022-2110. Leftover ini_locomotor.rs:527-574, ini_bridge.rs:93-112, maintain.rs:552-605. Live locomotor_bootstrap.rs:900-906, 953-955; object/physics.rs:1019-1063, 1768-1785.
close_reason: host_locomotor_binding_from_template copies Common Lift/LiftDamaged as already-per-frame2 (/900) and applies parseVelocityReal (/30) to authored SpeedLimitZ, matching leftover ini_bridge.rs:93-112. Omitted SpeedLimitZ stays BIGNUM.

title: [Cave] Occupant death never leaves CaveSystem pool
description:
C++ `Object::onDestroy` (`Object.cpp:720-728`) calls `m_containedBy->getContain()->removeFromContain(this)`. For caves that is `CaveContain::removeFromContain` (`CaveContain.cpp:54-83`): it removes the rider from the CaveIndex `TunnelTracker` *before* `onRemoving`, so a dying occupant frees the shared slot and a last-empty team revert can fire.

Leftover `CaveContain::remove_from_contain` (`cave_contain.rs:423-456`) does the same tracker remove then `on_removing`.

Live `process_destroy_list` (`destroy_list_bounty.rs:256-275`) only `remove_occupant`s the entrance's local list and `tunnel_network.record_exit`s GLA tunnels. There is no `cave_system.record_exit` / `index_holding_unit` cleanup on occupant death. Voluntary exit already goes through `exit_cave_unit` (`special_power_flights.rs:1709-1725`) — that is hq-ppun8, already closed. Death, splash, scripts, and bunker-buster force-exit (`missile_defenders.rs:2057-2066`, tunnel-only) leave the dead id in `cave_system.networks[idx].contained`.

Retail INI authors CaveContain + CaveIndex (civilian caves). Player-visible: a killed cave occupant leaks a slot (max 10), LastEmpty never reverts the network team, and later exits still list the corpse.
close_reason: Live process_destroy_list now calls exit_cave_unit (cave_system.record_exit + LastEmpty) on occupant death, matching C++ Object::onDestroy → CaveContain::removeFromContain tracker remove then onRemoving.

title: [Weapon] Frenzy apply keeps higher level and longer expiry
description:
## C++
`TempWeaponBonusHelper::doTempWeaponBonus` (`TempWeaponBonusHelper.cpp:65-83`): if `m_currentBonus != status` it `clearTempWeaponBonus()` first (clears the old `WeaponBonusCondition` + FRENZY tint), then `setWeaponBonusCondition(status)`, `m_currentBonus = status`, `m_frameToRemove = TheGameLogic->getFrame() + duration`. Re-applying the same status only resets the timer. FRENZY_ONE / TWO / THREE are distinct `WeaponBonusConditionType` values, so a later lower-level Frenzy pulse **downgrades** the multiplier and **shortens** the expiry to now+new-duration.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/object/helper/temp_weapon_bonus_helper.rs:100-119` `do_temp_weapon_bonus`: clears a different bonus before applying; same-bonus re-apply sets `frame_to_remove = current_frame + duration`. Tests cover timer reset and fanaticism clearing frenzy.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/game_logic/object/bonuses.rs:29-40` `apply_weapon_bonus_frenzy`: keeps the **higher** level (`if lvl > level` keep) and only **extends** the timer (`if until_frame > current` extend). Overlapping allied Frenzy casts (C++ `WeaponBonusUpdate` ALLOW_ALLIES, live `host_frenzy`) never downgrade 130%→110% and never shorten a longer remaining expiry.

## Evidence
C++ `TempWeaponBonusHelper.cpp:65-73`. Leftover `temp_weapon_bonus_helper.rs:100-119`. Live `bonuses.rs:29-40`. Distinct from closed hq-3ir6n (Allies filter + contained walk).

## Player-visible
Two allied Frenzy casters of different science tiers: a unit already under Frenzy 3 keeps 130% damage for the long timer after a Frenzy 1 pulse. C++/leftover drop to Frenzy 1 and restart the short timer.
close_reason: Live apply_weapon_bonus_frenzy now matches leftover do_temp_weapon_bonus: different FRENZY_* level clears then replaces (downgrade included); same-level re-apply always writes until_frame (shorten included). No keep-higher / keep-longer.

title: [Helix] Nuke bomb unpause maps to NuclearMissile
description:
## C++
Nuke Helix carries `Nuke_SpecialAbilityHelixNukeBomb` (`StartsPaused = Yes`) and `UnpauseSpecialPowerUpgrade` with `SpecialPowerTemplate = Nuke_SpecialAbilityHelixNukeBomb` / `TriggeredBy = Nuke_Upgrade_HelixNukeBomb`. `UnpauseSpecialPowerUpgrade.cpp:67-78` walks `getSpecialPower()` modules and unpauses the matching template. After unpause the ctor-started ReloadTime (10000ms) must elapse before the first drop.

## Leftover (right)
`object/upgrade/unpause_special_power_upgrade.rs:129-176` unpauses by SpecialPowerTemplate name, same as C++. `object/special_power_module.rs` initialize starts recharge then pauses `StartsPaused` modules.

## Live (wrong)
`host_upgrade_module_residuals.rs:150-153` `unpause_power_for_upgrade` maps any upgrade containing `"helixnuke"` to `SpecialPowerType::NuclearMissile`. `object_queries.rs:2573-2588` then unpauses NuclearMissile on the Helix (a power the Helix does not carry).

The power live actually fires is `SpecialPowerType::HelixNukeBomb` (`command_executor/special_power.rs:767-772` / `:1136-1148` gates on `Nuke_Upgrade_HelixNukeBomb`). `power_starts_paused` (`host_upgrade_module_residuals.rs:171-180`) omits `HelixNukeBomb`. `init_starts_paused_special_powers` candidates are only RadarScan / HelixNapalmBomb (`drones_and_garrison.rs:2346-2354`); a name containing `"helix"` also pauses HelixNapalmBomb, which a Nuke general can never unpause.

`host_helix_napalm.rs:110-115` documents the retail pair: `UPGRADE_HELIX_NUKE_BOMB = "Nuke_Upgrade_HelixNukeBomb"`, `HELIX_NUKE_BOMB_SPECIAL_POWER = "Nuke_SpecialAbilityHelixNukeBomb"`. `command_system/special_power.rs:258` already maps that template name to `HelixNukeBomb`.

## Evidence
C++ / leftover match template name. Live name-sniff sends the unpause to NuclearMissile. HelixNukeBomb is never StartsPaused, so `queue_helix_napalm_bomb` becomes legal the instant the upgrade is owned — no 10s reload.

## Player-visible
Researching Nuke Helix bomb lets the first drop fire immediately (C++ waits ReloadTime). The intended unpause never hits HelixNukeBomb.
close_reason: Live unpause_power_for_upgrade maps Nuke_Upgrade_HelixNukeBomb to HelixNukeBomb (not NuclearMissile). power_starts_paused and init_starts_paused name-sniff a Nuke Helix onto HelixNukeBomb so ctor start+pause + upgrade unpause match leftover UnpauseSpecialPowerUpgrade template-name walk.

title: [SpecialPower] StartsPaused unit init double-pauses so upgrade never arms
description:
## C++
`SpecialPowerModule::SpecialPowerModule` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/SpecialPower/SpecialPowerModule.cpp:76-101`) for a pre-built object calls `startPowerRecharge()` (non-SharedNSync) **then** `pauseCountdown(TRUE)` when `StartsPaused`. `UnpauseSpecialPowerUpgrade::upgradeImplementation` (`UnpauseSpecialPowerUpgrade.cpp:67-78`) matches `SpecialPowerTemplate` and calls `pauseCountdown(FALSE)` once. Unpause slides `availableOnFrame` by the paused duration, so the first fire still waits the authored ReloadTime (capture 15000ms, RadarVanScan 30000ms, HelixNapalm 10000ms).

Retail Object INI: Ranger/Rebel/RedGuard `SpecialAbility` + `StartsPaused = Yes` + `UnpauseSpecialPowerUpgrade TriggeredBy = Upgrade_InfantryCaptureBuilding`. Same pattern for `SpecialPowerRadarVanScan` / `Upgrade_GLARadarVanScan` and `SpecialAbilityHelixNapalmBomb` / `Upgrade_HelixNapalmBomb`.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/object/special_power_module.rs` `initialize` (`:204-216`): `start_power_recharge_at` then `pause_countdown(true)` for `starts_paused`. `object/upgrade/unpause_special_power_upgrade.rs` unpauses the matching template once.

## Live (wrong)
Two pause paths on every `create_object`:

1. `world_combat/drones_and_garrison.rs:2218` / `:2341-2359` `init_starts_paused_special_powers` pauses capture / RadarScan / HelixNapalmBomb **without** `start_power_recharge_with_frames` (only HDB at `:2324-2335` starts recharge first).
2. Then `create_destroy_die.rs:2226-2229` → `apply_create_modules_on_build_complete` → `production_eva.rs:1289-1318` `on_structure_superweapon_creation` walks parsed `special_power_modules` (includes `SpecialAbility`, `special_power.rs:274-280`) and does start-recharge **then pause again**.

`pause_special_power_countdown` is a refcount (`object/orders.rs:85-103`). Retail INI units therefore sit at pausedCount=2. `object_queries.rs:2554-2588` unpauses once on upgrade → still paused. Capture / RadarVanScan / Helix napalm never arm after research.

Name-sniff templates without `special_power_modules` only hit path 1: unpause leaves rem=0 (instant first fire). `world_tests/projectiles_air.rs:7-40` encodes that instant-ready as expected; it is not C++.

## Evidence
C++ ctor order `startPowerRecharge` then `StartsPaused`. Leftover `initialize` matches. Live comments at `drones_and_garrison.rs:2299` admit recharge-before-pause but the capture/radar/helix loop never starts recharge, and SpecialPowerCreate then pauses a second time.

## Player-visible
After researching Capture / Radar Van Scan / Helix Napalm, the button stays disabled (retail INI double-pause) or fires immediately with no ReloadTime (name-sniff path). C++ waits the authored reload after unpause.
close_reason: init_starts_paused now matches leftover SpecialPowerModule initialize: startPowerRecharge then pauseCountdown once. on_structure_superweapon_creation only re-pauses when has_special_power_create (C++ SpecialPowerCreate). Capture/Radar/Helix unpause leaves authored ReloadTime instead of pausedCount=2 or rem=0.

title: [Shroud] Object FOW mix reads square looker cells not DiscreteCircle
description:
C++ `PartitionManager::doShroudReveal` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/PartitionManager.cpp:3937-3956`) walks a `DiscreteCircle` of `worldToCellDist(radius)` (min 1) and `hLineAddLooker`s those cells. `PartitionData::getShroudedStatus` (`:1615-1674`) then mixes object FOW from those same DiscreteCircle cells.

Leftover `ShroudManager::do_shroud_reveal` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/system/shroud_manager.rs:486-509`) matches C++: `world_to_cell_dist` + `DiscreteCircle` + horizontal looker lines. Live look already stamps that grid (`spawn_templates.rs` `restamp_host_partition_look` → `shroud_mgr.do_shroud_reveal`). Radar overlay / `refresh_shroud_for_local_player` also read leftover ShroudManager.

Live object FOW mix does not. `update_main_crate_vision` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/spawn_templates.rs:4530-4552`) samples `partition_cell_shroud_status`, which prefers leftover `PARTITION_MANAGER` (`partition_data.rs:145-165`). That grid is painted by `PartitionShroudGrid::reveal_circle` (`partition_shroud.rs:137-163`): a square `±ceil(radius/40)` walk with world-space cell-center `r²` reject — not DiscreteCircle. Live also stamps that square grid via `stamp_partition_cell_lookers`.

Player-visible: object Clear/Fogged/Shrouded (drawable hide, radar blip `getShroudedStatus > PARTIAL_CLEAR`, stealth IR, FX gates) uses the square looker disk, while the minimap/terrain overlay uses leftover DiscreteCircle. Units on the rim of vision can be visible in one and fogged in the other. Same class as closed hq-rt74q (value/threat square falloff), but looker/object FOW was never filed.

Not leftovers-only: leftover ShroudManager DiscreteCircle is already on the live look path. Live mix queries the leftover-wrong square grid instead.
close_reason: Live object FOW mix now samples leftover ShroudManager DiscreteCircle looker cells instead of PARTITION_MANAGER square r2 disk.

title: [Locomotor] Wheeled MinTurnSpeed floor uses reduced speed not maxSpeed
description:
## C++
`Locomotor::moveTowardsPositionWheels` (Locomotor.cpp:1260-1286, 1316-1323):
- `maxSpeed = getMaxSpeedForCondition(bdt)` — damage-condition constant.
- `turnSpeed = m_minTurnSpeed; if (turnSpeed < maxSpeed/4) turnSpeed = maxSpeed/4;`
- Then `|relAngle| > PI/20` clamps `desiredSpeed` down to that **fixed** floor.

The floor is not lowered when `desiredSpeed` is already cut by group speed, blocked-wait `bumpSpeedLimit`, or approach braking. A truck approaching dest at 8 with maxSpeed 40 / MinTurnSpeed 0 still has floor 10; 8 < 10 so no extra clamp.

## Leftover (right)
`move_towards_position_wheels_physics` (GameLogic/src/locomotor/core_impl/move_ground.rs:126, 131, 139-142): `max_speed = get_max_speed_for_condition(condition)` then `if turn_speed < max_speed / 4.0 { turn_speed = max_speed / 4.0; }`. Matches C++.

## Live (wrong)
`update_movement` (Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/movement.rs:712-718):
```
let mut turn_speed = obj.min_turn_speed;
if turn_speed < speed / 4.0 { turn_speed = speed / 4.0; }
if delta.abs() > PI/20 && speed > turn_speed { speed = turn_speed; }
```
`speed` is already `effective_max_speed()` after `apply_do_locomotor_blocked_speed` (movement.rs:548) and `apply_cpp_approach_brake` (movement.rs:660-666). The same collapsed floor is fed into the 15° look-ahead probe (movement.rs:739-749).

Same reduced-speed floor is in test-only `Object::update_movement` (object/update.rs:~306-313). Live `wheeled_turn_factor` (object/physics.rs:433-446) correctly floors at `effective_max_speed()/4` — only the march SMALL_TURN clamp is wrong.

## Player-visible
Wheeled units with authored MinTurnSpeed < maxSpeed/4 (typical: omitted MinTurnSpeed = BIGNUM is fine; many trucks use 0 or a small value) crawl ~4× slower through every >9° turn while already slowed (approach-brake near dest, formation `group_speed_factor`, blocked bump cap). Example: max 40, MinTurnSpeed 0, braked to 8 → C++ floor 10 (no clamp) vs live floor 2 (clamps to 2).

Not a duplicate of hq-2rfrw/hq-glk4v (turnFactor on rotate) or hq-rqv8 (INI unit conversion).

## Evidence
C++ Locomotor.cpp:1260-1286, 1316-1323. Leftover move_ground.rs:126-142. Live movement.rs:548, 660-666, 712-718, 739-749.
close_reason: wheeled_turn_speed_floor uses damage-condition effective_max_speed()/4 not the already-reduced desiredSpeed, matching leftover move_ground.rs:126-142 and C++ Locomotor.cpp:1283-1323. Wired in movement.rs march and test-only update.rs.

title: [Hunt] PLAYER_HUNT never leaveGroup before aiHunt
description:
C++ Player::setUnitsShouldHunt (Player.cpp:1979-2019) sets m_unitsShouldHunt, then for every team-prototype instance member that is not KINDOF_DOZER/HARVESTER/IGNORES_SELECT_ALL: obj->leaveGroup() then aiHunt/aiIdle if AIUpdateInterface exists. leaveGroup drops the current AIGroup/selection so units hunt independently and later group orders on the old group do not cancel hunt.

Leftover Player::set_units_should_hunt (player/production.rs:172-228) matches: KindOf skip, leave_group(), then ai_hunt/ai_idle. Leftover do_player_hunt queues HostScriptHuntGuardRequest::PlayerHunt when OBJECT_REGISTRY is empty.

Live PlayerHunt drain (scripts_camera.rs:1707-1738) sets units_should_hunt and unit_command_patrol on every owned non-dozer/harvester/ignores-select-all unit. unit_command_patrol (unit_commands.rs:973-1006) stamps player command source and Patrolling/hunting but never leaveGroup / clear formation_id. Units stay in the prior AIGroup/formation, so a later group move on that group yanks them off map-wide hunt.

Evidence: C++ Player.cpp:2008 leaveGroup; leftover production.rs:218 leave_group; live unit_command_patrol has no leaveGroup/formation clear.
close_reason: Live PlayerHunt drain now leaveGroup (clear formation_id + leftover Object::leave_group) before unit_command_patrol, matching C++ Player::setUnitsShouldHunt / leftover set_units_should_hunt.

title: [Hunt] TEAM_HUNT_WITH_COMMAND_BUTTON skips command-type gate and template-falls-back
description:
C++ ScriptActions::doTeamHuntWithCommandButton (ScriptActions.cpp:2003-2147) first findCommandButton(ability); if NULL return. Then switch command type: allow SPECIAL_POWER only with COMMAND_OPTION_NEED_OBJECT_TARGET, plus SWITCH_WEAPON / FIRE_WEAPON / HIJACK / CARBOMB / SABOTAGE. HACK_INTERNET, GUARD, CONSTRUCT, and every other GUI command hit default, append the debug error, and return before any unit is armed. No template-name fallback.

Leftover command_button_is_hunt_capable (actions_team_command.rs:126-165) ports that switch. The dual-world path queues HostScriptHuntGuardRequest::TeamHuntWithCommandButton without re-checking type; the live drain must apply the same gate.

Live host_script_team_hunt_with_command_button (scripts_camera.rs:3317-3335) only checks unit_can_team_hunt_with_command_button (AI + command-set + CommandButtonHuntUpdate — hq-02k1a). start_command_button_hunt_named (crates.rs:170-203) then hunt_mode_from_button_name (name-sniff) and, on miss, hunt_mode_from_template: any template containing \"hacker\"/\"ranger\"/\"rebel\" becomes SpecialPower. So Command_HackInternet on ChinaInfantryHacker is a C++/leftover no-op but live arms special-power hunt.

Evidence: C++ default reject; leftover command_button_is_hunt_capable; live hunt_mode_from_template fallback after unrecognized button.
close_reason: Live TEAM_HUNT_WITH_COMMAND_BUTTON drain applies leftover command_button_is_hunt_capable (SPECIAL_POWER needs object target; SWITCH/FIRE/HIJACK/CARBOMB/SABOTAGE only). HACK_INTERNET/GUARD/CONSTRUCT no-op. start_command_button_hunt_named no longer template-falls-back when a button name is given.

title: [Team] TEAM_HUNT/GUARD live census uses faction Team not getTeamNamed
description:
C++ ScriptActions::doTeamHunt/doTeamGuard (ScriptActions.cpp:1882-1999) resolve TheScriptEngine->getTeamNamed (ScriptEngine.cpp:5933-5969) then iterate that instance (or getTeamAsAIGroup). getTeamNamed returns the calling/condition team, a singleton if active, or the first prototype instance — never every unit on a faction Team.

Leftover do_team_hunt / do_team_guard (actions_victory_team.rs:204-280) uses get_team_by_name / create_ai_group_from_team → TeamFactory::find_team (instance). When the dual-world registry is empty it queues HostScriptHuntGuardRequest with that team name.

Live apply_host_hunt_guard_script_requests (scripts_camera.rs:1668-1691) walks host_script_team_member_ids (scripts_camera.rs:3338-3355). That helper ORs (1) resolve_host_team_name faction aliases (teams.rs:534-548 strips a leading \"team\" so \"teamAmerica\" → USA), (2) team_instance_name, (3) obj.team.get_name(). TEAM_HUNT/GUARD/TEAM_HUNT_WITH_COMMAND_BUTTON on the default team therefore orders every USA/China/GLA unit, including other scripted squads C++ would leave alone.

Evidence: C++ getTeamNamed first-instance; leftover find_team; live resolve_host_team_name(\"teamAmerica\")==USA plus faction OR in host_script_team_member_ids.
close_reason: TEAM_HUNT/GUARD/TEAM_HUNT_WITH_COMMAND_BUTTON drain now censuses leftover TeamFactory::find_team members then live team_instance_name. No resolve_host_team_name faction OR, so teamAmerica no longer hunts every USA unit.

title: [Save] OpenContain which_exit_path never persisted
description:
## C++
`OpenContain::xfer` (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Contain/OpenContain.cpp:1574-1741) is version 2: UpdateModule base, contain list, player-who-entered, load/unload sound frames, `m_stealthUnitsContained`, `m_doorCloseCountdown`, condition flags, fire-point matrices/indexes, rally, enter/exit map, then `xferInt(&m_whichExitPath)` (line 1735). `m_whichExitPath` cycles 1..n when `numberOfExitPaths > 1` (`OpenContain.cpp:944-952`, `1063-1071`) so successive riders use `ExitStart01` / `ExitStart02` / … bones instead of piling on one door.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/object/contain/open_contain.rs` Snapshotable xfer (`:2581-2698`) writes the same table including `xfer_int(&mut self.which_exit_path)` (`:2692`). Default is 1 (`:658`). Tests round-trip `which_exit_path = 3`.

## Live
Host stores the cycle on `Object.which_exit_path` and `BuildingData.which_exit_path` (`Main/src/game_logic/object/mod.rs:1423-1424`, `buildings.rs:80`). `world_combat/drones_and_garrison.rs:1551-1574` reads that field and advances it via `open_contain_exit_path` on every non-garrison unload. `transport_exit_persist.rs` (hq-nkntu) writes only `frame_exit_not_busy`. Lifecycle envelope / ObjectSnapshot / persist_v18 never mention `which_exit_path`. Restore constructs a fresh Object (default 0) so the next rider always consumes ExitStart01.

## Player-visible
Save mid-unload of a multi-exit transport (Chinook, Sling, Combat Chinook, factories with numbered ExitStart bones). After load, remaining riders all walk out of the first door bone instead of continuing the 1..n cycle.

## Evidence
C++ OpenContain.cpp:1735; leftover open_contain.rs:2692; live drones_and_garrison.rs:1551-1574; transport_exit_persist.rs:28-31 (TXEB payload is object_id + frame only).
close_reason: Persist OpenContain which_exit_path via OXOB object_xfer suffix onto Object.which_exit_path. Restore writes the 1..n cycle only and never re-runs exitObjectViaDoor.

title: [Locomotor] Live path-raise kills 2x IS_BRAKING latch
description:
## C++
`Locomotor::locoUpdate_moveTowardsPosition` (Locomotor.cpp:980-992) is a single raise:

```
if (dist > onPathDistToGoal) {
    if (!obj->isKindOf(KINDOF_PROJECTILE) && dist > 2*onPathDistToGoal)
        setFlag(IS_BRAKING, true);
    onPathDistToGoal = dist;
}
```

When Euclidean 2D to the goal is more than twice remaining `onPathDistToGoal` (off-path / underestimated path remainder), C++ latches `IS_BRAKING` **before** raising the distance. Appearance movers then apply `braking_factor` even though the raised `onPath` is now larger than `slowDownDist`. Next frame `OBJECT_STATUS_BRAKING` pose-cheats toward dest (Locomotor.cpp:1092-1138). Physics skips XY while braking (PhysicsUpdate.cpp braking gate).

## Leftover (right)
`loco_update_move_towards_position` (GameLogic/src/locomotor/core_impl/move_dispatch.rs:74-83) matches C++: one `if dist_2d > on_path_dist_to_goal` that sets `FLAG_IS_BRAKING` when `dist_2d > 2.0 * on_path_dist_to_goal` (non-projectile), then assigns `on_path_dist_to_goal = dist_2d`. No invented pre-raise.

## Live (wrong)
`update_movement` (Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/movement.rs:619-630) splits the raise into two steps:

1. Invented `PATHFIND_CLOSE_ENOUGH = 1.0` pre-raise: if `dist > on_path_dist && on_path_dist > 1.0` then `on_path_dist = dist`. C++ Locomotor.cpp:980-992 has no such gate.
2. Then the C++ 2× latch: `if dist > on_path_dist { if !projectile && dist > 2.0 * on_path_dist { is_braking = true } }`.

After step 1, `dist == on_path_dist` whenever remaining path > 1.0 (every real path). Step 2 never fires. Off-path units keep full motive; `apply_cpp_approach_brake` sees the raised `on_path` above `slowDownDist` and also refuses to latch. They overshoot / take a wide turn instead of slamming brakes and cheating toward dest.

Not a duplicate of hq-7f4ct (NoSlowDown un-latch after far-from-goal clear) or hq-nj3s7 (approach-brake used lead-point not distAlongPath).

## Evidence
C++ Locomotor.cpp:980-992. Leftover move_dispatch.rs:74-83. Live movement.rs:619-630 (PATHFIND_CLOSE_ENOUGH pre-raise then dead 2× check).
close_reason: Removed invented PATHFIND_CLOSE_ENOUGH pre-raise. raise_on_path_dist_to_goal is the C++ single raise (Locomotor.cpp:980-992 / leftover move_dispatch.rs:74-83): latch IS_BRAKING when dist>2*on_path then raise. Far-clear stays only before the raise.

title: [Contain] Chinook Forbid HUGE_VEHICLE fail-closes all Enter
description:
C++ `OpenContain::isValidContainerFor` (`OpenContain.cpp:856-866`) + `TransportContain::isValidContainerFor` (`TransportContain.cpp:136-193`) apply `AllowInsideKindOf` / `ForbidInsideKindOf` as KindOf masks. Retail `AmericaVehicleChinook` / `AirF_AmericaVehicleChinook` author `AllowInsideKindOf = INFANTRY VEHICLE` and `ForbidInsideKindOf = AIRCRAFT HUGE_VEHICLE`. Infantry and ordinary vehicles board; only aircraft and huge vehicles (Overlord/Helix) are rejected.

Leftover `OpenContain::is_valid_container_for` (`open_contain.rs:838-858`) uses the same mask algebra. Infantry and Humvees remain valid riders; aircraft are forbidden.

Live `spawn_templates::parse_admission` (`spawn_templates.rs:1196-1208`) treats any forbid token other than INFANTRY/VEHICLE/AIRCRAFT/STRUCTURE/PORTABLE_STRUCTURE as `ContainAdmission::Unsupported`. `HUGE_VEHICLE` hits that default. `seed_asset_definition_templates` then writes that admission onto existing starter Chinooks (`spawn_templates.rs:3739-3743`). `Object::normal_enter_admission` (`orders.rs:987-988`) returns the parsed admission whenever `contain_module.kind != None`, so the Combat-Chinook `InfantryOrVehicle` fallback never runs. `can_unit_enter_normal_target` (`object_queries.rs:1027-1045`) then rejects every rider, including Rangers and Humvees.

Retail INI authors this path (documented in `host_combat_chinook.rs:12-13`). Player-visible: Chinooks cannot be loaded once Object INI is seeded.
close_reason: Live parse_admission now treats leftover-known Forbid HUGE_VEHICLE as a KindOf mask bit instead of Unsupported. Chinook Allow INFANTRY VEHICLE + Forbid AIRCRAFT HUGE_VEHICLE becomes InfantryOrVehicle; leftover OpenContain algebra rejects only huge vehicles.

title: [Weapon] MissileCallsOnDie remaps victim death instead of missile onDie
description:
## C++
`MissileAIUpdate::detonate` (`MissileAIUpdate.cpp:364-400`) calls `TheWeaponStore->handleProjectileDetonation` then, if `m_detonationWeaponTmpl->getDieOnDetonate()` (`Weapon.ini MissileCallsOnDie` → `WeaponTemplate::m_dieOnDetonate`), applies `DAMAGE_UNRESISTABLE` / `DEATH_DETONATED` / amount=`getMaxHealth()` to the **projectile Object** so its Die modules (`CreateObjectDie`, `FXListDie`, …) run. Victim splash uses the detonation weapon's authored `DeathType`. `getDieOnDetonate()` is never applied to the victim.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/object/update/missile_ai_update.rs:769-781` matches C++: `if weapon.die_on_detonate { obj_guard.attempt_damage(... Unresistable / Detonated / max_health) }` on the missile. `weapon_template.rs` parses `MissileCallsOnDie` onto `die_on_detonate`. Victim `deal_damage_internal` keeps the template `death_type`.

## Live (wrong)
1. `host_die_on_detonate_for_weapon_name` (`weapon_bootstrap/damage_kinds.rs:97-110`) is **seed-only** (`scud+missile`, `tomahawk`, `rocket+buggy|missile`, `stinger+missile`, `patriot+missile`, `inferno+cannon`). It never reads leftover `WeaponStore.die_on_detonate` even though `ini_template_loader.rs:1300-1303` already parses the field onto the store.
2. `Object::fire_at` (`object/attack.rs:414-416`) stamps that seed onto the projectile.
3. Every live detonate/splash path (`combat.rs:1453-1456`, `:1732-1735`, `:1806-1809`, `:2071-2074`, `:2088-2091`) remaps **victim** `death_type` to `HostDeathType::Detonated` when the flag is set.
4. Live never `attempt_damage`s the projectile, so MissileCallsOnDie Die modules never run. Kill-self hold (`missile_kill_self_started_frame`) only delays removal for contrails.

## Evidence
Tomahawk / Scud / Patriot / Inferno / rocket-buggy impacts play DETONATED victim death (wrong anim/FX) instead of authored DeathType. Missile CreateObjectDie / FXListDie never fire. Seed can invent the flag for name-matched weapons whose INI is `MissileCallsOnDie=No`, and miss store-true names the heuristic does not contain.

## Player-visible
Wrong death animations on splash victims; missing missile-death FX/OCL on MissileCallsOnDie weapons.
close_reason: Live die_on_detonate now reads leftover WeaponStore.die_on_detonate (not name seed). Victim splash/direct keep authored DeathType. Detonate queues projectile FXListDie+CreateObjectDie via impact_fx (C++ attempt_damage on the missile). AI fire-spawn/ground-fire stamp leftover store flag.

title: [Shroud] Live look never applies Object::shroud cover
description:
## C++
`Object::handlePartitionCellMaintenance` (`Object.cpp` via `handleShroud`) always `unlook` / `unshroud` / `shroud` / `look`. `Object::shroud` (`Object.cpp:5045-5080`) when `!UNDER_CONSTRUCTION && !dead && getShroudRange() > 0` builds a **non-ally** player mask (`getRelationship(currentPlayer->getDefaultTeam()) != ALLIES`) and `ThePartitionManager->doShroudCover(pos, getShroudRange(), shroudingMask)`. Default `m_shroudRange` is 0 (`Object.cpp:274`). `ActiveShroudUpgrade::upgradeImplementation` (`ActiveShroudUpgrade.cpp:58-65`) is the retail setter: `setShroudRange(m_newShroudRange)` then `handlePartitionCellMaintenance()` so cover applies immediately. Script `MAP_SHROUD_AT_WAYPOINT` (`ScriptActions.cpp:3011-3030`) is a separate dollop (`doShroudCover`+`undoShroudCover`).

## Leftover (right)
`Object::handle_shroud` (`GameLogic/src/object/object_vision.rs:116-120`) is `unlook` / `unshroud` / `shroud` / `look`. `shroud()` (`:270-310`) skips construction/dead/`get_shroud_range() <= 0`, then ORs every non-Allies player (Player relationship vs default team) and `partition.do_shroud_cover`. `ThePartitionManager::do_shroud_cover` (`object/collide/partition_manager.rs:1703-1707`) stamps leftover `ShroudManager`. Leftover `ActiveShroudUpgrade::apply_shroud_upgrade` (`object/upgrade/active_shroud_upgrade.rs:158-168`) calls `set_shroud_range` + `handle_partition_cell_maintenance` (Wave-448 empty-gates on unused dual-world registry).

## Live (wrong)
`update_main_crate_vision` (`Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/spawn_templates.rs:4206-4386`) only restamps **look** / `ShroudRevealToAllRange`. No `do_shroud_cover`, no `vision_last_shroud`, no read of `obj.shroud_range`. `apply_active_shroud_upgrade` (`world_objects/object_ai_combat.rs:416-422`) writes `obj.set_shroud_range` and records residual counters — never `handlePartitionCellMaintenance` / cover. Grep of Main for `do_shroud_cover` / `doShroudCover` / `vision_last_shroud` is empty. Distinct from closed hq-ivv1 (leftover factory register) and hq-pzyzt (looker ally mask).

## Evidence
C++ `Object.cpp:5045-5080` + `ActiveShroudUpgrade.cpp:58-65`. Leftover `object_vision.rs:116-120,270-310`. Live `spawn_templates.rs:4299-4364` look-only; `object_ai_combat.rs:416-422` range-only.

## Player-visible
A unit whose `ShroudRange` is set (ActiveShroudUpgrade / `setShroudRange`) never fogs enemies. Allies keep seeing through the intended cover disk.
close_reason: Live update_main_crate_vision restamps Object::shroud doShroudCover for non-allies when shroud_range>0; ActiveShroudUpgrade calls handlePartitionCellMaintenance equivalent immediately.

title: [EmergencyRepair] Heal uses faction Team, not ALLOW_ALLIES
description:
## C++
`AutoHealBehavior::update` radius path (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Behavior/AutoHealBehavior.cpp:224-232`) heals friendlies with `PartitionFilterRelationship(obj, ALLOW_ALLIES)` + alive + same-map. Retail SuperweaponEmergencyRepair is an OCL that creates `RepairVehiclesInArea_InvisibleMarker_*` with `AutoHealBehavior` KindOf=VEHICLE, SingleBurst, Radius=100, HealingAmount 100/200/300. ALLOW_ALLIES is player relationship (same controller or allied players), not faction identity. 2v2 USA+China heals Chinese vehicles; FFA USA-vs-USA does not heal the enemy.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/object/behavior/auto_heal_behavior.rs:1289-1296` keeps the C++ filter: `healer.get_relationship(&team_guard) == Relationship::Allies`. KindOf / ForbiddenKindOf / damaged / skip-self match the radius scan.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/game_logic/world_combat/heroes_and_plans.rs:2044-2069` `activate_emergency_repair` sets `same_team = obj.team == caster_team` (`Team::USA|China|GLA`). `host_emergency_repair.rs:190-197` `is_legal_emergency_repair_target` then requires that flag. Comment admits "Not full ally relationship filter (uses same-team residual)".

## Evidence
- C++: `AutoHealBehavior.cpp:226` `PartitionFilterRelationship::ALLOW_ALLIES`
- Leftover: `auto_heal_behavior.rs:1296` `rel == Relationship::Allies`
- Live: `heroes_and_plans.rs:2069` `obj.team == caster_team`

## Player-visible
2v2 USA+China Emergency Repair skips allied Chinese vehicles. FFA USA-vs-USA heals enemy USA vehicles (same faction `Team`).
close_reason: Live Emergency Repair now uses PartitionFilterRelationship ALLOW_ALLIES (player_relationship / same controller or allied players) instead of faction Team. 2v2 USA+China heals Chinese vehicles; FFA USA-vs-USA does not heal the enemy.

title: [Pathfind] Live crate path emits cell corners, not leftover adjustCoordToCell
description:
## C++
`Pathfinder::adjustCoordToCell` (AIPathfind.cpp:8936-8946) writes waypoint world coords as:
- `centerInCell` (odd-diameter / infantry): `(cellX+0.5)*PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE`
- else (even-diameter / vehicles): `(cellX+0.05)*PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE`
`prependCells` / `buildActualPath` (AIPathfind.cpp:9006-9063, 8954-8968) emit every intermediate node through that helper. `adjustDestination` (5331-5351) also adds `PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE/2` before `worldToCell` when `!center`.

## Leftover (right)
`pathfind_complete/snap.rs` `adjust_coord_to_cell` matches C++ center vs `+0.05` corner.
`pathfind_complete/occupancy.rs` `build_actual_path_for_object` walks goal→start and calls `adjust_coord_to_cell` for every non-goal node, then prepends unit feet.
`pathfind_complete/check_movement.rs` `adjust_destination_from` applies the half-cell seed before `GridCoord::from_world` when `!center_in_cell`.

## Live (wrong)
`PathfindingSystem::crate_path_to_world` (`Main/src/game_logic/pathfinding.rs` ~5334-5348) maps every A* cell through `grid_to_world` / `grid_to_world_on_layer`, which is cell origin `(origin + cell*size)` — no `+0.5` for infantry, no `+0.05` for vehicles.

title: [Weapon] Live projectiles collide with own structures
description:
## C++
`WeaponTemplate::shouldProjectileCollideWith` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Weapon.cpp:642-735`):
- Intended victim always collides.
- Never the launcher; never `launcher->getContainedBy()`.
- Flame/ParticleBeam skip `OBJECT_STATUS_BURNED`.
- Airfield reserved-space skip; sneaky-offset skip.
- Then builds `requiredMask`. For a structure (`Weapon.cpp:716-721`):
  - same `getControllingPlayer()` as the projectile → `WEAPON_COLLIDE_CONTROLLED_STRUCTURES` (0x0100) — "ONLY structures belonging to the projectile's controller" (`Weapon.h:124`).
  - otherwise → `WEAPON_COLLIDE_STRUCTURES` (0x0004) — "all structures EXCEPT for structures belonging to the projectile's controller" (`Weapon.h:118`).
- Default ctor `m_collideMask = WEAPON_COLLIDE_STRUCTURES` (`Weapon.cpp:272-273`). Omitted `ProjectileCollidesWith` therefore never intercepts the firer's own buildings.

## Leftover (right)
`WeaponTemplate::should_projectile_collide_with` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/weapon/weapon_template.rs:542-677`) ports the same gate: same controlling player → `CONTROLLED_STRUCTURES`, else `STRUCTURES`. Default `collide_mask` is `STRUCTURES` (`weapon_template.rs:214`). Leftover `template.rs:234-262` matches.

## Live (wrong)
`CombatSystem` intervening-structure intercept (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/combat.rs:1531-1594`) runs when `projectile_collides_structures(mask)` (`weapon_bootstrap/collide.rs:71-73`) — any `STRUCTURES|WALLS` bit. It skips shooter, intended victim, launcher container, burned, sneaky, under-construction, and airfield reserved-space — then detonates on **any** `KindOf::Structure` whose footprint contains the projectile. No `getControllingPlayer` / `CONTROLLED_STRUCTURES` test.

Live default seed is `PROJECTILE_COLLIDE_STRUCTURES | PROJECTILE_COLLIDE_WALLS` (`collide.rs:13-15`). Store-parsed `STRUCTURES` (retail default) also enables the intercept.

## Player-visible
Tank / missile / howitzer shells fired across the firer's own War Factory, Command Center, Patriot, or other completed buildings detonate on those buildings and splash the player's base. Retail C++ and leftover pass through unless the weapon authors `ProjectileCollidesWith = … CONTROLLED_STRUCTURES`.
close_reason: Live intervening-structure intercept now skips same-controller buildings unless ProjectileCollidesWith CONTROLLED_STRUCTURES (C++ Weapon.cpp:716-721 leftover should_projectile_collide_with). Neutral/enemy structures still intercept on STRUCTURES|WALLS.

description:

title: [Select] LMB commits selection on press not click
description:

GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/MessageStream/SelectionXlat.cpp:890-898 and :575-587.

:745-800 handle_left_button_up: if not dragging, emits MouseLeftClick at the *up* position.

Live path + behavior:

:1627-1647 handle_left_release: for a point click (within DragTolerance) it explicitly does not re-select — "Press already selected via select_left_click_target" (workaround for closed hq-r5dmm wipe).

close_reason: Point selection commits on non-drag LMB release at the up pixel. RAW LMB down only anchors feedback (SelectionXlat.cpp:890-898 / 575-587).

title: [Cam] Motion-blur follow never sees live scroll delta
description:
## C++
`ScreenMotionBlurFilter::postRender` (W3DShaderManager.cpp:978-989) for `FM_VIEW_MB_PAN_ALPHA*` uses the tactical view's current `scrollDelta` to set pan center and `m_maxCount`. `CAMERA_MOTION_BLUR_FOLLOW` (ScriptActions.cpp:6947-6948) sets that pan mode on `TheTacticalView`. W3DView `scrollBy` writes `m_scrollAmount` that the filter reads the same frame.

## Leftover (right)
`View::scroll_by` (GameClient/src/display/view.rs:946-950) stores `self.scroll_amount = *delta`. `View::filter_composite` (view.rs:1752-1756) passes `scroll_delta: self.scroll_amount` into the live filter blit. `script_camera_motion_blur_follow` (script_action_handler.rs:271-274) sets leftover View pan mode + MotionBlur, matching C++.

## Live (wrong)
`pipeline_execute.rs:345-373` composites leftover `filter_composite()` on the live 3D dest (hq-eb78a). Live camera pan (`mouse.rs` `camera_scroll_world_delta` / local `scroll_amount`) never calls leftover `View::scroll_by` and never stamps leftover `scroll_amount`. Follow/pan blur therefore always sees `(0,0)` while the player scrolls, so `CAMERA_MOTION_BLUR_FOLLOW` is a static overlay instead of a scroll-direction smear.

## Evidence
C++ W3DShaderManager.cpp:978-989; ScriptActions.cpp:6947-6948.
Leftover view.rs:946-950, 1752-1756; script_action_handler.rs:271-274.
Live pipeline_execute.rs:345-373; mouse.rs:2364-2378 (local scroll only).
close_reason: Live camera_scroll_world_delta now stamps leftover View.scroll_amount same-frame so filter_composite / live filter blit see pan delta (C++ W3DView m_scrollAmount + ScreenMotionBlurFilter pan).

title: [Pathfind] Aircraft attack approach skips leftover adjustTargetDestination
description:
## C++
`Weapon::computeAttackLocation` (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Weapon.cpp:2090-2099) places `approachTargetPos` at `getAttackRange()*0.9` along the source→target dir, then:
```
if (source->getAI() && source->getAI()->isAircraftThatAdjustsDestination())
    TheAI->pathfinder()->adjustTargetDestination(source, target, pos, this, &approachTargetPos);
```
`isAircraftThatAdjustsDestination` (AIUpdate.cpp:2388-2408) is HOVER or WINGS (not THRUST).
`Pathfinder::adjustTargetDestination` (AIPathfind.cpp:5428-5487) spirals up to 400 cells; each candidate must pass `checkForTarget` → `checkDestination(..., LAYER_GROUND)` + `weapon->isGoalPosWithinAttackRange` so two Comanches/Helixes do not occupy the same hover cell.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/weapon/weapon_approach.rs:118-144` calls `pf.adjust_target_destination` when `source_snap.adjusts_destination` (from leftover `is_aircraft_that_adjusts_destination` = HOVER|WINGS).
`pathfind_complete/check_movement.rs:727-840` is the C++ spiral + `check_for_target` (`is_destination_valid` + `in_range` = leftover `is_source_object_with_goal_position_within_attack_range`).

## Live (wrong)
`world_tick/shock.rs:695-718` `approach_pos_for_attack` only calls `weapon_bootstrap::compute_approach_target_pos` (pitch_range.rs:157-196) — a geometric standoff. No pathfinder spiral, no `checkDestination`, no `isGoalPosWithinAttackRange`.
`PathfindingSystem` has no `adjust_target_destination`. Live `is_aircraft_that_adjusts_destination` (pathfinding.rs:3034-3044) is used only for goalAircraft landing stamps (hq-0xpfm), not attack approach.

## Evidence
C++ Weapon.cpp:2096-2098 comment: "Adjust the target so that we are not stacked atop another aircraft."
Leftover weapon_approach.rs:118 `if source_snap.adjusts_destination { pf.adjust_target_destination(...) }`.
Live approach_pos_for_attack: only `compute_approach_target_pos(src, target_pos, weapon_range)`.

## Player-visible
Hover/wings aircraft attacking the same victim all fly to the identical 0.9-range point and stack. C++/leftover spiral them onto distinct in-range cells.

Distinct from closed hq-0xpfm (landing LZ goalAircraft), hq-7q7d9 (landing dest radius), hq-lolz2 (ground UNIT_GOAL).
close_reason: Live HOVER/WINGS attack approach calls leftover Pathfinder::adjust_target_destination after range*0.9; live PathfindingSystem destacks claimed hover cells so two Comanches/Helixes do not share a fire position.

title: [Cam] MOTION_BLUR_JUMP snaps live camera immediately
description:
## C++
`ScriptActions::doCameraMotionBlurJump` (ScriptActions.cpp:2906-2938) enables `FT_VIEW_MOTION_BLUR_FILTER`, sets `FM_VIEW_MB_IN_AND_OUT_*`, then `setViewFilterPos(&pos)`. `W3DView::setViewFilterPos` only stores `ScreenMotionBlurFilter::setZoomToPos`. `TheTacticalView->lookAt` runs only if the filter fails to apply.

`ScreenMotionBlurFilter::postRender` (W3DShaderManager.cpp:1014-1021) `lookAt`s the stored pos at blur peak (`m_maxCount>=MAX_COUNT` and `m_doZoomTo && m_zoomToValid`) — after zoom-in, before zoom-out.

## Leftover (right)
`script_camera_motion_blur_jump` (GameClient/src/core/script_action_handler.rs:246-268) matches C++: set MotionBlur + InAndOut mode + `set_view_filter_pos`; `view.look_at` only if `!passed`. Same in the trait impl at 1497-1526.

`scripts_camera.rs:4032-4051` calls leftover `script_camera_motion_blur_jump`, then **always** `request_camera_focus(*position)` for Jump. Camera snaps to the waypoint on the same frame instead of waiting for the blur peak. C++ and leftover never lookAt at action time when the filter applies.

## Evidence
C++ ScriptActions.cpp:2931-2938; W3DShaderManager.cpp:1017-1018.
Leftover script_action_handler.rs:246-268.
Live scripts_camera.rs:4048-4051.
close_reason: MOTION_BLUR_JUMP leftover set filter+pos only; request_cam/lookAt only if leftover !passed. filterPostRender lookAts leftover+live at MAX_COUNT peak (C++ ScriptActions.cpp:2906-2938 / W3DShaderManager.cpp:1014-1021).

title: [Locomotor] Jet/Chinook landing never PRECISE_Z_POS so lift ignores runway Z
description:
## C++
`Locomotor::handleBehaviorZ` SurfaceRelative / Absolute / SmoothHighest (`Locomotor.cpp:2296-2300`, `:2265-2267`) uses `preferredHeight + surfaceHt` unless `getFlag(PRECISE_Z_POS)`, in which case `preferredHeight = goalPos.z`. Lift is then `calcLiftToUseAtPt` + `applyMotiveForce`.

Callers that need a specific altitude stamp the flag:
- `JetTaxiToTakeoff` / `JetTakeoffOrLandingState` (`JetAIUpdate.cpp:259-260`, `:615-616`, `:725-726`, `:975-976`) `setUsePreciseZPos(true)` + `setUltraAccurate(true)` so runway/pad goal Z is the lift target.
- `HeliTakeoffOrLandingState` (`JetAIUpdate.cpp:961-1024`) same pair.
- `ChinookAIUpdate` takeoff/landing (`ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:223-225`) same pair.
- `DeliverPayloadAIUpdate` dive (`DeliverPayloadAIUpdate.cpp:166`) and `MissileAIUpdate` (`MissileAIUpdate.cpp:540`) also set it.

Without the flag, jets stay at authored PreferredHeight (cruise) instead of descending onto the deck.

## Leftover (right)
`lift_relative_to_layer` (`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/locomotor/core_impl/behavior_z.rs:166-168`) replaces preferred+surface with `goal_pos.z` only when `uses_precise_z_pos()`.

Leftover JetAI stamps the flag on both runway and heli paths (`object/update/ai_update/jet_ai_update.rs:774-784`). Leftover Chinook (`chinook_ai_update.rs:1188-1190`), DeliverPayload (`deliver_payload_ai_update.rs:1416-1417`), MissileAI (`missile_ai_update.rs:1088`), and SlavedUpdate (`slaved_update.rs:774`) match C++.

## Live (wrong)
1. Host never stamps `precise_z_pos` outside tests. `apply_host_locomotor_binding` / `choose_good_locomotor_from_current_set` (`object/physics.rs:765`) **clears** it. Jet/heli takeoff-or-landing (`world_tick/airfield.rs:642-643`, `:2310`) only calls `set_ultra_accurate(true)`.
2. `apply_live_handle_behavior_z` (`world_tick/physics.rs:966-993`) is invoked as `apply_live_handle_behavior_z(obj, surface_y, None)` from every `update_movement` site. `apply_surface_relative_lift` therefore never sees a goal Y even if the flag were set.
3. Jet RTB landing (`airfield.rs:2588-2590`) comments the symptom: *"taxi start is first ground contact when the landing path never lowered Y to the deck."* Approach/landing (`:2609-2640`) assigns a path through `update_movement` + `handleBehaviorZ` at PreferredHeight; wheels-down snaps when 2D to runway_start is close.

## Player-visible
Raptor/Aurora/Comanche landing stays at cruise altitude, then snaps onto the taxiway when the 2D runway point is reached (no lift descent onto the deck). Chinook/helipad leftover uses PRECISE_Z + loco lift; live `step_heli_takeoff_or_landing` kinematically lerps `set_position` and never stamps the flag.

## Evidence
Not hq-ryf26 (that was the opposite: live treated *any* goal_y as PRECISE_Z; close required the flag). Flag is never set and goal Y is never fed, so the close left landing altitude unused.
close_reason: Live JetTaxi/Takeoff/Landing and Chinook takeoff/landing now set leftover PRECISE_Z_POS + ULTRA_ACCURATE so handleBehaviorZ lift uses runway/pad goal Z, not cruise PreferredHeight.

title: [Save] Angry Mob spawn roster never persisted
description:
## C++
`SpawnBehavior::xfer` v2 (`SpawnBehavior.cpp:1058-1127`) writes `m_initialBurstTimesInited`, spawn template, `m_oneShotCountdown`, `m_framesToWait`, `m_firstBatchCount`, `m_replacementTimes`, `m_spawnIDs`, `m_active`, `m_aggregateHealth`, `m_spawnCount`. An Angry Mob mid-roster (dead members waiting SpawnReplaceDelay 30000ms) keeps that slave list and replacement schedule across load.

## Leftover
`SpawnBehavior::xfer` (`GameLogic/src/object/behavior/spawn_behavior.rs:1886-1949`) matches that table.

## Live
Stinger hive slaves are already in the lifecycle envelope (`TAG_SPAWN_BEHAVIOR` / `SpawnBehaviorHiveResidual`). Angry Mob is a separate `GameLogic.angry_mobs` registry (`host_angry_mob.rs` `HostAngryMobState`: `member_ids`, `member_count`, `replacement_times`). `construct` / reset clear the registry (`game_logic/construct.rs:255,852`). Snapshot never writes it.

First post-load tick (`world_scripts/angry_mob_aurora.rs:1502-1528`) calls `sync_mobs` which inserts `HostAngryMobState::new` with `member_count=0` and all 10 `replacement_times` due immediately (InitialBurst + ExitDelay), then `apply_due_expands` + `flush_angry_mob_member_spawns` spawn a fresh batch.

## Player-visible
Save a 6-member mob with 4 dead waiting 30s replacements: after load the nexus re-bursts toward 10 new members. Existing member objects (if restored) are no longer in `member_ids`, so DPS/replace/last-member-kills-nexus drift. Duplicate members can appear.

## Why leftover is right / live is wrong
Leftover matches C++ SpawnBehavior xfer. Live hive persist does not cover Angry Mob. The live registry is the authority and is wiped on load.

Not a duplicate of closed hq-vj1vd (Stinger hive roster) or hq-4rctc (exit InitialBurst runtime).
close_reason: Live HostAngryMobRegistry now round-trips on AMOB lifecycle_tail suffix (member_ids, replacement_times, member_count/m_spawnCount). Restore clears then rebinds so mid-roster load keeps slaves and SpawnReplaceDelay.

title: [Save] PowerPlant rods extended state never persisted
description:
## C++
`PowerPlantUpdate::xfer` v1 (`PowerPlantUpdate.cpp:117-131`) writes UpdateModule base plus `m_extended`. An overcharged Cold Fusion / Nuclear plant keeps POWER_PLANT_UPGRADED rods across load. `loadPostProcess` does not re-run `extendRods`.

## Leftover
`PowerPlantUpdate::xfer` (`GameLogic/src/object/behavior/power_plant_update.rs:248-257`) writes the same `extended` bool.

## Live
Live stores `Object.power_plant_rods_extended` + `power_plant_rods_done_frame` (`object/mod.rs:1184-1189`). Overcharge persist (`snapshot/builder.rs:862-908`) restores only `overcharge_enabled` and explicitly skips re-firing the enable path (power_provided already includes the bonus). Rods are never snapshotted (`save_load` has no `power_plant_rods_*`). Restore leaves both fields at construct defaults (`false` / `0`). `update_power_plant_rods` no-ops when `done_frame == 0`.

## Player-visible
Save an overcharged America/China power plant with rods out: after load the plant stays overcharged (energy drain continues) but the rods snap retracted until the player toggles Overcharge off and on.

## Why leftover is right / live is wrong
Leftover matches C++ `m_extended`. Live host owns rod model conditions and drops them on save/load even though overcharge itself is already persisted.
close_reason: Live Object.power_plant_rods_extended + power_plant_rods_done_frame now round-trip on PPRD lifecycle_tail suffix. Restore writes fields only; does not re-fire begin_power_plant_rods_extend or overcharge enable.

title: [Save] CleanupHazard area order never persisted
description:
## C++
`CleanupHazardUpdate::xfer` v1 (`CleanupHazardUpdate.cpp:309-341`) writes UpdateModule base plus `m_bestTargetID`, `m_inRange`, `m_nextScanFrames`, `m_nextShotAvailableInFrames`, `m_pos`, `m_moveRange`. A mid-CleanupArea ambulance keeps the click destination and remaining spray after load.

## Leftover

## Live
Live stores the same order on `GameLogic.cleanup_areas` as `HostCleanupAreaOrder` (`host_cleanup_area.rs:188-214`; `world_combat/heroes_and_plans.rs:1362-1485`). `construct` / reset call `cleanup_areas.clear()` (`game_logic/construct.rs:194,800`). Snapshot / persist suffixes never write the registry (`save_load/snapshot` has no cleanup-area persist). After load `update_cleanup_area_orders` sees an empty order list.

## Player-visible
Save while an ambulance is driving to / spraying a Cleanup Area click: after load the order is gone. Remaining toxin/radiation/mines stay, and the ambulance sits idle until the player re-issues Cleanup Area.

## Why leftover is right / live is wrong
Leftover matches C++ xfer. Live host is the authority for Cleanup Area and drops the live `m_pos` / `m_moveRange` order on save/load.
close_reason: Live HostCleanupAreaOrder registry now round-trips on CLHA lifecycle_tail suffix (caster, dest, move_range, next_shot_frame). Restore replaces orders so mid-CleanupArea ambulance dest resumes.

title: [Shroud] CIA/SatHack spies by faction Team not Player relationship
description:
## C++
`SpyVisionUpdate::doActivationWork` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/SpyVisionUpdate.cpp:178-182`) walks `ThePlayerList`. For each other player it tests `playerToSetFor->getRelationship(player->getDefaultTeam()) == ENEMIES` and then `player->setUnitsVisionSpied(setting, data->m_spyOnKindof, playerToSetFor->getPlayerIndex())`. That is Player relationship against the target's default team, not faction `Team`. `Object::look` (`Object.cpp`) then ORs `m_visionSpiedMask` into `lookingMask` via the same Player relationship. There is no extra `doShroudReveal` disk painted for every same-faction player.

## Leftover (right)
`SpyVisionController::do_activation_work_for_owner` (`GameLogic/src/object/update/spy_vision_update.rs:143-172`) uses `owner.is_enemy_with_player` → `Player::get_relationship == Enemies` (`player/relations.rs:150-153`). Leftover `Player::set_units_vision_spied` (`player/objects.rs:340-381`) then stamps `set_vision_spied_by_player` on the enemy player's owned objects. `Object::look` (`object_vision.rs:185-194` / `vision.rs:137-148`) builds `lookingMask` with `controller_relationship_to_player_default_team` and ORs `vision_spied_mask`. FFA same-faction enemies are spied; scripted cross-faction allies are not.

## Live (wrong)
`GameLogic::activate_cia_intelligence` (`Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/angry_mob_aurora.rs:72-80, 95-100, 158`) and `activate_satellite_hack_spy_vision` (`317-339, 386`) still:
1. Pick "enemies" with `obj.team != team` (faction Team, so FFA USA-vs-USA never spies; scripted USA+China allies are wrongly spied).
2. Build `player_mask` with `player.team == team` and call leftover `ShroudManager::do_shroud_reveal` / `queue_undo_shroud_reveal` for every same-faction player — C++/leftover never do this extra Team FOW disk.

`update_main_crate_vision` already ORs `vision_spied_mask` (hq-91zn6). The leftover-right path is relationship-based `setUnitsVisionSpied` + `Object::look`. Live still uses the Team residual for both victim pick and extra FOW.

## Evidence
- C++: `SpyVisionUpdate.cpp:178-182`
- Leftover: `spy_vision_update.rs:158`, `player/relations.rs:150-153`, `object_vision.rs:185-194`
- Live: `angry_mob_aurora.rs:72-80`, `95-100`, `158`, `317-339`, `386`
- Not a duplicate of hq-u1u9n (RadarVanScan/SpySat looker mask), hq-pzyzt (unit looker mask), hq-erh3x (spy disk radius), or hq-91zn6 (vision-spied moving lookers).
close_reason: Live CIA/SatHack spy units owned by ENEMIES via player_relationship (leftover is_enemy_with_player / C++ getRelationship defaultTeam). Same-faction enemy slots spy; allied same-faction do not. Caster-only player_mask (no same-faction shroud disk).

title: [Victory] killPlayer skips beacons that C++/leftover destroy
description:
## C++
`Team::killTeam` (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/RTS/Team.cpp:2414-2447): beacon template = `getControllingPlayer()->getPlayerTemplate()->getBeaconTemplate()`. Member filter skips effectively-dead objects UNLESS `isEquivalentTo(beaconTemplate)` — beacons stay in the kill list (comment: "beacons are effectively dead, so we need to destroy via a non-kill() method") and non-tech ones get `obj->kill()`.

## Leftover (right)
`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/team/team_actions.rs:54-119` — beacon name from `player.get_player_template().beacon_name`, skip only `destroyed || (effectively_dead && !is_beacon) || !same_team`, non-tech → `kill(Unresistable, Normal)`.

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/presence.rs:230-244` `kill_player_for_victory` — `is_beacon = obj.template_name.to_ascii_lowercase().contains("beacon")` → `continue` (beacon never destroyed), with comment "C++ Team::killTeam skips beacons" which misreads C++.
Live script-side `command_executor/leftover.rs:1237-1252 host_kill_player` DOES destroy beacons (`destroy_object` + `live_beacon_clear`), so the two live killPlayer implementations disagree.

## Effect
A defeated player's placed beacon (minimap marker) survives forever after victory-path elimination.

## Fix
Destroy beacons on the victory kill path the same way leftover/C++ does (template-equivalent beacon, not name-sniff skip).
close_reason: kill_player_for_victory no longer name-sniff skips beacons; Team::killTeam keeps them in the kill list and destroy_object them. host_kill_player shares that path.

title: [Score] Destroy/lost counters skip leftover scoreTheKill gates
description:
## C++
`Object::scoreTheKill` (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Object.cpp:2890-2931): victim playable-side check :2896-2900 and KINDOF_IGNORED_IN_GUI :2903-2905 both return BEFORE `addObjectLost` :2911-2913; relationship != ENEMIES :2915-2917 and controller==victimController :2920-2924 return BEFORE `addObjectDestroyed` :2927. Losses are only ever recorded through scoreTheKill, so killer-less deaths (sell/script destroy) never touch the keeper.

## Leftover (right)
`GameLogic/src/object/object_combat.rs:295-353` replicates the exact gate order (playable side, IgnoredInGui, add_object_lost_obj, Enemies, self-controller, add_object_destroyed_obj).

## Live (wrong)
`Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/destroy_list_bounty.rs` computes enemy_kill :716-725 and score_counts (playable+IgnoredInGui) :726 but they only gate bounty :750-755 and rank skill :760-763. `record_structure_destroyed` :736 / `record_unit_destroyed` :741 fire with only `!under_construction` + KindOf masks; `record_structure_lost` :804 / `record_unit_lost` :806 fire regardless of killer and without the victim gates. The leftover bridge `notify_live_object_destroyed` :768-776 forwards the same over-count into leftover ScoreKeeper shown on ScoreScreen.wnd.

## Effect
Allied friendly-fire kills add +1 Destroyed to the ally's victory-screen totals and +100 each in `calculate_score` (player.rs:1344-1357 subtracts only self-kills). Civilian/IGNORED_IN_GUI victims count as destroyed. Sold/script-destroyed objects inflate Units/Buildings Lost.

## Not a dupe
hq-yzp8o added the gates only for rank skill points. hq-x89dr only aligned KindOf masks. hq-yutaj only the self-exclusion in calculateScore.

## Fix
Apply leftover/C++ scoreTheKill gate order to live destroy/lost counters (and the leftover ScoreKeeper bridge).
close_reason: record_destruction applies leftover/C++ scoreTheKill order: lost only when a killer called scoreTheKill and victim is playable/not IGNORED_IN_GUI; destroyed only for ENEMIES and not self. Leftover ScoreKeeper notify follows the same gates.

title: [Victory] PLAYER_KILL never reaches live host; SP AI resurrect missing
description:
## C++
`ScriptActions::doPlayerKill` (ScriptActions.cpp:2510-2518) → `Player::killPlayer` (Player.cpp:2023-2071): evacuate all team containers, `m_isPlayerDead=TRUE`, `killTeam` (KINDOF_TECH_BUILDING→Neutral default team). In single-player a `PLAYER_COMPUTER` victim is resurrected (`m_isPlayerDead=FALSE; return;` at Player.cpp:2055-2063) BEFORE the local-player control-bar branch and `m_money.withdraw(countMoney())` — campaign AI slots stay alive for later script OCL spawns and keep their cash.

## Leftover (right)
`do_player_kill` (`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/scripting/executor/actions_player_display_camera.rs:133-161`) → leftover `Player::kill_player` (`GameLogic/src/player/production.rs:232-327`) which ports evacuate/mark-dead/kill_team plus `resurrect_sp_ai` early-return before the money withdrawal. No `request_host_*` bridge (unlike do_team_delete/do_team_hunt). Dual-world OBJECT_REGISTRY is empty on the host-only path.

## Live (wrong)
`ScriptActionType::PlayerKill` exists only as an enum token in `Main/src/core.rs:340` — no dispatch anywhere in Main. Both live kill implementations (`host_kill_player` leftover.rs:1197-1256, `kill_player_for_victory` presence.rs:184-276) omit the SP `PLAYER_COMPUTER` resurrect + money-preserve early return and always zero cash.

## Effect
A scripted PLAYER_KILL destroys nothing in the live host world (army + money survive). Campaign scripts that kill an AI slot to clear then respawn fail.

## Fix
Bridge leftover do_player_kill onto the live host (or drain ScriptActionType::PlayerKill) and honor C++ SP computer resurrect before cash wipe.
close_reason: do_player_kill always queues HostScriptPlayerMiscRequest::Kill; live drain calls kill_player_for_victory. SP computer (SinglePlayer + !local + !observer) resurrects before cash wipe.

title: [HUD] GameHUD invents game-started and power-low overlay messages
description:
## C++
`InGameUI::update` (`InGameUI.cpp:1776-1823`) writes `GUI:ControlBarMoneyDisplay` and shows/hides MoneyDisplay/PowerWindow. Low power is EVA (`EVA_LowPower`) plus the W3D PowerWindow fill (`W3DControlBar.cpp` log-scale production vs consumption). There is no `TheInGameUI->message` for "game started" or "power running low".

## Leftover
`ControlBar::update_money_and_power_windows` (`impl_lifecycle.rs:279-350`) formats money/power onto ControlBar.wnd and never queues an overlay toast. Leftover InGameUI has no initialize "Game started" string.

## Live
`GameHUD::initialize` (`Main/src/ui/hud.rs:791-797`) always `add_message("Game started - Good luck, Commander!", Info)`.
`GameHUD::update_resources` (`hud.rs:1095-1103`) invents `hud.message.power_low` / "Power running low - Build more generators!" when `ResourceDisplay::is_power_low` (`power/max_power < 0.3`). `hud_resource_triple` (`apply.rs:438-441`) sets `max_power = power.max(1)`, so the toast fires whenever `local_power == 0`.

## Evidence
C++ money path has no LowPower HUD message. Leftover `update_money_and_power_windows` has no `add_message`. Live: `self.add_message(&message, MessageType::Warning)` after invented 30% gate.

## Player-visible effect
Every match opens with a fake "Game started" HUD line. A 0-power start (or brownout) dumps an invented English warning leftover never shows; retail uses EVA + the power bar color, not this toast.
close_reason: Removed invented GameHUD initialize Game-started toast and update_resources power-low overlay. C++ InGameUI::update only writes MoneyDisplay/PowerWindow; low power stays EVA + PowerWindow fill. Test: game_hud_does_not_invent_game_started_or_power_low_overlay.

title: [HUD] Live command arming invents HUD instruction toasts
description:
