Stops only clear a local `looping_object_audio` HashSet then `continue` (`:495-499`, `:514-518` for `WeaponFireLoopStop`/`AfterburnerStop`) — never leftover `remove_audio_event` / `remove_playing_audio`. Sources: afterburner (`airfield.rs:340-348` queues `AfterburnerStop`), FireSound (`presentation_frame/apply.rs:665-668` `WeaponFireLoopStop`), move/ambient/under-construction (`move_ambient_audio.rs:15-16,94-95` and `production.rs:357-358` `.stopping()`).

## Player-visible
Raptor afterburner, gatling FireSound, SoundMoveLoop, UnderConstruction, and SoundAmbient keep playing after the unit stops/lands/dies. hq-tj04s closed the taxi-timing start; this remaining gap is the leftover TheAudio stop never being called. Not a dupe of hq-d84e (play API, not stop).
close_reason: Drain loop-stop now calls leftover TheAudio.remove_audio_event(handle) / remove_audio_event_by_name. FireSound and afterburner stops pass the playing event name.

title: [Physics] Stun-destruction kill skips Object::kill Die pipeline
description:
## C++
`PhysicsBehavior::testStunnedUnitForDestruction` (`PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1764-1791`) calls `obj->kill()` for upside-down, off-map, cliff-without-CLIFF loco, or water-without-WATER loco. `Object::kill` runs Body/Die modules (wreck, DieMux FX/OCL, scoring).

## Leftover
`physics_bounce.rs:81-108` calls `obj.kill(None, None)` on the same four gates. Unused by the host tick.

## Live
`test_stunned_unit_for_destruction` (`physics_motion.rs:946-968`) calls `kill_from_stun_destruction` (`:971-984`): `health.current = 0`, `status.destroyed = true`, `DeathType::Normal`, host_death_type_log only. No `take_damage_from_typed_death` / `Object::kill`. Distinct from closed hq-vqkzy (KillWhenResting now uses `Object::kill`; this is the bounce stun-kill path).

## Player-visible
Tanks/trucks tossed upside-down or into water/cliffs wink out with no wreck, no DieMux FX/OCL, and no death-weapon — unlike retail `kill()`.
close_reason: Live host: applyMotiveForce(0) on march; recrew gated on ignored_obstacle_id; COM pitch while stunned; stun-destruction uses Object::kill

title: [Physics] CenterOfMassOffset pitch damping skipped while stunned
description:
## C++
`PhysicsBehavior::update` (`PhysicsUpdate.cpp:715-727`) scales `pitchRateToUse` by `sin(remainingAngle)` from `getCenterOfMassOffset()` every frame inside `HAS_PITCHROLLYAW`. Shocked units keep pitch/roll rates, so the COM term is exactly when listing toward nose-up/down happens.

## Leftover
`physics_update.rs:930-941` applies the same `offset` / `remaining_angle.sin()` scale on the YPR pass with no stun early-out. Unused by the host tick.

## Live
`tick_physics_motion_step` (`physics_motion.rs:767-785`) runs the COM scale only when `shock_stun_frames == 0`. The sole stunned YPR pass (`tick_shock_stun_with_countdown` `:1025-1032`) calls `apply_physics_ypr` with raw `shock_*_rate * pitch_roll_yaw_factor` and never multiplies pitch by the COM sine. `apply_shock_wave_impulse` sets rates + stun together, so the live COM block is dead for tossed units.

## Player-visible
Shocked vehicles with authored CenterOfMassOffset (trucks, tanks) tumble with undamped pitch instead of listing toward their heavy end the way retail does.
close_reason: Live host: applyMotiveForce(0) on march; recrew gated on ignored_obstacle_id; COM pitch while stunned; stun-destruction uses Object::kill

title: [AIUpdate] Detected-stealthed idle still auto-acquires without Stealthed bit
description:
## C++
`AIUpdateInterface::getNextMoodTarget` (`AIUpdate.cpp:4499-4515`) on `calledDuringIdle`: if `OBJECT_STATUS_STEALTHED` and `!canAutoAcquireWhileStealthed()` (AAS_Idle_Stealthed / grant), return NULL unless the unit is in a passenger-allowed-to-fire container. DETECTED does not lift the STEALTHED veto. Stealthed Ninjas/Kell after being spotted still do not idle-acquire unless the Stealthed bit is authored.

## Leftover
`object/unit/combat.rs` `can_auto_acquire_now`: if `!auto_acquire_while_stealthed` and `guard.is_stealthed()`, return false. Status STEALTHED only; no DETECTED exception.

## Live
`world_tick/mood.rs` `get_next_mood_target` snapshots `stealthed = o.status.stealthed && !o.status.detected`. The idle STEALTHED bit gate (`AUTO_ACQUIRE_IDLE_STEALTHED`) therefore does not apply once DETECTED is set. A detected stealth unit idle-acquires with only `AutoAcquireEnemiesWhenIdle = Yes`.

Not hq-b2e1t / hq-zgfkq (bits were ignored entirely; those are closed). This is the remaining DETECTED hole.

## Player-visible
Spotted Jarmen Kell / Ninja / stealth fighter on the ground start shooting nearby enemies while still STEALTHED. Retail keeps them from idle-acquiring unless the INI Stealthed token is set.
close_reason: Idle mood STEALTHED veto uses status.stealthed only; DETECTED no longer lifts it.

title: [AIUpdate] Mood scan never applies AttackIgnoreInsignificantBuildings
description:
## C++
`getNextMoodTarget` (`AIUpdate.cpp:4592-4594`) ORs `AI::IGNORE_INSIGNIFICANT_BUILDINGS` when `TheAI->getAiData()->m_attackIgnoreInsignificantBuildings`. `findClosestEnemy` then drops structures that are not `KINDOF_FS` / CountsForVictory. AIData typically enables this so idle auto-acquire (including ATTACK_BUILDINGS) skips civilian huts.

## Leftover
`object/unit/ai_loco.rs` `get_next_mood_target_id` sets `IGNORE_INSIGNIFICANT_BUILDINGS` from AIData. `ai/mod.rs` `find_closest_enemy` skips `KindOf::Structure && !KindOf::CountsForVictory` when the qualifier is set.

## Live
`world_tick/mood.rs` `get_next_mood_target` never ORs `IGNORE_INSIGNIFICANT_BUILDINGS` into flags. `find_closest_enemy` binds `_ignore_insig` and never filters. Non-attacking buildings are already skipped unless `ATTACK_BUILDINGS`, but units authored `AutoAcquireEnemiesWhenIdle = Yes ATTACK_BUILDINGS` still acquire civilian/non-victory structures.

## Player-visible
Idle units with ATTACK_BUILDINGS auto-acquire (or mood scan) lock onto civilian huts and other non-CountsForVictory buildings that retail AI ignores.
close_reason: Mood scan ORs IGNORE_INSIGNIFICANT_BUILDINGS from AIData; find_closest_enemy drops non-FS non-victory structures.

title: [Player] ENABLE/DISABLE unit/base/factory scripts write leftover only
description:
## C++
`PLAYER_DISABLE/ENABLE_UNIT_CONSTRUCTION` call `Player::setCanBuildUnits` (Player.h m_canBuildUnits). `PLAYER_DISABLE/ENABLE_BASE_CONSTRUCTION` call `setCanBuildBase`. `PLAYER_DISABLE/ENABLE_FACTORIES` call `Player::setObjectsEnabled` (Player.cpp:2074-2097) which sets `OBJECT_STATUS_SCRIPT_DISABLED` on matching templates. `Player::allowedToBuild` (Player.cpp:2295-2305) and `Player::canBuild` / `BuildAssistant::canMakeUnit` then refuse structures or units. Campaign maps routinely disable construction at start and re-enable later.

## Leftover (right)
`do_player_disable/enable_unit_construction` and `do_player_disable/enable_base_construction` (GameLogic/src/scripting/executor/actions_player.rs:67-178) write leftover `PlayerList` `set_can_build_units` / `set_can_build_base`. `do_player_disable/enable_factories` calls leftover `Player::set_objects_enabled` (player/economy.rs:663-680) which marks leftover `TheGameLogic` objects script-disabled. Leftover `can_build_template` (player/production.rs:5-12) honors those flags.

## Live (wrong)
Live host `Player.can_build_units` / `can_build_base` (Main/src/game_logic/game_logic/player.rs:1471-1489) are what `allowed_to_build` and the production tick (world_tick/production.rs:557) read. Live `can_make_unit` (ui_production.rs:1473+) never checks leftover PlayerList flags and never checks live `allowed_to_build` either. Unlike money/science, these leftover actions have no `request_host_*` drain (`scripts_camera.rs` has no can_build apply). Campaign ENABLE/DISABLE therefore never stops or starts live production; leftover factory script-disable walks an empty leftover object registry.

## Evidence
Leftover writes: `actions_player.rs:67-178`. Leftover setObjectsEnabled: `economy.rs:663-680`. Live host flags exist but are only set by AI ctor (`apply_ctor_can_build_units`) and save restore — not leftover scripts. Closed hq-hgbrq / hq-v670s / hq-q4mg4 do not cover this script→live cutover.
close_reason: PLAYER_DISABLE/ENABLE unit/base/factory leftover actions now request_host_can_build. Live drain writes Player.can_build_units/base and set_script_disabled on matching host objects. can_make_unit honors allowed_to_build.

title: [BuildAssistant] TECHTREE_MODIFY_BUILDABILITY_OBJECT leftover override never gates live can_make_unit
description:
## C++
`ScriptActions::doModifyBuildableStatus` (ScriptActions.cpp:5037-5045) writes `TheGameLogic->setBuildableStatusOverride(templ, status)` (GameLogic.cpp:4365-4370). `ThingTemplate::getBuildable()` (ThingTemplate.cpp:1392-1398) returns that override before INI `m_buildable`. `Player::canBuild` (Player.cpp:2888-2895) and ControlBar hide (ControlBarCommand.cpp:1118-1121, 1174-1177) both use `getBuildable()`, so campaign `TECHTREE_MODIFY_BUILDABILITY_OBJECT` immediately locks/unlocks production and hides buttons.

## Leftover (right)
`do_techtree_modify_buildability_object` (GameLogic/src/scripting/executor/actions_world.rs:1221-1241) writes leftover `TheGameLogic::set_buildable_status_override`. Leftover `Player::can_build_template` (GameLogic/src/player/production.rs:14-39) reads that override first, then template `BuildableStatus` (`No` / `IgnorePrerequisites` / `OnlyByAi`).

## Live (wrong)
Live `GameLogic::can_make_unit` / `can_make_dozer_construct` (Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/ui_production.rs:1473-1681) never call leftover `find_buildable_status_override` and never consult `ThingTemplate.buildable_status` for IGNORE_PREREQUISITES / NO / ONLY_BY_AI. Live ControlBar hide uses INI-only `human_control_bar_buildable_hidden` (thing.rs:2644-2647). No host drain exists for TECHTREE_MODIFY (unlike money/science `request_host_*`). Campaign scripts that lock a unit type still enqueue on the live host.

## Evidence
Leftover script dispatch: `actions_world.rs:1240`. Leftover canBuild: `production.rs:14-39`. Live can_make_unit body has no `buildable_status` / `find_buildable_status_override`. Closed hq-4wkes only hid INI NO/AI-only buttons; it did not wire leftover GameLogic override into live canMake.
close_reason: Live can_make_unit/dozer_construct and ControlBar hide consult leftover TheGameLogic buildable override first (ThingTemplate::getBuildable). Leftover TECHTREE_MODIFY always writes leftover override by script name and request_host_buildable_status_override; live drain mutates host templates.

title: [HUD] Live strip ignores multi-select CommandSet intersection
description:
C++ ControlBar::addCommonCommands (ControlBarMultiSelect.cpp:46-120) intersects selected objects by slot. Only OK_FOR_MULTI_SELECT commands stay. A selected object with no CommandSet clears the common set. AttackMove is kept if any member contributes it in that slot.

Leftover populate_multi_select_commands_from_sets / sync_multi_select_command_sets_from_presentation (control_bar_multi_select.rs:16-55, impl_portrait.rs:622-728) implement that intersection. apply_to_control_bar (apply.rs:1304-1306) feeds leftover when selected_count > 1. leftover update_context_multi_select (impl_contexts.rs:8-85) then applies getCommandAvailability per member. hq-pwh4 / hq-mhct closed leftover no-op / first-unit fallback.

Live populate_command_set_strip (command_set_strip.rs:12-99) always uses panel.primary_object_id only. unit_command_buttons → apply_presentation_unit_commands never intersects. Selecting a Ranger + Crusader shows the primary unit's full CommandSet (including non-OK_FOR_MULTI_SELECT construct/specials) instead of the common Guard/Stop/AttackMove/etc. slots.
close_reason: Live populate_command_set_strip intersects selected CommandSets by slot (OK_FOR_MULTI_SELECT; AttackMove kept if any member contributes).

title: [HUD] Live command strip flattens CommandSet holes
description:
C++ ControlBar::populateCommand (ControlBarCommand.cpp:283-297) walks MAX_COMMANDS_PER_SET slots. An empty CommandSet slot does winHide(TRUE) on that WND index; later buttons stay in their authored slots. SCRIPT_ONLY also hides in place (303-306).

Leftover ControlBar sync_command_set_from_presentation (impl_portrait.rs:594-600) pushes 14 WND slots via command_from_set_slot, preserving holes. hq-2011 closed leftover populate flattening; leftover WND is now right.

Live command_set_buttons_for (presentation_frame/command_set_strip.rs:287-294) does set.buttons.iter().take(14).flatten() so empty slots disappear. populate_command_set_strip then packs remaining names left and also dedupes by name (77-84). apply_to_game_hud → apply_presentation_unit_commands (apply.rs:574-579, hud.rs:860-880) lays those packed names at start_x + i*(48+4).

A CommandSet with Construct in slot 1 and Sell in slot 14 therefore shows Sell in slot 2 on GameHUD. Leftover WND keeps Sell in slot 14.
close_reason: Live command_set_slots_for keeps 14 WND holes; SCRIPT_ONLY hides in place; apply_presentation_unit_commands preserves slot index.

title: [HUD] GameHUD strip skips leftover getCommandAvailability
description:
C++ updateContextCommand (ControlBarCommand.cpp:788-881) evaluates getCommandAvailability (993-1516) per shown button and applies COMMAND_HIDDEN / RESTRICTED / NOT_READY (inverse clock) / CANT_AFFORD (ALWAYS_COLOR) / ACTIVE (check-like). Gates include MUST_BE_STOPPED, NEED_UPGRADE, NOT_QUEUEABLE, single-use, SCRIPT_UNSELLABLE hide Sell, DISABLED_SUBDUED restrict Sell/Evacuate/Exit, Stop OPTION_ONE, ExecuteRailedTransport dock, special-power in-use / BattlePlan Active / Overcharge Active.

Leftover update_context_command (impl_command_context.rs:129-192) plus leftover_presentation_common_restricted / leftover_presentation_stop_or_rail (impl_presentation_availability.rs:83-143) match those states, including inverse clock and check-like Active. apply_to_control_bar + ControlBar::update (camera_drain.rs) tick leftover WND. hq-kxmwd / hq-sx0f2 / hq-06z4z / hq-n2svx closed leftover WND/presentation.

Live GameHUD strip is a parallel enabled-bool path. populate_command_set_strip only name-heuristics CombatDrop / Capture / Detonate / HackInternet packing / Evacuate / special-power ready, plus upgrade-name / CanMake / apply_host_disabled. apply_host_restrict_a_command_strip (restrict_a.rs:67-77) exists and is never called from populate_command_set_strip. MUST_BE_STOPPED, NEED_UPGRADE option bit, NOT_QUEUEABLE, single-use, SCRIPT_UNSELLABLE, SUBDUED sell/evac/exit, Stop OPTION_ONE, Railed dock, BattlePlan/Overcharge Active, and inverse-clock NOT_READY never reach apply_presentation_unit_commands (hud.rs:860-880 CommandButton.enabled only).
close_reason: Live strip calls leftover ControlBar::leftover_evaluate_named_command (getCommandAvailability) including SCRIPT_UNSELLABLE / SUBDUED / MUST_BE_STOPPED / NOT_READY.

title: [HUD] GameHUD ConstructionPanel invents faction cameos
description:
C++ ControlBar::populateCommand (ControlBarCommand.cpp:246-323) binds CommandSet.ini slots 1-14 only. There is no second faction-heuristic construction grid. Selecting a barracks/dozer/CC shows those CommandSet construct/upgrade/sell buttons in the CommandWindow.

Leftover ControlBar sync_command_set_from_presentation (impl_portrait.rs:555-600) and leftover Main ui/construction_panel.rs populate_from_command_set / show_for_building (construction_panel.rs:501-605) both resolve CommandSet.ini (or command_set_override) and never invent AmericaInfantryRanger/ChinaTankBattleMaster lists.

Live GameHUD ConstructionPanel (ui/hud.rs:337-662) is a parallel invented UI. setup_construction_options / add_infantry_units / add_vehicle_units / add_aircraft_units / add_building_structures pick hardcoded faction cameos from the producer name (barracks/warfactory/airfield heuristic). command_set_override is stored but ignored for the button list. PresentationFrame::apply_to_game_hud → sync_selection_from_presentation (hud.rs:1214-1229) shows this panel whenever UnitDisplayInfo.can_produce. handle_mouse_click (hud.rs:1061-1135) issues QueueUnitProduction / BeginStructurePlacement from those invented cameos. apply_presentation_unit_commands only overwrites the CommandSet strip, not this panel.

Selecting AmericaBarracks therefore offers both the CommandSet strip and a second invented infantry/building grid (including units that CommandSet/science would hide).
close_reason: Live ConstructionPanel populates from CommandSet.ini / command_set_override via leftover command_set_buildable_cameos. Invented faction cameo lists removed.

title: [LookAt] Ctrl+F1-F4 never save camera bookmarks
description:
## C++
`CommandMap.ini` binds `SAVE_VIEW1` to `KEY_F1` + `CTRL` and `VIEW_VIEW1` to `KEY_F1` + `NONE` (host residual `host_rank_ui_residual.rs:602-610` documents the retail English map). `MetaEvent.cpp:56-71` maps those names to `MSG_META_SAVE_VIEW1` / `MSG_META_VIEW_VIEW1`. `LookAtXlat.cpp:550-568` `MSG_META_SAVE_VIEW1..8` calls `TheTacticalView->getLocation` and prints `GUI:BookmarkXSet`. `LookAtXlat.cpp:572-587` `MSG_META_VIEW_VIEW1..8` recalls via `setLocation`.

## Leftover
`look_at_xlat.rs:439-451` `MetaSaveView(slot)` stores `view.get_location()` and posts `GUI:BookmarkXSet`. `look_at_xlat.rs:453-459` `MetaViewView` recalls only when `is_valid()`. Leftover MetaEvent parse (`meta_event_impl/parse.rs:157-172`) emits those messages. No debug-overlay steal.

## Live
`input.rs:221-235` routes Ctrl+F1..F4 to `handle_mapped_key_press` instead of `save_or_recall_camera_view`. `hotkeys.rs:318` `try_dispatch_command_map_remap` looks up CommandMap first, but the match (`hotkeys.rs:1403-1537`) has no `SAVE_VIEW*` / `VIEW_VIEW*` arms (`_ => false`). Fallthrough `hotkeys.rs:493-511` then treats Ctrl+F1..F4 as debug overlay / FPS / path-line residuals. Only F5-F8 Ctrl still save (`input.rs` `save_or_recall_camera_view`). Closed hq-qxulw (pose completeness) and hq-nlckm (generic remaps) do not cover this steal.

## Player-visible
Retail Ctrl+F1..F4 never store bookmarks 1-4. The player gets debug overlays instead of `GUI:BookmarkXSet`. Remapping SAVE_VIEW/VIEW_VIEW in Keyboard Options also never reaches LookAt. Slots 5-8 still save.

## Evidence
C++ LookAtXlat.cpp:550-587; leftover look_at_xlat.rs:439-459; live input.rs:221-235; live hotkeys.rs:318-320,1403-1537,493-511.
close_reason: input.rs routes F1-F8 through CommandMap; hotkeys.rs SAVE_VIEW/VIEW_VIEW remaps; Ctrl+F1-F4 save bookmarks (LookAtXlat.cpp:550-587) instead of debug overlays.

title: [Select] Alternate-mouse next blank LMB deselects after GUI command
description:
## C++
`SelectionXlat.cpp:928-944` RAW LMB-up in alternate mouse deselects only when there is no armed GUI command, no pending place source, and `!getPreventLeftClickDeselectionInAlternateMouseModeForOneClick()`. `GUICommandTranslator.cpp:471-473` sets that flag TRUE when a non-context GUI command (attack-move / guard / etc.) completes, then clears the GUI command. The issuing click is protected because `getGUICommand()` is still non-null on RAW-up; the *next* blank LMB is protected by the one-click flag so the army stays selected. `InGameUI.cpp:2981` also sets the flag when leaving place-build with a source dozer.

## Leftover
`selection_xlat.rs:770-790` `handle_left_button_up` honors `TheInGameUI::get_prevent_left_click_deselection_in_alternate_mouse_mode_for_one_click()`: if set, clear the flag and do not deselect. `message_stream/translators/gui_command.rs:140-143` sets the flag true after completing a non-context GUI command. Matches C++ one-click keep-selection.

## Live
`cnc_game_engine/mouse.rs:522-529` `alternate_mouse_blank_click_deselects` is only `use_alternate_mouse && !shift && !ctrl && !alt`. `handle_left_release` (`:1456-1468`) applies that on the next empty-ground point click with no prevent-flag read. `Code/Main` has zero callers of `set_prevent_left_click_deselection_*`. After attack-move/guard in alternate mouse, the next blank LMB clears the selection; C++/leftover keep it for one click.

## Evidence
Not hq-6r4n3 (classic empty drag, closed). Not leftovers-only: leftover SelectionXlat + GUICommandTranslator implement the C++ flag; live host reimplementation never consults it.
close_reason: Alternate-mouse next blank LMB honors one-click prevent flag after GUI command / leave place-build.

title: [Select] Force-attack pick omits KINDOF_FORCEATTACKABLE
description:
## C++
`SelectionInfo.cpp:227-232` `getPickTypesForContext`: always `PICK_TYPE_SELECTABLE`, and when `forceAttackMode` also `PICK_TYPE_FORCEATTACKABLE`. `SelectionInfo.cpp:312-313` `translatePickTypesToKindof` maps that bit to `KINDOF_FORCEATTACKABLE`. `W3DModelDraw.cpp:3078-3080` stamps the render object collision type so `W3DView::pickDrawable` can hit civ fences / cargo planes that are force-attackable but not selectable (`KindOf.h`: "unit is always attackable via force-attack, even if not selectable"). `SelectionXlat.cpp:427-431` mouseover even hardcodes `getPickTypesForContext(true)` so hover text works on those objects outside force-attack.

## Leftover
`message_stream/translators/flags.rs:61-67` `context_pick_profile` sets `include_force_attackable` when `force_attack_mode`. `message_stream/translators/pick.rs:15-21` and `:159-160` `object_matches_context_pick_profile` / catalog pick accept `KindOf::ForceAttackable` when that bit is set. Matches C++ `getPickTypesForContext(forceAttackMode)`.

## Live
`cnc_game_engine/selection.rs:20-45` `HostContextPickProfile` only stores mines/shrubbery. `host_context_pick_profile` never sets a FORCEATTACKABLE bit. `pick_ray.rs:85-99` `pick_object_id_along_camera_ray` only ranks `presentation_is_selectable` (requires `KindOf::Selectable`) or `presentation_is_attackable` (requires `KindOf::Attackable`). Ctrl+force-attack / hover therefore miss FORCEATTACKABLE-only objects (civ fences, cargo planes) and fall through to ground.

## Evidence
Not hq-bzidj (shrubbery/mines, already closed). Not leftovers-only: leftover pick profile is the C++ port; live host reimplementation dropped the bit.
close_reason: Force-attack/hover pick includes KINDOF_FORCEATTACKABLE via HostContextPickProfile + presentation is_force_attackable stamp.

title: [Physics] Infantry unmanned recrew skips C++ ignored-obstacle gate
description:
## C++
`PhysicsBehavior::onCollide` (`PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1182-1207`) recrews an unmanned vehicle only inside the `ai->getIgnoredObstacleID() == other->getID()` early-return. Any infantry walking into that ignored unmanned husk: `clearDisabled(DISABLED_UNMANNED)`, `setCaptured(true)`, `defect` to the infantry team, `transferObjectName`, `destroyObject` the infantry. A random bump (no ignored-obstacle) continues into bounce / crush, not recrew. Enter/path-into sets the ignored obstacle so the intended walk-in recrews.

## Leftover
`physics_collide.rs:85-107` matches: only when `ai.get_ignored_obstacle_id() == other_id` and infantry + `DisabledUnmanned`. Unused by the host tick.

## Live
`try_physics_collide` (`world_tick/physics.rs:247-264`) returns early on physics `is_ignoring_collisions_with` (different flag), then `try_infantry_unmanned_reclaim` on any infantry + `disabled_unmanned` pair. Host objects have no `AIUpdate::m_ignoreObstacleID` — ignore-obstacle exists only as a pathfinder query (`pathfinding.rs:3813-3938`). `can_execute_infantry_unmanned_recrew` (`object_queries.rs:714-740`) does not require ignored-obstacle.

## Player-visible
Any infantry that touches an unmanned husk (sniped tank, neutron pad) recrews it — including accidental bumps and enemy walk-bys — instead of only the unit that was ordered to Enter / path into that husk.
close_reason: Live host: applyMotiveForce(0) on march; recrew gated on ignored_obstacle_id; COM pitch while stunned; stun-destruction uses Object::kill

title: [Physics] Live march never applyMotiveForce(0) so collide shoves along heading
description:
## C++
`Locomotor::locoUpdate_moveTowardsPosition` (`Locomotor.cpp:1010-1014`) always calls `physics->applyMotiveForce(&nullAccel)` with a zero vector. Comment: the call flags the object as locomotor-driven so collide/friction treat it as driven rather than shoved. `PhysicsBehavior::applyForce` (`PhysicsUpdate.cpp:297-334`) then keeps only the lateral component while `isMotive()`. `applyFrictionalForces` skips forward friction while motive so march speed is not double-damped.

## Leftover
`loco_update_move_towards_position` (`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/locomotor/core_impl/move_dispatch.rs:85-86`) always `physics.apply_motive_force(&Coord3D::new(0,0,0))` before appearance dispatch. Unused by the host tick.

## Live
`GameLogic::update_movement` (`world_tick/movement.rs:176-765`) lerps `movement.velocity` and `set_position` — it never calls `apply_motive_force` / never sets `motive_frames_remaining`. `apply_physics_force` (`object/physics.rs:368-383`) and overlap collide (`apply_overlap_collide_force` → `apply_physics_force`) only strip to lateral when `is_motive()`. Wings idle is the only live path that arms `MOTIVE_FRAMES_RESIDUAL`.

## Player-visible
Marching columns get shoved along their heading when they bump (traffic jams push units through each other) and pick up extra forward friction, so formations smear instead of only sliding sideways like retail.
close_reason: Live host: applyMotiveForce(0) on march; recrew gated on ignored_obstacle_id; COM pitch while stunned; stun-destruction uses Object::kill

title: [Save] Live CHUNK_ScriptEngine still drops leftover ScriptEngine xfer tail
description:
## C++
`ScriptEngine::xfer` (`ScriptEngine.cpp:8812+`, registered as `CHUNK_ScriptEngine` in `GameState.cpp:297`) persists sequential scripts, counters, flags, attack-priority tables, per-object attack-priority sets, end/close-window timers, the named-object tracker, firstUpdate, cinematic fade, completed video/speech/audio/UI lists, per-player triggered/midway/finished special-power and upgrade/science lists, topple directions, breeze info, script difficulty, `freezeByScript`, named reveals, object-type lists, `objectsShouldReceiveDifficultyBonus`, `currentTrackName`, and `chooseVictimAlwaysUsesNormal`.

## Leftover
`XferSnapshot for ScriptEngine` (`GameLogic/src/scripting/engine/leftover.rs:220-667`) is the C++ v6 layout, including those fields. Per-object `is_receiving_difficulty_bonus` is also in leftover `Object::xfer` v5 (`object_xfer.rs:1079-1082`).

## Live
`write_script_engine_block` (`Main/src/save_load/snapshot/persist_v18.rs:1020-1098`) only writes sequential scripts, counters, flags, **empty** attack-priority counts, script actives, and named reveals. `parse_script_engine_block` restores only that subset. No named-object tracker, fade, freeze, timers, breeze, object-type lists, difficulty-bonus flag, music track, or ChooseVictimAlwaysUsesNormal. hq-i98ji closed counters/flags/actives only.

## Evidence
After load, runtime-named units, script attack-priority maps, mid-fade cinematics, `ENABLE_OBJECT_DIFFICULTY_BONUSES`, `ChooseVictimAlwaysUsesNormal`, and script freeze/end-game timers reset.
close_reason: Live CHUNK_ScriptEngine v8 now writes leftover ScriptEngine xfer tail (named objects, fade, freeze, timers, breeze, object types, difficulty bonus, track, ChooseVictimAlwaysUsesNormal, attack priorities) and restore_persist_v18 reapplies it.

title: [Save] Live CHUNK_GameStateMap hardcodes game_mode 0 and load keeps the current session mode
description:
## C++
`GameStateMap::xfer` v2 (`GameStateMap.cpp:293-297, 324-329`) writes `TheGameLogic->getGameMode()` after the portable map names, and on load calls `TheGameLogic->setGameMode(gameMode)` so `startNewGame(TRUE)` rebuilds the player list for the saved mode.

## Leftover
`GameStateMap::xfer` (`Common/src/system/SaveGame/game_state_map.rs:441-447, 492-497`) xfers `notify_get_game_mode()` and on load calls `notify_set_game_mode(game_mode)`. Matches C++.

## Live
`write_game_state_map_block` (`Main/src/save_load/save_file.rs:519-521`) always writes `game_mode = 0`. `extract_embedded_map` reads the int and discards it. `offline_restore_mode_for_save` (`host_authority.rs:1251-1270`) documents that a save does not serialize GameMode and, when already in SinglePlayer/Skirmish, **keeps the current session mode**. Loading a skirmish save from a campaign (or the reverse) therefore starts the wrong mode/player-list setup.

## Evidence
C++ `xferInt(&gameMode)` / `setGameMode`. Leftover hook round-trip. Live hardcoded 0 + `match active_mode { SinglePlayer | Skirmish => Ok(active_mode) }`.
close_reason: Live CHUNK_GameStateMap writes TheGameLogic game mode; load applies it via offline_restore_mode_for_save so skirmish/campaign no longer keep the current session mode.

title: [Audio] Live pause never calls leftover TheAudio.pauseAudio
description:
## C++
`GameLogic::setGamePaused` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/System/GameLogic.cpp:4178-4222`) is the live pause path (ESC/quit/victory/popup). It computes `AudioAffect audToAffect = pauseMusic ? AudioAffect_All : (AudioAffect_All & ~AudioAffect_Music)` then `TheAudio->pauseAudio(audToAffect)` on pause and `TheAudio->resumeAudio(audToAffect)` on unpause. Miles `pauseAudio` (`MilesAudioManager.cpp:569-583`) pauses playing sinks and discards pending `AR_Play`. Player-visible: campaign music, EVA, and combat SFX go silent while the pause/quit menu is up.

## Leftover (right)
`TheGameLogic::set_game_paused` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/helpers/game_logic.rs:187-217`) ports that exactly: `TheAudio.pause_audio(All)` when `pause_music`, else Sound+Sound3D+Speech; resume mirrors it. Leftover `AudioManager::pause_audio` (`game_audio.rs:1785-1802`) pauses rodio handles and drops pending `AR_Play`. Script `SUSPEND_BACKGROUND_SOUNDS` / `SOUND_AMBIENT_PAUSE` also hit leftover `TheAudio.pause_audio`.

## Live (wrong)
`host_set_paused` (`Main/src/cnc_game_engine/ui_commands.rs:1216-1237`) only latches `engine.game_paused` and `SessionControlOp::SetPaused`. Host `GameLogic::set_paused` (`world_combat/registries.rs:117-119`) sets `is_paused` and never calls leftover `TheGameLogic::set_game_paused` or leftover `TheAudio.pause_audio`/`resume_audio`. Presentation popup `pause_music` (`camera_drain.rs:162-165`) stops the parallel `background_music` rodio sink (synthetic/disabled), not leftover TheAudio music from `MUSIC_SET_TRACK`. Live `host_update_the_audio` still ticks leftover TheAudio every frame while paused, so Miles/rodio sinks keep playing.

## Evidence
- C++ `GameLogic.cpp:4183-4200, 4222`
- Leftover `helpers/game_logic.rs:201-216`, `game_audio.rs:1785-1802`
- Live `ui_commands.rs:1225-1226`, `host_ops_writeback.rs:281-282`, `registries.rs:117-119`, `camera_drain.rs:162-165`
- Not a dupe of closed hq-d10n (pauseAudio request discard, leftover impl) or hq-pcife (stopAudio zombies).
close_reason: Live GameLogic::set_paused now calls leftover TheGameLogic::set_game_paused(paused, true) so C++ setGamePaused pauseAudio/resumeAudio (default pauseMusic) runs on ESC/quit/victory/popup.

title: [Pathfind] findSafePath is one-repulsor no-extent Dijkstra
description:
## C++
`Pathfinder::findSafePath` (AIPathfind.cpp:10885+): Dijkstra from the unit away from *two* repulsor positions until a `checkDestination` cell is outside both radii (or budget 2000). Human `m_logicalExtent`, `checkChangeLayers`, then `buildActualPath` / `findPath` to the chosen cell.

## Leftover
`pathfind_complete/attack_path.rs` `find_safe_path` takes `repulsor_pos1` + `repulsor_pos2`, applies `is_human` extent, layer hops, `is_destination_valid`, then `find_path` to the flee cell.

## Live
`PathfindingSystem::find_safe_path` (`pathfinding.rs` ~5272) takes a single `repulsor`. No human extent, no layer hops, `cell_passable_for` only, reconstructs the Dijkstra polyline directly. `world_tick/movement.rs` ~213 passes one threat position.

## Player-visible
Repulsor civilians / flee orders run from one threat into the second, and can leave the playable map. C++ / leftover keep the flee cell outside both radii and inside the human extent.

## Evidence
Not hq-2g8d9 (that was a 20wu twitch; live now has a Dijkstra). Remaining leftover-right gaps are two-repulsor, extent, layers, and findPath-to-cell.
close_reason: find_safe_path_from takes two repulsors, dest_ok, human extent, findPath-to-cell. requestSafePath rotates m_repulsor2. world_tick passes both.

title: [Pathfind] allow_partial is not findClosestPath
description:
## C++
`Pathfinder::findClosestPath` (AIPathfind.cpp:8739+): on `findPath` failure, A* from the unit tracks the closest *valid destination* cell to the goal using screen distance plus `cost² * COST_TO_DISTANCE_FACTOR_SQR`. The goal cell itself need not be passable. Hierarchical closest-path probe first.

## Leftover
`pathfind_complete/find_path.rs` `find_closest_path` ports that search: `is_destination_valid` cells only, screen-dist + cost², aircraft goal short-circuit, human extent, layer hops.

## Live
`find_path_via_crate` (`pathfinding.rs` ~4342) falls back to crate A* `allow_partial=true`. That reconstructs to `best_key` by diagonal heuristic of any expanded cell, and crate A* returns None immediately if the goal cell is not passable (`pathfind_astar.rs` ~1066). Invalid/occupied clicks still refuse instead of marching to the nearest legal cell.

## Player-visible
Unreachable or occupied clicks still produce no path (unit stands) even after the hq-c48lz allow_partial fallback. C++ / leftover walk as close as a legal cell allows.

## Evidence
Not a refile of hq-c48lz (that bead claimed findClosest was missing entirely; live now has allow_partial, which is a different algorithm). Leftover `find_closest_path` is unused on the live host.
close_reason: find_path_via_crate exact-fail now calls find_closest_path (valid dest + screen-dist+cost2). Goal need not be passable. allow_partial leftover unused on live assign.

title: [Pathfind] Human units path outside m_logicalExtent
description:
## C++
`Pathfinder::checkForAdjust` (AIPathfind.cpp:5187-5192) and `examineNeighboringCells` / `examineCellsCallback` (6019-6024, 6159-6164) reject human cells outside `m_logicalExtent`. Computer players may leave the playable map; humans may not. `processPathfindQueue` refreshes `m_logicalExtent` from `TheTerrainLogic->getExtent` (5887-5897).

## Leftover
`pathfind_complete/construct.rs` `refresh_logical_extent` / `in_logical_extent`. `check_for_adjust_ex` (hierarchical.rs:288-291) and `find_path_internal` (find_path.rs:117-120, 247-252) pass `is_human` and refuse cells outside the logical extent.

## Live
`PathfindingGrid` / `find_path_via_crate` have no logical-extent field. `destination_cell_ok` never checks `is_human`. Crate A* `cell_allowed` is `None`. Human clicks and A* neighbors can walk into unused map padding.

## Player-visible
Human units march off the playable map into unused border/padding. C++ / leftover keep them inside the active extent.

## Evidence
Live `pathfinding.rs` `destination_cell_ok` (~2593) and `find_path_via_crate` (~4320) vs leftover `check_for_adjust_ex` + `in_logical_extent`. No closed bead for logical extent.
close_reason: C++ live-host pathfind A*: human m_logicalExtent clamp, DozerHack into crate A*, downhill_only not hardcoded false. See local://wave23-fix-04.md

title: [Pathfind] DozerHack never reaches live A*
description:
## C++
`examineNeighboringCells` (AIPathfind.cpp:6207-6226): if the neighbor fails `validMovementPosition` but the seeker is `KINDOF_DOZER`, the cell is `CELL_OBSTACLE`, and the obstacle object exists with relationship != ENEMIES, the step is allowed (`dozerHack`). `neighborFlags` is not set, so diagonals cannot squeeze through.

## Leftover
`pathfind_complete/occupancy.rs` `dozer_hack_allows_obstacle` + `object_is_dozer`. `find_path_internal` snapshots obstacle owners and passes `dozer_ok_ref` into crate A* `find_path_ex6`.

## Live
`find_path_via_crate` (`pathfinding.rs` ~4339) passes `None` for `dozer_obstacle_ok`. Friendly/neutral scaffolds and buildings stay hard-blocked for dozers.

## Player-visible
Dozers stuck against their own scaffold or a friendly/neutral building refuse the path instead of walking through the non-enemy obstacle the way C++ does.

## Evidence
Not hq-wd53t (AI builder ForUI teleport). Leftover wires dozerHack; live A* never gets the callback.
close_reason: C++ live-host pathfind A*: human m_logicalExtent clamp, DozerHack into crate A*, downhill_only not hardcoded false. See local://wave23-fix-04.md

title: [Pathfind] findAttackPath is a spiral not leftover A*
description:
## C++
`Pathfinder::findAttackPath` (AIPathfind.cpp:10530+): quick steps toward the victim, then hierarchical probe + A* whose goal is any in-range `checkDestination` cell with LOS. Human logical-extent and `checkChangeLayers` apply. Returns NULL if no reachable firing cell.

## Leftover
`pathfind_complete/attack_path.rs` `find_attack_path` ports that A*: in-range dest_ok + view_blocked, start-cell reject, closest-valid fallback, layer hops, `is_human` extent.

## Live
`find_attack_firing_position` (`pathfinding.rs` ~4547) is documented simplified: ring/spiral around the victim, pick the geometrically closest passable cell, then `find_path_ex`. No attack A*, no hierarchical probe, no human extent, no layer hops. `assign_unit_attack_path` then falls back toward the victim if that cell has no path.

## Player-visible
Attackers walk into the target building or stall when a reachable firing cell exists around it. They pick a close-but-walled cell instead of A*-searching for a reachable in-range spot.

## Evidence
Not hq-qvyaf / hq-5mxzk / hq-bw35t (LOS / see-through / fail-open). Leftover attack A* is unused on the live assign path.
close_reason: Live find_attack_firing_position now leftover A*: in-range dest_ok+LOS, start-cell reject, hierarchical probe, closest-valid fallback, human extent. No spiral.

title: [Pathfind] Downhill-only A* hardcoded false
description:
## C++
`examineNeighboringCells` (AIPathfind.cpp:6188-6202): if `locomotorSet.isDownhillOnly()` and parent ground Z < neighbor ground Z, skip the neighbor. Seed-line toward goal is also suppressed when downhill-only (6106).

## Leftover
`object_is_downhill_only` reads the current locomotor template. `find_path_internal` passes `downhill_only` into crate A* and sets `seed_line = !tunneling && !downhill_only`.

## Live
Host objects already store `downhill_only` (`locomotor_bootstrap.rs`). `find_path_via_crate` (`pathfinding.rs` ~4332) hardcodes `downhill_only: false` and still seeds the line (`!start_is_obstacle`). A* will plan uphill routes.

## Player-visible
Downhill-only units (ski/sled locos) receive A* paths that climb. They then stall on the slope because locomotor refuse-uphill cannot follow the planned route.

## Evidence
Not hq-33ajv / hq-vv3tk (locomotor march / physics downhill). This is the A* neighbor gate leftover already implements.
close_reason: C++ live-host pathfind A*: human m_logicalExtent clamp, DozerHack into crate A*, downhill_only not hardcoded false. See local://wave23-fix-04.md

title: [Hunt] Map-wide Hunt victim is dropped when farther than 1.5x weapon range
description:
## C++
`AIHuntState::update` (`AIStates.cpp:7125-7205`) every `ENEMY_SCAN_RATE` finds the closest enemy at range 9999.9 (`TheAI->findClosestEnemy(..., AI::CAN_ATTACK, info)`), writes `setTeamTargetObject`, then `m_huntMachine->setGoalObject(victim)` and if the hunt machine is idle, `setState(AI_ATTACK_OBJECT)`. Attack-object then paths to the victim. There is no 1.5x weapon-range Hold gate.

## Leftover
`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/states/hunt.rs` `classic_on_update` / `find_hunt_victim` matches C++: scan 9999.9, priority-compare team victim, set goal, enter `AI_ATTACK_OBJECT`. No `should_attack` wrap.

## Live
`world_objects/ai_authority.rs` `AIState::Patrolling` does find the map-wide victim (hq-88txa/hq-7sxye), then wraps it in `evaluate_enemy` → `AIDecisionSystem::should_attack`. That helper (`ai_decisions.rs:334-340`) returns `Hold` when `distance > attack_range * 1.5`. Hold maps to `None`, so `process_ai_behavior` issues no `AttackTarget`. Hunt therefore only engages enemies already inside ~1.5x weapon range. Distant seek-and-destroy never chases.

Not hq-6p7c2 (attack-move wrap, closed) and not hq-88txa (scan radius, closed).

## Player-visible
Seek-and-destroy / TEAM_HUNT / player Hunt only fights units that walk into weapon range. A Ranger hunting a Crusader across the map stands idle instead of marching.
close_reason: Hunt issues AttackTarget for the map-wide victim without should_attack Hold (1.5x range) wrap.

title: [Tunnel] Occupants fire from the entrance as if garrisoned
description:
## C++
`TunnelContain::isGarrisonable()` is FALSE (`TunnelContain.h:69`). Occupants are `DISABLED_HELD` (`TunnelContain.cpp:171-186`) and inherit OpenContain `PassengersAllowedToFire` default FALSE (`OpenContain.cpp:81`, leftover `open_contain.rs:1325-1329` same gate). They sit in the shared `TunnelTracker` pool and never shoot out of an entrance. The structure's own `TunnelNetworkGun` is the only attack.

## Leftover
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/contain/tunnel_contain.rs:399-416` `on_containing` sets `DISABLED_HELD` and does not stamp a garrison fire bonus. `OpenContain::is_passenger_allowed_to_fire` (`open_contain.rs:1325-1329`) returns false unless INI `PassengersAllowedToFire` is Yes (retail TunnelContain does not).

## Live
`support_states.rs:4201-4205` any structure that is not HealContain (including Tunnel Network) stamps occupant `AIState::Garrisoned`. `world_tick/combat.rs:56-67` then calls `try_garrison_residual_fire` for every Garrisoned unit. That helper (`drones_and_garrison.rs:837-853`) only silences `DISABLED_SUBDUED` — it never consults `is_garrison_contain()`, `isGarrisonable()`, or `passengers_allowed_to_fire`. `bonuses.rs:285-288` also applies GARRISONED RANGE 133% to those infantry (hq-jvy34 closed by using Garrisoned AI as the proxy).

## Player-visible
Infantry inside a GLA Tunnel Network shoot out of the entrance they entered, with bunker range. Retail occupants are invisible and silent until they exit another tunnel.

## Not a duplicate
Closed tunnel beads cover shared pool, nemesis, capture, neutron, cave-in, heal, DUMMY gun, inventory, shroud. hq-jvy34 only restricted the 133% multiplier to `AIState::Garrisoned`; it did not stop tunnel enter from using that state.
close_reason: Live host now matches C++: tunnel occupants Docked and cannot residual-fire; Fire Base skips GarrisonGun; poison skips FIRING_A; Fire Base exit snaps station Y to ground (Patch 1.01).

title: [AIGroup] Attack-ground never orders locked spawn slaves
description:
## C++
`AIGroup::groupAttackPosition` (`AIGroup.cpp:2199-2254`) for each member: if `contain->isPassengerAllowedToFire()`, order garrisoned members that `getAbleToUseWeaponAgainstTarget` says POSSIBLE / POSSIBLE_AFTER_MOVING; then if `SpawnBehaviorInterface && !doSlavesHaveFreedom()`, `orderSlavesToAttackPosition(&attackPos, maxShots, cmdSource)`; then `aiAttackPosition`.

## Leftover
`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/group.rs` `group_attack_position` ports passengers + `order_slaves_to_attack_position` when slaves lack freedom + `ai_attack_position`. Dual-world gated unused on host; leftover is the right reference.

## Live
`command_executor/attack.rs` `execute_attack_ground` fans passengers (infantry-only) then `unit_command_attack_ground_ex`. No `order_hive_slaves_to_attack_position` / SpawnBehavior slave fan-out. Object-attack already orders hive slaves (`order_hive_slaves_to_attack_target`, hq-x3hzm). Attack-ground does not.

## Player-visible
Force-attack-ground on a Stinger Site (or other locked-slave hive) never tells residual soldiers to fire the point. C++ slaves shoot the ground target; live only the hull (if it has a weapon) does.
close_reason: execute_attack_ground orders locked hive slaves via order_hive_slaves_to_attack_position before aiAttackPosition.

title: [Particle] Attached leftover systems destroy next tick — host IDs not leftover objects
description:
## C++
`ParticleSystem::update` (`ParticleSys.cpp:1854-1905`):
- `m_attachedToDrawableID` → `TheGameClient->findDrawableByID`; missing drawable clears the id and `destroy()`.
- else `m_attachedToObjectID` → `TheGameLogic->findObjectByID`; missing object clears the id and `destroy()`.
`W3DModelDraw::recalcBonesForClientParticleSystems` attaches ParticleSysBone systems with `attachToDrawable(getDrawable())` then local `setPosition` of the bone.

## Leftover (right)
`ParticleSystem::resolve_attached_parent` (`GameClient/src/effects/particle_system.rs:1769-1842`) matches C++: leftover `TheGameClient::find_drawable_by_id` (`DRAWABLE_STATE`) then leftover `TheGameLogic::find_object_by_id` (OBJECT_REGISTRY then leftover `GameLogic.objects`). Miss → `destroy()`.
Leftover `W3DModelDraw::recalc_bones_for_client_particle_systems` (`w3d_model_draw_impl/draw.rs:615`) calls `attach_particle_system_to_drawable`.
Leftover `ParticleSystemFXNugget::really_do_fx` (`fxlist_integration.rs:759-761`) `create_attached_particle_system` only when `AttachToObject`.

## Live (wrong)
Production never fills leftover OBJECT_REGISTRY / leftover `DRAWABLE_STATE` (Main has zero `DRAWABLE_STATE` writers).
Live still attaches leftover systems with host object ids:
- `combat_particles.rs:1389-1393` `attach_particle_system_to_object_local(template, owner.0, …)` for ParticleSysBone / body fire-smoke / DisableFX / OCL attach.
- `fx_list.rs:1675-1677` `do_fx_obj_host` passes `Some(primary.id)` into leftover `do_fx_obj` so `AttachToObject=Yes` nuggets `attach_to_object(host_id)`.
Next `update_presentation_shell` → `ParticleSystemManager::update` (`impl_update.rs:1345` / `particle_manager.rs:893`) runs leftover `resolve_attached_parent`, cannot find the host id, `destroy()`s the system before emit (`particle_system.rs:1516-1522`).

## Player-visible
Attached FX die on the first leftover tick: vehicle exhaust, ParticleSysBone jets/smoke, damaged-building FIRE/SMOKE, DisableFX BinaryShower, FXList `AttachToObject` fire/smoke. Unattached positional FXLists still work.

## Not a duplicate
hq-ocg22 fixed doFXObj spawn via `HostFxObjectPose` (not attach follow). hq-dwtov / hq-dfb1u / hq-i0p4c / hq-v12zi are transform/bone/shroud math on a found parent. hq-vwjo6 is destroy fade, not attach-miss destroy.
close_reason: resolve_attached_parent keeps host object IDs via host_fx_object_pose; presentation refresh + attach publish so leftover systems follow live host instead of destroy().

title: [Weapon] Live getAble misses passenger/slave/contained InvalidShot
description:
## C++
`WeaponSet::getAbleToUseWeaponAgainstTarget` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/WeaponSet.cpp:581-760`):
- Enclosing garrison: `calcBestGarrisonPosition` then `isSourceObjectWithGoalPositionWithinAttackRange` (not container origin).
- `KINDOF_IMMOBILE` / `KINDOF_SPAWNS_ARE_THE_WEAPONS` / `getContainedBy()` with a weapon but none in range → `ATTACKRESULT_INVALID_SHOT` (except `ATTACK_TUNNEL_NETWORK_GUARD`).
- `isAnyWithinTargetPitch` reject.
- Occupied container `isPassengerAllowedToFire` recurses into members (garrisoned building click-to-attack).
- Hive/spawn slaves `getCanAnySlavesUseWeaponAgainstTarget`; immobile + SPAWNS_ARE_THE_WEAPONS forces POSSIBLE (Stinger Site).

`ActionManager` / RMB attack cursor uses this result. `PossibleAfterMoving` is the "attack if I walk there" cursor.

## Leftover
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/weapon/weapon_set_able.rs:88-243` ports the same gates (`garrison_fire_goal`, immobile/spawn/contained abort, pitch, `passenger_fire_result`, `spawn_slave_result`). Closed leftover-only as hq-tsp8.

## Live
`GameLogic::get_able_to_use_weapon_against_target` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/mood.rs:766-928`):
- Early `InvalidShot` if no PRIMARY/SECONDARY (or locked) slot is bound — garrisoned buildings with `OBJECT_STATUS_CAN_ATTACK` but no own weapon never reach passenger recurse.
- Range is occupant/container `is_within_attack_range_for_slot` (no fire-goal).
- Comment: "Contact / invalid pitch residual not expanded — range gate only."
- Out of range: `can_move() || max_speed > 1e-3` → `PossibleAfterMoving`, else `InvalidShot`. Contained infantry stay "mobile" so they get the walk-there cursor.
- No passenger recurse, no spawn-slave POSSIBLE, no pitch reject.

Callers: `can_attack_target` (`command_system/system_impl.rs:1118-1144`) and AI/mood/guard.

## Player-visible
- Select a garrisoned civilian/faction building and RMB an enemy: no attack cursor; occupants only auto-fire.
- Garrisoned Ranger/Missile Defender vs a target past window range: "attack after moving" cursor instead of invalid.
- Stinger Site click-to-attack never falls through to the spawned soldiers.
- Pitch-limited weapons still show a legal attack cursor, then refuse to fire.

Not a refile of closed hq-tsp8 (that closed leftover `weapon_set.rs`, not this live host residual).
close_reason: Live getAble now matches C++ WeaponSet: garrison FIREPOINT goal range, immobile/spawn/contained InvalidShot (except TunnelNetworkGuard), pitch reject, passenger recurse, hive-slave POSSIBLE.

title: [Weapon] Live isWithinAttackRange skips bridge ends and contact collide
description:
## C++
`Weapon::isWithinAttackRange(source, target)` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Weapon.cpp:2152-2207`):
- `KINDOF_BRIDGE`: `TheTerrainLogic->getBridgeAttackPoints` and accept either end (distance to nearer abutment).
- Contact weapon (`attackRange * 1.05 < PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE`) vs `KINDOF_STRUCTURE`: after the numeric range test, also require `iteratePotentialCollisions` so the attacker is actually touching the building.

## Leftover
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/weapon/weapon_range.rs:13-99` ports both: nearer TerrainLogic bridge end, then `iterate_potential_collisions` for contact vs STRUCTURE. Closed leftover-only as hq-416r.

## Live
`Object::is_within_attack_range_for_slot` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/object/rtb.rs:414-435`) only compares `distance_to_object` (center-to-center XZ minus both bounding-circle radii) to min/max range + leech. No bridge-end branch. No contact-vs-structure collision iterate.

Aiming already uses nearer bridge end (`combat.rs:917` / `attack.rs:128`, closed hq-psn5v). Range legality still uses the span center.

## Player-visible
- Units standing on a long bridge abutment are out of range of "the bridge" (measured to mid-span) even though C++ (and live aim) treat the near end as the target. Attack cursor / auto-acquire fail along the deck.
- Contact weapons (TerroristSuicide, car-bomb, knife, dozer disarm) fire at a building as soon as surfaces are within ~5–9 wu. C++ requires actual geometry overlap.

Not a refile of closed hq-416r (leftover crate) or hq-psn5v (fire aim point).
close_reason: Live is_within_attack_range_for_slot uses bridge abutments and contact-vs-structure geometry overlap.

title: [Radar] Stealth garrison blip uses occupant color not getApparentControllingPlayer
description:
## C++
`Radar::addObject` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/System/Radar.cpp:427-434`) always asks `obj->getContain()->getApparentControllingPlayer(ThePlayerList->getLocalPlayer())` and paints that player's color (not `getIndicatorColor`) when a contain module is present.

`GarrisonContain::getApparentControllingPlayer` (`GarrisonContain.cpp:1167-1178`) returns the **original** owner to non-allies when `m_hideGarrisonedStateFromNonallies` is set (every occupant is `KINDOF_STEALTH_GARRISON` and the first is not DETECTED). Allies see the occupier's color; enemies see a civilian/neutral blip.

## Leftover
`GarrisonContain::get_apparent_controlling_player` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/contain/garrison_contain.rs:1118-1156`) ports that hide: if `hide_garrisoned_state_from_non_allies` and observer relationship is not Allies, return the original team's controlling player.
`resolve_radar_object_color` (`Common/src/common/system/radar/objects.rs:62-72`) then uses `contain_apparent_color` / `contain_apparent_player_index` from that apparent controller.

## Live
`GameLogic::host_radar_insert_spec` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/radar_live.rs:289-309`) takes the **first occupant's** `owner_player_id` and always sets `contain_apparent_color` to that occupant's color. It never reads `building_data.hide_garrisoned_state` or `original_team`, and never calls leftover `get_apparent_controlling_player`.

Live enter already `setTeam`s the building to the occupant (`object/orders.rs:876`), so even the fallback `owner_color` is the occupier's color. Presentation freeze zeros occupant_count for non-allies (closed hq-lgt8x) but radar walks real `contained_units()`.

## Player-visible
Pathfinder / Jarmen / Burton hiding in a civilian building still paint USA/GLA color on the enemy LeftHUD. C++ and leftover show the original civilian/neutral blip until DETECTED.

## Not a duplicate
Closed hq-lgt8x is MODELCONDITION_GARRISONED / occupied pip. hq-wjtil is setTeam on enter. hq-cy4s added first-occupant contain color (the wrong apparent controller). hq-9n1mj is hide KindOf bits, not radar color.
close_reason: Live radar addObject hide/disguise uses player_relationship; stealth garrison blip uses getApparentControllingPlayer (original team for non-allies).

title: [Radar] addObject ally/disguise/stealth hide uses faction Team not Player relationship
description:
## C++
`Radar::addObject` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/System/Radar.cpp:403-425`) colors a `KINDOF_DISGUISER` from `StealthUpdate::getDisguisedPlayerIndex()` only when `player->getRelationship(clientPlayer->getDefaultTeam()) != ALLIES` **and** the local player is active. `RadarObject::isTemporarilyHidden` (`Radar.cpp:118-125`) hides `STEALTHLOOK_INVISIBLE`, which `StealthUpdate::calcStealthedStatusForPlayer` assigns to non-allies of an undetected stealth unit.

`Player::getRelationship` is the player-relation map (scripted diplomacy / campaign overrides / skirmish alliances), not faction `Team`.

## Leftover
`resolve_radar_object_color` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/system/radar/objects.rs:51-79`) uses `spec.owner_is_ally_of_local` exactly as C++ uses `getRelationship != ALLIES`.
`RadarObject::is_temporarily_hidden` (`radar/mod.rs:768-783`) hides enemy+stealthed+undetected when `is_enemy` is true.
Leftover `Player::get_relationship` / `object_vision.rs:185-188` already walk Player relationship, not faction Team.

## Live
`GameLogic::host_owner_is_ally_of_local` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/radar_live.rs:248-263`) returns true on `owner_team == local.team` (faction Team) before any `alliance_team` check. It never calls the live `player_relationship` helper (`object_queries.rs:356-396`) that already implements C++ `Player::getRelationship` (map relations, lobby `alliance_team`, not faction).

That flag is then stamped onto every blip (`radar_live.rs:319` `is_enemy`, `:346` `owner_is_ally_of_local`) and drives disguise color (`objects.rs:55-59`) plus stealth hide (`mod.rs:778-782`).

Disguise color is also filled from `disguise_as_team` via the first player of that faction (`radar_live.rs:278-281`), not `getDisguisedPlayerIndex`.

## Player-visible
- Two same-faction FFA Americas: the other USA player's stealthed units stay on your radar, and a disguised bomb truck shows its true USA color instead of the disguise.
- Campaign / scripted `PLAYER_SET_RELATIONSHIP` alliances never change radar disguise or stealth hide (China ally still treated as enemy on the LeftHUD because Team differs).
- 2v2 mixed-faction allies only work if `alliance_team` is set; the Team-equality short-circuit still mis-allies same-faction enemies.

## Not a duplicate
Closed hq-pzyzt is shroud looker mask. hq-cy4s was addObject never called / all-white blips. hq-8udzn is EVA Team vs relationship. None cover leftover-right `resolve_radar_object_color` / `is_temporarily_hidden` vs live `host_owner_is_ally_of_local` Team equality.
close_reason: Live radar addObject hide/disguise uses player_relationship; stealth garrison blip uses getApparentControllingPlayer (original team for non-allies).

title: [Production] Closing factory door never pops to WAITING_OPEN for the next unit
description:
## C++
ProductionUpdate.cpp:762-776: when a completed unit is ready and the reserved door is already CLOSING (`m_doorClosedFrame != 0`), immediately set `m_doorWaitOpenFrame = now`, clear OPENING/CLOSING flags, and set WAITING_OPEN. Spawn then proceeds because doorWaitOpenFrame != 0 (:795). Back-to-back War Factory / Arms Dealer batches do not wait for the close animation to finish and reopen.

## Leftover
`GameLogic/src/object/production/production_update_complete.rs:1245-1252` `spawn_unit`: if `door.door_closed_frame != 0`, set `door_wait_open_frame = now`, clear `door_closed_frame`, clear OPENING+CLOSING model bits, set WAITING_OPEN. Matches C++.

## Live
`world_tick/production.rs:817-823` only `start_door_cycle` when `door_spawn_phase == 0` (fully closed). `production_door_allows_spawn` (`host_production_buildable_command_residual.rs:642-643`) is true only for phase 2 (WAITING_OPEN). Phase 4 CLOSING neither pops nor starts a new cycle. `object/pose.rs:379-397` `tick_one_production_door` finishes CLOSING to idle (0) unless hold_open. hq-rx2q3 closed "start cycle only from fully-closed"; hq-5scgf closed extra WAITING_TO_CLOSE pose. Remaining: CLOSING→WAITING_OPEN pop.

## Player-visible
If the next Crusader/Red Guard finishes while the factory door is closing, retail snaps the door back open and the unit exits. Live waits out remaining DoorCloseTime plus a full DoorOpeningTime before release — a 1–2s extra stall between units on door-animated factories.
close_reason: Live CLOSING factory door pops to WAITING_OPEN when the next unit is ready so spawn proceeds this frame (ProductionUpdate.cpp:762-776).

title: [Dozer] findGoodBuildOrRepairPosition never runs findPositionAround
description:
## C++
DozerAIUpdate.cpp:1855-1894 `findGoodBuildOrRepairPosition` seeds the closest side of the target (`getMajorRadius()/2` along me→them), then `ThePartitionManager->findPositionAround` with minRadius 0, maxRadius 100, `sourceToPathToDest = me`, `maxZDelta = 10` unless airborne, and `ignoreObject = target` for flyers. Failure keeps the seed. Comment at :1875-1878: this stops the dozer picking the bottom of a cliff when the building is on top. WorkerAIUpdate.cpp:620 calls the same helper. newTask stores that result as START/ACTION (and dozer END is 5 cells past it).

## Leftover
`GameLogic/src/object/update/ai_update/dozer_ai_update.rs:1418-1454` `find_good_build_or_repair_position` matches: major-radius seed, FindPositionOptions 0–100, source_to_path_to_dest_id, max_z_delta 10, ignore_object for airborne, then PartitionManager::find_position_around_with_options.

## Live
`host_repair.rs:82-94` `dozer_repair_approach_position` is only the half-`selection_radius` seed. No findPositionAround, no maxZDelta, no sourceToPathToDest. Callers (`command_executor/construct.rs:148`, `leftover.rs:1594`, `rebuild_dozer.rs:1062`, `unit_commands.rs:650`, `support_states.rs:3311`) path to that seed. hq-6gy32 closed as half-radius + ignoreObstacle only (test: "dock half-radius, ignoreObstacle"); hq-wps0l/hq-yfk9k closed ACTION-dock vs center. Remaining: cliff/blocked seed is used as the dock.

## Player-visible
Dozers/workers path to a point that can sit inside the pad, on a cliff cell, or on the far-Z bank. C++/leftover snap the dock onto a pathable cell within 100wu of the seed. Units get stuck circling or start construction from the wrong terrace.
close_reason: Live findGoodBuildOrRepairPosition now runs findPositionAround (0-100, maxZDelta 10, sourceToPathToDest, ignore target if airborne). Failure keeps the half-radius seed. newTask stores the snapped ACTION dock.

close_reason: adjust_destination_for_group does tightenPath+checkPathCost 1.4 gate; computeIndividualDestination path calls adjustDestination(groupDest) via unit_command_move_free / waypoints / shared spine.

title: [Radar] LeftHUD terrain never samples tile or bridge colors
description:
## C++
`W3DRadar::buildTerrainTexture` (`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/Common/System/W3DRadar.cpp:997-1228`) paints each 128² radar cell from a 3×3 neighborhood:
- land: `TheTerrainVisual->getTerrainColorAt(world.x, world.y)` then `interpolateColorForHeight(&color, z, getTerrainAverageZ(), mapExtent.hi.z, mapExtent.lo.z)` (`:1174-1178`)
- water: `WaterTransparency` radar color + water-table interpolate (`:1086-1088`)
- intact bridges: `TerrainRoads->findBridge(...)->getRadarColor()` and the span's average deck Z (`:1142-1167`)

`W3DLeftHUDDraw` then blits that texture into ControlBar LeftHUD (`W3DRadar.cpp:1370`).

## Live
Leftover `RadarSystem::build_terrain_texture_cpp` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/system/radar/terrain.rs:68-166`) has a `RadarTerrainPaintSource` hook for `terrain_color_at` / `bridge_at`, but **nothing in the repo ever calls `register_radar_terrain_paint_source`**. Land cells therefore always take `unwrap_or([0.45, 0.42, 0.32])` (`terrain.rs:147-149`). Bridges never receive Roads.ini radar colors.

The leftover interpolator is also invoked with `(height, mapHi.z, averageZ, mapLo.z)` (`terrain.rs:150-151`), which is the opposite of the C++ call-site argument order `(height, getTerrainAverageZ(), mapHi.z, mapLo.z)`. Retail therefore mostly darkens from map-max; live lightens/darkens around the average.

Main's GPUI/minimap path is not a substitute: `build_minimap_terrain_base_texture` (`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/graphics/render_pipeline/pipeline_minimap.rs:675-807`) invents an elevation ramp (48–201 / 62–177 / 44–128) plus a 14% waterline, and never calls `get_terrain_color_at`. GameClient already implements `TerrainVisual::get_terrain_color_at` (`impl_world.rs:224-226`) — it is just never bound into TheRadar.

`WindowManager::draw_all` presents leftover `w3d_left_hud_draw` (`ui_render_pass.rs:231`, `hud.rs:93-120`), so this is the player LeftHUD.

## Player-visible
The radar does not show grass vs dirt vs snow vs asphalt, and bridges are not the authored gray/colored spans. Every map's LeftHUD is a height-shaded tan (or GPUI green-brown ramp) instead of the retail tile-sampled terrain.
close_reason: LeftHUD leftover W3DRadar now samples GameClient get_terrain_color_at and intact-bridge Roads.ini radar_color; interpolator uses C++ call-site (avgZ, mapHi, mapLo).
