title: Named/Team ENTERED_AREA and EXITED_AREA script conditions stuck false: live executor not wired to host trigger-flag helpers
description: C++: ScriptConditions.cpp evaluateNamedEnteredArea/ExitedArea use Object::didEnter/didExit edge flags; evaluateTeamEnteredAreaEntirely/Partially and TeamExitedAreaEntirely/Partially use Team::didAllEnter/didPartialEnter/didAllExit/didPartialExit. Leftover: the host trigger-edge infrastructure already exists and is maintained every frame by Main (scripting/conditions/helpers.rs update_host_object_trigger_flags + host_object_did_enter/host_object_did_exit/host_team_did_all_enter/host_team_did_partial_enter/host_team_did_all_exit/host_team_did_partial_exit; Main game_logic/object/pose.rs calls update_host_object_trigger_flags per host object per frame), and it is consumed by the sibling paths (scripting/conditions/named.rs and scripting/evaluator/eval_area.rs). Live: the path the live game actually runs (scripting/executor/eval_named.rs eval_named_entered_area/eval_named_exited_area and scripting/executor/eval_basic.rs eval_team_entered_area_entirely/_partially/eval_team_exited_area_entirely/_partially) instead resolves the tracker id and calls OBJECT_REGISTRY.with_object(...did_enter/did_exit) or crate Team::did_all_enter, which is always empty on the live host, so all six edge conditions are permanently false. Player-visible: unit/team entered-or-left-area triggers (ambush zones, civilian-evac chains, area-arrival objective completion) never fire in live play.
close_reason: Live executor NAMED/TEAM ENTERED_AREA and EXITED_AREA now use host_object_did_enter/exit and host_team_did_all/partial_enter/exit when OBJECT_REGISTRY is empty.

title: Script condition NAMED_CREATED never true on live host (executor lacks host-snapshot fallback)
description: C++: ScriptConditions.cpp evaluateNamedCreated returns getUnitNamed(name) != NULL, i.e. true whenever the named unit exists. Leftover: the live ScriptEngine::update path evaluates via scripting/executor/eval_named.rs eval_named_created, which resolves the tracker id then requires TheGameLogic::find_object_by_id to see a crate Object; on the live host the registry is empty so it always returns False even though the unit exists on the host. The sibling ScriptEvaluator path already has the correct fallback (scripting/evaluator/eval_lifecycle.rs evaluate_named_created_condition uses crate::scripting::host_script_named_unit_alive when OBJECT_REGISTRY is empty), and the host snapshot feeds exactly that data (scripts_camera.rs inject_host_script_query_snapshot). Live: the fallback used by the sibling is not wired into the executor path that the live game actually runs. Player-visible: campaign/skirmish scripts gated on unit X existing (reinforcement-arrived chains, created-named-on-team-at-waypoint follow-ups) never fire.
close_reason: eval_named_created uses host_script_named_unit_present on the live empty-registry path (C++ getUnitNamed != NULL).

title: UndeadBody/HighlanderBody lethal clamp uses post-armor amount; C++ compares raw DamageInfo amount
description: C++ UndeadBody.cpp:52-68 triggers second life when damageInfo->in.m_amount (PRE-armor raw) >= getHealth(), then clamps in.m_amount and lets ActiveBody::attemptDamage re-apply armor; HighlanderBody.cpp:30-37 likewise clamps m_amount pre-armor. Live Main object/damage.rs take_damage_from_typed_death_with_host_hp passes POST-armor/post-scalar actual_damage into battle_bus_should_intercept_lethal (orders.rs:1286) and highlander_clamp_damage (host_highlander_body.rs:67). Player-visible: GLA Battle Bus at low HP hit by a big armor-mitigated hit (e.g. FLAME/POISON vs its armor coefficients) never enters second-life bunker mode on live host where C++ would trigger it (bus stays drivable instead of becoming a stationary firing bunker); conversely >100% coefficients (SNIPER 200% etc.) let highlander bodies (trees/rocks) survive hits C++ kills, and post-armor clamp lands at a different HP than C++ min(raw, hp-1)*coeff. Leftover GameEngine has no UndeadBody/HighlanderBody attemptDamage override to inherit; live Main owns the whole clamp. Fix locus: pass raw damage alongside armor-scaled amount to the intercept/clamp predicates.
close_reason: Live host take_damage now clamps/compares raw DamageInfo.in.m_amount before armor (UndeadBody.cpp:58-68, HighlanderBody.cpp:30-36). Battle Bus second-life and Highlander floor match C++ pre-armor semantics.

title: Script condition NAMED_TOTALLY_DEAD true at map load for every living named unit
description: C++: ScriptConditions.cpp evaluateNamedUnitTotallyDead returns false while getUnitNamed(name) resolves the live object; true only after the unit existed and is gone. Leftover/live: the live executor path (scripting/executor/eval_named.rs eval_named_totally_dead) resolves the name via NamedObjectTracker, then requires TheGameLogic::find_object_by_id to see a crate Object. On the live host Main injects every named map unit into the crate tracker at load (scripts_camera.rs inject_host_named_unit_map_into_crate_tracker, golden_campaign.rs), and NamedObjectTracker::register_named_object records the name in name_history immediately (scripting/events.rs), while find_object_by_id always returns None because OBJECT_REGISTRY stays empty. Result: the exists-branch falls through and did_object_exist() = true, so NAMED_TOTALLY_DEAD evaluates TRUE for every named unit while it is alive. Player-visible: map scripts gated on a named unit being totally dead (mission fail on hero death, post-kill confirmations, cleanup chains) fire instantly at map load for units that are still alive.
close_reason: NAMED_TOTALLY_DEAD queries host_script_named_unit_alive when OBJECT_REGISTRY is empty: Some(_) is getUnitNamed success (false); None + did_object_exist is totally dead (C++ evaluateNamedUnitTotallyDead). Live executor, leftover evaluator, and leftover NamedUnitTotallyDeadCondition all share that path; NamedTotallyDead is exempt from the empty-registry fail-close.

title: Script condition TEAM_DESTROYED true at map load and team census/area conditions dead on live host
description: C++: ScriptConditions.cpp evaluateIsDestroyed uses Team::hasAnyObjects() over real members (false while any member lives); evaluateHasUnits/evaluateTeamInsideAreaEntirely/Partially/evaluateTeamOutsideAreaEntirely walk live members; evaluateTeamCreated fires when the team instance is actually created with units. Leftover: GameEngine/GameLogic/src/team/team_members.rs has_any_objects()/has_any_units() early-out false when OBJECT_REGISTRY.is_empty(); Main sync_legacy_team_factory_from_team_dicts eagerly creates a crate Team instance for every map-declared team at load (with no members). Live: scripting/executor/eval_basic.rs eval_team_destroyed computes !has_any_objects() = TRUE from map load for every declared team; eval_team_has_units never true; team_inside_consideration() early-returns empty counts so TEAM_INSIDE_AREA_ENTIRELY/PARTIALLY never fire and TEAM_OUTSIDE_AREA_ENTIRELY is stuck true even when the real team stands inside the area; eval_team_created sees the eagerly created instance so TEAM_CREATED fires early. Player-visible: destroy-this-team objectives complete instantly, reinforcement-wave scripts gated on the previous team being destroyed fire immediately, team-has-units and team-inside-area gating never triggers.
close_reason: Live host stamps team_instance_name on spawn, fills snapshot team_instance_ids from live members, and no longer eagerly creates leftover Team instances at map load. Leftover TEAM_DESTROYED/HAS_UNITS/CREATED/area query host census (C++ hasAnyObjects/hasAnyUnits/getTeamNamed).

title: Script condition PLAYER_HAS_CREDITS compares leftover shadow money never synced with host economy
description: C++: ScriptConditions.cpp evaluatePlayerHasCredits compares the credits parameter against Player::getMoney()->countMoney(), the same balance the player spends and the HUD shows. Leftover/live: the live executor path (scripting/executor/eval_basic.rs eval_player_has_credits) reads gamelogic Player money, which on the live host is only ever written by map-load start-money deposit (world_save.rs sync_legacy_player_list_from_side_dicts) and by script actions PLAYER_SET_MONEY / PLAYER_GIVE_MONEY (scripting/executor/actions_player_display_camera.rs do_set_money/do_give_money write the crate Player only and never drain to the host). Host harvesting, spending, bounties and black-market/hacker income live in Main players and never flow back. Player-visible: [Player] has (comparison) N credits conditions diverge from the real balance the player sees (e.g. script gave 5000 but the player still cannot build; or condition fires long before the real balance reaches N), so credit-gated map scripts mis-fire for the whole match.
close_reason: Live PLAYER_HAS_CREDITS reads host Player money via HostScriptPlayerCensus (inject merge_host_player_census_into_snapshot). C++ evaluatePlayerHasCredits compares INT to countMoney(); leftover Player money is only start-money / script SET/GIVE. eval_basic.rs + leftover eval_player.rs prefer host census when present. Test: player_conditions_use_host_census_instead_of_stale_leftover_player.

title: Script conditions PLAYER_HAS_POWER always true and PLAYER_HAS_NO_POWER never true on live host
description: C++: ScriptConditions.cpp evaluatePlayerHasPower reads Player::getEnergy()->hasSufficientPower() from the real base power state. Leftover: GameEngine/GameLogic/src/player/energy_handicap.rs has_sufficient_power() = production >= consumption; nothing on the host path ever writes the crate PlayerEnergy (host power lives in Main game_logic players), so production=consumption=0 -> 0>=0 true. Live: scripting/executor/eval_basic.rs eval_player_has_power / eval_player_has_no_power / eval_player_power_compare_percent / eval_player_excess_power_compare_value evaluate the unsynced crate Energy every frame. Player-visible: PLAYER_HAS_POWER is true from map load even with zero power plants, PLAYER_HAS_NO_POWER never fires (blackout / low-power mission scripts dead), POWER_COMPARE_PERCENT and EXCESS_POWER_COMPARE_VALUE compare against a zeroed energy model instead of the real base.
close_reason: Live PLAYER_HAS_POWER/NO_POWER (and percent/excess) read host Energy via HostScriptPlayerCensus. C++ Energy::hasSufficientPower is production>=consumption (false while sabotaged). Leftover PlayerEnergy stays 0>=0. inject fills power_produced/consumed/sabotage from host Player. eval_basic.rs + leftover eval_player.rs prefer census.

title: Script conditions PLAYER_ALL_DESTROYED / BUILDFACILITIES_DESTROYED / N_OR_FEWER_BUILDINGS always true on live host
description: C++: ScriptConditions.cpp evaluateAllDestroyed/evaluateAllBuildFacilitiesDestroyed/evaluatePlayerHasNOrFewerBuildings(Faction) query Player::hasAnyObjects()/hasAnyBuildFacility()/countBuildings() over live objects; true only when the player genuinely lost them. Leftover: GameEngine/GameLogic/src/player/objects.rs has_any_objects()/has_any_build_facility() and player/core.rs count_buildings()/count_objects_by_kindof() early-out (0/false) when OBJECT_REGISTRY.is_empty(). Live: production host keeps OBJECT_REGISTRY empty (authoritative_world DualTickPolicy::AuthorityOnly; Main never mirrors host objects), and sync_legacy_player_list_from_side_dicts populates the crate PlayerList with real players, so the live executor (scripting/executor/eval_basic.rs eval_player_all_destroyed/eval_player_all_buildfacilities_destroyed/eval_player_has_n_or_fewer_buildings/_faction_buildings) resolves the player and computes !false = TRUE from frame one. Player-visible: any map script gated on player destroyed / all build facilities destroyed / N-or-fewer buildings fires instantly at map load (instant fail/win cascades); PLAYER_HAS_OBJECT_COMPARISON in the same census family counts 0 so has-at-least-N never fires and fewer-than-N fires immediately, and PLAYER_LOST_OBJECT_TYPE is stuck false.
close_reason: Live leftover executor/evaluator query host_query_player_census first (PLAYER_ALL_DESTROYED / BUILDFACILITIES_DESTROYED / N_OR_FEWER_BUILDINGS); live host inject_host_script_query_snapshot merges GameLogic player census so empty OBJECT_REGISTRY no longer inverts.

title: [Selection] Control-group recall drops garrisoned/transported squad members (SELECT_TEAM / ADD_TEAM)
description: C++ / leftover / live / player-visible. C++ SelectionXlat.cpp MSG_META_SELECT_TEAM (digit) and MSG_META_ADD_TEAM (Shift+digit) recall every Squad::getLiveObjects() member: Squad::getLiveObjects (GameLogic/AI/Squad.cpp) only prunes !Object::isSelectable(), and Object::isSelectable (Object.cpp:3001-3017) tests only ALWAYS_SELECTABLE/Selectable kindof + !OBJECT_STATUS_UNSELECTABLE + !effectivelyDead — it does NOT exclude contained or masked objects. The translator then calls TheInGameUI->selectDrawable(obj->getDrawable()) directly, so units garrisoned in structures, standing on a FireBase pad, or loaded in transports are re-selected on recall (they appear in the selection/control bar; orders apply to them). Entering an enclosing container sets OBJECT_STATUS_MASKED (Object.cpp:674-678) and maskObject deselects (Object.cpp:3317-3330), but hotkey-squad membership survives and recall re-selects. Live host hotkeys.rs select_control_group / add_control_group_to_selection filter the stored ids through PresentationFrame::filter_alive_selectable_ids (presentation_frame/alive.rs:203) which requires is_owned_by_local AND UnitControlSystem::presentation_is_selectable (unit_control.rs:323), and that predicate requires o.contained_by.is_none() and !o.masked. Result: recalling a group whose members are inside a transport or garrison silently shrinks the selection (missing portraits, orders hit fewer units) vs C++. Same stricter filter is reused in UnitControlSystem::select_control_group (unit_control.rs:862-870). Fix should special-case recall to C++ isSelectable semantics (dead/UNSELECTABLE only; SELECT keeps getControllingPlayer()==local gate, ADD has no owner gate).
close_reason: Live SELECT_TEAM/ADD_TEAM recall uses Object::isSelectable (filter_live_squad_ids), not CanSelectDrawable/contained_by. Leftover Squad::get_live_object_ids wired into leftover Player processSelect/AddTeam and leftover SelectionXlat. Garrisoned/transported/FireBase squad members stay selected on digit/Shift+digit.

title: [Transport] Combat Chinook vehicle riders fire out and arm the rider weapon set
description:
## C++
TransportContain::isPassengerAllowedToFire(ObjectID) (TransportContain.cpp:570-599) returns FALSE for any non-INFANTRY rider, and Object::isAbleToAttack (Object.cpp:3167) consults it, so a vehicle inside any TransportContain can never shoot out — the retail Combat Chinook is the TransportContain that admits vehicles (AllowInsideKindOf = INFANTRY VEHICLE). AIGroup::groupAttackObjectPrivate (AIGroup.cpp:2141-2150) skips riders whose getAbleToAttackSpecificObject is not POSSIBLE, so attack orders never reach vehicle riders. TransportContain::letRidersUpgradeWeaponSet (TransportContain.cpp:221-224) continues past non-infantry riders, so a vehicle aboard never sets WEAPONSET_PLAYER_UPGRADE.

## Live
world_combat/drones_and_garrison.rs try_transport_passenger_residual_fire gates infantry only for Helix and the overlord-bunker peel, so a vehicle rider docked in a Combat Chinook residual-fires from the FIREPOINT origin on auto-acquire. command_executor/attack.rs:202-239 pushes every contained passenger (no able-to-attack gate) when a passengers_allowed_to_fire container attacks, so the vehicle rider receives the attack order and fires. world_combat/special_power_flights.rs refresh_battle_bus_armed_riders_weapon_set + host_combat_chinook.rs combat_chinook_rider_has_viable_weapon (accepts is_vehicle=true) count vehicles as armed riders, binding ListeningOutpostUpgradedDummyWeapon and setting weapon_set_player_upgrade with only a vehicle aboard. Admission path object/orders.rs normal_enter_admission returns InfantryOrVehicle for the chinook, so vehicles really board.

## Player-visible
Load a Humvee or Technical into an Air Force General Combat Chinook in live: the vehicle shoots enemies from the chinook and flips the armed-riders weapon set / dummy weapon bind. In C++ vehicles ride silent — only infantry fire out and only infantry arm the rider weapon set.

## Not a duplicate
Closed hq-69h8 added the infantry-only gate for the Helix and the overlord bunker nest only; the Combat Chinook vehicle path remained unguarded. Closed hq-0gql is the parent-container consult.
close_reason: Live TransportContain::isPassengerAllowedToFire is infantry-only via leftover transport_contain_passenger_kind_allowed_to_fire. Combat Chinook vehicle riders no longer residual-fire, receive group attack, or arm WEAPONSET_PLAYER_UPGRADE (C++ TransportContain.cpp:576-578, Object.cpp:3167, letRidersUpgradeWeaponSet:226-229).

title: [Transport] Live unload while moving strands passengers until the hull stops
description:
## C++

MSG_EXIT single-rider unload is the same state machine. Retail troops bail out of a moving Humvee one every 250ms while it keeps driving.

## Live
command_executor/transport.rs:337-351 execute_exit drops the first rider, then sends the rest to pending_containers -> pending_evacuate_on_stop (transport.rs:514-518). world_combat/registries.rs evacuate_container_now is the same one-per-call plus pending_evacuate_on_stop = more_remain. The only drain is world_tick/movement.rs:482-492, gated on movement.path.is_empty() && !status.moving, so a transport with an active move order never drains.

## Player-visible
Evacuate/Exit on a moving loaded Humvee / Troop Crawler / Listening Outpost pops ONE soldier and holds the rest inside until the vehicle stops; C++ streams all of them out one per ExitDelay (250ms) while it drives on. A transport ordered across the map after an unload order carries its troops the whole way.

## Not a duplicate
Closed hq-c3opu added the ExitDelay stagger but its drain is stop-gated; closed hq-iwgts is airborne transports descending to Y=0; closed hq-cseyb is combat-drop rappel.
close_reason: Live execute_exit / evacuate_container_now now set pending_stream_exit so remaining riders keep polling ExitDelay like C++ AIExitState::update, with no hull-stop gate. move-to-and-evacuate still waits for arrival (prep_move clears the stream flag). Drain runs even under GW movement authority.

title: [Pathfind] Live A* always starts/adjusts on LAYER_GROUND — bridge decks unusable as start or destination
description: C++ / live / player-visible. C++ internalFindPath (AIPathfind.cpp:6448-6476) resolves destinationLayer = TheTerrainLogic->getLayerForDestination(to) (TerrainLogic.cpp:1668: bridge whose deck height is nearest the click Z) and starts the search on layer = obj->getLayer() via getClippedCell(layer, from); adjustDestination (AIPathfind.cpp:5355-5359) resolves the layer from dest/groupDest and checkForAdjust checks getCell(layer, i, j). Live host pathfinding.rs find_path_via_crate calls crate find_path_ex which hardcodes start_layer=PathfindLayerEnum::Ground (pathfind_astar.rs find_path_ex6 -> find_path_with_start_layer(Ground)); crate find_path_on_layer exists but has zero callers in Main; adjust_destination_ex/destination_cell_ok are ground-grid-only. Consequences on any bridge map (decks are stamped live via stamp_bridge_deck, world_save.rs:680 and special_power_flights.rs:1490): (1) destination clicked ON a deck: ground cell under deck is Water -> destination_cell_ok fails -> 400-cell spiral snaps the goal to a riverbank, so units ordered onto a bridge walk to the bank instead of the deck point (C++ targets the deck-layer Clear cell); (2) unit standing mid-deck re-ordered: start ground cell is Water -> snapped up to 64 cells to a bank, possibly the far side, so the path starts from the wrong end / unit jitters or stalls (C++ continues from the deck-layer cell); (3) group destinations and rally points on bridges snap off-deck the same way. Fix direction: resolve start layer from the unit's deck occupancy and goal layer via gamelogic terrain get_layer_for_destination (already used by ui_production.rs:828), pass start_layer into find_path_with_start_layer, and make adjust_destination/destination_cell_ok check layer_cell_type when the resolved layer != Ground.
close_reason: Live A* now starts on obj layer (getLayerForDestination of seeker pos) and adjusts/goals on dest layer. Host find_path_via_crate calls leftover find_path_with_start_layer(start_layer, dest_layer); adjust_destination_on_layer checks getCell(layer) passability. Bridge decks usable as start and destination.

title: [Locomotor] Treads never slow for turns — angleCoeff speed modulation missing on live march
description: C++: moveTowardsPositionTreads (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Locomotor.cpp:1167-1210) modulates goalSpeed by heading error: angleCoeff = |relAngle|/(PI/4) clamped to 1.0, then goalSpeed = (1-angleCoeff)*desiredSpeed, so treaded vehicles decelerate through turns (a 90-degree pivot drives goalSpeed toward 0). Near goal it additionally brakes tight pivots: if dx^2+dy^2 < (2*PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE_F)^2 and angleCoeff > 0.05 then goalSpeed = actualSpeed*0.6. Distinct from the distance-based braking curves (filed hq-iriyu, now implemented). / Leftover: GameEngine locomotor/core_impl/move_ground.rs:26-43 ports both the QUARTER_PI angleCoeff and the 0.6 near-goal clamp faithfully. / Live: production-default host march Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/movement.rs update_movement (GENERALS_GAMEWORLD_MOVEMENT_AUTHORITY default off per tick/authority.rs:104) computes speed = effective_max_speed(), then only dist-based apply_cpp_approach_brake (physics_motion.rs:1182-1213, angle-free Treads arm) and the wheeled PI/20 cap; no turn-angle speed factor exists anywhere on the live Treads path. object/update.rs:202-213 has the coeff but is a dead residual with no callers. / Player-visible: every treaded vehicle (Battlemaster, Paladin, Crusader, Scorpion, Overlord, Marauder, Nuke Cannon, tanks) turns while keeping full march speed instead of the retail slow-through-turn feel, and near-goal pivots swing wide at full speed.
close_reason: Live GameLogic::update_movement applies C++ treads angleCoeff (relAngle/(PI/4) clamp + near-goal 0.6).

title: Script camera shaker waveform diverges: 3.8x amplitude, 2-6Hz sway vs 12.5-15Hz sweep, no random fudge
description: C++ CameraShakerSystem (camerashakesystem.cpp): Add_Camera_Shake converts power degrees to radians (power*PI/180); each shaker gets random per-axis Omega in [12.5*360deg, 15*360deg]/s with omega(t)=omega+(END_OMEGA-omega)*elapsed sweeping toward 1 rev/s, random per-axis Phi, plus per-axis random fudge ±0.5*intensity accumulated three times (added inside the axis loop), then clamped to AXIS_ROTATION (7.5/15/5 deg). Live: cnc_game_engine/start_game.rs script_camera_shaker_rotations + ScriptCameraShaker::new (cnc_game_engine/types.rs:531-557) compute intensity=(amplitude_degrees/15.0) — ~3.82x stronger than C++ power*PI/180; use a fixed frequency_hz 2..6 with per-axis 1.0/0.79/1.17 harmonic multipliers instead of the random 12.5-15Hz END_OMEGA sweep; and add no random fudge. Player-visible live-path mismatch: scripted rotational camera shakes (campaign cinematics / superweapon scripts) wobble far more violently and as a slow sway instead of the retail fast buzz. Leftover GameClient/src/display/cinematic_camera.rs CameraShakeSystem has exact-constant parity including the triple-accumulated fudge quirk; live Main should route through it (or the hq-dhb57 fix) instead of its own approximation.
close_reason: ScriptCameraShaker uses power*PI/180, 12.5-15Hz omega sweep to 1Hz, and triple-axis fudge.

title: Camera shaker epicenter dropped: live uses camera_target instead of scripted waypoint position
description: C++: ScriptActions.cpp doC3CameraShake (CAMERA_ADD_SHAKER) passes the waypoint position to W3DView::Add_Camera_Shake; CameraShakerSystem::Compute_Rotations attenuates by 3D distance from the camera eye to that epicenter (intensity*(1-dist/radius), zero beyond radius) (camerashakesystem.cpp:112-137, applied in W3DView.cpp:393). Live: mission_scripts.rs keeps position in CameraAddShakerRequest, but the PresentationFrame freeze drops it (presentation_frame/build.rs:1932-1936 maps to (amplitude,duration,radius) only, .take(8)) and cnc_game_engine/camera_drain.rs:335-341 re-enqueues with position:self.camera_target; start_game.rs script_camera_shaker_rotations then measures 2D (x,z) distance from the eye to that target (the fixed boom offset) instead of 3D eye-to-waypoint. Player-visible live-path mismatch: scripted rotational shakes fire at full strength no matter how far the camera is from the scripted waypoint, or never fire when the script radius is smaller than the eye-to-look-target boom distance while C++ would shake. Leftover GameClient/src/display/cinematic_camera.rs CameraShakeSystem (+register_camera_shake_system) already has full parity and is unused by the live path.
close_reason: Presentation freeze keeps shaker xyz; drain uses waypoint, Compute_Rotations uses 3D eye distance.

title: [Terrain] Cliff cells use raw-sample 9.8 threshold instead of world-Z 9.8
description:

## Live
TerrainData::is_cliff_at_world converts corners to raw u8 and compares raw u8 delta > 9.8 — fires at delta 10 = 6.25 world units (~32°), ~2.56× stricter than C++.

## Player-visible

notes: Leftover remaining extra: after the raw-u8 four-corner test, is_cliff_at_world also ORs slope_at_world >= (9.8*MAP_HEIGHT_SCALE/scale_x)*0.85. C++ has no slope stand-in. Fix should drop the slope OR and use leftover is_cliff_cell / world-Z packed bits.
close_reason: Live is_cliff_at_world / cliff_cell_from_raw_heights_residual now use leftover terrain_cliff::is_cliff_from_raw_heights: raw*MAP_HEIGHT_SCALE vs 9.8 world Z (C++ setCellCliffFlagFromHeights). Dropped extra slope fallback that still marked 32-44° as cliff.

title: [Drawable] Blob shadow not dropped for detected stealth units (STEALTHLOOK_VISIBLE_DETECTED)
description:
## C++
`Drawable::draw` (Drawable.cpp:2627-2630): for any attached non-dead object it calls `setShadowsEnabled(m_stealthLook != STEALTHLOOK_VISIBLE_DETECTED)` every frame. A stealthed unit revealed to the local player through detection (detector unit/structure marks it DETECTED → calcStealthedStatusForPlayer returns VISIBLE_DETECTED) keeps drawing but its shadow is turned OFF. `setShadowsEnabled` propagates to every DrawModule's shadow (Drawable.cpp:857-869).

## Live
`shadows_enabled` on the frozen drawable comes only from `presentation_shadows_enabled()` (object/death.rs:712-717) = topple_data.shadows_enabled, i.e. only ToppleUpdate clears it. `collect_blob_shadows_from_presentation` (graphics/selection_renderer.rs:677-697) draws a dark blob disc for every `unit_render_inputs` row with `shadows_enabled`. Detected enemy stealth units stay in the mesh pass (correct: `local_viewer_hides_stealthed` only hides `effectively_stealthed` = stealthed && !detected), so a detected Burton/Jarmen/mine/tunnel keeps its blob shadow in live. No live path consults camo_stealth_look/StealthLook for shadows (host residuals Wave 79/97/1044 only freeze the ordinal).

## Player-visible
When your detector reveals an enemy stealth unit, C++ shows the model without a ground shadow; live shows a dark blob disc under it. For detected stealth structures (camo tunnels under CamoNetting with StealthLook=VISIBLE_DETECTED, camo_stealth_look=3) the blob also stays. Minor but a live-path visual difference on a recurring scenario (Pathfinder/outpost detection, detected mines).
close_reason: Detected stealth (VISIBLE_DETECTED) clears presentation_shadows_enabled so blob discs drop.

title: [Drawable] Own mines render at 50% opacity for friendly viewer — C++ KINDOF_MINE forces effective opacity 0
description:
## C++
`StealthUpdate::update` (StealthUpdate.cpp:628-634) special-cases mines every update: `if (self->isKindOf(KINDOF_MINE)) draw->setEffectiveOpacity(0.0f, 0.0f)` — m_stealthOpacity=0, effective=0, so `W3DScene` (W3DScene.cpp:1595) alphaOverride=0. This runs each frame BEFORE `setStealthLook` ( StealthUpdate.cpp:809-810), and setStealthLook's body is skipped when the look is unchanged, so the VISIBLE_FRIENDLY friendlyOpacity never sticks: mines are fully invisible to EVERY viewer, including their owner (you only find them via selection/radar).

## Live
The host already freezes the right value: `apply_mine_innate_stealth` sets `camo_friendly_opacity = MINE_STEALTH_OPACITY_RESIDUAL` (0.0, stealth.rs:225; constant host_radar_stealth_vision_residual.rs:351, re-asserted in world_scripts/stealth_mines.rs:876-880). But the mesh pass never reads it: `build.rs:767`/`overlay.rs:1974` freeze `friendly_stealth_opacity = template.stealth_friendly_opacity_min` (default 0.5, thing.rs:2518; mines have no FriendlyOpacityMin INI override in spawn_templates.rs:2737-2741), and `queries.rs:349-365` sets `input.presentation_opacity = object.friendly_stealth_opacity.clamp(0,1)` for `is_mine` under `local_viewer_uses_friendly_stealth_look`. Enemy viewers correctly hide undetected mines (`local_viewer_hides_stealthed`), but the friendly viewer sees every own mine/demo trap rendered at a static 50% alpha.

## Player-visible
Placing GLA mines / demo traps (or USA remote charges with mine kindof) leaves a half-visible model sitting on the field for the owner in live; in C++ the mine vanishes completely the moment it cloaks. Owner gets a permanent 50%-alpha marker C++ players never see (and 0.5 alpha also makes mine fields trivially scannable by scrolling the camera).
close_reason: Mines freeze camo_friendly_opacity (0) instead of template 0.5; mesh uses that for owner look.

So a GLA worker (or dozer) that is actively building/repairing and gets any player order abandons the task; the scaffold stays until re-ordered. / Leftover: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine GameLogic dozer_ai_update.rs / worker_ai_update.rs never model this cancel either. / Live: GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/command_executor/leftover.rs dozer_new_task_build parks dozer_task_build_target and only dozer_internal_task_complete (repair/construct completion paths) clears slots; execute_move (movement.rs), execute_stop (attack.rs) and GameLogic::unit_command_stop (unit_commands.rs:235-299) never clear the slots, and update_dozer_bored_repair + dozer_idle_resume_pending_build re-launch the parked BUILD as soon as the unit goes Idle. / Player-visible: order a building GLA worker to move away (or Stop it) — live walks it back to the scaffold and keeps building after the move completes; C++/retail leaves the half-built structure and an idle worker until the player re-orders.

title: [Drawable] Status tint applies instantly — C++ TintEnvelope ADSR ramps (30f disabled/frenzy, 150f subdual) missing
description:
## C++
`Drawable::updateDrawable` (Drawable.cpp:1228-1285) plays a TintEnvelope on tint-status edge: DISABLED and FRENZY use `play(color, 30, 30, SUSTAIN_INDEFINITELY)` (1s attack, 1s decay), GAINING_SUBDUAL_DAMAGE uses `play(SUBDUAL_DAMAGE_COLOR, 150, 150, SUSTAIN_INDEFINITELY)` (5s attack, 5s decay). `TintEnvelope::update` steps `m_currentColor` toward peak by `peak/frames` each frame, so the tint fades in/out gradually (TintEnvelope.cpp; TintEnvelope fields in Drawable.h:158-235).

## Live
`UnitRenderInput::from_renderable` (unit_render.rs:429-435) → `drawable_status_tint_rgb` (game_logic/object/stealth.rs:617-638) returns the full peak color `[-0.5,-0.5,-0.5]` / `[-0.2,-0.2,0.8]` / frenzy color immediately when the status bit is set, and `[0,0,0]` immediately when cleared. `render_item.apply_status_tint` (graphics/render_item.rs:834) applies it per frame with no ramp state. No envelope/attack/decay exists anywhere on the live path (no TintEnvelope host).

## Player-visible
EMP/black-lotus-disabled units snap to dark gray and snap back (C++: 1s fade in/out). Frenzy (Frenzy reward / China nationalism-era buff) tints snap on/off instead of 1s ramps. Subdual damage (microwave tanks, neutron-shelled units) blue tint snaps instantly in live; C++ slowly ramps over 5 seconds and fades out over 5 seconds — the C++ subdual tint is a slow 'freezing to death' cue, live is an instant flash.
close_reason: Live status tint samples TintEnvelope ADSR (30f disabled/frenzy, 150f subdual).

title: [Drawable] Disabled-status tint gate wrong: unmanned tints, underpowered/paralyzed/subdued/freefall do not
description:
## C++
`Object::setDisabledUntil` (Object.cpp:2099-2116) sets Drawable `TINT_STATUS_DISABLED` (dark gray `DARK_GRAY_DISABLED_COLOR {-0.5,-0.5,-0.5}`) on every disable edge whose type is NOT `DISABLED_HELD`, `DISABLED_SCRIPT_DISABLED`, or `DISABLED_UNMANNED` — i.e. DEFAULT, HACKED, EMP, PARALYZED, UNDERPOWERED, FREEFALL, AWESTRUCK, BRAINWASHED, SUBDUED, SCRIPT_UNDERPOWERED all tint dark gray. `clearDisabledUntil` (Object.cpp:2283-2302) clears the tint only when no non-exception disable flag remains. Note DISABLED_SUBDUED sets the *dark gray* tint, and TINT_STATUS_DISABLED outranks TINT_STATUS_GAINING_SUBDUAL_DAMAGE in `Drawable::updateDrawable`'s ladder (Drawable.cpp:1230-1253).

## Live
`UnitRenderInput::from_renderable` (Main/src/presentation_frame/unit_render.rs:429-435) computes `status_tint` via `drawable_status_tint_rgb(disabled_emp || disabled_hacked || disabled_unmanned, gaining_subdual || disabled_subdued, weapon_bonus_frenzy, infantry)`. Only EMP/HACKED/UNMANNED feed the dark-gray branch:
- UNMANNED wrongly included (C++ 'Doh^3. Unmanned is no tint too', Object.cpp:2112) — Jarmen-sniped vehicles glow dark gray in live, untinted in C++.
- UNDERPOWERED missing (live sets `obj.status.disabled_underpowered` from `update_power_disabled_state`, crates_radar_power.rs:1098, but presentation never tints) — low-power buildings stay normal-colored in live, dark gray in C++.
- PARALYZED, FREEFALL, DEFAULT, AWESTRUCK, BRAINWASHED, SCRIPT_UNDERPOWERED also missing.
- disabled_subdued feeds the blue SUBDUAL branch; C++ DISABLED_SUBDUED = dark gray with precedence.

## Player-visible
Low-power base: every powered building should turn dark gray (classic ZH low-power look) but stays bright in live. Subdual-disabled units show blue instead of dark gray. Sniped (unmanned) vehicles show a dark tint C++ never applies.
close_reason: Dark tint is EMP/hacked/paralyzed/underpowered/freefall/subdued/default/script_underpowered; unmanned excluded.

title: Live host: night maps never set MODELCONDITION_NIGHT on drawables (TOD ignored by presentation)
description: C++ / leftover / live / player-visible. C++ applies map TimeOfDay to every drawable at map load: W3DTerrainLogic.cpp:165-167 calls TheWritableGlobalData->setTimeOfDay + TheGameClient->setTimeOfDay (W3DGameClient.cpp:148-162), GameClient::setTimeOfDay walks all drawables into Drawable::setTimeOfDay (Drawable.cpp:4344-4354) which sets MODELCONDITION_NIGHT when tod==TIME_OF_DAY_NIGHT and restarts TOD ambient sounds; every newly created object also gets the bit at drawable bind (Object.cpp:2971-2974, m_forceModelsToFollowTimeOfDay defaults true, GlobalData.cpp:676). Live Main parses map time_of_day into global data (script_loader.rs:1040-1046, used only to pick lighting rows) but the presentation NIGHT bit comes from world_env.rs:619-620 is_night = weather_state.current_weather.contains("night"/"evening") — the runtime weather string is only ever normal/snowy/clear on map load (world_save.rs apply_world_info_weather), so is_night is always false on night maps; unit_render.rs:1117-1121 then clears the NIGHT bit on every unit. The GameClient refresh_drawable_time_of_day path (meta_event_impl/player.rs:332) sets the bit per drawable but is only triggered by the DEMO_TIME_OF_DAY demo command (dispatch.rs:541-552), never at map load. Result: on night maps (C++ TIME_OF_DAY_NIGHT) the live host renders day condition states — no lit-window/night-skin NIGHT models — while scene lighting does darken, so the mismatch is obvious. Fix: derive world_env is_night (and the drawable-map refresh) from global data time_of_day == Night after map load, mirroring C++ W3DTerrainLogic.cpp:165-167 + Object.cpp:2971-2974.
close_reason: world_env is_night follows GlobalData TimeOfDay::Night, not weather string.

title: Auto-reload clip state never refreshed when ClipReloadTime elapses (ammo stays 0, status stays ReloadingClip, RELOADING anim stuck)
description: C++/leftover/live three-way mismatch on the clip auto-reload completion. C++ (source of truth): Weapon.cpp:2628-2634 privateFireWeapon empties the clip -> reloadAmmo -> reloadWithBonus (Weapon.cpp:1884-1892) immediately refills m_ammoInClip to clipSize and sets m_whenWeCanFireAgain = now + ClipReloadTime; Weapon::getStatus (Weapon.cpp:2740-2755) lazily flips to READY_TO_FIRE the frame the reload elapses; ObjectWeaponStatusHelper (Module/ObjectWeaponStatusHelper.h:55) ticks every frame calling Object::adjustModelConditionForWeaponStatus (Object.cpp:4683-4752), which clears WSF_RELOADING once ready (or when not attacking) and pushes updateDrawableClipStatus(getRemainingAmmo()=FULL, clipSize) so HUD pips show a full clip; WeaponSet.cpp:869-877 keeps a PreferredAgainst weapon selected while merely reloading (weaponIsReady = status != OUT_OF_AMMO). Leftover GameEngine port (GameLogic/src/helpers/object_helpers.rs) models this via weapon instance reload_with_bonus/status. Live host (Code/Main): consume_ammo_on_fire_named (src/game_logic/object/rtb.rs:49-97) leaves weapon.ammo == Some(0) after the clip empties; the refill only happens inside the NEXT consume call (rtb.rs:73-74) — no tick-time refill exists (only reload_all_ammo and airfield rearm refill). refresh_weapon_fire_status is only invoked after a fire event (src/game_logic/object/attack.rs:389), so weapon_fire_status stays ReloadingClip and MC_BIT_RELOADING_* stays set long after the interval elapses. Player-visible on live path for every auto-reload clip weapon without AutoReloadWhenIdle (Patriot, Comanche rocket pods, SCUD toxin secondary, Tomahawk, etc.): (1) ammo pips / host_authoritative_projectile_clip_statuses (world_objects/host_ops_writeback.rs:1470-1505) and get_ammo_pip_showing_info -> presentation_frame/build.rs:784 report 0 rounds indefinitely after the reload completes where C++ reports a full clip; (2) the unit model stays in the RELOADING animation until its next shot where C++ clears it the frame the reload ends (or on attack end); (3) ini_preferred_slot_usable (object/weapons.rs) drops PreferredAgainst auto-selection during AND after the reload where C++ keeps it.
close_reason: Live host now completes auto-reload when ClipReloadTime elapses: complete_elapsed_auto_reload_clips refills ammo (C++ reloadWithBonus) and refresh_weapon_fire_status flips READY (C++ getStatus); ObjectWeaponStatusHelper-equivalent per-frame tick in world_tick/ai.rs.

title: [Crush] Pair collide runs one direction only — crushers with higher id never crush
description:
## C++
PartitionContactList::processContactList (PartitionManager.cpp:2479-2489) calls obj->onCollide(other) AND other->onCollide(obj) for every geom-colliding pair. Each side's PhysicsBehavior::onCollide -> checkForOverlapCollision (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1424) runs from its own perspective: the crusher side applies front/back/total crush points + HUGE DAMAGE_CRUSH; infantry victims die via SquishCollide::onCollide. Dead infantry also return TRUE from AIUpdateInterface::processCollision (AIUpdate.cpp:1530-1534) when the other can TEST_SQUISH_ONLY them, so crushers shove corpses aside.

## Leftover
GameEngine physics_collide/physics_crush ports both sides; not the live path.

## Live
tick_physics_collisions_all (world_tick/shock.rs:96-127) dedups pairs by (lo,hi) and calls try_physics_collide(a_id, b_id) with a = the lower ObjectId (mobile_ids sorted ascending); the reverse direction runs only via `else if` when the first call returns false — but try_physics_collide (world_tick/physics.rs:210-377) returns true on every path when both objects exist (ignore/parachute -> true; crush 'self being crushed -> passive' -> true; ai_process_collision !allow_force -> true; immobile bounce -> true). apply_overlap_crush_check (physics.rs:463-480) is only invoked with a as crusher, and the infantry squish lives only inside the crusher-side check_for_overlap_collision (physics_motion.rs:181-345).

## Player-visible
When the crusher's id is higher than the victim's — every tank built after pre-placed map infantry/cars, the common case — the victim-side call returns early (passive overlap) and the crusher side never runs: no squish/crush kill, no front/back crush flags, no CrushDie sounds, no corpse shoving; the tank ghosts through infantry and cars. Crushes only land when the crusher happens to have the lower id (all existing tests create the tank before the infantry), so drive-over kills inconsistently work.
close_reason: tick_physics_collisions_all runs both onCollide after geom hit so higher-id crushers crush.

title: [Player] Live MaxSimultaneous cap is a hero-name table, not INI
description:
## C++
`Player::canBuildMoreOfType` (`Player.cpp:2853-2876`) reads `whatToBuild->getMaxSimultaneousOfType()` (`ThingTemplate.cpp:1440-1448`: numeric INI or `TheGameLogic->getSuperweaponRestriction()` when `DeterminedBySuperweaponRestriction`). `countExisting` (`:2825-2849`) counts living objects by `isEquivalentTo` **or** shared `MaxSimultaneousLinkKey`, plus queued units for non-structures.

## Leftover player
`GameLogic/src/player/production.rs:81-164` `can_build_more_of_type` uses `template.get_max_simultaneous_of_type()` + link key + factory queues. Leftover `ThingTemplate` parses numeric `MaxSimultaneousOfType` (`thing_template.rs:3488-3493`).

## Live leftover player
`Main/src/game_logic/thing.rs` stores only `max_simultaneous_link_key` and the SW-restriction bool — **no numeric cap field**. `spawn_templates.rs:2373` only detects the `DeterminedBySuperweaponRestriction` token.
`can_make_unit` (`world_scripts/ui_production.rs:1475-1488`) calls `unit_max_simultaneous_of_type_residual` (`host_production_buildable_command_residual.rs:719-760`): a hardcoded Burton/Lotus/Kell name table (comment admits "not full INI parse matrix" / unique buildings). Count (`:1268-1290`) is exact template-name only — no `isEquivalentTo`, no link key.
Live leftover `Player` has no `canBuildMoreOfType`.

## Player-visible
Players can queue a second copy of any INI-capped unit that is not a named hero (unique buildings the residual comment itself lists as `MaxSimultaneousOfType=1`). Rebuild-hole / reskin link keys are ignored, so a hole plus original does not consume the cap. Leftover player's INI-correct gate is unused.

Distinct from closed hq-egcq (leftover BuildAssistant canMakeUnit ignored all limits — live now has a residual table, not INI).
close_reason: Live MaxSimultaneousOfType is parsed from INI (numeric or DeterminedBySuperweaponRestriction); can_make_unit and place count equivalent/link-key instead of the hero-name table.

title: [Dock] Queued docker death or re-task never cancels its live approach reservation — dock jams forever
description:
## C++
Any exit from AI_DOCK frees the dock: AIDockState::onExit (AIStates.cpp:6108-6117) halts+deletes the sub-machine, and AIDockMachine::halt (AIDock.cpp:46-60) calls dock->cancelDock(owner), freeing the approach slot + activeDocker (DockUpdate.cpp:349-376). New player orders reset the outer machine (StateMachine::internalSetState fires onExit(EXIT_RESET), StateMachine.cpp:340-341), and owner death tears the machine down the same way — the reserved DockWaiting slot never outlives its docker.

## Live
host_supply_gather.rs tick_live_dock_approach:34 queue.evict_dead(|_| true) — the predicate says every owner is alive, so evict_dead (:115-121) evicts nothing (dead mechanism, neutered call). cancel_live_dock_approach is only reachable via release_dock_if_holder (support_states.rs:6271) on the docker's own successful state transitions. Nothing fires on destruction (create_destroy_die.rs mark_object_for_destruction / destroy_list_bounty.rs process_destroy_list have no dock cleanup) and nothing fires on new player orders (command_executor has no dock release — re-tasking a Gathering/ReturningResources/SeekingRepair truck just overwrites ai_state).

## Player-visible
A killed or re-tasked queued truck/chinook leaves a ghost owner with reached=true at the lowest slot index. promote_active (host_supply_gather.rs:243-256) then returns the ghost every time dock_active_docker is empty, so tick_live_dock_approach never returns ClearToAct for any live docker — the supply center / warehouse / repair pad is permanently jammed and income stops until map end. Fixed-size queues (warehouse 9/5, repair 5, USA center 9) additionally lose capacity until is_clear_to_approach goes false, which also makes find_nearest_harvestable_supply_within skip the warehouse (object_queries.rs:131-135). One lost queued truck bricks the whole dock for every player.
close_reason: Closed

title: [Weapon] AutoChooseSources SECONDARY NONE ignored so Jarmen auto-snipes between rifle shots
description:
## C++
`WeaponSet::chooseBestWeaponForTarget` (`WeaponSet.cpp:816-822`) skips a slot unless `AutoChooseSources` includes the command source (or `CMD_DEFAULT_SWITCH_WEAPON`). `AutoChooseSources = SECONDARY NONE` means the slot is special/button-only: Jarmen Kell `GLAJarmenKellVehiclePilotSniperRifle`, Missile Defender laser, Toxin Tractor sprayer. During PRIMARY `DelayBetweenShots` the chooser keeps the unready primary as backup and never auto-picks the NONE secondary.

## Leftover
`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/weapon/weapon_set.rs` parses AutoChoose masks. Leftover `object/unit/combat.rs` / `object_combat.rs` are dual-world empty and never run.

## Live
`Main/src/game_logic/object/weapons.rs` `select_combat_weapon_slot` never reads AutoChooseSources for PRIMARY/SECONDARY (only hardcodes TERTIARY never-auto for Comanche pods). `thing.rs` stores `primary_auto_choose_none` for spawn, not chooser. Combat tick (`world_tick/combat.rs:267`) uses this chooser.

## Player-visible
Jarmen rifle Delay 1000ms / snipe Delay 0: after one rifle shot the live chooser auto-fires the 30s KILL_PILOT clip on ordinary attack — unmanned tanks and a wasted snipe. Missile Defender laser (300wu, 500ms) auto-fires during the 1000ms missile delay instead of staying special-only.
close_reason: C++ WeaponSet::chooseBestWeaponForTarget (WeaponSet.cpp:816-822) skips a slot unless AutoChooseSources includes the command source (or CMD_DEFAULT_SWITCH_WEAPON); AutoChooseSources=SECONDARY NONE is button-only. Live select_combat_weapon_slot already gates on ThingTemplate::slot_allows_auto_choose. Object::new bind_weapon_set_from_live_assets now always stamps retail SECONDARY NONE for Jarmen/Missile Defender/Toxin Tractor when the mask is still the 0xffffffff default, INI bits still win, create residuals re-stamp after binding the special secondary, and combat any_ready ignores NONE secondaries unless the player locked the slot — so rifle DelayBetweenShots no longer auto-fires the KILL_PILOT clip or MD laser.

title: [Airfield] GetRepaired heals airborne at TimeForFullHeal when landing fails
description:
## C++
`ActionManager::canGetRepairedAt` (`ActionManager.cpp:157-162`) only authorizes aircraft at `KINDOF_FS_AIRFIELD` while above terrain. `JetAIUpdate::privateGetRepaired` (`JetAIUpdate.cpp:2344-2356`) then `doLandingCommand` — the jet lands and parks. `ChinookAIUpdate::privateGetRepaired` (`ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:1177-1196`) `setAirfieldForHealing` + `MOVE_TO_AND_LAND`. Healing is `ParkingPlaceBehavior::update` (`ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:649-691`) at authored `HealAmountPerSecond` (AmericaAirfield **10 HP/s**) via `setHealee`, not `RepairDockUpdate::TimeForFullHeal`. Airfields have no RepairDockUpdate. A full hangar / failed reserve means no land and no heal.

## Leftover
`parking_place_behavior.rs` ports `setHealee` + 5 Hz pulse. Wave-310 empty dual-world gates leftover on the host path.

## Live
`command_executor/leftover.rs:687-698` `execute_get_repaired` tries `try_jet_enter_or_repair_airfield` → `do_jet_landing_command` (`world_tick/airfield.rs:1932-1974`). That returns **false** for every helipad/helo (`object_is_produced_at_helipad`) and when `reserve_airfield_parking_space` fails. Fallthrough is `AIState::SeekingRepair`. `support_states.rs:2745-2828` then applies `RepairDockUpdate` TimeForFullHeal (`(max-current)/5s`) as soon as the aircraft is within `HOST_REPAIR_INTERACT_RANGE` **14** and still `is_above_terrain`.

## Player-visible
Comanche / Chinook / Helix (and any jet that cannot reserve a stall) hover 14 units from the airfield and finish a full repair in 5 seconds. Retail they must land and heal at ~10 HP/s. A full 4-pad airfield still repairs a 5th jet in the air.

title: [Beacon] Enemy hide is unused — enemy beacons still draw and leak on the minimap
description:
## Why
C++ `BeaconClientUpdate::hideBeacon` hides the drawable and stops smoke so enemies never see ally beacons. Live only inserts an id into a process HashSet that presentation never reads, then still freezes the position onto the minimap.

## C++

`GameLogicDispatch.cpp:1698-1716` MSG_REMOVE_BEACON local-non-owner also `hideBeacon()`.

## Leftover

## Live

`execute_place_beacon` still `note_beacon_placed` for enemy drops (`:906-917`).
`presentation_frame/build.rs:1758-1762` dumps all `host_beacons`.
`presentation_frame/apply.rs:257-268` draws every beacon as a local-player-colored `minimap_beacons` dot.

## Player-visible

## Not a duplicate

title: [Worker] Gather never takes exclusive AS_SUPPLY_TRUCK — idle dozer resume steals ferrying workers
description:
## Why
C++ WorkerAIUpdate is a dual-brain: WorkerStateMachine is either AS_DOZER or AS_SUPPLY_TRUCK. Live gather never enters exclusive supply mode, so the dozer BUILD slot + idle resume keep running and steal a ferrying GLA worker back to the scaffold (or freeze it for everyone else).

## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/AIUpdate/WorkerAIUpdate.cpp`
- `AS_DOZER` / `AS_SUPPLY_TRUCK` (`:49-53`). `update` (`:257-288`) runs only the matching sub-machine; harvest branch also `setWeaponSetFlag(WEAPONSET_MINE_CLEARING_DETAIL)`.
- Enter supply: `supplyTruckSubMachineWantsToEnter` (`:1211-1224`) = `isForcedIntoWantingState() || masterState == AI_DOCK`.

title: [Chinook] Combat drop rappel is Y=0 path, not aiRappelInto garrison

After dump, `evacuate_container_now` (`registries.rs:770-772`) calls `command_evac([p.x, p.z, 0.0], true)` at the **LZ**. `MoveToAndEvacAndExitInit` (`host_combat_chinook.rs:718-720`) overwrites `original_pos = self.pos` (LZ). `HeadOffMap` then `dest = original_pos` (already here). `tick` only destroys when outside `map_lo`/`map_hi`, so the Chinook sits at the drop site forever.

Closed hq-5a7lk added the leftover/host state names; this leftover remaining path still never flies off-map.

## C++

## Leftover

title: [Chinook] Landed move-to-evac takeoff drops the pending evac dest
description:
## Symptom
A landed Chinook told to move-to-and-evacuate a distant point takes off (or taxis) and never flies to the dest / never dumps.

## C++
`aiDoCommand` (`ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:1263-1286`): if landed and dest farther than 3, `m_pendingCommand.store(*parms); m_hasPendingCommand=true; setMyState(TAKING_OFF)`. `update` (`:1073-1078`) when parent-idle reconstitutes the pending evac and issues `MOVE_TO_AND_EVAC[_AND_EXIT_INIT]`. Commands issued during takeoff/landing/combat-drop are also queued (`:1241-1248`).

## Leftover
`handle_command` (`chinook_ai_update.rs:1733-1745`) stores `pending_command` then TakingOff. Dual-world empty — not live.

## Live
Two leftover remaining holes:

1. `execute_move_to_and_evacuate` (`transport.rs:618-633`) never calls `HostChinookAI::command_evac`. Landed Chinooks path with the taxiing locomotor and dump via `pending_evacuate_on_stop` — no takeoff-first.

2. `command_evac` (`host_combat_chinook.rs:657-664`) when landed+far does `enter_state(TakingOff); return;` **without** storing dest/and_exit. `enter_takeoff_or_landing` overwrites `dest` to the vertical takeoff point. There is no `m_pendingCommand`. After takeoff `succeed()` goes Idle; passengers stay aboard.

## Player-visible
Script/AI `AICMD_MOVE_TO_POSITION_AND_EVACUATE` on a landed Chinook: either taxis on the ground or lifts off and hovers. Troops never arrive at the ordered dump point. Closed hq-5a7lk claimed command_evac; the pending-command reconstitution is still missing.
close_reason: Live host Chinook: leave DO_COMBAT_DROP, aiRappelInto roof dest, HeadOffMap spawn dest, pending evac dest on takeoff, hover geom+MinDropHeight, regular transport install, COMBATDROP_INTO gate.

## C++

Scripts that sequence "play briefing then spawn/move" wait until the VO ends.

## Leftover

`GameClientScriptActionHandler::is_speech_complete` tracks the real `add_audio_event` handle (`script_action_handler.rs:1266-1268`).

Live leftover executor therefore treats every speech as finished one frame later.

## Player-visible
Scripts gated on "speech finished" immediately continue: next spawn, camera cut, or objective fires over the first syllable instead of after the line.
close_reason: note_speech_started/is_speech_complete use TheAudio get_audio_length_ms converted to logic frames, matching C++ isSpeechComplete.

title: [Speech] SPEECH_PLAY ignores allowOverlap and never hits TheAudio
description:
## Why
C++ `SPEECH_PLAY` queues logical speech on `TheAudio` with `setUninterruptable(!allowOverlap)` so briefing lines do not talk over each other unless the script allows it. Live host `MissionScriptActionHandler::speech_play` ignores `allow_overlap` and `push_sound`s the name as a UI SFX.

## C++
`ScriptActions.cpp:6780-6781` `doSpeechPlay(name, param1 int)`.
`doSpeechPlay` (`:2743-2764`): `AudioEventRTS` + `setIsLogicalAudio(true)` + local player index + `setUninterruptable(!allowOverlap)` + `TheAudio->addAudioEvent`. Subtitle `DIALOGEVENT:{name}Subtitle` for 8000ms when the label exists and is not `*`.

## Leftover
Leftover executor `do_speech_play` (`actions_player_display_camera.rs:482-501`) reads `allow_overlap` and calls `handler.speech_play(name, allow_overlap)`.
`GameClientScriptActionHandler::speech_play` (`GameClient/src/core/script_action_handler.rs:1229-1241`) matches C++: `TheAudio::add_audio_event`, `set_uninterruptable(!allow_overlap)`, tracks the speech wait-slot handle.

## Live
`initialize_scripts` installs `MissionScriptActionHandler`, overwriting the GameClient handler.
`mission_scripts.rs:2521-2528` `speech_play` takes `_allow_overlap` unused; `note_speech_started` + `push_sound(name)`.
`scripts_camera.rs:529-530` drains sounds via `play_ui_sound` → `translate_audio_event` + generic `AudioEventRequest` (same path as UI clicks). No `set_uninterruptable`, no AT_Streaming speech event.

## Player-visible
Campaign briefing VO overlaps or is cut by the next line regardless of World Builder Allow Overlap. Speech is not the C++ uninterruptable streaming event (music was specially forwarded to TheAudio; speech was not).
close_reason: Live SPEECH_PLAY now queues TheAudio with setIsLogicalAudio + setUninterruptable(!allowOverlap), matching C++ doSpeechPlay. Dropped the UI SFX push_sound path.
