title: [Energy] Host power scan still counts EMP/hacked producers
description:
## C++
`Object::friend_adjustPowerForPlayer` (`Object.cpp:3770-3782`) returns immediately when the object is disabled and `getEnergyProduction() > 0` — "Disabledness only affects Producers, not Consumers."

`Object::onDisabledEdge` (`Object.cpp:3825-3854`) when a producer becomes disabled/enabled walks PowerPlantUpgrade + OverchargeBehavior and `adjustPower(energyProduction + EnergyBonus, !becomingDisabled)`. EMP, hack, unmanned, etc. drop that plant from the grid the same frame.

## Rust
Leftover `Object::adjust_power_for_player` (`object_upgrade.rs:362-390`) ports the disabled-producer skip, and leftover `on_disabled_edge` (`:322-356`) adjusts player energy. Live host never uses that path.

Live `GameLogic::update_player_resources` (`resources_income.rs:46-56`) folds `power_provided` / `power_consumed` for every `is_constructed() && is_alive()` owner object. No `is_disabled()` / EMP / hacked / unmanned filter. `apply_disabled_emp` / `apply_disabled_hacked` only flip status bits (`object/install.rs:531-572`).

## Evidence
C++: `if (isDisabled() && getTemplate()->getEnergyProduction() > 0) return;`
C++: `controller->getEnergy()->adjustPower(powerToAdjust, !becomingDisabled);`
Rust host scan: `.filter(|object| object.is_constructed() && object.is_alive())` then `produced.saturating_add(object.power_provided)`.

## Player-visible
EMP Pulse, Black Lotus Disable Building, or Kell snipe on a Cold Fusion / Nuclear Reactor leaves its +5/+10 (and rods/overcharge bonus) on the owner's grid. Defenses and factories stay powered while the plant is dark.
close_reason: live power scan skips disabled producers (C++ friend_adjustPowerForPlayer)

title: [Science] Leftover first_capable walks sample table, not ScienceStore::getPurchasableSciences
description:
## C++
`ScienceStore::getPurchasableSciences` (`Science.cpp:301-329`) walks every `m_sciences` final override: skip cost==0 (not purchasable), skip already owned, then `playerHasPrereqsForScience` → purchasable else `playerHasRootPrereqsForScience` → potentiallyPurchasable. It does not consult a hardcoded name list. ControlBar / scripts / AI consume those two vectors.

`playerHasPrereqsForScience` (`:257-275`) and `playerHasRootPrereqsForScience` (`:278-296`) read the same store that parsed Science.ini.

## Rust
Live `ScienceStore::get_purchasable_sciences` (`rts/science.rs:693-725`) matches the C++ walk, but the live host never calls it.

Leftover host Alt+G / `PurchaseScience` (`selection.rs:458-487`) calls `first_capable_purchase_science_residual` (`wave109.rs:917-935`), which walks `SCIENCE_STORE_TABLE_WAVE109` (~30 sample rows). The table omits `SCIENCE_CashBounty2` (so CashBounty3 is unreachable), SpectreGunship, EmergencyRepair2/3, Paradrop2/3, LeafletDrop, and every other Science.ini purchasable not in the sample.

Leftover `ini_science::ScienceStore` has no `getPurchasableSciences` / `playerHasPrereqsForScience` / `playerHasRootPrereqsForScience`. Leftover `science_prereqs_met_residual` (`wave109.rs:854-877`) asks the empty live rts store first, then a 2-slot residual row — it never reads leftover `ini_science` prereqs even though host INI populated that store.

Closed hq-nk2eh was the old 5–7 faction array. This leftover remaining still does not call `getPurchasableSciences`.

## Evidence
`Science.cpp:257-329` vs `wave109.rs:459-703,834-935` vs `selection.rs:458-487` vs leftover `ini_science.rs` (no purchasable/prereq APIs) vs live `rts/science.rs:693-725` (unused by host).

## Player-visible
Generals points still auto-buy only from the sample table. CashBounty2 never appears so CashBounty3 cannot chain. Rank 3/5 extras in Science.ini (Spectre, Leaflet, repair/paradrop tiers) stay unobtainable via leftover first-capable even when leftover `ini_science` has their real cost/prereqs.
close_reason: first_capable_purchase_science_residual walks leftover ini_science + live rts ScienceStore::get_purchasable_sciences (Science.ini order). Sample table is empty-store fallback only.

title: [Science] Host INI Science blocks populate leftover ini_science; live GrantScience/scripts use empty rts store
description:
## C++
One `TheScienceStore`. `INI::parseScienceDefinition` (`Science.cpp:355-358`) calls `ScienceStore::friend_parseScienceDefinition` (`:138-210`), which inserts into `m_sciences`. `GrantScienceUpgrade` (`GrantScienceUpgrade.cpp:70-71`), `ScriptActions` grant/purchase (`ScriptActions.cpp:5910-5925`), and `Player::grantScience` / `attemptToPurchaseScience` (`Player.cpp:2569-2634`) all call `TheScienceStore->getScienceFromInternalName` / `isScienceGrantable` / `getSciencePurchaseCost` / `playerHasPrereqsForScience` on that same store.

`getScienceFromInternalName` (`Science.cpp:67-74`) is NameKey identity: empty → `SCIENCE_INVALID`, else `(ScienceType)TheNameKeyGenerator->nameToKey(name)` even if the science is not yet registered. Callers then fail via `isScienceGrantable` / `isValidScience`.

## Rust
Two stores:

- Leftover `ini_science::ScienceStore` (`Common/src/common/ini/ini_science.rs`). Host `register_science_template` (`ini_template_loader.rs:1565-1586`) and `load_all_ini_templates` (`:598-601`) parse Science.ini from BIG archives into this leftover store only.
- Live `rts::science::ScienceStore` (`Common/src/common/rts/science.rs`). `ScienceSubsystem` (`:1168-1185`) loads `Data/INI/Science.ini` via `load_from_paths`. Host Main never registers/inits `ScienceSubsystem`.

Live GameLogic `GrantScienceUpgrade::resolve_science_type` (`grant_science_upgrade.rs:92-107`), `science_management.rs` grant/purchase (`:393-510`), and script `PlayerGrantScience` all call `rts::get_science_store()`. Live `get_science_from_internal_name` (`science.rs:462-471`) returns `SCIENCE_INVALID` unless the name is in that empty map.

Leftover host purchase (`player.rs:1006-1041`) consults leftover `ini_science` for cost, but leftover `science_ini_prereq_names` (`wave109.rs:834-847`) only reads the live rts store.

## Evidence
`Science.cpp:67-74,138-210,355-358` vs `ini_template_loader.rs:538-601,1565-1586` vs `rts/science.rs:462-471,1168-1185` vs `grant_science_upgrade.rs:92-107` vs `science_management.rs:393-510`. Main has no `ScienceSubsystem` init.

## Player-visible
PaladinTank / Pathfinder `GrantScienceUpgrade` never grants. Campaign `PLAYER_GRANT_SCIENCE` / `PLAYER_PURCHASE_SCIENCE` no-ops. Crate Player purchase sees an empty store. Science.ini is loaded, but into the leftover store nobody in GameLogic reads.
close_reason: register_science_template now ingest_definition into live rts ScienceStore as well as leftover ini_science. GrantScience/scripts/get_purchasable_sciences read the same INI-backed store.

title: [SpecialAbilityUpdate] Leftover steal/disable recharge is click-time or missing
description:
## C++
`SpecialAbilityUpdate::startPreparation` (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:1062-1067`) calls `getMySPM()->markSpecialPowerTriggered(NULL)` only after the unit is in range, unpacked, and facing — that is when the special-power reload starts. StealCashHack `ReloadTime = 2000`ms. DisableVehicleHack `ReloadTime = 0`. A cancelled approach does not start recharge.

## Rust
`DoSpecialPower` leftover (`command_executor/special_power.rs:255-331`) calls `consume_special_power_charge_for` on the click, then `execute_steal_cash_hack` / `execute_disable_vehicle_hack`. Dedicated `CommandType::StealCashHack` / `DisableVehicleHack` (`abilities.rs:642-819`) queue `PendingSpecialAbility` with **no** consume. Neither leftover completion arm calls `start_power_recharge` / `markSpecialPowerTriggered`. Capture and HDB correctly consume in `start_*_preparation`.

## Evidence
C++: recharge in `startPreparation` after unpack.
Rust leftover: consume-on-click (generic special-power path) or never (dedicated command). Completion: steal/disable just `stop_moving`.

## Player-visible effect
Via the command-button special-power path, Lotus's 2s steal cooldown starts when she is clicked on a distant supply center — cancel the walk and the power is already on cooldown. Via the dedicated leftover command, she can steal again immediately with no reload.
close_reason: leftover steal/disable consume at startPreparation (special_power.rs + leftover SA channel)

title: [SpecialAbilityUpdate] Leftover Burton/TNT plant skips unpack
description:
## C++
`SpecialAbilityUpdate::startUnpacking` + `handlePackingProcessing` (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:770-794`, `618-678`). Burton timed/remote C4 and Tank Hunter TNT use `UnpackTime` **5500**ms (`FlipOwnerAfterUnpacking` for Burton). During unpack, `LoseStealthOnTrigger` + `PreTriggerUnstealthTime` **5000**ms calls `StealthUpdate::markAsDetected` when `m_animFrames < preTriggerUnstealthFrames`. Plant happens only after unpack completes and preparation (0 for these) triggers.

No unpack timer, no `MODELCONDITION_UNPACKING`, no pre-trigger unstealth. Constants `BURTON_CHARGE_UNPACK_TIME_MS` / `BURTON_CHARGE_PRE_TRIGGER_UNSTEALTH_MS` exist only in honesty packs. Crate path is dual-world gated.

title: [SpecialAbilityUpdate] Leftover never flees after planting C4/TNT
description:
## C++
`SpecialAbilityUpdate::finishAbility` (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:1733-1818`). If `FleeRangeAfterCompletion` is set and there is a valid target/pos, C++ computes a flee point along `±getUnitDirectionVector2D() * fleeRange` (add if flip-after-pack/unpack, else subtract), steers away from the closest own `KINDOF_MINE` in that radius, applies a zero motive force so AI skips the idle pop, `aiMoveToPosition`, and `ignoreObstacle(target)`. Burton/TNT INI `FleeRangeAfterCompletion = 100`.

## Rust
Leftover plant arms (`support_states.rs:3056-3080`) only `stop_moving` + `set_target(None)`. `BURTON_FLEE_RANGE_AFTER_CHARGE = 100` is honesty-only; no leftover call site applies it. Crate `finish_ability` ports flee but is Wave 296 gated.

## Evidence
C++: `if (m_fleeRangeAfterCompletion && validTarget) { dir.scale(flee); aiMoveToPosition; ignoreObstacle; }`
Rust leftover: `obj.stop_moving(); obj.set_target(None);`

## Player-visible effect
Burton and Tank Hunters stand on the charge they just planted. Retail they immediately run ~100 wu away (and avoid walking back onto a previous mine).
close_reason: leftover flee after plant 100wu flip-after-unpack + own-mine steer

title: [SpecialAbilityUpdate] Leftover Lotus steal/disable skip unpack+prep+pack
description:
## C++
`SpecialAbilityUpdate::update` / `startUnpacking` / `startPreparation` / `startPacking` (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:388-442`, `770-794`, `963-1077`, `717-767`). After `isWithinStartAbilityRange`, C++ faces, unpacks (`UnpackTime`: Lotus steal **6730**ms, disable **2000**ms), then `startPreparation` (`PreparationTime` **6000**/**2000**ms): creates `BinaryDataStream` laser, sets `OBJECT_STATUS_IS_USING_ABILITY`, plays `PrepSoundLoop`, calls `markSpecialPowerTriggered`. On success it packs (`PackTime` **5800**/**1000**ms) with `Voice*Complete`. Lotus `StealthForbiddenConditions` includes `USING_ABILITY`.

## Rust
Crate `special_ability_update.rs` ports the state machine but Wave 296 `dual_world_registry_unavailable()` (`OBJECT_REGISTRY` empty) no-ops `trigger_ability_effect` / range / approach. Live leftover `AIState::SpecialAbility` (`support_states.rs:2661-3357`) walks to `BLACK_LOTUS_START_ABILITY_RANGE` **150** then instantly `steal_cash_from_team` / `apply_disabled_hacked`. No unpack, face, prep, pack, `BinaryDataStream`, or `set_status_using_ability`. Capture and HDB have dedicated channels; steal/disable do not. Host comments: "Not full SpecialAbilityUpdate preparation timers / packing".

## Evidence
C++: unpack → face → prep (laser + `IS_USING_ABILITY` + `markSpecialPowerTriggered`) → trigger → pack.
Rust leftover: `StealCashHack`/`DisableVehicleHack` arms apply the effect the first tick inside range 150 and `stop_moving`.

## Player-visible effect
Black Lotus steals $1000 or disables a vehicle the frame she enters range, stays cloaked (no `USING_ABILITY` break), and never plays the 8–13s unpack/hack/pack animation. Retail is a long visible hack the defender can interrupt.
close_reason: leftover Lotus steal/disable unpack/prep/pack + USING_ABILITY

title: [CommandXlat] Hijack/carbomb/sabotage context leftover unused; live attacks instead
description:
## C++
`evaluateContextCommand` (`CommandXlat.cpp:1856-1918`) before enter/attack: if not force-attack and `canSelectedObjectsDoAction` is true, hijack / convert-to-carbomb / sabotage issue `createEnterMessage` (`MSG_ENTER`). Hints are `MSG_HIJACK_HINT` / `MSG_CONVERT_TO_CARBOMB_HINT` / `MSG_SABOTAGE_HINT`. Attack is later (`:1962`).

## Rust
Leftover `evaluate_context_action` (`command_translator.rs:489-506`) ports the same order via `selection_can_hijack_target` / `selection_can_convert_to_carbomb_target` / `selection_can_sabotage_target` (`dual_world.rs:335-353, 616-628`). Unused on the live OS click path.

Live `classify_right_click_target_from_presentation` (`command_system/system_impl.rs:1152-1196`) does ordinary Enter (capacity/garrison) then `AttackObject` for enemies. No hijack / carbomb / sabotage predicates. Hijacker vs enemy vehicle is therefore an attack unless the control-bar button armed `PendingUnitAbility::Hijack`.

## Evidence
C++ :1856-1918 before :1941 enter and :1962 attack. Leftover `command_translator.rs:489-506`. Live `system_impl.rs:1152-1196` enter-then-attack only; hijack is button-only (`ui_commands.rs:1798-1800`).

## Player-visible
Right-clicking an enemy vehicle with a Hijacker (or a terrorist carbomb / saboteur on a building) issues Attack instead of Enter. Players must arm the ability button first. Retail context-click does it automatically.
close_reason: Live classify_right_click_target_from_presentation now evaluates hijack/carbomb/sabotage before enter/attack (C++ evaluateContextCommand CommandXlat.cpp:1856-1962). Issues CommandType::Hijack/ConvertToCarbomb/Sabotage so live executors run; leftover evaluate_context_action already posted MSG_ENTER in that order.

title: [W3DModelDraw] validateCachedBones never fills pristine bone cache
description:
## C++
`ModelConditionInfo::validateCachedBones` (`W3DModelDraw.cpp:566-689`) is the producer for `m_pristineBones`. It `Create_Render_Obj`s the state model if needed, poses frame 0 (or last if `PRISTINE_BONE_POS_IN_FINAL_FRAME`), identity×scale, then `doSingleBoneName` for every `StandardPublicBone` and the state's `publicBones` (turret/weapon/extra). `validateStuff` (`:545`) calls this before turret/barrel validation. Every bone query (`getProjectileLaunchOffset` `:3275`, `getPristineBonePositionsForConditionState`) re-validates.

## Rust
Leftover `ModelConditionInfo.pristine_bones` (`Module/wthree_d_model_draw.rs:222`) is never filled. Live `validate_runtime_caches` (`types.rs:469-475`) only ORs `PRISTINE_BONES_VALID` if the map is already nonempty; there is no `validateCachedBones` port and no W3D load that inserts bones. The only writers are tests (`tests.rs`) and xfer load of an already-empty map (`module_data.rs:440-450`). `validate_turret_info` / `validate_weapon_barrel_info` early-return when the map is empty (`types.rs:311-312`, `:360-361`).

## Evidence
C++: `robj = Create_Render_Obj(...); doSingleBoneName(...)` into `m_pristineBones`.
Live: `if !self.pristine_bones.is_empty() { valid |= PRISTINE_BONES_VALID }` — never populated.
Leftover: map stays default-empty.

## Player-visible
Turret/weapon/public bone indices stay 0. Launch matrices stay identity, recoil/muzzle bones never resolve, `ParticleSysBone` attach falls back to origin. Distinct from closed recoil/FX beads: those assume barrel/pristine caches exist.
close_reason: Live ModelConditionInfo::validate_cached_bones now produces m_pristineBones like C++ validateCachedBones (W3DModelDraw.cpp:566-689): do_single_bone_name for StandardPublicBones + state publicBones via register_pristine_bone_lookup_hook. GameClient ensure_logic_draw_hooks registers Create_Render_Obj analog (THE_RENDER_BRIDGE hierarchy/HLod bind pose). Turret/barrel validation no longer early-outs on empty map after the valid bit is set.

title: [InGameUI] Live disregardDrawable is a no-op so destroyed units stay selected
description:
## C++
`InGameUI::disregardDrawable` (`InGameUI.cpp:3415-3420`) calls `deselectDrawable` so a dying/removed drawable leaves the selection list. `GameClient` destroy-drawable notifies InGameUI.

## Rust
Leftover crate `InGameUI::disregard_drawable` (`selection.rs:1000-1001`) correctly deselects. The live registered backend is `InGameUISubsystem::disregard_drawable` (`subsystems.rs:1900-1904`) which returns `Ok(())` and does nothing. `GameClient::destroy_drawable` notifies that subsystem, not leftover `InGameUI`.

## Evidence
Live init registers `InGameUISubsystem` (`impl_init.rs:589-596`), not leftover `gui/ingame_ui`. Subsystem impl is an empty `Ok(())`. Distinct from closed selection-list / MaxSelectionSize beads.

## Player-visible
When a selected unit dies or its drawable is destroyed, it remains in the selection: portrait, command buttons, and group orders still target a ghost until the player manually deselects.
close_reason: C++ InGameUI::disregardDrawable (InGameUI.cpp:3415) now maps to leftover InGameUI::disregard_drawable + live InGameUISubsystem::disregard_drawable calling InGameUI::disregard_live_drawable so destroy_drawable deselects.

title: [InGameUI] leftover setGUICommand never enters GUI_COMMAND mouse mode
description:
## C++
`InGameUI::setGUICommand` (`InGameUI.cpp:2865-2918`) is the leftover command-button arming path: skip during replay playback; reject buttons that do not `COMMAND_OPTION_NEED_TARGET`; set `m_mouseMode = MOUSEMODE_GUI_COMMAND`; store `m_pendingGUICommand`; set mouse cursor ARROW; `setRadiusCursor(command->getRadiusCursorType(), specialPower, weaponSlot)` so the targeting circle bleeds out from under the panel. Clearing the command restores `MOUSEMODE_DEFAULT` and `setRadiusCursorNone()`. `createCommandHint` (`:2710-2769`) then uses the GUI_COMMAND branch for valid/invalid cursors.

## Rust
Leftover `InGameUI::set_gui_command` (`leftover.rs:397-399`) only stores `Option<String>` — no playback skip, no NEED_TARGET reject, no `MouseMode::GuiCommand`, no radius cursor. Live control-bar `set_pending_command_with_visual` (`commands.rs:57-65`) stores a `PendingCommand` struct but never calls `set_mouse_mode(MouseMode::GuiCommand)`. `set_mouse_mode` exists (`impl_input.rs:509`, `helpers.rs:1988`) but nothing passes `GuiCommand`. `create_command_hint`'s GUI_COMMAND branch (`impl_input.rs:1203-1229`) is therefore dead on both leftover and live paths.

## Evidence
Grep `MouseMode::GuiCommand` / `set_mouse_mode(`: only definitions and the unused hint match-arm. Distinct from closed hq-d77h / hq-38as / hq-4ce57 (radius texture/size/draw) — this is leftover `setGUICommand` never entering GUI_COMMAND mouse mode so the hint/cursor branch never runs.

## Player-visible
Clicking a need-target command (guard, special power, mine, rally, beacon, …) does not switch into targeting mouse mode. The cursor stays the default world cursor instead of the button's targeting/invalid cursor, and the leftover GUI_COMMAND hint path never applies.
close_reason: C++ InGameUI::setGUICommand (InGameUI.cpp:2865) leftover InGameUI::set_gui_command now sets MouseMode::GuiCommand / Default, skips playback, rejects non-NEED_TARGET; live TheInGameUI::set_pending_command_with_visual arms GUI_COMMAND via arm_gui_command_mouse_mode.

title: [AIGuard] Return and crate leftover issue a parent MoveTo instead of InternalMoveTo
description:
## C++
`AIGuardReturnState` (`AIGuard.h:193`) **is** `AIInternalMoveToState`. `onEnter` (`AIGuard.cpp:602-625`) sets the post as `m_goalPosition`, `adjustDestination`, `setAdjustsDestination(true)`, then `AIInternalMoveToState::onEnter()`. `update` (`:629-640`) re-scans `lookForInnerTarget()` on `m_guardEnemyReturnScanRate` and otherwise runs the move-to loop. The unit stays in `AI_GUARD`.

`AIGuardPickUpCrateState` extends `AIPickUpCrateState` on the **guard** machine (`:744-770`).

## Rust
Live `AIGuardReturnState::classic_on_enter` (`guard.rs:1536`) leftover-issues `ai.ai_move_to_position(..., CommandSourceType::FromAi)`. That is `execute_command(MoveToPosition)` (`ai_commands.rs:129-151`): if the parent is not idle (Guard is never `isIdle`), it `set_temporary_state(MoveTo, 20s)` on the **parent** `AIStateMachine`, leaving Guard. Return `update` then only polls `CLOSE_ENOUGH` and never runs `lookForInnerTarget` while the temp MoveTo is active.

Crate pickup (`guard.rs:1678`) leftover-issues the same parent `ai_move_to_position`.

## Evidence
C++: `class AIGuardReturnState : public AIInternalMoveToState` + `return AIInternalMoveToState::update()`.
Rust: `ai.ai_move_to_position(&self.goal_position, false, CommandSourceType::FromAi)` then parent `set_temporary_state(AIStateType::MoveTo, LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND * 20)`.

## Player-visible
A unit walking back to its Guard post (after a chase, or after the guarded object moved) drops out of Guard for up to 20 seconds, ignores new enemies that enter the guard radius, and can fail to resume Guard if the walk takes longer than the temp state.
close_reason: guard.rs: AIGuardReturnState/AIGuardPickUpCrateState now compose InternalMoveTo/AIPickUpCrateState instead of parent ai_move_to_position

title: [AIGuard] Inner/Outer/Aggressor leftover uses AttackStateMachine instead of AIAttackState
description:
## C++
`AIGuardInnerState::onEnter` (`AIGuard.cpp:397`), `AIGuardOuterState::onEnter` (`:520`), and `AIGuardAttackAggressorState::onEnter` (`:815`) construct a full `AIAttackState` on the parent machine with `&m_exitConditions`:
`newInstance(AIAttackState)(getMachine(), follow, true, false, &m_exitConditions)`.

That wrapper (`AIStates.cpp:5470-5701`) does mood-sleep abort, `chooseWeapon()` every frame + `adjustModelConditionForWeaponStatus`, victim-dead / `setCurrentVictim`, team-change + empty-garrison abort, locked-special-weapon abort, max-shot abort, `OBJECT_STATUS_IS_ATTACKING` + `MODELCONDITION_ATTACKING`, and `clearLeechRangeModeForAllWeapons()` on exit.

## Rust
Live `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/guard.rs` Inner (`:1003`), Outer (`:1373`), and Aggressor (`:1846`) construct `AttackStateMachine` directly and only `set_exit_conditions`. `AttackStateMachine::update` (`states/attack_machine.rs:557-561`) is `should_exit_attack()` then `base.update()` — no `AIAttackState` wrapper.

Leftover `ai/ai_states/combat.rs` `AIGuardState` does nest `AIGuardMachine` (same inner shortcut).

## Evidence
C++: `m_attackState = newInstance(AIAttackState)(...)`.
Rust guard.rs:1003-1013 / 1373-1383 / 1846-1856: `AttackStateMachine::new` + `set_exit_conditions` only.

## Player-visible
A unit on Guard that engages never re-chooses weapons, may not show the attacking pose, does not publish `currentVictim`, and will not abort when the target converts or a locked special weapon is swapped. Guard fights feel like a raw approach/aim/fire loop instead of a retail attack.
close_reason: guard.rs: Inner/Outer/Aggressor wrap AIAttackObjectState (C++ AIAttackState) instead of raw AttackStateMachine

title: [Team] initTeam never resolves teamHome waypoint
description:
## C++
`TeamTemplateInfo::TeamTemplateInfo` (`Team.cpp:669-679`) reads `TheKey_teamHome` and walks `TheTerrainLogic` waypoints. On name match it sets `m_homeLocation` and `m_hasHomeLocation=true`. AI recruit/spawn (`AIPlayer.cpp:1053-1058`, `:2558-2582`) uses that origin.

## Rust
Leftover `TeamTemplateInfo::from_dict` (`common/rts/team.rs:270-274`) returns defaults and never reads the dict.
Live `TeamFactory::init_team` (`team/factory.rs:158-369`) parses unit counts, scripts, transport, and reinforcement origin, but never `teamHome`. `well_known_keys.rs` has no `key_team_home`. `TeamPrototype::set_home_location` exists (`prototype.rs:125-128`) and is never called. `has_home_location()` stays false after `sync_teams_from_sides`.

## Evidence
C++ `Team.cpp:669-679`. Leftover `from_dict` stub. Live factory ends dict parse at `key_team_transports_exit` with no waypoint lookup. AI `impl_teams.rs:119-128` / `skirmish_player.rs:464` require `has_home_location()`.

## Player-visible
Map team Home waypoints are ignored. Campaign AI logs "no Home Position", recruits against (0,0,0), and produced units do not path to the designed gather point.
close_reason: init_team/from_dict now read teamHome and resolve waypoint via TerrainLogic (last name match). leftover TeamTemplateInfo::from_dict + live factory apply_team_home_from_dict/set_home_location. files: well_known_keys.rs, common/rts/team.rs, team/factory.rs

title: [Particle] First alpha/color keyframe ignored when frame is 0
close_reason: Particle::new now always seeds alpha/color from key 0 and computeAlpha/ColorRate (C++ Particle::Particle ParticleSys.cpp:269-283). Frame 0 is the start pose; unset Color1 stays black. Tests: particle_new_applies_frame_zero_keyframes, test_particle_creation.

title: [Particle] Attached systems use yaw-only parent and drop setPosition translation
description:
## C++
`ParticleSystem::setPosition` (`ParticleSys.cpp:1281-1286`) writes **local Matrix3D translation** and clears `m_isLocalIdentity`. `update` (`:1910-1931`) builds `m_transform = parentXfrm * m_localTransform` (or parent alone) from the drawable/object **full 4x4** (`getTransformMatrix`, `:1863` / `:1886-1890`). `generateParticleInfo` (`:1729-1771`) then `mulVector3`s emission pos/vel through that 4x4. Bone FX and `skipParentXfrm` rely on local translation living in the matrix.

## Rust
Live `set_position` (`particle_system.rs:1483-1491`) only stores a world `Point3`. `local_transform` is a **3x3** (`set_local_transform` `:1523-1526`) with no translation slot. `resolve_attached_parent` (`:1698-1732`) overwrites `position` with the parent world pos and sets `parent_transform` to **yaw-only** `Matrix3` from `orientation.sin_cos()`. `compute_particle_position` (`:2155-2156`) is `position + transform * local_vol`. Any prior `set_position` offset is lost on the next attach tick.

Leftover Main `effects/particle_system.rs` has no attach/parent matrix at all.

## Evidence
C++ `setPosition` → `Set_X/Y/Z_Translation`. Live `set_position` does not touch `local_transform` / `is_local_identity`. Attach resolve uses yaw, not `getTransformMatrix`. Distinct from closed hq-lf92 (attach was previously not resolved at all).

## Player-visible
Bone-offset FX (muzzle flash, repair weld, jet exhaust bones) emit from hull origin. Aircraft/slope-aligned units emit exhaust in yaw-only space so trails ignore pitch/roll.
close_reason: set_position writes local Matrix3D translation (ParticleSys.cpp:1281-1286). update_transform_from_parent concatenates parent 4x4 * local including translation (1910-1931). generate_particle_info mulVector3s pos/vel through that affine (1729-1771). resolve_attached_parent uses drawable/object getTransformMatrix not yaw-only. Tests: set_position_writes_local_translation, attached_parent_applies_set_position_through_full_rotation, skip_parent_xfrm_keeps_local_set_position.

title: [W3DModelDraw] Team/house color never reaches the render object
description:
## C++
`W3DModelDraw` ctor (`W3DModelDraw.cpp:1734-1742`) seeds `m_hexColor` from the object's night/day indicator color. `setModelState` (`:3010`) creates the render object with `Create_Render_Obj(model, scale, m_hexColor)`. `replaceIndicatorColor` (`:3188-3207`) is gated by `OkToChangeModelColor`; a new color ORs `0xFF000000`, then nulls `m_curState` and rebuilds so house-color / ZHC textures rematch. `Drawable::setIndicatorColor` (`Drawable.cpp:4081-4088`) walks every draw module and calls that method.

## Rust
Leftover Device `wthree_d_model_draw.rs:1647-1671` implements `replace_indicator_color` but only stores `hex_color` and logs "setModelState rebuild deferred". Live GameLogic `W3DModelDraw::new` (`draw.rs:106`) hard-inits `hex_color: 0` and never reads the owner indicator. Live `ObjectDrawInterface` (`draw_module.rs:198-374`) has no `replace_indicator_color`. Live `Drawable::set_indicator_color` (`drawable.rs:1746-1748`) only writes `self.indicator_color`. Submit still stamps `render_object_color = Some(self.hex_color as u32)` (`impl_anim.rs:560`) — always 0. Distinct from closed `hq-wzad` (Recolor_Asset now wired): the ModelDraw caller never feeds a non-zero color.

## Evidence
C++: `Create_Render_Obj(..., m_hexColor)` + `di->replaceIndicatorColor(color)`.
Leftover: rebuild is a debug log.
Live: `hex_color: 0` forever; GameLogic drawable does not dispatch.

## Player-visible
USA/China/GLA units and `OkToChangeModelColor` meshes stay unpainted house-color (default gray/tan skins). Capture, disguise, and night-indicator swaps never recolor the model.
close_reason: Live W3DModelDraw seeds hex_color from Object day/night indicator (C++ ctor W3DModelDraw.cpp:1734-1742), replace_indicator_color ORs 0xFF000000 and nulls cur_state then setModelState (cpp:3188-3207), Drawable::set_indicator_color walks ObjectDrawInterface, submit uses hex_color as Create_Render_Obj color. Leftover Device replace_indicator_color now rebuilds via set_model_state.

title: [ChinookAI] Live host never auto-lands for load/unload
description:
## C++
`ChinookAIUpdate::update` (`ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:1067-1087`): when parent-idle and `contain->hasObjectsWantingToEnterOrExit()` and `m_flightStatus != CHINOOK_LANDED`, `setMyState(LANDING)`. `getAiFreeToExit` (`:1022-1028`) is `FREE_TO_EXIT` only when landed (or combat-drop + `KINDOF_CAN_RAPPEL`). Passengers cannot walk out of a flying Chinook.

## Rust
Live host Combat Chinook residual (`host_combat_chinook.rs`, `orders.rs:1080-1098` `install_combat_chinook_transport`) is slots + passenger fire only. Fail-closed comment: "Not full C++ ChinookAIUpdate ropes / supply / rappel / combat drop". No flight status, no auto-LANDING when someone wants in/out. Units load/unload from a hovering airframe.

Leftover `update` (`chinook_ai_update.rs:1770-1771`) does request Landing when waiting, but Wave 349 empty `OBJECT_REGISTRY` returns `Ok(())` immediately (`:1721-1722`), so the live host never runs it.

Not a refile of `hq-iwgts` (AIGroup evacuate Y=0). This is ChinookAIUpdate auto-land for enter/exit.

## Evidence
- C++ `ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:1067-1087`, `:1022-1028`
- Live `host_combat_chinook.rs:28-29`, `orders.rs:1080-1098`
- Leftover `chinook_ai_update.rs:1721-1722`, `:1770-1771`

## Player-visible
Clicking a Chinook to load Rangers (or Evacuate) teleports them in/out in mid-air. The helicopter never descends, never taxis, and never holds until wheels are on the ground.
close_reason: Live host Object.chinook_ai + GameLogic::tick_chinook_ai + enter/evac WAIT_TO_EXIT implement C++ ChinookAIUpdate::update (1067-1087) idle+want auto-LANDING and getAiFreeToExit (1022-1028). Leftover set_my_state(LANDING) via chinook_should_auto_land. Tests: live_host_chinook_auto_lands_when_idle_and_wanting, host_chinook_ai_auto_lands_for_load_unload, chinook_idle_want_enter_exit_auto_lands.

title: [ChinookAI] Attack-command uses garrison ObjectStatus CAN_ATTACK, not KindOf
description:
## C++
`privateAttackObject` / `privateForceAttackObject` / `privateAttackPosition` (`ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:1408`, `:1497`, `:1574`) gate with `getObject()->isKindOf(KINDOF_CAN_ATTACK)`. Combat Chinook (`AirF_AmericaVehicleChinook`) authors KindOf CAN_ATTACK; vanilla Chinook does not.

`OBJECT_STATUS_CAN_ATTACK` is a **different** bit (`ObjectStatusTypes.h:25`) OR'ed only inside `isAbleToAttack()` for garrisoned buildings. GarrisonContain sets/clears it when soldiers enter/leave. Chinooks do not get that status.

## Rust
Leftover `private_attack_object` / `private_force_attack_object` / `private_attack_position` (`chinook_ai_update.rs:1268`, `:1337`, `:1436`) `test_status(ObjectStatusTypes::CanAttack)` and return. Combat Chinook KindOf is never consulted. Passenger + portable-structure attack-with-me therefore never runs on leftover dual-world objects.

Live host passenger fire is a separate residual (`host_combat_chinook` / closed `hq-yny`). This is leftover `ChinookAIUpdate` using the wrong flag family.

## Evidence
- C++ `ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:1408`, `:1497`, `:1574`
- C++ `ObjectStatusTypes.h:25`, `GarrisonContain.cpp:1602`
- Leftover `chinook_ai_update.rs:1268`, `:1337`, `:1436`

## Player-visible
On the leftover path, ordering a Combat Chinook to attack never tells the Rangers inside to fire. Only the (usually weaponless) airframe is considered.
close_reason: Leftover private_attack_object/force/position now gate with chinook_kind_of_can_attack (KindOf::CanAttack) matching C++ ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:1408/1497/1574 isKindOf(KINDOF_CAN_ATTACK). Host HostChinookAI::can_issue_attack is KindOf not ObjectStatus. Tests: chinook_attack_gate_is_kind_of_not_status, host_chinook_attack_uses_kind_of_not_status.

title: [ChinookAI] Leftover evac/evac-and-exit is a plain move — no land, dump, takeoff, or HeadOffMap
description:
## C++
`ChinookAIStateMachine` (`ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:817-833`) wires:
- `MOVE_TO_AND_EVAC` → `LAND_AND_EVAC` → `EVAC_AND_TAKEOFF` → `TAKING_OFF`
- `MOVE_TO_AND_EVAC_AND_EXIT_INIT` (`ChinookRecordCreationState` records spawn pos) → move → land → `ChinookEvacuateState` (`removeAllContained(FALSE)` + `team->setActive()`) → takeoff → `HEAD_OFF_MAP`

`ChinookHeadOffMapState` (`:134-165`) sets `OBJECT_STATUS_RIDER8`, `aiMoveToPosition(originalPos)`, `setAllowInvalidPosition(true)`, then `destroyObject` once outside `getExtentIncludingBorder`.

`aiDoCommand` (`:1263-1286`) maps `AICMD_MOVE_TO_POSITION_AND_EVACUATE[_AND_EXIT]` onto those states (take off first if landed and dest is farther than 3).

## Rust
Leftover `handle_command` (`chinook_ai_update.rs:1188-1204`) only queues takeoff when landed-and-far; otherwise returns `false`. `execute_command` then treats both evac cmds as a generic `MoveToPosition` (`ai_commands.rs:131-156`). There is no `ChinookEvacuateState`, no `ChinookHeadOffMapState`, no RIDER8, no off-map destroy.

Live `execute_move_to_and_evacuate` (`transport.rs:488-536`) paths then `evacuate_container_now`. Distinct from AIGroup beads: leftover Chinook never flies off the map after a scripted evac-and-exit.

## Evidence
- C++ `ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:817-833`, `:103-111`, `:134-165`, `:1263-1286`
- Leftover `chinook_ai_update.rs:1188-1204` (no TAKING_OFF/HEAD_OFF_MAP symbols in file)
- Leftover `ai_commands.rs:131-156`
- Live `transport.rs:488-536`

## Player-visible
USA reinforcement / script Chinooks that should land, dump troops, take off, and despawn at the map edge instead fly to the point and stay on the map forever (or just move without unloading).
close_reason: Leftover handle_command maps AICMD_MOVE_TO_POSITION_AND_EVACUATE[_AND_EXIT] to set_my_state MoveToAndEvac / MoveToAndEvacAndExitInit (land/dump/takeoff/HeadOffMap). Host HostChinookAI::command_evac + evacuate_container_now land-first + HeadOffMap destroy. C++ ChinookAIStateMachine 817-833. Tests: chinook_evac_is_land_dump_takeoff_headoffmap, host_chinook_evac_lands_dumps_takeoff_and_heads_off_map.

title: [ChinookAI] Combat drop starts ropes immediately without MoveToBldg height
description:
## C++
`privateCombatDrop` (`ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:1201-1228`) `setMyState(MOVE_TO_COMBAT_DROP)`. That is `ChinookMoveToBldgState` (`:692-745`): ultra-accurate loco, if goal is a live structure raise `preferredHeight` to `geom.maxHeightAbovePosition + MinDropHeight` (never below old preferred), dest Z = ground + that height, wait for 2D arrival **and** `|z-destZ|<=3` before `DO_COMBAT_DROP`. Only `ChinookCombatDropState::onEnter` then HELD + ropes + rappel.

## Rust
Leftover `private_combat_drop` (`chinook_ai_update.rs:1599-1654`) `set_movement_target` then immediately `flight_status = DoingCombatDrop`. `update` (`:1809-1822`) calls `start_combat_drop` on the next tick — ropes/rappel at the **current** position. No preferred-height raise, no 3D arrival gate.

Not a refile of closed `hq-cseyb` (AIGroup live combat drop / unload). This is leftover `ChinookAIUpdate` starting the drop before arriving.

## Evidence
- C++ `ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:692-745`, `:1201-1228`, `:461-523`
- Leftover `chinook_ai_update.rs:1599-1654`, `:1809-1822`

## Player-visible
Combat drop on a building: Chinook hangs ropes and rappels Rangers from wherever it currently is (often mid-map / too low), instead of climbing over the roof and dropping there.
close_reason: Leftover private_combat_drop set_my_state(MoveToCombatDrop); ropes only after ChinookMoveToBldg 2D+|z-destZ|<=3 (enter_move_to_bldg preferredHeight). Host HostChinookAI::command_combat_drop stays MoveToCombatDrop until dest Z. C++ ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:1201-1228 and MoveToBldgState 692-745. Tests: chinook_combat_drop_waits_for_move_to_bldg_height, host_chinook_combat_drop_waits_for_move_to_bldg_height.

title: [AutoHeal] Leftover host has no DefaultAutoHealBehavior self-heal
description:
## C++
Trainable units inherit `ModuleTag_DefaultAutoHealBehavior` (dropped only when `!isTrainable`). StartsActive=Yes, HealingAmount typically 2, HealingDelay 1000ms, StartHealingDelay 5000ms, radius 0. Ctor `giveSelfUpgrade` + random phase; `update()` self-heals then sleeps forever at max health; `onDamage` restarts after StartHealingDelay.

## Rust
Host leftover heal is ambulance radius + HealPad + emergency-repair SingleBurst only (`host_heal.rs`, `update_ambulance_auto_heal`, `host_emergency_repair.rs`). No DefaultAutoHeal / StartHealingDelay residual. Wave 306 leftover `dual_world_registry_unavailable()` fail-closes live `pulse_heal_object` / `check_for_auto_heal` / `get_object` when OBJECT_REGISTRY is empty (host-only presentation path).

## Evidence
Grep of Main host leftovers finds no DefaultAutoHeal / StartHealingDelay implementation. Live `heal_self_only` exists but is gated off on the empty-registry host path.

## Player-visible effect
On the host leftover path, damaged infantry and vehicles never passively regenerate after leaving combat. Only ambulance/heal-pad/emergency-repair leftovers restore HP.
close_reason: Leftover host DefaultAutoHealBehavior: HostDefaultAutoHealData + Object::install_default_auto_heal_if_needed (trainable only, C++ ThingTemplate.cpp:419-423) + GameLogic::update_default_auto_heal after ambulance tick. Retail StartsActive/HealingAmount=2/HealingDelay=1000ms/StartHealingDelay=5000ms/radius 0. Crate AutoHealBehaviorModuleData::default_auto_heal(). Standalone residual test green; cargo -p gamelogic blocked by sibling Team Cell/Sync.

title: [AutoHeal] onDamage never wakes self-heal after first full-health sleep
description:
## C++
`AutoHealBehavior::getInterfaceMask()` is UPDATE | UPGRADE | DAMAGE (`AutoHealBehavior.h:102`). `ActiveBody` walks damage modules and calls `onDamage`. For radius==0 self-heal, `onDamage` (`AutoHealBehavior.cpp:136-157`) resets `StartHealingDelay` or wakes immediately once `m_soonestHealFrame` has passed. `update()` at max health returns `UPDATE_SLEEP_FOREVER` and relies on that wake.

## Rust
Live factory registers AutoHeal as UPDATE | UPGRADE only (`module_factory.rs:72-75`). Leftover residual table already has UPDATE | UPGRADE | DAMAGE (`host_thing_factory_module_xfer_residual.rs:802-808`). `rebuild_behavior_list` wraps every template module in `TemplateModuleBehavior`, whose `get_damage()` is gated on the DAMAGE mask and whose `on_damage` is the trait default no-op (`object_modules.rs:1208-1228`, `specialized_behavior.rs:159-163`). Live `AutoHealBehavior::on_damage` is never reached.

## Evidence
`notify_damage_modules_on_damage` → `for_each_damage_module_mut` → `behavior.get_damage()`. Mask misses DAMAGE so get_damage is None. Even with the bit, the wrapper does not downcast to `AutoHealBehaviorModule`.

## Player-visible effect
DefaultAutoHealBehavior (trainable infantry/vehicles) heals at most until the first full-health sleep, then never restarts after later combat. StartHealingDelay (typically 5s) never applies.
close_reason: C++ AutoHealBehavior.cpp:136-157 onDamage now reachable: factory UPDATE|UPGRADE|DAMAGE, TemplateModuleBehavior::on_damage downcasts AutoHealBehaviorModule, AutoHealBehavior::on_damage set_wake_frame(StartHealingDelay) after update() SLEEP_FOREVER at max health. Leftover HostDefaultAutoHealData::on_damage re-arms the same delay. last_wake_sleep tests added. cargo -p gamelogic blocked by sibling Team Cell/Sync.

title: [GameLogic] Destroying a prison does not destroy contained prisoners
description:
## C++
`PrisonBehavior::onDelete` (`PrisonBehavior.cpp:117-141`) calls `OpenContain::onDelete()` first. That loop (`OpenContain.cpp:819-827`) `destroyObject`s every rider on the literal contain list, then the prison destroys yard drawables. `PropagandaCenterBehavior::onDelete` extends this after restoring brainwashed units' original teams.

## Rust
`PrisonBehavior::on_delete` / `PrisonBehaviorModule::on_delete` (`prison_behavior.rs:331-334, 700-703`) only `cleanup_visuals()`. They never call `contain.on_delete()` / destroy contained IDs. PropagandaCenter's `on_delete` restores teams then that same visual-only prison delete.

## Evidence
C++: `OpenContain::onDelete` → `TheGameLogic->destroyObject(rider)` for each contained. Rust: `cleanup_visuals()` only.

## Player-visible
Selling or destroying a prison / propaganda center leaves its prisoners alive in the world, often still `DISABLED_HELD`, instead of killing them with the building.
close_reason: prison_behavior.rs: on_delete now OpenContain::on_delete (destroy riders) then cleanup_visuals; Module/handle on_delete forward

title: [GameLogic] POW truck dock unload never transfers prisoners
description:
## C++
`POWTruckAIUpdate::unloadPrisonersToPrison` (`POWTruckAIUpdate.cpp:738-803`) walks the truck's real contain list via `iterateContained(putPrisonersInPrison)`. Each prisoner is `removeFromContain` on the truck then `addToContain` on the prison. `PrisonDockUpdate::action` (`PrisonDockUpdate.cpp:38-61`) calls this when a loaded POW truck docks.

## Rust
Live `POWTruckAIUpdate::unload_prisoners_to_prison` (`pow_truck_ai_update.rs:894-972`) reads `owner.get_contain().get_contained_objects()`. `Object` wiring (`object_modules.rs:897-916`) installs `POWTruckBehaviorContainHandle`, whose `get_contained_objects` is hardcoded `&[]` (`pow_truck_behavior.rs:480-482`). Leftover `object/update/ai_update/pow_truck_ai_update.rs` is only a re-export of this live impl.

## Evidence
C++ iterates the OpenContain rider list. Rust handle cannot return a borrowed slice of the Mutex-guarded list, so unload always sees zero IDs. `get_contained_count` on the same handle is correct, so the truck can look full and still dump nobody.

## Player-visible
A POW truck that docks at a prison (or propaganda center) never unloads prisoners, never pays bounty, and never shows `GUI:AddCash`. Prisoners stay in the truck.
close_reason: pow_truck_behavior.rs: POWTruckBehaviorContainHandle.get_contained_objects refreshes real OpenContain IDs via CachedContainIds; leftover pow_truck_ai_update re-exports live unload

title: [HordeUpdate] Leftover never sets horde terrain decals or fade
description:
## C++
Every `HordeUpdate::update` (`HordeUpdate.cpp:309-366`), when the unit is alive and `TheGameLogic->getDrawIconUI()`, sets infantry `TERRAIN_DECAL_HORDE` / `_WITH_NATIONALISM_UPGRADE` / `_WITH_FANATICISM_UPGRADE` or vehicle `TERRAIN_DECAL_HORDE_VEHICLE` (size `3.5 * majorRadius`), skips `KINDOF_PORTABLE_STRUCTURE`, clears to `TERRAIN_DECAL_NONE` when icon UI is off, and fades in/out at ±0.03 on join/leave (`:362-365`).

## Rust
Live crate `update_simple` (`horde_update.rs:541-570`) ports that matrix, but the Wave 378 empty-registry gate never lets it run on host-only. Leftover host/GW ticks only flip `weapon_bonus_horde` and refresh leftover weapons — they never call `set_terrain_decal` / `set_terrain_decal_size` / `set_terrain_decal_fade_target`. hq-f0hu (closed) implemented Drawable/W3D decal creation; leftover still never requests a horde type.

## Evidence
`update_battlemaster_horde_status` / `update_china_infantry_horde_status` / GW Wave 812/813 ticks have no decal calls. Honesty comments: "not full … terrain-decal flag matrix". `bd search` "terrain decal" only hits closed hq-1va1 (onDie fade) and hq-f0hu (renderer).

## Player-visible
China infantry/tank hordes never show the ground ring (plain / nationalism / fanaticism / vehicle-sized) or the fade-in when the blob forms. That ring is the main retail feedback that horde is active.
close_reason: Leftover horde ticks + peel now call Object::apply_horde_terrain_decal (type/size 3.5*radius/fade ±0.03). Live update_simple already had the C++ matrix; empty-registry Forever-sleep removed so it can run.

title: [HordeUpdate] Live module Forever-sleeps when OBJECT_REGISTRY is empty
description:
## C++
`HordeUpdate::update` (`HordeUpdate.cpp:235-371`) always runs. It rechecks membership (infantry every wake, vehicles every `UpdateRate` frames), calls `AIUpdateInterface::evaluateMoraleBonus`, and drives terrain-decal type/size/fade. Constructor (`:136-148`) only random-sleeps the first wake; it never refuses to update because a client registry is empty.

## Rust
Live `HordeUpdate::update_simple` (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/behavior/horde_update.rs:508-513`) returns `UpdateSleepTime::Forever` when `dual_world_registry_unavailable()` (`OBJECT_REGISTRY.is_empty()`). `check_horde_status` (`:403-407`) and `show_hide_flag` (`:373-376`) no-op on the same gate. Wave 378 residual (`host_live_horde_update_dual_world_empty_gate_residual_wave378.rs`) documents this as host-only fail-closed. Partition `get_objects_in_range_boundary_3d_from_object` (`object_queries.rs:463-466`) also returns empty on that gate.

## Evidence
Host play ticks leftover `update_battlemaster_horde_status` / `update_china_infantry_horde_status` (`world_tick/step.rs:333-350`) instead of the crate module. `bd search` HordeUpdate / dual_world_registry / empty-gate: no open or closed beads covering this gate.

## Player-visible
On the host-only path the real HordeUpdate module never joins a horde, never calls evaluateMoraleBonus, and never paints horde rings. China blobs rely on the incomplete leftover (no rub-off, no decals, hardcoded templates).
close_reason: Removed dual_world_registry_unavailable Forever-sleep/no-op gates from HordeUpdate show_hide_flag, check_horde_status, and update_simple. C++ update always runs.

title: [CrateSystem] Live crate drop ignores parsed Crate.ini gates
description:
## C++
`CrateSystem::parseCrateTemplateDefinition` (`CrateSystem.cpp:66-89`) plus `TheCrateTemplateFieldParseTable` (`:159-168`) load `CrateData` blocks: `CreationChance`, `VeterancyLevel` (`TheVeterancyNames`), `KilledByType` KindOf mask, `KillerScience`, repeating `CrateObject` name+chance, `OwnedByMaker`. `CreateCrateDie::onDie` (`CreateCrateDie.cpp:63-85`) looks up `TheCrateSystem->findCrateTemplate`, then `testCreationChance` / `testVeterancyLevel` / `testKillerType` / `testKillerScience` before `createCrate` weighted pick. `OwnedByMaker` assigns the crate to the dead unit's default team.

Retail SalvageCrateData is authored `KilledByType = SALVAGER` (host residual `SALVAGE_KILLED_BY_TYPE_RESIDUAL`). EliteTankCrateData / HeroicTankCrateData exist with CreationChance 0.75 / 1.0.

## Rust
Boot (`shell.rs:1529-1548`) parses `Data/INI/Default/Crate.ini` + `Data/INI/Crate.ini` into Common `ParsedCrateSystem` only. Leftover GameLogic `THE_CRATE_SYSTEM` (`object/crate_system.rs:322-332`) and leftover `CreateCrateDie` (`die/create_crate_die.rs:342-375`) implement the C++ gates but are never fed from that store and are not on the live death path.

Live `try_create_crates_on_die` (`world_tick/crates.rs:955-984`) calls `host_create_crate_die::try_roll_crate_spawn`, which looks up hardcoded `HOST_CRATE_TEMPLATES` (`host_create_crate_die.rs:186-237`): chance + weighted object name only. No `KilledByType` / `KillerScience` / `VeterancyLevel` / `OwnedByMaker`. `EliteTankCrateData` / `HeroicTankCrateData` are residual constants (`host_gamedata_lobby_residual.rs:421-424`) but are not in the host table, so `find_host_crate_template` returns None.

## Evidence
C++: `TheCrateSystem->findCrateTemplate` then four tests + `m_isOwnedByMaker`.
Rust live: `try_roll_crate_spawn` → `HOST_CRATE_TEMPLATES` (Salvage/dollar/supply/level/heal/shroud/crusaders only). `SALVAGE_KILLED_BY_TYPE_RESIDUAL` is honesty-only.
Leftover: Common `ini_crate.rs` store ≠ GameLogic `THE_CRATE_SYSTEM`; no conversion.

## Player-visible
Salvage crates drop when a non-salvager kills a marked unit. Elite/Heroic tank crate templates never spawn. `OwnedByMaker` crates stay Neutral so the killer's team (or anyone) can pick them. Map/INI crate overrides in Crate.ini have no live effect.
close_reason: THE_CRATE_SYSTEM imports ParsedCrateSystem; live try_roll_crate_spawn_gated applies chance/vet/KilledBy/science/OwnedByMaker

title: [FireWhen] Generic DeathWeapon peel stacks on specialized death residuals
description:
## C++
`FireWeaponWhenDeadBehavior::onDie` fires **once** via `TheWeaponStore->createAndFireTempWeapon(d->m_deathWeapon, obj, obj->getPosition())` for each qualifying module. Exclusive UpgradeMux ensures at most one of the mutually conflicting modules on a Bomb Truck / Nuclear Tank / etc. actually fires.

## Rust
`GameLogic::fire_temporary_weapons_for_pending_deaths` (`world_tick/step.rs` → `temporary_weapon_fire.rs:50-60`) may fire the typed ephemeral death weapon. Then `process_destroy_list` **always** calls `apply_fire_weapon_when_dead` (`destroy_list_bounty.rs:85-86`), which name-peels `death_weapon_for_template` and applies a second dual-ring splash (`create_destroy_die.rs:1618-1681`) unless `fire_weapon_when_dead_fired` was already set. After the object is removed, specialized residuals fire **again** for the same corpse:
- Bomb Truck HE/Bio (`destroy_list_bounty.rs:279-306` → `apply_bomb_truck_death_detonation_at`, default 1000/40 vs peel 400/40+100/70)
- Nuclear Tanks (`:309-323`)
- Demo SuicideBomb (`:326-341`)
- Toxin Tractor death field (`:252-276`) while peel also matches `toxin`+`truck` (`host_fire_weapon_when_dead.rs:99-106`)

Terrorist peel (`:78-86`, 700/r15, no secondary) stacks with the live terrorist suicide residual (SuicideDynamitePack dual-ring). The peel only skips if the typed path already set `fire_weapon_when_dead_fired`; ConflictsWith-skip (see sibling bead) usually prevents that.

## Evidence
- `GeneralsMD/.../FireWeaponWhenDeadBehavior.cpp:90-94`
- `GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/host_fire_weapon_when_dead.rs:26-107,111-119`
- `GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/create_destroy_die.rs:1618-1681`
- `GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/destroy_list_bounty.rs:85-86,252-341`

## Player-visible
Killing a Bomb Truck, Terrorist, Toxin Tractor, Demo Trap, Scud Storm, or Nuclear Tank can apply two (or three) overlapping death blasts with mismatched radii/damage. Nearby units die that should have survived the single retail death weapon.
close_reason: host_fire_weapon_when_dead.rs + apply_fire_weapon_when_dead: skip generic peel when specialized bomb-truck/toxin/nuclear residual covers, and skip terrorist SUICIDED (host_terrorist already fired SuicideDynamitePack)

title: [FireWhen] Live UpgradeMux never honors TriggeredBy and treats ConflictsWith as always-on
description:
## C++
`FireWeaponWhenDeadBehavior::onDie` (`FireWeaponWhenDeadBehavior.cpp:65-88`) returns unless `isUpgradeActive()` (UpgradeMux `m_upgradeExecuted`). `StartsActive` calls `giveSelfUpgrade()` in the ctor. Later `UpgradeMux::attemptUpgrade` sets that bit when `TriggeredBy` upgrades complete. `ConflictsWith` is **not** an always-off switch: the module still fires unless the **object** or **controlling player** `getCompletedUpgradeMask()` intersects the conflicting mask. Same UpgradeMux is on `FireWeaponWhenDamagedBehavior` (`upgradeImplementation` wakes continuous fire). Retail exclusive matrices (Bomb Truck default vs HE vs Bio, Nuclear Tanks, Demo SuicideBomb, Scud anthrax death weapon) are multiple modules: default `StartsActive=Yes` + `ConflictsWith=Upgrade_*`, upgraded modules `StartsActive=No` + `TriggeredBy=Upgrade_*`.

## Rust
Live host typed path (`temporary_weapon_fire.rs:80-84,122-126,166-177`; `TemporaryWeaponRuntimeBundle::from_thing_template` only sets `upgrade_executed` from `starts_active` for **dead** modules):
- `TriggeredBy` is parsed onto `FireWeaponUpgradeMuxMetadata` but never applied when a player/object completes an upgrade. `StartsActive=No` modules stay inert forever.
- `dead_ephemeral_spec` does `if !metadata.upgrade_mux.conflicts_with.is_empty() { continue; }` — any authored `ConflictsWith` list skips the module even when neither object nor player owns the conflicting upgrade.

GameEngine `fire_weapon_when_dead_behavior_new.rs` `apply_upgrade` exists but Main/GW never drive it; host fire uses the typed runtime above.

## Evidence
- `GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Behavior/FireWeaponWhenDeadBehavior.cpp:45-47,65-93`
- `GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Include/GameLogic/Module/UpgradeModule.h:72-77`
- `GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_combat/temporary_weapon_fire.rs:80-84,166-177`
- `GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/host_temporary_weapon_behavior.rs:154-158,881-882,1191-1195`
- Specialized residuals explicitly fail-closed on this matrix (`host_bomb_truck_detonate.rs:16-17`, `host_nuclear_tanks.rs:24-25`, `host_demo_suicide_bomb.rs:17-18`).

## Player-visible
Upgrade-gated death/reaction weapons never switch on the live typed path. Default modules that declare `ConflictsWith` never fire even before the upgrade is bought. Players keep the wrong (or no) death blast / reaction weapon until a separate name-peel residual happens to paper over a few templates.
close_reason: temporary_weapon_fire.rs + host_temporary_weapon_behavior.rs: TriggeredBy activates StartsActive=No; ConflictsWith skips only if object or player owns the upgrade; damaged construct sets upgrade_executed from starts_active

title: [BattlePlan] onObjectCreated never runs so veteran gun and turret disable are skipped
description:
## C++
`BattlePlanUpdate::onObjectCreated` (`BattlePlanUpdate.cpp:196-240`) after INI validation:
- looks up `m_specialPowerModule` from `SpecialPowerTemplate`
- loads all unpack/pack/idle/announcement `AudioEventRTS` names and `TheAudio->getInfoForAudioEvent`
- `getObject()->setWeaponSetFlag(WEAPONSET_VETERAN)` so the Strategy Center bombardment gun (`StrategyCenterGun`, typically the VETERAN weapon set) is selected
- if the building has AI: `setWeaponLock(PRIMARY_WEAPON, LOCKED_TEMPORARILY)`
- `enableTurret(false)` so the artillery cannot fire until Bombardment unpacks to ACTIVE

Object creation walks every module's `onObjectCreated` (`Object.cpp` / `invoke_on_object_created_after_install` counterpart).

## Rust
Live `BattlePlanUpdate` implements `BehaviorModuleInterface::on_object_created` (`behavior/battle_plan_update.rs:1100-1145`) with the same veteran flag / lock / `enable_turret(false)` work.

`BattlePlanUpdateModule` (`:1535-1555`) implements `Module` **without** overriding `on_object_created`. The default (`common/thing/module.rs:537`) is a no-op.

Live dispatch `Object::invoke_on_object_created_after_install` (`object_modules.rs:496-506`) only calls `module.on_object_created()` on the `Module` wrapper — it never reaches `BehaviorModuleInterface::on_object_created`.

Leftover `object/update/battle_plan_update.rs:139-164` has the same `on_object_created` body but is not the registered factory.

Peer modules (e.g. `BunkerBusterBehaviorModule`, `OverchargeBehaviorModule`) do forward `Module::on_object_created` / `on_delete` to the inner behavior.

## Evidence
- C++: `setWeaponSetFlag(WEAPONSET_VETERAN);` + `enableTurret(false);` in `onObjectCreated`
- Rust live wrapper: `impl Module for BattlePlanUpdateModule` has only `as_any` / name keys / `get_module_data`
- Dispatch: `for entry in &self.modules { entry.with_module(|module| module.on_object_created()); }`

## Player-visible
A finished Strategy Center never flips onto the VETERAN weapon set and never disables its turret. Bombardment either has no `StrategyCenterGun`, or the gun can fire before any plan is selected. C++ only enables the turret after Bombardment unpacks to ACTIVE.
close_reason: BattlePlanUpdateModule::on_object_created now forwards to BehaviorModuleInterface::on_object_created (C++ BattlePlanUpdate::onObjectCreated, BattlePlanUpdate.cpp:196-240) so live Object::invoke_on_object_created_after_install sets WEAPONSET_VETERAN, PRIMARY lock, and enable_turret(false).

title: [BattlePlan] onDelete never runs so army bonuses leak after Strategy Center dies
description:
## C++
`BattlePlanUpdate::onDelete` (`BattlePlanUpdate.cpp:164-191`) runs when the module is torn down (sell, script destroy, death → destroy):
- destroy the vision object if one exists
- if `m_planAffectingArmy != PLANSTATUS_NONE`, `player->changeBattlePlan(m_planAffectingArmy, -1, m_bonuses)` so army armor / sight / weapon-bonus flags are inverted off

C++ does **not** do this in `onDie`. `onDelete` is the only remove-bonus path. `Object::onDestroy` walks every module `onDelete`.

## Rust
Live `BattlePlanUpdate` puts the same cleanup on `BehaviorModuleInterface::on_die` (`behavior/battle_plan_update.rs:1148-1173`), not on `Module::on_delete`.

`BattlePlanUpdateModule` (`:1535-1555`) does not override `Module::on_delete` (default no-op). `Drop` only stops transition audio.

Live destroy (`object_lifecycle.rs:348-355`) calls `module.on_delete()` on the wrapper. `Object::on_die` walks **die** modules via `call_on_die_hooks` — BattlePlanUpdate is not a die module — so `BehaviorModuleInterface::on_die` is never invoked.

Leftover `object/update/battle_plan_update.rs:166-188` implements `on_delete` correctly but is not the registered factory.

Host leftover (`world_objects/create_destroy_die.rs`) never calls `apply_battle_plan_set_battle_plan(..., None, ...)` when a Strategy Center is destroyed.

## Evidence
- C++: `if (player && m_planAffectingArmy != PLANSTATUS_NONE) player->changeBattlePlan(m_planAffectingArmy, -1, m_bonuses);`
- Rust live: cleanup only in `on_die`; wrapper `on_delete` is the empty `Module` default
- Destroy path: `module.on_delete()` only

## Player-visible
Selling or destroying an active Strategy Center leaves Bombardment +20% damage, HoldTheLine 0.9 armor, and SearchAndDestroy +20% range/sight on the army until the match ends.
close_reason: BattlePlanUpdateModule::on_delete now calls BattlePlanUpdate::on_delete (C++ BattlePlanUpdate::onDelete, BattlePlanUpdate.cpp:164-191). Army changeBattlePlan(-1) and vision destroy run on Module::on_delete, not the unused on_die hook.

title: [ScriptCond] NAMED_DESTROYED true for never-existing names
description:

Never existed → FALSE; existing → isEffectivelyDead(); didUnitExist → true.
## Rust
Tracker miss returns TRUE; exists-case uses DESTROYED bit not effectively-dead.

eval_named.rs Object not in tracker considered destroyed.

Scripts fire instantly for typo'd/not-yet-spawned names.

Live ScriptConditionEvaluator::eval_named_destroyed now uses is_effectively_dead + NamedObjectTracker::did_object_exist (false on tracker miss). title: [Physics] STICK_TO_GROUND never set on live PhysicsBehavior — locomotor apply_physics_options drops it
description:
C++: Locomotor::setPhysicsOptions (Locomotor.cpp:925) calls physics->setStickToGround(getStickToGround()) every move-towards tick — 'walking guys aren't allowed to catch huge (or even small) air'. PhysicsBehavior::update (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:791-796) then clamps z to ground whenever z > groundZ and !ALLOW_TO_FALL, so ground locomotors terrain-follow. The flag only clears the branch via ALLOW_TO_FALL.

Rust: GameLogic/src/locomotor/core_impl/maintain.rs apply_physics_options sets extra friction + allow_airborne_friction then explicitly drops stick: '// C++ setStickToGround — PhysicsBehavior has no setter in this crate; extra friction + airborne-friction flags are the live PhysicsBehavior path. let _stick = self.template.stick_to_ground;'. No setter exists: FLAG_STICK_TO_GROUND (physics_update.rs:36) is only ever read (apply_random_rotation:539, update stick-clamp:864) — repo-wide grep shows no writer. The update-side clamp branch is therefore permanently dead on the GameEngine live path. The Main/src legacy host does honor it (physics_motion.rs:679 'if self.stick_to_ground && !self.allow_to_fall' + set_locomotor_physics_options tests), so the gap is the dual-world GameEngine path.

Evidence: maintain.rs:20-23 dead-binding comment; grep FLAG_STICK_TO_GROUND in GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine → reads only; ini_bridge.rs:169 carries stick_to_ground into the locomotor template so the data is available but unused.

Player-visible: infantry/vehicles descending slopes or small ledges gravity-fall instead of terrain-following — downhill hop/airborne stutter, WAS_AIRBORNE_LAST_FRAME flapping makes the landing path (bounce sound, onCollide, fall-damage slope test) run on ordinary downhill movement, and calcSleepTime's !isAboveTerrain term keeps physics permanently awake for ground units on rolling terrain.
acceptance_criteria: PhysicsBehavior trait gains set_stick_to_ground and locomotor apply_physics_options applies template.stick_to_ground like Locomotor.cpp:925, so the physics update z-clamp (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:791-796) is reachable on the live path.
close_reason: PhysicsBehavior::set_stick_to_ground sets FLAG_STICK_TO_GROUND (PhysicsUpdate.h:155). Locomotor::apply_physics_options applies template.stick_to_ground like Locomotor.cpp:925. Live AI locomotor_move_towards/along_path call apply_physics_options each move tick so update_simple z-clamp (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:779-782) is reachable.

title: [Physics] Live PhysicsBehavior::onCollide is dead code — never dispatched to any collision
description:
C++: PhysicsBehavior::onCollide (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1141-1400) is a CollideModuleInterface on every object with a PhysicsBehavior module. Object::onCollide (Object.cpp:2369) iterates ALL behavior modules via getCollide(); it is invoked from PartitionContactList::processContactList (PartitionManager.cpp:2450) for every contact pair and from the physics update ground-hit path (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:827). It implements: projectile pui first-chance; ground-collide forwarding to containedBy container (parachute landing); mutual-containment and both-parachuting skips; ai->getIgnoredObstacleID() skip plus the infantry-recrew-of-unmanned-vehicle steal (clearDisabled UNMANNED, setCaptured, defect, transferObjectName, destroy infantry); other-physics/immobile insubstantial gates; checkForOverlapCollision crush skip; AI processCollision gate; geometry center 2D/3D overlap test; lastCollidee; immobile structure-stiffness stop (nuke velocity, min bounce speed) with VehicleCrashesIntoBuildingWeapon/NonBuildingWeapon fire + destroyObject when falling below rubble height into a structure; parachute jam-out (reposition topmost containedBy + scrubVelocity2D(0)); overlap-capped (5.0) bounce-apart force.

Rust: the faithful port exists — GameLogic/src/object/behavior/physics_collide.rs on_collide (+ physics_crush.rs check_for_overlap_collision) — but it is unreachable. Its only entry is PhysicsBehaviorUpdate::on_collision (physics_update.rs:1054), and nothing in the tree calls CollideModuleInterface::on_collision on it (repo-wide grep: only pow_truck_behavior.rs:382 self-adapter). Object::on_collide (object_queries.rs:1040) dispatches exclusively to COLLISION_MANAGER-registered modules; register_collide_module callers are only crates/squish/fireweapon/shroud/powtruck adapters — physics never registers. collision_system.rs:241-243 fires COLLISION_MANAGER.handle_collision for each contact pair, so physics is structurally excluded from the dispatch the way Object::onCollide includes it in C++.

Evidence: grep '\.on_collision\(' across GeneralsRust/Code → single hit (pow_truck adapter); grep 'register_collide_module' → no physics registration; physics_collide.rs:22 'pub(super) fn on_collide' reachable only from physics_update.rs:1059.

Player-visible: vehicles hurled into buildings pass through instead of firing VehicleCrashesIntoBuildingWeapon and dying; tank-vs-car PhysicsBehavior crush (HUGE_DAMAGE_AMOUNT DAMAGE_CRUSH + crush FX probe) never happens; debris/corpses never bounce apart; infantry never re-crew unmanned vehicles through collision; parachuted cargo landing never reaches the container (ground-collide forwarding dead); m_lastCollidee stays INVALID forever. Main/src legacy host has try_physics_collide for this, but the GameEngine dual-world live path runs nothing.
acceptance_criteria: PhysicsBehaviorUpdate registered/dispatched as a collide module on the live path so physics_collide::on_collide runs for partition contacts and ground hits, matching PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1141-1400 (crush, crash weapons, bounce-apart, recrew, parachute jam, container ground-forward).
close_reason: Live COLLISION_MANAGER.handle_collision now iterates Object behavior get_collide() like Object.cpp:2369-2389, so PhysicsBehaviorUpdate::on_collision runs physics_collide::on_collide (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1141-1400) for partition contacts. Ground hits call physics_collide::on_collide directly from update_simple (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:831) then Object::on_collide.

title: [Dozer] Player resume-construction never paths the dozer so scaffolds never progress
description:
## C++
`DozerAIUpdate::privateResumeConstruction` (DozerAIUpdate.cpp:1836) -> `newTask(DOZER_TASK_BUILD, obj)` (1943) computes dock points via `findGoodBuildOrRepairPositionAndTarget`, then `DozerActionPickActionPosState::update` issues `ai->aiMoveToPosition(&goalPos, CMD_FROM_AI)` (line ~228) so the dozer physically walks to the scaffold before `DozerActionDoActionState` builds. Same flow in WorkerAIUpdate.cpp.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/command_executor/construct.rs` `execute_resume_construction` (~223) only calls `self.game_logic.resume_construction(units, target_id)`. `world_scripts/rebuild_dozer.rs` `resume_construction` (853-885) sets `target`/`AIState::Constructing`/`builder_id` but never issues a path. The AI path explicitly compensates (Main/src/ai.rs:708-712: "resume_construction creates the authoritative dock; this command restores the corresponding movement/path" -> `unit_command_begin_construct`); the player path does not. `world_tick/production.rs` `update_construction` only progresses when the dozer is within `BUILDER_RANGE = 30.0` of the building, and `world_objects/support_states.rs` has no Constructing approach branch (Repairing only).

## Evidence
- construct.rs:229 `if self.game_logic.resume_construction(units, target_id)` — no movement call, contrast construct.rs:125 `path_to_goal_with_state(unit_id, location, AIState::Constructing)` in `execute_dozer_construct` and leftover.rs:545 `begin_support_order(..., AIState::Repairing)` in `execute_repair`.
- rebuild_dozer.rs:860-867 sets state/builder only.
- production.rs:10 `BUILDER_RANGE: f32 = 30.0` gates `nearby_dozers`.
- rebuild_dozer.rs:841-846 `can_resume_construction_of` returns false while any same-player dozer is `Constructing` on the target — the wedged dozer also blocks reassignment.

## Player-visible
Select dozer, right-click / Alt+E resume on a distant unfinished building: dozer never moves, shows the constructing state, building percent stays 0 forever, and no other dozer can be assigned (resume of others refused). Only the skirmish-AI path actually walks there.
close_reason: Live resume_construction now paths via path_approach_with_state to dozer_repair_approach_position (C++ DozerAIUpdate::privateResumeConstruction -> newTask -> DozerActionPickActionPosState::update aiMoveToPosition, DozerAIUpdate.cpp:1837/1948/211). Player execute_resume_construction uses that GameLogic path.

title: [SlowDeath] Live SlowDeathBehavior never dispatched

title: [TerrainLogic] Edge-point spawns use max pathfind extent instead of active boundary extent
description:
C++:
TerrainLogic.cpp:2036-2116 findClosestEdgePoint/findFarthestEdgePoint both call getExtent(). W3DTerrainLogic::getExtent (W3DTerrainLogic.cpp:176-193) returns the ACTIVE boundary: hi = m_boundaries[m_activeBoundary] * MAP_XY_FACTOR.

Rust:
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/terrain.rs find_closest_edge_point / find_farthest_edge_point call self.get_maximum_pathfind_extent(), i.e. the LARGEST boundary, not get_extent() (the active-boundary version that already exists and is used by action_manager is_point_on_map).

Evidence:
Callers on both sides: OCL CreateAtEdge* (paradrop, A10 strike, artillery barrage, aurora, carpet bomb, fuel air bomb, nuclear missile, OCLUpdate, OCLSpecialPower), SpectreGunshipDeploymentUpdate edge spawns, DeliverPayloadAIUpdate map-enter point, AIUpdate guard-position clamp, GameLogicDispatch beacon placement. After a ChangeMapBoundary/setActiveBoundary script shrinks the playable area, Rust still picks edge points on the old largest boundary.

Player-visible:
On campaign/skirmish maps that shrink the map boundary mid-game, aircraft (Spectre, paradrops, strikes) and OCL spawns enter from off-map edges of the OLD boundary instead of the shrunken playable area; guard positions and beacons clamp to the wrong edge.
close_reason: Live find_closest_edge_point/find_farthest_edge_point now call get_extent() (active boundary, W3DTerrainLogic.cpp:176-193) instead of get_maximum_pathfind_extent(), matching TerrainLogic.cpp:2039 and :2091 getExtent().

title: [TerrainLogic] Bridge attack-point fallback returns map origin instead of bridge object position
description:
C++:
TerrainLogic.cpp:1905-1934 getBridgeAttackPoints: when no Bridge in the list matches the object ID, both attack points fall back to the bridge OBJECT position: attackInfo->attackPoint1/2 = *bridge->getPosition().

Rust:
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/terrain.rs:3311-3356 get_bridge_attack_points: fallback sets attack_point1/2 = Coord3D::origin() (0,0,0). Also weapon_range.rs leaves the freshly-newed (origin) info untouched when the terrain lock fails.

Evidence:
Rust callers that consume the fallback: weapon/weapon_range.rs:63-78 (is_within_attack_range, KindOf::Bridge targets), ai/turret.rs:534-538, weapon/weapon_template.rs:739-742. C++ callers: Weapon.cpp:822, 2165, 2256; TurretAI.cpp:1006; AIUpdate.cpp:1886. Any bridge-kind object not registered in TerrainLogic bridge list (script/OCL-created bridge objects, or lock unavailable) gets range-measured against the map corner.

Player-visible:
Units/turrets engaging an unregistered bridge object compute distance to (0,0,0): weapons show out-of-range and never fire, or fire from absurd ranges; turret target-point picking lands at the map corner.
close_reason: Live TerrainLogic::get_bridge_attack_points fallback now copies the bridge object position (TheGameLogic::find_object_by_id) for both attack points when no Bridge list entry matches, matching TerrainLogic.cpp:1936-1937 getBridgeAttackPoints. Origin remains only if the object itself is gone.

title: [AIGroup] Live tighten dissolves stamped formations; C++ never tightens them
description:
## C++
`groupMoveToPosition` (`AIGroup.cpp:1559-1566`) only tests the click-to-gather rect when `!isFormation`. A stamped formation always takes `friend_computeGroundPath` + `friend_moveFormationToPos` (`:1612-1615`) and is never tightened. Helipad/aircraft members can force `isFormation = FALSE`.

## Rust
Live `execute_move` (`command_executor/movement.rs:26-32`) calls `should_tighten_group_move` **before** any formation check. `execute_tighten_to_position` → `unit_command_tighten_to` (`unit_commands.rs:434-461`) does `set_formation(0, ZERO)` and paths every member to the raw click.

## Evidence
- C++ `AIGroup.cpp:1559-1566`, `:1612-1615`
- Live `movement.rs:26-32`; `unit_commands.rs:434-461`

## Player-visible
A player who created a formation and clicks inside the group's footprint gets the formation dissolved and every unit crammed onto the click. Retail slides the formation as a shape.
close_reason: leftover group_move_to_position only tightens when !is_formation; stamped formations take friend_move_formation_to_pos (GameLogic/src/ai/group.rs). Live execute_move matches.

title: [AIGroup] Live group-path distance counts aircraft and no-AI members
description:
## C++
`friend_computeGroundPath` (`AIGroup.cpp:517-549`) only measures distance for members with `AIUpdateInterface` that are `KINDOF_INFANTRY` or `KINDOF_VEHICLE`. Aircraft `continue` (`:542-544`); no-AI objects are skipped (`:537-539`).

## Rust
Leftover `friend_compute_ground_path` ports the C++ filters (dual-world gated).
Live `compute_ground_path_should_group` (`command_executor/group.rs:281-292`) sets `closest_sqr` from **every alive member** — aircraft, structures, no-AI props included. That value then fails the `min_d` / `distanceRequiresGroup` tests (`:302-304`).

## Evidence
- C++ `AIGroup.cpp:534-549`
- Live `group.rs:281-304`; callers `movement.rs:33`, `:51`

## Player-visible
Select jets + tanks and order a short/medium move: the aircraft's distance to the click suppresses group pathing, so the tanks fan out individually. Retail ignores aircraft distance and group-paths the ground units.
close_reason: leftover friend_compute_ground_path measures only AI infantry/vehicle (skips aircraft/no-AI). Live compute_ground_path_should_group matches.

title: [AIGroup] Live group special power fires only the first caster
description:
## C++
`AIGroup::groupDoSpecialPower` / `AtLocation` / `AtObject` (`AIGroup.cpp:2614-2735`) loop **every** member. Each object with a matching `SpecialPowerModule`, science, and `canDoSpecialPower*` fires `doSpecialPower*`.
`getSpecialPowerSourceObject` (`:3170-3186`) is only a cursor/ActionManager query (first capable member), **not** the fire loop.
Dispatch (`GameLogicDispatch.cpp:653-745`) calls `currentlySelectedGroup->groupDoSpecialPower*` on the whole selection.

## Rust
Leftover `group_do_special_power*` (`ai/group.rs:986-1018`) fans the leftover common helper (dual-world gated).
Live `execute_special_power` (`command_executor/special_power.rs:179-187`) comments that C++ "only the module owner fires" and sets `casters = vec![src]` from `special_power_source_object` (first living member whose cooldown map contains the power). Fallback to all units only when **no** member tracks the power.

## Evidence
- C++ `AIGroup.cpp:2614-2735` vs `:3170-3186`
- Live `special_power.rs:70-90`, `:179-187`

## Player-visible
Multi-select four Tank Hunters and click TNT: one charge plants, three sit idle. Same for any duplicated unit special power (demo charge, microwave, etc.). Retail fires every selected unit that can do the power.
close_reason: leftover group_do_special_power* already fans every capable member. Live execute_special_power now fires all tracked casters.

title: [AIGroup] Live combat drop never unloads / rappels passengers
description:
## C++
`AIGroup::groupCombatDrop` (`AIGroup.cpp:2867-2889`) calls `ai->aiCombatDrop(target, pos, cmdSource)` on each member. The transport flies to the target and rappels/unloads passengers there.

## Rust

Live `execute_combat_drop` (`command_executor/transport.rs:614-643`) only `path_to_goal_with_state(..., AIState::Entering)` and optionally `unit_command_set_order_target`. Nothing unloads passengers at the drop zone. Host combat-chinook residual documents rappel/combat-drop as fail-closed.

## Evidence
- C++ `AIGroup.cpp:2867-2889`
- Live `transport.rs:614-643`

## Player-visible
Chinook combat drop (Alt+C / combat-drop command): the transport flies to the marked point and hovers with troops still aboard. Troops never rappel out.
