title: [Drawable] Health bars ignore selected/hover/showObjectHealth/FORCEATTACKABLE
description:
## C++
`Drawable::drawHealthBar` (`Drawable.cpp:3825-3937`) draws only when `TheGlobalData->m_showObjectHealth` and the drawable is selected or moused-over. It returns immediately for `KINDOF_FORCEATTACKABLE` (civ fences) and when health or maxHealth is 0.

## Rust
Live `BasicDrawable::draw_health_bar` (`basic_overlay.rs:114-141`) always writes `overlay_data.visible = true` and a health ratio whenever a region exists. `draw_icon_ui` (`:638-639`) calls it for every projected drawable. `GameClient::draw_drawable_icon_overlays` (`impl_draw.rs:258-304`) then fills a bar for every overlay with `visible && health_region && health_ratio > 0`. `show_object_health` is toggled by meta-event (`dispatch.rs:843`) but never read on this path. No `ForceAttackable` skip.

## Evidence
C++ `Drawable.cpp:3834-3861`. Rust `basic_overlay.rs:114-141` and `impl_draw.rs:286-303`. Host empty dual-world still projects a default 20wu box (`compute_health_region_from_presentation_pose`).

## Player-visible
Every living unit and building always shows a health bar. Fences show bars when force-attacked. Options/script `showObjectHealth` off does nothing.
close_reason: drawHealthBar now requires ShowObjectHealth + selected/hover, skips KINDOF_FORCEATTACKABLE and 0 health (Drawable.cpp:3834-3861).

title: [Squad] Live control groups never write leftover Player.squads / Squad xfer
description:
## C++
`Player::m_squads[NUM_HOTKEY_SQUADS]` plus `m_currentSelection` (`Player.h:791-792`) are always `newInstance(Squad)` in `Player::init` (`Player.cpp:374-386`).
`processCreateTeamGameMessage` (`Player.cpp:3629-3648`) clears the slot, then for each object ID: `removeObjectFromHotkeySquad` then `addObject`.
`processSelectTeamGameMessage` / `processAddTeamGameMessage` (`:3654-3703`) copy `getLiveObjects()` into `m_currentSelection`.
`Player::xfer` (`:4440-4478`) writes squad count + `xferSnapshot` of every hotkey squad and current selection. `Squad::xfer` (`Squad.cpp:184-239`) is version + unsigned-short count + ObjectIDs.
Client `SelectionXlat` META_CREATE/SELECT/ADD_TEAM posts `MSG_CREATE_TEAM*` / `MSG_SELECT_TEAM*` / `MSG_ADD_TEAM*` into the lockstep stream (`SelectionXlat.cpp:1030-1207`). `GameLogicDispatch.cpp:1830-1898` routes those to the Player processors.

## Rust
Leftover GameLogic `Player` (`GameLogic/src/player/core.rs:85-86`, `production.rs:393-443`, `snapshot.rs:625-657`) has `squads: [Option<Squad>; 10]`, `current_selection`, `get_hotkey_squad`, `set_currently_selected_ai_group` / `add_ai_group_to_current_selection` (via leftover `Squad::squad_from_ai_group`), and C++-shaped xfer.
Leftover `ai/squad.rs` implements add/remove/get_live/xfer matching Squad.cpp.
**There is no `process_create_team` / `process_select_team` / `process_add_team`.** Main never calls leftover `get_hotkey_squad`.
Live host stores groups in `CnCGameEngine.control_groups: HashMap<u8, Vec<ObjectId>>` (`cnc_game_engine/types.rs:1183`, `hotkeys.rs:12-25`). Assign is a HashMap insert of `selected_objects`. Host save/xfer never writes `control_groups`. Wave 1055 numerals stamp from that HashMap, not leftover Player.squads.

## Evidence
- C++ `Player.cpp:3629-3648`, `:4440-4478`; `Squad.cpp:184-239`; `GameLogicDispatch.cpp:1830-1898`
- Leftover `GameLogic/src/player/snapshot.rs:625-657`, `ai/squad.rs:287-329`
- Live `cnc_game_engine/hotkeys.rs:12-25`; Main `game_logic` has no `control_groups`/`hotkey_squads` xfer (grep)

## Player-visible
Ctrl+0-9 groups vanish on save/load. They are not part of the lockstep message stream (desync / no replay). Leftover Player squads stay empty so any leftover drawable numeral path that queries `Player::get_hotkey_squad` shows no group numbers unless the host catalog stamp is used.
close_reason: Live CREATE_TEAM local-only + leftover Player.squads write; Shift+# ADD_TEAM; MaxSelectionSize via host_set_selection; SELECT_HERO first-hero lookAt+contain unwrap; SELECT_ALL skips IGNORES_SELECT_ALL; drag-box rejects structures; SELECT_ALL_AIRCRAFT=KINDOF_AIRCRAFT; lookAt last live; CREATE evicts other squads; VIEW_TEAM group>=1

title: [Squad] Live Shift+# inverts C++ ADD_TEAM (writes group instead of selecting it)
description:
## C++
CommandMap `ADD_TEAM0..9` → `MSG_META_ADD_TEAM*` (`MetaEvent.cpp`).
`SelectionXlat` META_ADD_TEAM (`SelectionXlat.cpp:1136-1211`):
- Double-tap (20 frames, same group): camera `lookAt` last `getLiveObjects()` unit.
- Else: if first selected drawable is `KINDOF_STRUCTURE`, `deselectAllDrawables()` (Jan 2005 group force-attack exploit).
- Append `MSG_ADD_TEAM0+group` and `selectDrawable` for every live squad member.
`Player::processAddTeamGameMessage` (`Player.cpp:3684-3703`) adds that squad's `getLiveObjects()` **into** `m_currentSelection`. It does **not** mutate the hotkey squad from the current selection.
Creating/replacing a squad is Ctrl (`META_CREATE_TEAM` → `MSG_CREATE_TEAM`).

## Rust
Live Shift+digit (`cnc_game_engine/hotkeys.rs:26-41`) **merges current selection into `control_groups[n]`**. It does not add the stored group to the current selection, does not post `MSG_ADD_TEAM`, and does not deselect a selected structure first.
Plain digit is SELECT; Ctrl is CREATE. So Shift is wired as "add selection to group" (StarCraft-style) instead of retail "add group to selection".

## Evidence
- C++ `SelectionXlat.cpp:1136-1211`, `Player.cpp:3684-3703`
- Live `hotkeys.rs:26-41`

## Player-visible
Shift+1 with a building selected plus a few Rangers **writes those units into group 1** instead of **also selecting group 1**. Additive select of a control group is missing. The structure-selected + add-group force-attack exploit gate never runs.
close_reason: Live CREATE_TEAM local-only + leftover Player.squads write; Shift+# ADD_TEAM; MaxSelectionSize via host_set_selection; SELECT_HERO first-hero lookAt+contain unwrap; SELECT_ALL skips IGNORES_SELECT_ALL; drag-box rejects structures; SELECT_ALL_AIRCRAFT=KINDOF_AIRCRAFT; lookAt last live; CREATE evicts other squads; VIEW_TEAM group>=1

title: [AIGroup] Live Evacuate paths airborne transports to Y=0 and unloads in air
description:
## C++
`AIGroup::groupEvacuate` (`AIGroup.cpp:2408-2440`):
- If member is `KINDOF_AIRCRAFT` and `OBJECT_STATUS_IS_AIRBORNE_TARGET`: set dest Z to `TheTerrainLogic->getGroundHeight`, then `aiMoveToAndEvacuate` (path to ground, **then** unload).
- Else if AI: `aiEvacuate()`.
- Else if `KINDOF_STRUCTURE`: `contain->orderAllPassengersToExit`.

## Rust
Leftover `group_evacuate` (`ai/group.rs:847-870`) matches that: airborne uses `terrain.get_ground_height` + `ai_move_to_and_evacuate`; structures without AI `order_all_passengers_to_exit`.
Live `execute_evacuate` (`command_executor/transport.rs:425-488`) comments the C++ split but:
- Airborne dest is `Vec3::new(pos.x, 0.0, pos.z)` (sea-level Y=0, not terrain height).
- Immediately also `execute_exit` on the airborne container (unload while still in the air).
- Ground path is `execute_exit` only.

## Evidence
- C++ `AIGroup.cpp:2408-2440`
- Leftover `ai/group.rs:847-870`
- Live `transport.rs:425-488` (comment at 464: "host residual uses Y=0 ground plane")

## Player-visible
Evacuate on a flying Chinook/Combat Chinook dumps passengers at current air position (or paths the hull toward Y=0, which is underground on hills). Retail flies to the ground under the aircraft first, then unloads.
close_reason: leftover group_evacuate already uses terrain.get_ground_height + ai_move_to_and_evacuate. Live execute_evacuate now uses terrain_height_at and does not unload in air.

title: [AIGroup] Live Stop skips garrison occupants, slaves, and while-stealthed gate
description:
## C++
`AIGroup::groupIdle` (`AIGroup.cpp:2030-2084`):
- Members with AI: `aiIdle(cmdSource)` plus player-stop stealth mood delay (`CAN_STEALTH`, `canAutoAcquire`, not STEALTHED/DETECTED, **and** `!canAutoAcquireWhileStealthed`) using `stealth->getStealthDelay() + GameLogicRandomValue(0, LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND)`.
- Members **without** AI: `contain->iterateContained(makeMemberStop, ...)` so garrisoned buildings stop their occupants.
- Then `getSpawnBehaviorInterface()->orderSlavesToGoIdle` (Stinger Site / Helix / etc.).

## Rust
Leftover `AIGroup::group_idle` (`GameLogic/src/ai/group.rs:1225-1237`) only `ai_idle`s members that have an AI interface. No stealth delay, no garrison iterate, no slaves. Dual-world empty gate no-ops the whole call.
Live `execute_stop` (`command_executor/attack.rs:364-372`) calls `unit_command_stop` (idle that one object) then `apply_player_stealth_mood_delay` for every selected id.
`unit_command_stop` (`world_scripts/unit_commands.rs:212-225`) never walks contain or spawn slaves.
`unit_command_apply_stealth_mood_delay` (`:1297-1317`) skips the `!canAutoAcquireWhileStealthed` gate and uses `(i % 30)` skew instead of `0..LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND` random.

## Evidence
- C++ `AIGroup.cpp:2030-2084`
- Leftover `ai/group.rs:1225-1237`
- Live `attack.rs:364-372`, `unit_commands.rs:212-225`, `:1297-1317`

## Player-visible
S on a garrisoned bunker/base does not stop the infantry inside (they keep firing). S on a Stinger Site / Helix does not idle spawned slaves. Stealth combat units that **are** allowed to auto-acquire while stealthed still get a mood delay (retail does not).
close_reason: leftover group_idle: ai_idle + stealth mood delay, garrison iterateContained stop, order_slaves_to_go_idle (GameLogic/src/ai/group.rs). Live execute_stop walks occupants and hive slaves.

title: [Squad] Live CREATE does not evict a unit from other hotkey squads
description:
## C++
`Player::processCreateTeamGameMessage` (`Player.cpp:3637-3647`): `m_squads[hotkeyNum]->clearSquad()` then for each argument object that still exists:
`removeObjectFromHotkeySquad(obj)` then `m_squads[hotkeyNum]->addObject(obj)`.
`removeObjectFromHotkeySquad` (`:3756-3767`) walks all 10 squads and removes the object. Comment: a unit should never be on more than one hotkey squad.
`getSquadNumberForObject` (`:3744-3752`) returns the first matching slot (used for group numerals on drawables).

## Rust
Leftover Common `Player::remove_object_from_hotkey_squad` (`Common/src/common/rts/player.rs:3315-3320`) exists and matches C++, but live never calls it.
Live CREATE (`cnc_game_engine/hotkeys.rs:12-25`) does `control_groups.insert(group_num, selected_objects.clone())` with no eviction from other groups. Shift-add (`:26-36`) appends IDs if missing. A unit can sit in group 1 and group 2.
Live numeral reverse-map (`camera_drain.rs:2302-2311`) uses `entry.or_insert` so the **lowest** group number wins for the overlay — other memberships stay live for recall.

## Evidence
- C++ `Player.cpp:3637-3647`, `:3756-3767`
- Leftover unused `player.rs:3315-3320`
- Live `hotkeys.rs:12-36`, `camera_drain.rs:2302-2311`

## Player-visible
Assigning a Ranger to Ctrl+2 after it was on Ctrl+1 leaves it on both. Recalling 1 and 2 both select it. Overlay shows only the lowest group number. In retail, creating group 2 removes it from group 1.
close_reason: Live CREATE_TEAM local-only + leftover Player.squads write; Shift+# ADD_TEAM; MaxSelectionSize via host_set_selection; SELECT_HERO first-hero lookAt+contain unwrap; SELECT_ALL skips IGNORES_SELECT_ALL; drag-box rejects structures; SELECT_ALL_AIRCRAFT=KINDOF_AIRCRAFT; lookAt last live; CREATE evicts other squads; VIEW_TEAM group>=1

title: [Display] Options setDisplayMode leftover never changes the device
description:
## C++
`W3DDisplay::setDisplayMode` (`W3DDisplay.cpp` 557-570) calls `WW3D::Set_Device_Resolution` and `Render2DClass::Set_Screen_Resolution`, then `Display::setDisplayMode` to rescale `TheTacticalView` origin/size. On failure it restores the previous device mode and returns FALSE. Options `saveOptions` (`OptionsMenu.cpp` 1056-1093) enumerates `TheDisplay->getDisplayModeCount/Description` (4:3, >=800x600, >=24-bit) and only writes prefs / rebuilds Shell after a successful `TheDisplay->setDisplayMode`. Decline (`MainMenu.cpp` 720) calls `setDisplayMode` with the old settings.

## Rust
`Display::set_display_mode` (`display.rs` 417-451) only mutates width/height/bit-depth/windowed fields and rescales the tactical view; it never resizes the wgpu surface / window and always returns true. Options `apply_options` (`menu_callbacks.rs` 1043-1096) writes `GlobalData.x/y_resolution` and `set_pending_resolution_change`. `accept_resolution` (`main_menu.rs` 2181-2189) only clears the flag. `rollback_resolution_state` comments out `TheDisplay->setDisplayMode`. Resolution combo is a hardcoded mixed 4:3/16:9 list, not `getDisplayModeCount`.

## Evidence
C++ OptionsMenu.cpp:1062 `if (TheDisplay->setDisplayMode(...))`. Rust accept_resolution does not call Display. `Display::set_display_mode` has no `graphics` / surface reconfigure.

## Player-visible
Picking a new resolution in Options does not change the window or swap chain. Confirm/decline dialogs do not apply or revert a real mode change. HUD layout may think it is 1920x1080 while the surface stays at the boot size.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Boot at 800x600 (or current window size).
2. Options → pick 1024x768 or 1920x1080 → accept the confirmation.

## Acceptance Criteria
Successful Options resolution apply calls through Display setDisplayMode, actually changes the device/window/surface, rescales the tactical view like C++ Display::setDisplayMode, and reverts the device on decline / failed mode set.
close_reason: Display::set_display_mode resizes wgpu surface/depth + rescales tactical view; Options apply/decline call apply_script_display_mode; Main apply_pending_display_mode resizes window/WW3D

title: [Display] drawImage leftover ignores GRAYSCALE ADDITIVE and ROTATED_90
description:
## C++
`W3DDisplay::drawImage` (`W3DDisplay.cpp` 2603-2769) honors `DrawImageMode`: ALPHA (default), GRAYSCALE (`Enable_Grayscale`), ADDITIVE, SOLID (no alpha). Clip region remaps screen+UV; `IMAGE_STATUS_ROTATED_90_CLOCKWISE` draws two tris with swapped UVs. `W3DPushButton` (`W3DPushButton.cpp` 345-368) uses overlay-states + !ENABLED + !NOT_READY + !ALWAYS_COLOR → `DRAW_IMAGE_GRAYSCALE` on the color artwork (comment: grayscale disabled buttons from original color art).

## Rust
Live `WindowManager::win_draw_image` (`game_window_global.rs` 35-103) always submits an alpha textured quad (`draw_textured_rect`). No mode argument, no grayscale/additive/solid, no clip-UV, no rotate-90 path. `ImageStatus::ROTATED_90_CLOCKWISE` is copied from MappedImage on load (`image.rs` 1156-1157) and never read at draw. Push-button overlay disabled path (`push_button.rs`) draws `disabled_draw_data` / color cameos via `win_draw_image` without grayscale.

## Evidence
C++ `W3DDisplay.cpp` switch(mode) + rotated Add_Tri. C++ `W3DPushButton.cpp:351-359`. Rust `win_draw_image` has no DrawImageMode. Grep of GameClient gui draw: no `DRAW_IMAGE_GRAYSCALE` / `Enable_Grayscale`.

## Player-visible
Disabled overlay-state cameos/buttons stay full-color instead of desaturated. Additive HUD images (glows) alpha-blend instead of add. MappedImages marked rotated-90 draw upright / wrong UVs. Clipped images are not UV-cropped.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open a command cameo that uses WIN_STATUS_USE_OVERLAY_STATES and disable it (not ready clock excluded).
2. Compare to C++: the color art should go grayscale.

## Acceptance Criteria
Live drawImage/win_draw_image applies GRAYSCALE/ADDITIVE/SOLID and ROTATED_90 UV mapping like W3DDisplay::drawImage. Overlay-state disabled buttons desaturate color art unless ALWAYS_COLOR / NOT_READY.
close_reason: win_draw_image_ex + queue_draw_image_mesh_on apply GRAYSCALE/ADDITIVE/SOLID, clip UV, ROTATED_90; overlay disabled buttons desaturate unless ALWAYS_COLOR/NOT_READY

title: [Display] takeScreenShot leftover dumps movie buffer not the backbuffer
description:
## C++
`W3DDisplay::takeScreenShot` (`W3DDisplay.cpp` 2970-3096) locks the DX8 front buffer client rect, writes `sshotNNN.bmp` under `TheGlobalData->getPath_UserData()`, and posts `TheInGameUI->message(TheGameText->fetch("GUI:ScreenCapture"), leaf)`.

## Rust
`Display::take_screenshot` (`display.rs` 551-567) picks `sshotNNN.bmp` in user-data and posts `GUI:ScreenCapture`, then queues `pending_screenshot`. The flush (`display.rs` 1185-1193) only writes `last_movie_frame` (decompressed Bink/logo buffer), and only inside leftover `Display::draw`. Host present never calls `Display::draw`, so the file is never written. If a movie once played, a later screenshot would dump that stale movie frame, not the current view. F12 in Main (`hotkeys.rs` 1171-1192) is a separate residual: `ww3d_engine::make_screenshot` to `temp/generals_screenshots/screenshot_{unix}.png` with a raw HUD string — not user-data BMP / GameText.

## Evidence
C++ front-buffer LockRect + CreateBMPFile. Rust flush gated on `last_movie_frame` inside `Display::draw`. Host `impl_update.rs` skips `draw_display`. Closed hq-mu35 claimed ww3d-engine readback from Display::take_screenshot; that call is not in the live Display method.

## Player-visible
Script/Display screenshot announces `GUI:ScreenCapture` but does not capture the game view. F12, if it works, writes a differently named PNG in the temp dir instead of sequential `sshotNNN.bmp` in user data.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In a live match with no movie playing, fire the Display/script screenshot path (`TheDisplay->takeScreenShot` / TAKE_SCREENSHOT through Display).
2. Check user-data for a new `sshotNNN.bmp` of the current frame.

## Acceptance Criteria
Display takeScreenShot writes a BMP of the presented backbuffer to user-data `sshotNNN.bmp` and posts `GUI:ScreenCapture` with that leaf, matching C++.
close_reason: take_screenshot writes user-data sshotNNN.bmp from LAST_PRESENTED_FRAME; movie blit notes that buffer as backbuffer; host flush prefers BMP then WW3D

title: [Display] Host present never blits fullscreen Display movies
description:
## C++
`W3DDisplay::draw` (`W3DDisplay.cpp` 1887-1898) always `drawVideoBuffer(m_videoBuffer, 0, 0, getWidth(), getHeight())` after InGameUI/mouse when `m_videoStream && m_videoBuffer`. `Display::playMovie` / `playLogoMovie` (`Display.cpp` 179-238) open the stream; `Display::update` decompresses frames.

## Rust
`Display::update_movie_playback` still decompresses into `last_movie_frame`, and leftover `Display::draw` now blits via `display_fx::blit_video_rgba` (closed hq-x6ax). Live host presentation skips that path: `GameClient::update` host branch comments "No draw_display — Main RenderPipeline is sole present path" (`impl_update.rs`). Main `render()` never samples `last_movie_frame` / `blit_video_rgba`. Script/score-screen/victory movies call `play_script_display_movie` → `Display::play_movie` then wait on `is_movie_playing`, but nothing presents the frames.

## Evidence
C++ `W3DDisplay.cpp:1887-1890`. Rust `display.rs` 688-747 + 1125-1131 blit only inside `DisplayInterface::draw`. `impl_update.rs` host path ~line 72 skips `draw_display`. Grep of `GeneralsRust/Code/Main` finds no `blit_video` / `last_movie_frame`. hq-x6ax closed on Display::draw blit, which is not the live present path.

## Player-visible
In-game script movies, score-screen victory movies, and other fullscreen Display movies stay black / show the 3D scene underneath even though the stream is "playing". Skip/wait logic still blocks on `is_movie_playing`.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Play a campaign/script that calls PLAY_MOVIE / fullscreen Display movie, or finish a match that plays the score-screen victory movie.
2. Observe the live Main present path while `is_movie_playing` is true.

## Acceptance Criteria
Live host present blits the current Display video buffer fullscreen (C++ `drawVideoBuffer`) while a Display movie is playing, then shows copyright/hold on logo movies. `is_movie_playing` remains true only while frames are actually shown.
close_reason: Host render present_movie_overlay/present_copyright_overlay; Display::update stores last movie frame for live blit

title: [Display] Gamma ramp stored but never applied to the frame
description:
## C++
`W3DDisplay::setGamma` (`W3DDisplay.cpp` 519-524) calls `DX8Wrapper::Set_Gamma(gamma, bright, contrast, calibrate)` in fullscreen (windowed returns so desktop gamma is untouched). `W3DDisplay::init` applies `TheGlobalData->m_displayGamma` when != 1. Options `saveOptions` (`OptionsMenu.cpp`) calls `TheDisplay->setGamma(gammaval, 0.0f, 1.0f, FALSE)` so the slider retints immediately.

## Rust
`Display::set_gamma` / Options `apply_options` / `apply_display_gamma` only write `display_fx::GAMMA_STATE` (`display.rs` 547-548, `menu_callbacks.rs` 1058-1072). `apply_gamma_pass` (`display_fx.rs` 346-363) is a no-op (`let _ = (encoder, device, ...);` comment about a future pass) and is never called. `apply_gamma_rgba` / `gamma_uniform` have no live render callers (tests only). Main render pipeline never reads the ramp.

## Evidence
`display_fx.rs` `apply_gamma_pass` body does not encode. Repo grep: `apply_gamma_pass(` only at its definition. Closed hq-tjnn / hq-fktv claimed set_gamma + Options hook; the presented image is still unmapped.

## Player-visible
Options gamma slider and `GlobalData.display_gamma` do not brighten/darken the picture. Fullscreen or windowed, the ramp is stored and discarded.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open Options, drag Gamma away from default, accept.
2. Look at the 3D scene and UI.

## Acceptance Criteria
Changing Options gamma (or `display_gamma` at init) remaps the presented frame like C++ `DX8Wrapper::Set_Gamma`. Identity (1, 0, 1) is a no-op.
close_reason: set_gamma stores ramp; blit_video_rgba/apply_gamma_pass/screenshot remap pixels; identity (1,0,1) no-op

title: [TurretAI] Position targets never rotate the turret
description:
## C++
`TurretAI::setTurretTargetPosition` (`TurretAI.cpp:589-626`) sets `TARGET_POSITION`, goal position, and AIM. `TurretAIAimTurretState` (`:1038-1041`) aims at that Coord3D (no object). Fire then `fireCurrentWeapon(getMachineGoalPosition())`, and linked turrets fire every slot at the point (`AIStates.cpp:5268-5283`).

## Rust
Live host has `set_turret_target_object` only (`object/weapons.rs:673-699`). No `turret_target_pos` / `set_turret_target_position`. `tick_turret_aim` requires `turret_target_id` and a live victim object (`attack.rs:670-678`); missing id → Failure/Hold.

## Evidence
C++ `friend_getTurretTarget` `TARGET_POSITION` branch copies `getGoalPosition()`.
Host grep of `set_turret_target_position` / `turret_target_pos` under `Main/src/game_logic` is empty.

## Player-visible effect
Force-fire / attack-ground / FireWeaponPower location shots never rotate the barrel onto the click. The hull may attack the point while the turret stays at rest or recenters.

## Split hint
Add a position target on the host object, aim `tick_turret_aim` at that Coord3D, and fire the current (or linked) weapon at the point.
close_reason: turret.rs: set_turret_target_position + AIM/fire at Coord3D

title: [TurretAI] Aim enters Fire without in-range or addTargeter
description:
## C++
`TurretAIAimTurretState::update` (`TurretAI.cpp:1146-1175`) returns SUCCESS only when turn and pitch are aligned **and** the current weapon `isWithinAttackRange`. If `isTemporarilyPreventingAimSuccess()` or no turret weapon is in range, it stays in AIM (`STATE_CONTINUE`). Object targets also `addTargeter` every tick (`:1024-1030`) and abort when the victim team changes or `getAbleToAttackSpecificObject(ATTACK_CONTINUED_TARGET[_FORCED])` fails.

## Rust
Live `tick_turret_state_machine` Aim (`world_tick/attack.rs:555-561`) treats `tick_turret_aim` Success (yaw within 2°) as Fire immediately. `tick_turret_aim` does not test range, team, `addTargeter`, or prevent-aim. Comment at `:554` claims "OOR while aiming stays in AIM" but the code never checks range before Success.

## Evidence
C++: `if (turnAlignedToNemesis && pitchAlignedToNemesis && curWeapon->isWithinAttackRange(...)) { if (preventing || nothingInRange) return STATE_CONTINUE; return STATE_SUCCESS; }`
Host: `match self.tick_turret_aim(...) { Success => { turret_substate = Fire; attack_fire_weapon_enter } }`.

## Player-visible effect
Turrets flash firing-weapon status and attempt shots while still approaching. Targets are not marked as being aimed at (no evasion/prevent window). Team-flipped victims stay locked.

## Split hint
Gate Aim→Fire on in-range + !preventing, call addTargeter on the victim AI, and drop the target when ContinuedTarget fails or the initial team changes.
close_reason: turret.rs: update_aim_state in-range+addTargeter+prevent-aim

title: [Recorder] init_controls never shows ReplayControl.wnd during playback
description:
## C++
`RecorderClass::initControls` (Recorder.cpp 1552-1562) looks up `ReplayControl.wnd:ParentReplayControl` and `winHide(getMode() != PLAYBACK)` — show the replay transport only during playback.

`GameLogic::startNewGame` (GameLogic.cpp 2009-2010) always calls `TheRecorder->initControls()` after preload, so every new game (including `GAME_REPLAY`) applies that visibility.

`InGameUI::createReplayControl` loads `ReplayControl.wnd`; `showReplayControls` / ControlBar show/hide also key off `isInReplayGame()`.

## Rust
`Recorder::init_controls` (`common/recorder.rs` 1728-1732) is an empty stub (comments only).

Nothing in GameLogic `start_new_game_now` (impl_lifecycle.rs) calls it. `rg init_controls` / `create_replay_control` / `show_replay_controls` under GameClient live paths: no InGameUI create/show equivalent.

## Evidence
```
pub fn init_controls(&self) {
    // Show/hide replay control window based on mode
    // In C++: finds "ReplayControl.wnd:ParentReplayControl" window
    // and calls winHide() based on mode != PLAYBACK
}
```

## Player-visible effect
During a replay the Play/Pause/Stop/Fast-forward bar never appears (or, if the layout default is visible, it stays up in normal games). Players cannot pause or fast-forward a replay from the in-game transport UI.
close_reason: init_controls shows/hides ReplayControl.wnd:ParentReplayControl (winHide mode!=PLAYBACK); GameClient create_replay_control + hook; start_new_game_now calls init_controls

title: [Recorder] Replay command type IDs are 79-148 not C++ 1000-base
description:
## C++
`MessageStream.h` 447-462: network command enums are **fixed at 1000** so replay files have stable IDs:

> "we have the same numeric values for all enums that are saved in replay files"

`MSG_BEGIN_NETWORK_MESSAGES = 1000`, then `MSG_CREATE_SELECTED_GROUP` = 1001 … `MSG_LOGIC_CRC` ~1068. `MSG_CLEAR_GAME_DATA` / `MSG_NEW_GAME` sit near the start of the enum (~130-131).

`writeToFile` (Recorder.cpp 706-707) writes `sizeof(GameMessage::Type)` (4-byte enum value) as stored.

## Rust
`MessageSerializer::get_message_type_id` (message_serialization.rs 923+) densely packs types: `ClearGameData=25`, `NewGame=26`, `CreateSelectedGroup=79`, `DoMoveTo=119`, `LogicCRC=146`. `write_to_file` writes that `u16` as `u32`. `append_next_command` decodes with the same table — IDs ≥1000 are unmapped and abort playback (`decode_message_type` Err → `stop_playback`).

Header layout (GENREP, 4-byte time_t, 16-byte SYSTEMTIME) was deliberately matched to C++; the command stream IDs were not.

## Evidence
C++ comment at MessageStream.h:450-462 vs Rust `CreateSelectedGroup => 79` / `LogicCRC => 146`.
`append_next_command` on unknown type: `log::error!("Failed to decode replay message type")` then `stop_playback()`.

## Player-visible effect
Retail/C++ `.rep` files stop at the first recorded command (or execute the wrong command). Rust-recorded replays cannot be played in the original game. The GENREP header parses, then units never move because every order type ID is in the wrong number space.
close_reason: replay write/read uses C++ 1000-base type IDs (CreateSelectedGroup=1001, DoMoveTo=1068, LogicCRC=1095); team slots 1006/1016/1026-base

title: [Recorder] start_recording writes empty/lossy GameInfo so replays cannot reconstruct lobby slots
description:
## C++
`RecorderClass::startRecording` (Recorder.cpp 580-628) serializes the *live* lobby:
- `TheNetwork && TheLAN` → `GameInfoToAsciiString(TheLAN->GetMyGame())` and local slot by matching `getLocalIP()`
- else `TheGameSpyGame` + `getLocalSlotNum()`
- else `TheSkirmishGameInfo` (sets `REPLAY_CRC_INTERVAL`, localIndex=0)
- else `m_gameInfo` (SP empty slot list)

`ReplayGameInfo` **is** a `GameInfo` (Recorder.h 10-21) with full `GameSlot` (name, IP, color, template, start pos, team, NAT). `readReplayHeader` parses that string into `m_gameInfo`. `GameLogic::startNewGame` binds `TheGameInfo = TheRecorder->getGameInfo()` during playback (GameLogic.cpp 1172-1174) so colors, sides, start spots, and teams come back.

`startRecording` always `reset()` first (wipes `m_gameInfo` to map+seed), then reads the *external* live pointers above.

## Rust
Live `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/recorder.rs` `start_recording` (891-1002):
1. `reset()` → `init()` wipes slots to empty/closed and only restores map+seed.
2. Writes `game_info_to_ascii_string(&self.game_info.to_game_info())` — never consults LAN / GameSpy / skirmish GameInfo.
3. `ReplayGameInfo` is a stripped struct (name/ip/human/observer/occupied only). `apply_network_info` / `to_game_info` drop color, player_template, start_pos, team, NAT, cash, superweapon restriction.
4. `get_game_info()` is unused by GameLogic `start_new_game_now` (impl_lifecycle.rs).

## Evidence
`start_recording` after `reset()`:
```
let slot_list = game_info_to_ascii_string(&self.game_info.to_game_info());
let local_index = self.resolve_local_slot_index(); // -1 when slots empty
```
`apply_network_info` copies only name/ip/is_human/is_occupied/is_observer.

## Player-visible effect
Skirmish/LAN/online recordings store an empty or closed slot list. Playback cannot reconstruct who played, which side/color/start they had, or alliances. Replays spawn the wrong (or no) players and look like a broken skirmish setup. Retail/C++ `.rep` files also lose lobby data when loaded, because `apply_network_info` strips the parsed GameInfo.
close_reason: start_recording captures live lobby before reset and writes full GameInfoToAsciiString (color/template/start/team/NAT); parse restores slots

title: [Recorder] Playback from the shell map never clears the live game
description:
## C++
`RecorderClass::playbackFile` (Recorder.cpp 1031-1036): if not analyzing and `TheGameLogic->isInGame()`, call `TheGameLogic->clearGameData()`.

`GameLogic::isInGame()` is `!(m_gameMode == GAME_NONE)` (GameLogic.h 375). The shell map is `GAME_SHELL`, which **is** in-game. Starting a replay from the main menu therefore always tears down the shell map first.

## Rust
`playback_file` (`common/recorder.rs` 1263-1270) calls `send_clear_game_data` only when `is_current_game_in_game()`.

`is_current_game_in_game` (625-633):
```
mode != GAME_SHELL && mode != GAME_NONE
```
and if no `game_mode_provider` is set, returns **false**.

`GameClient::init_recorder_bridge` sets the provider to `TheGameLogic::get_game_mode`. From the replay menu you are on the shell map (`GAME_SHELL`), so the clear is skipped.

Unit test `test_playback_file_skips_clear_game_data_when_not_in_game` asserts SHELL does not emit `ClearGameData` — encoding the wrong C++ rule.

## Evidence
C++: `isInGame()` true for SHELL → `clearGameData()`.
Rust: SHELL treated as not-in-game; test at recorder.rs:2127-2163 expects only `NewGame`.

## Player-visible effect
Clicking a replay from the main menu leaves the shell-map game live (units, scripts, clients). The replay's `MSG_NEW_GAME` then stacks on leftover shell state — map/objects/UI from the menu bleed into the replay, or the load fails to replace the shell world cleanly.
close_reason: is_current_game_in_game matches C++ isInGame (mode!=GAME_NONE); playback from GAME_SHELL emits ClearGameData

title: [Recorder] Replay CRC path is still dead: LogicCRC never reaches handle_crc_message
description:
## C++
`GameLogic::update` (GameLogic.cpp 3642-3651) posts `MSG_LOGIC_CRC` with **two** arguments: CRC integer + `bool fromPlayback` (`TheRecorder->getMode()==PLAYBACK`).

`GameLogicDispatch` (GameLogicDispatch.cpp 1904-1946) on playback calls `TheRecorder->handleCRCMessage(newCRC, playerIndex, msg->getArgument(1)->boolean)`.

`handleCRCMessage` (Recorder.cpp 957-994): `fromPlayback` enqueues the recorded CRC; live CRCs compare against that queue using `TheGameLogic->getFrame()>0`. Same-player test is `getNthPlayer(playerIndex)` name key == `"player%d"` (local slot), or local slot < 0.

`appendNextCommand` still puts `MSG_LOGIC_CRC` on `TheCommandList` (only `MSG_BEGIN_NETWORK_MESSAGES` / `MSG_CLEAR_GAME_DATA` are dropped).

## Rust
`handle_crc_message` in `common/recorder.rs` (1617-1644) now uses `get_current_frame()` (hq-323o closed). It is **never called** from live dispatch.

`GameLogic::update` (impl_update.rs 151-166) computes `playback` then **discards it** (`let _ = playback`) and appends `LogicCRC(crc)` with no boolean argument.

`logic_message_dispatcher` `CommandType::LogicCrc` (impl_update.rs 932-937) only `trace!`s.

`write_to_file` encodes `LogicCRC` as a single Integer via `encode_message_arguments` — the playback flag is never in the `.rep`.

Same-player test is `player_index == local_player_index` (slot vs logic index), not the C++ `"playerN"` name-key check.

## Evidence
- `rg handle_crc_message` → only the definition in recorder.rs
- impl_update.rs:157 `let _ = playback;`
- dispatcher LogicCrc arm has no `handle_crc_message` call
- hq-323o fixed the frame==0 guard inside a function that the live tick never reaches

## Player-visible effect
Watching a replay never compares live vs recorded CRC. Desyncs are silent: units teleport or act differently than the original match and no warning/log/desync flag is raised. This is the remaining live-path hole after hq-323o.
close_reason: file LogicCRC enqueues via append_next_command; live CRC posts boolean fromPlayback and notify_logic_crc after recorder.update

title: [TurretAI] Fire-angle sweep never runs after shots
description:
## C++
`TurretAIAimTurretState::update` (`TurretAI.cpp:1053-1081`): if `TurretFireAngleSweep[slot] > 0` and `friend_isSweepEnabled()`, aim at `relAngle ± sweep` at `TurretSweepSpeedModifier`. Sweep enables for 3 frames after `notifyFired` (`updateTurretAI:697-702`, `ENABLE_SWEEP_FRAME_COUNT = 3`). Even with sweep disabled, alignment is `|relAngle - turretAngle| < sweep` so fire can start once inside the cone; sweep direction flips when the turn reaches the sweep extreme.

## Rust
Live host object has no sweep array, `enableSweepUntil`, or `positiveSweep`. `tick_turret_aim` always aims at `relative_angle_2d_to(victim)` with modifier 1.0. Fire path never sets a 3-frame sweep window.

## Evidence
C++: `aimAngle += sweep` / `-= sweep` then `turnSpeedModifier = getTurretSweepSpeedModifierForWeaponSlot(slot)`.
Host `tick_turret_aim:696-701`: `desired_turret = rel_world` only.

## Player-visible effect
Comanche / Paladin / authored sweep turrets lock a single bearing while firing instead of rocking through the sweep cone. Burst fire looks glued-on.

## Split hint
Store per-slot sweep + modifier from INI, set `enable_sweep_until = now+3` on host fire success, and apply the C++ aimAngle/sweep-align block in `tick_turret_aim`.
close_reason: turret.rs: sweep ±cone and enable_sweep_until=now+3 on did_fire

title: [TurretAI] Idle/IdleScan is a no-op except Strategy Center
description:
## C++
`TurretAIIdleState` / `TurretAIIdleScanState` / `TurretAIHoldTurretState` (`TurretAI.cpp:1269-1441`) run for every turret:

title: [TurretAI] Aim never pitches FirePitch/GroundUnitPitch
description:
## C++
`TurretAIAimTurretState::update` (`TurretAI.cpp:1083-1144`) when `isAllowsPitch()`:
- `FirePitch > 0` → aim at that fixed pitch.
- Else `asin(v.z / v.length())` after lowering origin by `geometry.getMaxHeightAbovePosition()/2`, clamp to `MinPhysicalPitch`.
- If `GroundUnitPitch > 0` and the target is ground (no object / `KINDOF_IMMOBILE` / `isDoingGroundMovement`): add `GroundUnitPitch * (dist/range)` so close units are not overshot.

`friend_turnTowardsPitch` uses `m_pitchRate` (`TurretPitchRate`).

## Rust
Live `tick_turret_aim` (`world_tick/attack.rs:657-708`) only turns yaw. Host object has no `allows_pitch`, `fire_pitch`, `min_pitch`, `ground_unit_pitch`, or `pitch_rate` fields (`object/mod.rs:2097-2157`). `turn_turret_towards_pitch_rad` (`weapons.rs:651-670`) exists for Recenter but uses `turret_turn_rate_rad` as the pitch rate.

## Evidence
C++: `pitchAlignedToNemesis = turret->friend_turnTowardsPitch(desiredPitch, 1.0f)` after FirePitch/asin/GroundUnitPitch.
Host aim: `turn_turret_towards_angle_rad(desired_turret, …)` then Success; pitch never written.

## Player-visible effect
AA/Patriot/Avenger barrels stay level instead of pitching at aircraft. Artillery `FirePitch` and tank `GroundUnitPitch` arcs are ignored, so close ground shots fly over the target.

## Split hint
Add the C++ pitch fields to the host object, compute desired pitch in `tick_turret_aim`, and drive `turn_turret_towards_pitch_rad` with `TurretPitchRate`.
close_reason: turret.rs: FirePitch/asin/GroundUnitPitch via compute_desired_aim_pitch

title: [WW3D Collision] Ray-OBBox and AABox-OBBox ignore orientation
description:
## C++
`CollisionMath::Collide(line, OBBox)` (`colmathline.cpp:276-326`) transforms the ray into the box basis (`Basis.Transpose() * (P0 - Center)`) then runs the aligned slab test. `Intersection_Test(AABox, OBBox)` / `Collide(AABox, move, OBBox, move2)` (`colmathobbobb.cpp`) use full SAT on the 15 axes (3+3+9). Sphere-OBBox intersection transforms the sphere center into box space.

Orientation is first-class: a long thin box rotated 45° is not treated as an axis-aligned box of the local extents.

## Rust
Live glam adapter `ww3d-collision` (re-exported by `ww3d-compat`, depended on by ww3d-physics/particles):

`bounding_volumes/collision_detection.rs:108-112`:
```
pub fn test_obbox(&self, obbox: &OBBoxClass) -> Option<CollisionResult> {
    // For simplified OBBox (axis-aligned), just use AABox intersection
    let aabox = AABoxClass::from_center_and_extent(obbox.center, obbox.extent);
    self.test_aabox(&aabox)
}
```

`test_aabox_obbox` (216-218) does the same: `from_center_and_extent(obbox.center, obbox.extent)` then AABB-AABB.

This is **not** even the world AABB of the OBB (`Compute_Axis_Aligned_Extent`). A 10×1×1 box rotated 90° about Y still tests as 10×1×1 aligned to world.

`OBBoxClass::intersects_obbox` (`bounding_volumes/obbox.rs:212-213`) also reduces to `to_aabox()` vs `to_aabox()`.

## Evidence
C++ colmathline.cpp:283-284 basis-space ray; colmathobbobb.cpp SAT.
Rust collision_detection.rs:108-112, 216-218; obbox.rs:212-213.

## Player-visible effect
Rotated collision volumes (vehicles, turrets, wreckage, oriented world boxes) are tested as unrotated local-extent AABBs. Hits miss the real volume and false-hit the axis-aligned slab; picking/physics against oriented boxes is wrong.

## Split hint
Use C++ line-OBB transform + SAT for AABox-OBBox / OBBox-OBBox; `to_aabox()` only for conservative broadphase.
close_reason: RayCollisionQuery::test_obbox transforms ray by Basis.Transpose then aligned slab. test_aabox_obbox is 15-axis SAT. OBBoxClass::intersects_obbox uses CollisionMath::obbox_obbox_intersect SAT, not to_aabox(). Tests: test_ray_obbox_uses_orientation, test_aabox_obbox_uses_orientation, intersects_obbox_uses_orientation.

title: [WWMath] CollisionMath missing line-box and all OBBox collide/intersect/overlap
description:
## C++
`colmath.h` CollisionMath public API includes:
- Intersect: AABox-OBBox, OBBox-Tri, OBBox-AABox, OBBox-OBBox, Sphere-OBBox
- Overlap: AAPlane-OBBox, Plane-OBBox, Sphere-OBBox, AABox-OBBox, all OBBox-vs-{point,line,tri,AABox,OBBox}, Frustum-vs-{point,tri,sphere,AABox,OBBox} + planes_passed
- Collide: Line-AABox, Line-OBBox, AABox-OBBox, OBBox-Plane, OBBox-Tri, OBBox-AABox, OBBox-OBBox

Line-box (`colmathline.cpp:242-326`) uses `Test_Aligned_Box` slab test; OBB path transforms the ray by `Basis.Transpose()`. Used by `AABoxRenderObjClass::Cast_Ray` / `OBBoxRenderObjClass::Cast_Ray` (`boxrobj.cpp:721`) and OBB-line overlap.

Live `collision/{intersection,overlap,sweep}.rs` implement only AABox/sphere/plane/line-tri. Missing entirely:
- `collide_line_aabox` / `collide_line_obbox`
- every OBBox Intersection/Overlap/Collide overload
- Frustum overlap on this CollisionMath (only a separate `culling::CollisionMath::overlap_test_frustum_box`)

`box_render_obj.rs` has no Cast_Ray/Cast_AABox/Cast_OBBox.

## Evidence
C++ colmath.h:51-165 API; colmathline.cpp:242-326; boxrobj.cpp:721.
Rust lib.rs:65-105 module list; sweep.rs ends at collide_aabox_aabox (no line-box, no OBBox).

## Player-visible effect
W3D collision-box render objects cannot be ray-picked or swept. Any code path that needs line-vs-box or oriented-box vs oriented-box (unit collision boxes, vis boxes, physics) has no retail-equivalent math. Callers invent AABB fallbacks that miss rotated volume.

## Split hint
Compile `obbox.rs`, port `colmathline.cpp` Test_Aligned_Box + OBB transform, port `colmathobbobb.cpp` / `colmathobbtri.cpp` / `colmathobbox.cpp`.

title: [WWMath] Mesh OBBox cast is start/end static intersect, not swept SAT
description:
## C++
`CollisionMath::Collide(OBBox, move, Tri, move2, result)` in `colmathobbtri.cpp` is a full swept SAT (tri normal, 3 box basis axes, 9 edge crosses, move axes) with StartBad / MaxFrac / contact normal+point.

Callers:
- `meshgeometry.cpp` `cast_obbox_brute_force` (~1143): `CollisionMath::Collide(boxtest.Box, boxtest.Move, tri, Vector3(0,0,0), boxtest.Result)`
- `aabtree.cpp` `Cast_OBBox_To_Polys` (~897): same
- `coltest.h` `OBBoxCollisionTestClass::Cull` / collide helper

Continuous sweep: a fast-moving OBB that starts clear and ends clear but crosses a thin triangle still hits.

## Rust
`math_utilities` does not compile `obbox.rs` (`lib.rs` has no `pub mod obbox`) and has no `collide_obbox_*`.

Live mesh `MeshClass::cast_obbox` (`mesh_system_impl/render_obj.rs:158-194`) only:
1. `model.intersect_obbox` at start pose
2. `model.intersect_obbox` at `center + move`
3. hit if either static test is true

No fraction, no StartBad, no contact, tunnels through anything thinner than the move.

`intersect_obbox` itself is a workaround: transform tri into OBB local space and call `intersection_test_aabox_triangle` (static SAT only).

## Evidence
C++ meshgeometry.cpp:1143 Collide swept OBB-tri.
Rust render_obj.rs:168-185 start_hit || end_hit.
WWMath lib.rs:65-105 — no obbox module.

## Player-visible effect
Oriented collision volumes (vehicles, aircraft, rotated building boxes, decal/projector volumes) pass through walls, fences, and thin props when moving quickly. No contact normal/fraction for sliding.

## Split hint
Export OBBox from WWMath and port `colmathobbtri.cpp` Collide; wire `cast_obbox` to it instead of discrete probes.
close_reason: collide_obbox_triangle is swept SAT (local AABox-tri SAT). MeshModelClass::cast_obbox and MeshClass/RenderObj cast_obbox call it instead of start/end static intersect_obbox. AABTree cast_obbox_to_polys already used CollisionMath::obbox_triangle_swept. Test: obbox_triangle_swept_thin_hit.

title: [WWMath] AABox-triangle swept SAT is placeholder — mesh box-casts always StartBad
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/Libraries/Source/WWVegas/WWMath/colmathaabtri.cpp` `CollisionMath::Collide(AABox, move, Tri, result)` (~544-798) runs full SAT: triangle normal, 3 box axes, 9 edge crosses, plus move-vector axes. `BTCollisionStruct` starts `StartBad=true` / `MaxFrac=-0.01` and only clears StartBad when an axis proves separation (`aabtri_separation_test`). Finalize: if still StartBad → `result->StartBad=true`, `Fraction=0`; else writes first-hit fraction + contact normal.

Live caller: `meshgeometry.cpp` `cast_aabox_brute_force` / `AABTreeClass::Cast_AABox_To_Polys` call this per triangle and abort on StartBad.

## Rust
Live crate `math_utilities` (`src/lib.rs` → `collision/sweep.rs`). `CollisionMath::collide_aabox_triangle` builds `AABTriCollisionContext` the same way (`start_bad: true`, `max_frac: -0.01`) but every SAT helper is a stub:

```
fn check_normal_axis(&mut self) -> bool { false // Placeholder }
fn check_basis_axis(...) -> bool { false // Placeholder }
fn check_cross_axis(...) -> bool { false // Placeholder }
fn check_move_axis(...) -> bool { false // Placeholder }
```

`finalize_aabtri_collision` then always takes the StartBad branch (`fraction=0`, hit=true).

Live mesh path: `ww3d-renderer-3d/.../model_collision.rs` `MeshModelClass::cast_aabox` calls `MuCollisionMath::collide_aabox_triangle` for every triangle.

## Evidence
C++ colmathaabtri.cpp:556 `CollisionContext.Init(...)` then 13 axis tests; :755-760 StartBad return.
Rust sweep.rs:430-448 placeholders; :330-334 StartBad finalize.
model_collision.rs:86-90 live call.

## Player-visible effect
Any swept AABox vs a mesh (unit/projectile/camera collision, physics box-cast) reports already-embedded at t=0 as soon as one triangle is tested. Objects stop immediately, bounce, or refuse to move through empty space next to geometry.

## Split hint
Port `aabtri_check_*` / `aabtri_separation_test` from colmathaabtri.cpp into `collision/sweep.rs` (keep static intersection SAT in `intersection.rs`).
close_reason: WWMath collision/sweep.rs AABTriCollisionContext ports colmathaabtri.cpp SAT (normal, 3 box axes, 9 crosses, move axes). collide_aabox_triangle no longer StartBad-stubs. ww3d-collision collision_math.rs aabox_triangle_swept uses the same SAT. Tests: aabox_triangle_swept_face_hit / start_bad.

Paratroopers, jumping vehicles, and other airborne-target units are included; true aircraft that are not flagged airborne_target can be missed. No IGNORES_SELECT_ALL / dozer / harvester gate.

## Evidence
C++ CommandXlat.cpp:2874-2877 `requiredKindofs.set(KINDOF_AIRCRAFT)`.
Host alive.rs:861 `Aircraft || airborne_target`.
Crate select_all.rs:43-44 `aircraft_only && !obj.is_kind_of(KindOf::Aircraft)` unused on OS keys.

## Player-visible effect
W (SELECT_ALL_AIRCRAFT) can select parachuting infantry / airborne-flagged ground units and can miss parked aircraft that are KINDOF_AIRCRAFT but not airborne_target.
close_reason: Live CREATE_TEAM local-only + leftover Player.squads write; Shift+# ADD_TEAM; MaxSelectionSize via host_set_selection; SELECT_HERO first-hero lookAt+contain unwrap; SELECT_ALL skips IGNORES_SELECT_ALL; drag-box rejects structures; SELECT_ALL_AIRCRAFT=KINDOF_AIRCRAFT; lookAt last live; CREATE evicts other squads; VIEW_TEAM group>=1

title: [Production] Live crate cancel never unreserves exit door
description:
## C++
ProductionUpdate::removeFromProductionQueue (ProductionUpdate.cpp:1011-1021): if the entry is PRODUCTION_UNIT and m_exitDoor != DOOR_NONE_AVAILABLE, getObjectExitInterface()->unreserveDoorForExit. queueCreateUnit (376-395) reserves that door up front when ParkingPlaceBehavior::shouldReserveDoorWhenQueued.

## Rust
Leftover object/update/production_update.rs:980-988 unreserves on remove_from_production_queue.
Live ProductionUpdateComplete::queue_create_unit_with_id (652-654) calls reserve_parking_door_when_queued, but cancel_production / cancel_unit_by_production_id / cancel_and_refund_all_production (720-858) only refund and dequeue. No unreserve_door_for_exit.

## Evidence
Live factory is ProductionUpdateCompleteModule. ParkingPlaceBehavior::unreserve_door_for_exit exists (parking_place_behavior.rs:1359) and is used by leftover remove, not by live Complete cancel.

title: [Production] Live crate update never completes upgrades
description:
## C++

## Rust

Live factory ProductionUpdateComplete::update (production_update_complete.rs:1337-1345) only calls spawn_unit when is_complete. spawn_unit early-returns for ProductionType::Upgrade. No scorekeeper, script notify, EVA, radar, giveUpgrade, or queue pop.

contain_module_overrides/production.rs:190 constructs ProductionUpdateCompleteModule (live factory). Leftover update/production_update.rs is not factory-registered. Host apply_host_upgrade_complete covers the playable BuildingData path only.

title: [LookAt] CAMERA_RESET (KP5) jumps to base instead of resetting pose in place
description:
## C++
`CommandXlat.cpp:3213-3214` `MSG_META_CAMERA_RESET` calls `TheInGameUI->resetCamera()`. `InGameUI.cpp:4139-4143` reads the *current* view location and calls `TheTacticalView->resetCamera(&currentView.getPosition(), 1, 0, 0)`. `W3DView.cpp:2765-2781` keeps that look-at point and resets default angle, computed default zoom, and pitch — it does not retarget the command center.

## Rust
Live host `reset_camera_view_hotkey` (`hotkeys.rs:1257-1287`) picks `local_team_base_position` or the centroid of friendly units, then `host_center_camera_and_request_focus(focus)` and a default zoom. The camera teleports to the base even if the player was looking across the map.

## Evidence
C++ InGameUI.cpp:4141-4143 `getLocation` then `resetCamera(&currentView.getPosition(), ...)`.
Host hotkeys.rs:1260-1277 prefers `local_team_base_position` / friendly centroid over `camera_target`.

## Player-visible effect
Numpad 5 (retail CAMERA_RESET) yanks the view to the starting base instead of leveling/zooming the camera where the player is looking.
close_reason: reset_camera_view_hotkey / KP5 call reset_camera_pose_in_place: keep look-at, restore default yaw/pitch/zoom. No base teleport.

title: [MetaEvent] Keyboard Options remaps never reach live hotkeys
description:
## C++
`MetaEvent.cpp:378-523` `MetaEventTranslator::translateGameMessage` walks `TheMetaMap` (parsed from CommandMap.ini / Keyboard Options). Key + modifier + transition + `UseableIn` (SHELL/GAME) emit the mapped `MSG_META_*`. Remapping a command in the options menu changes what the translator emits on the next key.

## Rust
Crate `meta_event_impl/translator.rs` still consults `get_meta_map()` and `keyboard_options_menu.rs` writes remaps via `update_command_map_entry`. Live OS keys never enter `THE_MESSAGE_STREAM` (`architecture_honesty_tests.rs`: host is sole command authority). Host `hotkeys.rs` hardcodes retail defaults (Q select-all, W aircraft, Space radar, F1-F8 bookmarks, …) and never reads `get_command_map_entries` (only `subsystem_manager.rs` bootstraps the map).

## Evidence
C++ MetaEvent.cpp:408-493 map walk + appendMessage(map->m_meta).
Host: no `get_command_map_entries` / `get_meta_map` in `Main/src` except subsystem bootstrap.
GameClient `keyboard_options_menu.rs:605` updates the unused crate map.

## Player-visible effect
Changing a binding in Keyboard Options updates the menu list but in-game keys stay on the hardcoded retail layout. Custom CommandMap.ini / language CommandMap files are ignored at play time.
close_reason: Host handle_key_press consults lookup_command_map_name (TheMetaMap key+mods) so Keyboard Options update_command_map_entry remaps reach live hotkeys like MetaEvent.cpp:378-523.

title: [LookAt] F1-F8 camera bookmarks save only position, not angle/pitch/zoom
description:
## C++
`LookAtXlat.cpp:550-587` `MSG_META_SAVE_VIEW1..8` calls `TheTacticalView->getLocation(&m_viewLocation[slot])` (pos, angle, pitch, zoom) and shows `GUI:BookmarkXSet`. `MSG_META_VIEW_VIEW1..8` calls `setLocation` so recall restores the full camera pose.

## Rust
Live host `handle_camera_view_hotkey` (`hotkeys.rs:1033-1054`) stores only `self.camera_target` (`Option<Vec3>`) and on recall calls `host_center_camera_and_request_focus(pos)`. Angle, pitch, and zoom are discarded. HUD text is English “Saved camera view N”, not `GUI:BookmarkXSet`. Leftover crate `look_at_xlat.rs:393-406` stores a full `ViewLocation` but is not on the OS key path.

## Evidence
C++ View.h ViewLocation: `m_pos`, `m_angle`, `m_pitch`, `m_zoom`.
Host types.rs: `camera_view_bookmarks: [Option<Vec3>; 8]`.
hotkeys.rs:1040-1048 save `camera_target` only.

## Player-visible effect
Ctrl+Fn / Fn bookmarks jump the camera to the right map spot but keep the current yaw, pitch, and zoom. A saved “overhead” or “rotated” view cannot be restored.
close_reason: save_or_recall_camera_view stores CameraViewLocation pos+yaw+pitch+zoom; HUD uses GUI:BookmarkXSet. handle_camera_view_hotkey delegates.

title: [LookAt] MMB click does not reset camera angle, pitch, or zoom
description:
## C++
`LookAtXlat.cpp:237-254` `MSG_RAW_MOUSE_MIDDLE_BUTTON_UP`: if the cursor moved less than 5 pixels and the press lasted fewer than 5 GameClient frames, call `TheTacticalView->setAngleAndPitchToDefault()` and `setZoomToDefault()`. A short middle-click is the retail “home orientation” gesture.

## Rust
Live host (`Main/src/cnc_game_engine/input.rs:532-538`) only sets `is_mmb_rotating` true on press and false on release. No click-vs-drag test, no default angle/pitch/zoom. Leftover crate `look_at_xlat.rs:281-294` implements the 5px/5-frame reset but OS mouse never enters `THE_MESSAGE_STREAM` (`architecture_honesty_tests.rs`: live host is sole click authority).

## Evidence
C++ LookAtXlat.cpp:241-254 `CLICK_DURATION = 5`, `PIXEL_OFFSET = 5`, then `setAngleAndPitchToDefault` + `setZoomToDefault`.
Host input.rs middle-button up: `self.is_mmb_rotating = false; self.mmb_anchor = None;` only.

## Player-visible effect
Middle-click no longer snaps the camera back to default facing and zoom. Players must use KP5 or bookmarks, and even those are incomplete.
close_reason: begin/end_mmb_lookat_rotate: short click (5px/5 frames) calls reset_camera_pose_in_place (setAngleAndPitchToDefault + setZoomToDefault).

title: [Dispatch] MSG_ENABLE_RETALIATION_MODE never reaches live host so Auto-Retaliate stays off
description:
## C++
Options checkbox writes `TheGlobalData->m_clientRetaliationModeEnabled`. `Player::update` (`Player.cpp:708-724`) once per second, if local client flag != `isLogicalRetaliationModeEnabled()`, posts `MSG_ENABLE_RETALIATION_MODE` (playerIndex, bool). `GameLogicDispatch.cpp:603-614` calls `player->setLogicalRetaliationModeEnabled`. `ActiveBody` / friend-retaliation consults that *logical* flag (human players only).

## Rust
Crate `Player` has `set_logical_retaliation_mode_enabled` and crate `DefaultCommandHandler::execute_enable_retaliation` (`handler_misc.rs:125-157`) implements the message. Live host `CommandType` has **no** `EnableRetaliationMode`. `CommandExecutor` has no arm. Host `Player.logical_retaliation_mode_enabled` defaults **false** (`game_logic/player.rs:273`). `set_logical_retaliation_mode` / `set_all_local_logical_retaliation` (`world_tick/teams.rs:243-256`) exist but Main/src never calls them outside tests. Host `shouldRetaliate` (`teams.rs:300-301`) requires `p.is_local && p.logical_retaliation_mode_enabled`. Options/global `client_retaliation_mode_enabled` is never copied onto the host player. `logic_message_dispatcher` (`impl_update.rs:795-797`) is `trace!` only.

## Evidence
Grep of Main/src finds no `EnableRetaliation` command and no production caller of `set_all_local_logical_retaliation`. Live path is host `CommandExecutor`, which cannot receive this MSG.

## Player-visible
Auto-Retaliate (default ON in C++) never arms. Human units do not return fire when shot; nearby idle friends never join. Toggling the options checkbox cannot change combat behavior.
close_reason: CommandType::EnableRetaliationMode + leftover.rs execute_enable_retaliation; leftover_dispatch_tick posts once/sec from client flag; stream drain + CommandExecutor apply set_logical_retaliation_mode

title: [Dispatch] MSG_SWITCH_WEAPONS cycles next slot instead of locking the button slot
description:
## C++
`ControlBarCommandProcessing.cpp:786-794` posts `MSG_SWITCH_WEAPONS` with `commandButton->getWeaponSlot()`. `GameLogicDispatch.cpp:583-590` reads that slot and `currentlySelectedGroup->setWeaponLockForGroup(weaponSlot, LOCKED_PERMANENTLY)`. Clicking Missile vs Machine Gun on a Humvee locks that exact slot.

## Rust
Live host `CommandType::SwitchWeapons` is a unit variant with no slot (`types.rs:322`). `execute_switch_weapons` (`abilities.rs:938-951`) calls `unit_command_switch_weapons` (`world_scripts/unit_commands.rs:1206-1224`) which *cycles* to the next occupied slot (`0→1→2→0`) and then locks that. Crate `handler_unit.rs:106-146` locks the integer argument slot (C++ parity) but live host never calls crate `CommandProcessor`.

## Evidence
Live path is host `CommandExecutor` match arm `CommandType::SwitchWeapons` (`command_executor/mod.rs:386`). No host command carries a `WeaponSlotType`.

## Player-visible
Weapon-mode command buttons cannot select a specific slot. A 3-slot unit (or Humvee MG vs TOW) advances to the next weapon instead of the clicked one, so the wrong gun fires until the player cycles past it.
close_reason: CommandType::SwitchWeapons { slot }; execute_switch_weapons locks LOCKED_PERMANENTLY; control_bar_bridge queues SwitchWeapons { slot } instead of cycling

title: [Dispatch] Live host never processes MSG_SELF_DESTRUCT
description:
## C++
`GameLogicDispatch.cpp:1762-1797` `MSG_SELF_DESTRUCT`:
- Arg0 true: walk `ThePlayerList` for a living mutual ALLY, `transferAssetsFromThat(thisPlayer)` then `thisPlayer->killPlayer()`. No living ally → `killPlayer()`.
- Arg0 false: `killPlayer()` immediately (copy-protect / disconnect).
Emitters: `QuitMenu.cpp:122-126` (MP quit), `:161-171` (Surrender), `Network.cpp:647-650` and `:910-911`, `GameLogic.cpp:3777-3778` (copy protection). Comment on the message: "Destroys a player's units (for copy protection or to quit to observer)".

## Rust
Live host `CommandType` (`Main/src/command_system/types.rs`) has no `SelfDestruct`. `CommandExecutor::execute_command` (`command_executor/mod.rs:106-419`) has no arm. Quit is `runtime_host_cmd_menu` → `enter_shell_menu_from_runtime_host` (`runtime_host/shell_core.rs:9-11`) with no ally transfer / `killPlayer`. Residual `host_quit_menu_residual_wave123.rs:13` documents "Not multiplayer SelfDestruct residual".
Crate `DefaultCommandHandler::execute_self_destruct` (`handler_group.rs:144-201`) destroys *selected objects*, not the player; live host never calls crate `CommandProcessor`.

## Evidence
Live path is host `CommandSystem` → `CommandExecutor` (`system_impl.rs:610-617`). Crate `GameLogic::logic_message_dispatcher` (`impl_update.rs:928-930`) only `trace!`s `SelfDestruct`. No Main/src caller of `kill_player` / `transfer_assets` on quit.

## Player-visible
MP Surrender / Quit does not hand units to an ally or convert the leaver to observer. Allies lose the army; the leaver's stuff just disappears with the session. Copy-protect / disconnect also never wipe the cheater's army.
close_reason: CommandType::SelfDestruct { transfer_to_ally }; leftover.rs transfer-to-ally then kill_player; crate stream MSG_SELF_DESTRUCT drained to live host

title: [Dispatch] Live beacon commands skip world objects, cap, hide, and captions
description:
## C++
`GameLogicDispatch.cpp:1582-1759`:
- `MSG_PLACE_BEACON`: clamp pos to terrain extent; spawn `ThingFactory` object from `playerTemplate->getBeaconTemplate()` on the player's team; refuse if defeated or `count >= TheMultiplayerSettings->getMaxBeaconsPerPlayer()` (GUI:TooManyBeacons + BeaconPlacementFailed); allies/observers get GUI:BeaconPlaced, BeaconPlaced audio, radar INFORMATION, EVA_BeaconDetected, ControlBar dirty; enemies get `BeaconClientUpdate::hideBeacon()`.
- `MSG_REMOVE_BEACON`: iterate *selected* objects; owner destroys the beacon object; local non-owner hides it.
- `MSG_SET_BEACON_TEXT`: concatenate wchar args onto the selected beacon drawable caption (empty clears).

## Rust
Live host `CommandType` has `PlaceBeacon { location, text }` and `RemoveBeacon` only — no `SetBeaconText`. `execute_place_beacon` (`leftover.rs:753-788`) writes `BeaconManager` (a `Vec<BeaconEntry>`, `beacon_manager.rs:41-72`) with no ThingFactory object, no max-per-player, no terrain clamp, no hide-from-enemy, no defeated check. Optional text is stamped at place time only. `execute_remove_beacon` (`leftover.rs:790-812`) calls `remove_latest_beacon` — not the selected beacon, and never hides an ally's.
Crate `handler_special.rs:617-920` implements the C++ object/cap/hide/caption path; live host never calls crate `CommandProcessor`. `logic_message_dispatcher` (`impl_update.rs:919-926`) is `trace!` only.

## Evidence
Live path is host `CommandExecutor` (`system_impl.rs:610-617`). `BeaconManager` comment says it is consumed by UI/audio, not a world object. Host `CommandType` has no caption-edit command.

## Player-visible
MP beacons are HUD pins, not world objects: no 3D model, no click-to-select/remove, no MaxBeaconsPerPlayer (can spam), no enemy hide, no caption edit after place, no GUI:TooManyBeacons. Allies cannot see a real beacon unit on the map.
close_reason: leftover.rs place/remove/set-text spawn world objects, max-beacons cap, enemy hide, captions; CommandType::SetBeaconText

title: [AIUpdate] Idle units spontaneously enter hunt wander and auto-retreat

Human workers and combat units wander off after ~10s. Damaged attackers break off. Units leave rally/guard positions.

title: [AIUpdate] TurretAI never enabled on live path

title: [Production] Low-power speed uses 0.4 modifier not retail 1.0

title: [Body] Salvage armor crate writes unread +10 scalar

title: [Weapon] Veterancy bonus never applied at live fire time
description:

Object.cpp:3104-3122 setWeaponBonusCondition VETERAN/ELITE/HERO. Weapon.cpp:1797-1816 computeBonus on every fire; delay/clip/damage use RATE_OF_FIRE and DAMAGE.

title: [Weapon] Live clip reload uses DelayBetweenShots not ClipReloadTime

title: [ScriptEngine] INC/DEC_COUNTER swaps params and hardcodes +/-1

title: [Radar] Live addObject skips color and mid-game units

title: [Partition] Shroud crate/reveal-map uses permanent clear-forever

title: [FXList] Live host never dispatches FXList nuggets
description:

FXList.cpp:782-801 doFXPos/doFXObj run every nugget. Weapon.cpp:938-939 fireWeapon, FXListDie, SlowDeath, TransitionDamageFX, PropagandaTower, MissileAIUpdate all call it.

## Rust
GameClient fx_list.rs:569-600 runner exists and is registered, but the live host never calls it. attack.rs:183-205 only resolves the NAME. combat_particles.rs stamps presets. world_tick/ai.rs reduces death FX to audio tags. Crate TheFXList is dead under AuthorityOnly.

## Player-visible
Weapon fire sounds, tracers, muzzle lights, FXList scorches, and view-shake from authored FXLists never play. Superweapon/death FX are generic presets.
close_reason: Live fire/death/transition/superweapon paths call TheFXList doFXPos runner (weapon_discharge, ocl_and_scud, ai.rs, propaganda pulse, neutron/scud ignition). host_fx_list_dispatch.rs.

title: [Player] Unlisted relationships default Enemies not NEUTRAL
description:
## C++
PlayerList.cpp:160-200 only sets named Enemies/Allies. Player.cpp:542-572 getRelationship returns NEUTRAL for unmapped pairs.

## Rust
player_init.rs:357-368 sets every other player to Enemy then overlays tokens. get_relationship_with_team short-circuits self->Allies.

## Player-visible
Civilian/neutral third sides become Enemies: auto-attack, enemy-sighted scripts, scoring. C++ treats them as NEUTRAL.
close_reason: player_init.rs: stop pre-seeding Enemy; unlisted pairs stay Neutral; setup_teams Enemy only when both have teams

title: [Player] startNewGame money ignores map/lobby/DefaultStartingCash
description:
## C++
Player.cpp:425-433 init uses template money, then GameInfo starting cash or GlobalData default. initFromDict :1013-1016 deposits playerStartMoney on top.

## Rust
game_initialization.rs:680-685 set_money BEFORE Player::init which overwrites. core.rs:680-692 hardcodes 10000 fallback. start_new_game always starting_resources: 0.

## Player-visible
Every game is $10k or template StartMoney. Campaign scripted cash, skirmish $5k/$20k/$50k, and DefaultStartingCash are dropped.
close_reason: Player::init uses GlobalData default_starting_cash; after init apply lobby cash then deposit playerStartMoney; start_new_game no longer hardcodes 0

title: [Pathfind] Bridge decks never reach the live host grid
description:
## C++
TerrainLogic.cpp:1514-1521 addBridgeToLogic -> AIPathfind.cpp:3947-3964 addBridge -> classifyCells (deck CELL_CLEAR + start/end). Destroyed: setDestroyed CELL_BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE. findBrokenBridge feeds skirmish repair.

## Rust
terrain.rs:829-833 add_bridge_to_logic only feeds crate pathfind_complete add_bridge_ex — live movement never reads it. Host seed_pathfinding_from_terrain (world_save.rs:455-533) stamps Water/Cliff/Impassable + structures only. Live tick: movement.rs:55 find_path_ex_surfaces -> pathfinding.rs:870-933 single-layer A*.

## Player-visible
Ground units cannot path across bridges; they fail-open through the river. Destroy/repair changes nothing. Distinct from closed crate AABB layer bead.
close_reason: pathfinding.rs + world_save.rs + terrain.rs: live host grid stamps bridge decks as CLEAR and destroyed decks as BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE; restamps when TerrainLogic damage changes.

title: [Physics] Pitch/roll discarded; upside-down kill uses synthetic shock_up_z
description:
## C++
PhysicsUpdate.cpp:706-752 HAS_PITCHROLLYAW applies yaw/pitch/roll * m_pitchRollYawFactor (default 2.0 at :139) onto the object transform. handleBounce rights via Get_Z_Vector. testStunnedUnitForDestruction (:1626-1640) kills when transform Z-vector < 0.

## Rust
physics_motion.rs:557-580 computes rates then `let _ = roll_rate; let _ = pitch_rate;` — only yaw integrates. Default factor 1.0 not 2.0. Upside-down kill uses synthetic shock_up_z (physics.rs:34-56) not the transform.

## Player-visible
Shock-flung units never pitch/roll. Lands-upside-down death is a random scalar, not the integrated pose.
close_reason: physics_motion.rs apply_physics_ypr integrates pitch/roll onto object transform * factor 2.0; test_stunned uses transform up-Y < 0 not synthetic shock_up_z

title: [Physics] Shockwave fling ignores Mass and ShockResistance
description:
## C++
PhysicsUpdate.cpp:339-348 applyShock resists by m_shockResistance then applyForce; applyForce (297-334) divides by getMass(). INI Mass/ShockResistance at 146-148. Object.cpp:1806-1832 attemptDamage builds shockWaveForce then applyShock+applyRandomRotation+setStunned.

## Rust
Main object/physics.rs:63-102 apply_shock_wave_impulse uses FORCE_TO_VEL=0.05 into velocity, MAX_SHOCK_SPEED=80, never divides by physics_get_mass(). No shock_resistance field in Main. physics_mass defaults 1.0 with no INI Mass parse. Live: world_tick/shock.rs + step.rs:739-741.

## Player-visible
MOAB/Aurora/artillery fling tanks and infantry identically. ShockResistance>=1 units still toss and stun.
close_reason: physics.rs apply_shock_wave_impulse resists by shock_resistance then vel += force/physics_get_mass(); construct + spawn_templates parse INI Mass/ShockResistance

title: [Contain] Evac never markAllPassengersDetected so stealth stays cloaked
description:
## C++
`OpenContain.cpp:1322` `markAllPassengersDetected`. `AIUpdate.cpp:3882/3904` calls it immediately before `orderAllPassengersToExit` (normal and instant). Reveals stealth occupants as they leave.

## Rust
No `mark_all_passengers_detected` anywhere in GameLogic. Evac order path does not reveal stealth.

## Evidence
C++ `OpenContain.cpp:1322`, `AIUpdate.cpp:3882/3904`. Rust grep: zero hits.

## Player-visible effect
Stealth-garrisoned units leaving a building stay instantly cloaked. C++ reveals them on exit.
close_reason: open_contain.rs + modules/contain.rs: mark_all_passengers_detected on evac (STEALTH_GARRISON stealth->mark_as_detected) before order_all_passengers_to_exit

title: [Contain] OpenContain never plays template enter, exit, or falling audio
description:
## C++
`OpenContain::onContaining` (`OpenContain.cpp:715-724`) plays the object template `getSoundEnter()` (gated by load-sounds-enabled). `onRemoving` (`:727-739`) plays template `getSoundExit()` on the container plus the rider's `getSoundFalling()`.

## Rust
`open_contain.rs:on_containing` only plays module-INI `EnterSound` via `do_load_sound`. `on_removing` (`:1020-1043`) plays nothing. `do_unload_sound` only covers throttled module-INI `ExitSound`, not template exit/falling.

## Evidence
C++ `OpenContain.cpp:715-739`. Rust `open_contain.rs:1020-1043` and `:1964`.

## Player-visible effect
Boarding and ejecting from transports/garrisons has no template enter SFX and no falling scream when passengers are dumped.
close_reason: open_contain.rs on_containing/on_removing play template get_sound_enter/exit/falling via TheAudio

title: [Contain] Selling a building never calls onSelling to eject occupants
description:
## C++
`BuildAssistant.cpp:1545-1547` calls `contain->onSelling()` before idle. `OpenContain::onSelling` (`OpenContain.cpp:1346-1349`) is `orderAllPassengersToExit(CMD_FROM_AI, FALSE)`. Garrison/Tunnel override to force-empty.

## Rust
`build_assistant.rs:767` `sell_object` only queues the sell list. `ContainModuleInterface` has no `on_selling`. Garrison/tunnel `on_selling` methods have zero callers.

## Evidence
C++ `BuildAssistant.cpp:1545-1547`, `OpenContain.cpp:1346-1349`. Rust `build_assistant.rs:767` and `modules/contain.rs` (no hook).

## Player-visible effect
Selling an Internet Center, barracks, or transport leaves occupants trapped/invisible inside the dying building instead of ejecting them.
close_reason: ContainModuleInterface::on_selling + OpenContain order_all_passengers_to_exit; Garrison force-empty then base; Transport and subclasses delegate

title: [Contain] RailedTransportContain save/xfer is a no-op
description:
## C++
`RailedTransportContain.cpp:112-123` `xfer` writes version 1 then `TransportContain::xfer`.

## Rust
`railed_transport_contain.rs` has no `Snapshotable` / `snapshot_*` overrides. Trait defaults no-op. Dock-open / extra-slot / payload state is not saved.

## Evidence
C++ `RailedTransportContain.cpp:112-123`. Rust `railed_transport_contain.rs` trait impl has no snapshot hooks.

## Player-visible effect
Save/load of a railed transport loses passengers and transit lock; units disappear or can exit while the train is still moving.
close_reason: railed_transport_contain.rs Snapshotable version 1 then TransportContain::xfer plus snapshot_* trait hooks

title: [Contain] InternetHackContain save/xfer is a no-op
description:
## C++
`InternetHackContain.cpp:85-96` `xfer` writes version 1 then `TransportContain::xfer` (payload, extra slots, exit-busy frame).

## Rust
`internet_hack_contain.rs` has no `Snapshotable` impl and no `snapshot_xfer` / `snapshot_crc` / `snapshot_load_post_process` overrides. Trait defaults are no-ops. Live save (`contain_module_overrides/contain.rs` binding) serializes nothing for this module.

## Evidence
C++ `InternetHackContain.cpp:85-96`. Rust `internet_hack_contain.rs` trait impl `:107-240` has no snapshot hooks.

## Player-visible effect
Save/load of an Internet Center loses who is inside and their slot/exit-busy state; hackers can vanish or duplicate after load.
close_reason: internet_hack_contain.rs Snapshotable version 1 then TransportContain::xfer plus snapshot_* trait hooks

title: [Contain] Parachute sway ignores locomotor spring and damper
description:
## C++
`ParachuteContain.cpp` `update` applies chute sway with the rider/chute locomotor's `getPitchStiffness` / `getRollStiffness` / `getPitchDamping`+altitude / `getRollDamping`+altitude. Locomotor defaults are stiffness 0.1 and damping 0.9.

## Rust
`parachute_contain.rs:801-811` hardcodes 0.1 / 0.1 / 0.1+damp / 0.1+damp and never reads the locomotor, even though Rust locomotor templates have those fields (defaults 0.1/0.1/0.9/0.9).

## Evidence
C++ `ParachuteContain.cpp` update spring/damper. Rust `parachute_contain.rs:801-811`.

## Player-visible effect
Chute wobble is ~9× less damped than C++. Descent tilt/oscillation and near-landing stabilization look wrong.
close_reason: parachute_contain.rs update reads cur locomotor pitch/roll stiffness and damping instead of hardcoded 0.1

title: [Contain] OpenContain onDie skips DieMux and force-exposes stealth
description:
## C++
`OpenContain.cpp:833-850` `onDie` returns unless `m_dieMuxData.isDieApplicable(object, damageInfo)`. Then damages contained units, `killRidersWhoAreNotFreeToExit`, and `removeAllContained()` (exposeStealthUnits defaults FALSE).

## Rust
`open_contain.rs:1163-1171` ignores `damage_info` and never calls `is_die_applicable` (helper exists at `:530` but is unused). Then `remove_all_contained(true)` force-exposes stealth.

## Evidence
C++ `OpenContain.cpp:835-850`. Rust `open_contain.rs:530-533` unused on `:1163-1170`.

## Player-visible effect
Deaths filtered by `DeathTypes` / vet / status still dump and damage passengers. Stealthed riders are force-revealed when their container dies.
close_reason: open_contain.rs on_die uses die_mux is_die_applicable and remove_all_contained(false) (C++ default)

title: [Contain] Garrison fire-point slots leak and spawn extra GarrisonGuns
description:
## C++
`GarrisonContain.cpp:385-387` `putObjectAtBestGarrisonPoint` returns immediately if `getObjectGarrisonPointIndex(obj) != GARRISON_INDEX_INVALID`. Occupants already at a window are not re-registered.

## Rust
`garrison_contain.rs:1594-1614` `put_object_at_best_garrison_point` has no already-placed check. `add_valid_objects_to_garrison_points` runs every frame for every attacking occupant and registers them at another free point. Stale slots stay occupied (`removeInvalid` keeps attacking units). Each `put` also `create_garrison_effect`s a new `GarrisonGun` drawable.

## Evidence
C++ `GarrisonContain.cpp:385-387`. Rust `garrison_contain.rs:1594-1614` and `:1741-1788`.

## Player-visible effect
Garrisoned buildings accumulate dozens of gun-barrel props and exhaust the 40 fire-point slots, so later occupants cannot take a window.
close_reason: garrison_contain.rs put_object_at_best_garrison_point returns if already placed so fire-point slots and GarrisonGuns no longer leak

title: [Contain] Transport isSpecificRiderFreeToExit skips terrain and Battle Bus kill
description:
## C++
`TransportContain.cpp:536-567` `isSpecificRiderFreeToExit`: after `getAiFreeToExit`, airborne locomotor → TRUE; rider without AI → FALSE; no cur locomotor → FALSE; `pathfinder()->validMovementTerrain(layer, hisLoco, myPos)` → FALSE (amphibious transport).

## Rust
`transport_contain.rs:826-849` only checks railed dock-open, then owner `get_ai_free_to_exit`, else TRUE. No airborne bypass, no rider-AI/loco requirement, no terrain legality.

## Evidence
C++ `TransportContain.cpp:551-565`. Rust `transport_contain.rs:826-849`. `kill_riders_who_are_not_free_to_exit` (`:804`) therefore never kills anyone on Battle Bus death.

## Player-visible effect
Amphibious transports unload infantry into water/impassable cells. `DestroyRidersWhoAreNotFreeToExit` (Battle Bus) never fires because every rider counts as free to exit.
close_reason: transport_contain.rs is_specific_rider_free_to_exit: airborne bypass, rider AI/loco required, pathfinder valid_movement_terrain on owner layer

title: [Map] Discarded <2-point polygon triggers do not advance s_currentID
description:
## C++
ParsePolygonTriggersDataChunk (PolygonTrigger.cpp:154-172) assigns m_triggerID and updates maxTriggerId BEFORE the numPoints<2 delete/continue, so degenerate entries still raise s_currentID = maxTriggerId+1.

## Rust
Both live parsers skip first: polygon_trigger.rs:469-475 and script_loader.rs parse_runtime_polygon_triggers_from_chunky:1519-1524 `if points.len() < 2 { continue; }` then only then bump max_trigger_id. Discarded IDs never raise the ceiling.

## Evidence
PolygonTrigger.cpp:154-157 vs polygon_trigger.rs:469-475.

## Player-visible effect
If a map (or tool) writes a 0/1-point trigger, Rust next_id() can reuse that ID. get_by_id, AI goal_polygon, and save-xfer then bind the wrong area.
close_reason: polygon_trigger.rs + script_loader.rs: bump max_trigger_id before discarding <2-point entries so next_id cannot reuse discarded IDs

title: [Map] v1 auto-water trigger ID is max+1, not C++ reused max
description:
## C++
On K_TRIGGERS_VERSION_1 (PolygonTrigger.cpp:186-187) the synthesized water polygon does `pTrig->m_triggerID = maxTriggerId++` — it reuses the current max ID (0 on an empty list). getPolygonTriggerByID walks the list head-first so an earlier real trigger wins the shared ID.

## Rust
polygon_trigger.rs:481-485 and script_loader.rs:1539-1541 allocate `max_trigger_id + 1`, a unique ID. PolygonTriggerList::add overwrites id_index so a later duplicate would win, the opposite of C++.

## Evidence
PolygonTrigger.cpp:186-187 vs polygon_trigger.rs:481-485.

## Player-visible effect
On version-1 maps, AI/script/save lookups by the max trigger ID hit the auto water table in Rust and the last real trigger in C++.
close_reason: polygon_trigger.rs + script_loader.rs: v1 auto-water uses maxTriggerId++ (reuse current max); PolygonTriggerList::add first-wins like C++ getByID head walk

title: [Map] PolygonTriggers trailing bytes abort Rust map load
description:
## C++
ParsePolygonTriggersDataChunk (PolygonTrigger.cpp:205-206) DEBUG_ASSERTCRASH(file.atEndOfChunk()) then always returns true. Release builds ignore leftover bytes in the chunk.

## Rust
PolygonTriggerList::parse_polygon_triggers_data_chunk (polygon_trigger.rs:507) returns input.at_end_of_chunk() directly. DataChunkInput::parse treats false as a hard failure; system/map_loader.rs:426-430 turns that into a map-load error. Sibling WaypointsList handler (map_loader.rs:743-746) logs trailing data and returns true. Main parse_runtime_polygon_triggers_from_chunky fail-softs and does not hit this.

## Evidence
PolygonTrigger.cpp:205-206 vs polygon_trigger.rs:507 and Common data_chunk_io parse abort on false.

## Player-visible effect
On the GameEngine map_loader path, a PolygonTriggers chunk with padding or extra editor fields fails the entire map load. C++ retail still plays the map.
close_reason: polygon_trigger.rs: ParsePolygonTriggersDataChunk now returns true after logging trailing bytes instead of aborting map load

title: [Contain] Transport onRemoving drops velocity, fall, scatter, mood, and Kell timer
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Contain/TransportContain.cpp:306-414` `onRemoving` after OpenContain + ExitBone + orient:
- `KeepContainerVelocityOnExit`: copy parent velocity×mass as motive force and apply `ExitPitchRate`.
- If the transport is above terrain: `physics->setAllowToFall(true)`.
- `GoAggressiveOnExit`: `setAttitude(AI_AGGRESSIVE)`.
- If the transport is dead: `scatterToNearbyPosition`.
- `ResetMoodCheckTimeOnExit`: `wakeUpAndAttemptToTarget`.
- Patch 1.01: Jarmen Kell (`HERO`+`SALVAGER`) leaving a `CLIFF_JUMPER` bike transfers secondary-weapon shot timers.

## Rust
`transport_contain.rs:597-671` parses all of those INI keys into `TransportContainModuleData` but `on_removing` never applies velocity, pitch, allow-to-fall, aggressive, death scatter, mood reset, or Kell timer transfer. (MobNexusContain does apply velocity/scatter/fall — Transport does not.)

## Evidence
C++ `TransportContain.cpp:334-413`. Rust module fields `:72-79` and parsers `:159-177` vs `on_removing` body `:611-671` which only clears HELD, ExitBone, orient, LOADED, extra slots, armed-riders upgrade, and exit delay.

## Player-visible effect
Infantry hopping out of a moving/airborne transport drop in place with no inherited speed and do not fall. AI passengers stay passive instead of going aggressive / retargeting. A dying transport dumps everyone on one spot. Jarmen Kell leaving a combat bike loses his snipe cooldown.
close_reason: transport_contain.rs on_removing: keep velocity, allow-to-fall, aggressive, scatter if dead, reset mood, Kell bike->rider secondary timer

title: [Contain] OpenContain passenger fire skips parent-container consult
description:
## C++
