`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Contain/OpenContain.cpp:1127-1139` `OpenContain::isPassengerAllowedToFire`:
- If instance `m_passengerAllowedToFire` is false, return FALSE (upgrade can override template via `setPassengerAllowedToFire`).
- If this container is itself contained, return `getContainedBy()->getContain()->isPassengerAllowedToFire()` (no id) so the parent has veto.
- Else TRUE.

## Rust
`open_contain.rs:1285-1286` only returns `self.module_data.passengers_allowed_to_fire`. `set_passenger_allowed_to_fire` mutates that flag (upgrade path exists) but there is no nested-container consult. Any OpenContain subclass that does not override (Heal, Parachute, generic transport after its own checks) never asks the parent.

## Evidence
C++ `OpenContain.cpp:1132-1139`. Rust `open_contain.rs:1284-1286`.

## Player-visible effect
Passengers in a nested container fire whenever the inner flag is true, even when the outer container (Helix, Overlord, another transport) would deny fire.
close_reason: open_contain.rs is_passenger_allowed_to_fire consults parent container when this container is itself contained

title: [Contain] Garrison exit skips cliff-bunker terrain walk
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Contain/GarrisonContain.cpp:1473-1584` `exitObjectViaDoor`. Start is the building position. If the exiting unit’s locomotor cannot stand there (`validMovementTerrain`), C++ walks the start point to the front of the building (major-radius along facing), then the back, then reverts. Left/right evac uses the full transform matrix. Burst-from-center only `setPosition`s enclosing occupants (station units stay where they are).

## Rust
`garrison_contain.rs:692-788` skips the cliff/invalid-terrain walk. Left/right uses 2D yaw only. After computing start, it always snaps Z to ground and always `set_position(start)` — including non-enclosing/station occupants, who C++ leaves at their station.

## Evidence
C++ `GarrisonContain.cpp:1491-1506` (terrain walk), `:1512-1538` (matrix evac), `:1559-1564` (enclosing-only place). Rust `garrison_contain.rs:711-778`.

## Player-visible effect
Units evacuating a cliff bunker (or any garrison whose footprint is not valid locomotor terrain) spawn inside the cliff and get stuck. Non-enclosing garrison occupants snap to the building center on exit instead of walking off their station.
close_reason: garrison_contain.rs exit_object_via_door: cliff-bunker terrain walk, full transform left/right, burst-from-center only snaps enclosing occupants

title: [Contain] Transport passenger fire skips infantry-only and Overlord nest
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Contain/TransportContain.cpp:570-598` `TransportContain::isPassengerAllowedToFire(ObjectID id)`:
1. If the passenger exists and is not `KINDOF_INFANTRY`, return FALSE (vehicles must not shoot out).
2. If this transport is itself contained by an `isSpecialOverlordStyleContainer` (Overlord/Helix nest: bunker on Overlord inside Helix), delegate `hisContain->isPassengerAllowedToFire(id)`.
3. Else `OpenContain::isPassengerAllowedToFire()`.

## Rust
`transport_contain.rs:853-855` `is_passenger_allowed_to_fire` only does `self.base.is_passenger_allowed_to_fire(id)` (OpenContain module flag). No infantry-only filter. No Overlord-style parent redirect. Live callers include `chinook_ai_update.rs` with `Some(passenger_id)`.

## Evidence
C++ `TransportContain.cpp:576-593`. Rust `transport_contain.rs:852-855`. Closed `hq-yny` only covered Combat Chinook INI `PassengersAllowedToFire` + `ArmedRidersUpgradeMyWeaponSet`, not this override.

## Player-visible effect
Vehicles loaded in a Combat Chinook (or any transport with `PassengersAllowedToFire=yes`) can fire out. Infantry in an Overlord bunker that is itself hanging under a Helix do not get Helix/Overlord fire rules.
close_reason: transport_contain.rs is_passenger_allowed_to_fire: infantry-only then Overlord-style parent nest then OpenContain

title: [Contain] Garrison fire points stay local-space and skip FIREPOINT01+
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Contain/GarrisonContain.cpp` `loadGarrisonPoints` / `loadStationGarrisonPoints` / `redeployOccupants` / `calcBestGarrisonPosition`.
`Object::getMultiLogicalBonePosition("FIREPOINT"|"STATION", …)` (`Object.cpp:6063`) uses `getPristineBonePositions(prefix, startIndex=1)` then `convertBonePosToWorldPos` (`convertToWorld` defaults TRUE). After switching the drawable through garrisoned pristine/damaged/really-damaged, window positions are cached in world space as FIREPOINT01+. `WeaponSet.cpp:632-640` calls `contain->calcBestGarrisonPosition` so range checks assume the closest free window, not the building origin. `GarrisonContain::redeployOccupants` (virtual) rematches occupants and resets station points when art/damage changes.

## Rust
`garrison_contain.rs` `load_garrison_points` / `load_station_garrison_points` call `drawable.get_pristine_bone_positions("FIREPOINT"|"STATION", 0, …)` (local space; start_index 0 matches the exact name only, not FIREPOINT01+). `put_object_at_garrison_point` then `set_position`s those coords as world. `calc_best_garrison_position` is `dead_code` and is not on `ContainModuleInterface`. Live `weapon_set_able.rs` `garrison_fire_goal` returns `container.get_position()`. Garrison `redeploy_occupants` is `dead_code` and only calls `add_valid_objects_to_garrison_points`; `OpenContain::update` → `monitor_condition_changes` uses OpenContain’s FIREPOINT cycle instead of the garrison override.

## Evidence
C++ `Object.cpp:6068-6073` start=1 + world convert. Rust `garrison_contain.rs:1529-1552` and `:2061` start=0 local; `:1641-1644` set_position raw; `:1183-1186` dead redeploy; `modules/contain.rs` has no `calc_best_garrison_position`; `weapon_set_able.rs:441-466` uses building center.

## Player-visible effect
Garrisoned infantry do not occupy building windows. They fire from the building center (or local-space garbage near the origin), fail to rematch windows when the building is damaged, and range-check from the origin so far-side targets are wrongly in/out of range.
close_reason: garrison_contain.rs load_garrison_points/load_station use get_multi_logical_bone_position FIREPOINT/STATION (startIndex 1, world space)

title: [SpecialPower] Academy counts every ability as a superweapon
description:
## C++
`SpecialPowerModule::initiateIntentToDoSpecialPower` (`SpecialPowerModule.cpp:434`) calls `recordSpecialPowerUsed(template)`. `AcademyStats::recordSpecialPowerUsed` (`AcademyStats.cpp:460-465`) increments only when `getAcademyClassificationType() == ACT_SUPERPOWER`.

## Rust
`special_power_module.rs:444-454` remaps Superweapon→Superpower and everything else to None, then `Player::get_academy_stats_mut` (`player/academy_score.rs:138-142`) increments `special_powers_used` for every call, ignoring classification.

## Evidence
C++: `if (spTemplate->getAcademyClassificationType() == ACT_SUPERPOWER) m_specialPowersUsed++;`
Rust academy_score: `self.special_powers_used = self.special_powers_used.saturating_add(1);` with `_classification` unused.

## Player-visible effect
Using a unit special (Black Lotus, ambulance, capture) counts as firing a superweapon. Score-screen academy advice skips "try using superweapons" after any ability.
close_reason: special_power_module.rs: record academy special_powers_used only for ACT_SUPERPOWER/Superweapon

title: [CashHackSpecialPower] Floating text ignores GUI:AddCash/LoseCash
description:
## C++
`CashHackSpecialPower::doSpecialPowerAtObject` (`CashHackSpecialPower.cpp:137-151`) formats `TheGameText->fetch("GUI:AddCash")` over the caster (z+20, green) and `GUI:LoseCash` over the victim (z+30, red).

## Rust
Live `cash_hack_special_power.rs:241-277` hardcodes `+$N` / `-$N`. Other live cash floaters (`auto_deposit_update.rs`, `hack_internet_ai_update.rs`) already use `TheGameText::fetch("GUI:AddCash")`.

## Evidence
C++: `moneyString.format(TheGameText->fetch("GUI:AddCash"), cash);`
Rust: `TheInGameUI::add_floating_text(&format!("+${}", cash), ...)`

## Player-visible effect
Black Lotus cash-hack floaters ignore localized GUI:AddCash/LoseCash strings (wrong format/language).
close_reason: cash_hack_special_power.rs: floaters use TheGameText GUI:AddCash/LoseCash

title: [FireWeaponPower] Does not aim turrets after fire
description:
## C++
`FireWeaponPower::doSpecialPower / AtLocation / AtObject` (`FireWeaponPower.cpp:77-157`) after base: `reloadAllAmmo(TRUE)`, `aiAttackPosition/Object(..., maxShots, CMD_FROM_AI)`, then `for (i = 0; i < MAX_TURRETS; i++) setTurretTargetPosition/Object`.

## Rust
Live `object/special_powers/fire_weapon_power.rs` reloads and issues `ai_attack_position` / `ai_attack_object_id` only. No turret loop. Leftover `special_power_module/integration.rs` has the loop but is not on the live factory path.

## Evidence
C++: `for (Int i = 0; i < MAX_TURRETS; i++) ai->setTurretTargetPosition((WhichTurretType)i, loc);`
Rust `fire_weapon_at_location` / `do_special_power_at_object`: reload + AI attack, no `set_turret_target_*`.

## Player-visible effect
Turreted FireWeaponPower buildings (superweapon timers that fire a weapon) reload and order the hull AI but turrets never lock onto the click, so they keep idle aim.
close_reason: fire_weapon_power.rs: after reload/AI attack, loop MAX_TURRETS set_turret_target_position/object

title: [CleanupAreaPower] Location fire incorrectly recharges and plays EVA
description:
## C++
`CleanupAreaPower::doSpecialPowerAtLocation` (`CleanupAreaPower.cpp:63-82`) does not call `SpecialPowerModule::doSpecialPowerAtLocation`. It only finds `CleanupHazardUpdate` and `setCleanupAreaParameters(loc, m_cleanupMoveRange)`. No recharge, EVA, initiate sound, or academy record.

## Rust
`CleanupAreaPower::dispatch_do_special_power_at_location` (`cleanup_area_power.rs:161-169`) calls `base_module.do_special_power_at_location` first (trigger/recharge/EVA/scripts) then `set_cleanup_area_parameters`.

## Evidence
C++: no `SpecialPowerModule::doSpecialPowerAtLocation` in the override.
Rust: `self.base_module.do_special_power_at_location(...); CleanupAreaPower::do_special_power_at_location(self, location);`

## Player-visible effect
Ambulance/hazard cleanup starts the special-power cooldown and plays initiate/EVA/script notifications that retail never fires for this power.
close_reason: cleanup_area_power.rs: location fire no longer calls base do_special_power_at_location

title: [SpecialPower] Subclass xfer drops recharge and pause state
description:
## C++
Every SpecialPower subclass `xfer` (`OCLSpecialPower.cpp:247`, `CashHackSpecialPower.cpp:173`, etc.) does `xferVersion` then `SpecialPowerModule::xfer`: availableOnFrame, pausedCount, pausedOnFrame, pausedPercent. `loadPostProcess` calls `SpecialPowerModule::loadPostProcess` which re-registers SharedNSync public timers.

## Rust
Live subclass `Snapshotable::xfer` (ocl_special_power.rs:511, cash_hack, spy_vision, defector, fire_weapon, cleanup, cash_bounty, baikonur, special_ability, demoralize) writes version then returns. None call `base_module.xfer`. `load_post_process` is empty (CashBounty reapplies bounty instead of base).

## Evidence
C++: `SpecialPowerModule::xfer(xfer);` after version.
Rust: `xfer.xfer_version(&mut version, 1)?; Ok(())`

## Player-visible effect
Save/load resets every subclassed special-power cooldown and pause count. Shared superweapon public timers vanish after load.
close_reason: special_powers/*: subclass xfer/load_post_process now forward SpecialPowerModule recharge/pause + public-timer re-register

title: [CashBountyPower] Science purchase never applies cash bounty
description:
## C++
`CashBountyPower::onSpecialPowerCreation` (`CashBountyPower.cpp:145-156`) calls the base then `controller->setCashBounty(findBounty())` if bounty is greater — no science check. `addScience` walks modules and calls this when the palace power is unlocked. `onObjectCreated` (111-120) applies only if the player already has the required science.

## Rust
`impl_special_power_subclass!` always forwards `on_special_power_creation` to `base_module` only (`special_powers/interface.rs:56-60`). `CashBountyPower` never overrides it. Science purchase (`player/science_management.rs:354`) therefore starts the timer but never sets `cash_bounty_percent`. `on_object_created` applies bounty only when science is already owned.

## Evidence
C++: `SpecialPowerModule::onSpecialPowerCreation(); if (bounty > controller->getCashBounty()) controller->setCashBounty(bounty);`
Rust trait macro: `on_special_power_creation(&mut self.base_module)` with no `apply_bounty_if_applicable`.

## Player-visible effect
Buying a GLA cash-bounty general's power after the Palace exists never raises the kill-bounty percentage.
close_reason: cash_bounty_power.rs + interface.rs: on_special_power_creation applies bounty without science gate

title: [SpecialAbility] INI drops StartsPaused and UpdateModuleStartsAttack
description:
## C++
`SpecialAbility` inherits `SpecialPowerModuleData::buildFieldParse` (`SpecialPowerModule.cpp:53-67`): SpecialPowerTemplate, UpdateModuleStartsAttack, StartsPaused, InitiateSound, ScriptedSpecialPowerOnly.

## Rust
Live factory (`contain_module_overrides/install.rs`) constructs `object/special_powers/special_ability.rs`. `SPECIAL_ABILITY_FIELDS` is only `SpecialPowerTemplate`. StartsPaused / UpdateModuleStartsAttack / InitiateSound / ScriptedSpecialPowerOnly are dropped.

## Evidence
Retail INI: `Behavior = SpecialAbility` + `StartsPaused = Yes` (Rebel capture) and `UpdateModuleStartsAttack = Yes` (Microwave). Rust table: `const SPECIAL_ABILITY_FIELDS: ... SpecialPowerTemplate` only.

## Player-visible effect
Capture-building is ready without the infantry-capture upgrade. Microwave/hack recharge starts at click instead of when the update module actually begins the attack.
close_reason: special_ability.rs: INI table adds StartsPaused, UpdateModuleStartsAttack, InitiateSound, ScriptedSpecialPowerOnly

title: [SpecialPower] Subclass modules skip ctor recharge and StartsPaused
description:
## C++
`SpecialPowerModule::SpecialPowerModule` (`SpecialPowerModule.cpp:76-122`) always runs for every subclass:
- if the object is not `UNDER_CONSTRUCTION` and the template is not SharedNSync, `startPowerRecharge()`
- if `StartsPaused`, `pauseCountdown(TRUE)`
- if unpaused + SharedNSync + public timer + structure, `TheInGameUI->addSuperweapon`

## Rust
`special_powers/interface.rs` `make_base_module` only calls `SpecialPowerModule::new` (available_on_frame=0, paused_count=0). `initialize_from_owner` exists on the base (`special_power_module.rs:245`) and is hooked from `SpecialPowerModule::on_object_created`, but live subclasses (OCL, SpecialAbility, FireWeapon, CashHack, SpyVision, Defector, Cleanup, Baikonur) implement `Module` without forwarding `on_object_created`. CashBountyPower's hook only applies bounty.

## Evidence
C++ ctor: `if (!UNDER_CONSTRUCTION && !isSharedNSync()) startPowerRecharge(); if (md->m_startsPaused) pauseCountdown(TRUE);`
Rust: `SpecialPowerModule::new(...)` then no `initialize_from_owner` from any subclass Module impl except CashBounty's bounty-only hook.

## Player-visible effect
Map-placed superweapons and abilities start immediately ready. StartsPaused never applies, so capture/hack powers are usable before the required upgrade.
close_reason: special_powers/*: Module::on_object_created calls initialize_from_owner (ctor recharge, StartsPaused, public timer)

title: [ModelConditionUpgrade] ConditionFlag parser misses C++ flags and mis-maps crush bits
description:
## C++
ModelConditionUpgradeModuleData parses ConditionFlag via ModelConditionFlags::parseSingleBitFromINI (ModelConditionUpgrade.cpp:21-30) against the full ModelConditionFlagType table (ModelState.h:79-215): FRONTCRUSHED, BACKCRUSHED, PREATTACK_A/B/C, USING_WEAPON_A/B/C, DOCKING*, CLIMBING, RAPPELLING, RIDER1-8, DOOR_4_WAITING_TO_CLOSE, CONTINUOUS_FIRE_*, RAISING_FLAG, PREORDER, TURRET_ROTATE, etc. upgradeImplementation sets that single bit via setModelConditionState.

## Rust
model_condition_upgrade.rs:167-280 is a hand-rolled match. FRONTCRUSHED aliases TOPPLED and BACKCRUSHED aliases FLOODED (wrong distinct C++ bits). Missing C++ names include PREATTACK_A/B/C, BETWEEN_FIRING_SHOTS_A, RELOADING_A, USING_WEAPON_A/B/C, DOCKING/BEGINNING/ACTIVE/ENDING, CLIMBING, RAPPELLING, RIDER1-8, DOOR_4_WAITING_TO_CLOSE, CONTINUOUS_FIRE_SLOW/MEAN/FAST, RAISING_FLAG, PREORDER, TURRET_ROTATE.

## Evidence
C++ ModelState.h:79-81 TOPPLED, FRONTCRUSHED, BACKCRUSHED are sequential distinct flags. Rust model_condition_upgrade.rs:248-249 `"TOPPLED" | "FRONTCRUSHED" => TOPPLED` and `"FLOODED" | "BACKCRUSHED" => FLOODED`.

## Player-visible effect
A ModelConditionUpgrade whose ConditionFlag is any missing/mis-mapped name either no-ops (parse → None, empty flags, apply skips) or lights the wrong model state (crush vs topple/flood).
close_reason: model_condition_upgrade.rs ConditionFlag parser uses C++ BIT_NAMES; FRONTCRUSHED/BACKCRUSHED are distinct bits

title: [Upgrade] Object never dispatches Radar/PowerPlant/CostModifier onDelete/onCapture
description:
## C++
RadarUpgrade, PowerPlantUpgrade, and CostModifierUpgrade override BehaviorModule::onDelete/onCapture. Destroyed/captured upgraded buildings remove radar/power-bonus/kind-of cost change from the old player and add them to the new owner (RadarUpgrade.cpp:48-100, PowerPlantUpgrade.cpp:35-82, CostModifierUpgrade.cpp:96-138). Radar/PowerPlant skip work when the object is disabled (Radar always; PowerPlant onCapture only).

## Rust
Those methods exist on UpgradeModuleInterface (radar_upgrade.rs:257-294, power_plant_upgrade.rs:187-223, cost_modifier_upgrade.rs:172-218) but are never called:
- Object::on_destroy_internal (object_lifecycle.rs:345-346) calls Module::on_delete() (no object, default no-op), not UpgradeModuleInterface::on_delete.
- Object::on_capture (object_update.rs:399-402) comments "Upgrade modules are still updated through standard module ownership hooks" then does `let _ = (&old_owner, &new_owner);` — a no-op.

## Evidence
C++ virtual onDelete/onCapture on the three modules. Rust object_update.rs:399-402 no-op. object_lifecycle.rs:345-346 Module::on_delete only.

## Player-visible effect
Selling/destroying or capturing an upgraded radar van, control-rod power plant, or cost-modifier building leaves the old player's radar/power/discount in place and does not grant them to the new owner.
close_reason: object_lifecycle.rs on_destroy_internal and object_update.rs on_capture now dispatch UpgradeModuleInterface::on_delete/on_capture for Radar/PowerPlant/CostModifier

title: [ArmorUpgrade] Chem-suit decal uses incoming mask not isTriggeredBy
description:
## C++
ArmorUpgrade::upgradeImplementation (ArmorUpgrade.cpp:63-81) always sets ARMORSET_PLAYER_UPGRADE, then `if (isTriggeredBy("Upgrade_AmericaChemicalSuits"))` sets TERRAIN_DECAL_CHEMSUIT. `isTriggeredBy` (Module.cpp:248-261) matches the module's own TriggeredBy list (copied into m_triggerUpgradeNames by getUpgradeActivationMasks).

## Rust
armor_upgrade.rs:237-258 computes `apply_chem` from `upgrade_mask.intersects(ChemicalSuits mask)` — the *incoming* combined player/object mask — not the module's TriggeredBy names. Any ArmorUpgrade applied while the player also has ChemicalSuits paints the chem-suit decal.

## Evidence
C++ ArmorUpgrade.cpp:76-80 isTriggeredBy("Upgrade_AmericaChemicalSuits"). Rust armor_upgrade.rs:237-258 upgrade_mask.intersects(chemical_suits_mask).

## Player-visible effect
Composite-armor / other ArmorUpgrade units show the America chem-suit terrain decal whenever ChemicalSuits is researched, even if this module is not the chem-suit upgrade.
close_reason: armor_upgrade.rs chem-suit decal uses UpgradeMuxData::is_triggered_by(Upgrade_AmericaChemicalSuits) not incoming mask

title: [StealthUpgrade] can_upgrade ignores already-applied so slaves re-grant every update
description:
## C++
Object::updateUpgradeModules skips modules with isAlreadyUpgraded(). attemptUpgrade/wouldUpgrade also refuse if m_upgradeExecuted. upgradeImplementation runs once: set CAN_STEALTH and giveSlavesStealthUpgrade(TRUE) if KINDOF_SPAWNS_ARE_THE_WEAPONS.

## Rust
StealthUpgrade::can_upgrade (stealth_upgrade.rs:168-170) always returns true. apply_upgrade always calls upgrade_implementation, which does not early-out on self.applied before set_status/give_slaves_stealth_upgrade. Object::apply_upgrade_modules therefore re-runs it on every update_upgrade_modules_from_player.

Distinct from hq-0bsm (TriggeredBy never parsed / empty_upgrade_factories).

## Evidence
C++ UpgradeModule.cpp:105-111 !m_upgradeExecuted. Rust stealth_upgrade.rs:168-173 can_upgrade → true; apply_upgrade → upgrade_implementation every time.

## Player-visible effect
Once stealth is applied, every later player-upgrade update re-grants slave stealth. Spawned weapons/slaves can be repeatedly told to stealth; C++ does this once.
close_reason: StealthUpgrade can_upgrade/apply/upgrade_implementation refuse already-applied mux

title: [Upgrade] Live upgrade modules skip RemovesUpgrades except ObjectCreation/SubObjects
description:
## C++
`giveSelfUpgrade` (UpgradeModule.cpp:140-147) calls `processUpgradeRemoval` **before** `upgradeImplementation`. `UpgradeMuxData::muxDataProcessUpgradeRemoval` (Module.cpp:226-244) looks up each `RemovesUpgrades` name and `obj->removeUpgrade(template)` so mutually exclusive upgrades (bomb-truck payloads, etc.) reset.

## Rust
Only `ObjectCreationUpgrade` and `SubObjectsUpgrade` parse `RemovesUpgrades` and call `process_upgrade_removal`. All other live object/upgrade modules have no removal list and `apply_upgrade` never strips conflicting upgrades.

## Evidence
C++ Module.cpp:226-244. Rust leftover.rs upgrade_factories parse_from_ini without RemovesUpgrades. subobjects_upgrade.rs:157-158 and object_creation.rs:201-202 do process removals.

## Player-visible effect
Switching an exclusive upgrade (e.g. bomb-truck payload / conflicting object upgrades) leaves the previous upgrade executed; both stay on.
close_reason: RemovesUpgrades parsed on all live mux modules; apply_upgrade calls process_upgrade_removal before implementation

title: [Upgrade] Live upgrade modules never parse or play FXListUpgrade
description:
## C++
`UpgradeMuxData::getFieldParse` (UpgradeModule.h:76) parses `FXListUpgrade`. `giveSelfUpgrade` (UpgradeModule.cpp:140-147) calls `performUpgradeFX` before `upgradeImplementation`. `UpgradeMuxData::performUpgradeFX` (Module.cpp:217-222) runs `FXList::doFXObj`.

## Rust
Live `UpgradeMuxData` field table (`upgrade/modules/upgrade_mux.rs:373-390`) has TriggeredBy/ConflictsWith/RemovesUpgrades/RequiresAllTriggers but **no FXListUpgrade**. ObjectCreation and SubObjects (the only mux-wired live modules) therefore drop the key. Other live object/upgrade modules never store or play an FX list.

## Evidence
C++ UpgradeModule.h:76 `{ "FXListUpgrade", INI::parseFXList, ... }`. Rust UPGRADE_MUX_DATA_FIELDS omits the token. SubObjects/ObjectCreation field tables also omit it.

## Player-visible effect
Upgrade flash/sound authored as FXListUpgrade on ArmorUpgrade/WeaponSetUpgrade/ObjectCreationUpgrade/SubObjectsUpgrade/etc. never plays when the upgrade completes.
close_reason: FXListUpgrade added to UpgradeMuxData field table and live module INI tables; giveSelfUpgrade plays FX via perform_upgrade_fx

title: [Upgrade] Live upgrade modules skip TriggeredBy/ConflictsWith/RequiresAllTriggers
description:
## C++
Every Object/Upgrade module inherits UpgradeModule → UpgradeMux. `Object::updateUpgradeModules` (Object.cpp:2410-2438) calls `attemptUpgrade(playerMask|objectMask)`. `UpgradeMux::wouldUpgrade` (UpgradeModule.cpp:105-137) requires the module's INI `TriggeredBy` (activation), rejects `ConflictsWith`, and honors `RequiresAllTriggers`. `UpgradeMuxData::getFieldParse` (UpgradeModule.h:69-80) parses those keys on every upgrade module.

## Rust
Live factories are `contain_module_overrides/leftover.rs` `upgrade_factories!` → each module's `parse_from_ini`. Only `ObjectCreationUpgrade` and `SubObjectsUpgrade` parse mux fields and call `would_upgrade`. The other live modules (`armor`, `weapon_set`, `weapon_bonus`, `max_health`, `status_bits`, `radar`, `power_plant`, `command_set`, `cost_modifier`, `experience_scalar`, `grant_science`, `unpause_special_power`, `passengers_fire`, `model_condition`, `locomotor_set`, `active_shroud`, `replace_object`) have no UpgradeMuxData; `can_upgrade` is `!applied` (or always true). `Object::apply_upgrade_modules` (object_upgrade.rs:526-541) then applies them on any non-empty mask.

StealthUpgrade is worse (empty_upgrade_factories ignores INI entirely) and is already hq-0bsm.

## Evidence
C++ UpgradeModule.h:73-77 TriggeredBy/ConflictsWith/RequiresAllTriggers. C++ UpgradeModule.cpp:105-137 wouldUpgrade. Rust armor_upgrade.rs:346-373 can_upgrade accepts any mask. Rust leftover.rs:160-186 parse_from_ini with empty/no mux fields. ObjectCreation/SubObjects are the exceptions.

## Player-visible effect
The first completed player/object upgrade fires every mux-less upgrade module on the unit (wrong armor/weapons/command set/power/radar/HP/status/science/etc.) instead of waiting for that module's TriggeredBy research. ConflictsWith and RequiresAllTriggers are ignored.
close_reason: Live upgrade modules parse TriggeredBy/ConflictsWith/RequiresAllTriggers via UpgradeMuxData; can_upgrade uses would_upgrade (object/upgrade/* + upgrade_mux.rs)

title: [Weapon] Live Weapon.ini loader drops DamageStatusType
description:
## C++
TheWeaponTemplateFieldParseTable (Weapon.cpp:161) maps DamageStatusType via ObjectStatusMaskType::parseSingleBitFromINI onto WeaponTemplate::m_damageStatusType. Ctor default OBJECT_STATUS_NONE (Weapon.cpp:303). AvengerTargetDesignator authors DamageType=STATUS and DamageStatusType=FAERIE_FIRE so dealDamageInternal applies that status bit for the PrimaryDamage duration.

## Rust
Live combat copies template.damage_status_type onto DamageInfo (weapon_instance_combat.rs:280) and ActiveBody STATUS damage calls do_status_damage. GameLogic WeaponTemplate ctor defaults the field to None. Main register_weapon_template_from_properties (ini_template_loader.rs:862-1277) never reads DamageStatusType. The only parser for the key is the unused crate parse_weapon_fields_from_ini (weapon_template.rs:2355-2357). Common leftover ini_weapon.rs lists the token in CPP_WEAPON_TEMPLATE_FIELDS but only stashes it as an untyped property on the unused Common store.

## Evidence
C++ Weapon.cpp:161 DamageStatusType parseSingleBitFromINI.
Live loader: no DamageStatusType match in ini_template_loader.rs (grep of the apply path is empty).
Closed hq-01zi covered ContinuousFire / RadiusDamageAffects / LaserName / AutoReloadsClip / PreAttackType / WeaponBonus / scatter — not this key.

## Player-visible effect
Avenger designator (and any STATUS weapon) never applies FAERIE_FIRE from INI, so TARGET_FAERIE_FIRE rate-of-fire bonus never arms from the authored weapon.
close_reason: ini_template_loader.rs parses DamageStatusType via ObjectStatus bit-name index onto WeaponTemplate.damage_status_type (default NONE); host_damage_status_type_for_weapon_name reads the live store so Avenger FAERIE_FIRE is authored not hardcoded

title: [SpecialPower] Live GameLogic templates never receive SpecialPower.ini field table
description:
## C++
SpecialPowerStore::parseSpecialPowerDefinition (SpecialPower.cpp:117-166) reads the name, copies DefaultSpecialPower, then initFromINI with m_specialPowerFieldParse (170-188): ReloadTime (parseDurationUnsignedInt msec→frames), RequiredScience, InitiateSound, InitiateAtLocationSound, PublicTimer, Enum (SpecialPowerMaskType names), DetectionTime (default DEFAULT_DEFECTION_DETECTION_PROTECTION_TIME_LIMIT = 300 frames), SharedSyncedTimer, ViewObjectDuration, ViewObjectRange, RadiusCursorRadius, ShortcutPower, AcademyClassify.

## Rust
Boot shell.rs:1364-1375 parses SpecialPower.ini through Common BLOCK_PARSE_TABLE into common::rts::special_power::SpecialPowerStore, whose apply_field_parse implements the full C++ table. Live modules (SpecialPowerModule, command buttons, AI) call find_or_create_special_power_template (special_power_template.rs:402-419), which looks up leftover Common ini_special_power::get_special_power_store — a different singleton that boot never fills. Miss → SpecialPowerTemplate::new (reload 0, Enum Invalid, academy Invalid, radius 0, no sounds). Leftover ini_special_power.rs itself also has invented defaults (recharge_time 30, range 100, radius 50) and Enum via from_string("nuke") rather than SPECIAL_* names.

## Evidence
ini.rs:560-569 dispatches to rts::special_power::parse_special_power_definition_with_load_type.
special_power_template.rs:10-12 / 412-416 imports leftover ini_special_power store.
Two distinct statics: rts OnceLock vs ini_special_power OnceCell.

## Player-visible effect
Superweapons and unit specials keep ctor defaults: instant ReloadTime, no PublicTimer/ShortcutPower, no radius cursor, no initiate audio, Enum INVALID so type-specific modules never match, AcademyClassify never ACT_SUPERPOWER.
close_reason: special_power_template.rs: find_or_create reads boot-filled RTS SpecialPowerStore field table

title: [Upgrade] Live Upgrade.ini parse drops ResearchSound, UnitSpecificSound, AcademyClassify
description:
## C++
UpgradeTemplate::m_upgradeFieldParseTable (Upgrade.cpp:90-103) parses eight keys: DisplayName, Type, BuildTime, BuildCost, ButtonImage, ResearchSound (parseAudioEventRTS), UnitSpecificSound (parseAudioEventRTS), AcademyClassify (TheAcademyClassificationTypeNames: ACT_NONE, ACT_UPGRADE_RADAR, ACT_SUPERPOWER). Ctor defaults: type PLAYER, cost 0, buildTime 0, academy ACT_NONE. getResearchCompleteSound / getUnitSpecificSound / getAcademyClassificationType are live accessors. Player::academy record_upgrade treats ACT_UPGRADE_RADAR as researched radar.

## Rust
Common leftover ini_upgrade.rs update_from_properties does parse all eight keys into Common UpgradeCenter (unused for research). Live GameLogic UpgradeTemplate::UPGRADE_TEMPLATE_FIELDS (upgrade/template.rs:326-347) only has DisplayName, Type, BuildTime, BuildCost, ButtonImage. Main ini_template_loader.rs:1463-1472 UPGRADE_INI_SETTER_FIELDS is the same five-key list and documents that ResearchSound / UnitSpecificSound / AcademyClassify have no GameLogic setters. Fields exist on the struct (research_sound, unit_specific_sound, academy_classification) and stay at ctor empty/0. player_upgrade_manager.rs:217-228 playResearchSound no-ops because the event is empty. academy_score.rs:104-106 record_upgrade never sees classification 1.

## Evidence
C++ table: ResearchSound, UnitSpecificSound, AcademyClassify.
Rust live table: five keys only (upgrade/template.rs:326-347; ini_template_loader.rs:1466-1472).
Common leftover parser has the three keys but GameLogic UpgradeCenter is the live store (sell_upgrade.rs / load_upgrade_templates).

## Player-visible effect
Completing Radar / Comanche / BoobyTrap upgrades plays no ResearchSound and no UnitSpecificSound. Academy never records ACT_UPGRADE_RADAR, so radar-advice hints stay wrong.
close_reason: upgrade/template.rs + ini_template_loader.rs parse ResearchSound, UnitSpecificSound, AcademyClassify (ACT_NONE/ACT_UPGRADE_RADAR/ACT_SUPERPOWER)

title: [GUI Script] IMAGEOFFSET parsed from WND but never copied onto instance data
description:
## C++
`parseImageOffset` (`GameWindowManagerScript.cpp:545-556`) writes `IMAGEOFFSET` into `instData->m_imageOffset`. W3D gadget draws add that offset when blitting images.

## Rust
`window_script.rs:424-428` parses `IMAGEOFFSET` onto `WindowDefinition.image_offset`. Live `layout_load.rs` `create_window_from_definition` copies style, names, tooltip_delay, text, tooltip, text colors, and draw-data arrays — but never `data.image_offset = window_def.image_offset`. Instance data stays `(0,0)`. Draw paths (`game_window/callbacks.rs:69`, `w3d_gadget_draw/*`) do honor `inst_data.image_offset` when it is set.

## Evidence
C++: `instData->m_imageOffset.x/y = atoi(...)`.
Rust: parse stores on the definition; layout_load never assigns `WindowInstanceData.image_offset`.

## Player-visible effect
Any window whose `.wnd` has a non-zero `IMAGEOFFSET` draws gadget art at the unshifted origin instead of the authored pixel offset (misaligned button/slider/listbox images).
close_reason: layout_load.rs copies window_def.image_offset onto WindowInstanceData (C++ parseImageOffset).

title: [WinInstanceData] Default draw/text colors are 0, not WIN_COLOR_UNDEFINED
description:
## C++
`WinInstanceData::init` (`WinInstanceData.cpp:75-98`) sets every `m_enabledDrawData` / `m_disabledDrawData` / `m_hiliteDrawData` slot (`MAX_DRAW_DATA=9`) and enabled/disabled/hilite text colors to `WIN_COLOR_UNDEFINED`. Draw paths skip fill/border when color is that sentinel (`0x00FFFFFF`).

## Rust
`WindowDrawData` and `WindowTextColors` derive `Default` so `color`/`border_color` are `0`. `WindowInstanceData::default` (`game_window/font.rs:150-156`) uses those zeros. `WIN_COLOR_UNDEFINED` is correctly `0x00FFFFFF` (`game_window/messages.rs:17`) but is not used as the init value.

`default_draw_callback` (`game_window/callbacks.rs:99-110`) treats `color != WIN_COLOR_UNDEFINED` as defined and issues `ColorFill`. Color `0` therefore draws a black/transparent rect. Several gadget draws (`w3d_gadget_draw/check_radio.rs:95-110`) likewise open/fill when `!= WIN_COLOR_UNDEFINED`.

`layout_load` also never copies parsed `WindowDefinition.image_offset` onto `WindowInstanceData.image_offset` (`parseImageOffset` in C++ writes `instData->m_imageOffset` at `GameWindowManagerScript.cpp:545-556`).

## Evidence
C++ init: `color = WIN_COLOR_UNDEFINED` for all 9×3 draw slots + text colors.
Rust: `Default` u32 0; draw checks `!= WIN_COLOR_UNDEFINED`.

## Player-visible effect
Programmatic USER windows and gadget children created without WND draw data paint a black fill/border instead of staying unset. Authored `IMAGEOFFSET` never shifts gadget art.
close_reason: font.rs WindowDrawData/WindowTextColors/WindowInstanceData Default use WIN_COLOR_UNDEFINED like WinInstanceData::init.

title: [WinInstanceData] Default tooltip_delay is 10, not C++ -1
description:
## C++
`WinInstanceData::init` (`WinInstanceData.cpp:107`) sets `m_tooltipDelay = -1`. `GameWindowManager::winProcessMouseEvent` passes that value to `TheMouse->setCursorTooltip(text, m_tooltipDelay)`. `Mouse::setCursorTooltip` default arg is `-1`; `update_tooltip` uses the Mouse.ini global delay when override < 0.

GUIEdit always writes `TOOLTIPDELAY` (default -1).

## Rust
`WindowInstanceData::default` (`game_window/font.rs:158`) sets `tooltip_delay: crate::gui::TOOLTIP_DELAY` (`gui/mod.rs:351` = 10). `WindowDefinition` `Default` is `tooltip_delay: 0`. Live `layout_load.rs:177` copies `window_def.tooltip_delay` onto instance data. `window_manager/input.rs:376-379` passes `Some(delay)` to `Mouse::set_cursor_tooltip`. `mouse.rs:954-958` treats any `>= 0` as an absolute millisecond override.

Programmatic `create_window` never goes through WND parse, so every non-script window keeps 10.

## Evidence
C++ init: `m_tooltipDelay = -1`.
Rust Default: `TOOLTIP_DELAY` (10) / WindowDefinition 0.
Mouse: `if tooltip_delay_override_ms >= 0 { override } else { tooltip_delay_time_ms }`.

## Player-visible effect
Tooltips on programmatic windows (and any WND that omits TOOLTIPDELAY) pop after 10ms or immediately instead of waiting for the retail Mouse.ini tooltip delay (~hundreds of ms). Hover tips flash on as soon as the cursor stops.
close_reason: WindowInstanceData and WindowDefinition tooltip_delay default -1; TOOLTIPDELAY parse unwrap_or(-1).

title: [GUI Script] WINDOW LISTBOX/COMBOBOX*DRAWDATA never applied to gadget children
description:
## C++
`GameWindowManagerScript.cpp` `gameWindowFieldList` includes `LISTBOXENABLEDUPBUTTONDRAWDATA` … `COMBOBOXLISTBOXHILITEDRAWDATA` (2230-2277). `parseDrawData` (1222-1329) writes those tokens into file-level statics (`enabledUpButtonDrawData`, `enabledDropDownButtonDrawData`, etc.). `parseWindow` parses fields then immediately `createWindow`/`gogoGadgetListBox`/`gogoGadgetComboBox`, which copy those statics onto the child up/down/slider/dropdown/edit/list windows.

GUIEdit writes the keys **inside** the listbox/combo `WINDOW` block (`GeneralsRust/Code/Tools/GUIEdit/src/save.rs` extra_draw tokens).

## Rust
Live parser `window_script.rs` `parse_window_statement` (386-430) has no arms for `LISTBOX*` / `COMBOBOX*` draw-data keys (`_ => {}` drops them). `parse_layout_statement` only sees those keys outside a `WINDOW`. After a full-file parse, `layout.listbox_*` / `combo_*` stay empty.

`window_manager/gadgets.rs` `create_listbox_scrollbar_children` / `create_combo_box_children` apply those empty layout vecs via `apply_draw_data_set`. Children keep `WindowDrawData::default()` (no image).

## Evidence
C++: `parseDrawData` token → statics → gadget factory children.
Rust: `parse_window_statement` ignore + `gadgets.rs:445-513` / `:190-301` apply empty slices.

## Player-visible effect
Listbox scrollbar arrows/track and combo dropdown/edit/list chrome never get authored MappedImages. Skirmish/options/replay/save-load listboxes and combo boxes render as unskinned boxes instead of retail gadget art.
close_reason: window_script.rs parses LISTBOX/COMBOBOX*DRAWDATA on WINDOW; gadgets.rs applies window-level then layout-level child draw data.

title: [ObjectStatus] DieMux status mask truncated to u32, drops RIDER3–DEPLOYED
description:
## C++
ObjectStatusTypes.h: OBJECT_STATUS_COUNT=45, bits 0..44 including RIDER1=30 … RIDER8=37, FAERIE_FIRE=38, IMMOBILE=42, DISGUISED=43, DEPLOYED=44. DieMux ExemptStatus/RequiredStatus are ObjectStatusMaskType (full BitFlags). "These are saved. Do not insert or remove any." INI/xfer use ObjectStatusTypes.cpp s_bitNameList.

## Rust
Live Object xfer (`OBJECT_STATUS_XFER_NAMES`) and Common `ObjectStatusMaskType` bits/names match C++ (NONE=1<<0 … DEPLOYED=1<<44).

DieMux path does not: `die/mod.rs` `ObjectStatusMask` is `u32` with only NONE=0 / ALL=0xffffffff. `parse_object_status_mask_tokens` parses via full `ObjectStatusMaskType` then `from_bits_truncate(mask.bits() as u32)`, dropping bits 32–44. Module xfer of exempt/required status also `xfer_unsigned_int` of those u32 bits.

## Evidence
ObjectStatusTypes.h:19-70; ObjectStatusTypes.cpp:11-58; die/mod.rs:157-160,197-201,323-358; Common object_status_types.rs:104-153,345-391.

## Player-visible effect
Die modules ignore ExemptStatus/RequiredStatus for RIDER3–RIDER8, FAERIE_FIRE, MISSILE_KILLING_SELF, REASSIGN_PARKING, BOOBY_TRAPPED, IMMOBILE, DISGUISED, DEPLOYED. A die gated on IMMOBILE/DEPLOYED/DISGUISED fires (or is suppressed) incorrectly.
close_reason: die/mod.rs ObjectStatusMask is u64; parse/is_die_applicable/xfer no longer truncate RIDER3–DEPLOYED

title: [KindOf] Observer count bits remapped (SCORE=45 STRUCTURE=8)
description:
## C++
ControlBarObserver.cpp populateObserverInfoWindow counts via Player::countObjects with KindOf.h bits: SCORE=35, STRUCTURE=7, SCORE_CREATE=36, SCORE_DESTROY=37 (ALLOW_SURRENDER off).

## Rust
`GameClient/src/gui/control_bar/control_bar_observer.rs` hardcodes:

- KINDOF_SCORE = 1<<45 (C++ CAPTURABLE=45; remapped Salvager discriminant)
- KINDOF_STRUCTURE = 1<<8 (C++ INFANTRY=8; remapped Structure discriminant)
- KINDOF_SCORE_CREATE = 1<<46
- KINDOF_SCORE_DESTROY = 1<<47

Comment claims "matching C++ KindOf.h". Passed to `Player::count_objects_by_kindof` → `Object::is_kind_of_multi` → `get_kind_of()` remapped discriminant mask. STRUCTURE=1<<8 happens to match remapped Structure, but SCORE=1<<45 is Salvager (enum index 45), not Score.

## Evidence
KindOf.h SCORE=35 STRUCTURE=7; control_bar_observer.rs:21-25,287-291; player/core.rs:348-366; object_status.rs:509-533.

## Player-visible effect
Observer info window unit/building counts are wrong (infantry counted as structures if C++ mask is used; score units counted as salvagers under remapped mask).
close_reason: control_bar_observer.rs: SCORE=35 STRUCTURE=7 SCORE_CREATE=36 SCORE_DESTROY=37 (KindOf.h ALLOW_SURRENDER off)

title: [KindOf] Module/Object masks use remapped KindOf discriminants as bits
description:
## C++
KindOfMaskType is BitFlags<KINDOF_COUNT> keyed by KindOfType enumerators (INFANTRY=8 → bit 8). Module INI (AutoHeal KindOf/ForbiddenKindOf, EMP victim KindOf, Horde, GrantStealth, PointDefenseLaser, DemoTrap, BattlePlan Valid/InvalidMemberKindOf, DumbProjectile garrison KindOf) and BitFlags::xfer persist those bits by KindOf.cpp names.

## Rust
GameLogic `KindOf` is a remapped enum (Selectable=0, Unit=1, … Infantry=4, Structure=8). Live module parsers and mask builders OR `1u64 << (kind as u32)`:

- `auto_heal_behavior.rs` `parse_kind_of_mask` (shared by EMP/Horde/GrantStealth/PointDefense/DemoTrap)
- `dumb_projectile_behavior.rs` garrison KindOf
- `battle_plan_update.rs` `kindof_bit` (INI + xfer)
- `Object::get_kind_of` / `is_kind_of_multi` (`object_status.rs`)

`kindof_from_name` aliases INERT→Immobile (C++ INERT=84, IMMOBILE=2) and accepts invented tokens (UNIT, WEAPON, BARRIER) that are not KindOf.cpp names. `KindOf::Inert` is a const alias of Immobile — INERT is not a distinct bit.

These masks are then tested via `is_kind_of_multi` against `get_kind_of()` (same remapped encoding), so they are internally consistent with each other but not with Common `KindOfMask` (C++ bits) or save names written from KindOf.h indices.

## Evidence
KindOf.h:20-150; auto_heal_behavior.rs:197-213; battle_plan_update.rs:195-205,1463-1465; object_status.rs:509-533; enums.rs:605-748,758-830.

## Player-visible effect
INI `KindOf = INFANTRY` on AutoHeal/EMP/Horde/BattlePlan sets remapped bit 4 (C++ STICK_TO_TERRAIN_SLOPE) instead of bit 8. Healing, EMP victim filters, horde membership, battle-plan bonuses, and player `count_objects_by_kindof` disagree with Object.ini KindOf bits. INERT objects are treated as IMMOBILE.
close_reason: KindOf::cpp_mask() used by get_kind_of, parse_kind_of_mask, battle_plan kindof_bit, module testers; INERT is a distinct bit 84

title: [KindOf] kind_index/kind_of_indices/kind_of_bit still remapped vs KindOf.h
description:
## C++
KindOf.h / KindOf.cpp (ALLOW_SURRENDER undefined in retail ZH): KINDOF_COUNT=116, index==bit. STRUCTURE=7, INFANTRY=8, LINEBUILD=15, PROJECTILE=22, REPAIR_PAD=28, SCORE=35, CRATE=44, ALWAYS_SELECTABLE=53, FS_POWER=57, FS_AIRFIELD=106, HERO=85, IMMOBILE=2. PRISON/POW_TRUCK/CAN_SURRENDER omitted. BitFlagsIO xfer/INI uses KindOf.cpp s_bitNameList in that order.

## Rust
Three live tables still disagree with that layout:

1. `GameLogic/src/common/types/kind_indices.rs` `engine_kind_indices` — used by scripts (`scripting/engine/init.rs` `template_matches_kind` → Common `ThingTemplate::is_kind_of(idx)`) and crate name fallback. ALWAYS_SELECTABLE=57, CRATE=48, TECH_BUILDING=69, PROJECTILE=25, SALVAGER=19, FS_AIRFIELD=110, PRISON=15, CAN_SURRENDER=44 (surrender-on / +4). SCORE/HERO/IMMOBILE/MINE map to empty (`&[]`) so those queries never match.

2. `GameLogic/src/helpers/lookup.rs` `EngineThingTemplateAdapter::kind_index` — live `Object::is_kind_of`. Specials are surrender-on (RepairPad=31 not 28, Powered=70 not 66, Capturable=49 not 45). Fallback is `ALL_KIND_OF` position (Structure→8 not 7, so STRUCTURE tests INFANTRY). Adapter stores `get_kindof_mask() as u64`, dropping C++ bits 64–115 (AUTO_RALLYPOINT…IGNORE_DOCKING_BONES).

3. `Common/src/common/rts/action_manager.rs` `kind_of_bit` — ActionManager `ObjectDataProvider::is_kind_of`. TRANSPORT=21 not 18, BRIDGE=22 not 19, REPAIR_PAD=31 not 28, FS_AIRFIELD=110 not 106; unknown bits fail closed. `object_data_provider.rs` maps those wrong indices onto GameLogic `KindOf`.

Common `KindOfMask` / `KIND_OF_BIT_NAMES` already match KindOf.h (hq-a54v closed that layer only).

## Evidence
KindOf.h:20-150; KindOf.cpp:10-137; kind_indices.rs:8-146; lookup.rs:10,62,111-133,291-298; thing_template.rs get_kindof_mask `self.kindof as u64`; action_manager.rs:282-300; object_data_provider.rs:20-41; scripting/engine/init.rs:1195-1198.

## Player-visible effect
Script KindOf conditions, crate filters, unit is_kind_of (mobile/selectable/radar/AI), and ActionManager can-do checks test the wrong KindOf bits. Heroes/score/immobile script tests no-op. High KindOf bits (≥64) never reach GameLogic objects.
close_reason: kind_indices/lookup/action_manager/leftover now use KindOf.h bits; lookup stores get_kindof_bits() u128

title: [VeterancyGainCreate] on_create never notifies and host is a hardcoded subset
description:
## C++
`VeterancyGainCreate::onCreate` (`VeterancyGainCreate.cpp:56-73`) if the controlling player exists and (`ScienceRequired` is invalid or `hasScience`), and the tracker `isTrainable()`, calls `setMinVeterancyLevel(m_startingLevel)`. `setMinVeterancyLevel` (`ExperienceTracker.cpp:66-78`) raises level, seeds XP to `getExperienceRequired(newLevel)`, and calls `onVeterancyLevelChanged`. INI keys: `StartingLevel`, `ScienceRequired` (default REGULAR / SCIENCE_INVALID). USA Pilot omits science and starts Veteran; Red Guard / Technical / Battlemaster / artillery use science-gated modules.

## Rust
Crate `VeterancyGainCreate::on_create` (`create/veterancy_gain_create.rs:87-126`) does call `set_min_veterancy_level` when trainable + science ok, but crate `set_min_veterancy_level` only mutates the tracker and returns `Option` — no `on_veterancy_level_changed`. It also passes `DEFAULT_EXPERIENCE_REQUIRED` (template used only if owner lookup works). Live host ignores the module and uses `host_unit_training.rs` hardcoded science→level pairs (RedGuard Veteran, MiniGunner Elite, Battlemaster Elite, Artillery Veteran, Technical Veteran, Pilot always Veteran). Any other INI `VeterancyGainCreate` is dropped.

## Evidence
C++ `setMinVeterancyLevel` comment: "use setMin so we never lose levels". Host file header: "Fail-closed: not full IsTrainable / experience tracker exclusive module matrix". Crate create path never applies body/upgrade/FX for the granted min-level.

## Player-visible effect
Science-trained units on the crate path get a tracker rank without health/weapon bonuses. On the host path, only the hardcoded science list grants starting veterancy; other INI StartingLevel modules never fire.
close_reason: VeterancyGainCreate notifies on_veterancy_level_changed; host parses/applies INI StartingLevel+ScienceRequired

title: [VeterancyCrate] Host crate grants skip trainable and AddsOwnerVeterancy 0
description:
## C++
`VeterancyCrateCollide::isValidToExecute` (`VeterancyCrateCollide.cpp:45-96`) requires base crate validity, not dead, not significantly above terrain, `levelsToGain > 0`, `et->isTrainable()`, and `et->canGainExpForLevel(levelsToGain)`. `getLevelsToGain` (`:33-41`) returns 1 unless `AddsOwnerVeterancy`, then `(Int)owner->getVeterancyLevel()` (Regular=0, so the crate is invalid). Pilot crates also require same controlling player and reject airborne locomotors. `executeCrateBehavior` requires the crate owner's AI goal == collider.

## Rust
Crate module (`veterancy_crate_collide.rs:312-331,402-450`) mostly matches those gates, but `get_levels_to_gain` / `execute` / area collect all return 0/false/empty when `OBJECT_REGISTRY.is_empty()` (Wave 368 host-only path). Live host `execute_veterancy_crate_behavior` (`world_tick/crates.rs:851-893`) does `levels.max(1)`, always passes `can_level_up=true`, filters only same team + not structure + 2D range, and never checks trainable, above-terrain, airborne, same-player pilot, or AI goal.

## Evidence
Host comment at crates.rs:886: "can_level_up = trainable residual: not heroic already handled inside" — trainable is hardcoded true. Regular `AddsOwnerVeterancy` crates still grant +1.

## Player-visible effect
On the live host path, level-up crates promote untrainable units and treat a Regular owner crate as +1 level. Pilot-enter crates are not gated like retail. The crate GameLogic module is inert while the host registry is empty.
close_reason: host crate drops levels.max(1); trainable/same-player/under-construction gates; Regular AddsOwnerVeterancy stays 0

title: [Experience] score_the_kill promotions never notify Object
description:
## C++
`ExperienceTracker::addExperiencePoints` (`ExperienceTracker.cpp:161-165`) on a level change calls `m_parent->onVeterancyLevelChanged(oldLevel, m_currentLevel)`. Same for `setVeterancyLevel` / `setMinVeterancyLevel` / `setExperienceAndLevel`. That applies veterancy upgrades, body health bonuses, weapon-set flags, and promotion FX/sound.

## Rust
Crate `ExperienceTracker::add_experience_points` only returns `Option<old_level>` (`tracker.rs:228-274`) and never notifies. Canonical `Object::score_the_kill` (`object_combat.rs:357`) ignores the return: `tracker_guard.add_experience_points(experience_value, true, &[]);` with no `on_veterancy_level_changed`. ActiveBody death still calls this via `OBJECT_REGISTRY` (`active_body.rs:1540-1835`).

## Evidence
`on_veterancy_level_changed` exists (`object_combat.rs:366`) and crate/salvage collide paths call it. The kill path — C++'s only XP source — does not.

## Player-visible effect
A unit can have Veteran/Elite in the tracker after kills without the health bonus, veterancy weapon set, upgrade modules, or promotion anim/sound.
close_reason: object_combat score_the_kill notifies on_veterancy_level_changed after add_experience_points promotion

title: [Experience] Crate Object init skips ProductionVeterancyLevel
description:
## C++
`Object` ctor after allocating the tracker (`Object.cpp:451-456`) does `m_experienceTracker->setVeterancyLevel(controller->getProductionVeterancyLevel(getTemplate()->getName()))`. `Player::getProductionVeterancyLevel` (`Player.cpp:1958-1967`) looks up `m_productionVeterancyLevels` (copied from PlayerTemplate) and defaults to `LEVEL_FIRST`. This is the min-level path for General-specific starting ranks (e.g. America Ranger Veteran, Raptor Elite).

## Rust
Crate `init_modules_for` (`object/object_modules.rs:919`) only does `ExperienceTracker::new(id)` (Regular, 0 XP). GameLogic `Player` has no `get_production_veterancy_level` and does not store `m_productionVeterancyLevels` (only `PlayerTemplate` has the map). Host spawn (`world_objects/create_destroy_die.rs:1251-1252`) does call `set_min_veterancy_level` from Common PlayerTemplate; crate GameLogic objects never do.

## Evidence
Missing method: `Player::getProductionVeterancyLevel`. Missing side effect: Object construction never `setVeterancyLevel` from that map. C++ setVeterancyLevel also notifies `onVeterancyLevelChanged` so health/weapon-set/upgrade apply immediately.

## Player-visible effect
On the crate Object path, units that retail spawn Veteran/Elite from ProductionVeterancyLevel spawn Regular. Dual-world crate objects disagree with host objects of the same template.
close_reason: Player::get_production_veterancy_level + crate Object init setVeterancyLevel + notify

title: [Experience] set_experience_and_level skips isTrainable safety
description:
## C++
`ExperienceTracker::setExperienceAndLevel` (`ExperienceTracker.cpp:169-185`) after optional sink forward does `if (!isTrainable()) return;` before writing XP or recalculating level. `isTrainable()` is `parent->getTemplate()->isTrainable()` (default FALSE).

## Rust
`ExperienceTracker::set_experience_and_level` (`experience/tracker.rs:336-364`) has no trainable check. It always writes `current_experience` and runs `update_level_from_experience`. Live callers: unmanned/kill-pilot wipe (`object/disabled.rs:168-171` `set_experience_and_level(0, &[])`) and `rider_change_contain.rs:347-351`.

## Evidence
C++ comment: "safety". Rust `is_trainable()` itself also diverges when owner lookup fails (`tracker.rs:327-329`): `owner_is_trainable().unwrap_or_else(|| can_gain_exp_for_level(1))` treats any non-Heroic unit as trainable.

## Player-visible effect
Untrainable objects can be forced to a new XP/level (or wiped) by unmanned/rider paths. Buildings/dozers that C++ leave at Regular can change rank.
close_reason: set_experience_and_level isTrainable safety; is_trainable defaults FALSE from template

title: [Experience] Experience sink never forwards transferable XP
description:
## C++
`ExperienceTracker::addExperiencePoints` (`ExperienceTracker.cpp:126-135`) if `m_experienceSink != INVALID_ID` and the sink object still exists, forwards `experienceGain * m_experienceScalar` to the sink tracker and returns. `setExperienceAndLevel` forwards the raw amount (`:171-180`). `isAcceptingExperiencePoints` is true when a sink is set even if the source is not trainable. Callers: projectile fire (`Weapon.cpp:3021` sink=launcher), `NeutronMissileUpdate` (`:219`), `OverlordContain` rider (`:354-355` when `m_experienceSinkForRider`), `SpecialAbilityUpdate` spawned objects (`:1641`).

## Rust
Crate `ExperienceTracker::add_experience_points` (`experience/tracker.rs:234-249`) does implement sink forwarding. Live host `Object::gain_experience` (`object/update.rs:403-447`) has no sink field and always keeps XP on the attacker. Host residual `ExperienceTrackerResidual::add_experience_points` (`host_ai_path_combat_residual_wave105.rs:1200-1203`) fail-closes: `if self.experience_sink.is_some() { return; }` — points are dropped, not transferred.

## Evidence
Live kill path is host `continue_or_stop_after_kill` → `gain_experience`. Projectile/Overlord/special-ability crate setters exist (`weapon/template.rs:1122`, `overlord_contain.rs:373`, `special_ability_update.rs:1553`) but host combat never consults them.

## Player-visible effect
Jet/missile kills do not rank up the launching aircraft/airfield. Overlord bunker gunner XP stays on the rider (or vanishes). Sink-only units that C++ treats as accepting XP grant nothing.
close_reason: host experience_sink + award_experience forwards to sink/producer; residual records forward

title: [Experience] Live kill XP ignores ExperienceValue table and trainable gate
description:
## C++
`Object::scoreTheKill` (`Object.cpp:2932-2940`) awards XP only when `isAcceptingExperiencePoints()` (trainable or sink set) and the victim is not `UNDER_CONSTRUCTION`. Value is `victim->getExperienceTracker()->getExperienceValue(this)`: 0 if killer relationship is ALLIES, else `template->getExperienceValue(m_currentLevel)` (`ExperienceTracker.cpp:37-43`) — the per-level INI `ExperienceValue` list.

## Rust
Live host combat (`world_objects/object_ai_combat.rs:214-216`, `world_tick/shock.rs:677-679`) computes `template.experience_value * veterancy_xp_multiplier(level)` (1.0/1.25/1.5/2.0 in `spawn_templates.rs:37-43`) and always calls `gain_experience` with no `IsTrainable` / `isAcceptingExperiencePoints` / under-construction check. Host stores a single `experience_value` (first INI token only). Crate `score_the_kill` (`object_combat.rs:345-357`) does call `is_accepting_experience_points` but then `get_experience_value(victim_cost, …)` fabricates `cost * 0.5 * (1 + 0.25*level)` when template lookup fails (`tracker.rs:394-407`) and passes empty requirements.

## Evidence
C++ Ranger ExperienceValue is 20/20/40/60. Host awards 20 * 1.25 = 25 for a Veteran Ranger. Untrainable turrets/buildings that get a kill credit also gain XP because host `gain_experience` has no trainable gate.

## Player-visible effect
Kill XP (and who can even earn it) does not match retail. Elite/Heroic victims pay a fabricated multiplier instead of their INI table; non-trainable attackers can rank up.
close_reason: kill XP uses ExperienceValue table + isAccepting + UNDER_CONSTRUCTION; award_experience trainable/sink

title: [Experience] Live host XP ladder ignores INI ExperienceRequired
description:
## C++
`ExperienceTracker::addExperiencePoints` / `setVeterancyLevel` / `setMinVeterancyLevel` / `gainExpForLevel` (`ExperienceTracker.cpp:66-207`) always compare and seed XP from `m_parent->getTemplate()->getExperienceRequired(level)`. ThingTemplate parses the 4-int `ExperienceRequired` list (`ThingTemplate.cpp:111`, defaults all 0). Retail ladders differ by unit (Ranger 0/40/60/120, Pathfinder 0/50/100/200, USA tank 0/200/300/600).

## Rust
Live host `Object::gain_experience` (`Main/src/game_logic/object/update.rs:403-447`) levels against `thing.template.veterancy_xp_thresholds`, which defaults to `[60, 150, 300]` (`thing.rs:1150-1270`). Host `spawn_templates.rs` never copies INI `ExperienceRequired` into that field. Crate `ExperienceTracker` prefers the template table when `TheGameLogic` lookup works, else `DEFAULT_EXPERIENCE_REQUIRED = [0, 100, 300, 600]` (`experience/tracker.rs:45`).

## Evidence
Host template builder parses only the first `ExperienceValue` token (`spawn_templates.rs:308-313`) and never `ExperienceRequired`. Residual tables in `host_rank_ui_residual.rs` document the real ladders but are unused by `gain_experience`.

## Player-visible effect
Rangers promote too late and Crusaders/Battlemasters too early. Every unit shares one fake 60/150/300 ladder instead of its Object.ini thresholds.
close_reason: spawn_templates copies INI ExperienceRequired into veterancy_xp_thresholds

title: [PUC] Sabotage/timer reset does not pack
description:
## C++
When not in an active attack window, update() (ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:684-709) walks charge frames then:
else if status==ALMOST_READY: no-op
else if status==READY_TO_FIRE: setLogicalStatus(PACKING) — "timer has been reset (sabotaged?)"

## Rust
update_simple (particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:1612-1620) only has the ready/almost/preparing/charging arms. The READY_TO_FIRE → PACKING reset branch is missing, so a sabotaged/reset superweapon timer leaves the building deployed.

## Evidence
C++ ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:700-709.
Rust GameLogic/src/object/behavior/particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:1612-1620.

## Player-visible effect
Resetting or sabotaging the Particle Uplink timer does not pack the dish; it stays in the ready/deployed pose.
close_reason: PUC update_simple READY_TO_FIRE -> PACKING when timer reset (sabotaged)

title: [PUC] Scripted waypoint path never advances
description:
## C++
initiateIntent with a script waypoint (ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:270-300) stores m_nextDestWaypointID, picks a random first link, and sets m_overrideTargetDestination to that link. While driving, if distance < speed and scriptedWaypointMode (552-564), it advances to a random outgoing link.

## Rust
initiate_intent (particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:1696-1706) sets scripted_waypoint_mode and copies the first waypoint position to override, but never sets next_dest_waypoint_id or walks links. The drive block (1424-1427) is a leftover comment: "Handle waypoint advance if scripted here...".

## Evidence
C++ ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:270-300, 547-564.
Rust GameLogic/src/object/behavior/particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:1696-1706, 1424-1427.

## Player-visible effect
Script-fired Particle Cannon along a waypoint path sits on the first point instead of traveling the path.
close_reason: initiate_intent stores next_dest_waypoint_id + first random link; drive advances outgoing links

title: [PUC] Sold/construction/dead never abort charging
description:
## C++
update() (ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:373-392) tests SOLD first: if not IDLE, setLogicalStatus(IDLE) + killEverything() (destroy all FX/lasers/sounds). UNDER_CONSTRUCTION and isEffectivelyDead return without advancing charge/fire.

## Rust
update_simple (particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:1224-1226) has a comment claiming the BehaviorModule wrapper handles Sold / UnderConstruction / EffectivelyDead. No status test, no killEverything. Selling or dying mid-charge leaves status/FX running.

## Evidence
C++ ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:187-207, 373-392.
Rust GameLogic/src/object/behavior/particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:1213-1230.

## Player-visible effect
Selling, cancelling construction, or destroying the Particle Uplink while it is charging/firing leaves dish FX, beams, and the state machine running.
close_reason: update_simple aborts Sold (IDLE+removeAllEffects), UnderConstruction, EffectivelyDead

title: [PUC] DEPLOYED model condition never set
description:
## C++
setLogicalStatus (ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:1103-1183) drives model conditions:
- IDLE: clear PACKING|UNPACKING|DEPLOYED
- PREPARING: clear PACKING|DEPLOYED, set UNPACKING
- ALMOST_READY / READY_TO_FIRE / FIRING: clear PACKING|UNPACKING, set DEPLOYED
- PACKING: clear UNPACKING|DEPLOYED, set PACKING

## Rust
set_logical_status (particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:814-821) only toggles Packing/Unpacking. DEPLOYED is never set or cleared. After unpack the drawable falls back to the idle pose.

## Evidence
C++ ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:1103-1183.
Rust GameLogic/src/object/behavior/particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:800-842.

## Player-visible effect
The Particle Uplink building never holds the deployed dish/antenna pose while charging, ready, or firing.
close_reason: set_logical_status now sets/clears DEPLOYED with PACKING/UNPACKING per C++

title: [PUC] Damage-pulse remnant objects never spawned
description:
## C++
Each damage pulse (ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:650-662) if DamagePulseRemnantObjectName is set: ThingFactory->findTemplate + newObject on the owner's team at m_currentTargetPosition (fire-and-forget burning trail).

## Rust
INI key DamagePulseRemnantObjectName is parsed into damage_pulse_remnant_object_name (particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:586-590). The damage-pulse block (1537-1601) applies radius damage only; it never looks up or creates the remnant object.

## Evidence
C++ ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:650-662.
Rust GameLogic/src/object/behavior/particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:586-590, 1537-1601.

## Player-visible effect
The particle cannon leaves no lingering burn/damage remnant objects along the swath (the INI-authored trail).
close_reason: damage pulse spawns DamagePulseRemnantObjectName via ThingFactory at current target

title: [PUC] Outer dish-node bones never sampled
description:
## C++
calculateDefaultInformation (ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:1035-1063) calls getMultiLogicalBonePosition(outerEffectBaseBoneName, outerEffectNumBones) and convertBonePosToWorldPos into m_outerNodePositions / m_outerNodeOrientations. Wrong bone count marks m_invalidSettings.

## Rust
calculate_default_information (particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:907-924) only resizes the position/orientation/id vectors to zeros/identity and always returns true. create_outer_node_particle_systems then places systems at (0,0,0) or the object origin offset.

## Evidence
C++ ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:1035-1063, 999-1005.
Rust GameLogic/src/object/behavior/particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:907-924, 963-975.

## Player-visible effect
Outer-node charge flares do not sit on the dish rim bones; they clump at the building origin (or world 0).
close_reason: calculate_default_information samples outer dish bones via pristine transforms + convertBonePosToWorldPos

title: [PUC] Beams skip LaserUpdate initLaser growth
description:
## C++
createConnectorLasers / createGroundToOrbitLaser / createOrbitToTargetLaser (ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:793-978) newDrawable the laser template, find ClientUpdate LaserUpdate, and call initLaser(..., growthFrames). Per-frame steering re-inits the orbit beam via LaserUpdate and reads getCurrentLaserRadius for scorch/damage.

## Rust
Those helpers call TheGameClient::set_drawable_beam (particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:1003, 1126, 1449), which only writes beam_start/beam_end on a DRAWABLE_STATE map (game_client.rs:578-584). growth_frames arguments are ignored (`_growth_frames`). No LaserUpdate::initLaser, no widen/decay.

## Evidence
C++ ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:830-835, 913-942, 949-978, 588-595.
Rust GameLogic/src/object/behavior/particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:1106-1151; helpers/game_client.rs:578-584.

## Player-visible effect
Particle cannon beams appear at full width instantly (or as an un-widened stub), do not grow/decay with WidthGrowTime, and scorch/damage radii do not follow LaserUpdate's current radius.
close_reason: create/steer beams call TheGameClient::init_drawable_laser (LaserUpdate initLaser + growth) and get_current_laser_radius

title: [Particle] Options/LOD particle caps never applied at spawn
description:
## C++
ParticleSystem::createParticle (ParticleSys.cpp:1666-1699) reads live TheGlobalData->m_maxParticleCount / m_maxFieldParticleCount and TheGameLODManager->getMinDynamicParticlePriority / getMinDynamicParticleSkipPriority / isParticleSkipped every spawn.
Options, static LOD, and the particle-cap slider write GlobalData.m_maxParticleCount (GameLOD.cpp:326,518; OptionsMenu.cpp). Field default is 30 (GlobalData.cpp:786).

## Rust
Live ParticleSystemManager keeps private copies defaulting to max=2500, field=500, min_priority=WeaponExplosion, min_skip=Critical, skip_mask=0 (particle_manager.rs:592-597).
can_create_particle / should_skip_particle only consult those locals. set_lod_params exists but is called only from tests (fxlist_particle_spawn_lod.rs). GameLODManager::apply_dynamic_lod_level never pushes into the particle manager. Options menu writes global.max_particle_count but createParticle never reads it (only use_fx is read).

## Evidence
C++ ParticleSys.cpp:1666-1699; GlobalData.cpp:785-786; GameLOD.cpp:326,518.
Rust GameClient/src/effects/particle_manager.rs:1118-1254; Common/src/common/ini/ini_game_lod.rs:762-777; no Main/GameClient live set_lod_params caller.

## Player-visible effect
The particle-cap slider, static LOD MaxParticleCount, dynamic LOD skip masks, and MaxFieldParticleCount do not change how many FX spawn. Ground-aligned AREA_EFFECT (dust/scorch fields) can exceed the C++ field cap (30 / INI) up to 500.
close_reason: createParticle reads live GlobalData max/field caps and GameLOD skip/priority; field default 30

title: [PUC] removeAllEffects leaks particle systems
description:
## C++
removeAllEffects (ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:996-1028) calls TheParticleSystemManager->destroyParticleSystemByID for every outer-node, connector, and laser-base system, then destroys connector/base IDs. killEverything also destroys the orbit-to-target drawable and stops all four looped sounds.

## Rust
remove_all_effects (particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:768-798) only zeros outer_system_ids / connector_system_id / laser_base_system_id. It never calls destroy_particle_system. Status changes and shroud toggles call this, so old flares keep simulating.

## Evidence
C++ ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:187-207, 996-1028.
Rust GameLogic/src/object/behavior/particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:768-798, 1162.

## Player-visible effect
Particle Uplink dish flares and connector/base particles stack every charge/ready/fire/shroud transition instead of being replaced.
close_reason: remove_all_effects destroy_particle_system for outer/connector/base IDs before zeroing

title: [Particle] Wind defaults and ping-pong/circular motion mismatch
description:
## C++
ParticleSystemInfo ctor (ParticleSys.cpp:722-733) defaults windAngleChange=0.15, min=0.15, max=0.45, start 0..PI/4, end (TWO_PI-PI/4)..TWO_PI, movingToEndAngle=TRUE.
ParticleSystem ctor (1114-1125) copies those, then randomizes start/end from min/max and windAngle between start and end (always moving toward end).
Particle::update applies doWindMotion unless WIND_MOTION_NOT_USED (351-356), including INVALID/NONE.
updateWindMotion Circular (2185-2201) re-rolls angleChange when it is 0 and wraps both >TWO_PI and <0.

## Rust
Live ParticleSystemInfo::default (particle_manager.rs:445-456) zeros every wind scalar and sets moving_to_end=false.
ParticleSystem::new copies start=start_min / end=end_min then initialize_wind_motion (particle_system.rs:2300-2319) only randomizes wind_angle from the start range and forces moving_to_end=false; start/end are not randomized until a bounce.
do_wind_motion is gated to PingPong|Circular only (1935), so NONE/INVALID never pushes particles.
Circular update (2374-2380) never re-rolls a 0 change and never wraps negative angles.

## Evidence
C++ ParticleSys.cpp:351-356, 703-733, 1114-1125, 2085-2215.
Rust GameClient/src/effects/particle_manager.rs:445-456; particle_system.rs:1935-1936, 2300-2380.

## Player-visible effect
Wind-driven smoke/fire/dust (PingPong/Circular) starts on the wrong swing, can freeze when INI omits WindAngleChange*, and Circular systems do not keep a sane 0..2PI angle.
close_reason: ParticleSystemInfo C++ wind defaults; ctor randomizes start/end/angle toward end; doWind unless NotUsed; Circular re-roll+wrap

title: [Map] v1 PolygonTriggers auto-water uses wrong extent
description:
## C++
ParsePolygonTriggersDataChunk for K_TRIGGERS_VERSION_1 (PolygonTrigger.cpp:178-203) synthesizes a water area using TheGlobalData->m_waterExtentX / m_waterExtentY:
  (-30*MAP_XY_FACTOR, -30*MAP_XY_FACTOR, 7)
  (30*MAP_XY_FACTOR + waterExtentX, ...)
  (..., 30*MAP_XY_FACTOR + waterExtentY, 7)
so the default water table covers the configured water plane, not the heightmap.

## Rust
Live Main parser parse_runtime_polygon_triggers_from_chunky (script_loader.rs:1537-1550) on version==1 adds a square of only ±(30*MAP_XY_FACTOR) — no waterExtent. polygon_trigger.rs:480-503 (used by GameEngine map_loader) uses TerrainLogic::get_extent_including_border().hi instead of GlobalData water_extent_x/y.

## Evidence
PolygonTrigger.cpp:187-196 vs script_loader.rs:1545-1549 and polygon_trigger.rs:488-501. GlobalData water_extent_* is the C++ source.

## Player-visible effect
Version-1 maps (and any path that still hits the v1 fallback) get a tiny or heightmap-sized water polygon. Units/pathing/isUnderwater and water-handle height queries disagree with C++ across most of the map.
close_reason: polygon_trigger.rs + script_loader.rs: v1 auto-water extent uses GlobalData water_extent_x/y + 30*MAP_XY_FACTOR, not terrain hi or a ±30 square

title: [Map] Live fast SidesList write skips validateSides
description:
## C++
ParseSidesDataChunk always ends with TheSidesList->validateSides() (SidesList.cpp:283). validateSides (SidesList.cpp:693-806) guarantees a Neutral player, a singleton default team named team+playerName owned by that player, strips self/unknown tokens from playerAllies/playerEnemies, removes teams whose names collide with players, and reparents teams with missing/self owners to Neutral.

## Rust
sides_list.rs:464-568 implements validate_sides and parse_sides_data_chunk_internal calls it (line 663). The live Main populate path sync_legacy_sides_list_from_dicts (world_save.rs:2097-2103) only reset/add_side/add_team and never calls validate_sides. prepare_for_mp (which C++ follows with later validateSides after adding lobby slots) is also never called.

## Evidence
world_save.rs:2097-2103 vs SidesList.cpp:283 and GameLogic.cpp:1461 TheSidesList->validateSides() after slot sides are added.

## Player-visible effect
Maps missing a Neutral side or a default team never get team<player> created. Bad allies/enemies strings stay in the dict so relationship init can point at missing players. Team/player name collisions and orphan team owners are not repaired before TeamFactory init.
close_reason: sides_list validate_sides now runs after GameEngine map load (prepare_sides_for_new_game) and live sync_legacy_sides_list_from_dicts

title: [Map] Live SidesList populate never attaches map build lists to Player
description:
## C++
ParseSidesDataChunk (SidesList.cpp:227-251) reads each side's BuildListInfo chain (name, template, xyz with z forced 0, angle, initiallyBuilt, rebuilds, and v3 script/health/whiner/unsellable/repairable) onto SidesInfo. PlayerList::newGame (PlayerList.cpp:136-139) does p->setBuildList(side->getBuildList()); side->releaseBuildList() so AI processBaseBuilding can rebuild/auto-build those entries. initiallyBuilt means already placed via ObjectsList, not a second spawn.

## Rust
Main live path parse_runtime_sides_from_chunky (script_loader.rs:1613-1648) decodes side_builds, but sync_legacy_sides_list_from_dicts (world_save.rs:2087-2103) only add_side/add_team — SidesInfo.build_list stays None. spawn_side_build_list (world_save.rs:1526-1618) instantiates initiallyBuilt templates as extra objects and discards num_rebuilds/script_name; parse_side_build_entry (script_loader.rs:2412-2414) drops whiner/unsellable/repairable. GameEngine take_build_list (game_initialization.rs:696-698) would transfer a list if one existed; Main fast sync never writes one.

## Evidence
world_save.rs:2097-2103 reset/add_side/add_team only. spawn_side_build_list:1563-1616 skips !initially_built and lets _ = entry.num_rebuilds / script_name.

## Player-visible effect
AI never rebuilds map-planned faction bases after destruction. initiallyBuilt entries can double-spawn beside ObjectsList copies. Rebuild counts, on-build scripts, and unsellable/whiner flags never reach Player::build_list.
close_reason: world_save attaches SideBuildEntry chains onto SidesInfo and transfers via take_build_list; spawn_side_build_list no longer double-spawns initiallyBuilt

title: [Map] Live SidesList parse never attaches PlayerScriptsList to SidesInfo
description:
## C++
ParseSidesDataChunk (SidesList.cpp:265-282) always registers PlayerScriptsList, parses ScriptList::ParseScriptsDataChunk, and setScriptList on each SidesInfo. ScriptEngine::update (ScriptEngine.cpp:5555-5559) executes TheSidesList->getSideInfo(i)->getScriptList(). WorldHeightMap logical load registers SidesList::ParseSidesDataChunk (WorldHeightMap.cpp:495-496).

## Rust
system/map_loader.rs:759 uses parse_sides_data_chunk_without_scripts (sides_list.rs:675-680), which never registers PlayerScriptsList. Main fast path parse_runtime_sides_from_chunky stops after teams and never reads the child script chunk into SidesInfo. sync_legacy_sides_list_from_dicts does not set_script_list. GameInitializer::sync_side_scripts_to_script_engine (game_initialization.rs:1093-1136) then clear_script_lists and installs whatever is on SidesInfo (empty). Main load_map_scripts can feed ScriptEngine in parallel but never writes SidesInfo.scripts.

## Evidence
map_loader.rs:750-759 without_scripts. sides_list.rs:645-661 scripts only if parse_scripts=true. world_save.rs:2087-2103 no set_script_list.

## Player-visible effect
SidesInfo-backed consumers (skirmish script qualify, SidesList xfer of per-side scripts, GameEngine initialize_game script install) see empty lists. Combined with missing prepareForMP, campaign/skirmish map scripts do not land on the C++ ScriptEngine source of truth.
close_reason: map_loader uses parse_sides_data_chunk (PlayerScriptsList); live sync set_script_list from load_map_scripts_from_chunky

title: [Map] startNewGame never calls SidesList::prepareForMP_or_Skirmish
description:
## C++
GameLogic::startNewGame after TerrainLogic::loadMap (GameLogic.cpp:1289-1292) calls TheSidesList->prepareForMP_or_Skirmish() for multiplayer and skirmish. SidesList.cpp:446-529 copies map teams/sides into m_skirmishTeamrec/m_skirmishSides, removes every non-FactionCivilian map player, then if those saved sides have no scripts loads Data\\Scripts\\SkirmishScripts.scb (PlayerScriptsList + ScriptsPlayers + ScriptTeams) onto the skirmish sides.

## Rust
SidesList::prepare_for_mp_or_skirmish exists (sides_list.rs:334-416) but has zero callers. GameEngine start_new_game_now / GameInitializer::initialize_game never invoke it. Main host load_map (world_save.rs sync_legacy_sides_list_from_dicts) only reset+add_side/add_team. apply_skirmish_overrides (game_initialization.rs:751-753) returns immediately when get_num_skirmish_sides()==0.

## Evidence
rg 'prepare_for_mp_or_skirmish\(' only hits the definition in sides_list.rs. C++ call is GameLogic.cpp:1292.

## Player-visible effect
Official skirmish maps do not receive SkirmishScripts.scb AI/script teams. Lobby slots cannot replace map-authored players the C++ way; civilian-only keep plus slot rebuild never happens. apply_skirmish_overrides script qualify is dead.
close_reason: GameInitializer::prepare_sides_for_new_game and live map sync call SidesList::prepare_for_mp_or_skirmish for skirmish/MP/replay after map load

title: [Science] ScienceStore reset leaves map.ini science overrides in place
description:
## C++
ScienceStore::reset (Science.cpp 45-64) walks m_sciences and deleteOverrides(). Map.ini INI_LOAD_CREATE_OVERRIDES science blocks are popped; base Science.ini definitions remain. friend_parseScienceDefinition stacks overrides on Overridable (170-193).

## Rust
Live ScienceStore::reset (rts/science.rs 385-389) is a no-op. ingest_definition merges fields in place with no override chain. Next map keeps the previous map cost/prereq/grantable edits.

## Evidence
Science.cpp 45-64 and 170-193 vs science.rs 385-389 and 447-486. Comment: The Rust port does not use the Overridable pattern, so this is simplified.

## Player-visible effect
A map that overrides a science cost to 0 (unpurchasable) or changes PrerequisiteSciences permanently breaks that science for every subsequent map in the same session.
close_reason: science.rs ScienceStore stacks INI_LOAD_CREATE_OVERRIDES and reset() pops via deleteOverrides

title: [Science] Purchased science does not instantly ready required special powers
description:
## C++
`Player::addScience` (`Player.cpp` 2534-2538), used by `attemptToPurchaseScience` and rank grants: for every owned object's SpecialPowerModule whose `getRequiredScience() == science`, call `onSpecialPowerCreation()` then `setReadyFrame(TheGameLogic->getFrame())` — "instantly ready, because that is cool."

## Rust
Live purchase/grant path is GameLogic `science_management.rs` `add_science_impl` (306-375). It calls `on_special_power_creation()` only. That starts the recharge timer (`special_power_module.rs` 801-811). There is no `set_ready_frame(current_frame)`.

Common `Player::grant_science` is a HashSet insert with no SP walk at all (ControlBar queues into GameLogic, so Common is not the live purchase path).

## Evidence
`Player.cpp` 2534-2538 vs `science_management.rs` 349-355. `on_special_power_creation` starts recharge; C++ immediately overwrites ready frame to now.

## Player-visible effect
Buying a generals power (Spectre, A10, Paradrop, Anthrax Bomb, …) leaves that power on full cooldown instead of usable the same frame. Rank-granted SCIENCE_RankN unlocks that also gate an existing SP stay cooling down.
close_reason: science_management.rs add_science_impl calls set_ready_frame(current_frame) after on_special_power_creation

title: [RankInfo] RankInfoStore::reset does not restore base Rank.ini after map override
description:
## C++
`RankInfoStore::reset` (`RankInfo.cpp` 50-72) calls `deleteOverrides()` on each rank. Map.ini may only override existing ranks (`INI_LOAD_CREATE_OVERRIDES`, 111-137); reset restores SkillPointsNeeded / SciencesGranted / SciencePurchasePointsGranted from the base Rank.ini object.

## Rust
Live Common store is `ini_rank.rs` `RankInfoStore` (Player reads `get_rank_info_store()`). `reset()` only clears `is_override` flags (172-178); values stay overwritten. Override parse replaces the slot in place (244-253) instead of stacking.

## Evidence
`RankInfo.cpp` 50-72 and 111-137 vs `ini_rank.rs` 167-178 and 236-253. GameLogic `rank_info.rs` `reset()` is worse (clears all ranks) but Common Player does not use that store.

## Player-visible effect
A map that retunes SkillPointsNeeded or SciencesGranted leaves those thresholds/grants in effect for the rest of the session. Rank-up timing and rank-granted sciences (SCIENCE_RankN) stay wrong after leaving the map.
close_reason: ini_rank.rs + rank_info.rs stack map overrides; reset() restores base Rank.ini via deleteOverrides

title: [RankInfo] RankName skip parseAndTranslateLabel
description:
## C++
