`RankInfoStore::friend_parseRankDefinition` (`RankInfo.cpp` 104) uses `INI::parseAndTranslateLabel` for `RankName`. `getRankInfo(level)->m_rankName` is the localized rank title.

## Rust
`ini_rank.rs` `parse_rank_fields` stores RankName as the raw token (`SCIENCE:Rank1` / `RANK:Private`). Comment admits translation is skipped.

Live ControlBar (`impl_science.rs` 111) never reads RankInfo at all: `rank_title_label = format!("SCIENCE:Rank{}", rank_level)`. GameLogic `science_ui.rs` LevelUpNotification / RankProgress copies `rank_name` as-is.

## Evidence
`RankInfo.cpp` 104 vs `ini_rank.rs` 299-301. Unit test asserts `rank_name == "RANK:Private"` (untranslated).

## Player-visible effect
Rank-up banner and science-panel rank title stay as INI keys (`SCIENCE:Rank3`) instead of Private/Corporal/Sergeant (or the map-overridden translated name).
close_reason: ini_rank.rs RankName uses INI::translate_label (parseAndTranslateLabel)

title: [ControlBar] Purchase-science panel never binds PlayerTemplate Rank1/3/8 command sets
description:
## C++
`ControlBar::populatePurchaseScience` (`ControlBar.cpp` 143-174) reads `PlayerTemplate::getPurchaseScienceCommandSetRank1/3/8`, `findCommandSet`s each name, and fills `m_sciencePurchaseWindowsRank1/3/8` from those command buttons (enable/hide from prereqs, cost, disabled/hidden).

`PlayerTemplate.cpp` field table stores `PurchaseScienceCommandSetRank1/3/8` from INI.

## Rust
`PlayerTemplate` / `ini_player_template.rs` parse and store the three command-set names; GameLogic `from_common` copies them.

Live `ControlBar::populate_purchase_science` (`impl_science.rs` 94-117) only copies SPP/rank, synthesizes `SCIENCE:Rank{n}`, and **clears** `rank1/3/8_buttons`. It never calls `get_purchase_science_command_set_rank*` or `findCommandSet`.

## Evidence
`grep get_purchase_science_command_set` hits only template accessors + tests, never GameClient ControlBar. `populate_purchase_science` has no command-set lookup.

## Player-visible effect
Generals promotion panel never shows faction powers (Paladin, Spectre, Anthrax Bomb, etc.). Rank 1/3/8 purchase buttons stay empty even when the template names are loaded.
close_reason: impl_science.rs populate_purchase_science binds PlayerTemplate Rank1/3/8 command sets

title: [Science] DisplayName/Description skip parseAndTranslateLabel
description:
## C++
`ScienceStore::friend_parseScienceDefinition` (`Science.cpp` 147-153) uses `INI::parseAndTranslateLabel` for `DisplayName` and `Description`. `getNameAndDescription` returns the translated strings.

## Rust
Live INI path is `rts/science.rs` `parse_science_definition` / `ingest_science_file`: DisplayName and Description are stored as the raw INI token (`SCIENCE:PaladinTank`). No `INI::translate_label` / GameText fetch.

`control_bar_popup_description.rs` feeds `ScienceStore::get_name_and_description` straight into the tooltip name/body.

## Evidence
`Science.cpp` field parse table vs `science.rs` 737-758 and 906-911. PlayerTemplate DisplayName in the same crate *does* call `INI::translate_label`.

## Player-visible effect
Science purchase tooltips and UI labels show STR keys (`SCIENCE:PaladinTank`) instead of localized names/descriptions.
close_reason: science.rs DisplayName/Description use INI::translate_label (parseAndTranslateLabel)

title: [AIPlayer] Skirmish processBaseBuilding skips canMakeUnit NULL gate
description:
## C++
`AISkirmishPlayer::processBaseBuilding` (AISkirmishPlayer.cpp:199-221) requires a dozer, then `TheBuildAssistant->canMakeUnit(dozer, bldgPlan)`. `bldgPlan` is still NULL until a priority entry is chosen. `BuildAssistant::canMakeUnit` returns `CANMAKE_NO_PREREQ` when `whatToBuild == NULL` (BuildAssistant.cpp:1283-1284), so the automatic `isBuildable` assignment never runs. Automatic (non-priority) buildings are therefore only selected via the later power-plant override (223-228), not by walking the rest of the list.

## Rust
`AISkirmishPlayer::process_base_building` (skirmish_player.rs:909-938) skips `canMakeUnit` entirely. After `is_automatic_build` + `is_buildable` + dozer present, it assigns `selected_plan = cur_plan` on the first such entry.

## Evidence
C++ AISkirmishPlayer.cpp:199-228; BuildAssistant.cpp:1279-1284; Rust skirmish_player.rs:909-938.

## Player-visible effect
Rust skirmish AI auto-starts the first automatic/buildable structure (barracks, war factory, etc.) whenever a dozer exists. C++ waits for scripted priority builds or the under-power power-plant force.
close_reason: skirmish_player.rs process_base_building: keep findDozer/queueDozer for automatic entries, but do not assign selected_plan — matches C++ canMakeUnit(NULL)=CANMAKE_NO_PREREQ so only priority + power-plant override select

title: [AIPlayer] getMyEnemyPlayerIndex triggers acquireEnemy
description:
## C++
`AISkirmishPlayer::getMyEnemyPlayerIndex` (AISkirmishPlayer.cpp:444-456) returns `m_currentEnemy->getPlayerIndex()` if set, else the first human player index. It does not call `getAiEnemy` / `acquireEnemy`. Used by `buildAIBaseDefenseStructure` (no-center-waypoint fallback) and cluster-mine `computeSuperweaponTarget`.

## Rust
`get_my_enemy_player_index` (skirmish_player.rs:1533-1538) calls `self.get_ai_enemy()`, which every 5 seconds runs `acquire_enemy()` (556-561) and may replace `current_enemy` before returning the index.

## Evidence
C++ AISkirmishPlayer.cpp:444-456, 530-537, 605-608, 1134-1138; Rust skirmish_player.rs:555-561, 355-363, 614-624, 1533-1552.

## Player-visible effect
Placing a front defense without a SkirmCenter waypoint, or targeting cluster mines without a path waypoint, can retarget the skirmish AI's current enemy as a side effect and then aim at a different player than C++.
close_reason: skirmish_player.rs get_my_enemy_player_index: read current_enemy Weak directly; no get_ai_enemy/acquire_enemy side effect

title: [AIPlayer] Skirmish script wrappers call solo stubs for defense/building
description:
## C++
`AISkirmishPlayer` overrides `buildAIBaseDefense`, `buildAIBaseDefenseStructure`, and `buildSpecificAIBuilding` (AISkirmishPlayer.cpp:542-687, 391-437). `Player` / scripts call these virtually, so skirmish AI places front/flank defenses and marks existing build-list entries as priority.

## Rust
Live implementations exist as `AISkirmishPlayer::build_ai_base_defense`, `build_ai_base_defense_structure`, and `build_specific_ai_building` (skirmish_player.rs:213-456). The methods used by the live integration/script path do not call them:

- `AISkirmishPlayer::build_base_defense` (1846) → `self.base.build_ai_base_defense` (solo stub, impl_teams.rs:519)
- `build_base_defense_structure` (1850) → `self.base.build_ai_base_defense_structure` (solo stub)
- `build_specific_building` (1859) → `self.base.build_specific_ai_building` (solo stub, impl_teams.rs:537)

`IntegratedAiPlayer` (integration.rs:126-154) and script actions (`actions_skirmish.rs`, `player_command.rs`) use those wrappers. Solo stubs only log "Solo ai doesn't support …".

## Evidence
C++ AISkirmishPlayer.cpp:391-437, 542-687; Rust skirmish_player.rs:1846-1863; integration.rs:126-154; impl_teams.rs:518-540; GameLogic/src/scripting/executor/actions_skirmish.rs:16-17, 139-154.

## Player-visible effect
Skirmish scripts "Build base defense", "Build flank defense", "Build specific building", and Player::build_base_defense do nothing. C++ actually queues defenses on the approach circle and priority-builds listed structures.
close_reason: skirmish_player.rs build_base_defense/build_base_defense_structure/build_specific_building now call live AISkirmishPlayer impls instead of solo AIPlayer stubs

title: [AIPlayer] ctor ignores ScriptEngine global difficulty
description:
## C++
`AIPlayer::AIPlayer` sets `m_difficulty = TheScriptEngine->getGlobalDifficulty()` (AIPlayer.cpp:80). `checkForSupplyCenter` (179-188) uses `m_difficulty` to pick `AISideInfo` easy/normal/hard desired gatherers.

## Rust
`AIPlayer::new` hardcodes `difficulty: GameDifficulty::Normal` (impl_update.rs:63) and never reads ScriptEngine. `create_ai_player` / `insert_ai_player` (integration.rs:498-534) do not copy global or player difficulty. `check_for_supply_center` (impl_teams.rs:207-210) uses `self.difficulty`. `set_ai_player_difficulty` exists and game_initialization calls it, but any AI created outside that path (late `create_ai_player`, xfer ensure, tests of live ctor) stays Normal.

## Evidence
C++ AIPlayer.cpp:80, 166-195; Rust impl_update.rs:22-90; impl_teams.rs:176-230; integration.rs:498-534, 604-615.

## Player-visible effect
Until something explicitly calls `set_ai_player_difficulty`, Easy/Hard AI uses Normal harvester counts at each new supply center (typically 1 fewer or more trucks than the side's AIData easy/hard values).
close_reason: ai_player/impl_update.rs AIPlayer::new reads ScriptEngine get_global_difficulty() like C++ ctor; create/insert inherit via new()

title: [StealthUpgrade] TriggeredBy never parsed so upgrade never arms
description:
## C++
StealthUpgrade uses MAKE_STANDARD_MODULE_MACRO so UpgradeModuleData parses TriggeredBy/ConflictsWith. upgradeImplementation sets OBJECT_STATUS_CAN_STEALTH and giveSlavesStealthUpgrade when KINDOF_SPAWNS_ARE_THE_WEAPONS.

## Rust
Live object/upgrade/stealth_upgrade.rs ModuleData has only module_tag_name_key (no UpgradeMux/TriggeredBy). contain_module_overrides leftover.rs empty_upgrade_factories ignores INI (default()). upgrade_implementation itself matches C++ when called, but apply_upgrade ignores the mask and the module never matches an authored upgrade.

## Evidence
empty_upgrade_factories (leftover.rs:189-204) vs upgrade_factories which parse_from_ini. StealthUpgradeModuleData has no parse_from_ini / TriggeredBy field.

## Player-visible effect
Researching GLA Camouflage / other StealthUpgrade-triggered upgrades does not grant CAN_STEALTH on the GameLogic module path (host has a name-based Rebel residual only).
close_reason: StealthUpgradeModuleData parses TriggeredBy; leftover.rs upgrade_factories not empty

title: [StealthDetector] Detectors skip C++ random wake phase
description:
## C++
StealthDetectorUpdate.cpp:67-70 ctor: setWakeFrame(..., UPDATE_SLEEP(GameLogicRandomValue(1, data->m_updateRate))) so detectors do not all scan on the same frame.

## Rust
Live StealthDetectorUpdate::new sets next_call_frame_and_phase = 0 and never randomizes. Host stealth_mines.rs scans every detector whose next_detection_scan_frame is due; spawn typically leaves next=0 so the first scan is simultaneous.

## Evidence
C++ GameLogicRandomValue(1, m_updateRate) vs behavior/stealth_detector_update.rs:536 next_call_frame_and_phase: 0.

## Player-visible effect
All detectors ping IR/audio on the same frame after spawn, causing stacked discovery sounds and particle bursts.
close_reason: StealthDetectorUpdate::new GameLogicRandomValue(1, update_rate) set_wake_frame

title: [StealthDetector] Detected stealth never gets heat-vision second pass
description:
## C++
StealthDetectorUpdate.cpp:284-290: after markAsDetected, if drawable and not KINDOF_MINE, theirDraw->setSecondMaterialPassOpacity(1.0f) (heat vision). Mines are explicitly skipped.

## Rust
Live object/behavior/stealth_detector_update.rs::perform_detection_scan marks detected and may spawn IR grid, but never sets second-material-pass opacity. object/update leftover detector writes a drawable guard then drops it without setting opacity.

## Evidence
C++ 286-290 vs live perform_detection_scan (607-780) which has no set_second_material_pass_opacity / setSecondMaterialPassOpacity.

## Player-visible effect
Newly detected stealth units do not get the thermal overlay; they only flip DETECTED without the heat-vision pass (mines correctly stay without it only because nothing is applied).
close_reason: perform_detection_scan set_second_material_pass_opacity(1) after mark, skip mines

title: [StealthDetector] Contained detect ANDs garrisoned and transported flags
description:
## C++
StealthDetectorUpdate.cpp:139-161: if containedBy is garrisonable, require CanDetectWhileGarrisoned; else require CanDetectWhileTransported. One flag is enough for that container type.

## Rust
Live object/behavior/stealth_detector_update.rs:847-868: if contained_by exists, returns sleep unless BOTH can_detect_while_garrisoned AND can_detect_while_transported. Never inspects whether the container is garrisonable.

## Evidence
C++ if (contain->isGarrisonable()) { if (!m_canDetectWhileGarrisoned) sleep; } else if (!m_canDetectWhileTransported) sleep;
Rust: if contained { if !garrisoned { return sleep }; if !transported { return sleep } }.

## Player-visible effect
A Pathfinder in a Humvee (transported, CanDetectWhileContained=No typical) or a garrisoned detector cannot detect unless both INI flags are Yes; retail units with only one flag never detect while embarked.
close_reason: update_simple: garrisonable->CanDetectWhileGarrisoned else CanDetectWhileTransported

title: [ControlBar] StructureExit click does not emit MSG_EXIT for the clicked occupant
description:
## C++
`ControlBarCommandProcessing.cpp` `processCommandUI` GUI_COMMAND_EXIT_CONTAINER (657-695): scans `m_containData[i].control == control`, takes that `objectID`, `MSG_EXIT` with the occupant's ID.

## Rust
`impl_command_context.rs` `process_context_sensitive_button_click` looks up the clicked slot's `contain_data` only to *return* if empty, then `process_command("Command_StructureExit")` which `find`s the **first** button with that name. `host_request_from_button` / `DirectCommand` carries `selected_object_ids` (the building) and never `exit_object_id`. Fallback `execute_direct_command` runs `do_command_button` on selected objects (the container), not the occupant. Leftover `commands.rs` Exit also uses the selected building id.

## Evidence
C++ 666-693. Rust `impl_command_context.rs` 437-461 and 475-478; `host_command_bridge.rs` 562-589; `impl_execute.rs` 339-378.

## Player-visible effect
Clicking the 3rd garrison portrait does not eject that unit. At best the first occupant exits; on the host path the building itself is the command target and the slot occupant is dropped.
close_reason: impl_command_context.rs + host_command_bridge.rs + impl_execute.rs emit MSG_EXIT for clicked occupant

title: [ControlBar] doTransportInventoryUI leftover: structure rebuild wipes transport commands
description:
## C++
`ControlBarCommand.cpp` `populateCommand` (278-279) calls `doTransportInventoryUI` when `contain->isDisplayedOnControlBar()`. That helper only fills continuous `GUI_COMMAND_EXIT_CONTAINER` slots (hide overflow past `containMax - extraSlotsInUse`, disable empties, unmanned hide, portraits via populateInvDataCallback) and leaves every other CommandSet button in place. Garrisonable buildings *without* a CommandSet use a separate `CB_CONTEXT_STRUCTURE_INVENTORY` (`ControlBar.cpp` 1852-1865).

## Rust
`doTransportInventoryUI` / `populateInvDataCallback` are not ported. Live `add_object_commands` (Command context, including Humvee/Chinook) calls `append_structure_inventory_commands_with_presentation`, which `available_commands.clear()` and rebuilds slots 0-9 as StructureExit plus Stop/Evacuate at 10/11. `add_object_commands` also skips Evacuate from the CommandSet. Extra-slot occupancy is never subtracted.

## Evidence
C++ 124-241 and 278-279. Rust `impl_buttons.rs` 71-90; `control_bar_structure_inventory.rs` 54-63 and 99-164. Context switch: C++ isGarrisonable && empty command set vs Rust `impl_lifecycle.rs` 668-681 Command when a command set exists.

## Player-visible effect
Selecting a loaded transport replaces Move/Attack/etc. with a garrison-style 10-slot inventory. Multi-slot passengers do not hide extra cameos. Evacuate is missing from the original CommandSet path.
close_reason: control_bar_structure_inventory.rs do_transport_inventory_ui overlays EXIT slots without wiping CommandSet

title: [ControlBar] Inventory portraits leftover use template name instead of ButtonImage
description:
## C++
`ControlBarStructureInventory.cpp` `populateButtonProc` and `ControlBarCommand.cpp` `populateInvDataCallback` set each exit slot from `obj->getTemplate()->getButtonImage()` and `calculateVeterancyOverlayForObject`. Empty slots clear the overlay.

## Rust
hq-32v2 closed as ported, but leftover remains on the live path:
- `control_bar_structure_inventory.rs` `occupant_from_registry` sets `button_image: template_name` (e.g. AmericaInfantryRanger) instead of ThingTemplate `ButtonImage` / `get_button_image().get_name()`.
- Host/presentation path (`!used_registry`) pushes `StructureInventoryOccupant::default()` — empty image, no overlay — for each garrisoned count.
- Leftover `impl_portrait.rs` `sync_structure_context_from_presentation` still appends a generic nameless `Command_StructureExit` with no occupant portraits.

## Evidence
C++ StructureInventory 58-64; Command.cpp 94-106. Rust `control_bar_structure_inventory.rs` 70-78 and 178-203; `impl_portrait.rs` 633-644. Closed hq-32v2 is not actually fixed for art.

## Player-visible effect
Garrison/transport exit slots show missing or wrong cameos (template name is not a mapped image). Host-only presentation garrison shows blank slots plus Evacuate/Stop.
close_reason: occupant_from_registry uses ThingTemplate ButtonImage; leftover generic Exit stub removed

title: [ControlBar] empty multi-select common set falls back to first unit commands
description:
## C++
`ControlBarMultiSelect.cpp` `populateMultiSelect` / `addCommonCommands`: hide every command window, then intersect only `OK_FOR_MULTI_SELECT` slots. If a selected object has no CommandSet, the common set is cleared. No fallback to a single unit's full set.

## Rust
`impl_buttons.rs` `add_multi_select_commands` (98-147): after presentation-name intersect and OBJECT_REGISTRY intersect, `if context.available_commands.is_empty() { self.add_object_commands(context)?; }` which pushes the first selected object's full CommandSet (including non-OK_FOR_MULTI_SELECT build/sell/etc.).

## Evidence
C++ populateMultiSelect 198-205, addCommonCommands 64-85 and 107. Rust `impl_buttons.rs` 140-146.

## Player-visible effect
Selecting mixed units with no shared OK_FOR_MULTI_SELECT commands (or a missing CommandSet after a failed intersect) shows the first unit's private build/sell/specials as if the whole group could use them.
close_reason: impl_buttons.rs add_multi_select_commands no longer falls back to first unit CommandSet

title: [ControlBar] updateContextMultiSelect is a live no-op
description:
## C++
`ControlBarMultiSelect.cpp` `updateContextMultiSelect` (276-408): for every selected drawable (skipping KINDOF_IGNORED_IN_GUI), runs `getCommandAvailability` on each visible common-command window, applies hide/enable/NOT_READY/ALWAYS_COLOR and CHECK_LIKE, then *re-enables* a slot if `objectsThatCanDoCommand[i] > 0` (any selected unit can do it).

## Rust
Live `control_bar_impl/impl_contexts.rs` `update_context_multi_select` is `Ok(())`. `impl_lifecycle.rs` 165-168 calls it and **returns before** `refresh_button_states`, so multi-select never gets per-frame availability at all.

## Evidence
C++ 276-401. Rust `impl_contexts.rs` 8-10; `impl_lifecycle.rs` 165-168 vs 230-232.

## Player-visible effect
Mixed multi-select command buttons stay stuck at populate-time enabled. A group that includes one unit that can attack-move and several that cannot is never majority-enabled; MUST_BE_STOPPED / no-ammo / no-money never greys the shared buttons.
close_reason: impl_contexts.rs update_context_multi_select applies getCommandAvailability and any-can-do enable

title: [ControlBar] CommandSet populate flattens holes so buttons bind the wrong WND slots
description:
## C++
`ControlBarCommand.cpp` `populateCommand` and `ControlBarMultiSelect.cpp` `addCommonCommands` keep command *i* on `m_commandWindows[i]`. Empty CommandSet holes stay hidden in place (Sell stays on ButtonCommand14, AttackMove on its authored slot). `populateCommand` also hides SCRIPT_ONLY and NEED_SPECIAL_POWER_SCIENCE buttons the local player does not own, and copies upgraded general-power images/text from rank 1/3/8 purchase-science command sets.

## Rust
Live `impl_buttons.rs` `add_object_commands` and `control_bar_multi_select.rs` `push_common_slots` (plus `impl_portrait.rs` `sync_multi_select_command_sets_from_presentation`) `flatten()` / skip `None` slots into `available_commands`. `bind_command_windows` (`impl_execute.rs` 505-549) then maps `available_commands[i]` → `ControlBar.wnd:ButtonCommand{i+1}`. Science-gated hide / `copyImagesFrom` purchase-science art is not applied.

## Evidence
C++ populateCommand 283-456; addCommonCommands 98-171. Rust `impl_buttons.rs` 64-83; `control_bar_multi_select.rs` 173-188; `impl_execute.rs` 505-549.

## Player-visible effect
Command buttons slide left into earlier WND slots. Multi-select AttackMove/Stop appear on ButtonCommand01 instead of their CommandSet positions. Unowned general powers still show, and owned upgraded powers keep rank-1 art.
close_reason: impl_buttons.rs + control_bar_multi_select.rs keep CommandSet holes on WND slots

title: [ControlBar] getCommandAvailability leftover stubs most command gates and clocks
description:
## C++
`ControlBarCommand.cpp` `ControlBar::getCommandAvailability` (993-1516) gates script-disabled/unpowered, unmanned hide, single-use, MUST_BE_STOPPED, IGNORES_UNDERPOWERED, NEED_UPGRADE (player *and* object), NOT_QUEUEABLE when *any* production exists, then per-type: dozer construct (buildable/AI-only, pending dozer task, canBuild/canAfford), sell (script unsellable, subdued), unit build (queue max, canMake maxed/parking/money), player/object upgrade (already owned / in queue / science), FIRE_WEAPON clip reload inverse clock / NOT_READY, combat drop rappeller count, evacuate empty+subdued, railed dock closed, special-power ready clock + in-use + battle-plan ACTIVE, overcharge ACTIVE, switch-weapon ACTIVE, hack packing, strategy-center STOP OPTION_ONE.

## Rust
Live path is `control_bar_impl/impl_command_context.rs` `get_command_availability` (132-280), called from `update_context_command` and `refresh_button_states`. It handles a short disabled list (Sell/Evacuate/DoStop only), player NEED_UPGRADE, queue-max NOT_QUEUEABLE, then a handful of types and `_ => Available`. No unmanned/script hide, no MUST_BE_STOPPED, no object upgrades, no unit-build canMake, no fire-weapon/special-power clocks, Evacuate always Available, SpecialPower always Available. `force_disabled_evaluation` is hardcoded false. Leftover `commands.rs` `get_command_availability` is slightly broader but is not the live ControlBar update path.

## Evidence
C++ 1020-1514 vs Rust `impl_command_context.rs` 132-283. `refresh_button_states` (`impl_science.rs` 675-712) uses this stub for enablement.

## Player-visible effect
Build/upgrade/fire/special buttons stay enabled when they should be grey, hidden, or showing a reload/cooldown clock. Unmanned vehicles still show a full command set. Empty evacuate stays clickable.
close_reason: impl_command_context.rs get_command_availability gates unmanned/script/upgrade/evac/sell/unit-build

title: [ControlBar] updateContextCommand leftover skips inventory refresh, queue clock, and portrait swap
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/GUI/ControlBar/ControlBarCommand.cpp` `ControlBar::updateContextCommand` (678-890):
- if contain max > 0 and `getContainCount()` != `m_lastRecordedInventoryCount`, records the new count and calls `evaluateContextUI()` so transport inventory portraits rebuild the same frame
- shows `CP_BUILD_QUEUE` and `populateBuildQueue` when production starts; hides the queue and `setPortraitByObject(obj)` when the queue empties
- while the queue is visible, forces portrait off and draws `GadgetButtonDrawInverseClock` on `ButtonQueue01` from `getPercentComplete()`
- per visible command: `getCommandAvailability`, enable/hide/NOT_READY/ALWAYS_COLOR, veterancy overlay via `calculateVeterancyOverlayForThing`, CHECK_LIKE visual

## Rust
Live `control_bar_impl/impl_command_context.rs` `update_context_command` only optionally `populate_build_queue` and writes `button_states` from a stub `get_command_availability`. No contain-count → `evaluate_context_ui`. No `CP_BUILD_QUEUE` show/hide vs `setPortraitByObject`. No inverse clock on `ButtonQueue01`. No veterancy overlay on command buttons.

## Evidence
C++ 691-701, 713-786, 788-860. Rust `impl_command_context.rs` 4-125. Host path in `impl_lifecycle.rs` 192-193 even skips this update when OBJECT_REGISTRY is empty.

## Player-visible effect
Loading/unloading a transport does not refresh passenger cameos. A factory with a live queue still shows the building portrait instead of the queue clock, and build/special buttons never get chevrons or cooldown clocks from this update.
close_reason: impl_command_context.rs update_context_command refreshes inventory, queue clock, portrait swap

title: [Stealth] Black-market stealth uses template name not KINDOF_FS_BLACK_MARKET
description:
## C++
StealthUpdate.cpp:157-175 isBlackMarket: obj->isKindOf(KINDOF_FS_BLACK_MARKET) and not dead/under-construction/sold. allowedToStealth STEALTH_ONLY_WITH_BLACK_MARKET iterates the controlling player's objects with that callback.

## Rust
Live stealth_update.rs::check_black_market_available matches template_name.contains(\"blackmarket\"|\"black_market\"|\"black-market\") or (CashGenerator && name contains \"market\"). KindOf::FsBlackMarket exists but is unused here.

## Evidence
C++ isKindOf(KINDOF_FS_BLACK_MARKET) vs stealth_update.rs:951-960 name heuristics.

## Player-visible effect
Units with StealthForbiddenConditions = NO_BLACK_MARKET may fail to cloak next to a real GLA Black Market, or cloak from a misnamed market-like building.
close_reason: stealth_update.rs check_black_market_available uses KindOf::FsBlackMarket (C++ isBlackMarket)

title: [StealthDetector] IR pulse ignores stealthed-detector local-only gate
description:
## C++
StealthDetectorUpdate.cpp:338-397: IR ping/beacon particles and ping/loud-ping audio only if detector shroud <= PARTIAL_CLEAR AND (not STEALTHED OR controlling player is local). Stealthed detectors stay silent/invisible to enemies.

## Rust
Live object/behavior/stealth_detector_update.rs::update_simple only gates on shroud <= PartialClear (876-888). Missing the STEALTHED || local-player test. Host stealth_mines.rs detector scan has no IR pulse FX at all.

## Evidence
C++ 343: if (self->testStatus(STEALTHED)==FALSE || self->getControllingPlayer()==localPlayer). Rust is_visible is shroud-only.

## Player-visible effect
A stealthed Listening Outpost / Pathfinder still plays IR ping particles and sounds for enemy viewers, revealing the detector.
close_reason: IR pulse requires shroud<=PartialClear AND (!STEALTHED || local owner)

title: [Stealth] hintDetectableWhileUnstealthed never applied
description:
## C++
StealthUpdate.cpp:407-421 hintDetectableWhileUnstealthed: if local player owns the unit and status intersects HintDetectableConditions, drawable setSecondMaterialPassOpacity(1.0f). Called from update() when destalthing (751).

## Rust
Live StealthUpdateModuleData parses HintDetectableConditions into hint_detectable_states but update_stealth destalth path never calls any hint/second-pass. Leftover object/update has a stub comment only.

## Evidence
C++ destalth calls hintDetectableWhileUnstealthed(); live stealth_update.rs:400-408 only plays sound and clears STEALTHED.

## Player-visible effect
Local stealthed units that break cloak (attack/move) never get the heat-vision hint overlay while unstealthed.
close_reason: stealth_update.rs destalth calls hint_detectable_while_unstealthed + drawable set_second_material_pass_opacity

title: [Stealth] SPAWNS_ARE_THE_WEAPONS slaves do not share stealth
description:
## C++
StealthUpdate.cpp:253-266 allowedToStealth: if KINDOF_SPAWNS_ARE_THE_WEAPONS and spawn interface !areAllSlavesStealthed(), revealSlaves() and return FALSE so the master cannot stay cloaked.

## Rust
Live stealth_update.rs::allowed_to_stealth_runtime has no SPAWNS_ARE_THE_WEAPONS / are_all_slaves_stealthed / reveal_slaves check.

## Evidence
C++ lines 253-266 vs allowed_to_stealth_runtime (stealth_update.rs:716-888) which jumps from rider flags to attacking/ability/black-market/CAN_STEALTH.

## Player-visible effect
Overlord/Scorpion (and similar) can stay stealthed while a spawned slave is visible, or fail to reveal the whole pack when one slave is spotted.
close_reason: allowed_to_stealth_runtime: SPAWNS_ARE_THE_WEAPONS are_all_slaves_stealthed/reveal_slaves

title: [Tunnel] Occupant list is per-entrance cache not shared tracker
description:
## C++
`TunnelContain` / `CaveContain` redirect every list query to the shared `TunnelTracker`:
`getContainCount`, `getContainMax`, `getContainedItemsList`, `iterateContained` (`TunnelContain.cpp:243-263`, `CaveContain.cpp:176-192`).
Enter at A, select/evacuate at B sees the same communal list.

## Rust
Count/max go to the tracker, but `ContainModuleInterface::get_contained_objects` returns the per-module `contained_object_ids` cache (`tunnel_contain.rs:831-833`, `cave_contain.rs:936-938`). That cache is only updated on the entrance that performed add/remove.
Default `order_all_passengers_to_exit` / idle / hack iterate `get_contained_objects()` (`modules/contain.rs:276`).
Control bar inventory builds occupant buttons from `get_contained_objects()` (`control_bar_structure_inventory.rs:58-60`).

## Evidence
- C++ `TunnelContain.cpp:243-263`, `CaveContain.cpp:176-192`
- Rust `tunnel_contain.rs:103-104,153-155,831-833`, `cave_contain.rs:95-96,306-308,936-938`, `modules/contain.rs:276`, `control_bar_structure_inventory.rs:58-60`

## Player-visible effect
Enter tunnel/cave A and select allied entrance B: inventory is empty and Evacuate/Exit on B does nothing. Only the entrance that loaded the unit shows occupants.
close_reason: tunnel/cave get_contained_objects refresh from shared TunnelTracker so entrance B sees A's occupants

title: [Tunnel] Crate sell never dispatches onSelling so last tunnel cave-in-kills occupants
description:
## C++
`BuildAssistant` sell start (`BuildAssistant.cpp:1542-1547`) calls `contain->onSelling()`.
`TunnelContain::onSelling` (`TunnelContain.cpp:211-234`): if `friend_getTunnelCount()==1`, `removeAllContained(FALSE)` (eject, do not cave-in), then `onTunnelDestroyed` and `m_isCurrentlyRegistered=FALSE`.
Selling the last tunnel dumps occupants at the entrance like a bunker/palace instead of killing them.

## Rust
`ContainModuleInterface` has no `on_selling`. Crate `BuildAssistant::update` (`build_assistant.rs:445-489`) refunds and `destroy_object` without notifying contain.
`TunnelContain::on_selling` exists (`tunnel_contain.rs:452-481`) but has no crate caller. Destroy then hits `on_delete` → `on_tunnel_destroyed_id` while still registered and still occupied → last-tunnel cave-in destroys the shared pool.
Host residual `on_selling_container_residual` does last-tunnel eject; the crate live module path does not.

## Evidence
- C++ `BuildAssistant.cpp:1542-1547`, `TunnelContain.cpp:211-234`, `ContainModule.h:116`
- Rust `modules/contain.rs` (no on_selling), `build_assistant.rs:445-489`, `tunnel_contain.rs:452-481,576-596`

## Player-visible effect
Selling the last GLA Tunnel Network (crate/parity tick) kills everyone inside instead of ejecting them at the sold entrance.
close_reason: BuildAssistant::sell_object calls backend.on_selling; TunnelContain last-tunnel ejects instead of cave-in

title: [Cave] Live factory skips CreateInterface so CaveIndex and CaveSystem register never run
description:
## C++
`CaveContain` is a `CreateModuleInterface` (`CaveContain.h:56-58`).
- `onCreate` (`CaveContain.cpp:215-218`) copies INI `CaveIndex` into `m_caveIndex`.
- `onBuildComplete` (`CaveContain.cpp:221-233`) calls `TheCaveSystem->registerNewCave` then `onTunnelCreated`.
Map-placed and finished caves therefore join the indexed `TunnelTracker` network. `SET_CAVE_INDEX` / `tryToSetCaveIndex` can then switch networks.

## Rust
Live factory is `contain_module_overrides::ContainBindingModule` (`contain.rs:147-157`). It only `attach_contain_to_object` + `on_owner_created()`. It does **not** implement `get_create_interface`, so `on_create` / `on_build_complete` never run.
`CaveContain` does not override `on_owner_created` (trait default is a no-op). Constructor hardcodes `cave_index: 0` and never copies `module_data.cave_index_data`.
`CaveContain::on_create` / `on_build_complete` exist but are unreachable on the live path. Archival `module_overrides::CaveContainBindingModule` does wire CreateInterface; that factory is not the live one.

## Evidence
- C++ `CaveContain.cpp:215-233`, `CaveContain.h:56-90`
- Rust `contain_module_overrides/contain.rs:147-157,525-546` and `cave_contain.rs:112-123,551-580`

## Player-visible effect
Civilian/GLA caves never join a CaveSystem network. INI `CaveIndex` is ignored (every cave stays 0 and unregistered). Units cannot enter a shared cave, `SET_CAVE_INDEX` cannot rewire a never-registered entrance, and first-occupant capture cannot defect connected caves.
close_reason: CaveContain ctor copies CaveIndex; on_owner_created + live factory CreateInterface run onCreate/onBuildComplete register

title: [Tunnel] isValidContainerFor treats MaxTunnelCapacity 0 as unlimited
description:
## C++
`TunnelTracker::isValidContainerFor` (`TunnelTracker.cpp:132-150`): if not aircraft and `checkCapacity`, return `containCount < containMax` where `getContainMax()` is `TheGlobalData->m_maxTunnelCapacity` (default **0** in `GlobalData.cpp:834`).
`0 < 0` is false — an uninitialized or explicit-0 capacity admits nobody.

## Rust
Live `TunnelTracker::is_valid_container_for` (`tunnel_tracker.rs:74-77`): `contain_max <= 0 || count < contain_max`.
Fallback `max_capacity` defaults to **-1** when GlobalData is missing (`tunnel_tracker.rs:52,408-409`).
`ContainModuleInterface::get_max_capacity` for tunnels treats `max==0` as `usize::MAX` (`tunnel_contain.rs:843-849`).
Unit test comment claims C++ default 0 means unlimited — that is the opposite of C++.

## Evidence
- C++ `TunnelTracker.cpp:81-84,132-150`, `GlobalData.cpp:834`
- Rust `tunnel_tracker.rs:52,74-77,403-409`, `tunnel_contain.rs:843-849`

## Player-visible effect
If GameData has not applied `MaxTunnelCapacity` (or it is 0), C++ rejects every tunnel enter; Rust treats the network as unlimited. Control bar also treats 0 as infinite slots.
close_reason: TunnelTracker is_valid_container_for is containCount < containMax; 0 capacity admits nobody like C++

title: [Tunnel] loadPostProcess never unregisters occupants from partition
description:
## C++
`TunnelTracker::loadPostProcess` (`TunnelTracker.cpp:336-387`) resolves saved occupant IDs then for each:
`leaveGroup()`, `ThePartitionManager->unRegisterObject(obj)`, hide drawable, `pathfinder()->removeObjectFromPathfindMap(obj)`.
Occupants stay in the network but are not in the world partition until they exit.

## Rust
Live `TunnelTracker::load_post_process` (`GameLogic/src/tunnel_tracker.rs:545-588`) does `leave_group()`, pathfind obstacle remove, and hide drawable. It never unregisters from the partition manager.
`xfer_contain_list` is applied to `contained_ids`, but the objects remain partition-registered at their pre-save world positions.

## Evidence
- C++ `TunnelTracker.cpp:366-381`
- Rust `tunnel_tracker.rs:563-584`

## Player-visible effect
After loading a save with units in a tunnel/cave, those units remain clickable, collidable, and AI-visible on the map while also being treated as contained.
close_reason: TunnelTracker::load_post_process calls ThePartitionManager.unregister_object like C++ unRegisterObject

title: [Stealth] Disguise transition never swaps drawable on live update
description:
## C++
StealthUpdate.cpp:635-664 + changeVisualDisguise 960-1097: disguise_transition_frames decrement each update; at factor>=0.5 swap drawable via ThingFactory, bind, indicator color (night/day, ally vs enemy), DisguiseStarted/Revealed audio, FX, DISGUISED status/model, academy record, radar remove/add, forceRefreshSubObjectUpgradeStatus on reveal.

## Rust
Live stealth_update.rs::disguise_as_template sets disguise_transition_frames but update_stealth never decrements them or calls any visual swap. There is no change_visual_disguise on the live controller. Host object/stealth.rs ticks a residual opacity/template-name commit only (honesty: not full model/FX/radar).

## Evidence
Live update_stealth (330-422) has no disguise_transition_frames branch. disguise_as_template (441-466) only stores names/player index.

## Player-visible effect
Bomb trucks never morph into the target vehicle or restore their true model; disguise is a status bit without the halfway model swap.
close_reason: update_stealth ticks disguise_transition_frames; change_visual_disguise swaps drawable/status/FX/radar

title: [Stealth] xfer load never restores disguise visual
description:
## C++
StealthUpdate.cpp:1189-1203 loadPostProcess sets m_xferRestoreDisguise if isDisguised(). update() 572-589 then changeVisualDisguise() (preserving hidden-in-container) before normal stealth logic.

## Rust
Live StealthUpdateModule::load_post_process sets controller.xfer_restore_disguise = true when disguised, but update_stealth never reads that flag. Leftover object/update/stealth_update.rs:830-832 consumes it but is not factory-wired.

## Evidence
stealth_update.rs:1183-1190 sets the flag; update_stealth:330-422 never checks xfer_restore_disguise.

## Player-visible effect
Loading a save with a disguised bomb truck leaves the true model (or a broken drawable) instead of restoring the disguise appearance.
close_reason: update_stealth consumes xfer_restore_disguise via change_visual_disguise before enabled check

title: [Stealth] Mines never cloak or force zero opacity
description:
## C++
StealthUpdate.cpp:630-633: KINDOF_MINE every frame setEffectiveOpacity(0.0f, 0.0f) so mines stay fully hidden (no pulse). Mines also have InnateStealth StealthUpdate so OBJECT_STATUS_STEALTHED is set.

## Rust
Live stealth_update.rs::update_stealth has no KINDOF_MINE branch. Host world_scripts/stealth_mines.rs::place_mine_kind never sets stealthed / innate_stealth / CAN_STEALTH.

## Evidence
C++ mine special-case in update(); leftover object/update/stealth_update.rs:841-856 implements it but is unwired. Host place_mine_kind (stealth_mines.rs:1036-1044) only sets mine_data and strips weapons.

## Player-visible effect
Land mines and demo traps remain fully visible instead of staying invisible until a detector reveals them.
close_reason: update_drawable_visuals KINDOF_MINE set_effective_opacity(0,0) every frame

title: [Stealth] Live StealthUpdate never pulses drawable opacity
description:
## C++
StealthUpdate.cpp:667-670: every enabled frame (non-mine, no disguise transition) does draw->setEffectiveOpacity(0.5f + Sin(m_pulsePhase)*0.5f) and advances m_pulsePhase by 0.2.

## Rust
Live factory-wired stealth_update.rs::StealthController::update_stealth never touches drawable opacity or pulse_phase. pulse_phase is only xfer'd. Leftover object/update/stealth_update.rs:895-906 has the pulse but is not the registered module.

## Evidence
C++ update() drawable branch vs live update_stealth (stealth_update.rs:330-422) which only flips STEALTHED/DETECTED bits.

## Player-visible effect
Stealthed units do not shimmer between half and full opacity for the local/friendly viewer.
close_reason: update_drawable_visuals pulses 0.5+sin(phase)*0.5 and advances pulse_phase

title: [Weather] SnowTexture INI never binds; flakes drawn with the road atlas
description:
## C++
`WeatherSetting::m_snowTexture` default `EXSnowFlake.tga` (`Snow.h:40`), INI key `SnowTexture` (`Snow.cpp:85`).
`W3DSnowManager::ReAcquireResources` (`W3DSnow.cpp:118`) loads `Get_Texture(TheWeatherSetting->m_snowTexture.str())` and binds that texture when rendering point sprites or quads.

## Rust
`WeatherSetting.snow_texture` parses (`snow.rs:55`) and defaults to `EXSnowFlake.tga`.
`upload_snow_mesh` (`overlay_gpu.rs:623-647`) builds white quads (`color [1,1,1]`, `diffuse 0xc0ffffff`) and never samples `settings.snow_texture`.
`record_overlay_draws` (`overlay_gpu.rs:798-825`) draws `snow_mesh` with `road_pipeline` + `road_texture_bind_group` — the road atlas, not the flake TGA.
hq-huzx closed flake *positions*; texture bind was not in that fix.

## Evidence
Grep of `GameClient/src/terrain` for `snow_texture` / `EXSnowFlake` only hits the INI struct, not a GPU bind.

## Player-visible effect
Enabled snow is a grid of road-textured (or solid) quads, not EXSnowFlake / map-overridden flake art.
close_reason: Snow flakes bind WeatherSetting.snow_texture (EXSnowFlake.tga) via a dedicated overlay bind group instead of the road atlas.

title: [Weather] Live snow INI store is not the one GameLogic reset/override clears
description:
## C++
Single `TheWeatherSetting` (`Snow.cpp:80`). `INI::parseWeatherDefinition` (`Snow.cpp:102-130`): create, or CREATE_OVERRIDES copy+chain, else throw. Always `TheSnowManager->updateIniSettings()`.
`GameLogic::reset` does `TheWeatherSetting = ws->deleteOverrides()` so the next map drops map Weather.
`W3DSnowManager::render` (`W3DSnow.cpp:312`) requires `m_snowEnabled && m_isVisible`.

## Rust
Two stores:
1. `common/ini/ini_weather.rs` — registered as the default `Weather` block (`ini.rs:928-929`). Preload `Data/INI/Default/Weather.ini` + `Weather.ini` (`boot.rs:810-871`) writes here. `clear_weather_setting_overrides` only clears this chain.
2. `GameClient/src/snow.rs` — `register_weather_definition_parser` (`impl_init.rs:510`) replaces the Weather parser after preload. Live `overlay_gpu.rs:594-596` gates flakes on this store's `snow_enabled`.
GameClient parse (`snow.rs:103-135`) has no override chain; CreateOverrides just patches the existing GameClient object. `GameLogic::reset` (`impl_init.rs:196-197`) only calls `ini_weather::clear_weather_setting_overrides()`, never the GameClient store.
`initialize_snow_manager` (`impl_init.rs:613`) runs after preload, so `update_ini_settings` reads the still-default GameClient object.

## Evidence
hq-0t9z closed script `setVisible` vs SnowEnabled (different). Grep: reset touches Common only; overlay imports `crate::snow::get_weather_setting`.

## Player-visible effect
A snowy map.ini (`SnowEnabled=Yes`) turns snow on. Leaving that map / GameLogic::reset does not restore Weather.ini defaults, so the next non-snow map still snows. Global Weather.ini emitter keys parsed at boot never reach SnowManager.
close_reason: Single TheWeatherSetting store: GameClient Weather parser delegates to Common override chain; get_weather_setting reads the final override; GameLogic reset deleteOverrides restores Weather.ini.

title: [Water] Map WaterTransparency override skips copy, skybox replace, texture reload
description:
## C++
`INI::parseWaterTransparencyDefinition` (`INIWater.cpp:65-117`): first load constructs; `INI_LOAD_CREATE_OVERRIDES` copies the current setting, marks override, parses onto the copy; otherwise throws.
On CREATE_OVERRIDES it then calls `TheTerrainVisual->replaceSkyboxTextures(old,new)` for the five SkyboxTexture* faces.
After map load, `W3DTerrainVisual` calls `WaterRenderObjClass::updateMapOverrides` (`W3DWater.cpp:1110-1116`) to reload `m_riverTexture` if `StandingWaterTexture` changed.

## Rust
`parse_water_transparency_block` (`ini.rs:620-637`) on CreateOverrides builds `WaterTransparencySetting::new()` (ctor defaults, not a copy of the global Water.ini values), applies only keys present in the block, and `set_next_override`. No `replace_skybox_textures`. No `updateMapOverrides`.
`ensure_water_ini_skybox_faces_loaded` (`impl_world.rs:986-989`) returns early if any face is already bound. `water_texture_name_candidates` reads the final override only when the bind group is first created.
A parallel `script_loader` line-scan can hint skybox names only if all five SkyboxTexture* keys are present in map.ini.

## Evidence
Map.ini is loaded with `INILoadType::CreateOverrides` (`game_initialization.rs:358-361`). Parse path never calls `TerrainVisualImpl::replace_skybox_textures`.

## Player-visible effect
Partial map WaterTransparency blocks reset unspecified keys (texture/depth/color) to Water.h defaults. Custom map skybox faces and StandingWaterTexture often stay on the previous/global bind.
close_reason: WaterTransparency CreateOverrides copies the live base (not ctor defaults), queues replaceSkyboxTextures, and updateMapOverrides reloads StandingWaterTexture.

title: [Water] StandingWaterColor and AdditiveBlending never tint or blend water
description:
## C++
`WaterTransparencySetting` parse table (`Water.cpp:38-55`) includes StandingWaterColor (`INI::parseRGBColor`, stored 0-1 via /255) and AdditiveBlending.
`W3DWater.cpp` uses both on the live path:
- `m_standingWaterColor` tints river/trapezoid/flat water (`:2729-2734`, `:3078-3083`). RGB (1,1,1) keeps legacy lighting; any other value replaces vertex shade.
- `m_additiveBlend` selects `_PresetAdditiveShader` vs `_PresetAlphaShader` (`:174-178`, `:2927-2931`) and tweaks SRCBLEND on the JBA river pass.

## Rust
Keys parse into `WaterTransparencySetting` (`ini_water.rs:673-681`). Live plane/rivers never read `standing_water_color` or `additive_blending`.
`compute_standing_water_diffuse` (`w3d_overlay_mesh.rs:286-330`) implements the C++ tint but is test-only. `sync_global_water_plane` passes `0xffff_ffff`. `water.wgsl` always mixes albedo + Fresnel with alpha clamp.
Labelled `StandingWaterColor = R:255 G:255 B:255` is stored as (255,255,255) not C++ (1,1,1), so even if wired the 1.0 legacy-lighting branch would miss.

## Evidence
Grep of `GameClient/src/terrain` for `standing_water_color` / `additive_blend` is empty except the unused helper + INI struct.

## Player-visible effect
Maps that override water dye (green/brown/black water) or AdditiveBlending=Yes keep default teal/alpha water. No glow, no INI tint.
close_reason: StandingWaterColor parseRGBColor is 0-1; live plane uses compute_standing_water_diffuse and AdditiveBlending selects the additive wgpu pipeline.

title: [Water] WaterSet INI plane keys never reach the live water plane
description:
## C++
`INI::parseWaterSettingDefinition` (`INIWater.cpp:25-61`) matches the `WaterSet` name against `TimeOfDayNames[]` (`GameType.cpp`: NONE, MORNING, AFTERNOON, EVENING, NIGHT) and writes `WaterSettings[timeOfDayIndex]`.
`WaterSetting::m_waterSettingFieldParseTable` (`Water.cpp:17-35`) parses SkyTexture, WaterTexture, Vertex00/10/01/11Color, DiffuseColor, TransparentDiffuseColor, UScrollPerMS, VScrollPerMS, SkyTexelsPerUnit, WaterRepeatCount.
`WaterRenderObjClass::loadSetting` (`W3DWater.cpp:1339-1393`) copies those fields (textures, repeat, UV scroll, packed vertex/diffuse colors) into the renderer for TIME_OF_DAY_MORNING..NIGHT. Draw uses `m_settings[m_tod]`.

## Rust
Live `WaterSet` parser (`common/ini/ini.rs:605-617` → `IniWater::parse_water_setting_block`) stores into `ini_water::WATER_SETTINGS`.
`TIME_OF_DAY_NAMES` is Morning/Noon/Afternoon/Evening/Night (no NONE; extra Noon), so `WaterSet MORNING` lands at index 0. C++ `TIME_OF_DAY_MORNING` is 1.
`get_water_setting` has no GameClient/Device consumer. `TerrainVisualImpl::sync_global_water_plane` (`impl_gpu.rs:1631-1632`) bakes tiles with hardcoded `0xffff_ffff`. `compute_standing_water_diffuse` exists only in tests. `GameClient/src/water.rs` re-exports invented `terrain::water` `WaterManager`, not `Water.cpp`. Device `Water/water_config.rs` is an unused duplicate.

## Evidence
Retail test block uses `WaterSet MORNING` (`Common/tests/water_ini.rs`). Grep of `GameClient/src/terrain` for `get_water_setting` / `u_scroll` / `WaterRepeatCount` is empty.

## Player-visible effect
Water.ini TOD tints, UV scroll, repeat, and sky/water textures never change the standing plane. Morning/noon/night water looks identical; map WaterSet overrides do nothing.
close_reason: WaterSet names match C++ TimeOfDayNames (NONE/MORNING/AFTERNOON/EVENING/NIGHT); loadSetting fields (diffuse, UV scroll, repeat, WaterTexture) feed sync_global_water_plane.

title: [Campaign] gotoNextMission leaves last mission current so End Campaign never fires
description:
## C++
`CampaignManager::gotoNextMission` (CampaignManager.cpp:246-252) always assigns `m_currentMission = m_currentCampaign->getNextMission(m_currentMission)`. `Campaign::getNextMission` returns NULL when `m_nextMission` is empty or not found (lines 168-192). After the last authored mission, `getCurrentMap()` is therefore the empty string.

`ScoreScreen.cpp` `finishSinglePlayerInit` (787-873) calls `gotoNextMission()` then `if (TheCampaignManager->getCurrentMap().isEmpty())`: sets Continue to `GUI:EndCampaign`, writes USA/China/GLA/Challenge battle honors, hides score chrome, and plays `FinalVictoryMovie`.

## Rust
`CampaignManager::goto_next_mission` (`GameClient/src/gui/campaign_manager.rs:290-315`) returns `None` when `next_mission` is empty or missing **without clearing** `current_mission`. The unit test (`test_goto_next_mission`, lines 843-845) asserts the last mission stays current.

`score_screen.rs` `finish_single_player_init` (594-675) copies the C++ empty-map gate: `goto_next_mission()` then `get_current_map()`. Because the last map is still current, the gate never fires.

## Evidence
C++: `m_currentMission = getNextMission(...)` even when that is NULL.
Rust: `if next_name.is_empty() { return None; }` — `self.current_mission` unchanged.
Live caller: `GeneralsRust/.../callbacks/score_screen.rs:594-675` vs `ScoreScreen.cpp:787-873`.

## Player-visible effect
Beating the last USA/China/GLA (or last Challenge) mission shows Save and Continue instead of End Campaign, never awards campaign/challenge honors, never plays the final victory movie, and Continue replays the last map.
close_reason: goto_next_mission always assigns current_mission including None so get_current_map is empty and End Campaign fires.

title: [Campaign] CampaignManager xfer v5 omits live ChallengeGenerals and full ChallengeGameInfo
description:
## C++
`CampaignManager::xfer` (CampaignManager.cpp:403-475), version 5:
- v3: `xferUser(&m_difficulty, sizeof(m_difficulty))` — MSVC `GameDifficulty` is a 4-byte enum.
- v4: `xferBool(isChallengeCampaign)` then, if true, allocate/init `TheChallengeGameInfo` and `xferSnapshot(TheChallengeGameInfo)`. `SkirmishGameInfo::xfer` (GameInfo.cpp:1488-1588) writes preorder/crc/inGame/slots (MAX_SLOTS state/name/accept/mute/color/start/template/team/originals), localIP, map name/CRC/size/mask, seed, superweapon restriction, starting cash.
- v5: `playerTemplateNum = TheChallengeGenerals->getCurrentPlayerTemplateNum(); xferInt(&playerTemplateNum);` then store into `m_xferChallengeGeneralsPlayerTemplateNum`. Save always reads the **live** singleton.
`loadPostProcess` writes that number back onto `TheChallengeGenerals` (477-486). ScoreScreen Continue / Play Again uses `TheChallengeGenerals->getCurrentPlayerTemplateNum()`.

## Rust
`CampaignManager::xfer` (`gui/campaign_manager.rs:548-598`) and GameLogic `xfer_campaign.rs`:
- v3 CHUNK_Campaign path: `xfer_user(&mut self.difficulty)` uses `size_of::<GameDifficulty>()` (fieldless enum, 1 byte, no `repr`). GameLogic chunk instead `xfer_int`s an i32. The two campaign snapshots in one save disagree; C++ files misalign after difficulty.
- v4: only `challenge_map` + `challenge_template` via `snapshot_map_and_template` / `restore_map_and_template` — not `SkirmishGameInfo::xfer`.
- v5: xfers `self.xfer_challenge_generals_player_template_num`. ChallengeMenu (`challenge_menu.rs:341-347`) sets `ChallengeGenerals::set_current_player_template_num` and `set_campaign` but **never** `set_xfer_challenge_generals_player_template_num`. Capture/apply hooks use the stored 0. `apply_logic_chunk_state` does not call `load_post_process`.

Not a refile of closed `hq-oyne` (dummy snapshot discarded). Live hooks exist; the payload is still wrong.

## Evidence
C++ CampaignManager.cpp:427-473 and GameInfo.cpp:1488-1588.
Rust campaign_manager.rs:503-540, 548-598; xfer_campaign.rs:21-30; challenge_menu.rs:341-347; subsystems.rs:139-143 (`size_of::<T>()`); score_screen.rs:308-312 fallback to the stored field.

## Player-visible effect
Challenge mid-mission saves drop slot list, seed, map CRC, cash, and the selected General. After load, Continue/Play Again binds player template 0 instead of the chosen General. CHUNK_Campaign difficulty encoding also disagrees with C++ and with the GameLogic campaign chunk.
close_reason: Campaign xfer v5: 4-byte GameDifficulty, full SkirmishGameInfo snapshot for ChallengeGameInfo, live ChallengeGenerals template, load_post_process on apply.

title: [Campaign] setCampaignAndMission leaves stale mission when name is missing
description:
## C++
`CampaignManager::setCampaignAndMission` (CampaignManager.cpp:256-277): empty mission name falls through to `setCampaign`. If the campaign is found, it always does `m_currentCampaign = camp; m_currentMission = camp->getMission(mission);`. `getMission` returns NULL for an unknown/empty-after-lookup name (149-164), so current mission is cleared.

## Rust
`set_campaign_and_mission` (`GameClient/src/gui/campaign_manager.rs:319-341`) sets `current_campaign` when the campaign name matches, then searches missions. If no mission matches it `return`s and **leaves `current_mission` at the previous index**. `xfer` load and `apply_logic_chunk_state` both call this after reading saved names (572-573, 525).

## Evidence
C++: `m_currentMission = camp->getMission(mission); return;` (NULL if missing).
Rust: `self.current_campaign = Some(camp_idx);` then on miss `return;` with old `current_mission`.
Callers: `CampaignManager::xfer`, `apply_logic_chunk_state`, load-screen/test `set_campaign_and_mission`.

## Player-visible effect
Loading a campaign/mission save whose mission name is missing from the loaded Campaign.ini (or a set to a bad mission name) keeps the previous mission index. That can start the wrong map, or a mission from the newly selected campaign at the old index, instead of having no current mission like C++.
close_reason: set_campaign_and_mission clears current_mission when the mission name is missing, matching C++ getMission NULL.
