title: [SP] Academy specialPowersUsed never fed by live fire — War School always says TryUsingSuperweapons
description:
## C++
SpecialPowerModule::initiateIntentToDoSpecialPower (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/SpecialPower/SpecialPowerModule.cpp:434) unconditionally calls getObject()->getControllingPlayer()->getAcademyStats()->recordSpecialPowerUsed(m_specialPowerTemplate). AcademyStats::recordSpecialPowerUsed (AcademyStats.cpp:460-466) increments m_specialPowersUsed only when getAcademyClassificationType()==ACT_SUPERPOWER. evaluateTier1Advice (AcademyStats.cpp:572-577) keeps tip 7 ('did player ever use a generals power or superweapon?') available while m_specialPowersUsed==0; the counter is also Xfer'd (:1134).

## Leftover (right)
GameLogic/src/object/special_power_module.rs initiate_intent_to_do_special_power (:436-459) maps template AcademyClassificationType::Superweapon -> Superpower and calls player.get_academy_stats_mut().record_special_power_used(classification) (gate fixed by closed hq-g80a). player/academy_score.rs:164-169 increments special_powers_used; calculate_academy_advice (:234-236) emits ACADEMY:TryUsingSuperweapons while special_powers_used == 0.

## Live (wrong)
Live host fires never run the leftover module (empty dual-world): command_executor/special_power.rs dispatch and world_scripts/special_power_strikes.rs queue_special_power_strike (:306-355) record EVA / script notify / view object / audio but never academy stats — record_special_power_used has zero call sites in Main (grep). The War School bridge leftover_academy_from_live_notify (GameClient/gui/callbacks/score_screen.rs:1331-1334) -> AcademyStats::apply_live_notify_snapshot (academy_score.rs:195-215, closed hq-nh8k1) carries only researched_radar / generals_points_spent / upgrades_purchased / chose_a_strategy; special_powers_used is absent, so it stays 0 for the whole live match.

## Player-visible
Fire any ACT_SUPERPOWER power (Nuke / PUC / ScudStorm / A10 / Carpet / MOAB ...): the score screen War School still advises ACADEMY:TryUsingSuperweapons, and the tip chain never advances past it to ClearBuildings / UseTunnelNetwork / PickStrategyCenterPlan / PickUpSalvage in any live game.

## Not a duplicate
hq-g80a (closed) fixed the leftover classification gate only; hq-nh8k1 (closed) fed advice from the live-notify snapshot but that snapshot has no special-power counter. No open bead covers feeding this stat from live fire.
acceptance_criteria:
- Live special-power fire (superweapon strike queue path and generals-power activate_* paths) records special_powers_used on the controlling player with the C++ ACT_SUPERPOWER classification gate.
- After firing an ACT_SUPERPOWER power in a live match, War School no longer suggests ACADEMY:TryUsingSuperweapons and the chain can advance to later tips.
close_reason: Live queue_special_power_strike now increments host Player.special_powers_used and leftover AcademyStats::recordSpecialPowerUsed (ACT_SUPERPOWER). War School leftover_academy_from_live_notify clones that leftover counter so TryUsingSuperweapons retires after a live superweapon fire.

title: [EMP] Patriot intended-victim near-miss fallback never disables
description:
## C++
`EMPUpdate::doDisableAttack` end-of-function edge case (EMPUpdate.cpp:322-345): when the producer's current AI victim is an AIRCRAFT, was NOT processed by the radius loop (blast missed / victim moved during StartFadeTime), and is not EMP_HARDENED, it is still `setDisabledUntil(DISABLED_EMP, now + DisabledDuration)` when `lengthSqr <= radius*2.0f || lengthSqr <= 40.0f*40.0f` (C++ compares a squared length against radius*2 — faithful quirk).

## Leftover (right)
`emp_update.rs:542-557` ports the same fallback: `intended_victim_id` + `!intended_victim_processed` + `dist_sqr <= radius * 2.0 || dist_sqr <= 40.0 * 40.0` -> `set_disabled_until(DisabledEmp, ...)` for a non-hardened aircraft victim.

## Live (wrong)
SupW Patriot residual `apply_supw_patriot_emp_residual_at` (`world_combat/strategy_center.rs:1286-1392`) reads `intended_target` only for the Patch-1.01 `emp_skip_ground_when_airborne_only` gate (closed hq-5fdpj); after the radius loop there is no near-miss fallback disable. The superweapon spheroid path `apply_emp_pulse_disable_field_at` (`world_combat/drones_and_garrison.rs:2676+`) also has no producer-victim logic, but its OCL bomb producer has no AI victim in retail, so this is patriot-path only.

## Player-visible
A jet that slides just outside the 200-radius EMP blast still freezes for the full 30000 ms DisabledDuration in retail; on live it flies away untouched.
close_reason: Live host: Patriot intended-victim near-miss DISABLED_EMP; Spectre orbit acquire gates isFairDistanceFromShip (0.75x orbit).

title: [Spectre] Orbit acquire skips isFairDistanceFromShip — gattling hits targets under the gunship
description:
## C++
`SpectreGunshipUpdate::isFairDistanceFromShip` (SpectreGunshipUpdate.cpp:768-789) returns TRUE only when the target's 2D distance from the gunship's **current position** exceeds `GunshipOrbitRadius * 0.75` (retail 250 -> 187.5). Both acquire passes in `update` require it: the reticle pick and the AI-wide pick (update :519-556, target loop `isFairDistanceFromShip(theEnemy)`). A too-close target is skipped, so `m_positionToShootAt` stays the reticle and the gattling only `aiAttackPosition`s the ground.

## Leftover (right)
`spectre_gunship_update.rs:586-601` `is_fair_distance_from_ship` (ship pos vs target 2D > `gunship_orbit_radius * 0.75`), enforced at `:713-715` inside `find_target_in_radius` before the nearest-sort, for both reticle and wide-acquire callers.

## Live (wrong)
`plan_due_orbit_ticks` (`special_power_strikes/registry_fields.rs:513-640`) picks nearest-in-reticle (r25) then AI-wide (r200) via `pick_nearest_residual_target_xz` with no gunship-distance gate. `spectre_orbit_filtered_positions` / `spectre_orbit_target_allowed_by_id` (`world_scripts/special_power_strikes.rs:1389-1470`) filter only stealth/fog/neutral/air (closed hq-by6wm). `HostSpectreOrbitField` never stores the gunship's live position, so the 0.75x-orbit filter cannot run anywhere on live.

## Player-visible
Steering the reticle onto an enemy the orbiting gunship is passing over (or the AI wide-acquire picking one) damages/kills it on live; retail withholds gattling fire there (ground-position shot only, howitzer keeps walking to the aim point).
close_reason: Live host: Patriot intended-victim near-miss DISABLED_EMP; Spectre orbit acquire gates isFairDistanceFromShip (0.75x orbit).

title: [Phys/Bounce] Motion-step bounce only rights flipped bodies — tilted wrecks keep tilt through bounces
description:
LEFTOVER (C++ port, RIGHT): object/behavior/physics_bounce.rs handle_bounce — on every ALLOW_BOUNCE ground contact with vz<0 it rights the body: yaw = obj orientation, pitch_angle = 0, roll_angle = 0 (or PI if currently flipped via up vector); then physics_update.rs update_simple does `if bounce_force.is_some() { state.pitch_angle = 0.0; state.roll_angle = 0.0; }` so any body that produced a bounce force ends the frame upright (yaw preserved).

C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/PhysicsUpdate.cpp:503-514 — handleBounce vz<0 branch does setAngles(yawAngle, pitchAngle=0, rollAngle = zvec.Z>0 ? 0 : PI) on EVERY bounce contact; and 785-796 — `if (gotBounceForce)` rights the object again with setAngles(yawAngle, 0.0f, 0.0f) and re-stamps the transform. So retail rights pitch+roll to zero at each ground bounce, flipped or not.

LIVE (contradicts): Main/src/game_logic/object/physics_motion.rs compute_ground_bounce_force (~686-696, the non-stunned motion-step path used by slow-death falling wrecks — death.rs:357 sets shock_allow_bounce=true — and INI AllowBounce=Yes bodies) only rights when `physics_transform_up_y() < 0.0` (flipped); a tilted-but-upright body (e.g. nose-down 45° tumble) only gets its pitch/roll RATES zeroed and keeps the tilt frozen through every bounce. The stunned-path twin handle_shock_ground_bounce (physics_motion.rs:903-934) rights unconditionally via right_physics_pitch_roll — correct — so the divergence is specific to the motion-step path.

Observable: tumbling dead vehicles/debris in live land at an angle and stay tilted while bouncing/settling; retail rights them upright at first ground contact.

Acceptance: compute_ground_bounce_force rights pitch/roll (yaw-only transform) on every ground-bounce contact with vy<0, matching leftover handle_bounce + end-of-update righting (kill test for stunned units must still run before righting); leftover crate not edited; playable_claim stays false.
close_reason: compute_ground_bounce_force now first-rights leftover handleBounce (pitch=0, roll=0 or PI from up) on every vy<0 contact so tilted wrecks stand up; tick_physics_motion_step then setAngles(yaw,0,0) after test_stunned_unit_for_destruction so flip-kill still runs first. Leftover crate not edited.

title: [Phys/Bounce] OCL debris never bounce — live CreateDebris spawn omits setAllowBouncing(true)
description:
LEFTOVER (C++ port, RIGHT): GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object_creation_list/nuggets.rs:750-754 — CreateDebris SEND_IT_FLYING|SEND_IT_UP|RANDOM_FORCE nugget applies physics like C++: set_extra_bounciness(m_extraBounciness), set_extra_friction(m_extraFriction), set_allow_bouncing(true), set_bounce_sound(m_bounceSound). With ALLOW_BOUNCE set the leftover PhysicsBehavior bounce path runs (object/behavior/physics_bounce.rs handle_bounce + physics_update.rs update_simple): every ground contact with vz<0 gives bounce force = mass*|vz|*GroundStiffness(0.8), YPR damping 0.7, righting, repeated until settle — debris skip on the ground.

C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/ObjectCreationList.cpp:1121-1124 — objUp->setExtraBounciness(m_extraBounciness); objUp->setExtraFriction(m_extraFriction); objUp->setAllowBouncing(true); objUp->setBounceSound(&m_bounceSound); then handleBounce (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:481-531) drives the skips.

LIVE (leftover unreachable): Main/src/game_logic/world_combat/infantry_weapons.rs spawn_ocl_create_debris (~575-589) sets velocity, orientation nudge, set_extra_friction and set_bounce_sound but never set_allow_bouncing(true) (nor extra bounciness). Debris templates are ad-hoc ThingTemplate::new with allow_bouncing default false (game_logic/thing.rs:2033), and world_combat/ocl_and_scud.rs:238-242 (generic CreateObject path; comment cites ObjectCreationList.cpp:1086/1122/1124) also omits the 1123 setAllowBouncing(true). Object::set_allow_bouncing (object/physics_motion.rs:665) has no live caller outside tests. Net: live OCL debris take one ground-slam clamp and stop — leftover handle_bounce never fires for debris, so debris never bounce in live.

Acceptance: live CreateDebris + generic OCL spawn paths enable allow_bounce (and stamp extra bounciness) so debris bounce through the existing live bounce force path (compute_ground_bounce_force) until settle, matching leftover/C++; leftover crate not edited; playable_claim stays false.
close_reason: CreateDebris spawn enables allow_bounce + extra_bounciness on SEND_IT_FLYING|SEND_IT_UP|RANDOM_FORCE (ObjectCreationList.cpp:1121-1123). Generic OCL path stamps the same when those dispositions apply. Debris now enter compute_ground_bounce_force until settle.

title: [FX] Ricochet without secondary drops the object transform
description:
## C++
`ParticleSystemFXNugget::doFXObj` (`FXList.cpp:514-534`):
`if (m_ricochet && secondary) { aimingMatrix from attacker→victim; reallyDoFX(..., &aimingMatrix, ...) } else reallyDoFX(..., primary->getTransformMatrix(), ...)`.
Ricochet with no secondary still uses the primary object transform (offsets follow facing; OrientToObject still applies).

## Live
`ParticleSystemWrapper::do_fx_obj` / `do_fx_obj_host` (`fx_list.rs:1589-1647`):
`let mtx = if self.nugget.ricochet { secondary.map(|s| aiming_z_rot) } else { Some(primary_transform) };`
When `Ricochet=Yes` and secondary is None, `mtx` is None. `really_do_fx` then leaves authored Offset unrotated and skips `orient_to_object` `set_local_transform`.

## Player-visible
Ricochet-authored particle FX invoked via doFXObj without a secondary (death/transition/scripted object FX that omit the dealer) spawn unrotated — sparks/offsets ignore the object's facing. Distinct from closed hq-azxp, which wired the attacker→victim aiming matrix when secondary is present.
close_reason: C++ live-host FX/shadow parity on player path. See local://wave21-fix-16.md

title: [Helix] Passenger fire originates at FIREPOINT bones not hull+8 redeploy
description:
## C++
`HelixContain::redeployOccupants` (`HelixContain.cpp:112-123`) overrides OpenContain fire-point placement: every rider is `setPosition` at the Helix origin with `z += 8`. Called from `OpenContain::addToContain` / `monitorConditionChanges` so Helix infantry (and vehicles) always shoot from that raised hull point, not sequential FIREPOINT bones.

`HelixContain::update` (`:98-108`) also snaps the portable addon to hull position/orientation each frame.

## Live
`try_transport_passenger_residual_fire` (`drones_and_garrison.rs:694-699`) uses `transport_passenger_fire_origin` (`:112-118`): `getMultiLogicalBonePosition("FIREPOINT")` cycle, else hull center (no +8 Z). Helix is only special-cased for the GARRISONED 133% range multiply (`:685-692`), not redeploy.

Closed hq-ncs1d fixed generic transport fire from hull center to FIREPOINT. That is correct for Humvee/Chinook/Bus (`OpenContain::putObjAtNextFirePoint`) and wrong for Helix, which explicitly replaces that path.

## Player-visible
Helix BattleBunker infantry muzzle flashes and shot origins sit on FIREPOINT bones (or the cabin center) instead of 8 world units above the helicopter. Range checks and residual acquire use that wrong origin, so window/door bones can engage slightly earlier or later than retail.

Distinct from closed hq-ncs1d (generic FIREPOINT), hq-gxy20 (stock Helix fire gate), hq-xj9j7 (Overlord bunker fire).
close_reason: Live transport_passenger_fire_origin uses Helix hull+8 host-Y (C++ redeployOccupants z+=8), not FIREPOINT. Humvee/Chinook keep OpenContain bones. Test helix_fire_origin_is_hull_plus_eight_not_firepoint.

title: [Garrison] Exit never stamps safeOcclusionFrame so walk-out units immediately get behind-building silhouettes
description:
## C++
`GarrisonContain::onRemoving` (`GarrisonContain.cpp:1681-1683`) calls `obj->setSafeOcclusionFrame(TheGameLogic->getFrame()+obj->getTemplate()->getOcclusionDelay())` so a unit walking out of a building is not a potential occludee until OcclusionDelay (GameData DefaultOcclusionDelay 3000ms → 90f). Dead occupants inside get `HUGE_FRAME_IN_FUTURE` (`GarrisonContain.cpp:912-913`) so death never shows through the building. `TunnelContain` exit does the same stamp (`TunnelContain.cpp:200-202`).

`RTS3DScene` only adds a score-unit to `m_potentialOccludees` when `getSafeOcclusionFrame() <= currentFrame` (`W3DScene.cpp:474-475`, `:1936-1937`). Object create also seeds the stamp for factory exit (`Object.cpp:478-479`).

## Leftover
`garrison_contain.rs` and `tunnel_contain.rs` port `set_safe_occlusion_frame`. Unused by Main.

## Live
`GameLogic::garrison_exit_occupant_via_door` (`registries.rs:510-592`) and transport/tunnel exit paths never write an occlusion stamp. Live `Object` has no `safe_occlusion_frame` field (Main grep is empty).

`classify_occluded_player_overlays` / `OcclusionCandidate::from_renderable` (`occlusion_bridge.rs:54-79, 145-160`) treat every mobile unit as an occludee with no frame gate. Behind-building player-color silhouettes (closed hq-0usk) therefore apply on the first frame a garrisoned unit reappears.

## Player-visible
Evacuate a bunker/civilian building: C++ infantry stay fully drawn for ~3s while they walk out. Live immediately paints the ZH behind-building player-color silhouette as they pass the structure. Dead occupants inside can also silhouette through the hull.

Distinct from closed hq-0usk / hq-0mcc (silhouette pass itself now exists) and closed garrison walk-out beads (hq-2x44y / hq-6xv03).
close_reason: Live Object.safe_occlusion_frame seeded on create; garrison/tunnel exit stamp OcclusionDelay; dead garrison occupants stamp HUGE_FRAME_IN_FUTURE; occlusion_bridge skips silhouettes until that frame.

title: [Pathfind] moveAllies uses same-team ±1 cell, not ALLIES / radius / blockedByAlly
description:
## C++
`Pathfinder::moveAllies` (`AIPathfind.cpp:10088-10164`):
- Dozer/harvester always clear; everyone else only if `path->getBlockedByAlly()`.
- Walks path last→first; for each node, scans the **mover** `getRadiusAndCenter` footprint on `node->getLayer()`.
- Only `getRelationship==ALLIES`; skips self, ignoreObstacle, infantry-through-infantry, attacking, `OBJECT_STATUS_IS_USING_ABILITY`, `isBusy()`.
- Infantry movers do not push vehicles unless `blockedByAlly`.

## Live
`allies_to_nudge_off_path` (`pathfinding.rs:4886-4931`) always runs after a successful path (`movement.rs:104-123`). It:
- Requires `obj.team == mover.team` (not `player_ally_masks` / ALLIES).
- Tests waypoint cells with a hardcoded **±1** Chebyshev, not the mover radius (Overlord radius 2 ignored).
- Never reads `blockedByAlly` (live paths do not even set it on the host Path).
- Does not skip `ignoreObstacle`.

(Packing/busy skip from closed `hq-p1pwi` is present.)

## Player-visible
In team games, allied other-player units never scoot off your tank path. Own-player units fidget even when A* already went around them. Large vehicles leave units sitting inside their hull because only the waypoint cell ±1 is scanned.
close_reason: Live allies_to_nudge_off_path: ALLIES via player_ally_masks, mover getRadiusAndCenter footprint, blockedByAlly gate, skip ignoreObstacle.

title: [ControlBar] OBJECT_UPGRADE missing affectedByUpgrade; PLAYER vs OBJECT upgrade collapsed
description:
## C++
GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/GUI/ControlBar/ControlBarCommand.cpp:1204-1264
PLAYER_UPGRADE and OBJECT_UPGRADE are separate. OBJECT_UPGRADE returns CANT_AFFORD (keeps color) if the object already has the upgrade, it is in queue, or affectedByUpgrade() is false. PLAYER_UPGRADE checks player complete / in-production only.

## Live
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/command_button.rs:631 maps both INI types to CommandType::QueueUpgrade.
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/gui/control_bar/control_bar_impl/impl_command_context.rs:396-430 treats QueueUpgrade as one case (player complete OR in-production OR obj.has_upgrade → CantAfford). There is no affectedByUpgrade check. Presentation path leftover_presentation_can_make_restricted only grays when a can_make status is present.

## Player-visible
An object-upgrade button stays enabled on a unit that cannot receive that upgrade (C++ would keep it colored-disabled via CANT_AFFORD). Player vs object upgrade already-owned state can disagree, so a barracks may show an object upgrade as clickable after another building already queued/owns it, or the reverse.
close_reason: Live QueueUpgrade availability splits PLAYER vs OBJECT (ControlBarCommand.cpp:1204-1264). OBJECT_UPGRADE: no PU → Restricted; hasUpgrade / isUpgradeInQueue / !affectedByUpgrade → CantAfford. PLAYER_UPGRADE: player complete/in-production only. Leftover Object::affected_by_upgrade now walks wouldUpgrade (player|object|this mask).

title: [Pathfind] has_allied_goal tests only the seeker's own player bit — allied players' goals usurped, own goal wrongly refused
description: C++ / live / player-visible in team play. C++ checkDestination (AIPathfind.cpp:4900-4970): a cell reserved as UNIT_GOAL by the seeker itself is skipped (goalUnitID==objID -> continue), goals of ALLIES are refused ('Don"t usurp your allies goals', getRelationship==ALLIES -> return false), and enemy goals are fine unless the occupant is fixed and uncrushable. Live PathfindingGrid::has_allied_goal (Main pathfinding.rs:1493-1505) returns (goal & (1<<seeker_player)) != 0 — i.e. only the seeker's OWN player bit counts as allied. Result inverted both ways: (a) a unit re-ordered toward a cell already reserved by itself or a same-player sibling gets its destination refused and nudged by adjust_destination_ex / find_path_via_crate's allied-goal retry (C++ accepts own goals); (b) in 2v2/team games a unit happily takes a cell reserved by a DIFFERENT allied player's unit (bit not set, ally mask unused here), so teammates stack on one spot where C++ would spread them to neighboring cells. Fix: refuse when (goal & (ally_mask | bit)) != 0 minus the seeker's own reservation, not when (goal & bit) != 0.
close_reason: Live host pathfind: A* start/adjust on dest layer, has_allied_goal uses ally bits minus own reservation, occupancy matches examineNeighboringCells.

title: [Pathfind] Traffic occupancy cost model deviates from C++ examineNeighboringCells (enemy-moving penalty invented, allied-moving and goal costs wrong)
description: C++ / live / player-visible (subtle path-quality skew). Live find_path_via_crate extra-cost closure (Main pathfinding.rs:2640-2706) and occupancy_cost (:1105-1170) diverge from C++ examineNeighboringCells/checkForMovement (AIPathfind.cpp:4971-5080, 6097-6363): (1) Live adds +3*COST_DIAGONAL for enemy/non-friend MOVING occupants; C++ checkForMovement only sets allyMoving for relationship==ALLIES and examineNeighboringCells adds no cost for moving enemies (they are ignored entirely when considerTransient=false). (2) Live only charges the moving surcharge for the seeker's own player bit (moving & bit) and applies it map-wide; C++ charges allyMoving +3*COST_DIAGONAL for ALL allies (incl. other allied players) but only within dx<10 && dy<10 of the start cell (AIPathfind.cpp:6245-6247), so live over-avoids enemy traffic everywhere and under-avoids allied columns near the start. (3) Live adds +3*COST_DIAGONAL for ANY UNIT_GOAL reservation (own or enemy) in normal movement paths; C++ adds allyGoal cost only in attack paths (attackDistance != NO_ATTACK: vehicles +3*COST_ORTHOGONAL, infantry +COST_ORTHOGONAL, AIPathfind.cpp:6290-6300) and never in plain move paths, so live group moves spread/weave around each other's reserved destinations far more than retail. (4) Live infantry-through-infantry free pass requires goal_m == 0; the C++ INFANTRY_MOVES_THROUGH_INFANTRY continue (AIPathfind.cpp:5040-5044) is per-unit and unconditional, so infantry should stream through cells even when another unit reserved them as a goal.
close_reason: Live host pathfind: A* start/adjust on dest layer, has_allied_goal uses ally bits minus own reservation, occupancy matches examineNeighboringCells.

title: [Locomotor] Wheeled CanMoveBackwards reverse / three-point turn never runs on live march
description: C++: moveTowardsPositionWheels (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Locomotor.cpp:1298-1320, 1441-1470): when actualSpeed==0 and template m_canMoveBackward and |relAngle|>PI/2, set MOVING_BACKWARDS (and DOING_THREE_POINT_TURN when onPathDistToGoal > 5*majorRadius); while reversing, actualSpeed is negated, desiredAngle is mirrored by PI unless doing a 3-point turn, rotation aims at the mirrored backwardPos via rotateObjAroundLocoPivot, and the accel force sign flips; flag clears when |relAngle| < PI/2. This is the retail humvee/truck backing-up-to-nearby-goals behavior. / Leftover: GameEngine locomotor/core_impl/move_ground.rs:136-303 implements the full reverse + three-point turn (FLAG_MOVING_BACKWARDS / FLAG_DOING_THREE_POINT_TURN, mirrored angle, negated speed delta). / Live: Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/movement.rs update_movement never sets moving_backwards — the only writer is the dead residual object/update.rs:222-233 (no callers); physics.rs apply_forward_speed_force honors the sign but is never fed by the live march, so wheeled units always pivot nose-first. hq-2rfrw covered only the wheeled turnFactor. / Player-visible: wheeled units with retail Locomotor.ini CanMoveBackwards=Yes (humvee/technical-style) execute a forward U-turn on short move orders behind them instead of backing up or three-point turning. title: [CmdQueue] Stop on AI transports does not idle occupants
description:
## C++
`AIUpdateInterface::privateIdle` (`AIUpdate.cpp:3067-3090`) skip KINDOF_PROJECTILE, clear state machine, set AI_IDLE, then `contain->getContainedItemsList()` and `ai->aiIdle(cmdSource)` for every occupant. `AIGroup::groupIdle` (`AIGroup.cpp:2030-2084`) calls `aiIdle` on members **with** AI (which recursively idles riders) and only uses `iterateContained(makeMemberStop)` for members **without** AI.

## Live

Distinct from closed hq-kq3ki (garrison / no-AI members).

## Player-visible
Stop on a loaded Humvee/Battle Bus/Chinook leaves PassengersAllowedToFire riders shooting. Retail Stop idles those riders.
close_reason: unit_command_stop walks contained_units and recursively idles riders (C++ privateIdle contain list).

title: [SpecialAbility] Laser-guided Missile Defender stays on secondary after beam ends
description:
## Why
C++ killSpecialObjects for SPECIAL_MISSILE_DEFENDER_LASER_GUIDED_MISSILES setWeaponLock(PRIMARY_WEAPON, LOCKED_TEMPORARILY) so ending the laser snaps the unit back to normal missiles. Live leftover laser abort/trigger never resets PRIMARY.

## Leftover
special_ability_update.rs:1878-1887 ports the PRIMARY lock. Wave 296 unused.

## Live
missile_defenders.rs update_leftover_laser_guided_channels abort (:259-263) only take_leftover_channel. Trigger (:279-283) set_active_weapon_slot(1) SECONDARY then engage. No set_weapon_lock / PRIMARY reset on abort or end.

## Player-visible

title: [Terrain] Live never calls leftover newMap so water-grid passability stays dry
description:
## C++
`TerrainLogic::newMap` (TerrainLogic.cpp:1102-1121) after load snaps waypoint Z then `enableWaterGrid(WaveGuide1 != NULL)`. `enableWaterGrid` (1127-1222) loads GameData.INI vertex-water clamps/transform/resolution and `TheTerrainVisual->enableWaterGrid`. `getWaterHandle` (2197-2211) then returns the grid handle when `getWaterGridHeight` hits the mesh and meshZ >= polygon Z. `isUnderwater` (2138-2153) uses that mesh Z. `classifyMapCell` (4509-4512) marks CELL_WATER if any corner is underwater.

## Leftover
`TerrainLogic::new_map` + `terrain_water::enable_water_grid` port the same WaveGuide1 / GameData.INI path. `get_water_handle` / `is_underwater` sample leftover `get_water_grid_height` (on-mesh only). Live host never calls leftover `new_map` — `world_save.rs` only `reset()` + `load_map_data()`. No Main caller of `terrain.new_map`.

## Live host
`is_underwater_at_world` prefers leftover `get_water_handle` then leftover `is_underwater`. With the water grid never enabled, leftover `get_water_grid_height` is always None, so leftover never returns the grid handle. `seed_pathfinding_from_terrain` then only sees polygon water. Vertex-water mesh (dam / WaveGuide1 maps) stays CLEAR.

## Player-visible
On WaveGuide1 / vertex-water maps, ground under the deformable water mesh that is not covered by a water polygon stays walkable. C++ marks those cells CELL_WATER (boats/hover only). Distinct from closed hq-tdxnb (polygon copy) and hq-bq0q (visual mesh GPU).

## Not a duplicate
Closed hq-tdxnb wired leftover polygons into the host. Closed hq-xc1l3 restamps after script rise. Closed hq-bq0q is presentation-only. Closed hq-5j8m implemented leftover `terrain_water.rs` mesh sample — leftover `new_map` / `enable_water_grid` still never run on the live load path.
close_reason: Both leftover load_map_data sites in world_save.rs now call TerrainLogic::new_map(false) after load (C++ GameLogic.cpp:1629). WaveGuide1 enables leftover water grid so get_water_handle / is_underwater can sample vertex-water mesh.

title: AI: live host lacks aiPreTeamDestroy - wiped AI teams linger in build/ready queues up to 60-180s
description: C++ / leftover / live / player-visible(rare). C++ Player::preTeamDestroy (Player.cpp:1616-1623) -> AIPlayer::aiPreTeamDestroy (AIPlayer.cpp:836-864) removes every TeamInQueue matching the destroyed team from both TeamBuildQueue and TeamReadyQueue the moment all members die, so the AI immediately frees the slot and re-queues a replacement team. title: Live host: SnowManager visibility never reset between maps - SHOW_WEATHER=No sticks forever
description: C++ / leftover / live / player-visible (rare: needs a map script). C++ GameClient::reset (GameClient.cpp:447-452) calls TheSnowManager->reset() which restores m_isVisible=TRUE (Snow.cpp:79-83), so a map script SHOW_WEATHER=No (ScriptActions.cpp:3804 TheSnowManager->setVisible(FALSE)) stops applying on the next map and snow renders again wherever SnowEnabled. Live: SnowManager::reset exists (GameEngine/GameClient/src/snow.rs) but no live reset path calls it — GameClient reset (core/game_client/impl_init.rs:149) and Main game reset do not touch the snow manager; the only set_visible(true) callers are tests. GameLogic-side weather_state.visible is reset via RuntimeWeatherState::default() (world_save.rs/construct.rs:1202), so the host flag and the SnowManager static diverge: after one map hides weather, the SnowManager stays hidden for every later map (snow maps render without falling snow until some script runs SHOW_WEATHER=Yes). Fix: call SnowManager::reset() (set_visible(true)) from the live GameClient reset / new-game path like C++ GameClient.cpp:451-452.
close_reason: GameClient::reset now calls SnowManager::reset so SHOW_WEATHER=No does not stick across maps.

title: Live host: FXList RayEffect beams never expire - permanent additive beams accumulate
description: C++ / leftover / live / player-visible (data-dependent, rare). C++ W3DGameClient::createRayEffectByTemplate (W3DGameClient.cpp:121-143) creates a real drawable whose W3DLaserDraw + LaserUpdate own the beam lifetime: LaserUpdate::clientUpdate decays width to zero over setDecayFrames (LaserUpdate.cpp:176-208) and the drawable is destroyed, removing its RayEffectSystem entry (GameClient.cpp:1007-1013 removeFromRayEffects on drawable death) — beams fade out after their MaxIntensityLifetime/FadeLifetime. Live path: FXList RayEffect nugget (GameEngine/GameClient/src/fx_list.rs:1262-1302, driven from Main game_logic/host_fx_list_dispatch.rs weapon FX) calls ray_effect_system::create_ray_effect_by_template (effects/ray_effect_system.rs:73-105) which stores a LiveRayEffect with no lifetime, and particle_renderer.rs render_tracer_and_ray_fx (1104-1122, called from display.rs:1142/w3d/particles.rs:100 every frame) draws every stored ray as an additive billboard with fixed color [0.85,0.95,1.0] and width 0.4 at alpha 1.0 forever. delete_ray_effect/reset_ray_effects have zero live-path callers (tests only), so once any weapon FXList containing a RayEffect nugget fires, its beam stays on screen permanently and beams accumulate (up to the 128-slot store, which then silently recycles the oldest). The RayEffectManager configs spawned in fx_list.rs:1286-1299 (with proper per-name lifetimes) are never rendered. Fix: give LiveRayEffect the template laser lifetimes and remove entries when expired, or render the RayEffectManager instances instead of the raw store.
close_reason: LiveRayEffect stores MaxIntensity+Fade lifetime; update_ray_effects expires FXList beams; GameClient ticks it next to tracers.

title: ClipReloadTime=0 clip weapons get a fabricated reload wait (host substitutes max DelayBetweenShots)
description: C++ / leftover / live / player-visible ROF (P2: data-dependent — retail clip weapons usually author ClipReloadTime, but any ClipSize>0 weapon without it reloads slower than C++). C++ WeaponTemplate default m_clipReloadTime = 0 (Weapon.cpp:281) and reloadWithBonus (Weapon.cpp:1889-1891) uses it verbatim: reloadTime = m_clipReloadTime / RATE_OF_FIRE, so a clip weapon with ClipReloadTime absent/0 is ready to fire the frame after its clip empties (m_whenWeCanFireAgain = now + 0; JetOrHeliReloadAmmoState JetAIUpdate.cpp:1452-1455 even clamps the dock rearm to a 1-frame minimum for this case). Live host: ThingTemplate::weapon_from_store (src/game_logic/thing.rs:2237-2244) bakes clip_reload_time = max_delay_between_shots frames whenever the store's clip_reload_time is 0 and clip_size > 0, and live_reload_interval (object/attack.rs:638-644) then gates readiness on that fabricated interval — the unit waits a full between-shots delay after emptying its clip where C++ is instantly reloaded. Also makes refresh_weapon_fire_status report ReloadingClip (object/weapons.rs:376-377) for such weapons where C++ is READY next frame. Fix direction: keep clip_reload_time = 0 and let the ready gate treat an empty clip with zero reload time as immediately ready (min-1-frame clamp only for the airfield dock path, which already has it).
close_reason: Live weapon_from_store already keeps ClipReloadTime=0 (no DelayBetweenShots substitute); live_reload_interval / refresh treat 0 as same-frame ready; ReloadingClip percent-ready now uses clip_reload_time verbatim instead of falling back to DelayBetweenShots.

title: DelayBetweenShots Min/Max per-shot randomization dropped — live host always uses Min
description: C++ / leftover / live / player-visible ROF (P2: data-dependent — only weapons authoring Min != Max). C++ WeaponTemplate::getDelayBetweenShots (Weapon.cpp:475-490): when m_minDelayBetweenShots != m_maxDelayBetweenShots the per-shot delay is GameLogicRandomValue(min, max) (inclusive), then divided by the RATE_OF_FIRE bonus; privateFireWeapon (2645-2647) applies it per shot. Leftover GameEngine weapon_template/get_delay_between_shots mirrors the random draw. Live host: host_delay_between_shots_secs (src/game_logic/weapon_bootstrap/reload_aim.rs) collapses the pair to min if min > 0 else max, and live_reload_interval (object/attack.rs:631-651) prefers that fixed value for every store-backed weapon, so any Weapon.ini entry with Min < Max fires at the MINIMUM cadence every shot — faster than the C++ average (e.g. the documented retail pair ScudStormWeapon DelayBetweenShots 100:1000 ms: C++ spreads 9 shots over ~100-1000ms gaps, avg ~550ms; the standard live fire path would fire each gap at 100ms). The ScudStorm superweapon strike path already randomizes correctly (special_power_strikes/superweapon_kind.rs scud_delay_between_frames draws [3,30] frames); the standard store-driven combat path does not. Fix direction: draw the between-shots interval per shot from [min, max] via the host logic RNG residual.
close_reason: Live host_delay_between_shots_secs wires leftover WeaponTemplate::get_delay_between_shots (GameLogicRandomValue min..max inclusive, Weapon.cpp:475-490). Fire stamps the draw onto last_fire_time; live_reload_interval uses a deterministic Min yardstick so ready-checks do not re-roll (privateFireWeapon 2645-2647).

title: ROF bonus change does not restart an in-progress reload (C++ Weapon::onWeaponBonusChange)
description: C++ / leftover / live / player-visible timing (P2: sub-second windows, fires sooner than C++). C++ Weapon.cpp:1938-1975 onWeaponBonusChange: whenever the weapon-bonus set changes while status is RELOADING_CLIP or BETWEEN_FIRING_SHOTS, C++ RESTARTS the wait — m_whenLastReloadStarted = now; m_whenWeCanFireAgain = now + getClipReloadTime(bonus) or getDelayBetweenShots(bonus) with the NEW bonus — and, for ShareWeaponReloadTime objects, copies the new next-shot frame + RELOADING_CLIP status onto every sibling slot (1961-1972). So gaining a RATE_OF_FIRE bonus mid-reload (veterancy rank-up, horde bonus, battle plan, TOW/uranium-style upgrades) makes the unit wait the FULL new delay again. Live host: ready is computed live from last_fire_time with the CURRENT bonus every check (live_reload_interval attack.rs:631-651 divides by rof; effective_weapon_reload bonuses.rs:263) so a bonus gained mid-wait proportionally shortens the remaining wait and never restarts it, and sync_shared_weapon_reload is only invoked per shot (weapons.rs:594 record_shot_at_target) — no bonus-change hook exists (weapon_bonus_fields changes flow through in-place weapon rebuilds that preserve last_fire_time, e.g. world_combat/tanks_and_upgrades.rs). Net effect: live units fire sooner than C++ after any ROF bonus lands mid-cooldown. Fix direction: on weapon-bonus ROF change while a slot is within its reload interval, re-stamp last_fire_time = now (full new delay) and re-run sync_shared_weapon_reload for shared sets.
close_reason: Live Weapon::onWeaponBonusChange: RATE_OF_FIRE change while RELOADING_CLIP/BETWEEN restarts last_fire from now with the new delay; ShareWeaponReloadTime copies next-shot + RELOADING_CLIP to siblings. fire_at applies this before the ready check so mid-reload bonuses cannot fire early.

title: AutoReloadWhenIdle force-reload delay bound from PRIMARY weapon template only; C++ uses the fired weapon per shot
description: C++ / leftover / live / player-visible (P2: rare — no known retail non-primary AutoReloadWhenIdle weapon). C++ FiringTracker is per-object but reads the FIRED weapon's template on every shot: FiringTracker.cpp:101-104 shotFired uses weaponFired->getAutoReloadWhenIdleFrames() to push m_frameToForceReload = now + delay (and the same fired-weapon source for ContinuousFire thresholds/coast); FiringTracker.cpp:169-174 update then calls getObject()->reloadAllAmmo(TRUE) when idle long enough. Leftover GameEngine port matches: GameLogic/src/helpers/object_helpers.rs:131-187 shot_fired(&Weapon) reads template.auto_reload_when_idle_frames from the fired weapon. Live host: thing.rs weapon_tracker_bind/weapon_tracker_from_store (src/game_logic/thing.rs:2264-2290) binds ContinuousFire + AutoReloadWhenIdle fields from the template's PRIMARY weapon name only; construct.rs:802/1591 copies that single value onto Object.auto_reload_when_idle_frames; weapons.rs stamp_auto_reload_when_idle (942-959) then stamps frame_to_force_reload with the primary's delay regardless of which slot fired (world_tick/combat.rs:3016). Divergence for any unit whose SECONDARY/TERTIARY weapon authors AutoReloadWhenIdle (wrong force-reload deadline — earlier or later than C++ — or none at all when only the primary lacks it). Retail today: RocketBuggyMissileWeapon (6100ms) is PRIMARY so the live Rocket Buggy works; the structural per-shot source is still wrong vs C++.
close_reason: Live stamp_auto_reload_when_idle reads AutoReloadWhenIdle from the fired slot WeaponStore template (C++ FiringTracker::shotFired weaponFired->getAutoReloadWhenIdleFrames). Combat and fire_at_ex pass the fired slot; a zero delay no longer falls back to the PRIMARY construct-time bind.

title: Live host: place-beacon button never greys out at MaxBeaconsPerPlayer and targeting still arms
description: C++ / leftover / live / player-visible (rare - requires max beacons active). C++ ControlBar.cpp update() (~1487-1502) re-evaluates every update: counts the local player's beacon template objects and winEnable(FALSE)s ControlBar.wnd:ButtonPlaceBeacon once count >= TheMultiplayerSettings->getMaxBeaconsPerPlayer(); CommandXlat.cpp MSG_META_PLACE_BEACON (3063-3078) also refuses to arm the Command_PlaceBeacon GUI command at max. Live Main has no count-based gating for the place beacon button (control_bar_bridge.rs only checks is_multiplayer && is_player_active), and cnc_game_engine/ui_commands.rs CommandType::PlaceBeacon always arms the pending targeting cursor - the max check happens only at click-apply time in execute_place_beacon (TooManyBeacons message + BeaconPlacementFailed sound). Net flow difference: at max, retail blocks you before targeting; live host lets you target then errors on click. Fix: gate the button/arm on host_count_player_beacons vs host_max_beacons_per_player.
close_reason: Live host: enemy hide+drawable_hidden, BeaconClientUpdate pulse/smoke, captions on HUD, RadarVanPing shrink, GridDecal, silent selection-only delete, EVA own-place, MaxBeacons grey

title: [InGameUI] Military caption stays on screen as raw label after fade
description:
## C++
`InGameUI::postDraw` (`InGameUI.cpp:3461-3485`) draws only while `m_militarySubtitle` exists. After fade, `removeMilitarySubtitle` (`:4093-4112`) deletes it — nothing remains.

## Leftover
`messages.rs` `draw_military_subtitle` returns when `current_military_subtitle` is None. Matches C++.

## Live
`live_hud.rs` `step_subtitle` correctly drops the typed subtitle after fade. `InGameUISubsystem::push_military_subtitle` (`subsystems.rs:1549-1559`) also appends the raw label to an 8-deep `military_subtitles` queue that is never expired. `apply_presentation_military_caption` (`impl_update.rs:847-854`) early-returns when host caption becomes None and never clears the queue. `impl_draw.rs:140-147` snapshot falls back to `military_subtitles().back()`; `:221-229` then draws that raw string forever at INI pose, white 12px.

## Player-visible
After every briefing fades, the untranslated key (or leftover full string) stays stuck on screen. C++ goes blank.
close_reason: Live apply_presentation_military_caption(None) clears the raw-label queue; impl_draw no longer falls back to military_subtitles().back() after leftover fade.

title: [InGameUI] Floating cash pops at full opacity — vanish tail truncated
description:
## C++
`updateFloatingText` (`InGameUI.cpp:5053-5068`) after timeout: `amount = REAL_TO_INT(past * vanishRate)` then subtracts that from the stored alpha each frame. With vanishRate 0.1 and spawn alpha 255, fade lasts ~75 frames (~2.8s) before erase. Draw uses faded alpha + black drop shadow (`:5107-5112`).

## Leftover
`floating_text.rs` `floating_text_alpha_at_frame` matches the cumulative integer fade. Not the live drain filter.

## Live
`PresentationFloatingText::vanish_alpha_at` (`presentation_frame/floating_text.rs:96-104`) is `1.0 - past*0.1` and hits 0 at past=10. `is_active_at` (`:78-80`) uses that curve. `camera_drain.rs:2429` filters with `is_active_at` then strips RGB-only (`:2434`). `impl_draw.rs:264-267` reconstructs fade from spawn alpha 255 with the correct leftover helper — but the drain already dropped the entry at past=10 when C++ alpha is still ~254.

## Player-visible
Cash floaters pop out at full opacity after ~0.7s instead of fading over ~2.8s. Adjacent: authored alpha 230 is stripped so remaining frames would also start too opaque. Distinct from closed hq-a6qou (leftover fade+shroud now exist; live drain still truncates).
close_reason: is_active_at uses leftover cumulative integer vanish (~75 frames). Drain keeps authored RGBA; draw fades from spawn alpha not hardcoded 255.

title: [InGameUI] Drawable captions skip black box and InGameUI style
description:
## C++
`Drawable::drawCaption` (`Drawable.cpp:3737-3768`): worldToScreen of geometry center, x centered by string width, black fill (0,0,0,125) + 1px (20,20,20,255) open rect, text in `TheInGameUI->getDrawableCaptionColor()` with black drop shadow. Font from InGameUI DrawableCaption* (`InGameUI.cpp:1017-1020`, INI 812-815, GlobalLanguage `:1083-1087`) via `setCaptionText` (`Drawable.cpp:4307-4312`). Only producer is `MSG_SET_BEACON_TEXT` (`GameLogicDispatch.cpp:1741-1754`).

## Leftover
InGameUI stores drawable_caption font/size/bold/color (`types.rs:1155-1159`, INI + language override in `impl_update.rs`). Unused by live draw.

## Live
`camera_drain.rs:1927-1934` stamps `display_name` as caption when distinct from template. `basic_modules.rs:165-181` draws it at the control-group numeral anchor (`base_y+14`) with group-info font/color, left-aligned, no box. `impl_draw.rs:570-577` draws `overlay.caption` again at `(bar_x, bar_y-24)` white 10px. Beacon typed text (`host_beacon_caption`) never reaches this path.

## Player-visible
Beacon/unit captions have no black backing box, wrong font/color/anchor, and can double-draw. Typed beacon text never appears over the beacon.
close_reason: Live impl_draw uses C++ drawCaption (worldToScreen center, black 125 fill + 1px 20,20,20 outline, drop shadow). Leftover numeral-anchor caption paint removed.

title: [InGameUI] Factory hover never shows SET_RALLY_POINT flag cursor
description:
## C++
`CommandXlat.cpp:2180-2199` posts `MSG_SET_RALLY_POINT_HINT` when a locally-controlled AUTO_RALLYPOINT producer is selected and the cursor is over empty ground. `InGameUI::createCommandHint` (`InGameUI.cpp:2671-2675`) sets `Mouse::SET_RALLY_POINT` (flag cursor) unless the hover drawable is selectable.

## Leftover
`command_translator.rs` + `impl_input.rs:1217-1226` port the hint → SET_RALLY_POINT cursor. Not the live OS cursor path.

## Live
`host_resolve_context_cursor_icon` (`mouse.rs:2326-2529`) has a SetRallyPoint arm (`:2502-2504`) but `CommandSystem::determine_context_command` (`system_impl.rs:369-496`) never emits `SetRallyPoint` (defaults to MoveTo). Hover therefore hits `_ => ("Move", AllScroll)` (`mouse.rs:2522-2527`). Armed-button pending path uses Cell (`:2351`) only after Y/button arms pending.

## Player-visible
Selecting a factory and hovering open ground shows a generic move cursor, not the retail rally-flag cursor. Distinct from closed hq-7lbg (click still sets rally).
close_reason: Empty-ground factory hover returns SET_RALLY_POINT cursor; determine_context_command emits SetRallyPoint for AUTO_RALLYPOINT selection.

title: [InGameUI] SetRallyPoint accepts any structure not AUTO_RALLYPOINT
description:
## C++
`InGameUI::canSelectedObjectsDoAction(ACTIONTYPE_SET_RALLY_POINT)` (`InGameUI.cpp:4373-4380`) succeeds only when the object is `KINDOF_AUTO_RALLYPOINT` and `isLocallyControlled()`. Empty-ground click uses that gate (`CommandXlat.cpp:2180-2199`). Power plants / base defenses do not set rally.

## Leftover
`pick.rs` gates on locally-controlled + alive + production-update interface. Closer than live, unused by host click.

## Live
`host_selection_can_set_rally` (`ui_commands.rs:680-702`) returns true if every selected id is an alive `is_structure` / KINDOF Structure — no AUTO_RALLYPOINT, no local-owner test. `mouse.rs:1594-1598` then issues `SetRallyPoint`. `unit_command_set_rally_point` (`unit_commands.rs:1001-1026`) accepts any `building_data`.

## Player-visible
Selecting a power plant or base defense and clicking ground sets a rally (HUD message + swallowed click). Retail no-ops.
close_reason: host_selection_can_set_rally requires local + KINDOF_AUTO_RALLYPOINT; unit_command_set_rally_point rejects non-AUTO_RALLYPOINT.

title: [InGameUI] Rally flag is a yellow line; RallyPointMarker never reaches live scene
description:
## C++
`ControlBar::showRallyPoint` (`ControlBar.cpp:2669-2720`) `ThingFactory::newDrawable("RallyPointMarker")` (NO_SAVE), `setPosition`, `setOrientation(m_downwindAngle)`, indicator color = local player day/night. That 3D flag is the rally marker. InGameUI/W3DInGameUI do not draw a line.

## Leftover
`ControlBar::show_rally_point` (`impl_portrait.rs:114-167`) creates via leftover `TheGameClient.create_drawable` into GameLogic `DRAWABLE_STATE`. Live Main never reads that map. Template lookup can also miss if RallyPointMarker is not loaded.

## Live
Presentation apply (`apply.rs:1131-1133`) calls leftover `show_rally_point`. Visible overlay is invented amber line `pack_rally_point_lines` (`graphics/selection_renderer.rs:760-793`) from selected structure to rally.

## Player-visible
Selecting a factory shows a yellow world line instead of the player-colored RallyPointMarker flag. Distinct from closed hq-knawn (leftover spawn exists; it never reaches the live scene) and hq-zx8k (EXLaser waypoint path).
close_reason: Yellow rally line removed. unit_render_inputs injects leftover DRAWABLE_STATE RallyPointMarker (fallback selected-structure rally pose).

title: [InGameUI] Drag marquee flashes below Mouse DragTolerance
description:
## C++
`SelectionXlat.cpp:399-407` starts `m_dragSelecting` only when per-axis delta > `TheMouse->m_dragTolerance` (Mouse.ini DragTolerance; leftover/docs default 5px). `W3DInGameUI::draw` (`W3DInGameUI.cpp:373-375`) draws the 2px `0x9933FF33` open rect only while that flag is set.

## Leftover
`SelectionBox::is_significant` (`types.rs:592-595`) uses Euclidean `MIN_DRAG_DISTANCE=5` and gates `render_selection_box`. Leftover crate render is not the live draw.

## Live
`handle_left_click` (`mouse.rs:714-718`) sets `is_dragging=true` on press. Draw uses `DragSelectRect::is_valid` (`selection_renderer.rs:46-50`) `dx>2 || dy>2`. Click-vs-box release still uses 5px (`hq-kmgkv`). Color/width of the live marquee match C++ (`0x9933FF33` / 2px).

## Player-visible
A 3–4px twitch flashes a tiny green marquee then acts as a point click. Retail never draws the box until DragTolerance.
close_reason: DragSelectRect::is_valid is per-axis > Mouse.ini DragTolerance (default 5); 3-4px twitch no longer flashes the marquee.

title: [Crush] First-overlap 0-damage crush bookkeeping fires without geometry contact
description:
## C++
checkForOverlapCollision runs only inside PhysicsBehavior::onCollide, which PartitionContactList::processContactList (PartitionManager.cpp:2450-2508) invokes only after geomCollidesWithGeom passes for the two real geometries. The !wasPreviouslyOverlapped first-overlap branch (0-amount DAMAGE_CRUSH, 'just to trigger the minor DamageFX') therefore fires on first physical contact only.

## Leftover
GameEngine on_collide is reached only through the geom-tested contact list — same gate.

## Live
tick_physics_collisions_all (world_tick/shock.rs:96-127) gates only dispatch_collide_modules/dispatch_host_collide_modules behind host_geom_collides. try_physics_collide runs for every COI-shared-cell neighbor pair regardless: apply_overlap_crush_check -> check_for_overlap_collision (physics_motion.rs:181-310) stamps physics_current_overlap + last_collidee and fires the 0-amount Crush damage packet before any overlap test — can_crush_only plus non-tiny velocity is enough while the pair merely shares a partition cell (PARTITION_CELL_SIZE 40wu, no touching).

## Player-visible
A moving crusher sharing a cell with a crushable enemy (up to tens of world units away) triggers the victim's crush DamageFX (0-amount packets wired since hq-iux6m) before contact, and consumes the first-overlap flag so the true first-contact FX is skipped; last_collidee also stamps from range.
close_reason: try_physics_collide/first-overlap 0-damage only after host_geom_collides, not shared-cell.

title: [Dock] Blocked dockers never bail after 30s — missing WaitForClearance timeout
description:
## C++
AIDockWaitForClearanceState::update (AIDock.cpp:230-252): if the docker is still not clear to enter after m_enterFrame + 30*LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND (900 frames), the state returns STATE_FAILURE, exiting the dock machine (AIDockState::onExit -> halt -> cancelDock frees the approach slot) and handing control back to the supply-truck state machine, which re-evaluates (regroup / pick another dock / force-wanting retry).

## Live
Blocked dockers just 'continue' every tick with no deadline: support_states.rs:5014-5016 (Gathering at a full warehouse), :5301-5303 (ReturningResources at an occupied center), :2803-2806 (SeekingRepair at an occupied pad). The approach reservation stays held and the docker stands in contact range indefinitely.

## Player-visible
Trucks queued behind a slow or stalled active docker stand forever instead of giving up after 30 seconds and re-tasking like C++ (drive off, re-seek, or regroup). Amplifies the ghost-reservation jam: a dock C++ would self-clear via periodic 30s bail-outs never recovers on the live host.
close_reason: Closed

title: [Player] Dozer place/cancel ignores calcCostToBuild handicap
description:
## C++
Placement and cancel-construct refund both use `ThingTemplate::calcCostToBuild(player)` (`ThingTemplate.cpp:1508-1516`): `BuildCost * (1+ProductionCostChange) * KindOf factor * Handicap::getHandicap(BUILDCOST, this)` (BUILDINGS column for `KINDOF_STRUCTURE`).
`GameLogicDispatch.cpp:1430-1435` refunds that amount unless `OBJECT_STATUS_RECONSTRUCTING`.

## Leftover player
`PlayerHandicap` 2x2 matrix + `get_cost_multiplier_for_template` (`energy_handicap.rs:270-275`). Leftover `calcCostToBuild` multiplies `player.get_build_cost_handicap(self)`.

## Live leftover player
`modified_build_cost_supplies` (`world_combat/drones_and_garrison.rs:2049-2080`) now applies handicap (closed hq-hvo7u) and is used by **unit production** enqueue and **sell** refund.
Dozer/AI **place** still charges raw `template.build_cost` (`command_executor/construct.rs:37-73`, `ai.rs:1670-1705`).
Cancel-construct refunds raw `obj.thing.template.build_cost.supplies` (`construct.rs:367-375`), not `calcCostToBuild`. Reconstructing=0 matches C++.

## Player-visible
Easy/handicap maps and SidesList `HANDICAP_BUILDCOST_BUILDINGS` cheapen trained units and sell refunds, but a War Factory still costs the full INI price to place and refunds that full price if cancelled. Placement cost disagrees with production cost on the same handicap.

Distinct from closed hq-hvo7u (helper now multiplies; this path never calls it) and hq-9jwcd (leftover refund BUILDINGS column).
close_reason: Dozer place and cancel-construct refund use ThingTemplate::calcCostToBuild via modified_build_cost_supplies (handicap BUILDINGS column).

title: [Weapon] Weaponset change never unlocks unless WeaponLockSharedAcrossSets
description:
## C++
`WeaponSet::updateWeaponSet` (`WeaponSet.cpp:279-286`): when the selected `WeaponTemplateSet` changes, unless `WeaponLockSharedAcrossSets`, `releaseWeaponLock(LOCKED_PERMANENTLY)` and `m_curWeapon = PRIMARY_WEAPON`. Parsed on WeaponSet (`WeaponSet.cpp:136`). Default is false — most veterancy/salvage/crate set swaps drop a Humvee TOW / Ranger flashbang permanent lock.

## Leftover
`weapon_set.rs` has `is_weapon_lock_shared_across_sets` and unlocks on set change. Leftover path is not live.

## Live
`thing.rs` `apply_weapon_set_definition` binds PreferredAgainst + ShareWeaponReloadTime only — no `WeaponLockSharedAcrossSets`. `try_bind_authored_veterancy_weapon_set` (`object/update.rs:460-491`) replaces slot Weapon instances and does not `release_weapon_lock`. Crate/salvage weaponset swaps same.

## Player-visible
Player locks Humvee TOW or Ranger flashbang, then the unit ranks up or salvages a new WeaponSet: C++ returns to PRIMARY gun; live keeps the old permanent lock on the new set (or a now-missing slot).
close_reason: Live updateWeaponSet parity: setWeaponSetFlag/crate/veterancy now release LOCKED_PERMANENTLY and return to PRIMARY unless the incoming set has WeaponLockSharedAcrossSets.

title: [Weapon] ShareWeaponReloadTime never marks sibling ReloadingClip so remaining ammo stays full
description:
## C++
`Weapon::reloadWithBonus` (`Weapon.cpp:1898-1909`) and `privateFireWeapon` (`:2655-2664`): if `sourceObj->isReloadTimeShared()`, every slot gets the firing weapon's `m_whenWeCanFireAgain` **and** `setStatus(RELOADING_CLIP)` / `BETWEEN_FIRING_SHOTS`. `getRemainingAmmo` (`Weapon.h:666`) returns 0 while `RELOADING_CLIP` even though ammo was refilled.

## Leftover
`weapon_instance.rs` `propagate_shared_timing` copies when+status via leftover `OBJECT_REGISTRY` (empty on live).

## Live
`object/weapons.rs` `sync_shared_weapon_reload` (hq-8l63a) back-computes sibling `last_fire_time` so next-shot timing matches. It does **not** set sibling `ReloadingClip` / remaining-ammo-0. `refresh_weapon_fire_status` and model conditions only follow the active slot. `get_ammo_pip_showing_info` uses raw `w.ammo`.

## Player-visible
Comanche `ShareWeaponReloadTime`: cannon clip-reload correctly gates Hellfire/rocket-pod fire time, but switching to those slots still shows remaining missiles and BETWEEN (not RELOADING) instead of empty/reloading pips and RELOADING_B/C.
close_reason: Live sync_shared_weapon_reload now setStatus(RELOADING_CLIP) on every ShareWeaponReloadTime sibling before last_fire is back-computed, matching Weapon.cpp:1898-1909 / getRemainingAmmo. Switching slots keeps ReloadingClip, remaining ammo 0, and shared next-shot time.

title: [Weather] Snow flakes ignore terrain visible-box — fall underground
description:
## Why
C++ clips the snow emitter cube to the terrain-and-sky visible AABB so flakes do not fall under the ground. Live leftover `flake_positions_y_up` emits the full camera box with no terrain clip.

## C++
`W3DSnowManager::render` (`W3DSnow.cpp:338-363`) calls `TheTerrainRenderObject->getMaximumVisibleBox(frustum, &bbox, TRUE)` (terrain-and-sky tight volume), expands X/Y by `m_amplitude+m_quadSize`, then clips `cubeOriginX/Y` and `cubeDimX/Y` to that AABB. Comment: culls particles falling under the ground. Then `renderSubBox` / `renderAsQuads` only emit inside the clipped extents.

## Leftover
`SnowManager::flake_positions_y_up` (`snow.rs:278-334`) uses the unclipped camera box: `half = floor(boxDim/spacing*0.5)`, `origin = cubeCenter-half`, `dim = cubeCenter+half`. No leftover `getMaximumVisibleBox` / terrain AABB clip.

## Live
Live host draws leftover overlay snow from those unclipped centers (`overlay_gpu.rs:616-647` `upload_snow_mesh`). Leftover `weather.rs` / `weather_complete.rs` snow systems are unused on the live path (`WeatherType::None`).

## Player-visible
On snowy maps with hills, valleys, or raised terrain, flakes keep falling through the ground and inside cliffs instead of vanishing below the terrain ceiling.

## Not a duplicate
Closed `hq-9tp3` is ParticleSys visible-box cull (`doParticles`), not SnowManager. Closed `hq-3w6u` was sparse grid / unused noise table. Closed `hq-huzx` was flakes never rendering.
close_reason: flake_positions_y_up_clipped clips the emitter cube to getMaximumVisibleBox terrain-and-sky AABB expanded by amplitude+quadSize.

title: [RepairDock] Slave drone stays damaged while master docks
description:
## C++
`RepairDockUpdate::action` (`RepairDockUpdate.cpp:67-128`) heals the docker over `TimeForFullHeal`, then if `drone` is non-null heals the drone to **full max health** every frame (`attemptHealing` amount = `getMaxHealth()`). `AIDockProcessDockState::update` (`AIDock.cpp:606-609`) passes `findMyDrone()`: first cached `m_droneID`, else player iterate `KINDOF_DRONE` whose `getProducerID()` is the docker (`:623-666`). Battle / Scout / Hellfire drones therefore snap to full HP while the Humvee is on the pad.

## Leftover
`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/production/dock_update.rs:1151-1171` `RepairDockUpdate::action` does heal the drone to max. Not the live host path (empty dual-world / leftover factory).

## Live
`host_repair.rs:18` still documents "Not full RepairDockUpdate dock bones / drone heal matrix". `support_states.rs:2800-2857` SeekingRepair only `obj.heal(rate * dt)` on the docker. No `findMyDrone` / `KindOf::Drone` + `producer_id` walk. Leftover crate is unused.

## Player-visible
A damaged Battle/Scout/Hellfire drone stays wounded after its Humvee (or other master) finishes a Repair Bay / China War Factory dock. Retail the drone is fully healed by the time the vehicle undocks.
close_reason: Closed

title: [Dock] Approach queue never drives DockWaiting bones — units stack at center
description:
## C++
`DockUpdate.cpp` is the shared machine (everything except `action()`). `loadDockPositions` (`:467-509`) reads pristine `DockStart` / `DockAction` / `DockEnd` / `DockWaiting` unless `KINDOF_IGNORE_DOCKING_BONES`. `reserveApproachPosition` + `computeApproachPosition` (`:112-161`, `:422-462`) convert `DockWaiting` bones to world (boneless docks bias toward the caller by half major radius) then `findPositionAround`. `AIDock` drives Approach → Enter → Dock → Exit along those points; `update` (`:391-403`) only promotes a docker who has **reached** their slot.

## Leftover
`object/behavior/dock_update.rs` (hq-fab9u) ports the approach/bone machine. Wave-355 empty-registry gate was removed from leftover get_enter/dock/exit. Still not the live host path.

## Live
`host_supply_gather.rs:17-51` `tick_live_dock_approach` serializes `m_activeDocker` (hq-yq1qp / hq-qu19p close) but immediately `on_approach_reached` + promote + `ClearToAct`. `DockApproachTick::PathTo` is never returned. `HostDockApproachQueue::set_waiting_bones` exists (`:109-113`) and is **never called**. `number_approach_position_bones` stays 0. Repair / warehouse / center `try_claim_dock` (`support_states.rs:6210-6254`) then acts at `HOST_REPAIR_INTERACT_RANGE` / gather center distance.

## Player-visible
Trucks and vehicles take turns at a dock but still pile on the building center instead of lining up on `DockWaiting` bones (USA Supply Center 9 slots, Repair Bay 5). Closed hq-yq1qp added the turn-taking queue; this remaining leftover is the missing bone path.
close_reason: Closed

title: [Supply] Worker keeps MOVING walk while docking at warehouse
description:
## C++
`DockUpdate::update` (`DockUpdate.cpp:405-415`) after an `m_activeDocker` is set: if the dock is `KINDOF_SUPPLY_SOURCE` and the docker is `KINDOF_DOZER` **and** `KINDOF_HARVESTER` (GLA Worker), and the docker drawable has `MODELCONDITION_DOCKING_BEGINNING`, clear `MODELCONDITION_MOVING`. Workers stop the walk cycle for the dock/gather pose.

## Leftover
`object/behavior/dock_update.rs` `update` ports the worker MOVING clear. Not the live host path.

## Live
`support_states.rs:6291-6321` `apply_docking_model_conditions` sets/clears `DOCKING` / `DOCKING_BEGINNING` / `DOCKING_ACTIVE` / `DOCKING_ENDING` on claim/release. It never clears `MOVING`. Warehouse gather (`support_states.rs` DockingWarehouse) does not special-case Worker.

## Player-visible
GLA Workers keep the walk cycle (or moonwalk) while standing at a Supply Dock / pile. Retail they snap to the docking/gather pose as soon as `DOCKING_BEGINNING` is set.
close_reason: Closed

title: [Weather] Snow flakes are world-axis cards, not camera-facing billboards
description:
## Why
C++ snow quads (and point sprites) always face the camera. Live leftover overlay builds world-axis XY cards that stay fixed in world space, so flakes look like standing cards or thin slivers instead of falling sprites.

## C++
`W3DSnowManager::renderAsQuads` (`W3DSnow.cpp:437-554`) transforms each flake center into view space (`Matrix3D::Transform_Vector(view, snowCenter, &snowCenterVS)`), then adds view-space offsets `(-0.5,0.5,0) * m_quadSize` and draws with the view matrix set to identity so every flake is a camera-facing billboard. Hardware point sprites (`W3DSnow.cpp:409-429`) are also camera-facing. Point sprites vs quads is the DX/wgpu-allowed split; the quad fallback is still camera-facing.

## Leftover
`SnowManager::flake_positions_y_up` (`snow.rs:278-334`) ports C++ emitter centers (64×64 noise, sine drift, camera box). `TerrainVisualImpl::upload_snow_mesh` (`overlay_gpu.rs:589-647`) then expands each center into a world-axis quad:
`[cx±quad, wy±quad, cz]` — a vertical XY card facing −Z, not the camera.

`effects/weather.rs` `SnowSystem` still documents WGPU snow as deferred and is unused by the live host.

## Live
Live host draws leftover overlay snow (`overlay_gpu.rs:825-833` via leftover `TerrainVisual` + `record_overlay_draws`). No leftover camera-facing rebuild. Leftover `weather_complete` stays `WeatherType::None` (no extra spawn-based snow).

## Player-visible
On SnowEnabled maps, flakes appear as world-aligned cards/diamonds that do not face the camera. Orbiting or pitching the RTS camera turns them into thin slivers instead of always-facing flakes.

## Not a duplicate
Closed `hq-huzx` was flakes never rendering. Closed `hq-3w6u` was the old 24×24 sparse grid / unused noise table. Closed `hq-3zg3` was SnowTexture binding. Billboard orientation remains.
close_reason: Live overlay snow quads use camera right/up (C++ renderAsQuads view-space offsets), not world-axis XY cards.

title: [SpySat] DynamicShroud GridDecal ring never draws for SpySatellitePing or RadarVanPing
description:
## Why
C++ SpySatellitePing and RadarVanPing draw GridDecalTemplate rings that grow/shrink with DynamicShroudClearingRangeUpdate. Live FOW lookers change radius (SpySat) or pop (RadarVan) with no ground ring.

## C++
`DynamicShroudClearingRangeUpdate` parses `GridDecalTemplate` and `create_grid_decals` / `animate_grid_decals` around the ping object as `m_currentClearingRange` changes.
SpySatellitePing: grow 0→300 over 1000ms, sustain, shrink 300→0 over 5000ms after 10000ms delay.
RadarVanPing: instant 150, shrink after 7500ms.

## Leftover
`dynamic_shroud_clearing_range_update.rs:555-560` `create_grid_decals` returns immediately when `dual_world_registry_unavailable()` (Wave 383). Live host never attaches this module to ping objects.

## Live
`host_spy_satellite.rs:16` / `host_radar_scan.rs:16` / `host.rs:466-470` document GridDecal GPU fail-closed.
`spawn_spy_satellite_ping` / `spawn_radar_van_ping` create residual objects for destalth/lifetime, not GridDecal draw.
SpySat FOW curve is applied (`apply_spy_satellite_dynamic_shroud`); the visible ring is not.

## Player-visible
Spy Sat and Radar Van Scan never show the expanding/shrinking ground decal ring that marks the scan on terrain.

## Not a duplicate
Closed `hq-1f47g` is leftover GameLogic `RadiusDecal::addDecal` for Spectre/payload delivery rings. GridDecalTemplate on DynamicShroud is a different draw path. Closed `hq-ycwy3` is FOW radius, not the decal.
close_reason: Live host: enemy hide+drawable_hidden, BeaconClientUpdate pulse/smoke, captions on HUD, RadarVanPing shrink, GridDecal, silent selection-only delete, EVA own-place, MaxBeacons grey

title: [Beacon] Captions never reach world text or EditBeaconText on the live HUD
description:
## Why
C++ selected local beacons show `EditBeaconText` / label / clear, and `setCaptionText` draws over the world object. Live stores captions in a HashSet map that presentation and leftover ControlBar never consume on the host path.

## C++
`GameLogicDispatch.cpp:1731-1758` MSG_SET_BEACON_TEXT concatenates wchar args onto `Drawable::setCaptionText` / `clearCaptionText`.
`ControlBarBeacon.cpp:20-59` `populateBeacon`: locally controlled shows `ControlBar.wnd:EditBeaconText` (focused, filled from caption), `StaticTextBeaconLabel`, `ButtonClearBeaconText`; non-local hides them.
`BeaconWindowInput` ESC deselects.

## Leftover

title: [BombTruck] Leftover onDie fires only the first FireWeaponWhenDead module and stamps fired before splash
description:
## Why
C++ Bomb Truck death runs every FireWeaponWhenDead module independently (default ConflictsWith HE, HE TriggeredBy HE, Bio poison as its own module/OCL) so HE+Bio combine. - Each module `onDie`: skip if upgrade inactive, die mux no, `OBJECT_STATUS_UNDER_CONSTRUCTION`, or object/player completed ConflictsWith.
- Then `TheWeaponStore->createAndFireTempWeapon(d->m_deathWeapon, obj, pos)` — full weapon pipeline (DamageType EXPLOSION, DeathType EXPLODED, armor).
- Multiple modules on one truck each receive `onDie`. Exclusive mux selects default vs HE; Bio still fires when owned.

## Leftover

- `dead_ephemeral_spec` (`:167-207`) walks authored `fire_weapon_when_dead_behaviors`, then `break`s on the first matching spec.
- `execute_temporary_weapon_on_die` (`:40-47`) sets `fire_weapon_when_dead_fired = true` *before* `create_and_fire_temp_weapon`. Store miss / not READY returns 0 (`temporary_weapon_force.rs:54-55`) with the flag already set.
- `world_tick/step.rs:1146` runs leftover before `process_destroy_list`.

## Player-visible

title: [Audio] VoiceCrush force-move uses Team== + cell, not drawable canCrushOrSquish
description:
## C++

title: [Crush] Crush points use selection_radius not majorRadius
description:
## C++
`PhysicsBehavior::checkForOverlapCollision` (`PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1490`) sets crush-point offset to `crusheeOther->getGeometryInfo().getMajorRadius() / 2`. Front/back/center points and the `2.25 * offset²` past-point window all use that major radius.

## Leftover
`physics_crush.rs:79` ports `get_major_radius() / 2.0`. Unused by Main.

## Live
`Object::check_for_overlap_collision` (`physics_motion.rs:290-291`) uses `other.selection_radius.max(5.0) / 2.0`. `selection_radius` is `geometry_info.bounding_circle_radius()` when authored (`construct.rs:54-55`) — for BOX cars that is `sqrt(major²+minor²)`, not `majorRadius` — or a KindOf table (infantry 8 / vehicle 15) when geometry is not authored.

Live `fire_crush_die_from_crusher` already uses authored `major_radius` (`death.rs:516-519`); only the physics crush *points* still use selection radius.

## Player-visible
Cars/props crush at the wrong front/back/center points: too early, too late, or the opposite end. BOX vehicles crush from farther away than C++ because the bounding-circle offset is larger than majorRadius/2.
close_reason: Live crush points use authored majorRadius/2 (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1490), not selection_radius.

title: [Crush] Live canCrush is TEST_CRUSH_ONLY — leftover SquishCollide unused
description:
## C++
`Object::canCrushOrSquish` (`Object.cpp:1109-1137`): `TEST_SQUISH_ONLY` / `TEST_CRUSH_OR_SQUISH` returns true if the victim has a `SquishCollide` module — independent of `crushableLevel`. `TEST_CRUSH_ONLY` is levels only (`crusherLevel > crushableLevel`).

`SquishCollide::onCollide` (`SquishCollide.cpp:73`) only needs `other->getCrusherLevel() > 0` (plus ally / 1.0 geom / velocity-toward). It does **not** consult crushableLevel.

Callers of `TEST_CRUSH_OR_SQUISH` (default): `AIUpdate::blockedBy` (`AIUpdate.cpp:1289`), `wantToSquishTarget` (`AIStates.cpp:1140`), force-move `VoiceCrush` (`CommandXlat.cpp:415`), pathfind occupancy.

## Leftover
`object_combat.rs:1046-1052` `can_crush_or_squish` ports the SquishCollide module test. Unused by Main.

## Live
`Object::can_crush_only` (`physics_motion.rs:158-166`) is `TEST_CRUSH_ONLY` only (levels + ally + unmanned). Instant-squish is gated on that predicate, then `KindOf::Infantry` as a SquishCollide proxy (`physics_motion.rs:201-205`). `spawn_templates.rs` never peels a SquishCollide module.

`ai_blocked_by`, `want_to_squish_target`, occupancy crush-through, and `force_move_has_crush_target` all call `can_crush_only`.

## Player-visible
Infantry whose authored `CrushableLevel` is missing (default 255) or `>=` the vehicle `CrusherLevel` are still run over in C++ (module / `TEST_SQUISH`). Live tanks treat them as blockers, skip instant-squish, and play VoiceMove instead of VoiceCrush. Leftover already has the C++ test; live never calls it.
close_reason: Live can_crush_or_squish includes SquishCollide module; instant-squish no longer TEST_CRUSH_ONLY+KindOf.

title: [SquishCollide] Crusher geom forced to cylinder, not authored BOX
description:
## C++
`SquishCollide::onCollide` (`SquishCollide.cpp:83-84`) runs `geomCollidesWithGeom` against the crusher's **real** `GeometryInfo` (BOX for tanks/humvees) and orientation. Only the victim geom is forced to 1.0 major/minor.

## Leftover

## Live

## Player-visible

close_reason: squish_geom_collides_with uses authored crusher GeometryInfo (BOX), not a selection cylinder.

description:

title: [JetAI] Presentation wipes takeoff JETAFTERBURNER — only crash shows it
description:
## Why
C++ takeoff afterburner is `MODELCONDITION_JETAFTERBURNER` for the pause+roll window only. ## C++

title: [Chinook] Combat drop hover uses object Y, not geometry height + MinDropHeight
description:
## Symptom
Combat Drop on a tall structure hovers at preferred height (100) instead of roof + MinDropHeight. Chinook clips the building; rappellers start inside geometry.

## C++
`ChinookMoveToBldgState::onEnter` (`ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:702-718`): if goal is a live `KINDOF_STRUCTURE`, `newPreferredHeight = geom.getMaxHeightAbovePosition() + MinDropHeight` (never below old preferred). `m_destZ = getGroundHeight(dest) + newPreferredHeight`. Wait for 2D arrival **and** `|z-destZ|<=3`.

## Leftover
`enter_move_to_bldg` ports that formula. Dual-world empty — not live.

## Live
`execute_combat_drop` (`transport.rs:733-737`) passes `building_height = target.get_position().y.max(0.0)` — the object's world Y, not `geometry_info.max_height_above_position`. `command_combat_drop` (`host_combat_chinook.rs:688-700`) then `combat_drop_dest_z = dest[2] + new_pref`. Ground-placed buildings have Y≈0 so hover stays at PreferredHeight 100 even when the roof is 80+ and C++ would hover at 120.

Closed hq-n0wit added the MoveToBldg wait; the height input is still wrong.

## Player-visible
Combat Drop onto Command Centers / bunkers / Tech buildings: Chinook flies through the roof. Rappellers spawn inside the mesh.
close_reason: Live host Chinook: leave DO_COMBAT_DROP, aiRappelInto roof dest, HeadOffMap spawn dest, pending evac dest on takeoff, hover geom+MinDropHeight, regular transport install, COMBATDROP_INTO gate.

title: [Cam] RESET_CAMERA drops ease-in/out
description:
## Why
C++ `RESET_CAMERA` eases heading/zoom/pitch back to defaults over the scripted seconds (`easeIn`/`easeOut`). Leftover dispatcher never reads those params; live host always stores 0/0 so the reset is linear (or a snap after the closed yaw/zoom bugs).

## C++
`ScriptActions.cpp:6500-6501` `doResetCamera(wp, sec, easeIn, easeOut)`.
`doResetCamera` (`:896-904`): `TheTacticalView->resetCamera(&destination, sec*1000, easeIn*1000, easeOut*1000)`.
`W3DView::resetCamera` animates move + `zoomCamera`/`pitchCamera` with those EaseClass times.

## Leftover
`do_reset_camera` (`actions_player_display_camera.rs:385-417`) reads only waypoint + duration (`params 0,1`). Params 2/3 (ease) are dropped.
Handler trait `reset_camera_to(x,y,z,duration)` has no ease fields.

## Live
`MissionScriptActionHandler::reset_camera_to` (`mission_scripts.rs:2039-2052`) writes `ease_in_seconds: 0.0`, `ease_out_seconds: 0.0`.
Closed hq-9o5v4 (default yaw / zoom-pitch snap) and hq-2mgn1 (zoom/pitch/rotate ease) do not restore RESET_CAMERA ease params.

## Player-visible
Cinematic camera resets pop linearly instead of the authored ease-in/out (e.g. mission intro "reset to Player_1_Start" over 2s with ease).
close_reason: do_reset_camera reads easeIn/easeOut; ScriptActionHandler::reset_camera_to and MissionScriptActionHandler push CameraResetRequest with those ease times.

title: [ControlBar] leftover tooltip populate stubs prereqs/CanMake and skips hover delay
description:
## Why
C++ `populateBuildTooltipLayout` (`ControlBarPopupDescription.cpp:225-662`) appends CanMake reasons (no money, queue full, parking, maxed), overcharge on/off, upgrade conflicting/purchased/missing-science, and real `ProductionPrerequisite::getRequiresList`. Leftover `populate_layout_for_command` (`gui_callbacks/control_bar_popup_description.rs:192-340`) builds prereqs as `let list = String::new()` (always empty), uses `calc_cost_to_build(None)` instead of the local player, and omits CanMake/overcharge/upgrade labels. `show_build_tooltip_layout` also sets `wait_initialized = true` on first hover of a new window, skipping the C++ tooltip delay (first hover starts wait and returns).

- Live leftover control_bar UI

title: [ControlBar] leftover setControlCommand never registers commandButtonTooltip
description:

title: [ControlBar] leftover inventory ALWAYS_COLOR keeps subdued exit cameos colored
description:

title: [Cam] Save/Use camera in replay stay off until Options opens
description:
## Why
C++ OptionPreferences defaults SaveCameraInReplays / UseCameraInReplays to TRUE when the key is missing, and GlobalData init copies those into m_saveCameraInReplay / m_useCameraInReplay. Live Common GlobalData constructs both false and nothing at boot applies Options.ini, so LookAt never records camera and playback never applies it.

## C++
OptionsMenu.cpp:361-382 missing key → TRUE.
GlobalData.cpp:1210-1211 TheWritableGlobalData->m_saveCameraInReplay / m_useCameraInReplay from optionPref at init.
LookAtXlat.cpp:459 emit MSG_SET_REPLAY_CAMERA only if m_saveCameraInReplay && (SP || skirmish).
GameLogicDispatch.cpp:1803 apply only if playback && m_useCameraInReplay && observer==thisPlayer.

## Leftover
GameClient options_menu.rs:352-357 get_bool_yes(..., true). menu_callbacks.rs:732-733 load Options.ini with default true, but only when the Options menu is constructed; apply writes common::global_data at 1111-1112.

## Live
common/global_data.rs:443-444 save_camera_in_replay / use_camera_in_replay default false.
Main mouse.rs:282 should_emit_host_replay_camera reads that flag. record_tap.rs:438 host_should_apply_replay_camera reads use_camera_in_replay. Boot never copies OptionPreferences into Common GlobalData.

## Player-visible
Unless the player opens Options (which then writes the prefs), replays record no camera path and playback never follows the recorded view. Defaults in retail are both on.

## Not a duplicate
hq-ceylk / hq-j3ufr / hq-kroc5 / hq-nqmua are observer apply / record-args / pitch (closed). This is the boot default that keeps those paths dark.
close_reason: GlobalData save_camera_in_replay / use_camera_in_replay default true to match OptionPreferences missing-key TRUE.

title: [Replay] Replay list dates are always 2001-01-01
description:
## Why
C++ writes SYSTEMTIME from GetLocalTime into the .rep header and ReplayMenu shows getUnicodeTimeBuffer(header.timeVal). Live maps that timestamp through a stub that freezes the calendar at 2001-01-01.

## C++
Recorder.cpp:557-560 fwrite SYSTEMTIME GetLocalTime.
ReplayMenu.cpp:149 displayTimeBuffer = getUnicodeTimeBuffer(header.timeVal); column 1 of the listbox.

## Leftover
common/recorder.rs:1592-1593 write_system_time_to_file(Local::now()) stores a real local date.

## Live
GameClient shell/replay_menu.rs:148-158 system_time_to_value hardcodes year=2001, month=1, day=1 and only derives hour/minute/second from UNIX epoch. map_common_header:166 uses that for every list row.

## Player-visible
Every replay in ReplayMenu shows a 2001-01-01 date. Sort-by-date and the date column are wrong.

## Not a duplicate
No closed bead covers ReplayMenu date display.
close_reason: system_time_to_value converts recorded SystemTime through chrono Local instead of freezing 2001-01-01.

title: [Replay] Last replay lists as 00000000 not GUI:LastReplay
description:
## Why
C++ records to 00000000.rep and the Replay browser relabels that stem GUI:LastReplay. Live leftover ReplayMenu compares against hardcoded LastReplay.rep, so the default file shows as 00000000.

## C++
Recorder.cpp:33 lastReplayFileName = \"00000000\"; startRecording writes getLastReplayFileName()+.rep.
ReplayMenu.cpp:144-147 if lastReplayFName.compareNoCase(asciistr)==0 then replayNameToShow = TheGameText->fetch(\"GUI:LastReplay\").
GetReplayFilenameFromListbox:69-72 reverse-maps GUI:LastReplay back to TheRecorder->getLastReplayFileName().

title: [Replay] ReplayMenu greys every .rep and always warns OlderReplayVersion
description:
## Why
C++ ReplayMenu colors and testVersionPlayback compare the file header against TheVersion + TheGlobalData exe/ini CRC. Live ReplayMenu hardcodes version 1.0 / number 100 / CRC 0, so every leftover-recorded GENREP looks incompatible.

## C++
ReplayMenu.cpp:203-230 white vs grey from versionString, versionNumber, exeCRC, iniCRC vs TheVersion / TheGlobalData.
ReplayMenu.cpp:536-538 Load uses TheRecorder->testVersionPlayback then GUI:OlderReplayVersion OkCancel.
Recorder.cpp:999-1021 testVersionPlayback compares those same five fields.

## Leftover

Recorder::test_version_playback matches C++.

## Live
GameClient shell/replay_menu.rs:459-463 ReplayMenu::new hardcodes last_replay_filename LastReplay, current_version \"1.0\", current_version_number 100, current_exe_crc 0, current_ini_crc 0. populate_replay_listbox:593-599 and load_replay:679-687 use those stubs. callbacks/replay_menu.rs:211-224 surfaces GUI:OlderReplayVersion on every load.

Every replay row is grey. Play always pops GUI:OlderReplayVersion even for a file just recorded this session.

## Not a duplicate
hq-pwhva / hq-f3tw9 / hq-323o are logic CRC on the sim tick, not ReplayMenu exe/ini version coloring.
