title: [SuperweaponCountdown] Live HUD ignores script hide, merges objects, shows READY
description:
## Why
C++ InGameUI SuperweaponCountdown is a per-object SuperweaponInfo list: integer mm:ss (0:00 when ready), ready-font + flash, skip UC, keep the row until module dtor (sell finish), SharedNSync dedupe only, honor global/per-object script hide. Live presentation builds one unlocked row per player+power and the drain always paints it.

hq-mns1 / hq-x3ve closed leftover crate InGameUI only.

## C++
`InGameUI.cpp:3535-3687` postDraw: skip `OBJECT_STATUS_UNDER_CONSTRUCTION`; `readySecs = (getReadyFrame()-now)/LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND` integer; format `%d:%2.2d` even when ready (0:00); ready font + `m_superweaponFlashDuration` flash; `isReady()` (pause/disabled) gates EVA/bold; SharedNSync `break` after first valid; `m_superweaponHiddenByScript` / per-info `m_hiddenByScript`.
`SpecialPowerModule.cpp:132-140` dtor `removeSuperweapon` — sell keeps the object (and row) until destroy.
`Player.cpp` sold skip is fire/count only, not HUD remove-on-sell-start.

## Leftover
`GameClient/src/gui/ingame_ui/impl_update.rs` leftover draw honors hide/science/flash. Not what the player runs.

## Live
`presentation_frame/build.rs:1183-1304` one row per PublicTimer power; structure-bound uses `min(remaining)` across all living constructed buildings; no sold filter, no `superweapon_display_enabled` / `superweapon_hidden_objects` filter (those fields are copied at `:1877-1887` but unused by the row builder).
Sell sets `construction_percent=0.999` (`rebuild_dozer.rs:545`) so `is_constructed()` is false and the row vanishes immediately.
`cnc_game_engine/camera_drain.rs:2445-2466` filters only `unlocked`, prints `"READY"` when `remaining<=0`, no flash. `ready` is `remaining<=0` — disabled/paused still READY.

## Player-visible
Campaign HideSuperweaponDisplay still shows the strip. Two PUCs show one soonest timer, not two rows. Ready reads READY not 0:00 and does not flash. Sell click deletes the countdown before the building finishes selling. Brownout/disabled ready PUC still reads READY (C++ 0:00, not bold).
close_reason: Live HUD honors script hide, emits per-object rows (SharedNSync still one), keeps sold until destroy, paints 0:00 not READY, brownout not bold.

title: [Partition] Value/threat cells use square world falloff, not DiscreteCircle cell-index
description:
## Why
C++ `doValueAffect` / `doThreatAffect` paint a DiscreteCircle of partition cells and fall off by **cell-index** distance over `(cellRadius+1)`. Live host now stamps cash/threat into leftover `PARTITION_MANAGER` (hq-iw8qa closed), but that leftover painter still uses a square ring and `1 - worldDist/worldRadius`. Skirmish `SKIRMISH_ATTACK_NEAREST_GROUP_WITH_VALUE` and leftover `getMostValuableLocation` therefore pick the wrong cell.

## C++
`PartitionManager.cpp:4087-4216` + `hLineAddThreat`/`hLineAddValue` `:5637-5745`:
- `worldToCell` + `worldToCellDist(radius)` (min 1), `DiscreteCircle(cx, cy, cellRadius)`.
- `mulVal = 1 - sqrt((x-xCenter)^2+(y-yCenter)^2) / (cellRadius+1)` where x/y are cell indices.
- `getNearestGroupWithValue` / `getMostValuableLocation` (`:4705-4798`) read those same `m_cells[]` cash/threat arrays. ScriptActions.cpp:5353-5355 and Player.cpp:1984 use `VOT_CashValue`.

## Leftover
`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/collide/partition_manager.rs:1439-1483` `distribute_cell_value`:
- Square `[-cell_radius..=cell_radius]` of cells.
- `mul = clamp(1 - hypot(cellCenter-worldCenter) / worldRadius, 0, 1)`.
Faithful DiscreteCircle + cell-index falloff lives only on `ShroudManager` (`shroud_manager.rs:638-684`) which is a **50wu** grid (closed hq-bfby9) and is **not** what `get_nearest_group_with_value` reads.

## Live
`Main/src/game_logic/partition_manager.rs:17-38` `HostPartitionAffectStamp::apply` → leftover `ThePartitionManager::do_value_affect` (`helpers/object_queries.rs:791-804`) writes **both** ShroudManager and leftover `PARTITION_MANAGER`. Live ScriptEngine (`world_scripts/scripts_camera.rs:475-490`) runs leftover `do_skirmish_attack_nearest_group_with_value` (`actions_skirmish.rs:465-476`) which reads leftover `get_nearest_group_with_value`.

## Player-visible
Skirmish AI `SKIRMISH_ATTACK_NEAREST_GROUP_WITH_VALUE` attack-moves to the wrong 40wu cell (corners over-painted, edge cells under-painted vs retail). Distinct from closed hq-iw8qa (never stamped) and hq-c3q9 (disconnected stores — live now writes leftover cells).
close_reason: Leftover do_value/do_threat use DiscreteCircle + cell-index falloff over (cellRadius+1).

title: [Physics] Friction skipped for debris and disabled; ExtraFriction never applied
description:
## C++
PhysicsUpdate.cpp:427-476 applyFrictionalForces every non-HELD PhysicsBehavior::update (630-631). getForward/Lateral/AeroFriction add m_extraFriction (OCL ObjectCreationList.cpp:1122 setExtraFriction, SlowDeath.cpp:282). Debris and disabled units still run physics (DISABLEDMASK_ALL).

## Leftover
GameEngine physics_update.rs:841 apply_frictional_forces on every update; extra_friction stored on PhysicsBehaviorState.

## Live host
world_tick/shock.rs:48 applies apply_frictional_forces only if can_move() || destroyed || !alive. can_move (orders.rs:5) is false for !is_mobile debris, EMP/unmanned/hacked/freefall, stun-flail, deployed. extra_friction is written only by set_locomotor_physics_options (physics.rs:644-645 loco Extra2D + ultra). OCL/SlowDeath never call setExtraFriction.

## Player-visible
Death debris and disabled/unmanned wrecks keep sliding instead of scrubbing to rest, so KillWhenRestingOnGround never fires. OCL ExtraFriction=-0.3 flying chunks stop as fast as normal units instead of skating.
close_reason: Live host: bounce audio only if authored BounceSound; ExtraFriction from OCL/SlowDeath; wrecks stay in partition and collide; mobile collide is -overlap applyForce; KillWhenResting uses Object::kill.

title: [Physics] Landing always plays BodyFallGeneric
description:
## C++
PhysicsUpdate.cpp:822-824, 1089-1092: WAS_AIRBORNE_LAST_FRAME && !airborneAtEnd && !IMMUNE → doBounceSound(prevPos). doBounceSound returns immediately unless m_bounceSound was set (OCL ObjectCreationList.cpp:1124 setBounceSound, or SlowDeath). Retail does not compile FIX_AUDIO volume shaping.

## Leftover
GameEngine physics_bounce.rs:112-114 plays only if bounce_sound is Some; comments that FIX_AUDIO is not retail.

## Live host
Main/src/game_logic/object/construct.rs initializes bounce_sound_name = BodyFallGeneric on every object. physics_motion.rs:468-476 record_bounce_land always increments bounce_audio_pending and defaults empty names to BodyFallGeneric. world_tick/shock.rs:198-212 drains that into TheAudio.

## Player-visible
Every airborne→ground land (shock toss, jet landing, parachute, hop) plays a generic body-fall thud. C++ is silent unless the template/OCL authored a BounceSound. Authored OCL bounce events are replaced by BodyFallGeneric.
close_reason: Live host: bounce audio only if authored BounceSound; ExtraFriction from OCL/SlowDeath; wrecks stay in partition and collide; mobile collide is -overlap applyForce; KillWhenResting uses Object::kill.

title: [Physics] Mobile collide force is +0.5 kick not -overlap push
description:
## C++
PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1386-1398 when processCollision returns true (panic infantry, or no-AI bounce): overlap capped at 5, force = -overlap * delta/dist, applyForce. Immobile uses structure stiffness instead.

## Leftover
GameEngine physics_collide.rs:264-278 implements the same -min(overlap,5)*delta/dist apply_force path. Not live.

## Live host
world_tick/physics.rs:313-360: mobile-mobile goes through ai_process_collision; if it returns true (panic infantry / immobile-other fallback) live adds velocity += 0.5 * unit XZ separation. No overlap-magnitude force, no applyForce.

## Player-visible
Panicking infantry and other processCollision=true pairs barely nudge instead of being pushed apart by overlap. Units remain interpenetrated; crowd bounce looks wrong vs retail.
close_reason: Live host: bounce audio only if authored BounceSound; ExtraFriction from OCL/SlowDeath; wrecks stay in partition and collide; mobile collide is -overlap applyForce; KillWhenResting uses Object::kill.

title: [Physics] Dead wrecks skip collide force and pass through buildings
description:
## C++
PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1255-1265: dead or parachuting vs immobile skips processCollision and still applies collide force (1312-1398 structure-stiffness bounce, crash weapons, vel nuke). Dead objects stay in PartitionManager and onCollide.

## Leftover
GameEngine physics_collide.rs:198 applies immobile bounce when !obj.is_destroyed() for stiffness path, but dead+immobile still reaches force when the AI gate is skipped in C++ order. Live leftover on_collide is not what the player runs.

## Live host
world_tick/shock.rs:73-74: destroyed / !alive objects are not partition-registered, so try_physics_collide never sees wrecks. apply_immobile_collide_bounce (world_tick/physics.rs:509-510) also returns false if mover.status.destroyed.

## Player-visible
Exploded vehicle hulks (Euler now runs; hq-5fef6 closed) fly through buildings and units instead of bouncing off / crashing into them.
close_reason: Live host: bounce audio only if authored BounceSound; ExtraFriction from OCL/SlowDeath; wrecks stay in partition and collide; mobile collide is -overlap applyForce; KillWhenResting uses Object::kill.

title: [Physics] KillWhenResting uses stun-destroy not Object::kill
description:
## C++
PhysicsUpdate.cpp:883-892: KillWhenRestingOnGround && !airborneAtEnd && isVerySmall3D(vel) → obj->kill() unless a living manned drone. kill() runs Body/Die modules (FX, OCL chunks, scoring).

## Leftover
GameEngine physics_update.rs:1032-1040 calls obj.kill(None, None) on the same gate.

## Live host
physics_motion.rs:537-552 maybe_kill_when_resting_on_ground calls kill_from_stun_destruction: HP=0, destroyed=true, DeathType::Normal, no DieMux / death weapon / death OCL. Also uses height>0.05 as airborne instead of isAboveTerrain (height>0).

## Player-visible
Rest-kill debris/props (rocks, bones, spent projectiles) wink out with no death FX/OCL. Combined with the friction can_move gate they often never settle, so they linger sliding instead of vanishing.
close_reason: Live host: bounce audio only if authored BounceSound; ExtraFriction from OCL/SlowDeath; wrecks stay in partition and collide; mobile collide is -overlap applyForce; KillWhenResting uses Object::kill.

title: [Bounty] Live doBountyForKill skips ScoreKeeper money_earned
description:
## C++
Player.cpp:2400-2426 doBountyForKill deposits cash then m_scoreKeeper.addMoneyEarned(bounty). ScoreKeeper.cpp:315-330 calculateScore adds m_totalMoneyEarned 1:1. Crates/supply/hack also go through addMoneyEarned.

Never add_money_earned (player.rs:887-891). destroy_list_bounty.rs:678-685 awards via do_bounty_for_kill. calculate_score (player.rs:1196-1204) uses money_earned, not resources_collected. Supply/crate/hack paths already call add_money_earned.

GLA cash-bounty kills add cash to the bank and the victory \"Collected\" column, but the C++ score number (and any overlay using calculate_score) is short by every bounty dollar.

title: [Bounty] Cash bounty uses raw BuildCost not victim calcCostToBuild
description:
## C++
Player.cpp:2409-2410 Int costToBuild = victim->getTemplate()->calcCostToBuild(victim->getControllingPlayer()); bounty = ceil(cost * m_cashBountyPercent). ThingTemplate.cpp:1508-1516 applies production-cost-change percent, KindOf cost change, and Handicap::BUILDCOST. No player → 0.

## Leftover
common/rts/player.rs:2903-2906 and GameLogic player/production.rs:459-467 use victim.get_build_cost(). Leftover BountyObject (object_thing.rs:391-394) calls calc_cost_to_build(None) which leftover thing_template.rs:3106-3107 returns 0.

## Player-visible
Cash bounty pays the victim's INI BuildCost. Killing a cost-modified unit (GLA worker discount, CostModifierUpgrade, BUILDCOST handicap) over/under-pays vs C++. Leftover scoreTheKill path would pay $0.
close_reason: Live destroy_list_bounty uses victim calcCostToBuild (modified_build_cost_supplies + owner handicap/kindof/template). Leftover BountyObject/do_bounty_for_kill_obj use controlling-player calc_cost_to_build; no player → 0.

title: [ClusterMines] DropVariance never offsets the field
description:
## C++
`SUPERWEAPON_ClusterMines` DeliverPayload authors `DropVariance X:20 Y:20 Z:0`. The cargo plane drops `ClusterMinesBomb` at click + variance, then GenerateMinefieldBehavior SmartBorder (DistanceAroundObject 80) places ChinaClusterMine pads around that offset point.

## Leftover
`generate_minefield_behavior.rs` is Wave 386 empty-registry gated and never runs live. Helpers `host_mines.rs` `apply_cluster_mines_drop_variance` and `host_deliver_payload.rs` constants exist but are honesty-only.

`world_combat/special_power_flights.rs` `update_cluster_mines_flights`: bomb is created at exact `target` (Y=80) and on impact `place_cluster_mines(team, impact, producer)` uses that same click. title: [FXList] Live host never calls doFXObj so death/damage FX stay unoriented
description:
## C++
`FXList::doFXObj` (`FXList.cpp:794-804`) is the object form used by FXListDie, SlowDeath phase FX, TransitionDamage one-shot FX, DamageFX, Upgrade `FXListUpgrade`, InstantDeath. `ParticleSystemFXNugget::doFXObj` (`:514-534`) passes the object transform (or ricochet Z-matrix) and `thingToAttachTo=primary` so `AttachToObject` + `OrientToObject` + Offset follow the wreck. `FXListAtBonePos` (`:673-676`) **only** works via doFXObj (`doFXPos` crashes "You must use the object form").

## Leftover

## Live
`host_fx_list_dispatch.rs:43-58` only `TheFXList::do_fx_at_position_ex` → leftover `do_fx_pos` with **mtx=None** and **no object**. Callers: `world_tick/ai.rs:374/422` death + TransitionDamage FX names, `host_transition_damage_fx.rs:605`, `object/death.rs` topple/bounce, `host_fx_list_die.rs` only returns names (`orient_to_object` stored, unused).

Closed hq-br7up was "never dispatches" — they now dispatch **doFXPos**. Remaining is the object form.

## Player-visible
Death/damage/upgrade FX spawn at object center, unoriented. `AttachToObject` fire/smoke do not follow a sinking wreck. `FXListAtBonePos` never runs (turret/bone death FX missing).
close_reason: dispatch_fx_list_at_object calls leftover TheFXList::do_fx_obj; death/transition FX in world_tick/ai.rs use object form

title: [Particles] Attached fire/smoke follow is world translation not parent*local
description:
## C++
`ActiveBody::createParticleSystems` (`ActiveBody.cpp:1033-1041`): `createParticleSystem`, `setPosition(pos)` in **local bone space** from `getMultiLogicalBonePosition`, `attachToObject`. `ParticleSystem::update` (`ParticleSys.cpp:1910-1927`) `m_transform = parentXfrm * m_localTransform` so fire/smoke rotate with the hull.

`ParticleSystem::setPosition` (`:1281-1286`) writes **local Matrix3D translation**, not world.

## Leftover
`helpers/particles.rs:311-319` `attach_particle_system_to_object` attaches without `setPosition`. Leftover GameClient `set_position` writes local translation and `resolve_attached_parent` concatenates parent 4x4 (hq-dwtov closed leftover). Live does not drive that path for tracked systems.

## Live
`combat_particles.rs:1360-1420` `spawn_body_systems_on_bones`: `spawn_with_template` at **world** bone (mirrors an unattached client system via `create_preset_system_xyz`), then leftover attach creates a **second** system whose id is discarded because `client_system_id` is already set. `attach_offset = world - origin` (world-space).

`follow_attached_body_particles` (`:1034-1062`): `position + attach_offset` only — no yaw. `mirror_update_client_system_position` overwrites leftover attach with a world point.

Closed hq-so1vh / hq-2vh87 were "spawn at center / never spawn bones". They now spawn on bones; remaining is attach follow.

Also `spawn_auto_aflame_particles` (`combat_fire_fx.rs:146-156`) stamps `AutoAflame` through `spawn_weapon_fire_fx_named` at origin (WeaponMuzzleFlash / FXList path) while `replace_body_auto_particles` already attaches AFLAME-prefix systems.

## Player-visible
Fire/smoke on a turning damaged vehicle stay at the old world offset instead of rotating with the hull. Extra AutoAflame cue at the object's feet when ignited. Leftover attached systems are orphaned.
close_reason: attach_offset is unyawed local; follow is parent*local yaw; leftover attach not overwritten with world setPosition; extra AutoAflame muzzle spawn removed

title: [INI] Object DisplayName is stored untranslated so unit captions show OBJECT: keys
description:

title: [Radar] Shroud copy treats partition cells as radar cells so FOW is the wrong scale
description:
## C++
PartitionManager.cpp:1263-1265 / 3009-3011 calls TheRadar->setShroudLevel(m_cellX, m_cellY, status) with partition shroud-cell indices. W3DRadar.cpp:1252-1311 setShroudLevel converts those cells to world (cell * shroudCellWidth/Height) then worldToRadar, and paints the radar-pixel rectangle. Radar is a fixed 128x128 sample of the map, not 1:1 with the 40wu partition grid.

## Leftover
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/system/shroud_manager.rs:2136-2153 refresh_radar_shroud_for_player walks shroud_grid (SHROUD_GRID_CELL_SIZE 40) and calls radar.set_shroud_level(x, y, status) with the same x,y. leftover radar/mod.rs:1685-1695 set_shroud_level indexes the 128x128 radar shroud_grid directly — no worldToRadar.

## Live
GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/radar_live.rs:77-86 host_refresh_radar_shroud and :349-352 host_radar_sync_live_objects push leftover ShroudManager cells onto TheRadar via that 1:1 copy.

close_reason: ShroudManager now calls set_shroud_level_from_partition_cell: partition cell * 40wu → worldToRadar rectangle, matching W3DRadar.cpp:1252-1311.

title: [Radar] Terrain sample_cell is always flat; live never queues terrain refresh
description:
## C++
Radar.cpp:42 / 294-301 / 1320-1345: queueTerrainRefresh records the current frame; update rebuilds after RADAR_QUEUE_TERRAIN_REFRESH_DELAY (3s). W3DRadar.cpp:1421-1429 refreshTerrain rebuilds the terrain texture from TerrainVisual / water / bridges. BridgeBehavior.cpp:675-676 queues on rubble edge. title: [Radar] Hidden drawables still blip; leftover isTemporarilyHidden skips C++ drawable hidden
description:

Radar.cpp:118-125 RadarObject::isTemporarilyHidden returns true when Drawable::getStealthLook()==STEALTHLOOK_INVISIBLE OR Drawable::isDrawableEffectivelyHidden() (m_hidden || m_hiddenByStealth). Hijacker-in-vehicle, script-hidden, and fully stealthed drawables drop off the radar each draw.

title: [HordeUpdate] Live ignores infantry vs vehicle UpdateRate sleep
description:
## C++
`HordeUpdate::update` (`HordeUpdate.cpp:253-294`, `:369`): infantry always rechecks membership on wake, then `UPDATE_SLEEP(UpdateRate)` (retail 1000ms → 30f). Vehicles return `UPDATE_SLEEP_NONE` (decal size refresh every frame after model-state rebuild) but membership is gated on `frame > lastHordeRefreshFrame + UpdateRate`. Constructor random-sleeps first wake 1..UpdateRate (`:146-147`).

title: [HordeUpdate] Live Fanaticism decal skips C++ weapon-bonus nesting

title: [Radar] Construction/upgrade/battle-plan/overcharge never ping TheRadar
description:
## C++
Radar.cpp:995-1075 createEvent / createPlayerEvent write a 64-slot ring buffer ping (color table, 4s live, 0.5s fade, last-event except beacon). Callers:
- DozerAIUpdate.cpp:620 RADAR_EVENT_CONSTRUCTION on build complete

title: [Pathfind] moveAllies scoots packing and busy units that C++ leaves planted

## C++

title: [Pathfind] Queue overflow drops the oldest waiter instead of refusing the new request
description:
## Why
C++ `queueForPath` is a 512-slot ring: duplicate ObjectID is a no-op; a full queue DEBUG_CRASH/returns false and leaves already-queued units in place. Live `queue_path` pops the oldest PendingHostPath so that unit stays `waiting_for_path` with no request left.

Closed hq-is19 (async vs sync / PATHFIND_CELLS_PER_FRAME) and hq-ah4jh (queued move marched at dest) are different. Live now defers one frame and sits still — remaining queue gap is overflow eviction.

## C++
`AIPathfind.h:418` PATHFIND_QUEUE_LEN=512. `queueForPath` (`AIPathfind.cpp:5624-5662`): scan for existing id; if nextSlot==head return false. `processPathfindQueue` (`:5857-5938`) drains while `m_cumulativeCellsAllocated < PATHFIND_CELLS_PER_FRAME` (5000). AIUpdate `requestPath` (`AIUpdate.cpp:480-497`) sets m_waitingForPath then queues the ObjectID (dest lives on AIUpdate).

## Leftover
`pathfind_complete/construct.rs:139-163` `queue_path_request` / `queue_for_path`: dedupe + `Err("Pathfind queue full")` / false. `process_queue` respects PATHFIND_CELLS_PER_FRAME.

## Live host
`pathfinding.rs:2130-2134` `queue_path`: if `pending_paths.len() >= PATHFIND_QUEUE_LEN` pop_front then push. No dedupe. `world_save.rs:837-857` sets waiting_for_path and zeroes velocity before enqueue. Evicted unit is never taken by `process_pathfind_queue` (`:1088-1140`).

## Player-visible
Select-all move on a 512+ army evicts the first units' pending paths. Those units stand forever in waiting_for_path (zero velocity) until another order. C++ keeps the oldest waiters and refuses the newest.
close_reason: queue_path dedupes ObjectID and refuses when full (no pop_front). world_save only sets waiting_for_path after a successful enqueue.

title: [Pathfind] Structure-aware zones treat water as walkable so rally crosses rivers
description:

Closed hq-996dq (no rally gate) and hq-9erk0 (ForUI terrain-only) are the earlier rally beads. Live now calls structure-aware `quick_path_exists` — remaining water bug is that those zones include water.

## C++
`Pathfinder::clientSafeQuickDoesPathExist` (`AIPathfind.cpp:7997-8044`): `validMovementPosition(false, destLayer, loco, to)` then `getEffectiveZone(loco.surfaces, false, zone)`. Ground-only BasicHumanLocomotor (rally) fails water dest and water-split zones.
`validLocomotorSurfacesForCellType` (`:4734-4756`): CELL_WATER → SURFACE_WATER|AIR only.
`classifyMapCell` (`:4506-4512`): any of 4 corners underwater → CELL_WATER.

## Leftover

## Live host
`pathfinding.rs:756-764` `path_zone_passable` excludes Impassable/Obstacle/BridgeImpassable/Cliff but **includes Water**. `quick_path_exists` (`:813-829`) only hard-rejects cliff and non-fence obstacle goals. Rally (`world_scripts/unit_commands.rs:1001-1009`) uses that check. `terrain_zone_passable` (`:680-688`) does split on water, but rally does not use ForUI.

## Player-visible
Player can set a factory rally across a river or in the water — no GUI:RallyPointNoPath. Produced tanks walk into the drink or stall. Distinct from closed water-rise (hq-xc1l3) and classify water-wins-cliff (hq-498le).
close_reason: path_zone_passable excludes Water; quick_path_exists rejects a water dest. Rally no longer treats rivers as walkable structure-aware zones.

title: [Topple] Fall always pitches +X instead of crush direction
description:
## C++
`ToppleUpdate::applyTopplingForce` (`ToppleUpdate.cpp:161-186`) orients so the model's X is perpendicular to the topple direction (planar props fall flat). `update` (`:268-271`) applies `In_Place_Pre_Rotate_X(-vel * dir.y)` and `In_Place_Pre_Rotate_Y(vel * dir.x)` so the tree falls away from the crusher / blast.

## Live host

title: [Tracer] FireFX tracers get weaponSpeed=0 so streaks die instantly
description:
## C++
`Weapon::fireWeaponTemplate` (`Weapon.cpp:923-939`) passes `getWeaponSpeed()` into `Drawable::handleWeaponFireFX` then `FXList::doFXPos(..., primarySpeed, victimPos, ...)`. `TracerFXNugget::doFXPos` (`FXList.cpp:148-193`) requires primary+secondary, uses `m_speed` or `primarySpeed` when authored Speed is 0 (default), then `setTracerParms(speed,...)` and expires in `ceil((dist-length)/speed * DecayAt)` frames. Line3D translates local-X by that speed every draw.

## Leftover

Expiration uses leftover `tracer_expiration_frames` (`tracer_fx.rs:81-87`): `dist/speed` when `speed >= 0`. Speed 0 → inf → `as u32` 0 → expire same frame. `do_draw_module` also skips the local-X translate when speed is 0.

description:

title: [Weapon] Garrisoned 133% range applies to every contained unit
description:
## Why
C++ applies `WEAPONBONUSCONDITION_GARRISONED` (GameData RANGE 133%) only when GarrisonContain (or Helix) `onContaining` sets the flag. Live multiplies range by 1.33 for every unit with `contained_by`.

## C++

title: [Garrison] Fire points stay on pristine bones after Damaged/ReallyDamaged
description:

`loadGarrisonPoints` (`GarrisonContain.cpp:1282-1370`) temporarily sets MODELCONDITION_GARRISONED + each damage flag, `getMultiLogicalBonePosition("FIREPOINT")` into `m_garrisonPoint[PRISTINE|DAMAGED|REALLY_DAMAGED]`, then restores flags.
`findConditionIndex` (`:211-248`) picks the array from `body->getDamageState()`.
`calcBestGarrisonPosition` / `putObjectAtGarrisonPoint` use that index. Damage-state change calls `redeployOccupants`.

## Leftover

After a garrisoned building is Damaged or ReallyDamaged, window shots still come from the pristine-model FIREPOINT locations. Retail re-aims from the damaged model's windows.

title: [Heal] HealContain auto-exit dumps in an 8-unit circle instead of ExitStart/End
description:
## Why

## C++

`OpenContain::exitObjectViaDoor` (`OpenContain.cpp:915-1028`): ExitStart/ExitEnd bones (cycled if `NumberOfExitPaths > 1`), layer match, pathfind add, 1s collision ignore, `aiFollowPath` through end + rally.

title: [Garrison] Stealth hide uses STEALTHED bits not KINDOF_STEALTH_GARRISON count
description:
## Why
C++ hides a garrisoned building from non-allies only when every occupant is `KINDOF_STEALTH_GARRISON` and the first is not DETECTED. Live hides when every occupant is currently `stealthed && !detected`.

## C++
`recalcApparentControllingPlayer` (`GarrisonContain.cpp:1201-1204`): `m_hideGarrisonedStateFromNonallies = (!detected && getStealthUnitsContained() == getContainCount())`. `stealthUnitsContained` increments only for `KINDOF_STEALTH_GARRISON` (`OpenContain.cpp:347-350`). MODELCONDITION_GARRISONED is set only if the first occupant is DETECTED or the local player is the apparent controller (`:1227-1244`).

## Leftover
`garrison_contain.rs` ports the kind-count hide flag. Dual-world empty.

## Live
`recalc_garrison_apparent_controller` (`drones_and_garrison.rs:1008-1019`): `all_stealth = occupants.iter().all(|o| o.status.stealthed && !o.status.detected)`; `hide = !first_detected && all_stealth`.
`note_garrison_occupant_entered` (`orders.rs:735`) seeds hide from a single occupant's stealthed bit.

## Player-visible
- A building full of ordinary stealthed infantry (not STEALTH_GARRISON) looks empty to enemies; retail shows it occupied.
- STEALTH_GARRISON occupants who destalth while firing reveal the building; retail keeps hide from the kind count until DETECTED.

## Not a duplicate
hq-lgt8x (closed) added the hide freeze (occupant_count zeroed for non-allies). The hide *predicate* still does not match C++ kind-count.

title: [Contain] Transport passenger fire originates at hull center not FIREPOINT bones

title: [Burn] Presentation clobbers live AFLAME from death type name
description:
## C++
`FlammableUpdate::tryToIgnite` (`FlammableUpdate.cpp:175-177`) sets `OBJECT_STATUS_AFLAME` + `MODELCONDITION_AFLAME` while the object is still alive. Burned timer (`:122-123`) adds `MODELCONDITION_SMOLDERING` while still aflame, then `BURNED` after `AflameDuration`. Death type is unrelated.

title: [Cam] MOVE_CAMERA_TO_SELECTION starts a new lookAt, not path retarget
description:
## C++
`ScriptActions::doModCameraMoveToSelection` (`ScriptActions.cpp:867-889`) averages selected drawable positions and calls `TheTacticalView->cameraModFinalMoveTo`. `W3DView::cameraModFinalMoveTo` (`W3DView.cpp:2637-2654`) is a path modifier: no-op during rotate; if a waypoint path is running, it shifts waypoints `[2..num]` so the path *ends* at the selection centroid. UI name: "End movement at selected unit."

## Leftover
`script_action_handler.rs:824-859` + `view.rs:2503-2524` `camera_mod_final_move_to` retargets leftover `camera_path` / in-flight `camera_move`. Not on the live OS camera path.

## Live
`MissionScriptActionHandler::move_camera_to_selection` queues a hook. `scripts_camera.rs:494-502` drains it into `request_camera_focus(selected_objects_center)` (clears follow). `camera_drain.rs:189-191` `center_camera_on` that point — a new lookAt, not a retarget of the current MOVE/PATH.

## Player-visible
A cinematic MOVE_CAMERA_ALONG_WAYPOINT_PATH followed by MOVE_CAMERA_TO_SELECTION should bend the remaining path onto the selected unit. Live cancels/ignores that path and snaps/re-centers on the selection centroid.
close_reason: MOVE_CAMERA_TO_SELECTION retargets ScriptCameraPathMove/MoveTo (C++ cameraModFinalMoveTo [2..num]); no new lookAt.

title: [Cam] Default control bar never shrinks live 3D tactical viewport to 80%
description:
## C++
`ControlBar::setDefaultControlBarConfig` (`ControlBar.cpp:3001-3014`) sets `TheTacticalView->setHeight(0.80 * displayHeight)`. `setLowControlBarConfig` (`:3030-3046`) restores full display height. `W3DView::setHeight` (`W3DView.cpp:180-190`) updates the 3D camera viewport (`vMax.Y = (originY+height)/displayHeight`) and aspect ratio so the bottom 20% is HUD-only. Look-at, edge-scroll, and picks use that 80% rect.

## Leftover
`impl_science.rs:598-614` `leftover_set_tactical_view_height` writes leftover `View::set_height` (80% or full). `View::set_height` (`view.rs:828-830`) only stores an integer — no WGPU viewport.

## Live
Main 3D camera / pick / edge-scroll always use the full window (`viewport_size`, `mouse.rs` NDC). No consumer of leftover `View::height()`. `shell.rs` `switch_control_bar_stage(Default)` never shrinks the live frustum. Distinct from closed hq-sx1jf (leftover bar stage now writes leftover height).

## Player-visible
Default control bar overlays the 3D world. Units under the bar stay visible and clickable. Screen-center look-at and edge-scroll bands sit on the full window, not the retail 80% tactical rect.

title: [Hijack] Stolen vehicle keeps its own vision/shroud ranges
description:
## C++
`ConvertToHijackedVehicleCrateCollide::executeCrateBehavior` (`ConvertToHijackedVehicleCrateCollide.cpp:221-223`) copies the hijacker's vision and shroud-clearing ranges onto the vehicle after hide-in-vehicle: `other->setVisionRange(getObject()->getVisionRange())` and `setShroudClearingRange`. title: [Hijack] Ride-hide never hides drawable or unregisters partition
description:

When the target has `EjectPilotDieInterface` (`ConvertToHijackedVehicleCrateCollide.cpp:180-233`), execute does not destroy the hijacker: `leaveGroup`, `aiIdle`, `OBJECT_STATUS_NO_COLLISIONS|MASKED|UNSELECTABLE`, `ThePartitionManager->unRegisterObject`, and `getDrawable()->setDrawableHidden(true)`. title: [Weapon] Live splash applies RadiusDamageAffects to the intended target
description:
## Why
C++ always damages the designated primary victim and only then applies `RadiusDamageAffects` to bystanders. Live splash with `explosion_radius > 0` emits only an Area event and runs `radius_damage_affects_victim` on every object, including the intended target.

## C++
`Weapon.cpp:1316-1375`: `if (curVictim != primaryVictim)` then SELF / NOT_SIMILAR / NOT_AIRBORNE / ALLIES|ENEMIES|NEUTRALS. Primary skips the entire mask.
`Weapon.cpp:1296-1306` / `:1440-1452`: `WEAPON_KILLS_SELF` deals `HUGE_DAMAGE_AMOUNT` to self.

## Leftover
`weapon_instance_combat.rs` `is_primary_victim` bypasses the mask. `damage_application.rs` `should_apply_damage(..., is_primary_victim=true)` always true. Dual-world empty-gate; unused.

## Live
`combat.rs` target-hit with `explosion_radius > 0` pushes `DamageEvent::Area` only (no Direct). Area loop calls `radius_damage_affects_victim` with no primary-id exception. That helper returns false for allies when the mask is the default ENEMIES|NEUTRALS, and treats self as SELF-only (never `WEAPON_KILLS_SELF` huge).

## Player-visible
Ctrl-fire on an ally with a splash gun (Battlemaster r=5, most tank guns) deals no damage. NOT_AIRBORNE poison / neutron splash skips a targeted aircraft. SUICIDE weapons on the generic fire path do not guarantee self-kill.

## Not a duplicate
Closed collide / FireWhen / suicide-residual beads cover named peels, not `dealDamageInternal` primary-victim exemption on live splash.
close_reason: Intended primary victim skips RadiusDamageAffects; WEAPON_KILLS_SELF deals huge self damage.

title: [Weapon] Splash secondary ring ignores live DAMAGE bonus
description:
## Why
C++ scales both splash rings with `WeaponBonus::DAMAGE` at fire/detonate time. Live applies `effective_weapon_damage` only to the primary amount and stamps store `SecondaryDamage` / `SecondaryDamageRadius` raw.

## C++
`Weapon.cpp:507-527` `getPrimaryDamage` / `getSecondaryDamage` / radii all multiply bonus fields.
`Weapon.cpp:1797-1816` `computeBonus` every fire (veterancy, PLAYER_UPGRADE, frenzy, …).
`Weapon.cpp:1438` outer ring uses `secondaryDamage` already bonus-scaled.

## Leftover
`weapon_instance_combat.rs` `get_primary_damage(bonus)` / `get_secondary_damage(bonus)`. Unused on the live path.

## Live
`object/attack.rs` `weapon_damage = effective_weapon_damage(template_damage)` for `PendingProjectile.damage`.
`secondary_damage` / `secondary_damage_radius` come from `host_secondary_damage_*_for_weapon_name` with no DAMAGE/RADIUS multiply.
`weapon_bonus_fields` returns only (DAMAGE, RANGE, ROF, PRE_ATTACK) — no RADIUS slot.

## Player-visible
Veteran / Uranium / AP / Frenzy splash: inner ring grows, outer ring stays retail-base (Overlord 25 not 31.25; Scud / nuke cannon outer ring unbuffed). Nearby units in the secondary ring take less damage than retail.

## Not a duplicate
`hq-mc8j9` (closed) was veterancy never applied at fire — live now scales primary. This is the remaining secondary-ring miss.
close_reason: fire_at stamps SecondaryDamage with WeaponBonus DAMAGE via effective_weapon_damage.

title: [Weapon] Live splash uses center distance not FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_3D
description:
## Why
C++ `dealDamageInternal` iterates splash with `DAMAGE_RANGE_CALC_TYPE = FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_3D` (center-to-center minus victim bounding-sphere radius). Live combat area damage uses raw `Vec3::distance` to object origin, so large tanks and buildings whose hull is inside the ring but whose center is outside take no splash.

## C++
`Weapon.cpp:70` `DAMAGE_RANGE_CALC_TYPE = FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_3D`.
`Weapon.cpp:1283` `iterateObjectsInRange(pos, radius, DAMAGE_RANGE_CALC_TYPE)`.
`Weapon.cpp:1438` amount is primary vs secondary from that partition `curVictimDistSqr`, not raw center.

## Leftover
`weapon_template.rs` `get_objects_in_range` calls `partition.get_objects_in_range_boundary_3d`. Unused while `OBJECT_REGISTRY` is empty.

## Live
`combat.rs` Area handler: `let dist = op.distance(*position);` then `dist <= primary_r` / `outer`. No bounding-sphere subtraction. Fired from `object/attack.rs` `queue_projectile` → `CombatSystem::update_projectiles`.

## Player-visible
Scud / Overlord / Battlemaster splash misses nearby structures and large vehicles that retail would clip with the hull. Aircraft altitude also shrinks the ring because height is included with no sphere credit.

## Not a duplicate

title: [Production] Factory exit uses generic path, not aiFollowExitProductionPath
description:
## C++
`ProductionUpdate::update` (`ProductionUpdate.cpp:802-803`) hands every finished unit to `ExitInterface::exitObjectViaDoor`.

`DefaultProductionExitUpdate::exitObjectViaDoor` (`DefaultProductionExitUpdate.cpp:41-97`):
- transform INI `UnitCreatePoint` through the producer matrix
- snap Z to `getLayerHeight` and copy the producer layer
- build a 2-point path: natural rally (offset=TRUE), then `adjustDestination` of the custom rally if set
- `aiFollowExitProductionPath(path, factory)` so the unit walks through the door, ignores the producer, and can path through other units

`QueueProductionExitUpdate::exitObjectViaDoor` (`QueueProductionExitUpdate.cpp:47-143`) additionally `pathfinder->snapPosition` on the natural rally and **doubles** that snapped point when there is no custom rally (Red Guards must not stack).

## Leftover
`queue_production_exit_behavior.rs:510-540` and `default_production_exit_behavior.rs` port snap + `ai_follow_exit_production_path`. Unused on the live host (`OBJECT_REGISTRY` empty).

## Live
`world_tick/production.rs` `host_apply_production_spawn_ready_completions` (`:1377-1406`) does `path_approach_with_state(new_id, natural)` then `append_unit_waypoint` for custom/doubled rally. It never:
- calls `ExitInterface` / `aiFollowExitProductionPath`
- passes the producer as `ignore_obstacle` (`path_approach_with_state_ignoring` exists unused)
- `snapPosition`s the Queue natural rally
- `adjustDestination`s the custom rally
- snaps spawn Z to terrain layer (`transform_model_exit_offset` keeps producer Y + INI Z)

## Player-visible
New infantry/vehicles stack at the barracks door, path around the factory instead of through the exit, stall on the producer footprint, and pop out at the building origin height on slopes.
close_reason: Live factory exit now uses aiFollowExitProductionPath: ignore producer, snap Queue natural, adjustDestination custom rally, snap spawn Z to terrain.

title: [Terrain] Dozer flatten is cylinder-only; box buildings leave sloped corners
description:

## C++
`TerrainLogic.cpp:2620-2746` GEOMETRY_BOX: Cos/Sin oriented corners, Point_In_Triangle_2D, average height, `setRawMapHeight` 3x3 (only lowers).
Cylinder/sphere (`:2748+`) uses majorRadius disk.
`DozerAIUpdate.cpp:1692-1698` flattenTerrain then getGroundHeight Z snap then addObjectToPathfindMap.

## Leftover
`GameLogic/src/terrain.rs` `flatten_terrain` (`:3080-3256`) ports both Box and Cylinder. Crate `build_assistant_bridge.rs:94-99` calls `flatten_terrain(&new_object)` (full geom). Not the live host path.

## Player-visible

title: [Campaign] Load-screen briefing voice plays after prelude; C++ ZH MD never plays it

`SinglePlayerLoadScreen::init` (`LoadScreen.cpp:393-591`) fills objective/unit/location text from `TheCampaignManager->getCurrentMission()`, then opens the intro movie. `moveWindows` (`:217-220`) is the only caller of `TheAudio->friend_forcePlayAudioEventRTS(&mission->m_briefingVoice)` at frame 255 and the objective teletype — but the movie loop marks it `// PULLED FROM THE MISSION DISK` (`:532-533`) and never calls it. title: [Radar] hasRadar ignores disable-proof so GLA van dies with brownout
description:
## C++
`Player::hasRadar` (`Player.cpp:3207-3213`): if `m_radarDisabled && m_disableProofRadarCount == 0` return false; else `m_radarCount > 0`. `addRadar(true)` (`:3132-3140`) increments both counts. GLA RadarVan `RadarUpgrade DisableProof=Yes` therefore stays online through `onPowerBrownOutChange` → `disableRadar()`.

## Leftover
`GameLogic/src/player/economy.rs:353-377` and `Common/src/common/rts/player.rs:1897-1930` increment `disable_proof_radar_count` but `has_radar` is `radar_count > 0 && !radar_disabled`. Leftover brownout *does* set `radar_disabled`, so a leftover van would go dark.

## Live
`Player::add_radar` (`game_logic/player.rs:515-518`) takes `_disable_proof` and ignores it. No `disable_proof_radar_count` field. `has_radar` is the same two-term check. `host_radar.rs:22` notes disable-proof vs brownout is fail-closed. Today live never sets `radar_disabled` (see sister brownout-radar bead), so the van only looks correct by accident.

## Player-visible
Once brownout sets `radar_disabled`, GLA radar-van minimap goes off with the CC path. C++ van stays up. Distinct from the brownout-never-sets-flag bead (USA/China radar stays on today).
close_reason: Live host: brownout sets radar_disabled; hasRadar honors disable-proof; 0/0 grid low-energy penalty; save sabotage frame; new Cold Fusion gets EnergyBonus after Control Rods.

title: [Science] Leftover PLAYER_CAN_PURCHASE_SCIENCE only checks prereqs

title: [Object] Hacked spawn-weapon sites do not disable slaves
description:
## Why
C++ `setDisabledUntil` on `KINDOF_SPAWNS_ARE_THE_WEAPONS` orders slaves disabled for the same type/frame, and `isAbleToAttack` also rejects HACKED/EMP on those kinds. Live `apply_disabled_hacked` only flags the site.

## C++
`Object.cpp:2129-2140` `orderSlavesDisabledUntil(type, frame)`.
`Object.cpp:3182-3186` portable-structure / spawns-are-the-weapons cannot attack while HACKED or EMP.
`clearDisabled` `orderSlavesToClearDisabled`.

## Leftover
`GameLogic/src/object/disabled.rs` `order_spawn_slaves_disabled_until`.

## Live host
`object/install.rs` `apply_disabled_hacked` sets `disabled_hacked` + until-frame, idles that object only.
`host_hacker_disable.rs` residual apply is site/vehicle target id.
No slave walk.

## Player-visible
China Hacker / EMP / saboteur hack on a Stinger Site (or other spawn-weapon) darkens/stops the bunker but the stinger soldiers keep shooting. Retail the hive and its slaves all go dark for EffectDuration.

## Not a duplicate
Closed hq-xgf3 is leftover setDisabledUntil dropping slaves (leftover now ports it). Closed hive beads (hq-c5cin / hq-tvoos / hq-j6a24) are hit-target / spawn existence. Skip closed EMP/microwave application; this is the remaining HACKED slave propagate.
close_reason: Live disable mask: script Enabled/Powered, paralyzed can_move, unmanned XP/AutoHeal wipe, hacked slave propagate, Battle Bus HELD, GameWorld step_movement is_disabled

title: [Object] Battle Bus second life never HELD so wreck still acts
description:
## Why
C++ Battle Bus first-death landing sets `DISABLED_HELD` so the wreck is `isDisabled` / not mobile / physics-held. Live only stamps SECOND_LIFE and idles once; there is no HELD bit, and `is_physics_held` is `contained_by` only.

## C++
`BattleBusSlowDeathBehavior.cpp:185-199`: `MODELCONDITION_SECOND_LIFE`, AI idle, scrub velocity, `setDisabled(DISABLED_HELD)`.
`isMobile` / group move / physics Euler all treat HELD as disabled/held.

## Leftover
`DisabledType::Held` is a first-class mask bit; contain onAdding/onRemoving set/clear it.

## Live host
`object/orders.rs` `tick_battle_bus_slow_death` sets model-condition SECOND_LIFE, `stop_moving`, Idle. No `disabled_held`.
`object/physics.rs` `is_physics_held` = `contained_by.is_some()`.
`can_move` does not treat the wreck as disabled.

## Player-visible
After the GLA Battle Bus "dies" into its second-life hulk, the player can order it to drive or shoot. Retail the hulk is frozen in place (held) until empty-hulk destruction or real death.

## Not a duplicate
Closed hq-0hj42 is contained Euler. Closed hq-6rcz6 is SlowDeath HELD corpses. Closed hq-a6cpd / hq-fkyu are Battle Bus contain/passenger damage.
close_reason: Live disable mask: script Enabled/Powered, paralyzed can_move, unmanned XP/AutoHeal wipe, hacked slave propagate, Battle Bus HELD, GameWorld step_movement is_disabled

title: [Rebuild] Hole and 20s worker clock start only after topple destroy
description:
## C++
`RebuildHoleExposeDie::onDie` (`RebuildHoleExposeDie.cpp:80-151`) runs at death start with the other die modules, then `startRebuildProcess` → `newWorkerRespawnProcess` sets `m_workerWaitCounter = WorkerRespawnDelay` (FactionBuilding.ini 20000ms = 600f) immediately. Structure topple/collapse may still play on the dying husk; the hole and the 20s worker clock are already live.

`RebuildHoleBehavior::update` (`RebuildHoleBehavior.cpp:203-208`) decrements that counter every frame and spawns the worker when it hits 0.

## Leftover
Crate `RebuildHoleExposeDie::on_die` + `RebuildHoleBehavior::start_rebuild_process` match C++ timing, but `dual_world_registry_unavailable()` (wave 331/450) no-ops on the live host.

## Live host
`create_destroy_die.rs` `mark_object_for_destruction` (`:2511-2577`) peels EjectPilot / DamDie / UpgradeDie / InstantDeath / CreateObjectDie at death start. It never calls `maybe_spawn_rebuild_hole`. Hole spawn waits for `process_destroy_list` (`destroy_list_bounty.rs:107-112`).

Every structure first hits `try_begin_structure_topple_instead_of_destroy` (`create_destroy_die.rs:3039-3108`). Destroy (and therefore the hole + `rebuild_ready_frame = now+600`) is deferred until topple/collapse reports Done.

## Player-visible
GLA buildings fall over with no hole underneath. The 20s worker clock starts only after the death animation finishes, so reconstruction begins a topple-duration later than retail. If collapse/topple never reaches Done, the hole never appears.
close_reason: Live host uses INI HoleName, death-start clock, dying owner spawn, destroy_object finish

title: [Rebuild] Hole/worker/scaffold spawn via faction Team not dying owner
description:
## C++
`RebuildHoleExposeDie::onDie` (`RebuildHoleExposeDie.cpp:115-116`) `newObject(holeTemplate, us->getTeam())` — the dying object's exact `Team*` (player-owned, not a faction enum). Worker spawn (`RebuildHoleBehavior.cpp:216`) is `newObject(workerTemplate, hole->getTeam())`. Reconstruction is `ai->construct(..., hole->getControllingPlayer(), TRUE)` (`:235-239`). Two GLA players keep distinct teams.

## Leftover
Crate `create_hole` / `spawn_worker_and_construct` pass `dying_object.get_team()` / `hole.get_team()` into `ThingFactory::new_object`. Dual-world empty-gate: leftover does not run on the live host.

## Live host
`host_spawn_rebuild_bound_object` (`production.rs:994-1035`) only takes `Team` and calls `create_object(template, team, pos)`. That resolves owner via `unique_player_id_for_team` (`spawn_templates.rs:3516-3526`) — `None` when two living players share the faction.

`maybe_spawn_rebuild_hole` / `update_rebuild_holes` then `set_team_and_owner` (`visual.rs:67-75`) which only writes `team` / `owner_player_id` / color. It does not re-run create-time `apply_difficulty_bonuses_for_object`, `host_radar_add_object`, or `record_structure_completion` that already ran with `owner=None` (`create_destroy_die.rs:1893-1935`).

## Player-visible
GLA-vs-GLA (or any two same-faction owners): hole, UNSELECTABLE worker, and scaffold are created unowned. Difficulty HP bonuses and radar registration use no controlling player. The rebuilt building can have the wrong HP/radar identity until something else rebinds it.
close_reason: Live host uses INI HoleName, death-start clock, dying owner spawn, destroy_object finish

title: [Rebuild] Finished hole is hashmap-removed so crater ghosts remain
description:
## C++
`RebuildHoleBehavior::update` (`RebuildHoleBehavior.cpp:298-310`) when reconstruction finishes: `transferObjectName`, then `TheGameLogic->destroyObject(worker)` and `TheGameLogic->destroyObject(hole)`. `destroyObject` unregisters radar, pathfinder, partition, and the drawable (dtor also kills a leftover worker).

## Leftover
Crate `finish_reconstruction` (`rebuild_hole_behavior.rs:487-496`) calls `destroy_object_by_id` for worker and hole. Dual-world empty-gate: leftover does not run on the live host.

## Live host
`update_rebuild_holes` finished branch (`rebuild_dozer.rs:1609-1628`) transfers the script name and `destroy_object(worker)`, then `holes_to_remove.push(hole_id)`. The drain is `self.objects.remove(&hid)` (`:1799-1800`) — not `destroy_object`.

That skips the live destroy path in `destroy_list_bounty.rs` (`host_radar_remove_object`, `host_destroy_log`, `eager_unmap_host_destroy_if_coupled`, pathfind rubble stamps). `golden_skirmish.rs:1020` already forbids `objects.remove` as a die-module bypass.

## Player-visible
After a GLA building finishes rebuilding, the hole crater can stay on radar / pathfind / GameWorld as a ghost next to the new building.
close_reason: Live host uses INI HoleName, death-start clock, dying owner spawn, destroy_object finish

title: [Parking] Helos never heal — no setHealee list, reserved-stall gate
description:
## C++
Healing is a **list**, not containment. `setHealee` (`ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:542-571`) add/remove; list "can be larger than the parking space count". `update` (`649-691`) every `HEAL_RATE_FRAMES` (`LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND/5`) applies `attemptHealing` with `DAMAGE_HEALING`, amount `HEAL_RATE_FRAMES * m_healAmount * SECONDS_PER_LOGICFRAME_REAL` (authored `HealAmountPerSecond`). JetAI (`JetAIUpdate.cpp:1834-1852`) while idle/RELOAD_AMMO calls `setHealee(jet, !ALLOW_AIR_LOCO)` — parked **and taxiing** jets heal. Helipad units (`KINDOF_PRODUCED_AT_HELIPAD`) never take a stall (`doLandingCommand` / `reserveDoorForExit` → `DOOR_NONE_NEEDED`) but still get `setHealee`. ChinookAI sets healee when `CHINOOK_LANDED`. Full-HP helos then `setHealee(false)` and take off.

## Leftover
`parking_place_behavior.rs` `set_healee` + `update_simple` port the list and pulse formula. Leftover JetAI/Chinook call `set_healee`. Dual-world empty makes leftover `update_simple` a no-op (`959-960`).

## Live
No healee list. `tick_airfield_parking_heal` (`world_tick/airfield.rs:1984-2048`) heals only aircraft with `contained_by` + `airfield_has_reserved_space`, via `jet.heal(heal_amount_per_second / LOGIC_FRAMES_PER_SECOND)` every frame (not `attemptHealing`). `finish_helipad_landing` sets `contained_by` but **does not reserve a stall** (helos are supposed to skip hangars). Heal then `continue`s at the reserved-space gate. Taxiing jets are not contained.

## Player-visible
Damaged Comanche/Chinook/helipad aircraft sit on the pad and never regenerate; C++ heals them at `HealAmountPerSecond` then auto-launches at max HP. Taxiing jets also miss the C++ ground-loco heal window. Docked jets that do have a stall get raw `heal()` (no `DAMAGE_HEALING` body/FX path) instead of the 5 Hz pulse.
close_reason: Live airfield_healing list + pulse_airfield_healees apply DAMAGE_HEALING every HEAL_RATE_FRAMES (ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:542-571, 649-691). jet_should_be_airfield_healee covers parked/taxiing !ALLOW_AIR_LOCO (JetAIUpdate.cpp:1834-1852), helipad contained, and Chinook CHINOOK_LANDED (ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:1055).

title: [Parking] Queued jet never holds reservedForExit stall
description:
## C++
`reserveDoorForExit` (`ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:695-715`) `buildInfo`/`purgeDead`, then for non-helipad units `findEmptyPPI()` and sets `m_reservedForExit = true` **without** assigning `m_objectInSpace`. Production queues a door at enqueue time. `hasAvailableSpaceFor` / `findEmptyPPI` / landing `reserveSpace` all skip `reservedForExit` stalls, so a returning jet cannot steal the pad promised to the jet still in the factory.

## Leftover
`ModuleExitInterface::reserve_door_for_exit` (`parking_place_behavior.rs:1352-1383`) sets `reserved_for_exit = true` on the first empty stall (and `DOOR_NONE_AVAILABLE` when full). Dual-world empty gate makes leftover exit a no-op on the live host.

## Live
`AirfieldParkingSpace.reserved_for_exit` exists (`player.rs`) and is honored when counting free slots / finding empties, but **nothing ever writes `true`**. Production (`world_tick/production.rs`) only checks `count_free_airfield_parking_slots` at complete time; it never calls a `reserveDoorForExit` equivalent when the unit is queued. `reserve_airfield_parking_space` assigns `object_id` only when a live jet exists.

## Player-visible
3 parked + 1 jet in the build queue: C++ has 0 free stalls (the queued door is reserved). Live still shows 1 free stall, so a returning/allied jet can land in it. The factory then holds (or, if it already spawned, `reserve_produced_aircraft_parking_space` fails and `destroy_object`s the new jet).
close_reason: enqueue_production calls reserve_airfield_door_for_exit which sets reserved_for_exit=true without object_id (ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:695-715 reserveDoorForExit/findEmptyPPI). Landing reserveSpace skips those stalls so a returning jet cannot steal the queued pad.

title: [Parking] Runway reserve first-free when jet has no stall
description:
## C++
`reserveRunway` (`ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:453-502`): look up the jet's parking stall, take `ppi->m_runway`. No stall → `DEBUG_CRASH("only planes with reserved spaces can reserve runways")` and return false. Never first-free across columns. `transferRunwayReservationToNextInLineForTakeoff` / `wasInLine` stay per that column.

## Leftover
`reserve_runway` (`parking_place_behavior.rs:771-807`) requires a stall (`spaces.iter().find(object_in_space == id)`); no stall → false. Column + next-in-line + was_in_line match C++.

## Live
`reserve_airfield_runway_ex` (`world_tick/airfield.rs:1296-1367`) does bind `airfield_parking_runway_column` when a stall exists (hq-sv4tj close), but if that is `None` it **falls back** to the first empty runway slot (`or_else slots.iter().position(|s| s.is_none())`). Takeoff then **releases the stall** (`release_jet_from_airfield_parking` at 1498) and immediately re-reserves the runway (1503), so the fallback is the live takeoff path.

## Player-visible
Two jets from the same hangar column can grab two different runways; a jet that already released its pad can steal the other column's runway instead of queueing `nextInLine` on its own strip. C++ never lets a no-stall jet onto a runway.
close_reason: reserve_airfield_runway_ex requires airfield_parking_runway_column from the jet stall (ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:453-472, m_runway=col at buildInfo:91). No stall returns None; no first-free runway steal across columns.

title: [PUC] Beam damage radius is 50 not retail 44.2
description:
## C++
`ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate::update` (`ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:588-594`): `damageRadius = LaserUpdate::getCurrentLaserRadius() * m_damageRadiusScalar`. `getCurrentLaserRadius` = OuterBeamWidth×0.5 × widthScalar. Retail OuterBeamWidth **26**, DamageRadiusScalar **3.4** → peak hold **13 × 3.4 = 44.2**. Pulses use that radius at `FROM_CENTER_2D` (`:639`).

## Leftover
`particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:1616-1617` uses `base_laser_radius * data.damage_radius_scalar` (correct formula). `update_simple` returns immediately when `OBJECT_REGISTRY` is empty (`:1328-1330`) — leftover never runs on the live host.

## Live host
`particle_beam_damage_radius` (`special_power_strikes/particle_uplink.rs:648-649`) is `PARTICLE_BEAM_RADIUS * width_scalar` with `PARTICLE_BEAM_RADIUS = 50.0` (`:19`). Honesty residual `particle_retail_damage_radius` computes 44.2 but `plan_due_beam_ticks` (`registry_fields.rs:1084-1085`) applies the r50 path. Comments at `particle_uplink.rs:17-19,42-43` and `mod.rs:51-53` document the fail-closed cap.

WidthGrow scalar itself is present (0→1 grow, hold, 1→0 decay). Only the **peak combat radius** is wrong.

## Player-visible
Particle Cannon pulses hit a 50wu disk (25wu at half-grow) instead of 44.2 (22.1). Units 45–50wu from the beam take 35 damage/pulse and can die when C++ would miss them.
close_reason: PARTICLE_BEAM_RADIUS is 44.2 (13 x 3.4). Combat pulses use that peak times WidthGrow scalar.

title: [CommandXlat] Context hover cursors miss Dock/Heal/Hack/Hijack/OutRange
description:
## Why
C++ HintSpy/`createCommandHint` maps each context hint to a Mouse.ini cursor (Dock, GetHealed, DoRepair, Hack, EnterAggressively, OutRange, ParticleUplink override, …). Live `host_resolve_context_cursor_icon` only names Attack/ForceAttack/Enter/GetRepaired/Resume/Capture/Move/Waypoint/Guard. Dock, heal, hack, hijack, sabotage, carbomb, override-dest, and out-of-range fall through to Select (hover) or Move (ground).

## C++
`HintSpy.cpp:46-75` forwards `MSG_DOCK_HINT`, `MSG_GET_HEALED_HINT`, `MSG_DO_REPAIR_HINT`, `MSG_HIJACK_HINT`, `MSG_SABOTAGE_HINT`, `MSG_CONVERT_TO_CARBOMB_HINT`, `MSG_HACK_HINT`, `MSG_DO_ATTACK_OBJECT_AFTER_MOVING_HINT`, `MSG_DO_SPECIAL_POWER_OVERRIDE_DESTINATION_HINT`, `MSG_IMPOSSIBLE_ATTACK_HINT` to `createCommandHint`.
`InGameUI.cpp:2631-2684`: Dock→`DOCK`, GetHealed→`GET_HEALED`, DoRepair→`DO_REPAIR`, hijack/sabotage/carbomb→`ENTER_AGGRESSIVELY`, Hack→`HACK`, after-moving→`OUTRANGE`, override→`PARTICLE_UPLINK_CANNON`, invalid→`GENERIC_INVALID`.

## Leftover
`command_translator.rs:605+` `evaluate_context_hint` emits the matching `*Hint` messages. Unused live (Main never posts into that stream).

## Live
`cnc_game_engine/mouse.rs:2394-2434` match: AttackObj, ForceAttack*, EnterFriendly, GetRepaired (also used for `CommandType::Repair`), ResumeConstruction, CaptureBuilding, Move/Salvage/AttackMove, Waypoint, Guard.
`_ =>` hover→`Select` / else `Move`.
No arms for Dock, Gather, GetHealed, Hijack, ConvertToCarbomb, Sabotage, DisableVehicleHack, StealCashHack, HackerDisableBuilding, OverrideSpecialPowerDestination, SetRallyPoint (context, not pending), ImpossibleAttack.

## Player-visible
Supply truck over a warehouse shows the Select pointer, not Dock. Injured infantry over a heal pad shows Select, not GetHealed. Lotus/Hacker hover after auto-hack classify shows Select, not Hack. Hijacker over a tank shows Select, not EnterAggressively. Dozer repair uses the GetRepaired (pad) cursor name. Out-of-range enemies never show OutRange.

## Not a duplicate
Closed hq-s3ml is unreachable-ground invalid-move. Closed hq-p3jt is W3D cursor textures existing. Closed hq-02q9 is HintSpy leftover mapping. This is the live host match table still missing those hint types.
close_reason: Live CommandXlat/ActionManager: RMB attack is weapon-legal (neutrals/tech; dozer DISARM only vs mines). Unmanned husk Enter for any !REJECT_UNMANNED infantry plus arrival recrew. Repair/GetRepaired/GetHealed before hijack/enter/attack/capture. Hover cursors Dock/DoRepair/GetHealed/Hack/EnterAggressively/OutRange.

title: [CommandXlat] Repair is after enter/attack/capture so mixed dozer groups skip repair
description:
## Why
C++ `evaluateContextCommand` checks `ACTIONTYPE_REPAIR_OBJECT` (and get-repaired / get-healed) immediately after Dock, before hijack/enter/attack/capture. Live presentation classify runs Repair after Enter, Attack, Capture, and the three hacks. Mixed dozer+combat selections therefore steal the click.

## C++
`CommandXlat.cpp:1758-1788` `ACTIONTYPE_REPAIR_OBJECT` (`SELECTION_ANY`) → `MSG_DO_REPAIR` / `MSG_DO_REPAIR_HINT`.
Then get-repaired (`:1790`), get-healed (`:1824`), hijack/carbomb/sabotage (`:1856-1918`), salvage (`:1921`), enter (`:1941`), attack (`:1962`), capture (`:2005`).
`ActionManager.cpp:359-422` `canRepairObject`: not enemies, structure, damaged, dozer, not under-construction / hole / bridge / shroud / contained.

## Leftover
`command_translator.rs:494-504` repair then get-repaired then get-healed, still before hijack/enter/attack. Unused live.

## Live
`system_impl.rs:1260-1352` order: hijack/carbomb/sabotage → Enter (`can_be_entered`) → Attack (enemy tint) → Capture → hacks → Repair (`hint.is_structure && is_damaged && (friendly||neutral) && any_repairer`).
GetHealed (`:1356`) is also before GetRepaired (`:1381`); C++ is GetRepaired then GetHealed.

## Player-visible
Select a dozer + Ranger and RMB a damaged garrisonable ally: retail Repair, live Enter. Dozer + Colonel on a damaged civilian/tech building: retail Repair, live Capture. Hover cursor follows the stolen command.

## Not a duplicate
Closed hq-5b8wz is execute_repair accepting holes/bridges. Closed hq-7lbg is factory rally. Wave13 left this as an unfinished edge; it is a live context-order bug.
close_reason: Live CommandXlat/ActionManager: RMB attack is weapon-legal (neutrals/tech; dozer DISARM only vs mines). Unmanned husk Enter for any !REJECT_UNMANNED infantry plus arrival recrew. Repair/GetRepaired/GetHealed before hijack/enter/attack/capture. Hover cursors Dock/DoRepair/GetHealed/Hack/EnterAggressively/OutRange.

title: [Countermeasures] Live flares sit at static offsets with no arc/velocity
description:
## C++
`launchVolley` (`CountermeasuresBehavior.cpp:273-331`): for each flare in the volley, ratio `i / (volleySize-1) * 2 - 1` (0 if size==1) times `m_volleyArcAngle` (retail **90°**). Take `getUnitDirectionVector3D`, flatten XY, `Vector2::Rotate(angle)`, scale by `max(velocity, treat <1 as -10) * VolleyVelocityFactor` (retail **2.0**). Spawn `FlareTemplateName` (`CountermeasureFlare`) on the owner's default team at the aircraft position/orientation, `transferVelocityTo` the flare physics, then `applyMotiveForce`. Flares fly backward in a fan. `calculateCountermeasureToDivertTo` (132-173) picks the closest (2D center) of the newest `volleySize` IDs so seekers chase those moving decoys. Lifetime is the flare object's LifetimeUpdate (**3000 ms**).

## Leftover
`create_countermeasure` (559-624) ports facing-relative rotate + motive force + `set_velocity(owner)` and pushes IDs for the closest-flare walk (`.iter().rev().take(volley_size)`). Empty dual-world never creates objects.

## Live
`spawn_countermeasure_flare_object` (`helix_radar.rs:1612-1675`) places a host `CountermeasureFlare` at a **static** offset: `t = volley_index / (VOLLEY_SIZE-1)`, `angle = (t-0.5) * 90°`, `dist = 12 + 2*index`, `place = origin + (cos*dist, y+8, sin*dist)`. No owner facing, no `VolleyVelocityFactor`, no `transferVelocityTo` / motive force. Flares sit until `FLARE_LIFETIME_FRAMES` (90) then `note_flare_expired`. Host comments: "Not full bone volley arc / VolleyVelocityFactor locomotor matrix" / "Not full active-flare lifetime list / bone volley FX".

## Player-visible
Retail flares streak out behind the jet in a 90° fan at ~2× airspeed and missiles chase the nearest new one. Live flares pop in a small ring around the aircraft and hang still for 3 s; nothing seeks them.
close_reason: launchVolley at aircraft pose with 90-degree facing fan, transferVelocityTo + VolleyVelocityFactor motive

title: [Stealth] Live detector scan uses Team inequality not ALLOW_ENEMIES|NEUTRAL
description: C++ StealthDetectorUpdate.cpp:167-170 PartitionFilterRelationship ALLOW_ENEMIES|ALLOW_NEUTRAL. Live stealth_mines.rs:893 uses det_team != s_team. Allied players on different Team enums destalth each other (global DETECTED). Reuse player_relationship like gps_grant_is_ally. Do not implement here — PlayerLocoP1s owns relationship files.
close_reason: Detector scan uses player_relationship ALLOW_ENEMIES|NEUTRAL. Allied players no longer destalth each other.

title: [Radar] Presentation minimap dots skip FOW so enemies always leak
description:
## C++
`W3DRadar::renderObjectList` (`W3DRadar.cpp:636-638`) skips blips when `getShroudedStatus(playerIndex) > OBJECTSHROUD_PARTIAL_CLEAR`. Fogged/shrouded enemies do not appear on the radar overlay.

## Leftover
Leftover `should_render_object_overlay_blip` (`radar/mod.rs:1973-1989`) also requires a Clear cell. N/A for Main-side PresentationFrame dots.

## Live host
Legacy logic path gated dots: `ui_production.rs:96-121` via `is_object_visible_on_minimap_for_team` (`spawn_templates.rs:3646-3677`) — own team always, enemies only when shroud-visible, explored structures kept.

The live PresentationFrame path that replaced it does **not** consult FOW: `presentation_frame/apply.rs:329-375` `minimap_unit_dots` and `:431-445` `hud_minimap_units` filter only `!destroyed && !sold`. `ui/hud.rs:72-88` `MiniMap::update_units` applies no FOW. The frame already carries `fow_visibility` / `drawable_shroud` (`presentation_frame/types.rs:929-936`) and never uses them for dots.

## Player-visible
Any consumer of presentation minimap dots (HUD unit-count / future dot renderer) sees every living enemy regardless of fog. Intel leak vs retail radar overlay. Bounded today (graphical consumers limited) but the in-game overlay path is the live one.
close_reason: Presentation minimap dots skip drawable_shroud > PARTIAL_CLEAR.

title: [Microwave] Emitter cooks neutrals; C++ ENEMIES only
description:
## C++
`MicrowaveTankEmitterWeapon` `RadiusDamageAffects` ENEMIES NOT_AIRBORNE. Neutral/civilian infantry in the 100 cook field take no MICROWAVE.

## Leftover
Leftover `FireWeaponUpdate` fires the INI template with that affect mask.

## Live
`host_microwave.rs:195-207` `is_legal_microwave_emitter_target` rejects same-team then `let _ = target_is_neutral; true` — neutrals pass. Comment claims neutrals are fail-closed out; the code does the opposite. `gps_and_fields.rs:788-796` uses this filter.

## Player-visible
A Microwave tank parked by civilians/neutral infantry cooks them. C++ the field only hurts enemies.
close_reason: C++ microwave: clearer 100ms/3f, SUBDUAL_BUILDING to maxHealth, emitter Microwave not Unresistable, ENEMIES only

title: [ECM] Vehicle jam radius 150 not disabler AttackRange 200
description:
## C++
`ECMTankVehicleDisabler` `AttackRange` 200. A Battlemaster 175 units from the ECM tank is a legal beam target and accumulates SUBDUAL_VEHICLE. Missile-jammer splash radius is separately 150.

## Leftover
Leftover `FireWeaponUpdate` / weapon store would use the INI AttackRange 200 for the disabler shot.

`gps_and_fields.rs:257` vehicle-jam aura uses `HOST_ECM_JAM_RADIUS` 150 (missile-jammer PrimaryDamageRadius). `ECM_VEHICLE_DISABLER_ATTACK_RANGE` 200 (`host_ecm_jam.rs:59-60`) is honesty-only and never applied to the aura.

## Player-visible
Park a tank at 160–200 from an ECM: live it keeps shooting. C++ the disabler beam reaches it.
close_reason: Live ECM: SUBDUAL_VEHICLE accumulate (not instant jam); vehicles+missiles only; projectileNowJammed scatter no 100 HP; AttackRange 200

title: [CommandXlat] F9 hides the control bar during replay playback
description:
## Why
C++ TOGGLE_CONTROL_BAR is a no-op while TheRecorder is in PLAYBACK. Live F9 always toggles the HUD.

## C++
CommandXlat.cpp:3156-3170 ToggleControlBar only when !(TheRecorder && getMode()==RECORDERMODETYPE_PLAYBACK).

## Leftover
None on the live path.

## Live

title: [Pathfind] Live water cells use center sample and lose to cliff
description:
## Why
C++ marks a pathfind cell `CELL_WATER` if any of its four corners is underwater, and water wins over cliff. Live samples only the cell center, then overwrites Water with Cliff/Impassable from slope. Shoreline cells with a dry center stay Clear (infantry walk the wet edge); wet cliff-base cells block amphibious `SURFACE_WATER` units that C++ would allow.

## C++
`AIPathfind.cpp:4491-4521` `classifyMapCell`:
- Cliff test at the cell's top-left corner
- Water if any of 4 corners `isUnderwater` — assigned *after* cliff so water overrides
- No terrain-slope Impassable gate

## Leftover
Crate pathfind classify is a different slice; live host seeds its own grid.

## Live host
`Main/src/game_logic/world_save.rs:536-554` `seed_pathfinding_from_terrain`:
- `is_underwater_at_world(center)` then `slope>MAX_SLOPE` → Impassable else `is_cliff_at_world(center)` → Cliff, overwriting Water.

## Player-visible
Narrow rivers and wet shores vanish from the grid (ground units walk them). Hovercraft/amphibious units cannot cross wet cliff-base cells that C++ treats as water.

## Not a duplicate
Closed hq-tdxnb is `is_underwater` always dry. Closed hq-d10g is crate `is_cliff_cell` bits. Closed hq-muu69 is adjustDestination.
close_reason: C++ live host: waveguide WaveGuide1 dest+WET+Water/Flooded+stop; water damage rise-only; leftover restamp live Water cells; GenericBridge spawn; deck Z snap; rubble restamp+splat; 4-corner water wins; no slope>4 Impassable

title: [Drawable] Live friendly stealth opacity is static min, no pulse
description:
## C++
`StealthUpdate` every enabled non-mine frame (`StealthUpdate.cpp:667-670`) does `draw->setEffectiveOpacity(0.5f + Sin(m_pulsePhase)*0.5f)` and advances `m_pulsePhase` by 0.2. `Drawable::setEffectiveOpacity` (`Drawable.cpp:1102-1114`) writes the stealth floor then `m_effectiveStealthOpacity = stealth + (1-stealth)*pulseFactor`. `getEffectiveOpacity` is `m_explicitOpacity * m_effectiveStealthOpacity`. Friendly cloak shimmers between FriendlyOpacityMin and 1.0.

## Leftover
Closed `hq-eu5o`: leftover `StealthUpdate::update_drawable_visuals` pulses GameLogic `Drawable::set_effective_opacity`. GameClient `BasicDrawable::set_effective_opacity` (`basic_core.rs:899-911`) matches C++. That opacity is not the live mesh input.

## Live host
`unit_render_inputs` (`queries.rs:340-341`) sets `presentation_opacity = object.friendly_stealth_opacity` which is frozen from `obj.thing.template.stealth_friendly_opacity_min` (`build.rs:698`) — a static min, never `min + (max-min)*sin(phase)`. Camo-netting pulses `camo_friendly_opacity` on the object; presentation does not read it for the mesh. Tests assert allied opacity == 0.5 exactly.

## Evidence
C++ `StealthUpdate.cpp:667-670` + `Drawable.cpp:1102-1114`.
Leftover pulse on GameLogic drawable (hq-eu5o).
Live `build.rs:698` + `queries.rs:340-341` static min; no pulse_phase on `UnitRenderInput`.

## Player-visible effect
Friendly stealthed units sit at a flat 50% alpha. They never shimmer between half and full opacity the way C++ cloak does.

## Split hint
Freeze leftover `effective_stealth_opacity` (or host pulse_phase + min/max) onto `presentation_opacity` instead of the authored min alone.
close_reason: Live friendly stealth presentation_opacity now pulses via C++ setEffectiveOpacity (0.5+sin(phase)*0.5 mapped onto FriendlyOpacityMin..1.0) from object-id seed + 0.2 rad/frame. Mines stay static min.

title: [Replay] SET_REPLAY_CAMERA apply ignores observer look-at player
description:

Camera recorded by the original local player therefore stops driving the view when the observer switches to another player.

No `getObserverLookAtPlayer()==message player` test. Recording/arg layout already closed (hq-j3ufr, hq-nqmua).

close_reason: SET_REPLAY_CAMERA apply now requires playback + useCameraInReplay + observer look-at == message player (GameLogicDispatch.cpp:1803). Pose stores player_index; mouse.rs discards pose when observer bar is on another player.

title: [Replay] Playback never remirrors recorded selection onto observer InGameUI

close_reason: Playback remirrors issuing-player selection onto observer InGameUI after network commands and SELECT/ADD_TEAM (GameLogicDispatch.cpp:1970-1984). Team ops apply to message player; host_set_selection updates rings/control bar.

title: [HordeUpdate] Live count/rub-off uses 2D center not FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_3D
description:
## C++
`HordeUpdate::update` (`HordeUpdate.cpp:257-259`) iterates `ThePartitionManager->iterateObjectsInRange(..., md->m_minDist, FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_3D)`. Distance is 3D center-to-center minus bounding-sphere radii, so BOX tanks (major 13 / minor 9) count from farther than a raw 75 center. Rub-off then uses `FROM_CENTER_2D` vs `sqr(RubOffRadius)` (`:272-280`).

## Leftover crate
`check_horde_status` (`horde_update.rs:437-438`) uses `get_objects_in_range_boundary_3d_from_object` then 2D-center rub-off (`:510-513`). Unused by the live host tick.

## Live
`evaluate_leftover_horde_blob` (`host_battlemaster.rs:444-480`) measures XZ `distance_2d` for **both** the Count-1 pass and the RubOff pass (`dist <= radius && dist <= rub_off_radius`). Infantry Radius 30 / vehicle Radius 75 are center-to-center. No sphere subtraction.

## Player-visible
Five Battlemasters whose centers are just past 75 still horde in C++ (sphere slack ~major/bounding) and get 150% ROF + vehicle rings. Live leftover ticks leave them out. Honorary rub-off candidates are also a smaller 2D set than C++'s 3D scan.
close_reason: Live horde count uses FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_3D; RubOff stays FROM_CENTER_2D on the 3D-scan set.

title: [Shroud] ShroudRevealToAllRange never applied on live look
description:

title: [Pathfind] Optimize skips C++ collinear H/V/diag force-passable
description:

title: [Pathfind] CPOP lead only when offset < 1.5 cells
description:
## C++
Path::computePointOnPath (AIPathfind.cpp:898-967) always tries isLinePassable(pos, nextNode) regardless of offset. k=offset/(3*CELL) only blends when the lead fails; k>0.5 tries the remaining-segment midpoint.

## Live
pathfinding.rs compute_point_on_path_ex only leads when offset < 1.5*CELL (max_err*0.5). Units 2 cells off a clear path hug the closest point instead of cutting to the next node.

## Acceptance
Off-path unit with a clear line aims at the next node. Blocked lead still refuses to aim through buildings.
close_reason: Live PathfindingSystem::compute_point_on_path_for always tries isLinePassable to next node (AIPathfind.cpp:910-966); k>0.5 mid-segment fallback; blocked lead stays on closest point. movement.rs uses it. Test cpop_leads_when_two_cells_off_clear_path.

title: [Locomotor] Live brake is dest=0 dist/dt snap not C++ curves
description:
## C++
`calcSlowDownDist` (Locomotor.cpp:62-73) with desired=minSpeed for legs/other (1648-1653, 2368-2374). Treads (1187-1221) use `slowDownDist = (actual/1.5)*(actual/braking)`, square braking_factor, clamp MAX_BRAKING_FACTOR=5, then step goalSpeed by braking/2. Wheels (1332-1430) add +1 frame and donut timer (DONUT_DISTANCE 40, 2.5s) that forces IS_BRAKING. Dispatcher (1089-1138) then cheat-snaps XY (or 3D for projectiles) while OBJECT_STATUS_BRAKING. Wings never brake (1047-1050).

title: [ControlBar] IGNORES_UNDERPOWERED does not require sole underpowered flag
description:

Any second flag (EMP, hack, paralyzed) keeps the button Restricted.

title: [Pathfind] Queued move marches straight at dest before A* returns
description:
## C++
Pathfinder::queueForPath (AIPathfind.h:608) only enqueues ObjectID. The unit sits in waiting_for_path; locomotor does not integrate toward the raw click. processPathfindQueue later installs the computed Path (AI.cpp). No pre-path velocity.

## Leftover
pathfind.rs has no queue; leftover Pathfinder::find_path_astar is synchronous. leftover complete pathfind_complete has a request_queue but leftover Pathfinder::find_path still computes immediately.

## Live host
world_save.rs assign_unit_path_inner:731-760: on loaded maps, sets waiting_for_path, target_position=destination, AIState::Moving, AND velocity = normalize(dest-start)*max_speed before queue_path. PendingHostPath has no crusher. process_pathfind_queue later replaces the path, but one-or-more frames of GameWorld/host integrate have already marched the unit toward the raw click (through buildings if they sit on the line). Distinct from closed hq-is19 (sync vs async) and hq-3plv (permanent fail-open).

## Player-visible

title: [Pathfind] CPOP lead skips isLinePassable so units aim through buildings
description:
## C++
Path::computePointOnPath (AIPathfind.cpp:732-1014) projects onto the optimized polyline, then if the unit is close to the path (offset < 3*CELL) it leads to the next node only when isLinePassable(obj, surfaces, layer, pos, next, blocked=false, allowPinched=true). tryAhead to the next-segment midpoint is also gated on isLinePassable and canOptimize / same layer. Far off-path blends toward the closest point.

## Leftover
pathfind.rs Path::compute_point_on_path (549-620) is geometric closest-point only: no lead, no isLinePassable, and dist_along_path is distance from start (C++ returns remaining distance to end).

## Live host
Closed hq-9yz3f added PathfindingSystem::compute_point_on_path (pathfinding.rs:2428-2480). If offset < 15 it blindly returns the next waypoint (or mid of the following segment when t>0.5) with no isLinePassable / canOptimize / layer gate. movement.rs:251-262 then marches that lead every tick.

## Player-visible
A unit that drifted a cell off its path charges the next waypoint in a straight line through a building or cliff instead of sliding back onto the polyline.
close_reason: Live host pathfinding.rs/movement.rs: adjustDestination refuses uncrushable FIXED occupants; rally uses structure-aware quick_path_exists; dead structures stamp CELL_RUBBLE; queued move sits still until A*; CPOP lead gated on isLinePassable; optimize aborts occupancy/pinched and collapses un-pinched cliffs; fences classified by FenceWidth not name.

title: [Pathfind] Optimize ignores occupancy and un-pinched cliffs
description:
## C++
Path::optimize (AIPathfind.cpp:450-573) shortcuts via isLinePassable(obj, surfaces, layer, a, b, blocked, allowPinched=false). linePassableCallback (9553-9591) aborts on checkForMovement allyFixed/enemyFixed, pinched cells, and invalid surfaces. Un-pinched CELL_CLIFF is forced passable (506-509) so cliff-ramp segments can collapse. Path::optimizeGroundPath uses isGroundPathPassable(crusher, diameter).

## Leftover
pathfind.rs Path::optimize (391-535): passable closure returns false when blocked (never skip) and otherwise uses TerrainLogic::is_clear_line_of_sight — not isLinePassable. No occupancy, no pinched, no un-pinched-cliff exception. When TheTerrainLogic is missing (dual-world empty) every segment is treated as passable.

## Live host
Closed hq-o1pc0 added PathfindingGrid::optimize_ground_path. It only calls line_passable → cell_passable_for (terrain/structure/crusher). No occupancy, no blocked flag, no pinched abort, no un-pinched CELL_CLIFF exception (pathfinding.rs:1266-1349). Distinct from PathB hq-6p032 (A* extra-cost hard-block of other-player UNIT_PRESENT_FIXED).

close_reason: Live host pathfinding.rs/movement.rs: adjustDestination refuses uncrushable FIXED occupants; rally uses structure-aware quick_path_exists; dead structures stamp CELL_RUBBLE; queued move sits still until A*; CPOP lead gated on isLinePassable; optimize aborts occupancy/pinched and collapses un-pinched cliffs; fences classified by FenceWidth not name.

title: [Pathfind] Live fences classified by name not FenceWidth
description:
## C++

Closed hq-yqr7q added fence bits, but apply_structure_static_blocks (pathfinding.rs:1800-1816) decides is_fence by name.contains(\"fence\"|\"chainlink\"|\"chain_link\") and uses selection_radius*2 as width, fence_x_offset=0. classify_fence_world exists and would honor real FenceWidth, but no live object field is read.

title: [AIPlayer] Extra random supply/power pads invented outside the build list
description:

Low cash / brown-out only changes **which list entry** is chosen (power override) and StructureSeconds wealth mods. Extra depots come from `buildBySupplies` (AIPlayer.cpp:1826) which still places a **named** template near `findSupplyCenter`, not a random offset around base center. Desired gatherers come from `AISideInfo` easy/normal/hard + 1 freebie (`checkForSupplyCenter`).

If `power_available < 0`, `try_build_power_plant` (1327) appends a PP at rng(-60,60) up to 2. These are not list entries and ignore automatic/priority/AIData gatherer counts.

title: [AIPlayer] Skirmish newMap skips AIData SideBuildList and adjustBuildList

## C++
`AISkirmishPlayer::newMap` (AISkirmishPlayer.cpp:1051-1085) **replaces** the player build list with `AIData` `m_sideBuildLists` for `player->getSide()`, then `adjustBuildList` (941-1041): destroy the map-placed Command Center, mark the list CC InitiallyBuilt, rotate/translate every entry around the start slot (3x3 grid + `m_rotateSkirmishBases` + 3π/4), `computeCenterAndRadiusOfBase`, `buildStructureNow` InitiallyBuilt, `incrementNumRebuilds` on the rest.

title: [AIPlayer] Captured/destroyed pads never unbind or rebind GLA holes
description:
## C++
`AISkirmishPlayer::processBaseBuilding` (AISkirmishPlayer.cpp:100-172): if the listed object exists but `getControllingPlayer() != m_player`, clear objectID + stamp timestamp (captured). If missing, stamp timestamp and scan `KINDOF_REBUILD_HOLE` for `RebuildHoleBehavior::getSpawnerID() == priorID`, then bind the hole so GLA reconstruction is tracked. title: [AIPlayer] queueUnits never recruits existing units into the team
description:

`AIPlayer::queueUnits` (AIPlayer.cpp:2630-2693) for each waiting WorkOrder loops `team->tryToRecruit(thing, home, m_maxRecruitDistance)` until full or none left, `setTeam`s the unit, then `aiMoveToPosition(home)` or `aiIdle`. title: [JetAI] Runway handoff waits until the leader is 120u airborne

title: [JetAI] Empty clip aborts every order and never resumes guard
description:

After RELOAD_AMMO, update (1868-1878) reconstitutes m_mostRecentCommand so the jet resumes guard/hunt. Attack orders are not interrupted this way.
