Both are unused on the live host (OBJECT_REGISTRY empty / Main never ticks crate ProductionUpdate).

## Live host
pose.rs CONSTRUCTION_COMPLETE_DURATION_FRAMES_RESIDUAL is hardcoded 45 (1500ms). set_construction_complete_condition_at always arms that deadline. parse_production_door_ini_fields (host_production_buildable_command_residual.rs:400-424) reads NumDoorAnimations/Door*Time only — ConstructionCompleteDuration is listed in the field-name table but never parsed.

## Player-visible
Every factory (including producers that author duration 0) keeps the construction-complete pose for 1.5s after each unit. Retail barracks/war factories with a short or zero duration flash the complete pose for one frame, then go idle.
close_reason: parse_production_door_ini_fields reads ConstructionCompleteDuration; pose deadline uses producer INI frames (default 0 → one-frame flash).

title: [Production] Object upgrades can be re-queued after they already completed
description:
## C++
ProductionUpdate::queueUpgrade (ProductionUpdate.cpp:250-256) refuses UPGRADE_TYPE_OBJECT when the producer already hasUpgrade(upgrade) or !affectedByUpgrade(upgrade), before withdrawing money. isUpgradeInQueue also blocks a second copy on the same producer.

## Leftover Rust
object/update/production_update.rs queue_upgrade ports has_upgrade / affected_by_upgrade. Unused on the live host.

## Live host
Player::queue_upgrade (player.rs:907-922) skips the player-wide complete/in-production gate for object-scoped upgrades and only spends. BuildingData::add_upgrade_to_queue refuses a duplicate name still in the queue, but not an upgrade the producer already finished. execute_queue_upgrade checks queue-full and in-queue name only.

## Player-visible
After an Overlord/Helix addon or other OBJECT upgrade completes on that unit, clicking the button again charges and queues it a second time. Retail ignores the click (already has the add-on). Distinct from closed hq-3txwb (OBJECT upgrades landing in the player set).
close_reason: execute_queue_upgrade refuses OBJECT upgrades when producer.has_object_upgrade_complete; ui_production producer_refuses_completed_object_upgrade helper.

title: [Door] Multi-door factories animate as one shared DOOR_1
description:
## C++
ProductionUpdate keeps DoorInfo m_doors[DOOR_COUNT_MAX] and updateDoors walks each door independently (ProductionUpdate.cpp:518-581). Completing a unit opens only the reserved ExitDoorType (DOOR_1..4). AmericaAirfield authors NumDoorAnimations=4 so hangar doors can be on different phases.

## Leftover Rust
object/update/production_update.rs and production_update_complete.rs keep a 4-door DoorInfo array. Unused on the live host.

## Live host
pose.rs start/tick/apply write only door_1_* model bits. One production_door_phase is shared. presentation_frame/unit_render.rs stamps that single phase onto all four door banks in lockstep. hq-wtksw fixed NumDoorAnimations parse for spawn gating, not per-door animation.

## Player-visible
An airfield with four hangars opens and closes every door together whenever any jet is produced. Retail opens only the reserved hangar.
close_reason: per-door phases[4] + reserved ExitDoorType; only that hangar opens. Presentation no longer locksteps DOOR_2..4.

title: [SpecialPowerCreate] SharedNSync and scripted powers skipped on build complete
description:
## C++
`SpecialPowerCreate::onBuildComplete` (`SpecialPowerCreate.cpp:34-48`) if `shouldDoOnBuildComplete()` walks **every** `getSpecialPower()` behavior and calls `onSpecialPowerCreation()`.

`SpecialPowerModule::onSpecialPowerCreation` (`SpecialPowerModule.cpp:178-212`):
1. `startPowerRecharge()`
2. if `isSharedNSync()`: `Player::expressSpecialPowerReadyFrame(..., now)` then copy the player ready frame (Dustin: start ready to fire)
3. if `StartsPaused`: `pauseCountdown(TRUE)`
4. if `hasPublicTimer` + controlling player + KINDOF_STRUCTURE: `TheInGameUI->addSuperweapon`

No filter for SharedNSync or ScriptedSpecialPowerOnly. Command Centers (and other SpecialPowerCreate buildings) therefore express **all** SharedNSync generals powers ready-now when the building finishes — including resetting an already-ticking player-shared A10/Paradrop/SpyDrone timer when a second CC completes. Scripted-only modules also start recharge.

`CashBountyPower::onSpecialPowerCreation` (`CashBountyPower.cpp:145-156`) extends the base then `setCashBounty` if the palace bounty is higher.

## Leftover Rust
`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/create/special_power_create.rs:28-54` walks every `get_special_power()` via owner TLS and calls `on_special_power_creation()`. Empty `OBJECT_REGISTRY` → leftover no-op; live host is what the player runs.

## Live host
`production_eva.rs` `on_structure_superweapon_creation` (called from `apply_create_modules_on_build_complete` in `create_destroy_die.rs`):
- requires alive + constructed
- walks `special_power_modules`
- **filters out** `shared_n_sync` and `scripted_special_power_only`
- `start_power_recharge_with_frames` + `StartsPaused` pause only for the remainder

Comment says SharedNSync is handled by `on_special_power_science_creation` (`object_queries.rs:1579-1645`), which only runs on science **purchase** (`sell_upgrade.rs` / `ui_production.rs`) and only express-ready-now — it never runs on CreateModule onBuildComplete.

Public-timer HUD is rebuilt from living structures (`presentation_frame/build.rs`) so missing `addSuperweapon` is not the gap. Cash bounty is applied on science unlock, not palace create.

`has_special_power_create` is parsed on the template but never used as a gate (not filed: typical SP buildings also author SpecialPowerCreate).

## Player-visible result
Finishing a Command Center (or any SpecialPowerCreate building) does not express SharedNSync generals powers ready-now. A second CC does not refresh an A10/Paradrop/SpyDrone cooldown the way retail does. Campaign/scripted special-power modules on those buildings never start their Create recharge. Science purchase still readies SharedNSync powers once; build-complete does not.
close_reason: on_structure_superweapon_creation walks every special power including SharedNSync (express ready-now) and scripted (start ReloadTime).

title: [MoneyCrate] Live crate cash skips ScoreKeeper addMoneyEarned
description:
## C++
`MoneyCrateCollide::executeCrateBehavior` (`MoneyCrateCollide.cpp:30-44`) deposits `m_moneyProvided + getUpgradedSupplyBoost(other)` then `getScoreKeeper()->addMoneyEarned(money)` and plays `m_crateMoney` on the picker. `getUpgradedSupplyBoost` (`:48-70`) walks INI `UpgradedBoost` pairs and returns the first complete player upgrade amount.

## Leftover Rust
`money_crate_collide.rs:392-437` deposits via leftover `player_list()` and calls `add_money_earned_to_score`. Leftover `on_collide` is not the live path (host objects are not in leftover `TheGameLogic` / `OBJECT_REGISTRY`).

## Live host
`update_money_crate_collides` (`crates_radar_power.rs:592-597`) credits via `player.credit_supplies(amount)` only. `credit_supplies` (`player.rs:898-905`) bumps `statistics.resources_collected` and `apply_supply_gain`. It does **not** call `add_money_earned` (`player.rs:847-852`, which writes `statistics.money_earned`). Salvage-money fallback uses the same pickup arm.

## Player-visible result
Picking a dollar crate / supply-drop crate / salvage-money crate increases cash but the end-of-match / score-screen \"money earned\" total omits that crate income. Retail counts crate cash as money earned.
close_reason: MoneyCrate credit_supplies plus ScoreKeeper add_money_earned

title: [CrateCollide] Live pickup skips HumanOnly and ForbidOwnerPlayer
description:
## C++
CrateCollide::isValidToExecute (CrateCollide.cpp:127-168) rejects: null/ground, neutral, no AIUpdateInterface unless BuildingPickup+KINDOF_STRUCTURE, isKindOfMulti(required, forbidden), dead, crate isAboveTerrain (except building pickup), ForbidOwnerPlayer when crate owner player equals picker player (not picked up by the dead guys team), HumanOnly unless PLAYER_HUMAN, PickupScience unless hasScience, and KINDOF_PARACHUTE. On success onCollide (:91-124) plays ExecuteFX on the picker, destroys the crate, then addWorldAnimation if DrawIconUI.

## Leftover Rust
crate_collide.rs:243-311 implements HumanOnly, ForbidOwnerPlayer, PickupScience, KindOf::Parachute, above-terrain, and building-pickup. Leftover crate modules are not dispatched for host objects (OBJECT_REGISTRY empty / TheGameLogic lookup miss).

## Live host
update_money_crate_collides (crates_radar_power.rs:212-440) is a radius residual. After closed hq-xipgk it checks salvage SCIENCE_GLA and KindOf::Parachute (not parachuting status). It still never reads HumanOnly or ForbidOwnerPlayer. Same-owner death crates (try_create_crates_on_die sets owner_player_id = victim_owner when owned_by_maker) can be picked by that players units. AI players can pick HumanOnly mission crates.

## Player-visible result
In missions, HumanOnly crates are collected by computer players. Death crates authored ForbidOwnerPlayer=Yes can be scooped by the victims own army. Retail leaves those crates for the enemy / human player.
close_reason: CrateCollide HumanOnly + ForbidOwnerPlayer on live pickup

title: [Physics] Ground slam ignores carrier deck height offset
description:
## C++
PhysicsUpdate.cpp:739-743 groundZ = TerrainLogic::getLayerHeight then if OBJECT_STATUS_DECK_HEIGHT_OFFSET, groundZ += getCarrierDeckHeight(). Bounce, slam, stun-kill, and fall damage all use that deck plane.

## Leftover

## Live host
Closed hq-wvlfr fixed stun ground_y=0 to terrain_height_at. world_tick/shock.rs:157-163 and tick_physics_motion_step still use raw terrain height only. No DECK_HEIGHT_OFFSET / landing_deck_height_offset is added. Distinct from closed hq-45zk/hq-8l7k (deck taxi friction).

## Player-visible
Stunned or falling jets on a carrier slam through the deck to sea level. testStunnedUnitForDestruction then sees underwater without water locomotor and kills them.

title: [Physics] Shock toss velocity hard-capped at 80
description:
## C++
PhysicsUpdate.cpp:342-348 applyShock only scales by (1-shockResistance) then applyForce (a=F/m). No post-impulse speed cap.

## Leftover
PhysicsBehaviorHandle::apply_shock (physics_update.rs:543-546) matches C++ (resist then apply_force). Empty registry → no-op.

Closed hq-5fqyz added mass/resistance. apply_shock_wave_impulse (object/physics.rs:78-85) still clamps |v| to MAX_SHOCK_SPEED=80 after the impulse (comment: so MOAB does not fling off-map).

## Player-visible
MOAB / nuke / demo-trap tosses travel a capped distance instead of retail mass-scaled flings.
close_reason: Shock toss no invented 80 speed cap

title: [Physics] KillWhenResting drone gate is name substring not KINDOF_DRONE
description:
## C++
PhysicsUpdate.cpp:883-892 killWhenRestingOnGround kills when settled on ground unless KINDOF_DRONE and alive and not DISABLED_UNMANNED.

Rest-kill debris/wrecks with KillWhenResting also delete living KindOf drones whose template name lacks \"drone\". Conversely a non-drone named *Drone* is wrongly spared.

title: [Physics] Non-stun landing skips bounce sound and ground onCollide
description:
## C++
PhysicsUpdate.cpp:822-831: WAS_AIRBORNE_LAST_FRAME && !airborneAtEnd && !IMMUNE → doBounceSound(prevPos) then obj->onCollide(NULL) (parachute container land) then falling-damage peel.

## Leftover
physics_update.rs:983-996 calls do_bounce_sound + physics_collide::on_collide(INVALID_ID) + obj.on_collide(None). Empty registry → no-op. Closed hq-7nh6 covered leftover bounce/right-up/stun-kill.

## Live host
tick_physics_motion_step (physics_motion.rs:713-718) on landing only apply_shock_fall_damage. record_bounce_land is only called from tick_shock_stun_with_countdown (line 915) while stunned. No ground onCollide(NULL) from the general Euler path.

Non-stun falls (parachute drop after stun expires, cliff drive-off, wreck without shock) play no land thud and never notify the container, so chutes/riders miss the retail land collide.

title: [Physics] INI friction/COM/fall/KillWhenResting never applied
description:
## C++
PhysicsBehaviorModuleData::buildFieldParse (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:140-173) loads Mass, ShockResistance, ShockMaxYaw/Pitch/Roll, Forward/Lateral/Z/AeroFriction (per-sec→per-frame), CenterOfMassOffset, AllowBouncing, AllowCollideForce, KillWhenRestingOnGround, MinFallHeightForDamage (heightToSpeed), FallHeightDamageFactor, PitchRollYawFactor, crash weapon templates.

Friction stays ctor defaults (0.15/0.15/0.8/0). kill_when_resting_on_ground stays false. center_of_mass_offset stays 0 so pitch damping toward vertical never runs. apply_shock_fall_damage hardcodes FALL_HEIGHT_DAMAGE_FACTOR=1.0 and height_to_fall_speed(40).

Authored heavy/light friction, tumbling COM, splat damage scale, and KillWhenResting debris never take effect. Units all slide/tumble/splat with the same defaults.

title: [Physics] Forward/lateral friction floor is 0 not MIN_NON_AERO 0.01
description:
## C++
PhysicsUpdate.cpp:268-283 getForwardFriction/getLateralFriction clamp extraFriction+base to [MIN_NON_AERO_FRICTION=0.01, MAX_FRICTION=0.99]. Ice/negative Extra2DFriction cannot cancel all scrub.

## Leftover
physics_update.rs:713-725 clamp_friction(..., MIN_NON_AERO_FRICTION). Empty registry → no-op.

host_partition_collision_physics_residual.rs defines PHYSICS_MIN_NON_AERO_FRICTION_RESIDUAL=0.01 but object/physics.rs:1226-1234 get_forward_friction/get_lateral_friction do `f.clamp(0.0, MAX_FRICTION_RESIDUAL)`. set_locomotor_physics_options adds loco_extra_2d_friction (can be negative) into extra_friction.

## Player-visible
Low-friction / extra-negative locomotor units lose all ground scrub and skate; retail always keeps at least 1% per-frame friction.

title: [Physics] Stun relief uses on-ground 5cm not 3-frame fall height
description:
## C++
PhysicsUpdate.cpp:672-682 clears IS_STUNNED when |vel|<STUN_RELIEF_EPSILON (0.5) OR isSignificantlyAboveTerrain()==FALSE (height ≤ 9 with g=-1). Units recover while still falling the last few units.

hq-yopy2 closed the 45-frame grounded stun, but maybe_clear_shock_stun_relief (physics_motion.rs:962-975) still uses `y <= ground_height+0.05` (or vel<0.5). That is "fully grounded", not C++'s 3-frame threshold.

## Player-visible
Tossed squads stay stunned/unable to fire for the whole remaining fall after they drop below ~9 height, instead of recovering as soon as they are no longer significantly airborne.
close_reason: Stun relief uses 3-frame fall height not 5cm ground

title: [Garrison] Script evac-to-left/right dumps in a circle
description:
## C++
`GarrisonContain::setEvacDisposition` + `exitObjectViaDoor` (`GarrisonContain.cpp:1473-1585`). Script `doNamedSetGarrisonEvacDisposition` (`ScriptActions.cpp:1579-1594`) sets `EVAC_TO_LEFT` / `EVAC_TO_RIGHT`. Exit then places each occupant at a random doorway pocket on that side and `aiFollowPath`s them out to `minorRadius * 10` spread. Campaign/script "pour out the left/right side of the building" just piles infantry in a small ring at the origin. They do not walk out a doorway or spread along the authored side.

title: [Garrison] Live fire uses 8-point ring not FIREPOINT bones
description:
## C++
`GarrisonContain::calcBestGarrisonPosition` / `putObjectAtBestGarrisonPoint` / `trackTargets` / `loadGarrisonPoints` (`GarrisonContain.cpp:256-400, 658-752, 1282-1382`): enclosing garrisons load art `FIREPOINT` bones (up to 40, per pristine/damaged/really-damaged condition). Not a duplicate of closed hq-omm0 (leftover local-space / skip FIREPOINT01+), hq-s8e65 (fire-goal used container center), or hq-u0smx (single PRIMARY from center). Those symptoms were replaced by this ring residual.

title: [Garrison] Fire Base infantry hide instead of station bones
description:
## C++
`GarrisonContain::matchObjectsToGarrisonPoints` / `positionObjectsAtStationGarrisonPoints` / `pickAStationForMe` (`GarrisonContain.cpp:953-1070, 1958-2026`): when `IsEnclosingContainer=No` (retail AmericaFireBase and variants), occupants stay at pre-assigned station bones, remain visible, and fire from those stations. They are not snapped to the building center or shuffled between FIREPOINTs.

title: [Garrison] Occupied building never gets CAN_ATTACK
description:
## C++
`GarrisonContain::onContaining` (`GarrisonContain.cpp:1589-1625`) sets `OBJECT_STATUS_CAN_ATTACK` on the structure once anyone is inside, plus `DISABLED_HELD` and `WEAPONBONUSCONDITION_GARRISONED` on the occupant. `onRemoving` clears `CAN_ATTACK` when the last occupant leaves. The player can select the garrisoned building and issue attack orders.

A garrisoned civilian bunker cannot be given attack / attack-move orders. The player cannot aim window fire at a chosen target; only the residual auto-acquire path shoots.

title: [Garrison] Enter never deselects the occupant
description:
## C++
`GarrisonContain::onContaining` (`GarrisonContain.cpp:1620-1622`): if the occupant's drawable is selected, `TheInGameUI->deselectDrawable`. Infantry disappear from the selection roster when they enter so the player is not left commanding hidden units.

Selected Rangers/Rebels stay selected after vanishing into a building. The selection box / control-bar portraits remain on hidden infantry instead of transferring off them (or onto the building).

title: [Sell] Campaign unsellable buildings still have a working Sell button

`ControlBarCommand.cpp:1156-1161` hides `GUI_COMMAND_SELL` when `obj->testScriptStatusBit(OBJECT_STATUS_SCRIPT_UNSELLABLE)`. title: [Build] Illegal place never bibs the blocking building, only the ghost

title: [Build] Placement ignores stealth and busy-ally gates
description:
## C++
`isLocationLegalToBuild` preview (`InGameUI.cpp:1454-1462`) passes `IGNORE_STEALTHED` so unseen stealthed units do not redden the ghost. Confirm-place uses `FAIL_STEALTHED_WITHOUT_FEEDBACK` (`BuildAssistant.h:98-99`, `isLocationClearOfObjects` `:662-678`): click fails without bib feedback.

Patch 1.01 (`BuildAssistant.cpp:681-688`): allied units with `OBJECT_STATUS_IS_USING_ABILITY` or `ai->isBusy()` return `LBC_OBJECTS_IN_THE_WAY` so a building cannot be dropped on a hacking Black Lotus to cancel the hack.

`FoundationValidator::validate_placement` (`construction.rs:299-317`) implements IGNORE_STEALTHED / FAIL_STEALTHED but only when `OBJECT_REGISTRY` is non-empty. Empty-registry skips object probes (`:299-300`). Leftover is not the live host legal-build path.

## Live host
`legal_build_code_at_for_builder` (`ui_production.rs:541-564`) treats every living Enemy / Immobile / Disabled / Structure as a blocker. No stealth / DETECTED / DISGUISED test. No USING_ABILITY / isBusy ally test.

`move_objects_for_construction` (`:732-734`) **skips** `status.using_ability` (will not scoot them) but placement still succeeds, so the building drops on top of the busy ally.

## Player-visible
Hovering a stealthed rebel/Jarmen Kell reddens the place ghost (stealth leak). Clicking to place on a hacking Black Lotus succeeds — the 1.01 exploit C++ closed.
close_reason: legal_build preview IGNORE_STEALTHED, confirm FAIL_STEALTHED, busy-ally USING_ABILITY/isBusy blocks

title: [Weapon] Live stream name peels PRIMARY seed only, ignores store ProjectileStreamName
description:
## C++
`Weapon.cpp` `fireWeaponTemplate` (1116) always calls `firingWeapon->newProjectileFired`. That uses **this** template's `m_projectileStreamName` (INI `ProjectileStreamName`) and creates/reuses a per-weapon stream object. Secondary/tertiary stream weapons get their own ribbon.

## Leftover Rust
Store/template parse `ProjectileStreamName` (`weapon_template.rs` / `ini_template_loader.rs:1012-1013`). `new_projectile_fired` uses `self.template.projectile_stream_name`. Empty-registry leftover never runs.

## Live host
`weapon_bootstrap/damage_kinds.rs` `host_projectile_stream_name_for_weapon_name` (34-55) is **seed-only** (flame/dragon → DragonTankFlameStream, toxin spray/stream → ToxinStream, microwave, cleanup). It never reads `wt.projectile_stream_name` from the live WeaponStore. `world_tick/step.rs` (836-847) always peels `thing.template.primary_weapon_name`, even when the shot came from secondary/tertiary. Closed hq-jay8 only wired leftover `new_projectile_fired`.

## Player-visible
Authored streams that are not in the seed (Aurora/comet-style ProjectileStreamName, any non-primary slot stream) never appear. A unit whose PRIMARY is a gun and whose stream weapon is another slot draws nothing, or the wrong ribbon.
close_reason: damage_kinds reads store ProjectileStreamName; step uses firing/historic slot not PRIMARY-only seed

title: [Weapon] ShareWeaponReloadTime copies last_fire_time not the firing slot next-shot frame
description:
## C++
`Weapon.cpp` `privateFireWeapon` (2655-2665): if `sourceObj->isReloadTimeShared()`, every slot gets `setPossibleNextShotFrame(m_whenWeCanFireAgain)` and `BETWEEN_FIRING_SHOTS`, where `m_whenWeCanFireAgain` is **now + the firing weapon's DelayBetweenShots**. `reloadWithBonus` (1898-1909) does the same with `RELOADING_CLIP` and the firing weapon's ClipReloadTime. Parsed on WeaponSet (`WeaponSet.cpp:135` ShareWeaponReloadTime).

## Leftover Rust
`weapon_instance.rs` `propagate_shared_timing` / `reload_with_bonus` copy the firing weapon's `when_we_can_fire_again` + status. Empty-registry leftover is not live.

## Live host
`object/weapons.rs` `sync_shared_weapon_reload` (588-607) only copies the **max last_fire_time** across slots 0/1/2. Ready checks then use each slot's own `live_reload_interval` (DelayBetweenShots or that slot's ClipReloadTime). Closed hq-y55ip wired the copy; it did not match C++ shared next-shot frame/status.

## Player-visible
Comanche (ShareWeaponReloadTime Yes): after the chaingun fires, rocket pods wait their own long delay (retail waits the gun's short delay). After rocket-pod fire, the gun is ready on the gun interval (retail waits the rocket delay). Multi-weapon jets desync clip cadence vs retail.
close_reason: sync_shared_weapon_reload copies firing-slot next-shot via last_fire back-compute; reload_aim helpers

title: [Weapon] Live scatter offset is pairing-deterministic so repeat shots land in the same miss
description:
## C++
`Weapon.cpp` `fireWeaponTemplate` (979-989): each shot rolls `GameLogicRandomValueReal(0, scatterRadius)` and `GameLogicRandomValueReal(0, 2*PI)` independently from the global logic RNG. Successive shells vs the same infantry/building land in different places.

## Leftover Rust
Leftover `fire_weapon_template` uses `get_game_logic_random_value_real`. Empty `OBJECT_REGISTRY` leftover fire is not the live path.

## Live host
`Main/src/game_logic/combat.rs` (971-980) seeds `scatter_aim_offset` with `shooter_id * const + target_id * const` — **no frame**. `weapon_bootstrap/scatter.rs` `scatter_aim_offset` (213-221) is a pure ADC function of that seed. Same shooter+target therefore produces the identical XZ offset every shot. (`scatter_seed_for_shot` includes frame but drain does not call it.)

## Player-visible
Crusader / Inferno / Tomahawk / Fire Base / Strategy Center vs the same infantry always miss (or hit) the same offset. Retail walks the miss cone around the target.
close_reason: combat drain uses scatter_aim_offset_logic GameLogicRandomValueReal per shot, not pairing seed

title: [Weapon] Live projectile streams never break on retarget or skim vehicle roofs
description:
## C++
`ProjectileStreamUpdate.cpp` `addProjectile` (61-108): when the victim object or victim position changes, insert `INVALID_ID` into the circular `m_projectileIDs` ring so `getAllPoints` writes a (0,0,0) hole and the ribbon breaks. `getAllPoints` (131-183): for a live projectile owned by a `KINDOF_VEHICLE`, if the point is within 1.5× major radius of the owner, raise Z to `geometry.maxHeightAbovePosition + pos.z + 0.5` so the stream skims the hull instead of clipping through it. `Weapon.cpp` `newProjectileFired` (2388-2414) creates/reuses that stream Thing from the firing template's `ProjectileStreamName`.

## Leftover Rust
`GameLogic/src/object/behavior/projectile_stream_update.rs` `add_projectile` (111-133) and `get_all_points` (140-187) port the hole + vehicle-roof skim. `weapon_instance.rs` `new_projectile_fired` (882-971) creates the stream Thing via `TheThingFactory`. With empty `OBJECT_REGISTRY` the factory/lookup path no-ops, so leftover never draws.

## Live host
`Main/src/game_logic/host_projectile_stream.rs` `add_point` (34-49) only `push`es positions (cap 20) and overwrites `target_id`/`target_pos` — no INVALID hole on retarget. No vehicle-roof Z raise. `world_tick/step.rs` (832-861) feeds current projectile positions every frame. Presentation packs those points as a continuous polyline (`presentation_frame/build.rs` + `laser_segment_upload.rs`).

## Player-visible
Dragon Tank / Toxin Tractor / microwave / cleanup streams stay one connected ribbon when the unit switches targets (retail breaks the trail). Flame/toxin also clips through the vehicle hull instead of riding the roof.
close_reason: host_projectile_stream + step: INVALID hole on retarget, vehicle roof skim, laser pack skips holes

title: [Weapon] Live scatter aims at structure origin not geometry center
description:
## C++
`Weapon.cpp` `fireWeaponTemplate` (960-967): when applying ScatterRadius / ScatterRadiusVsInfantry, if the victim is `KINDOF_STRUCTURE`, `getGeometryInfo().getCenterPosition` so the random disk is around the building volume, not the ground stamp. Then Z is snapped to the victim's pathfind layer.

## Leftover Rust
Leftover fire template has the structure-center branch; empty-registry leftover is not live.

## Live host
`Main/src/game_logic/combat.rs` (933-981) takes `obj.get_position()` (ground origin) then adds `scatter_aim_offset` / ScatterTarget table. Table path may snap Y to `ground_height` when `ground_height_from_terrain`; there is no geometry-center lift for structures.

## Player-visible
Artillery / tank / missile scatter vs buildings clusters around the footprint origin (often a corner/feet). Retail walks the miss cone around the building center, so more shells clip the volume instead of hitting dirt beside the door.
close_reason: combat scatter aims KINDOF_STRUCTURE at geometry center then snaps Y to ground

title: [TurretAI] Sweep FirePitch RecenterTime FiresWhileTurning INI unused
description:
## C++
`TurretAIData` INI (`TurretAI.cpp:212-237`): `TurretFireAngleSweep`/`TurretSweepSpeedModifier` per slot, `AllowsPitch`, `FirePitch`, `MinPhysicalPitch`, `GroundUnitPitch`, `RecenterTime`, `FiresWhileTurning`, `InitiallyDisabled`. Sweep enables 3 frames after `notifyFired` (`:697-702`). RecenterTime default `2*LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND` (60); Humvee authors **5000 ms → 150** frames. FiresWhileTurning keeps rotate/pitch sound across the fire/sweep window (`:683-688`).

## Leftover
`ai_update_interface.rs:533-673` parses every field. Unused when `OBJECT_REGISTRY` is empty.

## Live host
`set_turret_fire_angle_sweep` / `set_turret_pitch_params` / `set_turret_idle_scan_params` (`attack.rs:718-762`) exist but have **zero spawn callers**. Seed only hardcodes FirePitch for names containing `strategycenter` (45°) or `tomahawk` (70°). `fire_angle_sweep` stays `[0,0,0]` so the closed hq-3bka9 mechanism never runs in a match. `turret_recenter_frames` stays 60 for everyone (`HUMVEE_TURRET_RECENTER_FRAMES` unused). No `fires_while_turning` field — `TurretMoveLoop` drops the instant `turret_rotating` is false.

## Player-visible
Gattling/QuadCannon never waggle after bursts. Nuke Cannon/Inferno never use authored pitch. Humvee recenters after 2s instead of 5s. Rotate loop stutters between shots on FiresWhileTurning units.
close_reason: Spawn applies Sweep/FirePitch/RecenterTime/FiresWhileTurning from INI or honesty (Humvee 150f, SC/Tomahawk FirePitch, Gattling sweep). files: object/turret_spawn.rs world_tick/attack.rs

title: [Fire] Tree-to-tree spread is a fixed 1.5s 2D check, not random 3D
description:
## C++
`FireSpreadUpdate::calcNextSpreadDelay` (`FireSpreadUpdate.cpp:149-155`) `GameLogicRandomValue(MinSpreadDelay, MaxSpreadDelay)` (trees 1000–2000ms → 30–60f), min 1. `update` (`:123`) `getClosestObject(..., FROM_CENTER_3D, PartitionFilterFlammable)` so height (cliffs / bridges) counts.

## Leftover Rust
`fire_spread_update.rs` `calc_next_spread_delay` uses `game_logic_random_value` and Center3D. Wave 447 empty-registry `update_simple` Forever-sleeps on the live path.

## Live host
`HostFireSpreadData::calc_next_spread_delay` (`host_fire_spread.rs:174-179`) is the midpoint of min/max (always 45f / 1.5s). `update_fire_spread` (`infantry_weapons.rs:1452-1456`) uses `sqrt(dx*dx + dz*dz)` — Y ignored.

## Player-visible result
A row of trees ignites in lockstep every 1.5s. Trees on a cliff vs the valley floor can catch (or miss) as if they were on the same plane.
close_reason: calc_next_spread_delay uses GameLogicRandomValue(min,max) min 1. update_fire_spread closest flammable uses FROM_CENTER_3D (dx,dy,dz) not planar xz.

title: [Fire] AFLAME/SMOLDERING model and auto-aflame particles never apply
description:
## C++
`tryToIgnite` (`FlammableUpdate.cpp:175-177`) `setStatus(AFLAME)`, `body->setAflame(TRUE)`, `setModelConditionState(MODELCONDITION_AFLAME)`. Burned timer (`:122-123`) adds MODELCONDITION_SMOLDERING while still aflame. `ActiveBody::updateBodyParticleSystems` (`ActiveBody.cpp:1108-1175`) when OBJECT_STATUS_AFLAME upgrades fire/smoke bones (small→medium, smoke→fire, countModifier 2) and attaches `m_autoAflameParticleSystem`.

## Leftover Rust
`behavior/flammable_update.rs` sets AFLAME status + model condition on ignite (best-effort if the object is in a registry) but Wave 379 empty-registry never ticks, never sets SMOLDERING on the live path.

## Live host
`update_fire_spread` only `apply_status_bits_upgrade_masks(&["AFLAME"])` / `BURNED` (`infantry_weapons.rs:1466-1474`). That writes `object_status_bits` and does **not** set model bits. `refresh_model_condition_bits` (`object/pose.rs:636-888`) rebuilds from body/motion and never stamps AFLAME/SMOLDERING from status. Presentation Wave 511/524 stamps those bits from **death type**, not live burning. No `setAflame` / auto-aflame particle bones.

## Player-visible result
A burning tree keeps its normal mesh and normal damage-smoke particles. C++ swaps to the AFLAME model and bigger fire bones for the whole burn, then SMOLDERING while still aflame.
close_reason: refresh_model_condition_bits stamps AFLAME/SMOLDERING from status + fire_spread. apply_flammable_visuals sets AFLAME/BURNED bits + body_aflame. spawn_auto_aflame_particles attaches AutoAflame on ignite.

title: [Fire] Burning loop never plays
description:
## C++
`FlammableUpdate::tryToIgnite` calls `startBurningSound` (`FlammableUpdate.cpp:217-223`): `AudioEventRTS(m_burningSoundName, objId)` + `TheAudio->addAudioEvent`. `stopBurningSound` (`:227-233`) removes the handle when aflame ends or the module dies. Retail trees use `GenericFireMediumLoop`.

## Leftover Rust
`object/update/flammable_update.rs` `start_burning_sound` plays if `ctx.audio` is set. Registered leftover `behavior/flammable_update.rs` `try_to_ignite` never starts the loop; `update_simple` Wave 379 empty-registry no-op.

## Live host
`TREE_BURNING_SOUND = "GenericFireMediumLoop"` is an honesty constant in `host_fire_spread.rs:39`. `try_to_ignite` / `tick_flammable` / `update_fire_spread` never queue it. No `addAudioEvent` / fire-loop start on ignite.

## Player-visible result
Burning trees and (if ignition is added) buildings are silent. C++ loops GenericFireMediumLoop for the whole AflameDuration.
close_reason: tryToIgnite / first aflame tick queues looping GenericFireMediumLoop (AudioEventRequest.looping). stop_fire_spread_burning_sound on aflame_end.

title: [Fire] FlameDamageExpiration never resets — spaced hits always ignite
description:
## C++
`FlammableUpdate::onDamage` (`FlammableUpdate.cpp:82-88`): if `now - FlameDamageExpiration > m_lastFlameDamageDealt` (default 2s / 60f), reset `m_flameDamageLimit` to the authored limit, then subtract this hit. Spaced-out small flame ticks do not accumulate across the expiration window.

## Leftover Rust
`behavior/flammable_update.rs` `on_damage` and `update/flammable_update.rs` both port the expiration reset. Leftover never runs on the live host (OBJECT_REGISTRY empty).

## Live host
`HostFireSpreadData::apply_flame_damage` (`host_fire_spread.rs:160-171`) only `flame_damage_accum += amount` with no last-dealt timestamp and no reset. `damage.rs:389-400` feeds every Flame/ParticleBeam hit into that accum.

## Player-visible result
A tree that takes 1 flame damage, waits three seconds, then another 1 damage ignites (limit 2). In C++ the threshold would have reset and it would still need two hits inside two seconds.
close_reason: apply_flame_damage matches FlammableUpdate.cpp:82-88: if now-expiration > lastDealt reset remaining limit to authored, then subtract. Spaced hits no longer accumulate across the 2s window.

title: [Fire] Aflame always becomes permanently Burned; no SMOLDERING-while-aflame
description:
## C++
`FlammableUpdate::tryToIgnite` (`FlammableUpdate.cpp:192-194`): `m_burnedEndFrame = burnedDelay ? now+delay : 0` (0 = never burned). `update` (`:119-143`): at burned_end independently sets OBJECT_STATUS_BURNED + MODELCONDITION_SMOLDERING **while still AFLAME**. At aflame_end: if already BURNED stay FS_BURNED (never re-ignite); else return FS_NORMAL and can catch fire again.

## Leftover Rust
`behavior/flammable_update.rs` `update_simple` ports the independent timers, but Wave 379 empty-registry Forever-sleeps so it never runs live.

## Live host
`HostFireSpreadData::try_to_ignite` (`host_fire_spread.rs:145-146`) always sets `burned_end_frame = now + burned_delay.max(aflame_duration)`. `tick_flammable` (`:199-201`) on aflame_end **always** `state = Burned` / `became_burned` — never returns to Normal, never applies SMOLDERING while still AFLAME. Trees (BurnedDelay 75f, AflameDuration 105f) skip the 30-frame smoldering-while-burning window.

## Player-visible result
Burning trees jump straight to permanently burned when the flame timer ends. Objects that should go out and be re-ignitable stay charcoal forever. No smoldering model while still on fire.
close_reason: tryToIgnite burned_end = burnedDelay ? now+delay : 0. tick_flammable sets SMOLDERING/BURNED status while still AFLAME; at aflame_end stay Burned if already burned else return Normal (re-ignitable).

title: [Fire] Spreading trees never spawn OCL BurningEmbers
description:
## C++
`FireSpreadUpdate::update` (`FireSpreadUpdate.cpp:93-134`) while OBJECT_STATUS_AFLAME always `ObjectCreationList::create(d->m_oclEmbers, getObject(), NULL)` (retail `OCL_BurningEmbers`) before the closest-flammable ignite.

## Leftover Rust
`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/update/fire_spread_update.rs` `update` / `update_simple` can create the OCL, but Wave 447 empty-registry gate makes `update_simple` return Forever on the live path. Closed `hq-f0s1` only covers this leftover crate.

## Live host
`update_fire_spread` / `apply_fire_spread_tick_event` (`world_combat/infantry_weapons.rs:1369-1445`) set `spawn_embers` then `let _ = TREE_OCL_EMBERS` — honesty name only, fail-closed, no OCL objects.

## Player-visible result
Forest fires have no ember spray / ember objects when they tick-spread. Trees may still ignite neighbors, but the C++ ember FX is missing.
close_reason: FireSpreadUpdate tick now ObjectCreationList::create(OCL_BurningEmbers) via spawn_fire_spread_embers (parsed OCL or BurningEmbers object + combat particle ocl_list_name). infantry_weapons no longer let _ = TREE_OCL_EMBERS.

title: [AIGuard] EnterGuard/HijackGuard unused so Hijackers shoot instead of boarding
description:
## C++
`ThingTemplate` `EnterGuard` / `HijackGuard` (`ThingTemplate.cpp` parse, `isEnterGuard`/`isHijackGuard`).
`AIGuardMachine::lookForInnerTarget` (`AIGuard.cpp` ~221) and `AIGuardInnerState::onEnter` (~364): if EnterGuard, filter `PartitionFilterPossibleToEnter` (HijackGuard: enemies + `PossibleToHijack`; else neutrals) and run `AIEnterState` instead of `AIAttackState`. Same in `AIGuardRetaliate` (~229, ~345). Hijacker / Terrorist / similar INI set these flags so Guard means "board/hijack anything in the circle", not shoot it.

## Leftover
`GameEngine/Common/src/common/thing/thing_template.rs` parses `EnterGuard`/`HijackGuard`. `ai/guard.rs` `scan_guard_inner_target` + `AIGuardInnerState::classic_on_enter` enter/hijack. Empty-registry leftover unused.

## Live host
Main `ThingTemplate` has **no** `enter_guard`/`hijack_guard` field (no parse in `Main/src/assets`). `support_states.rs` Guard always `get_able_to_attack_specific_object` + `engage_target_decision_aware` → `attack_target` (guns). No enter/hijack branch.

## Player-visible
Order a GLA Hijacker or Terrorist to Guard a parking lot: they shoot the vehicles instead of hijacking / converting to carbomb. Retail Guard on those templates is a boarding hunt inside the circle.
close_reason: EnterGuard/HijackGuard on ThingTemplate+INI; Guard boards not shoots; files: thing.rs spawn_templates.rs support_states.rs

title: [AIStates] Hunt/Guard/Attack-Move never pick up crates they created
description:
## C++
Crate pickup is wired into every combat-wander state, not just idle:
- `AIGuardIdleState::update` (`AIGuard.cpp` ~704) → `AI_GUARD_GET_CRATE`
- `AIGuardRetaliateIdleState::update` (`AIGuardRetaliate.cpp` ~idle crate branch)
- `AIHuntState::update` (`AIStates.cpp` ~7139) → `AI_PICK_UP_CRATE`
- `AIAttackMoveToState::update` (`AIStates.cpp` ~3607) → `AI_PICK_UP_CRATE`
- `AIIdleState::update` (`AIStates.cpp` ~1399) → `aiMoveToObject(crate)`

## Leftover
`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/guard.rs` `AIGuardPickUpCrateState`, `guard_retaliate.rs` crate state, `states/hunt.rs` crate branch, leftover attack-move. Empty-registry leftover is unused.

## Live host
`world_tick/teams.rs` `try_idle_crate_pickup` **requires `AIState::Idle`** (comment: "C++ only while idle" — that comment is wrong vs C++). Called from `world_tick/ai.rs` before `process_ai_behavior`. Hunt/Patrol (`Patrolling`), Guard (`GuardingArea`/`GuardingObject`), Attack-Move (`AttackMoving`), and Guard-Retaliate never consume `crate_created`.

## Player-visible
A computer unit that kills something while Hunting, Guarding, Attack-Moving, or Retaliating leaves the money/veterancy crate on the ground and walks away. Only a fully Idle unit ever stoops to pick it up. Retail units grab the crate before resuming the order.
close_reason: Crate pickup from Idle/Hunt/Guard/AttackMove/GuardRetaliate; combat states keep parent AI; files: teams.rs

title: [AIGuard] Guard range is hardcoded 80/1.5x not mood-adjusted vision
description:
## C++
`AIGuardMachine::getStdGuardRange` (`AIGuard.cpp` ~176) = `TheAI->getAdjustedVisionRangeForObject(obj, AI_VISIONFACTOR_OWNERTYPE | AI_VISIONFACTOR_MOOD | AI_VISIONFACTOR_GUARDINNER)`.
Inner exit radius is that value. Outer (`AIGuardOuterState::onEnter` ~504) uses vision **without** GUARDINNER, plus `m_guardChaseUnitFrames` give-up timer that **resets** if the victim re-enters inner vision. WithoutPursuit skips outer entirely. Area-guard uses polygon radius/center and `m_guardEnemyScanRate` / trigger-area dirty stamp.

## Leftover
`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/guard.rs` `get_std_guard_range` / outer chase frames / area scan-rate. Unused on empty `OBJECT_REGISTRY`.

## Live host
`world_objects/support_states.rs` GuardingArea: `radius = guard_radius.max(80.0)`; Normal acquire = `radius * 1.5`; return home if `distance(anchor) > radius * 0.6`. No mood/owner vision, no chase-timer, no polygon area, no scan-rate. GuardingObject uses `find_nearest_enemy_for_attacker(..., radius)` with the same 80 floor.

## Player-visible
A Sleep/Passive guard still uses the full 80/120 bubble. An Aggressive guard does not get the C++ mood-widened vision. Units start walking back at 0.6× (48wu at the floor) instead of chasing for `GuardChaseUnitFrames` and only giving up outside outer vision. Area-guard (Guard Area on a trigger) is not a polygon at all — it is the same 80-circle. Posts feel too small, too sticky, or both, depending on the unit's authored vision.
close_reason: Guard range mood-adjusted vision (OWNERTYPE|MOOD|GUARDINNER) + outer; return at inner not 0.6x80; files: teams.rs support_states.rs

title: [AIGuard] Guarding units never interrupt to return fire at last attacker
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/AI/AIGuard.cpp` `hasAttackedMeAndICanReturnFire` (~39) is a **state-condition** on INNER, RETURN, and IDLE (ctor ~150-164).
Uses `BodyModule::getClearableLastAttacker`, requires ENEMIES, not dead, `isAbleToAttack`, `getAbleToAttackSpecificObject(ATTACK_NEW_TARGET) == POSSIBLE|POSSIBLE_AFTER_MOVING`. Transitions to `AI_GUARD_ATTACK_AGGRESSOR` (`AIGuardAttackAggressorState::onEnter` ~788) which overwrites nemesis from last-damage `sourceID` and attacks with inner-range + chase-timer exit conditions.

Same condition exists on `AIGuardRetaliate` RETURN/IDLE (`AIGuardRetaliate.cpp` ~38, ctor ~157).

## Leftover
`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/guard.rs` `has_attacked_me_and_i_can_return_fire` + `last_damage_overrides_nemesis` (closed leftover `hq-k7fiw`). Unused when `OBJECT_REGISTRY` is empty.

## Live host
`world_objects/support_states.rs` GuardingArea/GuardingObject only pick the nearest legal enemy inside `acquire_radius`. No last-attacker condition, no `AI_GUARD_ATTACK_AGGRESSOR`. `tick_guard_retaliate` only keeps the original victim locked.

## Player-visible
Snipe a guarding Ranger from just outside the 80/1.5x bubble (or while they are walking back): they do not spin onto you. Retail Guard immediately returns fire at the unit that shot them, even if another enemy is closer to the flag.
close_reason: Guard last-attacker interrupt via getClearableLastAttacker; files: support_states.rs teams.rs

title: [FXListDie] DeathFX ignores StartsActive ConflictsWith authored list
description:
## C++
`FXListDie.cpp:23-72` / `FXListDie.h:31-36`: ctor `giveSelfUpgrade` if `StartsActive` (default TRUE). `onDie`: require upgrade active, DieMux, skip if object or player `ConflictsWith` mask matches, then `FXList::doFXObj` (OrientToObject default TRUE) or `doFXPos` with authored DeathFX.

## Leftover Rust
`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/die/fx_list_die.rs:284-387` ports StartsActive, ConflictsWith, DieMux, doFXObj/doFXPos via leftover TheFXListStore / TheGameLogic. Leftover modules not attached on live host.

## Live host
`host_fx_list_die.rs:39-89` name peels (bombtruck/terrorist/scud/nuke/tank/vehicle/building) to generic FX names. No StartsActive, no ConflictsWith, no DieMux, OrientToObject always false. `fire_fx_list_die` queues those names. Closed hq-br7up was FXList nugget runner never called (now dispatched); this is authored FXListDie gating vs peels.

## Player-visible
Death explosions use generic FX_VehicleDie / FX_StructureDie instead of authored DeathFX. ConflictsWith upgrades do not suppress death FX. StartsActive=No FXListDie still fires. Orient-to-attacker explosions face world axes.
close_reason: FXListDie StartsActive default TRUE, ConflictsWith skip, OrientToObject default TRUE, authored DeathFX

title: [CrushDie] Crush deaths never play CrushDie sounds
description:
## C++
`CrushDie.cpp:139-184` `onDie`: DieMux + DAMAGE_CRUSH only. `crushLocationCheck` picks TOTAL/FRONT/BACK. If crush sound event is non-empty and `GameLogicRandomValue(0,99) < crushSoundPercent` (default 100), `TheAudio->addAudioEvent` with object ID. Then set body front/back crushed and MODELCONDITION_FRONTCRUSHED/BACKCRUSHED.

## Leftover Rust
`GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/die/crush_die.rs:308-432` ports crushLocationCheck, `play_crush_sound` via leftover `TheAudio`, and model conditions. Leftover TheGameLogic::find_object_by_id for crusher — empty-registry no-op on live host.

## Live host
`object/physics_motion.rs:220-311` sets front/back crushed and `apply_crush_die_model_conditions` (model bits only). No TotalCrushSound / FrontEndCrushSound / BackEndCrushSound / percent roll. No crush audio event queued.

## Player-visible
Tanks crushing infantry/cars are silent. Retail CrushDie percents (often 100) never fire. Visual crush bits may still flip.
close_reason: CrushDie sounds: Total/Front/Back percent roll queued as pending death audio on crushed death

title: [Sticky] Timed and remote charges never play UnitBombPing
description:
## C++
`StickyBombUpdate.cpp` `initStickyBomb` (134-136) plays per-unit `StickyBombCreated`. `update` (180-189): every `LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND` plays per-unit `UnitBombPing` on the charge object so timed and remote C4 tick once per second until they blow.

## Leftover Rust
`sticky_bomb_update.rs` ports both audio events, gated by Wave 305 empty-registry no-op so leftover never plays live.

## Live host

title: [Sticky] Building C4 snaps to structure center not plant XY
description:

title: [Poison] Anthrax/SCUD/bio fields damage aircraft

title: [Poison] DoT ticks play Unresistable FX not poison
description:
## C++
PoisonedBehavior::update (PoisonedBehavior.cpp:99-105) retakes the original amount as DAMAGE_UNRESISTABLE so it does not re-infect, but sets m_damageFXOverride = DAMAGE_POISON. ActiveBody::attemptDamage (ActiveBody.cpp:299-304) uses the override for doDamageFX so each DoT pulse plays the armor-set poison FX (green splat / poison audio), not Unresistable FX.

## Leftover Rust
poisoned_behavior.rs:237-243 sets damage_fx_override = DamageType::Poison on the Unresistable DoT, matching C++. Empty OBJECT_REGISTRY no-ops the update, so leftover never plays FX on the host-only path.

world_tick/ai.rs:106-112 and apply_host_residual_mutation_op PoisonDot (host_ops_writeback.rs:481-492) call take_damage_from_typed_death(..., Unresistable, death_type) with no FX override field. damage.rs:371-375 dispatch_armor_damage_fx(self, damage_type, actual_damage) looks up DamageFX.ini by Unresistable, not Poison. Green TINT_STATUS_POISONED still applies (is_poison_tinted / apply_poison_tint).

## Player-visible
Poisoned infantry/vehicles pulse the wrong hit FX (or none) every ~100ms instead of the retail poison DamageFX. Tint is green, but the per-tick spark/splat/audio is Unresistable.
close_reason: DoT applies Unresistable via take_damage_from_typed_death_fx with poison FX override (C++ m_damageFXOverride=DAMAGE_POISON).

title: [Body] Health box uses fixed 20-wide pose, ignores geometry

title: [FlightDeck] Deck jets never taxi forward; ramp/catapult never fire
description:
## C++
`FlightDeckBehavior::update` parking cleanup (`FlightDeckBehavior.cpp:1094-1162`) every `ParkingCleanupPeriod` promotes an idle/reloading jet from a rear stall on the same runway into a vacant front stall, sets `OBJECT_STATUS_REASSIGN_PARKING`, and `aiFollowExitProductionPath` to the new prep. After a front-row move it waits `HumanFollowPeriod` before the next shuffle. Launch also drives ramp model conditions (`MODELCONDITION_DOOR_2_OPENING/CLOSING` per runway) and fires `RunwayNCatapultSystem` at the takeoff-start transform after `CatapultFireDelay`. `calcBestParkingAssignment` (`:827-926`) is the same-runway bubble used by JetAI taxi.

## Leftover Rust
`update_parking_assignments` + `update_launch_waves` (`flight_deck_behavior.rs:917-1273`) port cleanup, REASSIGN_PARKING, ramp flags, and catapult particle create. Leftover never ticks on the live host.

## Live host
Land `airfield.rs` has no FlightDeck cleanup, no per-runway front-only takeoff, no REASSIGN_PARKING taxi, no ramp modelcondition, no catapult particle. `apply_authored_parking_place_metadata` drops `FlightDeckBehavior` so carriers have no stall roster at all.

## Player-visible result
Even if payload jets existed, they would sit in their original stalls instead of bubbling to the catapult. Carrier ramps never raise/lower and catapult steam never plays.
close_reason: same-runway taxi promote + DOOR_2 ramp + catapult fire (host_flight_deck.rs)

title: [Score] Starting CC/units never call onStructureComplete/onUnitCreated
description:
## C++
`placeNetworkStartingUnits` (`GameLogic.cpp:555-584`):
- Starting construction yard: `onStructureCreated` then `onStructureConstructionComplete(..., FALSE)` → `addObjectBuilt` + `addMoneySpent(calcCostToBuild)`.
- Each `StartingUnit0..N`: `onUnitCreated(NULL, unit)` → `addObjectBuilt`.

Skirmish/MP scoreboard therefore includes the free starting CC and dozer/worker in Buildings/Units Built (and CC cost in money spent).

## Rust
`spawn_skirmish_starting_units` (`world_tick/production.rs:1467-1620`) calls `create_object_for_player` only. That helper (`create_destroy_die.rs:241-251`) never invokes `Player::on_unit_created` or `on_structure_construction_complete`.

## Evidence
C++ `GameLogic.cpp:555-584` vs Rust `production.rs:1528,1589` + `create_destroy_die.rs:241-251`.

## Player-visible
Skirmish/MP Units Built starts at 0 instead of counting the starting dozer/worker; Buildings Built omits the starting command center. Money spent is short by the CC cost (not shown on the main Resources line, but used by leftover `get_total_score` if displayed).
close_reason: spawn_skirmish_starting_units notifies leftover Player addObjectBuilt+addMoneySpent via notify_skirmish_starting_object

title: [NeutronMissile] Live never detonates on terrain or object collision
description:
## C++
`NeutronMissileUpdate::update` (`NeutronMissileUpdate.cpp:496-504`): if state is not PRELAUNCH/DEAD and `!getObject()->isAboveTerrain()`, calls `onCollide(NULL, pos, down)` (normal 0,0,-1). That routes to `projectileHandleCollision` (`:406-423`): ignore if unarmed or `other` is the launcher; else `detonate()` (`kill()`, hide drawable, `OBJECT_STATUS_NO_COLLISIONS`) so SlowDeath can run on the missile.

Armed mid-air hits on other objects also detonate.

## Rust
**Leftover** `neutron_missile_update.rs:697-722, 803-818` ports both the terrain `onCollide` and launcher-skip collision.

**Live** `host_neutron_missile_update.rs:217-228` only grounds when `new_pos.y <= dest.y.max(0) + 2`. No `isAboveTerrain` at the missile’s XY, no object-collision arming. `update_neutron_missile_flights` (`registries.rs:726-782`) then immediately `mark_object_for_destruction` after spawning the slow-death field.

## Evidence
C++ `NeutronMissileUpdate.cpp:406-423, 496-504`. Leftover `neutron_missile_update.rs:697-818`. Live `host_neutron_missile_update.rs:205-228` + `world_combat/registries.rs:726-789`.

## Player-visible
Over hills the nuke can fly through terrain or explode in the air at the click’s Y. It also never detonates on a unit/building it strikes on the way down — only when it reaches the target’s stored height.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Live dive uses isAboveTerrain at current XY (not dest.y epsilon)
- [ ] Armed collision with a non-launcher object detonates
- [ ] Unarmed / launcher hits stay inert
close_reason: live terrain isAboveTerrain + armed object collide skip launcher; leftover already matched

title: [NeutronMissile] Live blast falloff is 2D; C++ uses 3D distance
description:
## C++
`doBlast` iterates `FROM_CENTER_2D` so anything in the ground cylinder is a candidate, then falloff uses **3D** `forceVector.length()` (`NeutronMissileSlowDeathUpdate.cpp:308-335`):
- `dist <= innerRadius` → `maxDamage`
- else `maxDamage * (1 - (dist-inner)/(outer-inner+0.01))`, clamped to `minDamage`

Retail Blast6: inner 60, outer 210, max 3500, min 300. An aircraft 80 above the epicenter at 0 XY has 3D dist 80, so it is already outside the inner ring.

## Rust
**Leftover** `do_blast` (`neutron_missile_slow_death_update.rs:434-464`) uses 3D `force_vector.length()` after a 2D XY range query — matches C++.

**Live** `plan_neutron_frame` (`host_neutron_missile_slow_death.rs:314-324`) computes `dist = hypot(dx, dz)` only (host Y-up). `blast_damage_at_distance` is documented as “2D distance”. Aircraft / elevated objects in the cylinder get full inner-ring 3500.

## Evidence
C++ `NeutronMissileSlowDeathUpdate.cpp:291-335`. Leftover `behavior/neutron_missile_slow_death_update.rs:429-464`. Live `host_neutron_missile_slow_death.rs:173-190, 314-324` and apply `world_scripts/special_power_strikes.rs:578-670`.

## Player-visible
Planes and high props over a nuke take the full inner blast. Retail reduces that by 3D distance (often to the 300 minimum or less).

## Acceptance
- [ ] Live candidate gather stays 2D cylinder (FROM_CENTER_2D)
- [ ] Falloff distance is 3D length including height
- [ ] Blast6 at (0,80,0) vs epicenter (0,0,0) is not maxDamage 3500
close_reason: live blast falloff uses 3D forceVector.length after 2D candidate query

title: [NeutronMissile] Live blast topple is name-gated; C++ topples any ToppleUpdate
description:
## C++
`NeutronMissileSlowDeathBehavior::doBlast` (`NeutronMissileSlowDeathUpdate.cpp:302-316`) walks every object in `outerRadius` (`FROM_CENTER_2D`) and calls `other->topple(&forceVector, toppleSpeed, NO_BOUNCE|NO_FX)`.

`Object::topple` (`Object.cpp:1171-1184`) applies only if the victim has `ToppleUpdate` and `isAbleToBeToppled()`. There is **no** name/kind filter in the blast. Retail blasts 1–6 all have `ToppleSpeed` 0.35–0.5.

## Rust
**Leftover** `neutron_missile_slow_death_update.rs:437-449` finds `ToppleUpdate` on each candidate — matches C++.

**Live** `world_scripts/special_power_strikes.rs:642-662` only topples when `template_name` contains `tree`/`shrub` **or** `is_topple_capable_template` (tree/shrub/bush/palm/pine/oak/birch/lightpole/streetlight/sign/fence). Vehicles, crates, and other `ToppleUpdate` props in the ring stay upright. `plan_neutron_frame` still records `topple_speed` for every hit.

## Evidence
C++ `NeutronMissileSlowDeathUpdate.cpp:313-315` + `Object.cpp:1171-1184`. Leftover `behavior/neutron_missile_slow_death_update.rs:437-449`. Live apply `special_power_strikes.rs:642-662` + `host_topple.rs:150-163`. Retail table `host_neutron_missile_slow_death.rs:67-135` (Blast1–6 topple speeds).

## Player-visible
A nuke shockwave only knocks over name-peeled trees/signs. Retail topples every ToppleUpdate object in each expanding ring (including other props that have the module).

## Acceptance
- [ ] Live blast topple attempts every in-radius object
- [ ] Actual fall still gated only by ToppleUpdate + isAbleToBeToppled (C++ Object::topple)
- [ ] NO_BOUNCE|NO_FX options preserved
close_reason: live topple any ToppleUpdate/isAbleToBeToppled; leftover already matched

title: [Dock] Repair/WarFactory never sends units to rally after dock
description:
## C++
`DockUpdate::isRallyPointAfterDockType` defaults FALSE (`DockUpdate.h:104`).
`RepairDockUpdate` overrides it to TRUE (`RepairDockUpdate.h:47`).
After `AI_DOCK_MOVE_TO_EXIT`, `AIDockMachine` enters `AI_DOCK_MOVE_TO_RALLY` (`AIDock.cpp:35-36`).
`AIDockMoveToRallyState::onEnter` (`:749-765`) issues `aiMoveToPosition` to the building `ExitInterface::getRallyPoint()` when the dock is a rally-after-dock type and a rally exists. Supply-center docks keep the default FALSE so collectors do not peel to rally.

## Rust
Live crate `RepairDockUpdate::is_rally_point_after_dock_type` returns true (`production/dock_update.rs:1205-1206`). Leftover `AIDockMoveToRallyState` (`ai/dock.rs:1404-1435`) implements the C++ gate.
Live host never runs that machine. After SeekingRepair full heal, `support_states.rs:2132-2133` only `set_target(None)` — no rally command. Host residual documents `REPAIR_DOCK_RALLY_AFTER_DOCK_RESIDUAL = true` (`host_dock_contain_exit_heal_residual.rs:112-113`) but does not issue the move.

## Evidence
C++ `RepairDockUpdate.h:47` + `AIDock.cpp:749-765`.
Live crate returns true but host `support_states.rs` SeekingRepair completion clears the target.
Not the closed TimeForFullHeal beads (hq-4ksp / hq-ezp4v) and not factory ground-click SetRallyPoint (hq-7lbg).

## Player-visible
A Humvee or Overlord that finishes repair at a WarFactory / RepairPad sits on the pad instead of rolling to the factory rally point. The next vehicle then piles onto the same pad instead of the first one clearing to rally.
close_reason: host support_states.rs: after SeekingRepair full heal, RepairPad/WarFactory issue path_approach_with_state to building_data.rally_point (C++ RepairDockUpdate isRallyPointAfterDockType + AIDockMoveToRallyState). Supply/heal pads stay false.

title: [Dock] Leftover DockUpdate is invented service-time queue, not C++ approach/bone machine
description:
## C++
`DockUpdate.cpp` is the shared dock machine (everything except `action()`).
Ctor (`:42-81`) sizes `m_approachPositions` / owners / reached from INI `NumberApproachPositions` (or `DEFAULT_APPROACH_VECTOR_SIZE=10` when `DYNAMIC_APPROACH_VECTOR_FLAG=-1`).
`isClearToApproach` / `reserveApproachPosition` / `advanceApproachPosition` / `isClearToEnter` (`dockerID == m_activeDocker`) / `isClearToAdvance` manage a single-file approach line.
`loadDockPositions` (`:467-509`) reads pristine `DockStart` / `DockAction` / `DockEnd` / `DockWaiting` bones unless `KINDOF_IGNORE_DOCKING_BONES`.
`getEnterPosition` / `getDockPosition` / `getExitPosition` convert those bones to world (airborne enter falls back to building pos).
`onEnterReached` / `onDockReached` / `onExitReached` / `cancelDock` set/clear `MODELCONDITION_DOCKING*` on dock and docker.
`update()` (`:391-419`) promotes the first reached approach owner to `m_activeDocker` unless `m_dockCrippled`; supply-source workers drop `MODELCONDITION_MOVING` while `DOCKING_BEGINNING`.
`xfer` v1 persists enter/dock/exit, approach vectors, owners, reached, `m_activeDocker`, `m_dockerInside`, `m_dockCrippled`, `m_dockOpen`.

## Rust
Leftover `object/behavior/dock_update.rs` (re-exported by leftover `object/update/dock_update/dock_update.rs`) is an invented `VecDeque` service-time queue:
- INI fields are `num_docks` / `service_time` / `allow_multiple_docks` / 2D relative points — not `NumberApproachPositions` / `AllowsPassthrough`.
- `request_dock` sorts by invented priority; `update_approaching` instantly marks `Docked`; `perform_service` is a no-op.
- No approach-slot reservation, no `activeDocker` / `isClearToEnter`, no bone load, no `MODELCONDITION_DOCKING*`, no crippled enter gate, no `findPositionAround`.
- `xfer` writes invented queue length/state/priority, not C++ v1.

Live factory (`contain_module_overrides`) uses `object/production/dock_update.rs` instead.

## Evidence
Leftover `DockUpdateModuleData` (`behavior/dock_update.rs:112-134`) vs C++ `DockUpdateModuleData::buildFieldParse` (`DockUpdate.cpp:25-39`).
Leftover `update_approaching` (`:285-300`) vs C++ `reserveApproachPosition` + `onApproachReached` + `update()` promotion.
Leftover `Snapshotable::xfer` (`:429+`) vs C++ `DockUpdate::xfer` (`:532-601`).
Pattern matches leftover invented modules already filed this wave (e.g. leftover LaserUpdate invented DPS).

## Player-visible
Any leftover DockUpdate path never queues units at DockWaiting bones, never drives DockStart/Action/End, never plays docking animations, and cannot load C++ dock snapshots. Collectors and repair vehicles pop through a fake service timer instead of the authored dock line.
close_reason: leftover object/behavior/dock_update.rs rewritten from invented VecDeque service-time queue to C++ DockUpdate approach/bone machine: NumberApproachPositions, reserve/advance/isClearToEnter, activeDocker promotion, Dock* bones, MODELCONDITION_DOCKING*, xfer v1.

title: [Upgrade] Leftover remove_upgrade skips resetUpgrade so RemovesUpgrades cannot re-arm
description:
## C++
`UpgradeMux::resetUpgrade` (`UpgradeModule.cpp:191-201`) if `keyMask` intersects the module's activation mask **and** `m_upgradeExecuted`, sets `m_upgradeExecuted = false` and returns true. It does **not** undo `upgradeImplementation` effects.

`Object::removeUpgrade` (`Object.cpp:4491-4503`) clears the object completed bit then calls `resetUpgrade` on every upgrade module. `UpgradeMuxData::muxDataProcessUpgradeRemoval` looks up each `RemovesUpgrades` name and `obj->removeUpgrade(template)` so mutually exclusive payloads (bomb-truck HE vs bio, etc.) can re-arm.

## Rust
Leftover live `object/upgrade/*` modules implement `remove_upgrade` as a no-op (or a comment that C++ does not revert effects). None call `UpgradeMux::reset_upgrade` / clear `applied`.

`Object::remove_upgrade_mask` (`object_upgrade.rs:482-507`) clears the object bit then `upgrade.into_interface().remove_upgrade(mask)` — that leftover interface method is not `resetUpgrade`.

`mux_give_self_upgrade` (`upgrade_module.rs:28-31`) does run leftover `process_upgrade_removal` → `remove_upgrade_mask`, so RemovesUpgrades **does** strip the object bit, but the previous module stays `applied`/`upgrade_executed` and will never `would_upgrade` again.

Live `upgrade/modules/upgrade_mux.rs:309-319` has a correct `reset_upgrade`, but leftover `object/upgrade/*` (the factory-wired modules `apply_upgrade_modules` walks) do not use it.

## Evidence
C++ `UpgradeModule.cpp:191-201`; `Object.cpp:4491-4503`.
Rust leftover `object/upgrade/subobjects_upgrade.rs:403-405`, `weapon_set_upgrade.rs:159-161`, `stealth_upgrade.rs:205-207`, etc.; `object_upgrade.rs:482-507`; `upgrade_module.rs:28-31`.

## Player-visible
Switching exclusive object upgrades (bomb-truck bio ↔ HE, Helix payload swaps) never re-arms the removed module. Re-researching or re-granting the first payload is a no-op; both visuals/effects can stick or the first one can never return.
close_reason: C++ Object::removeUpgrade + UpgradeMux::resetUpgrade. Leftover object/upgrade/* remove_upgrade now calls mux_reset_upgrade / mux.reset_upgrade to clear applied/executed so RemovesUpgrades can re-arm. Effects are not undone.

title: [Upgrade] Live UpgradeCenter::init never creates Upgrade_Veterancy_* templates
description:
## C++
`UpgradeCenter::init` (`Upgrade.cpp:236-254`) always creates three OBJECT-type templates via `friend_makeVeterancyUpgrade`: `Upgrade_Veterancy_VETERAN`, `Upgrade_Veterancy_ELITE`, `Upgrade_Veterancy_HEROIC` (names from `TheVeterancyNames`). They receive sequential mask bits from `newUpgrade` **before** Upgrade.ini is parsed.

`Object::onVeterancyLevelChanged` (`Object.cpp:3064-3070`) then `findVeterancyUpgrade(newLevel)` and `giveUpgrade(up)`, which ORs that object mask and re-runs `updateUpgradeModules`. Any UpgradeMux `TriggeredBy` those names (and object-completed-mask queries) depend on those templates existing.

Leftover Common `parseUpgradeDefinition` is the only INI entry; there is one `TheUpgradeCenter`.

## Rust
Live `THE_UPGRADE_CENTER` is `Lazy::new(UpgradeCenter::new)` (`upgrade/center.rs:20-21`). `UpgradeCenter::init` (`:47-54`) that creates the three veterancy rows is only called from the unit-test helper (`:285-286`). `load_upgrade_templates` (`ini_template_loader.rs:430-490`) and `register_upgrade_template` never call `init`.

Leftover Common boot (`shell.rs:1512-1523`) calls `ini_upgrade::initialize_upgrade_center()` which is `UpgradeCenter::new()` with **no** veterancy rows (`ini_upgrade.rs:500-503`). Leftover `UpgradeCenter::parse_upgrade_definition` (`:483-486`) is a `println!` stub.

`Object::on_veterancy_level_changed` (`object_combat.rs:394-406`) does `find_veterancy_upgrade("VETERAN"|"ELITE"|"HEROIC")` then `give_upgrade`. That lookup is always `None` on live boot.

## Evidence
C++ `Upgrade.cpp:246-253` init; `Object.cpp:3068-3070` giveUpgrade.
Rust `upgrade/center.rs:20-21,47-54,145-147`; `ini_template_loader.rs:430-490`; `shell.rs:1512-1523`; `ini_upgrade.rs:483-486,500-503`; `object_combat.rs:394-406`.

## Player-visible
Promoted units never receive `Upgrade_Veterancy_*` object bits. Mux modules TriggeredBy those names stay inert. Object completed-upgrade mask / save / script checks miss the retail veterancy upgrade flags (weapon-set VETERAN/ELITE/HERO bits are a separate path).
close_reason: C++ UpgradeCenter::init creates Upgrade_Veterancy_VETERAN/ELITE/HEROIC OBJECT templates before Upgrade.ini. Live THE_UPGRADE_CENTER Lazy and load_upgrade_templates call init; leftover Common initialize_upgrade_center does the same with sequential mask bits.

title: [RadiusDecal] Host delivery uses hardcoded RGB not Color==0 player color
description:
## C++
`createRadiusDecal` (`RadiusDecal.cpp:65`): `setColor(m_color == 0 ? owningPlayer->getPlayerColor() : m_color)`. Template default `m_color = 0`. Host residual comments for SUPERWEAPON_ScudStorm list Texture / OpacityMin/Max / Throb / OnlyVisibleToOwningPlayer and do **not** list a Color key, so retail Color stays 0 → player color.

## Rust
`HostRadiusDecalTemplate::scud_storm` hardcodes `color_rgb: [33, 255, 67]`; `nuclear_missile` hardcodes `[255, 0, 0]` (`host_radius_decal_update.rs:57-78`). `enqueue_delivery_decal` always uses that RGB (`radius_decal.rs:197-200`). No player-color fallback. Particle-cannon / Spectre host names also fall through `default_delivery_decal_template_for_host` to the scud peel (`host_radius_decal_update.rs:290-301`).

## Evidence
C++: `m_color == 0 ? owningPlayer->getPlayerColor() : m_color`.
Rust: `handle.set_color(((r as u32)<<16)|((g as u32)<<8)|b)` from the peel.

## Player-visible
Every Scud delivery ring is the same neon green and every nuke ring the same red, ignoring custom MP player colors. Particle Cannon / Spectre host peels also draw the GLA Scud texture/color.
close_reason: host templates color=0 player color via ThePlayerList GameMakeColor

title: [RadiusDecal] Host delivery update ignores getDrawIconUI
description:
## C++
`RadiusDecal::update` (`RadiusDecal.cpp:180-188`): if `!TheGameLogic->getDrawIconUI()` then `setOpacity(0)` ("Scripts turned this off, so don't show them!"). Campaign `OPTIONS_SET_DRAWICON_UI_MODE` hides radius decals with the rest of icon chrome.

## Rust
Live GameClient `RadiusDecal::update` (`radius_decal.rs:496-503`) honors `TheGameLogic::get_draw_icon_ui()`. Leftover GameLogic `RadiusDecal::update` (`update_context.rs:348-351`) does too. Live **host** `HostRadiusDecal::update` (`host_radius_decal_update.rs:170-189`) always writes the throb opacity onto the ShadowHandle. No DrawIconUI test.

## Evidence
C++: `if (TheGameLogic->getDrawIconUI()) { opac = ... } else { opac = 0; }`.
Rust host: `handle.set_opacity((self.opacity.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 255.0).trunc() as i32)` with no gate.

close_reason: host HostRadiusDecal::update get_draw_icon_ui opacity 0

title: [RadiusDecal] Host delivery throb is triangle/birth-phase not C++ sine of global frame
description:
## C++
`RadiusDecal::update` (`RadiusDecal.cpp:172-190`):
`theta = 2*PI * (now % throbTime) / throbTime`, `percent = 0.5 * (Sin(theta) + 1)`, then lerp min..max. `now` is `TheGameLogic->getFrame()` (global phase). All live decals pulse in lockstep.

## Rust
Live GameClient `RadiusDecal::update` (`radius_decal.rs:483-504`) matches the sine. Live **host** delivery path does not: `HostRadiusDecal::update` (`host_radius_decal_update.rs:170-189`) uses a triangle wave over `2 * throb_frames` from `birth_frame` (`phase <= period` rise, else fall). Each strike starts at OpacityMin independently.

## Evidence
C++: `Sin(theta)` of `now % m_opacityThrobTime`.
Rust host: `t = phase/period` then `2 - phase/period`; `opacity = min + (max-min)*t`.

## Player-visible
Scud / nuke / other host delivery rings fade linearly in and out, out of phase with each other and with radius-cursor rings, instead of the retail sine pulse.
close_reason: host update sine of global frame not triangle birth

title: [RadiusDecal] Host delivery create ignores OnlyVisibleToOwningPlayer
description:
## C++
`createRadiusDecal` (`RadiusDecal.cpp:47-73`) sets `result.m_empty = false` first (net-sync: `isEmpty()` is independent of visibility), then only `addDecal` when `!m_onlyVisibleToOwningPlayer || ownerIndex == localPlayerIndex`. Default `m_onlyVisibleToOwningPlayer = true` (`RadiusDecal.cpp:28`).

## Rust
Live GameClient `create_radius_decal` (`radius_decal.rs:291-336`) matches that gate. Live **host** `HostRadiusDecal::create` (`host_radius_decal_update.rs:139-167`) always `enqueue_delivery_decal` when `tmpl.valid()`. `only_visible_to_owner` is stored on `HostRadiusDecalTemplate` (scud/nuke peels set it true) and never read.

## Evidence
C++: `if (!m_onlyVisibleToOwningPlayer || owningPlayer->getPlayerIndex() == ThePlayerList->getLocalPlayer()->getPlayerIndex())`.
Rust host: no owner/local compare; `enqueue_delivery_decal` is unconditional.

## Player-visible
In multiplayer, replay, or observer view, enemy Scud/nuke delivery rings appear for everyone. Retail only the owning player sees them.
close_reason: host create empty=false then addDecal only if !OnlyVisible||owner==local

title: [RadiusDecal] Live radius-cursor templates skip parse so rings never throb
description:
## C++
`InGameUI::s_fieldParseTable` (`InGameUI.cpp:820-853`) parses each `*RadiusCursor` block through `RadiusDecalTemplate::parseRadiusDecalTemplate` (`RadiusDecal.cpp:94-109`): Texture, Style, OpacityMin/Max (percent), OpacityThrobTime (duration), Color (`parseColorInt` `R:G:B:[A:]`), OnlyVisibleToOwningPlayer. Retail blocks set OpacityMin/Max so `RadiusDecal::update` sine-throbs (`RadiusDecal.cpp:172-190`).

## Rust
`radius_cursor_templates_from_ini` (`radius_cursor_ini.rs:80-123`) only `RadiusDecalTemplate::with_texture(authored)`. Defaults stay `min_opacity=1.0`, `max_opacity=1.0`, `opacity_throb_time=LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND`, `color=0`. `parse_radius_decal_template` exists on live `radius_decal.rs` but has **zero callers**. Its `parse_color` is `token.parse::<u32>()` (`radius_decal.rs:396-403`), not `parseColorInt`. Common `ini_in_game_ui.rs` still has no `*RadiusCursor` keys (hq-38as only fixed authored textures).

## Evidence
C++ field table Texture/Style/OpacityMin/OpacityMax/OpacityThrobTime/Color/OnlyVisibleToOwningPlayer.
Rust: `templates.push(RadiusDecalTemplate::with_texture(texture))`.
`handle_radius_cursor` does call `cur_radius_decal.update()`, but min==max so the sine is a constant 1.0.

## Player-visible
Targeting rings sit at solid full opacity. Retail rings pulse between authored OpacityMin/Max (typically 25–50%).
close_reason: parse_color parseColorInt ARGB; radius_cursor_ini from_radius_cursor_texture parse throb

title: [SpecialPower] Live pauseCountdown is a set; unpause of ready restarts reload
description:
## C++
`SpecialPowerModule::pauseCountdown` (`SpecialPowerModule.cpp:728-752`) is a **refcount**:
- First pause (`m_pausedCount == 0`) snapshots `m_pausedOnFrame` and `m_pausedPercent = getPercentReady()`.
- Nested pauses only increment the count.
- Unpause decrements only while `m_pausedCount > 0`. Final unpause (`count == 0`) does `m_availableOnFrame += (now - m_pausedOnFrame)`.

A power that was **ready** when paused (`availableOnFrame <= now`) therefore stays ready after unpause (`available` slides to now). Two pause sources (StartsPaused + script stop, or StartsPaused + EMP `pauseAllSpecialPowers`) need two unpauses.

## Rust
Leftover `pause_countdown` (`special_power_module.rs:875-896`) matches the C++ refcount.

Live `Object::pause_special_power_countdown` (`object/orders.rs:88-117`) is a `HashSet`:
- Pause = insert. Two pause() calls collapse to one flag.
- Unpause = remove, then if remaining cooldown `<= 0` **insert a full reload** (`special_power_reload_seconds`, or **1.0s** when ReloadTime is 0: "StartsPaused peels without ReloadTime residual default to 1s").

`script_pause_special_power_countdown` and `UnpauseSpecialPowerUpgrade` both use this helper.

## Evidence
- C++ `SpecialPowerModule.cpp:728-752`.
- Leftover refcount: `special_power_module.rs:875-896`.
- Live set + restart: `orders.rs:88-117`.
- Callers: `object_queries.rs:1413-1496` (scripts), `object_queries.rs:2156-2171` (upgrade unpause), `production_eva.rs:1114-1115` (StartsPaused).
- Closed hq-srjay (script reach) / hq-nbwn (ctor StartsPaused) / hq-7cf8 (INI flags) do not cover this pause math.

## Player-visible
`NAMED_START` after `NAMED_STOP` on a ready Radar Scan / Helix napalm / Lotus capture (ReloadTime 0) starts a new 1s–full cooldown instead of staying ready. StartsPaused + a script stop: researching Capture (one unpause) clears both pauses, so the unit can capture while the script still wanted it stopped.
close_reason: special_power_paused is HashMap refcount; final unpause of ready does not insert reload

title: [CommandSet] getCommandButton leftover ignores GameLogic control-bar slot overrides
description:
## C++
`CommandSet::getCommandButton` (`ControlBar.cpp:810-818`) is the single lookup used by populate, multi-select, BuildAssistant, `canProduceUpgrade`, CommandXlat, and AIGroup:

```
if (TheGameLogic && TheGameLogic->findControlBarOverride(m_name, i, button))
    return button;  // may be NULL (script-removed slot)
return m_command[i];
```

Scripts `doRemoveCommandBarButton` / `doAddCommandBarButton` (`ScriptActions.cpp:6253-6301`) write `GameLogic::setControlBarOverride(templ->friend_getCommandSetString(), slot, button|NULL)`. Key is `'0'+slot` + command-set name (`GameLogic.cpp:4389-4413`). Overrides are not baked into the CommandSet object.

## Rust
Leftover `CommandSet::get_command_button` (`command_button.rs:128-133`) returns `self.buttons[index]` only. It never calls `GameLogic::find_control_bar_override` (`impl_save.rs:73-81`), which does exist and uses the same `'0'+slot` key (`xfer_helpers.rs:81-87`).

Leftover script actions (`actions_world.rs:1241-1310`) mutate the **ControlBarBridge snapshot** via `set_command_set_slot_override` (and also write the GameLogic map). Live GameClient `impl_buttons.rs:68-69` reads `command_set.buttons.get(slot)` — the snapshot — not `get_command_button`. A later `refresh_control_bar_bridge_from_common()` (shell load + GameLogic reset) rebuilds the snapshot from leftover INI and **drops** script slot overrides. Leftover AIGroup / canProduceUpgrade / CommandButtonHunt still use `get_command_button` and never see the GameLogic map.

## Evidence
- C++ lookup: `ControlBar.cpp:814-817`.
- Leftover lookup: `command_button.rs:128-133` no override consult.
- Leftover map is written (`control_bar.rs:387-388`) but unread by `get_command_button`.
- Bridge refresh: `control_bar.rs:56-101` copies leftover INI slots only.

## Player-visible
Campaign/skirmish scripts that add or remove a command-bar button (tutorial lockouts, mission-granted buttons) either fail after a ControlBar refresh or never affect leftover production/AI/hunt paths. Script-nulled slots still fire as the original CommandSet button.
close_reason: leftover command_button.rs CommandSet::get_command_button consults GameLogic::findControlBarOverride (script-removed slot returns None; replaced slot matches by name).

title: [Score] finishSinglePlayerInit never frees InGameUI message resources
description:
## C++
`finishSinglePlayerInit` (`ScoreScreen.cpp:908-916`) always calls `TheInGameUI->freeMessageResources()` before destroying `Menus/BlankWindow.wnd`. Comment: fix for black-screen text that appears after the loading sequence.

`initSinglePlayer` (`:739-743`) also `winClearStatus(WIN_STATUS_IMAGE)` on the blank window's first child so the overlay is a clean cover.

## Rust
`finalize_single_player_init` (`score_screen.rs:494-517`) destroys `blank_layout` and shows Ok/Continue. It never calls `InGameUI::free_message_resources` (or equivalent). `init_single_player` (`:388-392`) creates BlankWindow but does not clear `WIN_STATUS_IMAGE`.

## Evidence
C++ `ScoreScreen.cpp:739-743,908-916` vs Rust `score_screen.rs:388-392,494-517`.

## Player-visible
Campaign score screen can keep the last military-subtitle / UI messages (and blank-window image bits) over the results layout — the black-screen text C++ explicitly cleared.
close_reason: finalize_single_player_init calls TheInGameUI::free_message_resources; init_single_player clears blank WIN_STATUS_IMAGE

title: [Score] Score-screen music uses PlayerList template, not GameInfo slot
description:
## C++
`ScoreScreenUpdate` (`ScoreScreen.cpp:406-428`) plays music after `clearGameData` wiped PlayerList. It reads `TheGameInfo->getSlot(localSlotNum)->getPlayerTemplate()`, or `FactionObserver` if the slot template is < 0, then `PlayerTemplate::getScoreScreenMusic()` with fade.

Comment at `:406-408`: GameLogic::clearGameData runs after Init and before the first Update, so music was moved here and must not touch PlayerList.

## Rust
`update_score_screen_music` (`score_screen.rs:188-221`) reads `ThePlayerList` local player's template `get_score_screen_music()`. No `TheGameInfo` slot lookup, no `FactionObserver` fallback.

If the host consumes `MSG_CLEAR_GAME_DATA` (`host_consume_clear_game_data`) before the first ScoreScreen update, PlayerList is empty and music never starts. Observer slots with template < 0 also miss the FactionObserver track.

## Evidence
C++ `ScoreScreen.cpp:409-428` vs Rust `score_screen.rs:199-212`.

## Player-visible
End-of-match score screen is silent (or plays the wrong side track for observers) instead of the faction ScoreScreenMusic.
close_reason: score-screen music reads GameInfo local slot template or FactionObserver, never PlayerList after clearGameData

title: [Score] grabMultiPlayerInfo lists every non-neutral player and skips MutiPlayer backdrop
description:
## C++
`grabMultiPlayerInfo` (`ScoreScreen.cpp:2008-2060`):
- Sets parent image `MutiPlayer_ScoreScreen` and `WIN_STATUS_IMAGE` (`:2025-2030`).
- Looks up only `player0`..`player{MAX_SLOTS-1}` via `findPlayerWithNameKey` (`:2034-2046`).
- Sorts those slot players by `calculateScore()`.

Civilian / script / extra sides are not named `playerN` and do not appear.

`grab_multi_player_info` (`score_screen.rs:796-823`) iterates `PlayerList` and keeps every `PlayerType != Neutral`. No `MutiPlayer_ScoreScreen` image / `WIN_STATUS_IMAGE`. Sort uses leftover `get_total_score()`.
