title: [EMP] Live EMPUpdate sparks skip setSystemLifetime and setInitialDelay
description:
## C++
`EMPUpdate::doDisableAttack` (`EMPUpdate.cpp:277-314`) for each victim drawable creates `m_disableFXParticleSystem` (retail EMPSparks) `MAX(15, ceil(sparksPerCubicFoot * footprintArea * min(height,10)))` times, then:
- `sys->setSystemLifetime(MAX(0, DisabledDuration - 30))`
- `sys->setInitialDelay(GameLogicRandomValue(1,100))`
Volume uses `getFootprintArea()` + `makeRandomOffsetWithinFootprint` + integer `GameLogicRandomValue(3, victimHeight)`.

## Rust
Live `do_disable_attack` (`emp_update.rs:453-496`) creates/attaches/positions systems but never sets lifetime or initial delay. `TheParticleSystemManager` helper (`helpers/particles.rs`) has no `set_system_lifetime` / `set_initial_delay` wrappers. Footprint area is AABB `(max.x-min.x)*(max.y-min.y)` not `getFootprintArea()` (πr² cylinder / 4·major·minor box); XY offset is AABB min/max not rejection-sampled circle.

Leftover `apply_emp_pulse_at` never spawns EMPSparks at all (generic `WeaponImpact` only) — particle leftover already hunted; this bead is the live EMPUpdate path that does spawn sparks.

## Evidence
- C++: `setSystemLifetime(MAX(0, data->m_disabledDuration - 30)); setInitialDelay(GameLogicRandomValue(1,100));`
- Live: `create_particle_system` + `attach_particle_system_to_object` + `set_particle_system_position` only.
- Helper API ends at attach/position/destroy; no lifetime/delay.

## Player-visible
On a live EMPUpdate spheroid, EMPSparks on disabled tanks persist for the template default (or forever) instead of ~DisabledDuration−30 frames, and all emitters start together instead of staggering over 1–100 frames. Spark count is also high for cylinder geometry.
close_reason: live emp_update.rs sparks: getFootprintArea + makeRandomOffsetWithinFootprint + GameLogicRandomValue(3,height) z, setSystemLifetime(DisabledDuration-30), setInitialDelay(1..100). Particle helper + client bridge wrappers added.

title: [EMP] Leftover EMP Pulse spheroid never scales or tints
description:
## C++
`EMPUpdate::update` (`EMPUpdate.cpp:120-134`) every frame: lerp `m_currentScale` toward random TargetScaleMin/Max (`* 0.05`), `drawable->setInstanceScale`, saturate StartColor×2 + `colorTint` until `m_tintEnvPlayFrame`, then saturate EndColor×5 + `colorFlash(9999, fadeFrames, TRUE)`. Retail spheroid StartScale 0.01 → 3–4, StartColor (32,64,255).

## Rust
hq-46l3 closed this on **live** `EMPUpdate::update_simple`. Leftover `spawn_emp_pulse_spheroid` (`special_power_flights.rs:284-316`) only sets `emp_pulse_spheroid` + expire frame; `update_emp_pulse_spheroids` only kills the dummy. No instance scale, no colorTint/colorFlash. Host comments: “GPU scale/tint fail-closed.”

## Evidence
- C++: `m_currentScale += (m_targetScale - m_currentScale) * 0.05f; dr->setInstanceScale; colorTint/colorFlash`.
- Leftover spheroid: `ThingTemplate` stub with Immobile + 1 HP; no EMPUpdate module, no drawable scale/tint.
- hq-46l3 close reason is live `emp_update.rs` only.

## Player-visible
China EMP Pulse / Patriot EMP blast has no growing, saturating blue sphere. Players see a generic impact puff (or nothing) instead of the retail EMP bubble.
close_reason: leftover EMPUpdate scale lerp 0.05 + saturate StartColor×2 / EndColor×5 on HostEmpPulseSpheroid; instance scale applied to leftover geometry.radius.

title: [EMP] Leftover EMP Pulse disables instantly; C++ waits StartFadeTime
description:
## C++
`EMPUpdate` ctor (`EMPUpdate.cpp:74-76`) sets `m_tintEnvPlayFrame = now + StartFadeTime` and `m_dieFrame = now + Lifetime`. `update` (`:123-135`) only calls `doDisableAttack()` on the exact frame `now == m_tintEnvPlayFrame`. Retail `EMPPulseEffectSpheroid` StartFadeTime is 300 ms → 9 frames; Lifetime 3000 ms → 90 frames. The sphere grows/tints first, then the disable pops.

## Rust
Leftover `update_emp_pulse_flights` detonates at `pos.y <= 5` and immediately `apply_emp_pulse_at` (`special_power_flights.rs:480-492`). `spawn_emp_pulse_spheroid` is a lifetime-only dummy (`emp_pulse_spheroid_expires_frame`); it never runs `EMPUpdate::update` / StartFadeTime. Live `EMPUpdate::update_simple` does wait for `tint_env_play_frame`, but leftover never constructs that module on the spheroid.

## Evidence
- C++: `if (now == m_tintEnvPlayFrame) { colorFlash(...); doDisableAttack(); }`
- Leftover: bomb Y<=5 → `apply_emp_pulse_at` same frame; spheroid expire is a separate 90-frame kill of the dummy.
- Host constants document StartFadeTime 9f but nothing waits on it.

## Player-visible
China EMP Pulse disables vehicles the instant the bomb hits dirt. C++ waits ~0.3s while the blue sphere grows, then the disable hits.
close_reason: apply_emp_pulse_at only spawns EMPPulseEffectSpheroid; doDisableAttack waits StartFadeTime (9f) via HostEmpPulseRegistry + apply_due_emp_pulse_disables on spheroid/flight/shadow ticks.

title: [EMP] Leftover EMP Pulse uses 2D XZ center radius not FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_3D
description:
## C++
`EMPUpdate::doDisableAttack` (`EMPUpdate.cpp:180-185`) iterates `ThePartitionManager->iterateObjectsInRange(pos, radius, FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_3D)`. Distance is 3D center-to-center minus the victim bounding-sphere radius. Default `EffectRadius` is 200 when INI omits it (`EMPUpdate.h:52`).

## Rust
Leftover `in_emp_pulse_radius_2d` (`host_emp_pulse.rs:157-161`) is ground-plane `dx*dx + dz*dz <= radius*radius` (host XZ). `apply_emp_pulse_at` and Patriot EMP both use that 2D center check with no bounding-sphere subtraction.

Live `EMPUpdate` uses `get_objects_in_range_boundary_3d` (`object_queries.rs:417-452`), which mirrors FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_3D — leftover host never calls it.

## Evidence
- C++: `iterateObjectsInRange(pos, radius, FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_3D)`.
- Leftover: `in_emp_pulse_radius_2d(center, (pos.x, pos.z), HOST_EMP_PULSE_RADIUS)` / Patriot `(dx*dx+dz*dz).sqrt() > radius`.
- Comment on leftover: “2D distance check residual (ground plane x/z; host gameplay convention).”

## Player-visible
A jet 250 world-units up at the same XZ is inside leftover EMP Pulse (2D) but outside C++ 3D radius 200. A large building whose sphere overlaps 200 but whose center is at 205 is hit in C++ and missed leftover.
close_reason: leftover apply_emp_pulse_at/Patriot use in_emp_pulse_radius_from_bounding_sphere_3d (center-to-center minus sphere). Host 2D helper kept for honesty only.

title: [EMP] Leftover EMP skips under-construction buildings C++ still disables
description:
## C++
`EMPUpdate::doDisableAttack` has no under-construction skip. A faction structure with `OBJECT_STATUS_UNDER_CONSTRUCTION` still passes the VEHICLE/STRUCTURE/SPAWNS filter and `isFactionStructure()` and receives `setDisabledUntil(DISABLED_EMP, …)`.

## Rust
Leftover `is_legal_emp_disable_target` (`host_emp_pulse.rs:139-141`) returns false when `under_construction`. `apply_emp_pulse_at` sets that from `obj.status.under_construction || obj.construction_percent + 0.001 < 1.0`. Patriot leftover `is_legal_supw_patriot_emp_target` also rejects `under_construction`.

Live `EMPUpdate::do_disable_attack` does not skip under-construction (matches C++), but leftover is the playable EMP Pulse / Patriot path.

## Evidence
- C++ filter list: own-buildings, kindof VEHICLE/STRUCTURE/SPAWNS, airborne kill, `isFactionStructure`, allies reject. No construction bit.
- Leftover: `if !is_alive || under_construction || is_emp_hardened { return false; }`.

## Player-visible
An incomplete War Factory / Command Center in the EMP blast stays powered and producing. C++ freezes it for the DisabledDuration.
close_reason: is_legal_emp_disable_target and is_legal_supw_patriot_emp_target no longer skip under_construction. C++ EMPUpdate has no construction gate.

title: [Score] Skirmish honor persist skip does not match C++ sandbox/defeat
description:
## C++
`populatePlayerInfo` skirmish local branch (`ScoreScreen.cpp:1566-1576`):

```
if (isSandbox() || !(isLocalAlliedDefeat() || isLocalAlliedVictory())) {
    if (player->isPlayerActive())
        return; // skip persist
}
```

Sandbox or undecided games skip only while the local player is still active. A finished defeat always records a loss, even if the player is still active (watching remaining AI). Sandbox victories are skipped.

## Rust
`populate_player_info` (`score_screen.rs:1256-1262`):

```
if (sandbox || !victory) && player.is_player_active() && !victory {
    return;
}
```

Any non-victory while the player is still active is skipped (including a real allied defeat). Sandbox + victory does not skip, so sandbox wins write honors/streaks.

## Evidence
C++ `ScoreScreen.cpp:1566-1576` vs Rust `score_screen.rs:1256-1262`.

## Player-visible
Losing a skirmish while still alive (allied defeat / timer) does not increment losses or reset win streak. Winning a sandbox skirmish awards wins, streaks, and battle honors C++ never grants.
close_reason: score_screen persist skip is sandbox || !(defeat||victory) then active-only, matching ScoreScreen.cpp:1568-1576

title: [Score] Leftover ScoreKeeper ignores GameLogic isScoringEnabled
description:
## C++
Every ScoreKeeper mutator gates on `TheGameLogic->isScoringEnabled()` (`ScoreKeeper.cpp:101,162,198,231,275`). Campaign scripts `DISABLE_SCORING` / `ENABLE_SCORING` (`ScriptActions.cpp:6792-6796`, `GameLogic.h:166-167`) freeze units built/lost/killed and captures so cinematic/scripted waves do not pollute the score screen.

Money earned/spent is *not* gated (inline `ScoreKeeper.h:114-115`).

## Rust
Live leftover `ScoreKeeper` (`academy_score.rs`) `add_unit_built`, `add_building_built`, `add_object_lost_obj`, `add_object_destroyed_obj`, `add_object_built_obj`, `add_object_captured_obj` never call `TheGameLogic::is_scoring_enabled()`.

`TheGameLogic::set_scoring_enabled` exists (`helpers/game_logic.rs:145-148`) and script actions wire it (`actions_skirmish.rs:882-889`), but the leftover keeper never reads the flag.

Common `ScoreKeeper` has a private `scoring_enabled` field, not the GameLogic flag, and live Player does not use that type.

## Evidence
C++ `ScoreKeeper.cpp:101` vs leftover `academy_score.rs:369-371,512-514,542-605`. Script path: `ScriptActions.cpp:6795-6796` / `actions_skirmish.rs:888-889`.

## Player-visible
Campaign maps that turn scoring off (USA/China/GLA scripted battles, challenge intros) still increment Units/Buildings Built/Lost/Destroyed, so the end-mission scoreboard includes cinematic fodder.
close_reason: leftover ScoreKeeper mutators return unless TheGameLogic::is_scoring_enabled; money earned/spent ungated

title: [Score] Honor KindOf filter compares retail template bits to ScoreKeeper local enum
description:
## C++
`ScoreKeeper::getTotalUnitsBuilt(valid,invalid)` (`ScoreKeeper.cpp:134-145`) walks `m_objectsBuilt` and tests `theTemplate->isKindOfMulti(validMask, invalidMask)` using retail KindOf bits (`KindOf.h`: VEHICLE=9, AIRCRAFT=10).

`updateSkirmishBattleHonors` (`ScoreScreen.cpp:1155-1165`) awards Battle Tank for `VEHICLE` and not `AIRCRAFT` (>=50) and Air Wing for `AIRCRAFT` (>=20).

## Rust
Leftover `get_total_units_built_filtered` (`academy_score.rs:436-485`) loads `template.get_kindof_mask()` (retail/layout bits) then `kindof_matches_multi` tests `1u64 << (ScoreKindOf as u32)` where local `ScoreKindOf::Aircraft = 6`, `Vehicle = 5` (`score_keeper.rs:90-98`).

Bit 6 in retail KindOf is `KINDOF_SHRUBBERY`, not aircraft. Bit 5 is `KINDOF_CAN_CAST_REFLECTIONS`. Even after `objects_built` is filled, Air Wing / Battle Tank never match real planes/tanks.

`Object::get_score_kindof_mask` (`object_thing.rs:352-378`) also never maps `KindOf::Aircraft`.

## Evidence
C++ `ScoreKeeper.cpp:134-145` + `KindOf.h` AIRCRAFT vs `academy_score.rs:461-485` + `common/rts/score_keeper.rs:90-98`.

## Player-visible
Air Wing and Battle Tank medals stay locked (or, if the factory lookup fails, the fallback `units_built` awards them for any 20/50 units).
close_reason: academy_score get_total_units_built_filtered uses retail KindOf bits (VEHICLE=9 AIRCRAFT=10) not ScoreKindOf discriminants

title: [Stealth] Listening Outpost stays cloaked while Tank Hunters fire
description:
## C++

Retail China Listening Outpost `StealthForbiddenConditions = MOVING RIDERS_ATTACKING`, `PassengersAllowedToFire = Yes`, InitialPayload TankHunter x2.

## Rust
Leftover `object/behavior/stealth_update.rs:636-639` `has_riders_attacking` fail-closes to false when `OBJECT_REGISTRY` is empty (playable host). Host `listening_outpost_stealth_desired` (`host_listening_outpost.rs:301-316`) only tests MOVING; comment: "RIDERS_ATTACKING not modeled (passengers may fire while cloaked)". Host tick `stealth_mines.rs:185-205` uses that helper. Live crate `allowed_to_stealth_runtime` (`stealth_update.rs:1218-1239`) ports the C++ gate but dual-world empty no-ops.

## Player-visible
Tank Hunters (or any firing passenger) can shoot from a cloaked Listening Outpost. Retail uncloaks the outpost the frame a rider attacks.
close_reason: LO destalth on riders attacking: leftover behavior has_riders_attacking + is_passenger_allowed_to_fire; host listening_outpost_stealth_desired + stealth_mines tick

title: [Stealth] Leftover contained-in-transport check is a no-op so cloak survives Humvee/Chinook
description:
## C++
`allowedToStealth` (`StealthUpdate.cpp:365-373`): if `getContainedBy()` and contain is not garrisonable, return FALSE (transports destalth occupants). `StealthUpdate.h:103` `getDisabledTypesToProcess = DISABLED_HELD` so the module still ticks while held.

## Rust
Leftover `object/update/stealth_update.rs:501-505` sees `container_id` and does nothing ("rely on status bits"). Leftover `Module` impl has no `get_disabled_types_to_process` (default empty). Leftover behavior `receive_grant` / `allowed_to_stealth` never inspect garrisonable. Playable host `update_stealth_and_detection` has no contained-by destalth. Live crate `allowed_to_stealth_runtime` (`:1200-1215`) ports the C++ gate but dual-world empty no-ops; live `StealthUpdateModule` also omits `DISABLED_HELD`.

A stealthed Pathfinder, Rebel, or hero loaded into a Humvee/Chinook stays cloaked inside and can exit already stealthed. Retail destalths on enter (non-garrison container) and starts StealthDelay.

title: [Stealth] Leftover FIRING_PRIMARY collapse destalths Burton knife and any fire
description:
## C++
`allowedToStealth` (`StealthUpdate.cpp:323-363`): if only some of `STEALTH_NOT_WHILE_FIRING_*` are set, destalth only when that slot's `weapon->getLastShotFrame() >= now-1`. Burton INI is `FIRING_PRIMARY` only — secondary knife does not destalth. Sentry is `FIRING_PRIMARY MOVING`.

## Rust
Leftover `object/update/stealth_update.rs:492-498` if any firing bit is set and `IS_FIRING_WEAPON`, `return false` ("For now, simple check") — no per-slot last-shot. Playable host `stealth_mines.rs:542-550` passes `status.attacking || Attack/AttackMove/AttackingGround` into `burton_stealth_desired(..., firing)` even though `BURTON_STEALTH_BREAKS_ON_KNIFE = false`. Live crate (`stealth_update.rs:1164-1197`) has the per-slot last-shot path but is not the host tick.

## Player-visible
Burton knife-kills destalth him. Retail stays cloaked on secondary knife and only uncloaks on primary rifle fire.

title: [Stealth] Leftover temp grant ignores CMD_FROM_PLAYER so stash stealth is an exploit
description:
## C++
`StealthUpdate::update` (`StealthUpdate.cpp:696-714`): while `m_framesGranted > 0`, decrement; if `ai->getLastCommandSource() == CMD_FROM_PLAYER`, `receiveGrant(FALSE)` immediately (comment: "No exploits"). Timer expiry also `receiveGrant(FALSE)`. `receiveGrant` (`:178-214`) always applies when `active` (sets `CAN_STEALTH|STEALTHED`, `m_framesGranted = frames`) even if already enabled. GPS uses `frames=0` (forever, not stripped). GLA Supply Stash `GrantTemporaryStealth = 20000`ms → 600 frames on units without innate `CAN_STEALTH`.

## Rust
Leftover `object/update/stealth_update.rs:916-932` decrements `frames_granted` then explicitly stubs the player-command check (`"rely on frames_granted timer for now"` / `drop(ai.lock())`). Leftover `receive_grant` (`:326`) only arms when `active && !self.enabled`, so a refresh while already enabled never resets the timer. Live crate `stealth_update.rs:416-430` does implement `CommandSourceType::FromPlayer`. Playable host `apply_grant_stealth` (`object/stealth.rs:271-279`) has no frames; `expire_temporary_stealth_grant` (`support_states.rs:4859-4873`) only breaks when `frame >= temporary_stealth_expires_frame`.

## Evidence
C++ `StealthUpdate.cpp:700-708`. Leftover `object/update/stealth_update.rs:920-928`. Host `support_states.rs:4859-4873` + `4956-4958`. Live crate path is not the host tick.

## Player-visible
A GLA worker/truck that unloads at a stealthed Supply Stash stays cloaked for the full 20s even after the player right-clicks move/attack. Retail destalths on the first player order.
close_reason: CMD_FROM_PLAYER strips temp grant in leftover update+behavior; receive_grant always applies when active; host expire_temporary_stealth_grant on move/attack

title: [Recorder] MSG_SET_REPLAY_CAMERA written with 7 args not C++ loc/angle/pitch/zoom/cursor/pixel
description:
## C++
`LookAtXlat.cpp:463-469` records `MSG_SET_REPLAY_CAMERA` with **six** arguments: `location`, `angle`, `pitch`, `zoom`, `MouseCursor` int, `ICoord2D` pixel. `GameLogicDispatch.cpp:1807-1821` reads those six on playback (pose + cursor/mouse restore when the mouse has not moved recently).

## Rust
Leftover emit (`look_at_xlat.rs:252-261`) and live `tap_replay_camera` (`record_tap.rs:180-189`) both:
1. pack `GameMessageType::SetReplayCamera(coord, angle, zoom)` — **pitch dropped**, angle stored in the pitch slot;
2. append only `loc, angle, pitch, zoom` — **cursor + pixel missing**.

`Recorder::write_to_file` (`recorder.rs:1553-1556`) then concatenates `encode_message_arguments` (`loc, pitch=angle, zoom`) **plus** the explicit args, writing **seven** values. Playback decode consumes the encode layout, so camera pose/cursor never match C++.

## Evidence
C++ arg 1 is yaw/angle, arg 2 pitch, arg 4 cursor, arg 5 mouse pixel. Rust file stream is `loc, angle, zoom, loc, angle, pitch, zoom`. hq-j3ufr closed "never recorded"; this is the leftover argument layout.

## Player-visible
Replay camera jumps to the wrong angle/pitch/zoom and never restores the recorded cursor or mouse position, even with `useCameraInReplay`.
close_reason: leftover write_to_file set_replay_camera_file_args + live tap_replay_camera emit loc/angle/pitch/zoom/cursor/pixel: C++ LookAtXlat 6-arg MSG_SET_REPLAY_CAMERA

title: [Recorder] cleanUpReplayFile deletes the .rep instead of preserving it
description:
## C++
`RecorderClass::cleanUpReplayFile` (`Recorder.cpp:265-330`) is DEBUG/INTERNAL + `m_saveStats` only: it **copies** the `.rep` (and a tail of the debug log) into `m_baseStatsDir`. It never deletes the original. `stopRecording` (`:681-687`) calls it only when `TheNetwork && m_wasDesync`. `m_wasDesync` is set only inside that same DEBUG `logCRCMismatch` stats block (`:169-172`). `GameEngine::execute` (`GameEngine.cpp:827-828`) also copies on crash if mode is RECORD and `isMultiplayer()`.

## Rust
`Recorder::log_crc_mismatch` (`recorder.rs:2136`) **always** sets `was_desync = true` (retail too). `stop_recording` (`:1526-1528`) then always calls `cleanup_replay_file`, which `std::fs::remove_file`s the replay (`:2188`). Live `GameEngine` has no crash-copy path.

## Evidence
C++ `CopyFile(oldFname, fname, TRUE)` vs leftover `remove_file`. Comment in leftover still says "copies the replay to a stats directory".

## Player-visible
If a desync (or a future Network `log_crc_mismatch` hook) is recorded, the `.rep` is deleted instead of kept. Crash-during-record never preserves the replay either.
close_reason: leftover cleanup_replay_file copies to base_stats_dir never deletes; log_crc_mismatch was_desync only debug+save_stats; stop_recording only when is_multiplayer: C++ cleanUpReplayFile preserve

title: [LaserUpdate] setDecayFrames never wired — PUC beams stay full width then pop
description:
## C++
`LaserUpdate::setDecayFrames(decayFrames)` (`LaserUpdate.cpp:210-218`): if `decayFrames > 0`, sets `m_decaying`, `m_decayStartFrame = now`, `m_decayFinishFrame = now + decayFrames`, `m_currentWidthScalar = 1`. `clientUpdate` (`:181-193`) then `scalar = 1 - (now-start)/(finish-start)` so the beam shrinks to 0.

Callers (not via negative `initLaser` sizeDelta):
- PUC orbital beam at `LASERSTATUS_BORN` → `setDecayFrames(m_widthGrowFrames)` (`ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:440-447`).
- PUC `STATUS_POSTFIRE` on the ground-to-orbit beam (`:1275-1290`): `setDecayFrames(0)` on reveal, else `setDecayFrames(m_widthGrowFrames)`.

`WidthGrowTime` is 2000ms (60 frames). The player sees the orbital and uplink beams **thin out** over 2s, then the drawable is destroyed at `orbitalDeathFrame`.

## Rust
`LaserUpdate::set_decay_frames` exists on the struct (`laser_update.rs:653-660`) but is **not** on `LaserUpdateInterface` (`Common/.../module.rs:355-370`: dirty/start/end/width/init_laser only). Grep finds **no callers**.

Leftover PUC:
- `LaserStatus::Born` only flips `laser_status = Decaying` (`particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:1409-1413`) — comment "Start decay animation" but no `setDecayFrames`.
- `STATUS_POSTFIRE` (`:1282-1292`) recreates ground-to-orbit with growth 0 and stores `ground_to_orbit_decay_end_frame` locally; never talks to LaserUpdate.

`init_drawable_laser` can start **widening** via `size_delta_frames > 0`, but cannot start decay after the beam is already at full width. Host PUC honesty samples a parallel residual scalar; the live LaserUpdate width stays 1 until the drawable is deleted.

## Evidence
C++ LaserUpdate.cpp:181-218; ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:440-447, 1275-1290.
Rust `module.rs:355-370`; `laser_update.rs:653-660` (dead); PUC leftover `:1282-1292`, `:1409-1413`.

## Player-visible effect
Particle Uplink Cannon beams stay full width through POSTFIRE / orbital death, then pop off. C++ shrinks them over WidthGrowTime (2s). Scorch/damage radius that reads `getCurrentLaserRadius()` also stays at full template width for the whole tail instead of tapering.
close_reason: LaserUpdateInterface::set_decay_frames + leftover PUC Born/POSTFIRE call set_drawable_laser_decay_frames

title: [LaserUpdate] initLaser recreates muzzle/target particles every call
description:
## C++
`LaserUpdate::initLaser` (`LaserUpdate.cpp:286-345`) creates muzzle/target particle systems **once**:

```
if (!m_particleSystemID) {  // last-day NULL check; INVALID==0
  if (!parent || parent->getShroudedStatus(local) <= OBJECTSHROUD_PARTIAL_CLEAR) {
    create MuzzleParticleSystem → m_particleSystemID
    create TargetParticleSystem → m_targetParticleSystemID
  }
}
// then always find+setPosition existing systems
```

`clientUpdate` does **not** spawn or move particles. PUC re-calls `initLaser` every steering frame (`ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:591-592`); SpecialAbility re-inits during prep (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:1121`). Re-init only repositions the same two systems.

Dtor (`LaserUpdate.cpp:76-83`) destroys both IDs.

## Rust
`LaserUpdate::init_laser` always calls `create_particle_systems` (`laser_update.rs:500-501, 680-715`) with **no** existing-ID guard. If `MuzzleParticleSystem` / `TargetParticleSystem` are non-empty it `create_particle_system` and **overwrites** `particle_system_id` / `target_particle_system_id` without destroying the previous IDs.

`client_update` (`:609-618`) extra-follows the *latest* IDs when dirty. `Drop` (`:812-822`) only destroys the last pair.

PUC leftover `init_drawable_laser` every orbit steer (`particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:1563-1567`) and leftover SpecialAbility `init_laser` every prep tick (`special_ability_update.rs:728-740`) hit this path.

## Evidence
C++ LaserUpdate.cpp:286-345 (create-once + reposition), 76-83 (dtor).
Rust `laser_update.rs:500-501, 609-618, 680-715, 812-822`.
Callers: PUC `init_drawable_laser` per-frame; SpecialAbility leftover `init_laser` per prep.

## Player-visible effect
Lasers authored with muzzle/target particle systems (Patriot BinaryDataStream, PUC beams, hacker/Lotus streams) spawn a **new** flare/impact system every re-init frame. Old systems leak until process death. The beam is buried in multiplying FX; save/load IDs only name the last pair.
close_reason: init_laser creates muzzle/target particles once; re-init only repositions existing IDs

title: [LaserUpdate] Leftover LaserUpdate is invented DPS Behavior, never initLaser
description:
## C++
`LaserUpdate` is a **ClientUpdate** on the laser drawable (`LaserUpdate.h:42-67`, `LaserUpdate.cpp`). It is not an object Behavior and never deals damage.

INI (`LaserUpdate.cpp:36-47`): `MuzzleParticleSystem`, `TargetParticleSystem`, `PunchThroughScalar` (default 0).

Runtime:
- `initLaser(parent, target, start, end, parentBone, sizeDeltaFrames)` (`:223-369`) records parent/target drawable IDs, samples the parent bone, grows/decays width, creates muzzle/target particle systems once, and **must** `draw->setPosition` to parent or the start/end midpoint or the beam will not render.
- `clientUpdate` (`:176-208`) retargets start/end and animates width.
- `setDecayFrames` (`:210-218`) starts the shrink.
- Xfer v1 (`:407-458`): start/end, dirty, particle IDs, widen/decay, width scalar, parent/target drawable IDs, bone name.

Weapon/PUC/SpecialAbility/AssistedTargeting all `findClientUpdateModule("LaserUpdate")` and call `initLaser`. Damage comes from the **weapon**, not LaserUpdate.

## Rust
Leftover `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/behavior/laser_update.rs` is an invented **Behavior**:
- Parses `LaserBoneName` / `LaserDuration` / `LaserDamage` (defaults 1s / 10 dmg). Drops the three C++ keys.
- `update_simple` deals `DamageType::Laser` every frame while `activate_laser` is live.
- Xfer is `current_target` / `laser_active` / `laser_end_frame` / damage+duration overrides — not the C++ client layout.
- No `initLaser`, particles, punch-through, widen/decay, or drawable placement.

Leftover `module_overrides/install.rs:775-779` registers this as `ModuleType::Behavior` **"LaserUpdate"** next to the real ClientUpdate factory (`:477-481`). Leftover `Weapon::create_laser` (`weapon.rs:1402-1458`) only walks `get_laser_behavior_control_interface()` and `activate_laser` — it never `findClientUpdateModule` / `initLaser`. Live `create_laser_object` still tries the leftover Behavior hook first (`weapon_instance_combat.rs:1132-1145`) before the client `init_laser`.

## Evidence
C++ LaserUpdate.cpp:36-47, 176-218, 223-369, 407-458; Weapon.cpp:2418-2451 (`findClientUpdateModule` + `initLaser`).
Rust leftover `behavior/laser_update.rs:21-90, 149-202, 234-279`; `module_overrides/install.rs:775-779`; leftover `weapon.rs:1446-1457`.

## Player-visible effect
On the leftover path, laser objects never get the C++ client laser (no beam growth, muzzle/target FX, punch-through, or save-compatible state). If the leftover Behavior attaches, the "laser" silently ticks invented Laser DPS instead of drawing a beam. Leftover `create_laser` cannot initialize the real ClientUpdate module at all.
close_reason: leftover LaserUpdate is ClientUpdate not DPS; leftover weapon + live create_laser_object call init_laser

title: [AssistedTargetingUpdate] Live makeFeedbackLaser skips LaserUpdate and uses a 15-frame snapshot beam
description:
## C++
`AssistedTargetingUpdate::makeFeedbackLaser` (`AssistedTargetingUpdate.cpp:94-117`):
- Requires `getObject()->getControllingPlayer()`.
- `TheThingFactory->newObject(laserTemplate, defaultTeam)`.
- `laser->setPosition(from->getPosition())`.
- Finds ClientUpdate `LaserUpdate` on **the laser object's drawable**.
- If missing: `TheGameLogic->destroyObject(laser)` and return.
- Else `LaserUpdate::initLaser(getObject(), to, fromPos, toPos, "")` (parent = assistant, endpoints + optional muzzle/target particles, drawable placed at parent/midpoint so it actually draws).
- Lifetime is the laser ThingTemplate's (PatriotBinaryDataStream `DeletionUpdate` **600ms** / 18 frames). `update()` only caches templates and returns `UPDATE_SLEEP_FOREVER`.

`assistAttack` (`:74-89`) only reaches lasers after `getAI()` is non-null; then `setWeaponLock(slot, LOCKED_TEMPORARILY)` + `aiAttackObject(victim, clipSize, CMD_FROM_AI)`.

## Rust
Live `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/behavior/assisted_targeting_update.rs` (leftover `object/update/assisted_targeting_update.rs` is a re-export of the same type):
- `make_feedback_laser` (`:109-167`) `factory.new_object` then **`TheGameClient::create_drawable` + `set_drawable_beam`** (snapshot endpoints).
- Never `find` ClientUpdate `LaserUpdate`, never `init_laser` / `init_drawable_laser` (that helper already exists on GameClient; SpecialAbilityUpdate leftover already uses `get_laser_update_interface`).
- Never `destroyObject` when LaserUpdate is missing.
- Hardcoded `FEEDBACK_LASER_LIFE_FRAMES = LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND/2` (**15** frames / 500ms), then `destroy_drawable` from `update_simple`. Factory-created laser objects are not destroyed here.
- `update_simple` wakes every frame while `feedback_beams` are live (C++ sleeps forever; LaserUpdate/DeletionUpdate own the object).

## Evidence
- C++ `AssistedTargetingUpdate.cpp:94-117,121-132` and `LaserUpdate.cpp:223-369` (`initLaser`).
- Live `assisted_targeting_update.rs:31,109-167,170-195`.
- Live LaserUpdate port exists at `GameLogic/src/object/update/laser_update.rs:448-504` and is unused by this module.
- Host residual `host_base_defense.rs` already documents retail DeletionUpdate **600ms** (`PATRIOT_ASSIST_LASER_LIFETIME_FRAMES = 18`). Closed `hq-cmm` is that **host** residual (fail-closed on full W3DLaserDraw), not this live module path.
- Closed `hq-2tfk` wired `process_request_assistance` → `assist_attack`; this gap is inside `makeFeedbackLaser` after that call.

## Player-visible
Patriot (and any `AssistedTargetingUpdate`) assist feedback: C++ spawns real `PatriotBinaryDataStream` objects whose LaserUpdate draws/tracks and whose DeletionUpdate removes them at 600ms, with template particle flares. Live shows a 500ms static client beam and can leave the factory laser object behind. Nearby Patriots still lock/fire the assist clip; only the feedback laser object path is wrong.
close_reason: make_feedback_laser finds ClientUpdate LaserUpdate, init_laser, destroyObject if missing; update sleeps forever

title: [Slaved] Live drones stay selectable after enslave
description:
## C++
`startSlavedEffects` (`SlavedUpdate.cpp:700-701`) sets `OBJECT_STATUS_UNSELECTABLE` so the player cannot pick or order the slave. `stopSlavedEffects` (`:725`) clears it when the slaver dies.

## Rust
Leftover `start_slaved_effects` (`slaved_update.rs:532`) sets `UNSELECTABLE`, but `on_enslave` (`:1292-1294`) returns `Ok(())` when `OBJECT_REGISTRY` is empty, so host-only attach never marks the drone.

Live `residual_attach_slave_drone` (`missile_defenders.rs:1747-1751`) only writes `producer_id` + UpgradeDie. It never calls `set_status_unselectable`. Host drone templates even add `KindOf::Selectable`.

## Evidence
C++ `:700-701` vs leftover `:532` gated by `:1292-1294` vs live attach `:1747-1751`.

## Player-visible
Scout/Hellfire/Battle drones can be selected and given independent move/attack orders instead of staying locked to the master.
close_reason: residual_attach_slave_drone sets set_status_unselectable(true) matching startSlavedEffects OBJECT_STATUS_UNSELECTABLE

title: [Slaved] Leftover onObjectCreated packing never dispatched
description:
## C++
`SlavedUpdate::onObjectCreated` (`SlavedUpdate.cpp:61-65`): if `m_repairRatePerSecond > 0`, set `MODELCONDITION_PACKING` so the Battle drone arm starts retracted. `setRepairState` later unpacks/extends/welds/retracts via `MODELCONDITION_UNPACKING` / `FIRING_B` / `FIRING_C`.

## Rust
Leftover `on_object_created_internal` (`slaved_update.rs:510-517`) ports the packing set, and `BehaviorModuleInterface::on_object_created` (`:1269-1271`) calls it. Live leftover dispatch is `Module::on_object_created` (`object/mod.rs:2419-2420`). `SlavedUpdateModule` (`:1412-1432`) does **not** override `Module::on_object_created` (default no-op in `Common/.../module.rs:537`). Contrast `BattlePlanUpdateModule`, which explicitly forwards that hook.

Live host residual comments "Not full Battle Drone arm pack/unpack weld FX anim interleave" and never sets packing/unpacking/firing-B/C.

## Evidence
C++ `:61-65` vs leftover behavior hook unused by `SlavedUpdateModule` vs live no model-condition weld machine.

title: [GameLOD] Leftover getSlowDeathScale ignores live dynamic LOD
description:
## C++
`setDynamicLODLevel` / `applyDynamicLODLevel` (`GameLOD.cpp:639-661`) copies `m_slowDeathScale` from the selected `DynamicGameLODInfo` (INI `SlowDeathScale`). `getSlowDeathScale()` returns that live field.

`W3DDisplay::draw` (`W3DDisplay.cpp:1653-1659`) calls `findDynamicLODLevel(avgFPS)` then `setDynamicLODLevel` every frame (or forces VERY_HIGH when dynamic LOD is off). `SlowDeathBehavior` (`SlowDeathBehavior.cpp:215-219`, `366-370`) reads `TheGameLODManager->getSlowDeathScale()` so low FPS accelerates / skips death anims.

`CommandXlat` debug cycle also calls `setDynamicLODLevel`.

## Rust
Live draw (`Main/src/cnc_game_engine/run_loop.rs` → `GameEngine::apply_draw_dynamic_lod`) correctly updates the **manager** via `ini_game_lod::set_dynamic_lod_level` (masks, priorities, `manager.slow_death_scale`).

Leftover `game_lod::get_slow_death_scale` (`game_lod.rs:596-603`) ignores the manager. It keys a separate HashMap (raw-text `SlowDeathScale` parse) by leftover `get_dynamic_lod()` string, which defaults to `"High"` and is **never written by `apply_draw_dynamic_lod`**.

`TheGameLODManager::get_slow_death_scale` (`GameLogic/src/helpers/globals.rs:65-67`) and `SlowDeathBehavior` (`slow_death_behavior.rs:830`, `1106`) use the leftover function.

`set_dynamic_lod_from_string` / `cycle_dynamic_lod_level` (`meta_event_impl/helpers.rs:136-150`) only write the leftover name string — they do not call `set_dynamic_lod_level`, so particle/debris skip masks also stay put for the debug cycle.

## Evidence
- C++ apply 651-661; SlowDeathBehavior 215-219 / 366-370.
- Rust manager apply: `ini_game_lod.rs:749-776`.
- Leftover: `game_lod.rs:173-177`, `562-603`; helpers.rs:65-67; `slow_death_behavior.rs:830`.
- Closed SlowDeath beads (`hq-dqdob` etc.) cover dispatch/FX, not this GameLOD leftover/live split.

## Player-visible
When FPS drops, particles/debris skip via the live manager but death animations keep High's scale (usually 1.0). Units linger through full death sequences on a struggling machine instead of accelerating or popping. Debug "Dynamic Game Detail" cycle does not change skip masks either.
close_reason: get_slow_death_scale reads live GameLODManager.slow_death_scale; set_dynamic_lod_from_string calls set_dynamic_lod_level

title: [GameLOD] Custom Options.ini keys missing or wrong on init
description:
## C++
When `OptionPreferences` StaticGameLOD is Custom, `GameLODManager::init` (`GameLOD.cpp:320-336`) copies saved options into GlobalData **before** `setStaticLODLevel(CUSTOM)`:

- `getTextureReduction()` → `TextureReduction`
- `get3DShadowsEnabled()` / `get2DShadowsEnabled()` → `UseShadowVolumes` / `UseShadowDecals`
- `getBuildingOcclusionEnabled()` → `BuildingOcclusion` → `m_enableBehindBuildingMarkers`
- `getParticleCap()` → `MaxParticleCount`
- `getDynamicLODEnabled()` → `DynamicLOD` → `m_enableDynamicLOD`
- `getFPSLimitEnabled()` → `FPSLimit` → `m_useFpsLimit`
- lightmap/cloud/smooth water
- `getUseHeatEffects()` → **`HeatEffects`**
- `getExtraAnimationsDisabled()` → `ExtraAnimations` → `m_useDrawModuleLOD` and `m_useTreeSway = !m_useDrawModuleLOD`
- `getTreesEnabled()` → **`ShowTrees`**

`refreshCustomStaticLODLevel` then snapshots those live GlobalData values into the Custom slot.

## Rust
`load_game_lod_ini_presets_and_options` Custom branch (`game_lod.rs:522-554`) only applies:

`TextureReduction`, `UseShadowVolumes`, `UseShadowDecals`, `MaxParticleCount`, `UseLightMap`, `UseCloudMap`, `ShowSoftWaterEdge`, **`UseHeatEffects`**, **`UseTrees`**.

Missing: `DynamicLOD`, `FPSLimit`, `ExtraAnimations` (+ tree-sway borrow), `BuildingOcclusion`.

Wrong keys vs C++ / vs the live options saver (`menu_callbacks.rs:1080-1084` writes `HeatEffects` and `ShowTrees`). Restart therefore cannot reload heat or trees.

## Evidence
- C++ `GameLOD.cpp:320-336` and `OptionsMenu.cpp` getters (`HeatEffects` 602-611, `ShowTrees` 578-587, `DynamicLOD` 614-623, `FPSLimit` 626-635, `ExtraAnimations` 590-599, `BuildingOcclusion` 662-671).
- Rust `game_lod.rs:522-554` vs `menu_callbacks.rs:1072-1084`.
- Residual of closed `hq-trsv`/`hq-hm2ao` (load+apply user level exists; Custom field list is still incomplete).

## Player-visible
Custom graphics do not survive restart: extra animations / scaffolds, behind-building markers, dynamic-LOD toggle, FPS cap, heat distortion, and trees revert to GameData/preset defaults. A retail `Options.ini` with Custom + `HeatEffects`/`ShowTrees` is ignored.
close_reason: Custom Options.ini applies HeatEffects ShowTrees DynamicLOD FPSLimit ExtraAnimations BuildingOcclusion (C++ OptionPreferences keys)
