title: [Parking] Live+leftover miss HeliPark01 exit/rally contract
description:
## C++
`exitObjectViaDoor` for `KINDOF_PRODUCED_AT_HELIPAD` (`ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:752-814`) reads bone `HeliPark01` for hangar/parking pose, then `aiMoveToPosition` to `getRallyPoint()` if set, else to that parking space. `getExitPosition` / `getNaturalRallyPoint` (`859-870`) both return `HeliPark01`. `setRallyPoint` / `getRallyPoint` store `m_heliRallyPoint`.

## Rust
Leftover `exit_object_via_door` does look up `HeliPark01` and follows heli rally. Leftover `ExitInterface` / `ModuleExitInterface` have no `get_exit_position` / `get_natural_rally_point`, so rally-placement UI / default-rally callers cannot read `HeliPark01`. Live `reserve_produced_aircraft_parking_space` only assigns a slot index; no `HeliPark01`, no heli rally, no `getExitPosition`.

## Evidence
C++ `ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:752-870` vs leftover `parking_place_behavior.rs:1378-1516` (exit) + `specialized_behavior.rs:183-231` (trait missing those two methods) vs live `world_tick/airfield.rs:270-287`. `bd search HeliPark01` / `heli rally` empty.

## Player-visible

close_reason: Leftover ExitInterface/ParkingPlace get_exit_position+get_natural_rally_point return HeliPark01; live reserve_produced skips hangar slot and ticks HeliPark01+rally.

title: [Parking] Live never builds bone PPInfo stall/runway poses
description:
## C++
`buildInfo` (`ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:56-125`) builds one `ParkingPlaceInfo` per NumRows×NumCols from logical bones `Runway{col}Park{row}Han`, `Runway{col}Parking{row}`, `Runway{col}Prep{row}`, plus `RunwayStart{col}` / `RunwayEnd{col}` when `HasRunways`. `calcPPInfo` fills `PPInfo` (hangar vs `ParkInHangars` parking location/orient, prep, runway start/end, approach = end + 0.75*(end-start) + ApproachHeight + LandingDeckHeightOffset, takeoff dist). `reserveSpace` applies `parkingOffset` along stall orientation.

## Rust
Leftover `build_info` / `calc_pp_info` look up those bones (calc no-ops if `HasRunways=No` so PPInfo stays origin). Live host never builds bone PPInfo. `try_return_to_base_rearm` / `try_runway_takeoff_from_airfield` snap jets to airfield center + `PARKING_PLACE_RUNWAY_PREP_SPACING` along X and `landing_deck_height_offset` / `approach_height` on Y (`airfield.rs:457-465,767-783`). `ParkInHangars` is unused for pose (only misused as a door-hold bool).

## Evidence
C++ `ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:56-125,357-399,339-346` vs leftover `parking_place_behavior.rs:391-502,695-747` vs live `world_tick/airfield.rs:405-480,761-803`. Not JetAI takeoff/park-orient (`hq-xl7qa` / `hq-gomww` / `hq-fya6a` consume PPInfo; this is ParkingPlace never producing bone stalls).

## Player-visible
Produced and RTB jets park at the airfield origin instead of hangar/parking bones. Taxi, prep, and approach points are a flat X offset, so jets stack and ignore authored stall layout.
close_reason: Live airfield.rs calc_airfield_pp_info builds stall/runway PPInfo (hangar/parking/prep/start/end/approach 0.75 + heights, wasInLine start=prep); takeoff/rearm use it.

title: [Parking] Live runway reserve is first-free with no next-in-line queue
description:
## C++
`reserveRunway` (`ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:453-502`) binds a jet to the runway column of its parking space (`ppi->m_runway`). If that runway is free, assign `m_inUseBy` and honor `m_nextInLineForTakeoff` / `m_wasInLine`. If busy and `!forLanding`, queue as `m_nextInLineForTakeoff` and return false. `transferRunwayReservationToNextInLineForTakeoff` promotes the waiter; `calcPPInfo` then sets `runwayStart = runwayPrep` when `m_wasInLine`.

## Rust
Leftover `reserve_runway` / `transfer_runway_reservation_to_next_in_line_for_takeoff` port the C++ queue (transfer skips `purgeDead`). Live `reserve_airfield_runway` (`world_tick/airfield.rs:367-384`) takes the first empty slot among all runways — no per-space column, no `nextInLineForTakeoff`, no `wasInLine`. A second jet either steals another column or stays docked until a distance-based clear tick.

## Evidence
C++ `ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:453-502,437-449,391-397` vs leftover `parking_place_behavior.rs:775-829,1665-1672` vs live `airfield.rs:364-395`. Distinct from already-filed JetAI `findWaiter` (`hq-n3qjx`). `bd search next-in-line` empty.

## Player-visible
Two jets from the same hangar column do not queue on that runway. They either take the other runway (wrong taxi) or sit in the hangar until the first jet is far away. No prep-start takeoff for the waiter.
close_reason: Live reserve_airfield_runway_ex binds ppi.m_runway column, queues m_nextInLineForTakeoff when !forLanding, transfer on clear, wasInLine for PPInfo.

title: [Parking] Live sell/die kill only contained occupants, not reserved taxiing jets
description:
## C++
`BuildAssistant` sell (`BuildAssistant.cpp:1553-1561`) and `onDie` (`ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:643-646`) call `killAllParkedUnits`. That walks `m_spaces` (not contain roster): skip dead; skip `isAboveTerrain() && !takeoffOrLanding`; otherwise `obj->kill()` (`ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:614-640`). Taxiing / landing jets in a reserved space die with the airfield.

## Rust
Leftover `kill_all_parked_units` matches the space walk + above-terrain skip. Live `on_selling_container_residual` (`rebuild_dozer.rs:315-468`) only kills `contained_units` / `contained_by == structure` aircraft whose `airborne_target` is false and `position.y <= 5.0`. It never walks `airfield_parking_spaces`. Reserved-but-not-contained taxiing jets survive. The `y > 5` heuristic also spares jets slightly above the hangar.

## Evidence
C++ `ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:614-646` + `BuildAssistant.cpp:1553-1561` vs leftover `parking_place_behavior.rs:888-924` vs live `rebuild_dozer.rs:337-353,446-468`. `bd search killAllParked` / `parked` empty of this gap.

## Player-visible
Selling or destroying an airfield leaves taxiing and landing jets alive on the pad. Jets a few units above the hangar also survive the sell kill.
close_reason: Live tick_airfield_parking_lifecycle kill_all_parked_units walks airfield_parking_spaces; kills reserved taxiing/landing; skips airborne cruise.

title: [Parking] Live KindOf drops PRODUCED_AT_HELIPAD so helos consume hangar slots
description:
## C++
`shouldReserveDoorWhenQueued` / `hasAvailableSpaceFor` / `reserveDoorForExit` (`ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:267-283, 695-702`) treat `KINDOF_PRODUCED_AT_HELIPAD` as unlimited: never reserve a door, always report space, return `DOOR_NONE_NEEDED`. title: [Parking] Live capture never defects parked jets
description:
## C++
`Object::defect` (`Object.cpp:6194-6202`) walks behavior modules and calls `ParkingPlaceBehavior::defectAllParkedUnits`. That walks `m_spaces`: grounded / takeoff-or-landing jets `defect(newTeam, detectionTime)` with the airfield; airborne jets that are not mid takeoff/landing `releaseSpace` and clear producer if the new controlling player differs (`ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:575-611`).

title: [FireWhen] Live onDamage reaction always classifies damage as EXPLOSION
description:
## C++
`FireWeaponWhenDamagedBehavior::onDamage` (`FireWeaponWhenDamagedBehavior.cpp:154-156`) requires `getDamageTypeFlag(d->m_damageTypes, damageInfo->in.m_damageType)`. Default module data is `DAMAGE_TYPE_FLAGS_ALL`. Authored `DamageTypes = NONE +FLAME +POISON` (etc.) must see the **actual** incoming type. C++ `DAMAGE_EXPLOSION` is ordinal 0.

## Rust
Live typed reaction is driven from `host_damage_log` (`HostDamageEvent` has amount/source/destroyed only — **no damage type**). `world_tick/ai.rs:284-285` always calls `execute_temporary_weapon_on_damage(object_id, event.amount, 0)`. `damaged_reaction_plan` then does `metadata.damage_types.contains_ordinal(damage_type_ordinal)` (`temporary_weapon_fire.rs:86-88`). Every reaction is classified as `DAMAGE_EXPLOSION`.

Host leftover peel (`object/damage.rs:361-371`) uses a hardcoded exclusion list (Healing/Status/Hack/Deploy/Disarm/KillPilot/KillGarrisoned) instead of the parsed mask.

## Evidence
- `GeneralsMD/.../FireWeaponWhenDamagedBehavior.cpp:154-160`
- `GeneralsMD/.../FireWeaponWhenDamagedBehavior.h:46` default ALL
- `GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/host_damage_log.rs:13-20`
- `GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/ai.rs:284-285`
- `GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/world_combat/temporary_weapon_fire.rs:63-88`
- `GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/object/damage.rs:360-371`

## Player-visible
Objects whose `FireWeaponWhenDamaged` INI restricts `DamageTypes` (e.g. flame/poison-only reaction) either never spark on the intended damage or spark on every explosion-classified hit. Default-ALL modules still fire, so this is most visible on authored type filters (toxic fields, fire-only reactions).
close_reason: host_damage_log record_typed + object/damage.rs + world_tick/ai.rs pass C++ DamageType ordinal; leftover on_damage uses parsed DamageTypes mask instead of hardcoded exclusion

title: [FireWhen] Leftover residual falls back across body states and ticks at 1 Hz
description:
## C++
`onDamage` / `update` pick **exactly one** body-state weapon (Rubble / ReallyDamaged / Damaged / else Pristine) and fire only if that slot's Weapon `getStatus()==READY_TO_FIRE` (`FireWeaponWhenDamagedBehavior.cpp:165-241`). No fallback to another state's weapon. Continuous rate is the owned Weapon clip / delay-between-shots, not a fixed timer. Ctor uses `reloadAmmo` (clip reload delay), not `loadAmmoNow`.

## Rust
When `temporary_weapon_runtime.damaged` is empty (name-peel leftover, or parse fail-closed), host uses `HostFireWeaponWhenDamagedData`:
- `weapon_for_state` falls back `Rubble → really → damaged → pristine` (`host_fire_weapon_when_damaged.rs:108-113`). A BattleshipTarget with no rubble reaction still fires the really-damaged weapon as it dies.
- Continuous tick uses a hardcoded `FWWDB_CONTINUOUS_RELOAD_FRAMES = 30` (1s @ 30fps) instead of the weapon's READY_TO_FIRE / DelayBetweenShots (`:23-26,141-164`). GameWorld shadow copies the same 30-frame timer (`status_timers_structure.rs:176-192`) even though its slot pick is exact.
- Peel only attaches BattleshipTarget + toxic-bunker-ish names (`fire_when_damaged_config_for_template`); other INI users get nothing on this leftover path.
- GameEngine live module (`fire_weapon_when_damaged_behavior_new.rs:496-498`) calls `load_ammo_now` (instant) instead of C++ `reloadAmmo`, so first reaction/continuous shot ignores clip reload.

## Evidence
- `GeneralsMD/.../FireWeaponWhenDamagedBehavior.cpp:52-54,165-241`
- `GeneralsMD/.../Weapon.cpp:1828-1833,1877-1891`
- `GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/host_fire_weapon_when_damaged.rs:23-26,92-164,196-213`
- `GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/gameworld_shadow/tick/status_timers_structure.rs:171-196`
- `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/behavior/fire_weapon_when_damaged_behavior_new.rs:483-501`

## Player-visible
Battleship-target style reaction can explode on rubble when C++ would be silent. Toxic-bunker continuous poison ticks at a fake 1 Hz instead of the authored weapon cadence. Units that only exist on the leftover peel list (or GameEngine `load_ammo_now` path) fire too soon after spawn if `ClipReloadTime > 0`.
close_reason: host_fire_weapon_when_damaged.rs exact body-state slot (no fallback); continuous rate from DelayBetweenShots; first tick reloadAmmo; GameEngine allocate_weapon reload_ammo; GameWorld FWWDB first-tick clip clock

title: [BattlePlan] Host leftover SearchAndDestroy never doubles Strategy Center vision/shroud
description:
## C++
`BattlePlanUpdate::setBattlePlan(PLANSTATUS_SEARCHANDDESTROY)` (`BattlePlanUpdate.cpp:804-810`) if `m_strategyCenterSearchAndDestroySightRangeScalar != 1.0f`:
- `obj->setVisionRange(vision * scalar)`
- `obj->setShroudClearingRange(shroud * scalar)`

Removal (`:745-749`) divides both ranges by the same scalar. Retail INI scalar is **2.0**, so the Strategy Center's own look/shroud-clear doubles while SearchAndDestroy is ACTIVE.

## Rust
Live GameLogic `apply_search_and_destroy_bonuses` (`behavior/battle_plan_update.rs:844-856`) and leftover `object/update/battle_plan_update.rs:512-523` both apply the scalar to vision + shroud.

Host leftover `apply_battle_plan_set_battle_plan` (`world_combat/heroes_and_plans.rs:801-815`) enables the StealthDetector residual then **discards** the building sight scalar:

```
let _ = STRATEGY_CENTER_SEARCH_AND_DESTROY_SIGHT_SCALAR;
```

Removal (`:626-635`) likewise never divides vision/shroud. Mood-target helper `strategy_center_mood_vision_range` uses 2.0 only for idle-gun acquire, not for the building's `vision_range` / shroud-clearing.

## Evidence
- C++: `setVisionRange` + `setShroudClearingRange` × `m_strategyCenterSearchAndDestroySightRangeScalar` (2.0)
- Host leftover: `let _ = STRATEGY_CENTER_SEARCH_AND_DESTROY_SIGHT_SCALAR;` on both apply and remove
- Live GameLogic module does apply the scalar (gap is leftover host path, which is the running Main sim)

## Player-visible
While SearchAndDestroy is active, the Strategy Center does not double its vision or shroud-clearing range. Fog stays at the default 400 instead of 800; the player cannot see as far from the building as in retail.
close_reason: host_strategy_center.rs apply/remove_strategy_center_search_and_destroy_sight + heroes_and_plans.rs apply_battle_plan_set_battle_plan now multiply/divide Strategy Center vision_range and shroud_clearing_range by 2.0 (C++ BattlePlanUpdate.cpp:804-810 / 745-749). Live leftover battle_plan_update already applied the scalar.

title: [Physics] scrubVelocity2D with negative desired speed reverses velocity instead of stopping
description:
C++: PhysicsBehavior::scrubVelocity2D (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1012-1027) gates on `desiredVelocity < 0.001f` — ANY negative desired velocity zeroes m_vel.x/m_vel.y (clamp-to-stop), and the else branch only ever scales down toward a positive cap.

Rust: the trait default (GameLogic/src/modules/physics.rs:167-183) gates on `desired_velocity.abs() < 0.001` and then computes scale = desired_velocity / cur — for negative desired this multiplies x/y by a negative factor, FLIPPING the velocity direction and rescaling it, instead of stopping. PhysicsBehaviorHandle inherits the same default (no override in physics_update.rs).

Evidence: live caller locomotor/core_impl/move_dispatch.rs:72 `physics.scrub_velocity_2d(desired_speed)` in the blocked path mirrors C++ Locomotor.cpp:1031 `physics->scrubVelocity2D(desiredSpeed)`; desiredSpeed is negative when the locomotor is moving backwards, which is exactly the case where C++ stops the unit and Rust flings it the opposite way. (ai_core.rs:576 rappel and battle_bus 0.0 calls are unaffected — only signed args diverge.)

Player-visible: a unit driving backwards that gets path-blocked snaps into forward motion at the scaled magnitude instead of halting — blocked reversing units lurch towards the obstacle they were trying to avoid.
acceptance_criteria: scrub_velocity_2d matches PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1012-1027 exactly: gate on desired < 0.001 (not abs), zeroing x/y for negative desired velocities; add a regression test with a negative desired value asserting velocity is zeroed, not reversed.
close_reason: scrub_velocity_2d gates on desired < 0.001 like PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1012-1027, zeroing x/y for negative desired instead of reversing. Regression tests on trait default and PhysicsBehaviorHandle.

title: [Physics] getForwardSpeed2D/3D missing — live code substitutes unsigned velocity magnitude
description:
C++: PhysicsBehavior::getForwardSpeed2D/3D (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:939-983) return SIGNED speed along the object's facing (2D unit dir / 3D X-vector); negative when moving backwards. Callers rely on the sign: AIStates.cpp:2364/3054 pursuit ('Real victimSpeed = victim->getPhysics()->getForwardSpeed2D(); if (victimSpeed >= ourMaxSpeed) return false' — a victim reversing towards the hunter is catchable), Locomotor.cpp:1126, 1186, 1289, 1612, 1769 (moveBackwards negation), 1897 (getForwardSpeed3D braking), 2337, 2536 (braking distance and stop decisions).

Rust: the PhysicsBehavior trait (GameLogic/src/modules/physics.rs) has no forward-speed accessor at all; live call sites improvise with plain magnitude: ai_targeting.rs:642, states/move.rs:986-992, formation_manager.rs:369, stealth_update.rs:512/535, ai_group.rs:863, jet_ai_update.rs:2199 — all `get_velocity().length()`. A unit moving backwards at speed v reads as 'moving away at v'.

Evidence: grep get_forward_speed in GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine → only GameClient physics_visual/types.rs forward_speed_2d (visual host struct), nothing in GameLogic; grep get_velocity().length() → the substitution sites above.

Player-visible: AI pursuit gives up on targets that are reversing toward them (C++ would keep chasing since signed speed is negative); locomotor braking-distance and 3-point-turn decisions treat lateral slide + reverse as forward motion, so reversing units brake late/turn wrong.
acceptance_criteria: PhysicsBehavior trait exposes signed forward speed (2D from unit direction vector, 3D from transform X vector) per PhysicsUpdate.cpp:939-983 and the pursuit/locomotor call sites use it instead of raw velocity magnitude.
close_reason: PhysicsBehavior::get_forward_speed_2d/3d match PhysicsUpdate.cpp:939-980 signed facing speed. Live pursuit (AIStates.cpp:2364/3054) and locomotor currentSpeed/braking cheat (Locomotor.cpp:1126,1186,1769) use get_forward_speed_2d instead of unsigned magnitude.

title: [WorkerAI] Leftover resume-construction ignores build-time rate and never heals the building
description:
## C++
Resume construction is a normal DOZER_TASK_BUILD: `WorkerAIUpdate::privateResumeConstruction` -> `newTask(DOZER_TASK_BUILD)` -> `DozerActionDoActionState` BUILD case advances `constructionPercent += 100.0f / calcTimeToBuild(player)` per frame AND heals `internalChangeHealth(maxHealth / framesToBuild)` per frame (DozerAIUpdate.cpp:505-540), so the building reaches full HP exactly at 100%.

## Rust
GameEngine leftover resume uses neither the build-time rate nor health scaling:
- `supply_system/worker.rs` `WorkerDozerTaskType::ResumeConstruction` arm (~line 805): `new_percent = (current_percent + repair_rate * 100.0 * SECONDS_PER_LOGICFRAME_REAL).min(100.0)` — uses RepairHealthPercentPerSecond (~2%/s) as the build rate, so any building takes ~50 s regardless of BuildTime, and the arm never touches health (no set_health), so `handle_build_completion` finishes the building at whatever HP it had (typically 1).
- `object/update/ai_update/dozer_ai_update.rs` `set_resume_construction_target` creates the task with `build_total_frames: 0` (~line 863) and the Build arm calls `manager.start_construction(..., task.build_total_frames.max(1), ...)` (~line 1231) -> 1-frame instant completion.

## Evidence
- DozerAIUpdate.cpp:515-527 (percent + health per frame via framesToBuild).
- worker.rs:806-816 repair_rate-based percent, no health write in the arm; handle_build_completion has no full-HP restore.
- dozer_ai_update.rs:861-866 build_total_frames: 0; :1231 `.max(1)`; production/construction.rs update_frame computes 100/total per frame.

## Player-visible
With the dual-world module active: a dozer resuming an unfinished building finishes it instantly (1 frame); a GLA worker resumes at repair pace (2%/s — ~50 s for everything) and the finished building pops at ~1 HP (one bomb kills it), instead of healing progressively to full like C++.
close_reason: Leftover WorkerAIUpdate resume uses calc_time_to_build frames: +100/frames percent and +maxHealth/frames heal (C++ DozerAIUpdate.cpp:515-526). Leftover DozerAIUpdate::set_resume_construction_target stores those frames instead of 0->.max(1) instant complete.

title: [DozerAI] Leftover repair gate uses builder_id instead of sole healing benefactor
description:
## C++
Dozer/worker repair exclusivity uses the SOLE HEALING BENEFACTOR, not the builder: `DozerActionMoveToActionPosState::update` (DozerAIUpdate.cpp:283-296) aborts repair when `goalObject->getSoleHealingBenefactor()` is another unit, and `DozerActionDoActionState` repairs via `goalObject->attemptHealingFromSoleBenefactor(health, dozer, 2)` (line 699) which rejects all other healers for 2 frames. `WorkerAIUpdate::privateRepair` (WorkerAIUpdate.cpp:561-563) likewise checks `getSoleHealingBenefactor`. The builder id is NOT consulted for repair — buildings keep their original builder after completion, so any dozer may repair them.

## Rust
GameEngine leftover repair arms gate on `target_builder_id` instead: `object/update/ai_update/dozer_ai_update.rs` `update_dozer_task` Repair arm (`if target_builder_id != INVALID_ID && target_builder_id != self.object_id { self.internal_task_complete(DozerTask::Repair); return; }`, ~line 1083) and `supply_system/worker.rs` `update_dozer_task` Repair arm (~line 760). `set_repair_target` in both files also never checks `get_sole_healing_benefactor` (C++ privateRepair does), and healing is a direct `set_health`, never `attempt_healing_from_sole_benefactor`.

## Evidence
- DozerAIUpdate.cpp:283-284, 699-708; WorkerAIUpdate.cpp:561-563 (sole benefactor).
- builder_id persists after construction (setBuilder at newTask, DozerAIUpdate.cpp:1986; never cleared on completion).
- dozer_ai_update.rs:1083-1087 and worker.rs:760-764 use `target_builder_id` for REPAIR.
- The live host does this correctly (`world_objects/support_states.rs` attempt_healing_from_sole_benefactor + sole_benefactor_repair_rejects) — only the dual-world leftover module diverges.

## Player-visible
When the dual-world GameEngine module is active: a dozer/worker ordered to repair any building that was BUILT BY A DIFFERENT dozer (the common case) instantly cancels the repair on arrival; meanwhile two dozers can both be tasked (and heal) the same building since no sole-benefactor claim is taken.
close_reason: Leftover DozerAIUpdate/WorkerAIUpdate repair now gates on get_sole_healing_benefactor and heals via attempt_healing_from_sole_benefactor (C++ DozerActionMoveToActionPosState::update DozerAIUpdate.cpp:283-296; DozerActionDoActionState 699; WorkerAIUpdate::privateRepair 561-563). BUILD still uses builder_id exclusivity (cpp:305).

title: [DozerAI] AI-player dozer bored scan drops the 2x AIDozerBoredRadiusModifier
description:
## C++
`DozerAIUpdate::getBoredRange` (DozerAIUpdate.cpp:2305-2312): for PLAYER_COMPUTER dozers returns `TheAI->getAiData()->m_aiDozerBoredRadiusModifier * m_boredRange`. Default modifier is 2.0 (AI.cpp:920 `m_aiDozerBoredRadiusModifier(2.0)`). So a bored AI dozer scans 2x BoredRange for auto-repair targets and mines.

## Rust

The dormant GameEngine leftover does apply the modifier (`object/update/ai_update/dozer_ai_update.rs` `get_bored_range` reads `ai_dozer_bored_radius_modifier`), and `Common/src/common/ini/ini_ai_data.rs:197` keeps the 2.0 default, but the live bored path never consults it.

## Evidence
- DozerAIUpdate.cpp:2307-2310 (PLAYER_COMPUTER -> modifier * boredRange).
- AI.cpp:920 default 2.0; ini_ai_data.rs:197 same default.
- rebuild_dozer.rs:909/956/1056 all use `host_repair::DOZER_BORED_RANGE` directly; no player-type check anywhere in the bored path.

## Player-visible
Skirmish AI dozers only auto-repair damaged structures / auto-clear mines within 150 units instead of 300: AI bases decay and minefields near (but not on top of) AI dozers are never swept, weakening the AI vs C++ retail behavior.
close_reason: Live dozer_bored_scan_range applies AI_DOZER_BORED_RADIUS_MODIFIER 2.0 for computer dozers registered in ai_manager (C++ DozerAIUpdate::getBoredRange, DozerAIUpdate.cpp:2305-2312; AI.cpp:920). Workers keep unmodified WorkerAIUpdate::getBoredRange.

title: [TerrainLogic] setActiveBoundary drops fogged-cell preservation and ghost-object lock dance
description:
C++:
TerrainLogic.cpp:2545-2617 setActiveBoundary: flush pending undo shroud queue; PartitionManager storeFoggedCells(TRUE); GhostObjectManager releasePartitionData(); all objects friend_prepareForMapBoundaryAdjust; storeFoggedCells(FALSE); PartitionManager reset() + init(); TheRadar newMap(TheTerrainLogic); restoreFoggedCells(FALSE); lockGhostObjects(TRUE); all objects friend_notifyOfNewMapBoundary; restoreFoggedCells(TRUE); GhostObjectManager restorePartitionData(); lockGhostObjects(FALSE); TheTacticalView forceCameraConstraintRecalc.

Rust:
terrain.rs set_active_boundary: flush pending queue, prepare objects, assign boundary, partition_manager_mut().clear() (no re-init), radar refresh_terrain(), notify objects, camera recalc. No fogged-cell store/restore (shroud_manager.rs has no store/restore API at all), no GhostObjectManager lock/release/restore even though those APIs exist (object/ghost_object.rs, THE_GHOST_OBJECT_MANAGER) and object.rs even documents the lock as used during map border resizing.

Evidence:
ScriptActions.cpp:4928 calls setActiveBoundary (script boundary change); TerrainLogic xfer load also calls it. Rust scripting/executor/actions_world.rs:542-544 calls terrain.set_active_boundary(border_index).

Player-visible:
After a script shrinks/grows the map boundary (and on save-load with a non-default boundary), shroud/fog/explored state is wrong: previously explored cells can be lost or wrongly revealed, ghost objects (stealth residues) can drop out of the partition during the resize, and the radar rebuild is incomplete.
close_reason: set_active_boundary now does C++ TerrainLogic.cpp:2545-2615 dance: flush pending undo shroud, store fogged+revealed cells, GhostObjectManager/W3D releasePartitionData, prepare objects, store permanent reveal, partition clear, radar refresh, restore revealed, lockGhostObjects, notify objects, restore fog (addLooker+removeLooker), restorePartitionData, unlock, camera recalc.

title: [Die] EjectPilotDie plays eject VO when the chosen OCL is missing

An airborne death with only `GroundCreationList` (or vice versa) is a silent no-op.

## Rust

## Evidence

title: [Die] UpgradeDie INI drops DeathTypes and other DieMux keys
description:
## C++
`UpgradeDie.h:27-38` `buildFieldParse` calls `DieModuleData::buildFieldParse(p)` then adds `UpgradeToRemove`. DieMux keys `DeathTypes`, `VeterancyLevels`, `ExemptStatus`, `RequiredStatus` are therefore legal on every UpgradeDie block (`DieModule.cpp:37-40`).

## Rust
Live `object/die/upgrade_die.rs` `UPGRADE_DIE_FIELDS` (`:178-181`) is only `UpgradeToRemove`. `parse_from_ini` (`:71-72`) never walks `DIE_MODULE_DATA_FIELDS`. Factory `contain_module_overrides/death.rs:13-18` uses that parser. Other live die modules (FXListDie, CreateObjectDie, …) do include the four DieMux keys.

## Evidence
C++ `UpgradeDie.h:30` `DieModuleData::buildFieldParse(p);` then `:34` `UpgradeToRemove`. Rust `upgrade_die.rs:178-181` single FieldParse. Unknown DieMux tokens make `init_from_ini_with_fields` return `UnknownToken` (`ini.rs:1924-1925`), so the rest of the UpgradeDie block (including UpgradeToRemove if it appears after) can fail to parse.

## Player-visible effect
An UpgradeDie authored with any DieMux filter either ignores those keys (if parse is allow-unknown on some path) or aborts the module-data parse. Scout-drone / hero-slot units then free the producer upgrade on the wrong death types, or never install UpgradeToRemove so the upgrade slot stays locked after the unit dies.
close_reason: UpgradeDie UPGRADE_DIE_FIELDS includes DieMux keys via DieModuleData::buildFieldParse (UpgradeDie.h:30)

title: [AIGroup] Live/leftover group move never clamps waypoint to map extent
description:
## C++
`AIGroup::groupMoveToPosition` (`AIGroup.cpp:1569-1593`) walks members for helipad/aircraft extra margin (`STD_AIRCRAFT_EXTRA_MARGIN` / geometry radius), then `clampWaypointPosition(position, margin)` (`:619-650`):
- Human: `TheTerrainLogic->getExtent` (visible map).
- Computer: `getMaximumPathfindExtent`.
- Shrink by `PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE_F` plus the margin so clicks stay on the playable map.

## Rust
Leftover `group_move_to_position` (`ai/group.rs:584-606`) computes `STD_WAYPOINT_CLAMP_MARGIN + extra_margin` then `let _ = _margin;` — the clamp is discarded. Dual-world empty gate may no-op the whole move.
Live `execute_move` (`command_executor/movement.rs:26-74`) never clamps the click/goals to map extent. No `clamp_waypoint` / `getExtent` in the command_executor movement path.

## Evidence
- C++ `AIGroup.cpp:1569-1593`, `:619-650`
- Leftover `ai/group.rs:584-606` (`let _ = _margin`)
- Live `movement.rs:26-74` (no clamp)

## Player-visible
A group-move click near or past the map edge sends units toward (or off) the border. Retail pulls the waypoint back onto the visible map (farther in for aircraft). Units can path into the black/shroud rim or stall on the edge.
close_reason: leftover group_move_to_position now calls clamp_waypoint_position (ai/ai_group). Live execute_move uses clamp_group_waypoint.

title: [PreorderCreate] Host name-heuristic sets PREORDER on wrong buildings
description:
## C++
`PreorderCreate::onBuildComplete` (`PreorderCreate.cpp:40-49`) if `getControllingPlayer()->didPlayerPreorder()` sets `MODELCONDITION_PREORDER`, else clears it. No `shouldDoOnBuildComplete` gate. Module is INI-authored on the buildings that should show the preorder cosmetic (flag/model).

## Rust
Crate `preorder_create.rs:29-55` matches the set/clear logic but re-locks the object via `find_object_by_id` + `write()` while `Object::on_build_complete` already holds that lock.
Playable host (`host_preorder_create.rs:47-62` + `production_eva.rs:1157-1177`) applies the bit only when `is_preorder_create_template` name-contains `commandcenter|warfactory|barracks|supplycenter|airfield|strategycenter|propagandacenter|palace|blackmarket|scudstorm|nuclearmissile|particlecannon`. FakeCommandCenter matches `commandcenter`. Buildings that actually carry `PreorderCreate` but miss those substrings never get the bit. Extra name hits get the bit without the module.

## Evidence
C++ `PreorderCreate.cpp:40-49`. Host `host_preorder_create.rs:46-62` and `production_eva.rs:1157-1177`. Crate `preorder_create.rs:29-55`.

## Player-visible effect
Preorder-bonus flag/model appears on the wrong buildings (Fake CC, extra factories) and is missing on any PreorderCreate structure whose template name is outside the substring list. Non-preorder players can still show the bit on those extra names if a prior set is not cleared (host only touches the heuristic set).
close_reason: PreorderCreate::onBuildComplete uses INI module + didPlayerPreorder (PreorderCreate.cpp:40-49), not template-name heuristic.

title: [Drawable] Ammo and contain pips skip local-player and showObjectHealth gates
description:
## C++
`drawAmmo` (`Drawable.cpp:2865-2870`) and `drawContained` (`:2923-2928`) require `TheGlobalData->m_showObjectHealth`, selected-or-moused-over, and `obj->getControllingPlayer() == ThePlayerList->getLocalPlayer()`. Ammo uses `SCPAmmoFull/Empty` at `m_ammoPipWorldOffset` + geometry height. Contain pips tint infantry green / vehicles blue.

## Rust
`draw_ammo` / `draw_contained` (`basic_overlay.rs:243-367`) only check `selected_or_moused_over_for_icon_pips()`. No local-player test, no `show_object_health`. Live draw (`impl_draw.rs:328-364`) paints 3px colored squares under the health bar, ignoring mapped `SCPAmmo*` / `SCPPip*` images that `init_static_images` already resolved.

## Evidence
C++ `Drawable.cpp:2865-2870, 2923-2928`. Rust `basic_overlay.rs:268, 321` (comment mentions the C++ local-player gate but does not implement it).

## Player-visible
Mousing an enemy unit shows its clip and garrison pips. Toggling object-health off still shows them. Pips sit on the health bar instead of the authored world/screen offset.
close_reason: drawAmmo/drawContained now require ShowObjectHealth + selected/hover + local player; live HUD uses SCPAmmo*/SCPPip* (Drawable.cpp:2865-2928).

Sold / not-under-construction frees the DisplayString.

## Rust
Live HUD (`impl_draw.rs:306-313`) draws `format!(\"{pct}%\")` in white at `bar_y - 12` with no GameText lookup. `CONTROLBAR:UnderConstructionDesc` has zero Rust references. Overlay only stores `construction_percent` as 0..1.

## Player-visible
Construction overlay is a bare \"42%\" instead of the localized CONTROLBAR string, uncentered on the model.
close_reason: drawConstructPercent formats CONTROLBAR:UnderConstructionDesc like Drawable.cpp:3707.

title: [Drawable] Health bar color skips construction/disabled cyan and really-damaged
description:
## C++
`drawHealthBar` (`Drawable.cpp:3871-3916`) uses blue-to-cyan (`GameMakeColor(0, healthRatio*255, 255, 255)`) when `OBJECT_STATUS_UNDER_CONSTRUCTION` or disabled (except HELD). Otherwise it interpolates red↔green and averages toward red if `MODELCONDITION_REALLY_DAMAGED` or toward green if not DAMAGED.

## Rust
`draw_drawable_icon_overlays` (`impl_draw.rs:292-298`) uses a 3-band table: green >0.66, yellow >0.33, else red. Overlay data stores only `health_ratio` — no construction/disabled/really-damaged color channel. `draw_health_bar` (`basic_overlay.rs:114-141`) never writes those states into the overlay.

## Evidence
C++ `Drawable.cpp:3872-3916`. Rust `impl_draw.rs:292-298`. wgpu-vs-D3D is not the issue: the authored color function is missing.

## Player-visible
Building-under-construction and EMP/hacked units show the same green/yellow/red bar as healthy combat units. Really-damaged units are not biased red.
close_reason: Health bar uses C++ cyan construction/disabled and red-green really-damaged mix (Drawable.cpp:3871-3916).

title: [Drawable] drawIconUI ignores getDrawIconUI and script fade
description:

## Rust
Live `BasicDrawable::draw_icon_ui` (`basic_overlay.rs:612-681`) has no `get_draw_icon_ui` or fade check. `GameClient::draw_drawable_icon_ui` (`impl_draw.rs:50-55`) always runs it for visible drawables. `TheGameLogic::set_draw_icon_ui` exists and scripts call it (`actions_skirmish.rs:818-824`); floating text honors the gate (`floating_text.rs:41-43`) but drawable HUD does not. Camera fade is computed in `status_circle.rs` and never consulted here.

C++ `Drawable.cpp:2740`. Rust `basic_overlay.rs:612` has no gate. Script setter is live; overlay consumer is not.

## Player-visible
Cinematic fades and scripted icon-UI-off still show health bars, pips, construct %, and captions over every unit.
close_reason: drawIconUI is a no-op unless TheGameLogic::getDrawIconUI and ScriptEngine fade==FADE_NONE (Drawable.cpp:2740).

title: [AIGroup] Live group-path gate skips infantry line-passable fallback
description:
## C++
`AIGroup::friend_computeGroundPath` (`AIGroup.cpp:504-616`) decides whether to build a shared ground path. After distance / `m_distanceRequiresGroup` / `m_minDistanceForGroup` / infantry>6 / vehicle>4 tests, if still not `closeEnough` it walks infantry and sets `closeEnough` when **every** infantry has `pathfinder()->isLinePassable` from self to the center vehicle (`:590-611`). Then `findGroundPath` from that center.

## Rust
Leftover `group.rs` `friend_compute_ground_path` is the leftover port (dual-world gated). Live host uses `compute_ground_path_should_group` (`command_executor/group.rs:253-330`) from `execute_move_to` (`movement.rs:32-54`) to decide `assign_shared_group_paths`.
Live copies the count/distance/formation tests but **omits the infantry line-passable fallback**. Small clustered infantry (≤6) with a clear line to the group center therefore return false and take free-move individual destinations.

## Evidence
- C++ `AIGroup.cpp:590-616`
- Live `command_executor/group.rs:253-330` (no `isLinePassable` / `is_line_passable`)
- Live caller `movement.rs:32-54`

## Player-visible
A handful of Rangers/Red Guards given a medium-range move do not share a column/spine path even when the space between them is open. They each path independently and clump/cross. Retail still group-paths them when lines to the center unit are passable.
close_reason: leftover friend_compute_ground_path already has infantry is_line_passable fallback. Live compute_ground_path_should_group now has infantry_line_passable_to_center.

title: [AIGroup] Live Scatter uses selection_radius not bounding circle
description:

title: [Display] Logo copyright leftover skips GlobalLanguage font and black draw
description:
## C++
`Display::update` last-frame hold (`Display.cpp` 282-300) builds `m_copyrightDisplayString` from `GUI:EACopyright`. Font is `TheGlobalLanguageData->m_copyrightFont` (name/size/bold via `adjustFontSize`) else Courier 12 bold. `W3DDisplay::draw` (`W3DDisplay.cpp` 1891-1897) draws it black (`GameMakeColor(0,0,0,255)`), transparent back, at `((width-dX)/2, height-dY-20)`.

## Rust
`ensure_copyright_display_string` (`display.rs` 672-685) always uses Courier 12 bold — never reads `GlobalLanguage.copyright_font`. `draw_copyright_hint` (`display_fx.rs` 274-282) draws white 14px text at `(width*0.5-120, height-36)` and only from leftover `Display::draw` after a movie blit. Host present never draws the copyright string.

## Evidence
C++ `Display.cpp:291-299` + `W3DDisplay.cpp:1891-1897`. Rust `display.rs:678` `FontDesc::new("Courier", 12, true)`. `display_fx.rs:278-280` white, hardcoded offset. Main has no copyright draw.

## Player-visible
EA logo hold either shows no copyright on the live host path, or (leftover Display::draw) a white Courier line instead of the localized copyright font, black, bottom-centered.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Play the EA logo movie (`playLogoMovie` 5000/3000 hold).
2. At last frame, wait for the copyright hold.

## Acceptance Criteria
During logo hold the localized `GUI:EACopyright` string is drawn with GlobalLanguage CopyrightFont (fallback Courier 12 bold), black, bottom-centered `height - textHeight - 20`, on the live present path.
close_reason: Logo copyright uses GlobalLanguage CopyrightFont (fallback Courier 12 bold), drawn black at height-dY-20 on leftover and host present

title: [Display] Movie capture leftover records movie-buffer BMPs not the frame
description:
## C++
`W3DDisplay::toggleMovieCapture` (`W3DDisplay.cpp` 3099-3101) calls `WW3D::Toggle_Movie_Capture("Movie", 30)` and dumps the presented framebuffer (AVI / frame sequence) at 30 fps.

## Rust
`Display::toggle_movie_capture` (`display.rs` 535-539) flips `movie_capture_enabled` and resets a serial. Dump (`display.rs` 1176-1183) writes `MovieNNNNN.bmp` from `last_movie_frame` (video-stream RGBA), only inside leftover `Display::draw`. Host present never runs that draw. Gameplay frames are never captured. `DEMO_TOGGLE_AVI` / `toggle_script_display_movie_capture` still hit this leftover.

## Evidence
C++ WW3D movie capture of the backbuffer. Rust dump is `rgba_to_bgr(last_movie_frame)` gated on `Display::draw`. Closed hq-6zxk claimed "last presented buffer"; live code still uses the movie decode buffer and is skipped on the host path.

## Player-visible
Toggling movie capture during play produces no gameplay frames. At best, leftover Display::draw writes BMPs of a playing Bink, not the rendered scene.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Toggle movie capture (`DEMO_TOGGLE_AVI` / `TheDisplay->toggleMovieCapture`) during a match with no fullscreen movie.
2. Look for a Movie/ frame sequence of the presented scene.

## Acceptance Criteria
Toggle starts/stops capture of the presented framebuffer (C++ WW3D 30 fps Movie sequence), not only a Bink decode buffer, on the live present path.
close_reason: Movie capture writes MovieNNNNN.bmp from presented backbuffer via write_backbuffer_movie_frame; host also drives WW3D 30fps capture

title: [TurretAI] Disabled turret cannot finish Recenter; UnderConstruction ignored
description:

Recenter/idle-scan/`isTurretInNaturalPosition` also short-circuit while `OBJECT_STATUS_UNDER_CONSTRUCTION` (`:638-639`, `:1207-1208`, `:1361-1362`) so building defenses do not waggle.

## Rust
Live `tick_turret_state_machine` (`attack.rs:520-522`) returns Failure immediately when `!u.turret_enabled`. Recenter never runs while the turret is off. No UnderConstruction test on Recenter/IdleScan/natural-position.

## Evidence
C++: `if (m_enabled || m_turretStateMachine->getCurrentStateID() == TURRETAI_RECENTER)`.
Host: `if !u.turret_enabled || !u.is_alive() { return Failure; }` before the state match.

## Player-visible effect
Battle-plan / deploy / disable-turret leaves the barrel stuck at the last combat angle instead of finishing recenter. Base defenses under construction idle-scan/recenter as if finished.

## Split hint
Allow Recenter when disabled; freeze Recenter/IdleScan/natural while UnderConstruction (treat as already natural).
close_reason: turret.rs: Recenter while disabled; UnderConstruction freeze

title: [Recorder] PixelRegion replay args use x,y,w,h not C++ lo/hi
description:
## C++
`IRegion2D` (BaseType.h) is `{ ICoord2D lo, hi }`. `writeArgument` / `readArgument` for `ARGUMENTDATATYPE_PIXELREGION` fwrite/fread the whole struct (lo.x, lo.y, hi.x, hi.y). `MSG_AREA_SELECTION` is a network message (between BEGIN/END) so box-selects are recorded this way.

## Rust
`message_stream::game_message::IRegion2D` is `{ x, y, width, height }`. `Recorder::write_argument` / `read_argument` emit/consume those four ints. A C++ region (100,100)-(200,200) becomes Rust (100,100) size 200×200 or vice versa.

## Evidence
C++ analysis log: `"Pixel Region argument: %d,%d -> %d,%d"` uses `reg.lo` / `reg.hi`.
Rust recorder.rs 1118-1122 writes `x,y,width,height`.

## Player-visible effect
Recorded area-selects play back as the wrong rectangle (wrong units selected, or none). C++ and Rust `.rep` files disagree on every `AreaSelection` command.
close_reason: PixelRegion replay args write/read C++ IRegion2D lo/hi (x,y,x+w,y+h)

title: [Audio] Leftover TheAudio add_audio_event invents blank AudioEventInfo instead of AHSV_Error
description:
## C++
`AudioManager::addAudioEvent` (`GameAudio.cpp:391-396`) calls `getInfoForAudioEvent` and returns `AHSV_Error` if the name is not in `m_allAudioEventInfo`. `newAudioEventInfo` (`:811-820`) is only for INI parse of new definitions, not the play path.

## Rust
Live `AudioManager::add_audio_event` (`game_audio.rs:706-708`) still returns `AHSV_ERROR` when info is missing. Leftover GameAudio facade `TheAudio::add_audio_event` / `get_audio_length_ms` (`helpers/audio.rs:397-405`, `:470-478`) calls `new_audio_event_info` on a miss, which inserts a blank SoundEffect (`game_audio.rs:1442-1472`: empty `sounds`, volume 0.5, `type_field` 0) and then plays it. Leftover GameLogic drawable `find_or_create_audio_event_info` (`drawable.rs:2958-2965`) does the same. Leftover INI `AudioEventRTS::play` (`ini_misc_audio.rs:139-141`) also fabricates.

Blank info: `sounds: Vec::new()`, `type_field: 0` (no player restriction → shouldPlayLocally true).

## Player-visible effect
Unknown leftover names (defaults like `crate_heal`, script/FX typos, template names not in SoundEffects.ini) get a real handle instead of AHSV_Error. Combined with leftover `is_currently_playing` (handle!=0), modules think the silent event is playing and never retry. The blank entry also occupies the live registry so a later real definition of the same name is not inserted (`new_audio_event_info` returns the existing blank).
close_reason: Leftover TheAudio::add_audio_event no longer invents blank AudioEventInfo; missing names return AHSV_Error like C++ AudioManager::addAudioEvent (GameAudio.cpp:391-396).

title: [WW3D Collision] AABTree AABox-tri collide is sweep-AABB vs tri-AABB, not SAT
description:
## C++
`AABTreeClass::Cast_AABox_To_Polys` (`aabtree.cpp:802+`) calls `CollisionMath::Collide(boxtest.Box, boxtest.Move, tri, boxtest.Result)` — the full AABox-tri swept SAT with fraction, StartBad, and contact normal.

`Cast_OBBox_To_Polys` uses `CollisionMath::Collide(OBBox, move, tri, 0, result)` similarly.

## Rust
`ww3d-collision/src/aabtree.rs` `aabox_triangle_collide` (330-369) is labeled "Simplified" / "would need a full SAT". It only tests whether the **sweep AABB** overlaps the **triangle AABB**. No SAT, no fraction, no StartBad, no normal. Any leaf whose swept volume's AABB touches a triangle's AABB reports a hit.

`collision_math.rs` `aabox_triangle_swept` (109-165), used by `aabtree_extended.rs` OBB casts, is a plane-only test: reject if moving away from the triangle normal, then ray-vs-plane from box center + 2D point-in-triangle. Misses edge hits, StartBad embedding, and all SAT axes. Unused expanded-vertex locals (`_expanded_tri_v*`).

## Evidence
C++ aabtree.cpp:834 Collide SAT.
Rust aabtree.rs:335-365 AABB-AABB; collision_math.rs:123-159 plane-only sweep.
aabtree_extended.rs:180 `obbox_triangle_swept`.

## Player-visible effect
If this AABTree path is used (ww3d-collision / physics / compat), box-casts false-hit whenever the swept volume's AABB comes near a triangle's AABB (including misses above/beside the actual surface) and miss real edge collisions. No usable contact fraction for sliding.

## Split hint
Call WWMath `collide_aabox_triangle` (once SAT is ported) from `aabox_triangle_collide`; replace plane-only `aabox_triangle_swept` with the same SAT.
close_reason: AABTree::aabox_triangle_collide now calls CollisionMath::aabox_triangle_swept (full SAT, fraction, StartBad, normal) instead of sweep-AABB vs tri-AABB. aabtree_extended cast_obbox_to_polys uses obbox_triangle_swept SAT.
