title: [InGameUI] SELECT_ALL is whole-map not screen-first
description:
## C++
InGameUI.cpp:4877 screen pass then map fallback. CommandXlat.cpp:2862-2900 excludes IGNORES_SELECT_ALL and 1.03 incompatible-deselect.

## Rust
selection.rs:1484 iterates ALL frame.objects. No screen region, no IGNORES_SELECT_ALL, no HUD message. Q and Ctrl+A.

## Player-visible
Q grabs the entire army including far-away units C++ would leave unselected.
close_reason: selection.rs SELECT_ALL is screen-first then map, excludes IGNORES_SELECT_ALL, HUD SelectedAcrossScreen/Map; crate select_all.rs same.

title: [Radar] tryEvent uses real distance instead of C++ precedence quirk
description:
## C++
Radar.cpp:1293-1294 distSquared uses operator precedence so the 250*250 close-enough check is effectively always false; same-type events throttle map-wide for 10s.

## Rust
try_event.rs:26-41 computes true dx*dx+dy*dy <= 62500. Host eva_camera.rs:206-221 same. Tests pin far-away events still fire.

## Player-visible
Rust allows a second UnderAttack ping 250wu away within 10s; C++ suppresses any same-type event anywhere on the map for 10s.
close_reason: tryEvent + eva_camera match C++ 250sq precedence quirk: same-type events throttle map-wide for 10s

title: [Partition] Value/threat cell map never stamped on live host
description:
## C++
Object.cpp:4765-4890 onPartitionCellChange stamps BuildCost/ThreatValue via doValueAffect/doThreatAffect. Consumers: getNearestGroupWithValue, getMostValuableLocation.

## Rust
Crate handle_value_map is dead on live. ShroudManager::do_value_affect has zero live callers. actions_skirmish.rs:456-468 reads zeros and attacks Coord3D::ZERO. set_units_should_hunt does no getMostValuableLocation.

## Player-visible
Attack-nearest-value scripts send teams to (0,0,0). Hunt mode never seeds the richest cluster.
close_reason: object pose/create/destroy + partition_manager.rs + production.rs: live host stamps doValueAffect/doThreatAffect on cell change; hunt queries getMostValuableLocation.

title: [Partition] Live ShroudGrid is 50wu not PartitionCellSize 40
description:
## C++
PartitionManager.cpp:2567 m_cellSize = GlobalData PartitionCellSize (retail 40). All shroud/threat/value quantize on that grid.

## Rust
shroud_manager.rs:63 SHROUD_GRID_CELL_SIZE=50. fow_rendering.rs:932 and wthree_d_shroud.rs:33 also 50. Distinct from closed 100wu partition-object grid.

## Player-visible
Spy-drone/radar/superweapon FOW reveals cover fewer cells and look blockier.
close_reason: shroud_manager.rs + wthree_d_shroud.rs + fow_rendering.rs + fow_terrain_overlay.rs: live ShroudGrid cell size is PartitionCellSize 40.

title: [FXList] FXList names fed to audio as sound events
description:
## C++
FXList.cpp:79-103 SoundFXNugget plays AudioEventRTS(m_soundName) — the name INSIDE the FXList.

## Rust
world_tick/ai.rs:322,339 queues AudioEventRequest(\"FX:{name}\"). apply.rs:770-775 uses the FXList template name as the audio event. process_audio_events forwards verbatim with no FXList lookup.

## Player-visible
Per-weapon C++ sounds defined inside FXList Sound nuggets never play even when audio hardware works.
close_reason: Stopped FX:{template} audio; process_audio_events and apply.rs resolve Sound nugget m_soundName via host_fx_list_dispatch + GameClient store.

title: [Player] is_playable_side is !observer not template PlayableSide
description:
## C++
Player.cpp:3929-3933 isPlayableSide = template->isPlayableSide(). Callers: scoreTheKill, TechBuilding CAPTURED, OCL color.

## Rust
economy.rs:4-6 is_playable_side = !is_observer. Common crate has the faithful version; live sim uses GameLogic.

## Player-visible
Civilian kills award score/XP. Tech buildings under civilian control show CAPTURED. OCL spawners tint with player color.
close_reason: GameLogic Player::is_playable_side uses template playable flag not !observer

title: [Camera] Player zoom is a 0.1-5.0 multiplier not C++ HAG +/-10
description:
## C++
LookAtXlat.cpp:341-348 wheel -> zoomIn/Out. View.cpp:104-112 setHeightAboveGround(HAG +/- 10). W3DView.cpp:1902-1927 clamps to GameData Min/MaxCameraHeight when zoomLimited.

## Rust
mouse.rs:946-958 camera_zoom -= delta*0.1 clamp (0.1, 5.0). KP8/KP2 same. GameData min/max height never bound player zoom.

## Player-visible
Wheel zoom can go far beyond retail MaxCameraHeight and closer than MinCameraHeight. Per-detent step is multiplicative not 10wu.
close_reason: Player zoom is HAG +/-10 clamped to GameData Min/MaxCameraHeight: View::zoom_in/out + set_height_above_ground (zoomLimited), host mouse wheel/KP8/KP2 apply_player_height_zoom_steps. view.rs + mouse.rs.

title: [Camera] Follow hard-snaps every frame with no followFactor or airborne yaw
description:
## C++
W3DView.cpp:1101-1124 followFactor ramps 0.05/frame. LOCK_FOLLOW airborne matches object yaw *0.1. Ground level from objpos.z.

## Rust
camera_drain.rs:149-152 center_camera_on(follow) overwrites target each frame. No ramp, no airborne yaw, no tether vs follow distinction.

## Player-visible
Follow is bolted from frame one. Following aircraft never swings behind them.
close_reason: Follow uses C++ followFactor ramp 0.05/frame and airborne yaw *0.1 (View::apply_camera_lock_one_frame + host apply_camera_follow_or_tether). view.rs + camera_drain.rs.

title: [Camera] Rotate-toward-object snapshots position instead of tracking
description:
## C++
W3DView.cpp:2432-2458 rotateCameraTowardObject trackObject=TRUE; :2973-3010 re-finds the object every frame and holds numHoldFrames.

## Rust
scripts_camera.rs:729-751 resolves object position once into a fixed CameraLookTowardWaypointRequest. hold_seconds dropped.

## Player-visible
Rotate-to-face-unit on a moving target aims at where it was when the script fired.
close_reason: rotate_camera_toward_object tracks object each frame with hold_seconds (script_action_handler + View). Host scripts_camera keeps script_look_toward_object_id and refreshes pending position.

title: [Camera] Script look-toward freezes to instant yaw snap
description:
## C++
W3DView.cpp:2460-2501 rotateCameraTowardPosition sets numFrames from milliseconds; :2951-3020 eases m_angle across those frames.

## Rust
PresentationFrame.camera_look_toward is Option<[f32;3]> only. build.rs:1657-1659 drops duration. camera_drain.rs:210-218 applies duration_seconds: 0.0 even though scripts_camera sets real durations.

## Player-visible
Rotate-camera-to-face scripts jump-cut instead of 1-3s eased rotates.
close_reason: Look-toward uses View::rotate_camera_toward_position with ms duration; PresentationFrame.camera_look_toward_duration no longer dropped; camera_drain applies real duration.

title: [Camera] Scripted move/path drops orient=true yaw to travel direction
description:
## C++
ScriptActions.cpp:782 doMoveCameraTo and :943 doCameraFollowWaypointPath hardcode orient=true. W3DView.cpp:2860-2893 setupWaypointPath computes cameraAngle per segment; :3156-3182 lerps m_angle every frame.

## Rust
script_camera.rs ScriptCameraMoveTo/PathMove have no angle field. scripts_camera.rs:1312-1352 update_script_camera only request_camera_focus(position). CAMERA_MOD_FREEZE_ANGLE is vacuous.

## Player-visible
Cinematic pans slide sideways at the old yaw instead of turning to face travel direction.
close_reason: orient=true move_camera_to uses waypoint path; path angles match setupWaypointPath (acos/dir, first=current, average middles). Host update_script_camera looks toward travel when not freeze_angle. view.rs + scripts_camera.rs + script_camera.rs.

title: [Camera] CAMERA_TETHER_NAMED is plain follow, no LOCK_TETHER play
description:
## C++
ScriptActions.cpp:4483-4497 doCameraTetherNamed setSnapMode(LOCK_TETHER, play). W3DView.cpp:1216-1244 drifts inside partitionCellSize, pulls halfway beyond.

## Rust
scripting/engine/types.rs:103-108 default camera_tether_object calls camera_follow_object and discards play. Main has no override. camera_drain.rs:149-152 instant re-center every frame.

## Player-visible
Tether scripts glue the unit to screen center with zero play radius.
close_reason: LOCK_TETHER: View::apply_camera_lock_one_frame partitionCellSize halfway pull + 0.01*play drift. Main camera_tether_object no longer discards play (CameraTetherRequest + camera_tether_play). camera_drain apply_camera_follow_or_tether.

title: [Pathfind] CLEAR_PATH residual is a straight-line walk not zone connectivity
description:
## C++
AIPathfind.cpp:8055-8101 clientSafeQuickDoesPathExistForUI is a zone-connectivity check (terrain-only, ignores structures). BuildAssistant.cpp:986-989 LBC_NO_CLEAR_PATH.

## Rust
ui_production.rs:632-666 quick_path_available_residual Bresenham-walks static-blocked cells. Extra 64wu short-circuit at 623-628. Live via builder_has_clear_path_to -> legal_build_code_at_for_builder.

## Player-visible
Placement rejected when a structure sits on the straight dozer-to-pad line even if a detour exists. Placement accepted across unconnected water because water is not static-blocked.
close_reason: pathfinding.rs + ui_production.rs: CLEAR_PATH uses terrain-zone connectivity (ignores structures, splits on water/cliff) matching clientSafeQuickDoesPathExistForUI.

title: [Pathfind] SetRallyPoint skips reachability gate and RallyPointNoPath
description:
## C++
GameLogicDispatch.cpp:117-157 doSetRallyPoint checks clientSafeQuickDoesPathExist. Failure: GUI:RallyPointNoPath + UnableToSetRallyPoint, does not set. Success: GUI:RallyPointSet + RallyPointSet sound.

## Rust
leftover.rs:706-725 execute_set_rally_point -> unit_commands.rs:880 sets rally unconditionally. No check, no message, no audio. Crate handler_build.rs:311-339 same.

## Player-visible
Rally points can be set on islands/cliffs. Produced units beeline toward impossible destinations.
close_reason: unit_commands.rs + handler_build.rs: SetRallyPoint gates on UI zone path; fail plays GUI:RallyPointNoPath + UnableToSetRallyPoint, success GUI:RallyPointSet + RallyPointSet.

title: [Physics] Stun freefall integrator hardcodes ground y=0
description:
## C++
PhysicsUpdate.cpp:749-755 groundZ = TheTerrainLogic->getLayerHeight (plus carrier deck). Slam/bounce/fall-damage/righting use that height.

## Rust
physics_motion.rs:792 tick_shock_stun_with_countdown uses `let ground_y = 0.0`. The later tick_physics_motion_step clamps to real terrain (step.rs:739 then :741), so the two passes fight on hills. maybe_kill_when_resting_on_ground uses absolute y>0.05.

## Player-visible
Stunned units jitter/sink on elevated terrain. Bounce/fall damage vs sea level. KillWhenRestingOnGround on hilltops never rest-dies.
close_reason: tick_shock_stun_all samples terrain_height_at into ground_height; stun integrator and maybe_kill_when_resting_on_ground use height-above-terrain

title: [Object] PreAttack does not stretch the drawable animation
description:
## C++
`Object::adjustModelConditionForWeaponStatus` (`Object.cpp:4763-4769`) when condition is WSF_PREATTACK: `m_drawable->setAnimationLoopDuration(preAttackDone - now)` so the pre-attack anim matches PreAttackDelay.

## Rust
`object_combat.rs:1654-1746` `adjust_model_condition_for_weapon_status` handles slot/condition/READY_TO_FIRE→BETWEEN but has no pre-attack branch, no `get_pre_attack_finished_frame`, no `set_animation_loop_duration`.

## Evidence
C++: `if (conditionToSet == WSF_PREATTACK) { ... setAnimationLoopDuration(preAttackDone - now); }`
Rust adjust_model_condition: no PREATTACK / set_animation_loop_duration.

## Player-visible effect
Launcher-raise / bomb-bay-open anims finish at default speed and pop back before the shot.

## Split hint
When setting PreAttack, stretch drawable loop duration to remaining pre-attack frames.
close_reason: adjust_model_condition PreAttack stretches drawable animation_loop_duration

title: [Object] FiringTracker spin-up never sets CONTINUOUS_FIRE model flags
description:
## C++
`FiringTracker::speedUp` / `coolDown` set/clear `MODELCONDITION_CONTINUOUS_FIRE_FAST/MEAN/SLOW` via `clearAndSetModelConditionFlags`.

## Rust
`helpers/object_helpers.rs` speed_up/cool_down start with empty `ModelConditionFlags` and call `clear_and_set_model_condition_flags(empty, empty)`. Weapon-bonus bits are toggled; drawable conditions are not.

## Evidence
C++: `set.set(MODELCONDITION_CONTINUOUS_FIRE_FAST); clr.set(MODELCONDITION_CONTINUOUS_FIRE_MEAN);`
Rust: `let clear = ModelConditionFlags::empty(); let set = ModelConditionFlags::empty();`

## Player-visible effect
Barrel-spin / sustained-fire poses never play or wind down.

## Split hint
Fill the same FAST/MEAN/SLOW flags C++ uses before the drawable call.
close_reason: FiringTracker speed_up/cool_down set CONTINUOUS_FIRE_FAST/MEAN/SLOW model flags

title: [Production] ParachuteContain ignores UseSpawnRallyPoint
description:
## C++
ParachuteContain.cpp:504-508: only if transportProducer->getObjectExitInterface()->useSpawnRallyPoint() does it call exitObjectViaDoor(rider, DOOR_1). DefaultProductionExitUpdate authors UseSpawnRallyPoint; most producers are No, so riders land and aiIdle.

## Rust
parachute_contain.rs:545-557 calls exit_object_via_door for any ExitInterface. ModuleExitInterface has no use_spawn_rally_point (DefaultProductionExitBehavior::use_spawn_rally_point exists but is not on the trait).

## Evidence
C++: if (exitInterface && exitInterface->useSpawnRallyPoint()) { exitObjectViaDoor(...); }
Rust: ungated exit_object_via_door(rider, Primary).

## Player-visible effect
Paradropped riders from ordinary factories teleport to UnitCreatePoint and walk the exit path (and can get SupplyCenter force-Wanting) instead of idling at the landing.

## Split hint
Add use_spawn_rally_point to ModuleExitInterface and gate ParachuteContain like C++.
close_reason: ExitInterface::use_spawn_rally_point added; DefaultProductionExit exposes INI flag; ParachuteContain only calls exit_object_via_door when the producer authored UseSpawnRallyPoint.

title: [Production] Repair dock heal skips attemptHealing side effects
description:
## C++
RepairDockUpdate::action (RepairDockUpdate.cpp:113-119) builds DamageInfo with DAMAGE_HEALING and calls body->attemptHealing. ActiveBody::attemptHealing applies armor DAMAGE_HEALING scale, records last healing, and notifies DamageModules onHealing. PoisonedBehavior::onHealing stops poison.

## Rust
Crate RepairDockUpdate::repair_unit (dock_update.rs:999) calls unit_guard.heal() which set_health / internal_change_health and bypasses armor and onHealing. ActiveBody::attempt_healing exists and is unused. Host SeekingRepair also uses Object::heal at a flat rate (see hq-4ksp).

## Evidence
C++: body->attemptHealing(&healingInfo) with m_damageType = DAMAGE_HEALING.
Rust: let _ = unit_guard.heal(self.health_to_add_per_frame);

## Player-visible effect
Repairing at a war factory / pad does not cure poison and ignores DAMAGE_HEALING armor.

## Split hint
Call attempt_healing with DamageType::Healing from both crate action and host SeekingRepair.
close_reason: RepairDockUpdate::repair_unit and drone heal now call Object::attempt_healing (DAMAGE_HEALING) instead of heal()/heal_completely().

title: [Object] BuildingLost EVA never plays: MP_COUNT_FOR_VICTORY KindOf unparsed
description:
## C++
`Object::onDie` (`Object.cpp:4597-4599`) plays `EVA_BuldingLost` when `isKindOf(KINDOF_STRUCTURE) && isKindOf(KINDOF_MP_COUNT_FOR_VICTORY)`. INI token is `MP_COUNT_FOR_VICTORY` (KindOf.cpp).

## Rust
`object_lifecycle.rs:956` tests `KindOf::CountsForVictory`. `kindof_from_name` maps `COUNTS_FOR_VICTORY` only, not `MP_COUNT_FOR_VICTORY`. Retail INI uses the MP_ token, so the bit is never set.

## Evidence
C++: `isKindOf(KINDOF_MP_COUNT_FOR_VICTORY)` / KindOf.cpp token `MP_COUNT_FOR_VICTORY`
Rust enums.rs: `COUNTS_FOR_VICTORY` only.

## Player-visible effect
Losing a command-center-class victory building never plays the Building Lost EVA. Victory-count consumers also miss the flag.

## Split hint
Alias MP_COUNT_FOR_VICTORY → CountsForVictory in kindof_from_name.
close_reason: kindof_from_name aliases MP_COUNT_FOR_VICTORY to CountsForVictory so BuildingLost EVA can fire

title: [Object] handle_death releases riders and sets DESTROYED too early
description:
## C++
`Object::onDie` does not clear the AI group or release contained objects. Riders die via contain Die modules. `OBJECT_STATUS_DESTROYED` is set later in `GameLogic::destroyObject`, so slow-death objects are not DESTROYED during the death animation.

## Rust
`object_lifecycle.rs` `handle_death` immediately `set_effectively_dead` + `status.set_status(Destroyed)`, then after `on_die` clears `group_id` and `release_object` on every contained id.

## Evidence
C++ destroyObject sets DESTROYED; onDie has no rider release.
Rust: `self.status.set_status(ObjectStatusTypes::Destroyed);` then `contain_guard.release_object(contained_id)`.

## Player-visible effect
Passengers walk out of a dying transport instead of dying with it. Scripts/status checks see DESTROYED for the whole slow-death window.

## Split hint
Leave DESTROYED to GameLogic::destroy_object; let contain Die modules handle riders.
close_reason: handle_death no longer sets DESTROYED or releases riders; destroyObject owns DESTROYED

title: [Object] Command-button extra validity gates drop hijack and no-target powers
description:
## C++
No-target `GUI_COMMAND_SPECIAL_POWER` always calls `doSpecialPower` even if the button needs an object target.
At-object hijack/carbomb/sabotage is unconditional `ai->aiEnter(obj)` (`Object.cpp:5593-5600`). `isValidObjectTarget` is relationship-only.

## Rust
No-target SpecialPower (`object_special_power.rs:234-240`) returns if options include NEED_TARGET_*_OBJECT.
Hijack/CarBomb/Sabotage (`457-467`) call `is_valid_command_target`, which also rejects destroyed / UnderConstruction / NEED_TARGET_PRISONER→is_captured, and defaults true when no relationship bits (C++ defaults false).

## Evidence
C++ hijack: `ai->aiEnter(obj, cmdSource); return;`
Rust: `if !self.is_valid_command_target(target, options) { return Ok(()); }`
C++ no-target SP: no option check. Rust: `if options.intersects(NEED_TARGET_*) { return Ok(()); }`

## Player-visible effect
Script firing an object-targeted power with no target does nothing. Hijack/carbomb/sabotage of under-construction or otherwise extra-invalid targets is silently dropped.

## Split hint
Remove the no-target SP option check; hijack arm should match C++ unconditional aiEnter.
close_reason: removed no-target NEED_TARGET_* gate; hijack/carbomb/sabotage is unconditional aiEnter

title: [Object] look/shroud use Team relationship instead of Player::getRelationship
description:
## C++
`Object::look` / `shroud` (`Object.cpp:4949-4958`, similar in shroud) build the player mask with `getControllingPlayer()->getRelationship(currentPlayer->getDefaultTeam())`. `Player::getRelationship(Team*)` (Player.cpp:542-569) is team-override → player-override → NEUTRAL, with no same-team-id shortcut. Reveal-to-all uses `ThePlayerList->getPlayersWithRelationship(..., ALLOW_ENEMIES|ALLOW_NEUTRAL)` which is the same helper.

## Rust
`object_vision.rs` look/shroud compare `controller.get_default_team()` vs each player's default team via `Team::get_relationship`, which short-circuits same team id to Allies and reads the *team's* override maps. The matching helper `Player::get_relationship_with_team` (`player/relations.rs`) exists and is unused here.

## Evidence
C++: `getControllingPlayer()->getRelationship(currentPlayer->getDefaultTeam()) == ALLIES`
Rust: `a_guard.get_relationship(&b_guard)` on default teams.

## Player-visible effect
Scripted diplomacy / shared-default-team setups share or hide fog incorrectly — allies may not see a unit's reveal, or enemies may.

## Split hint
Call get_relationship_with_team from look/shroud/reveal-to-all.
close_reason: object_vision.rs look/shroud/reveal-to-all use Player::get_relationship_with_team on each player's default team

title: [Object] Team switch does not apply prototype attack priority
description:
## C++
`Object::setOrRestoreTeam` (`Object.cpp:858-872`) after joining the new team: `ai->setAttitude(proto->getTemplateInfo()->m_initialTeamAttitude)` and if `proto->getAttackPriorityName()` is set, `ai->setAttackInfo(TheScriptEngine->getAttackInfo(name))`.

## Rust
`object_lifecycle.rs:702-734` `apply_team_ai_profile` only maps prototype attitude onto `set_attitude`. No attack-priority name lookup or `setAttackInfo`.

## Evidence
C++: `if (proto->getAttackPriorityName().isNotEmpty()) { ai->setAttackInfo(TheScriptEngine->getAttackInfo(name)); }`
Rust apply_team_ai_profile: attitude match only.

## Player-visible effect
Units transferred onto a scripted team ignore that team's AttackPriority list, so they pick the wrong targets (e.g. hunt infantry instead of the designated hero/building).

## Split hint
After set_attitude, resolve the prototype attack-priority name through ScriptEngine.
close_reason: Not a remaining gap: live AI hunt/attack paths call resolve_attack_priority_info_for_object (ai/mod.rs) which reads the team prototype AttackPriority name. set_or_restore_team attitude-only is OK.

title: [Object] xfer load does not remove the object from radar
description:
## C++
`Object::xfer` (`Object.cpp:4168-4173`) on load, if `m_radarData` is set, `TheRadar->removeObject(this)` before the radar chunk re-adds objects. Comment: radar reloads itself as a separate save chunk.

## Rust
`object_xfer.rs` has no radar remove on load (grep for radar/remove_object is empty). Field order after the closed xfer beads otherwise matches C++ v9.

## Evidence
C++: `if (xfer->getXferMode() == XFER_LOAD && m_radarData) TheRadar->removeObject(this);`
Rust object_xfer.rs: no radar call between team restore and geometry/sighting xfer.

## Player-visible effect
Loading a save can leave stale or duplicate radar blips until the next full radar rebuild.

## Split hint
One removeObject at the C++ site (after smcUntil, before experience tracker).
close_reason: object_xfer.rs: on load, if radar_data is set, TheRadar remove_object after smc_until and before experience tracker

title: [Object] onDie unit-lost radar event is not the C++ fake ping
description:
## C++
`Object::onDie` (`Object.cpp:4601-4605`) for locally controlled infantry/vehicle: EVA UnitLost then `TheRadar->tryEvent(RADAR_EVENT_FAKE, getPosition())` so spacebar jumps to the death. Separately `TheRadar->removeObject(this)` (`4569-4570`) so the blip disappears.

## Rust
`object_lifecycle.rs:913-920` pushes `RadarEventType::UnitDestroyed` for every death with a player. The EVA path (`984-990`) pushes another `UnitDestroyed`. No `RADAR_EVENT_FAKE`. No `TheRadar->removeObject`.

## Evidence
C++: `TheRadar->tryEvent(RADAR_EVENT_FAKE, getPosition());` + `TheRadar->removeObject(this);`
Rust: `RadarEventType::UnitDestroyed` only.

## Player-visible effect
Dead units may stay on radar. Spacebar does not jump to the last lost unit the way retail fake pings do.

## Split hint
removeObject on death; fake radar event only on the local infantry/vehicle EVA path.
close_reason: onDie removes radar object; local infantry/vehicle EVA path fires RADAR_EVENT_FAKE

title: [Object] Shockwave stun uses STUNNED instead of STUNNED_FLAILING
description:
## C++
`Object::attemptDamage` (`Object.cpp:1807-1834`) applies shock only if physics exists, not airborne, and not `KINDOF_PROJECTILE`. Sets `MODELCONDITION_STUNNED_FLAILING`.

## Rust
`object_combat.rs:1329-1366` applies shock when physics exists and not airborne, but does not exclude projectiles. Sets `ModelConditionFlags::STUNNED` (not STUNNED_FLAILING).

## Evidence
C++: `!isKindOf(KINDOF_PROJECTILE)` + `setModelConditionState(MODELCONDITION_STUNNED_FLAILING)`
Rust: no projectile kind check; `set_model_condition_state(ModelConditionFlags::STUNNED)`

## Player-visible effect
Shockwaved units play the generic stun pose instead of the flail. Projectiles can be shockwaved and go idle mid-air.

## Split hint
Match the C++ eligibility and model flag in attempt_damage_with_return.
close_reason: shockwave excludes KINDOF_PROJECTILE and sets STUNNED_FLAILING

title: [Object] onDie does not fade the terrain decal
description:
## C++
`Object::onDie` (`Object.cpp:4574-4575`) `draw->setTerrainDecalFadeTarget(0.0f, -0.03f)` so scar/decal under the corpse fades out.

## Rust
`object_lifecycle.rs:925-927` only `log::trace!("fading terrain decal")` inside `if let Some(_drawable)`.

## Evidence
C++: `if (draw) draw->setTerrainDecalFadeTarget(0.0f, -0.03f);`
Rust: unused `_drawable` + trace log.

## Player-visible effect
Building/unit ground decals stay at full strength after death.

## Split hint
Forward to Drawable terrain-decal fade from on_die.
close_reason: die_hooks.rs: drawable set_terrain_decal_fade_target(0.0, -0.03)

title: [WW3D] HLOD hidden BOUNDINGBOX OBBOX never updates animated bounds
description:
## C++
`HLodClass` stores `BoundingBoxIndex` (`hlod.h:227`). After construction it scans the highest LOD for a child whose name is `BOUNDINGBOX` and `Class_ID()==CLASSID_OBBOX` (`hlod.cpp:3280-3310`). `Get_Bounding_Sphere` / `Get_Bounding_Box` (`hlod.cpp:1304-1417`) then `Simple_Evaluate_Bone` that child's bone so the volume follows animation. `Render` skips `CLASSID_OBBOX` so the box is never drawn (`hlod.cpp:2029-2030`).

## Rust
Live Main never parses `W3D_CHUNK_BOX` and has no BOUNDINGBOX/OBBOX path (grep of `Main/src` is empty). HLOD bounds come from static mesh AABBs / bind-pose spheres. Library `ww3d-geometry` HLod has no BoundingBoxIndex field.

## Evidence
C++: `if (::stricmp(name, "BOUNDINGBOX") == 0) BoundingBoxIndex = index;` then `Simple_Evaluate_Bone(Lod[LodCount-1][BoundingBoxIndex].BoneIndex, &box_tm)`. Rust live collect uses mesh-local transforms only.

## Player-visible effect
Animated units keep bind-pose / mesh AABB for culling and screen-size. Fast-moving or stretched skinned poses get clipped too early or stay "visible" when the posed body has left the frustum; picking spheres do not follow the posed skeleton.
close_reason: HLod BoundingBoxIndex scan + posed OBBOX bounds (hlod_bounding_box.rs geometry+assets+Main); CLASSID_OBBOX skipped at render.

title: Object construction percent is 0-100 i32, C++ Real with CONSTRUCTION_COMPLETE=-1
description:
C++ BuildAssistant.h:25 `enum { CONSTRUCTION_COMPLETE = -1 }`; Object.h:376-377 `setConstructionPercent(Real)` / `getConstructionPercent()` returns the raw Real (Object.cpp:268 default -1). W3DModelDraw.cpp:2005-2009 applies the construction height sink only when `pct >= 0.0f`, so completed buildings (pct=-1) are not sunk. Selling drives percent below 0 to -50 (BuildAssistant.cpp:196,226).

Rust GameLogic Object stores `construction_percent: Real` but:
- `object/mod.rs` CONSTRUCTION_COMPLETE = 100.0 (not -1)
- `object_upgrade.rs` `get_construction_percent()` clamps to 0..100 and returns i32
- `set_construction_percent()` clamps to 0..100 so sell-down cannot go negative
- Common `build_assistant.rs` already has CONSTRUCTION_COMPLETE: i32 = -1 (inconsistent)

W3DModelDraw adjust_transform_mtx now matches C++ (`pct >= 0` then Translate_Z). The Object getter can never return -1, so the complete-sentinel skip is approximated by construction-state flags / dz=0 at 100%. Fractional dozer progress is quantized to integer percent.

Not fixed here: exclusive files are w3d_model_draw_impl only.

C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Include/Common/BuildAssistant.h:25, Object.h:376-377, W3DModelDraw.cpp:2005-2009
Rust: GameLogic/src/object/object_upgrade.rs get/set_construction_percent, object/mod.rs CONSTRUCTION_COMPLETE
close_reason: object/mod.rs CONSTRUCTION_COMPLETE=-1.0; object_upgrade.rs get/set raw unclamped Real, is_under_construction is pct>=0; auto_deposit_update/impl_dozer/worker callers no longer treat 100 as complete

title: [Physics] Carrier deck taxiing does not apply ground friction
description:
## C++
`applyFrictionalForces` (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:427-434): ground-friction branch if APPLY_FRICTION2D_WHEN_AIRBORNE || !isSignificantlyAboveTerrain() || deckTaxiing, where deckTaxiing = OBJECT_STATUS_DECK_HEIGHT_OFFSET && AI && curLocomotorSet == LOCOMOTORSET_TAXIING. Planes on a carrier deck therefore get 2D lateral/forward friction instead of aero drag.

## Rust
`apply_frictional_forces` (`physics_update.rs:609-611`) is only `APPLY_FRICTION2D_WHEN_AIRBORNE || !is_significantly_above_terrain()`. No deck-height-offset / TAXIING set check.

## Evidence
```
let apply_ground = state.has_flag(FLAG_APPLY_FRICTION2D_WHEN_AIRBORNE)
    || !obj.is_significantly_above_terrain();
```

## Player-visible effect
Aircraft taxiing on an aircraft-carrier deck keep airborne aero drag (or none) and slide as if flying. They cannot brake/turn on deck like C++.

## Split hint
One predicate next to apply_frictional_forces; no new file.
close_reason: apply_frictional_forces now treats deckTaxiing = DECK_HEIGHT_OFFSET && AI && LOCOMOTORSET_TAXIING as ground 2D friction, matching PhysicsUpdate.cpp:427-434.

title: [Physics] xfer flag bit values remapped vs C++ save format
description:
## C++
`PhysicsFlagsType` (PhysicsUpdate.h:220-235), comment \"written out in save/load xfer; don't change these numbers\":
STICK_TO_GROUND=0x0001, ALLOW_BOUNCE=0x0002, APPLY_FRICTION2D_WHEN_AIRBORNE=0x0004, UPDATE_EVER_RUN=0x0008, WAS_AIRBORNE_LAST_FRAME=0x0010, ALLOW_COLLIDE_FORCE=0x0020, ALLOW_TO_FALL=0x0040, HAS_PITCHROLLYAW=0x0080, IMMUNE_TO_FALLING_DAMAGE=0x0100, IS_IN_FREEFALL=0x0200, IS_IN_UPDATE=0x0400, IS_STUNNED=0x0800.
`xferInt(&m_flags)` in version 2 (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1858-1859).

## Rust
`physics_update.rs:52-62` remaps: FLAG_IS_IN_UPDATE=1<<0 (C++ STICK_TO_GROUND), FLAG_STICK_TO_GROUND=1<<6 (C++ ALLOW_TO_FALL), FLAG_ALLOW_BOUNCE=1<<8 (C++ IMMUNE_TO_FALLING_DAMAGE), FLAG_IS_STUNNED=1<<10 (C++ IS_IN_UPDATE). xfer writes this remapped int.

## Evidence
C++ STICK_TO_GROUND=0x0001. Rust FLAG_IS_IN_UPDATE = 1<<0. A retail save with stick-to-ground infantry loads as IS_IN_UPDATE.

## Player-visible effect
Save/load: infantry start catching air; bounce/stun/fall-damage-immune flags swap; wrecks freeze mid-update or never bounce.

## Split hint
Use the C++ hex values as named constants; do not pack a different order.
close_reason: Physics flags use C++ hex values (STICK_TO_GROUND=0x0001 ... IS_STUNNED=0x0800) including ALLOW_COLLIDE_FORCE=0x0020. xfer writes the C++ bit layout.

title: [Physics] getMass ignores contained cargo mass
description:
## C++
`PhysicsBehavior::getMass` (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1073-1080): `mass = m_mass + contain->getContainedItemsMass()`. Used by applyForce, friction, bounce, fall damage, collide push.

## Rust
`PhysicsBehaviorHandle::get_mass` (`physics_update.rs:379-381`) returns `self.state.mass` only. Friction and bounce use `state.mass` directly.

## Evidence
```
fn get_mass(&self) -> Real { self.state.mass }
```
No get_contained_items_mass call on the owner's contain module.

## Player-visible effect
Loaded transports/Chinooks/Overlord/Battle Bus are too light: they accelerate, bounce, and take fall damage as if empty. Crush/push forces (once collide is live) will also be wrong.

## Split hint
Keep get_mass on PhysicsBehavior; query contain through the object, no new module.
close_reason: get_mass / friction / bounce / fall damage / collide push add contain cargo via contained_items_mass (sum of contained physics get_mass), matching PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1073-1080.

title: [Locomotor] xfer flag bits remapped vs C++ LocoFlag
description:
## C++
`LocoFlag` (Locomotor.h:395-407), saved as `xferUnsignedInt(m_flags)` version 2. Bits are `1<<enum` in declaration order: IS_BRAKING=0x1, ALLOW_INVALID=0x2, MAINTAIN_POS=0x4, PRECISE_Z=0x8, NO_SLOW_DOWN=0x10, OVER_WATER=0x20, ULTRA_ACCURATE=0x40, MOVING_BACKWARDS=0x80, THREE_POINT=0x100, CLIMBING=0x200, CLOSE_ENOUGH_3D=0x400, OFFSET_INCREASING=0x800.

## Rust
`locomotor.rs:51-64` skips OVER_WATER in the sequence: ULTRA_ACCURATE=0x20 (C++ OVER_WATER), CLOSE_ENOUGH_3D=0x40 (C++ ULTRA_ACCURATE), OVER_WATER=0x400 (C++ CLOSE_ENOUGH_3D), plus extra FLAG_SLIDING_INTO_PLACE=0x1000.

## Evidence
C++ OVER_WATER is bit 5 (0x20). Rust FLAG_ULTRA_ACCURATE = 0x20. Save/load swaps ultra-accurate with over-water and close-enough-3D with over-water.

## Player-visible effect
Loaded saves: hovercraft water state becomes ultra-accurate (or vice versa); 3D close-enough and climbing flags misread. Jets land imprecise; infantry wander offset direction flips.

## Split hint
Use a C++-identical bit enum; drop FLAG_SLIDING_INTO_PLACE from the saved word.
close_reason: GameLogic locomotor: C++-matching flags/defaults/INI bridge/dispatcher/motive/Z/thrust/hover/upgrade

title: [Production] Supply-center cash skips ScoreKeeper addMoneyEarned
description:
## C++
`SupplyCenterDockUpdate::action` (`SupplyCenterDockUpdate.cpp:77-89`):
`while (loseOneBox()) value += ownerPlayer->getSupplyBoxValue();` then `value += getUpgradedSupplyBoost();` then `Money::deposit(value)` **and** `ownerPlayer->getScoreKeeper()->addMoneyEarned(value)`.

## Rust
Crate `SupplyCenterDockUpdate::action` (`dock_update.rs:1417-1430`) deposits via `get_money_mut().deposit(value)` only — no `add_money_earned` / ScoreKeeper.
Host live deposit (`support_states.rs:3600-3604`) uses `credit_supplies` which increments `statistics.resources_collected` (`player.rs:666-672`) but **not** `add_money_earned` (`player.rs:615-620`, the ScoreKeeper residual).

## Evidence
C++: `ownerPlayerMoney->deposit(value); ownerPlayer->getScoreKeeper()->addMoneyEarned(value);`
Crate: deposit only.
Host: `credit_supplies` → `resources_collected` + `apply_supply_gain`, no `money_earned`.

## Player-visible effect
Skirmish/campaign score and money-earned stats ignore supply-drop cash. Rank/score screens under-count GLA/USA/China gather income.

## Split hint
Call `add_money_earned` next to `deposit` / `credit_supplies` in both crate action and host deposit.
close_reason: SupplyCenterDockUpdate::action calls get_score_keeper_mut().add_money_earned(value) next to deposit.

title: [Production] ProductionUpdate xfer is not C++ v1 layout
description:
## C++
`ProductionUpdate::xfer` (`ProductionUpdate.cpp:1203-1372`) version 1:
`xferVersion` → base UpdateModule → `UnsignedShort` count → per entry (`ProductionType` user, AsciiString name, ProductionID user, Real percent, Int frames, Int qtyTotal, Int qtyProduced, Int exitDoor) → uniqueID → productionCount → constructionCompleteFrame → `DoorInfo[DOOR_COUNT_MAX]` blob → clearFlags → setFlags → flagsDirty.

## Rust
Live `ProductionUpdateComplete::xfer` (`production_update_complete.rs:1399-1473`) writes `u32` version, queue_len as u16 of **queued-only** entries (current production is a following bool + extra qty/door), then unique_id, construction_complete_frame, **current_door**, **production_enabled**, **last_update_frame**, then per-door fields. `xfer_build_queue_entry` adds priority/cost/build_time/time_spent/player_id/is_repeat/queue_index that C++ never saved. Missing `m_productionCount`, `m_clearFlags`/`m_setFlags`/`m_flagsDirty`. CRC uses a dummy u8 version.

## Evidence
C++ entry: type, name, productionID, percentComplete, framesUnderConstruction, qtyTotal, qtyProduced, exitDoor.
Rust entry: type, name, priority, cost, build_time, time_spent, player_id, is_repeat, production_id, queue_index.

## Player-visible effect
Retail `.sav` production queues (in-progress Red Guards, doors mid-open, unique ProductionID) cannot round-trip through the live crate module. Reloaded factories lose progress, door art, or cancel identity.

## Split hint
Match C++ field order exactly; keep host bincode migration (`hq-ddv`) separate from this Xfer block.
close_reason: ProductionUpdateComplete::xfer matches C++ v1: version, UpdateModule base, u16 count, per-entry type/name/id/percent/frames/qty/door, uniqueID, productionCount, constructionCompleteFrame, DoorInfo[4], clear/set flags, flagsDirty.

title: [Assets] iniCRC hashes GameData.ini only, not the full GameEngine init table
description:
## C++
`GameEngine::init` (`GameEngine.cpp:314-530`) opens `XferCRC xferCRC` and passes `&xferCRC` into every `initSubsystem` INI load (GameData, Science, Multiplayer, Terrain, Roads, Rank, PlayerTemplate, FXList, Weapon, OCL, Locomotor, SpecialPower, DamageFX, Armor, Object dir, Upgrade, AI, Crate, plus Water/Weather `ini.load`). `xferCRC.close(); TheWritableGlobalData->m_iniCRC = xferCRC.getCRC()`. That CRC is the retail INI identity for MP/replay compatibility.

## Rust
`config/global_data.rs:753-803` `calculate_xfer_crc` only loads `Data/INI/Default/GameData.ini`, `Data/INI/GameData.ini`, and debug `GameDataDebug.ini`. Live boot later parses Science/Rank/Weapon/Object/etc. **without** that XferCRC (`shell.rs` `extract_ini_text_from_archives` + `INI::parse_current_file`). Comment claims C++ 314-530 parity but the path list is GameData-only.

## Evidence
C++: one XferCRC spanning the whole initSubsystem table.
Rust: `let ini_paths = [\"Data/INI/Default/GameData.ini\", \"Data/INI/GameData.ini\", ...];` then `self.global_data.ini_crc = self.calculate_xfer_crc()`.

## Player-visible effect
`m_iniCRC` / replay-or-MP INI mismatch checks cannot see Weapon/Object/Upgrade/AI changes. Two clients with different Object.ini but the same GameData.ini look compatible; retail would refuse the session.

## Split hint
Thread one XferCRC through the live boot INI worker (same files/order as GameEngine.cpp), then store it on GlobalData.
close_reason: ini_crc_boot.rs hashes the full GameEngine.cpp initSubsystem table (GameData/Water/Weather/Science/MP/Terrain/Roads/Rank/PlayerTemplate/FXList/Weapon/OCL/Locomotor/SpecialPower/DamageFX/Armor/Object dir/Upgrade/AI/Crate) plus debug GameData. Boot worker and ConfigurationSystem::calculate_xfer_crc both use it and publish m_iniCRC.

title: [Xfer] GameLogic::xfer CampaignManager snapshot is dummy-written and discarded on load
description:
## C++
GameLogic::xfer (GameLogic.cpp:4790) always xferSnapshot(TheCampaignManager) after the object list. CampaignManager::xfer persists current campaign/mission/rank/difficulty/challenge/generals template into the GameLogic chunk (in addition to CHUNK_Campaign).

## Rust
xfer_game_logic_state (xfer_helpers.rs:386) calls xfer_campaign_manager_snapshot (xfer_helpers.rs:438-471). That helper writes CampaignManager v5 layout (version, campaign, mission, rank, difficulty, challenge map/template, generals template) into local Strings/ints and then `let _ = (campaign, mission);` — it never reads or writes TheCampaignManager. On save the strings are empty; on load C++ bytes are consumed and thrown away.

## Evidence
xfer_helpers.rs:444-470 local campaign/mission vars, then `let _ = (campaign, mission);`.
C++ GameLogic.cpp:4790 `xfer->xferSnapshot( TheCampaignManager );`

## Player-visible effect
A Rust-written GameLogic chunk stores empty campaign/mission. Loading that save in C++ lets GameLogic::xfer overwrite TheCampaignManager after CHUNK_Campaign, wiping campaign side/mission/rank. Restart-mission / next-mission / generals selection after load can reset. Same-engine Rust load still works only because CHUNK_Campaign is applied and this helper does not overwrite it.
close_reason: GameLogic chunk xfers live CampaignManager via Common capture/apply hooks

title: Live named timers never reach InGameUI postDraw
description:
## Why
C++ ScriptActions::doAddNamedTimer / doDisplayCountdownTimer calls TheInGameUI->addNamedTimer; postDraw (InGameUI.cpp:3699-3784) reads TheScriptEngine->getCounter, formats mm:ss, and DisplayString::draw.

## Gap
Live host drains NamedTimerMutation into:
- GameLogic.script_named_timers: HashMap<String,(String,bool)> (no remaining frames)
- script_action_handler::script_add_named_timer (same tuple, private ScriptUiState)
- PresentationFrame / GameUIState.named_timers as Vec<(String,String,bool)>

None of those call GameClient InGameUI::add_named_timer / update_named_timers / draw_named_timers. HUD never formats remaining frames as m:ss or draws them.

Crate leftover.rs now ticks remaining frames, formats m:ss, and can draw when InGameUI is used. Live production path does not use it.

## Cite
- GeneralsMD InGameUI.cpp:709-727 addNamedTimer, 3699-3784 postDraw
- GeneralsMD ScriptActions.cpp:4021-4063
- GeneralsRust Main world_scripts/scripts_camera.rs drain_named_timer_mutations
- GeneralsRust GameClient core/script_action_handler.rs:264-281
close_reason: script_add_named_timer calls live InGameUI add_named_timer; postDraw formats remaining frames as m:ss and draws them (live_hud.rs, script_action_handler.rs, impl_draw.rs).

title: [AI States] Guard onExit never clears guard target type
description:
## C++
`AIGuardState::onExit` (AIStates.cpp:6698-6704) deletes the nested `AIGuardMachine` and then `obj->getAI()->clearGuardTargetType()`. That pops the guard-target stack (`GUARDTARGET_LOCATION`/`OBJECT`/`AREA` → `NONE`) so a later idle/attack is not treated as still guarding.

## Rust
Live `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/states/guard.rs` `AIGuardState::classic_on_exit` (184-188) only `halt()`s the nested machine. `UnitAIUpdate::clear_guard_target_type` exists (`object/unit/ai_core.rs:253`) but no state onExit calls it. Guard-retaliate and tunnel-network onExit have the same omission (C++ TN/retaliate also clear on their machines; main `AIGuardState` is the one that always clears the AIUpdate stack).

## Evidence
C++: `obj->getAI()->clearGuardTargetType();`
Rust guard.rs:184-188: take/halt only.

## Player-visible effect
After leaving Guard (stop, new move, death cleanup), `getGuardTargetType()` still reports a location/object/area. Follow-up AI (auto-acquire, “is guarding?” UI/scripts, stacking a new guard) behaves as if the unit is still on the old guard order.

## Split hint
Call `clear_guard_target_type` from `AIGuardState::classic_on_exit` (and TN/retaliate if their C++ counterparts clear).
close_reason: guard.rs: AIGuard/Retaliate/TN onExit halt nested machine then clear_guard_target_type (C++ obj->getAI()->clearGuardTargetType).

title: [AI States] Face xfer omits canTurnInPlace
description:
## C++
`AIFaceState::xfer` (AIStates.cpp:7379-7387) version 1 writes `m_canTurnInPlace` (set in `onEnter` from `locomotor->getMinSpeed()==0`). After load, `update` still uses that cached flag to choose `setLocomotorGoalOrientation` vs `setLocomotorGoalPositionExplicit`.

## Rust
Live `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/states/face.rs` `AIFaceObjectState` / `AIFacePositionState` store `can_turn_in_place` but have no `Snapshotable` / xfer of that field (`StateImplementation::xfer_snapshot` is not implemented; only enter/update/exit). Mid-face save/load re-defaults the flag to `false`.

## Evidence
C++: `xfer->xferBool(&m_canTurnInPlace);`
Rust face.rs structs: `can_turn_in_place: bool` with no xfer impl.

## Player-visible effect
Loading a save while a unit is facing (scripted face, deploy align) treats turn-in-place locos as drive-to-point: infantry/vehicles that should spin in place instead roll forward to the target, or vice versa after the first post-load update.

## Split hint
Add versioned xfer on both face states matching C++ field order (version, bool).
close_reason: face.rs: AIFaceObject/Position Snapshotable xfer version 1 + can_turn_in_place, matching C++ AIFaceState::xfer m_canTurnInPlace.

title: [Weapon] loadAmmoNow skips reloadWithBonus scatter-target rebuild
description:
## C++
`Weapon.cpp` `loadAmmoNow` (1820-1824) is `computeBonus` + `reloadWithBonus(..., loadInstantly=true)`. That path refills ammo, sets RELOADING_CLIP with zero delay, shares reload if needed, and `rebuildScatterTargets()` so a brand-new clip has the full unused scatter index list.

## Rust
Live `weapon_instance.rs` `load_ammo_now` (615-618) only sets `ammo_in_clip` and `ReadyToFire`. It does not call `reload_with_bonus`, does not rebuild `scatter_targets_unused`, and is what `WeaponSet::switch_weapon_template_set` uses for every new slot (weapon_set.rs:579-580), matching C++ updateWeaponSet's loadAmmoNow.

## Evidence
```
self.ammo_in_clip = ammo_count_for_clip_size(self.template.clip_size);
self.status = WeaponStatus::ReadyToFire;
Ok(())
```
weapon_instance.rs:616-618. rebuild_scatter_targets only runs from reload_with_bonus (675).

## Player-visible effect
New units and weapon-set swaps (veteran/upgrade) fire their first clip of a ScatterTarget-pattern weapon as a single unpatterned shot (or radius scatter only) until a real clip reload rebuilds the list.

## Split hint
Make load_ammo_now a one-liner through reload_with_bonus(instant).
close_reason: load_ammo_now is compute_bonus + reload_with_bonus(instant), which rebuilds scatter_targets_unused like C++ reloadWithBonus.

title: Crate OCLSpecialPower::doSpecialPower creates owner (createOwner=true)
description:
## Why
C++ no-target OCL fire passes createOwner=false so DeliverPayload reuses the firing object as the transport. The crate no-target path calls the angle create API (createOwner default true) and would spawn a duplicate cargo plane.

## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/SpecialPower/OCLSpecialPower.cpp:210-223`
```
SpecialPowerModule::doSpecialPowerAtLocation(&creationCoord, INVALID_ANGLE, commandOptions);
ObjectCreationList::create(ocl, getObject(), &creationCoord, &creationCoord, false);
```
The Bool overload is createOwner (`ObjectCreationList.h` create(..., Bool createOwner, ...)). DeliverPayloadNugget honors it: createOwner=false uses the primary object instead of `newObject(transport)`.

`USE_OWNER_OBJECT` location path (183-186) also passes createOwner=false (with angle).

## Rust
`GameLogic/src/object/special_powers/ocl_special_power.rs:361-395` `do_special_power`:
```
ocl.create_with_angle(&ctx, Some(&*owner_guard), &pos, &pos, 0.0, 0);
```
That is the angle createInternal (C++ 1524), not the owner-flag createInternal (1509). Location USE_OWNER_OBJECT correctly uses `create_with_angle_and_owner_flag(..., false, ...)` (297-306).

Live host `execute_ocl_special_power` always `create_object` a new transport — same createOwner=true mistake if a no-target / USE_OWNER_OBJECT OCL is fired there.

## Player-visible
Script/no-click OCL (and USE_OWNER_OBJECT sneak-style lists) spawn an extra deliverer instead of launching from the source object.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Crate do_special_power calls create_with_owner_flag(..., false) matching C++ false
- [ ] Live host USE_OWNER_OBJECT / no-target OCL does not spawn a second transport
close_reason: ocl_special_power.rs do_special_power now calls create_with_owner_flag(..., false); live execute_ocl_special_power skips a second transport when create_owner=false (USE_OWNER_OBJECT / execute_ocl_special_power_no_target).

title: Crate SpyVisionUpdate marks active before owner lookup; SpecialPower extra fire paths
description:
## Why
C++ SpyVisionUpdate only sets m_currentlyActive after a valid player list/owner, and SpyVisionSpecialPower only overrides doSpecialPower. The crate sets currently_active first (failed activate still looks on), only caps duration when MaxDuration>0, and also activates from at-object/at-location dispatch.

## C++
`SpyVisionUpdate.cpp:170-185` `doActivationWork`:
- if `playerToSetFor == NULL || ThePlayerList == NULL` return (m_currentlyActive unchanged)
- enemy players: `setUnitsVisionSpied(setting, m_spyOnKindof, playerIndex)`
- then `m_currentlyActive = setting`

`SpyVisionUpdate.h:31-38` default: NeedsUpgrade/SelfPowered false; durations 0; `m_spyOnKindof = KINDOFMASK_NONE; flip()` (all kinds).

`SpyVisionSpecialPower.cpp:64-103` only `doSpecialPower`: disabled; base `SpecialPowerModule::doSpecialPower`; duration = base + containCount*bonus; **always** `if (duration > m_maxDurationInFrames) duration = max` (max default 0, so a contain module with bonus and unset MaxDuration collapses to 0); findUpdateModule("SpyVisionUpdate"); `activateSpyVision(duration)` (duration 0 → deactivateFrame UINT_MAX / forever).

No doSpecialPowerAtObject/AtLocation override.

## Rust
`GameLogic/src/object/update/spy_vision_update.rs:174-188` `do_activation_work_for_current_owner`:
```
self.currently_active = setting;
let Some(spying_player_id) = OBJECT_REGISTRY.with_object(...) else { return; };
```
Empty dual-world / missing owner still latches currently_active. Wave 434 empty-registry then returns without setUnitsVisionSpied.

`spy_vision_special_power.rs:141-145`: cap only if `max_duration_in_frames > 0`.
`193-211`: `dispatch_do_special_power_at_object` / `_at_location` also call `do_special_power` (C++ would only run the base recharge/view-object path).

Live CIA residual (`host_cia_intelligence.rs` / `activate_cia_intelligence`) does duration math with captured_count but is not full SpyVisionUpdate (no kindof mux, no duration==0 forever, no onCapture flip, no sabotage setDisabledUntilFrame on the module).

## Player-visible
Failed/empty-world activate still thinks spy vision is on (no deactivate). Location/object command on a SpyVision module would start a second vision-spy. Unset MaxDuration + contain bonus lasts forever in Rust and 0 frames in C++.

## Acceptance
- [ ] currently_active assigned only after player/list checks succeed
- [ ] SpyVisionSpecialPower only activates from doSpecialPower (not at-object/at-location)
- [ ] Duration cap matches C++ (`duration = max` whenever duration > max, including max==0)
close_reason: spy_vision_update.rs: currently_active set only after player/list checks succeed. spy_vision_special_power.rs: only doSpecialPower activates (at-object/at-location are base-only); duration cap applies whenever duration > max including MaxDuration==0.

title: [GameClient] Skirmish map preview never places supply/tech icons or MapSelectorTooltip
description:
## C++
`SkirmishGameOptionsMenu.cpp`:
- `InitSkirmishGameGadgets` sets `windowMap->winSetTooltipFunc(MapSelectorTooltip)` (1084)
- `positionStartSpots` always calls `positionAdditionalImages` (715, 753)
- `positionAdditionalImages` (631-691) fills `TheSupplyAndTechImageLocations` from `MapMetaData::m_supplyPositions` / `m_techPositions` in map-window space (`SUPPLY_TECH_SIZE`)
- `MapSelectorTooltip` (527-574) hit-tests those lists so hovering a depot/tech building on the preview shows the retail tooltip

Draw of those lists is the shared map-window overlay used by skirmish/LAN/WOL setup.

## Rust
Live `update_map_preview` (`skirmish_game_options_menu.rs:267-283`) only sets the preview image, start-spot buttons, and map name. Grep of GameClient finds no `positionAdditionalImages`, `TheSupplyAndTechImageLocations`, `MapSelectorTooltip`, or `supply_pos_list`.

## Evidence
C++ 527-574, 631-691, 1084. Rust 267-283.

## Player-visible effect
Skirmish (and shared LAN/WOL setup preview) map window never shows supply-crate / tech-building markers and hovering the preview never names those sites.

## Not a dupe
Existing "supply" beads are collector economy / KindOf, not this menu overlay. No MapSelectorTooltip bead.
close_reason: skirmish_map_preview.rs + skirmish_game_options_menu.rs: position_additional_images fills TheSupplyAndTechImageLocations from MapMetaData supply/tech positions (SUPPLY_TECH_SIZE); MapWindow winSetTooltipFunc MapSelectorTooltip hit-tests those lists; update_map_preview always calls it

title: [GameClient] MainMenu Online leftover never startOnline-pushes GameSpyLoginProfile.wnd
description:
## C++
MainMenu ButtonOnline (`MainMenu.cpp:1444-1456`) calls `StartPatchCheck()`. `MainMenuUtils.cpp` `startOnline` (157-226) after the HTTP/DNS/patch countdown: tears down the cancel window, optionally prompts for patches, then `signalUIInteract(SHELL_SCRIPT_HOOK_MAIN_MENU_ONLINE_SELECTED)`, `SetUpGameSpy`, and `TheShell->push(\"Menus/GameSpyLoginProfile.wnd\")` (or Quick login if ALLOW_NON_PROFILED_LOGIN).

Every MainMenu frame also runs `HTTPThinkWrapper()` + `GameSpyUpdateOverlays()` (`MainMenu.cpp:907-908`).

## Rust
Live `handle_button_selected` queues `StartPatchCheck` (`shell/main_menu.rs:1696-1707`). `start_patch_check` (1268-1276) only sets `checking_for_patch_before_gamespy` / `checks_left_before_online=4`. `http_think_wrapper` (2314-2332) decrements the counter then `finish_online_handoff_state` (2299-2311) only signals the shell hook and logs. No `SetUpGameSpy`, no `TheShell->push(\"Menus/GameSpyLoginProfile.wnd\")`.

WOL/GameSpy *callbacks* exist and compile (`online_ui` default; hq-iy1a closed) but this leftover MainMenu Online path never opens them.

## Evidence
C++ MainMenuUtils.cpp:157-226. Rust main_menu.rs:1268-1276, 2299-2332.

## Player-visible effect
Clicking Online on the live MainMenu counts down internally and never presents GameSpyLoginProfile / WOL welcome. Online is leftover UI with no login screen.

## Not a dupe
`hq-ae2b` (closed) was GameNetwork `connect_to_gamespy` simulate comments, not this GameClient handoff. No GameSpyLogin / startOnline bead. Do not redesign GameNetwork.
close_reason: main_menu_online.rs + shell/main_menu.rs: after patch countdown start_online tears down cancel state, signals SHELL_SCRIPT_HOOK_MAIN_MENU_ONLINE_SELECTED, SetUpGameSpy, TheShell->push Menus/GameSpyLoginProfile.wnd (or StartDownloadingPatches if queue nonempty)

title: [Physics] handleBounce never calls testStunnedUnitForDestruction
description:
## C++
PhysicsBehavior::handleBounce (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:481-531): on successful upward bounce (`bounceForce.z > 0`) calls testStunnedUnitForDestruction() (:517) then returns true.
testStunnedUnitForDestruction (:1753+): if IS_STUNNED, kill when upside-down, off-map, cliff without cliff locomotor, or underwater without water locomotor.

## Rust
physics_update.rs handle_bounce (:646-676): applies YPR damping 0.7 and returns Some(bounce_force) when z>0. No test_stunned_unit_for_destruction call. Host Object::test_stunned_unit_for_destruction exists on physics_motion.rs residual but crate PhysicsBehaviorUpdate::update_simple bounce path does not invoke it.

## Effect
Stunned vehicles that bounce (shock/EMP tumble) survive upside-down / cliff / water landings that C++ destroys.
close_reason: handleBounce now calls testStunnedUnitForDestruction when bounceForce.z>0 (physics_bounce.rs): stunned + upside-down / off-map / cliff-without-loco / water-without-loco kills.

title: [Physics] applyFrictionalForces omits C++ deck-taxiing ground friction
description:
## C++
PhysicsBehavior::applyFrictionalForces (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:427-476):
`deckTaxiing = OBJECT_STATUS_DECK_HEIGHT_OFFSET && getAI() && getCurLocomotorSetType()==LOCOMOTORSET_TAXIING`
Ground 2D friction applies if APPLY_FRICTION2D_WHEN_AIRBORNE || !isSignificantlyAboveTerrain() || deckTaxiing.

## Rust
physics_update.rs apply_frictional_forces (:609-643):
`apply_ground = FLAG_APPLY_FRICTION2D_WHEN_AIRBORNE || !obj.is_significantly_above_terrain()`
No DECK_HEIGHT_OFFSET / LOCOMOTORSET_TAXIING test. Aircraft on a carrier deck that are still “above terrain” by deck height get aero friction instead of taxi 2D friction.

## Effect
Carrier-deck taxi (and any deck-height-offset ground roll) slides as if airborne. Crate update_simple does add deck height to ground_z for clamp (:772-774) but friction still uses the airborne branch.
close_reason: Same deck-taxiing predicate as hq-45zk in apply_frictional_forces: DECK_HEIGHT_OFFSET && AI && TAXIING applies ground 2D friction instead of aero.

title: [Pathfind] Live PathfindingGrid::grid_to_world always emits Y=0 (no terrain/layer Z)
description:
## C++
PathNode positions include terrain/layer height. Pathfinder::worldToGrid uses REAL_TO_INT on X/Y; node Z comes from TerrainLogic::getLayerHeight / layer.

## Rust
Main pathfinding.rs PathfindingGrid::grid_to_world (:230-236):
`Vec3::new(origin.x + x*size, 0.0, origin.z + y*size)`
find_path comment (:942-945) then lerps start.y→goal.y so followers do not dive to Y=0 — invented residual, not C++ layer height.

## Effect
Waypoint Z is never the ground/bridge/wall layer. Aircraft/hover preferred-height and ground-hug paths start from a flat plane. world_to_grid truncate (hq-i1ut) is already fixed; this is the inverse mapping.
close_reason: GameLogic GridCoord::to_world, Pathfinder::grid_to_world, and path.rs grid_to_world sample TerrainLogic::getLayerHeight instead of emitting Y=0.

title: [GameClient] Skirmish honors ListboxInfo is a text checklist, not C++ InsertBattleHonor medals

close_reason: skirmish_battle_honor_display.rs: populateSkirmishBattleHonors binds BattleHonorTooltip then InsertBattleHonor image rows (China/GLA/USA Gold/Silver/Bronze via get*CampaignComplete, Challenge MAX_GLOBAL_GENERAL_TYPES, Endurance official MP maps, Blitz 5/10, streak 3/10/25/100/500/1000, domination 100/500/1000/10000, Ultimate brutal AI all official MP, Officers Club Preorder)

title: [FXList] fxlist_integration execute_fx_pos has no CELLSHROUD_CLEAR gate

The parallel play path GameClient/src/effects/fxlist_integration.rs execute_fx_pos / execute_fx_obj (lines ~484-516) still iterates nuggets with no shroud check, so Sound/Particle/Tracer via that store can leak in unexplored cells.

Not the crate FXListManagerBridge live path; still a second play API.

title: [GameLogic] Partition range queries use 3D center distance, not DistanceCalculationType
description:
## C++
`PartitionManager::getClosestObjects` (`PartitionManager.cpp:3172-3207`) takes `DistanceCalculationType dc` and dispatches `theDistCalcProcs[dc]`: FROM_CENTER_2D / FROM_CENTER_3D / FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_2D / FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_3D. Bounding-sphere variants subtract each object's 2D/3D radius before comparing to maxDist. Most AI/weapon/iterateObjectsInRange callers use 2D or bounding-sphere 2D.

## Rust
Crate `partition_manager.rs` `find_objects_in_radius` (417-473) always does 3D center-to-center:
```
let dz = partition_obj.position.z - center.z;
let dist_sqr = dx*dx + dy*dy + dz*dz;
if dist_sqr <= radius_sqr { ... }
```
No `DistanceCalculationType`, no radius subtract. `find_closest_objects` (476-500) sorts that same 3D center distance. Live host `ids_in_radius` is cell-ring only (XZ), still center-based, no bounding-sphere subtract.

## Evidence
C++ `DistCalcProc distProc = theDistCalcProcs[dc]` vs Rust hardcoded 3D center. HUGE_DIST crate const is also `1e10` vs C++ `1000000.0f` (`PartitionManager.h:45`).

## Player-visible effect
Acquire/weapon/iterate-in-range on the crate path treats flying/high objects as farther than retail 2D, and misses units whose bounding circles overlap the radius but whose centers do not. AI vision and closest-enemy picks diverge from ZH.
close_reason: find_objects_in_radius_dc uses DistanceCalculationType (default FromCenter2D) via partition_distance::within_radius.

title: [GameLogic] Collide tests drop orientation; live uses selection-radius spheres
description:
## C++
`PartitionData::collidesWith` / `PartitionManager::geomCollidesWithGeom` (`PartitionManager.cpp:1964-1993`) build `CollideInfo(pos, geom, angle)` with **object orientation** and dispatch `theCollideTestProcs` (sphere/cylinder/box matrix). Box vs box uses rotated rectangles.

## Rust
Crate `collision_system.rs` (201-202) and `partition_manager.rs` `test_collision_between` (550-551) always pass `angle = 0.0`. `PartitionObject` does not store orientation. Live host `try_physics_collide` (`world_tick/physics.rs:582-585`) uses XZ `selection_radius` spheres, not GeometryInfo + angle.

(`geom_collides_with_geom` in crate partition_manager.rs:1490 does take angles, but the live contact path never feeds them.)

## Evidence
C++ CollideInfo angle from `object->getOrientation()`. Rust contact path hardcodes 0. Host: selection_radius spheres.

## Player-visible effect
Rotated buildings/vehicles collide as axis-aligned (or as loose circles on the live path). Tanks clip through corners of angled walls; crush/squish/enter contact is too fat or too skinny vs retail box geometry.
close_reason: CollideInfo uses stored PartitionObject.angle; host_geom_collides passes get_orientation().

title: [GameLogic] findPositionAround try_position skips pathfinder + sourceToPathToDest
description:
## C++
`PartitionManager::tryPosition` (`PartitionManager.cpp:3719-3833`):
1. Floor world pos to PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE, reject `CELL_IMPASSABLE`; if `FPF_CLEAR_CELLS_ONLY` require `CELL_CLEAR`.
2. After object overlap, if `sourceToPathToDest` has AI, `clientSafeQuickDoesPathExist(locoSet, srcPos, pos)` must succeed.

## Rust
Crate `partition_manager.rs` `try_position` (773-896):
- Impassable block is a comment stub: \"A full implementation would consult the AI pathfinder's cell grid.\"
- Object overlap uses `find_objects_in_radius` + major-radius, not `iteratePotentialCollisions` 5.0 sphere geom.
- Closing comment: \"The C++ also does a pathfinding check when sourceToPathToDest is set. ... we skip it.\"

## Evidence
C++ lines 3719-3730 and 3823-3831 vs Rust 773-787 and 891-895.

## Player-visible effect
`findPositionAround` (crate spawn, production exit, rally, script place) can return cliff/impassable cells or positions the source cannot path to. Units spawn/exit inside rocks or on the far side of a wall.
close_reason: try_position rejects Impassable/CLEAR_CELLS_ONLY via pathfind cell type and client_safe_quick_does_path_exist when source_to_path_to_dest is set.

title: [GameLogic] CrateCollide treats KindOf PARACHUTE as Parachuting status
description:
## C++
`CrateCollide::isValidToExecute` (`CrateCollide.cpp:164-165`):
```
if( other->isKindOf( KINDOF_PARACHUTE ) )
    return FALSE;
```
`KINDOF_PARACHUTE` is the parachute *object* KindOf (`KindOf.h` PARACHUTE bit). Units under a chute collide as the parachute thing; infantry with OBJECT_STATUS_PARACHUTING is a different test.

## Rust
`crate_collide.rs` `is_kind_of` (430-443) uses a local `KINDOF_PARACHUTE = 1 << 1` key then:
```
if _kind == KINDOF_PARACHUTE {
    return guard.test_status(ObjectStatusTypes::Parachuting);
}
```
Common already has `KindOf::PARACHUTE = 1 << 73` (`kind_of.rs`).

## Evidence
C++ `isKindOf(KINDOF_PARACHUTE)` vs Rust `test_status(Parachuting)`. Local mask `1<<1` is not the retail KindOf bit.

## Player-visible effect
A parachute object (no Parachuting status) can pick up crates. A parachuting infantry (status set, not KindOf PARACHUTE) is wrongly rejected. Retail rejects the chute object, not the rider status.
close_reason: CrateCollide is_kind_of(KINDOF_PARACHUTE) maps to KindOf::Parachute, not Parachuting status.

title: [W3D] W3DShaderManager filters still 2D tints; no RTT, ST_MASK, or fade-pattern
description:
## C++
`W3DView::draw` calls `W3DShaderManager::filterPreRender` / `filterPostRender`. Filters render the 3D scene to `m_renderTexture` (`startRenderToTexture` / `endRenderToTexture`, `W3DShaderManager.cpp:2808-2865`) then composite:
- `ScreenBWFilter` pixel shader (or DOT3 fallback)
- `ScreenMotionBlurFilter` accumulated viewport copies (`MAX_COUNT=60`)
- `ScreenCrossFadeFilter` uses `m_fadePatternTexture` + `ST_MASK_TEXTURE` (`MaskTextureShader::set` ~1370; `W3DMaskMaterialPassClass::Install_Materials` `W3DShroud.cpp:781-783`)
MD also keeps `ScreenDefaultFilter` so heat-haze can sample the previous frame.

## Rust
hq-1bkq closed as Display blit of `View::filter_composite`. Live `display.rs:630-660` draws a fullscreen UI rect (gray/red/green tint, dark fade, or a second offset rect for motion blur). No render-to-texture, no `ST_MASK_TEXTURE` / fade-pattern projection, no motion-blur accumulation, no previous-frame texture for smudge.

Crate `wthree_d_shader_manager.rs` `filter_pre_render` / `start_render_to_texture` only flip CPU flags and are unused by Main/GameClient.

## Player-visible
Death-cam is a gray overlay, not desaturated scene. Superweapon zoom-blur is a dark smear, not accumulated frames. Scripted crossfades are a black fade, not a masked reveal of two scene captures.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Live filters use a scene render-target (or equivalent) rather than a UI color quad
- [ ] Crossfade uses a mask texture analog of ST_MASK_TEXTURE / fade-pattern
- [ ] Verified against W3DShaderManager filter symbols, not crate bookkeeping
close_reason: display/shader_filter.rs RTT start_render_to_texture + ScreenBW/MotionBlur/CrossFade ST_MASK composite (wgpu analog of W3DShaderManager filterPre/PostRender).

title: [W3D] River and trapezoid water skip JBA river pixel shader (sparkles/noise/alpha-edge)
description:
## C++
ZH default `WaterType=0` (`GlobalData.cpp:626`) uses `renderWater()`: rivers call `drawRiverWater` + `setupJbaWaterShader` (`W3DWater.cpp:173-247`, ~2876-2885). That binds `m_riverTexture`, `m_riverAlphaEdge` (stage 3), `m_waterSparklesTexture` (stage 1), `m_waterNoiseTexture` (stage 2 camera-space + `m_riverVOrigin` scroll), optional `m_riverWaterPixelShader` / `m_trapezoidWaterPixelShader`. Type-2 bump-mapped `drawSea` is compiled out in MD (`W3DWater.cpp:1023` `#if 0`).

## Rust
hq-ecj5 closed polygon tessellation only. Live `record_extra_water_draws` (`overlay_gpu.rs:825-845`) draws river strips and trapezoids with the same TWWater01 `water.wgsl` pipeline as the global plane. No river/alpha-edge/sparkle/noise textures, no JBA pixel-shader analog. `overlay.river_v_origin` advances (`overlay_gpu.rs:268`) and is used as a UV offset on the same standing-water albedo. `overlay.bump_frame` increments (`NUM_BUMP_FRAMES=32`) and is never sampled (type-2 leftover).

## Player-visible
Rivers look like the same flat lake material. No edge foam, sparkle, or scrolling noise layer.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Live river/trapezoid draws use river texture + alpha-edge + sparkle/noise (or a faithful combined shader) like `setupJbaWaterShader` / `setupFlatWaterShader`
- [ ] Do not implement disabled MD type-2 bump-sea as a substitute
close_reason: river_gpu.rs JBA river pipeline binds river/sparkle/noise/alpha-edge; overlay_gpu.rs draws jba river/trapezoid meshes with that pipeline.

title: [W3D] WaterTracks soft-edge / transparent-depth gate never wired from GlobalData
description:
## C++
`WaterTracksRenderSystem::flush` (`W3DWaterTracks.cpp:840-841`) returns immediately when `!TheGlobalData->m_showSoftWaterEdge` or `TheWaterTransparency->m_transparentWaterDepth == 0`. Options checkbox ShowSoftWaterEdge therefore hides beach/pond wakes.

## Rust
CPU flush has the same predicate (`water_tracks.rs:789-791`) behind `set_render_enabled`. Defaults are `show_soft_water_edge=true`, `transparent_water_depth=1.0` (`water_tracks.rs:608-609`).

`set_render_enabled` is only called from `GameClient/tests/water_tracks.rs`. Live `TerrainVisualImpl::update` / `flush_water_tracks` never copies `GlobalData.show_soft_water_edge` or `WaterTransparency.transparent_water_depth`. `rebuild_shoreline` reads those flags for shoreline tiles (`overlay_gpu.rs:35-45`) but does not pass them to `water_tracks`.

## Player-visible
Turning off Smooth Water still shows `.wak` shore waves. Maps with zero transparent-water depth still draw wakes.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Live flush uses the same GlobalData + WaterTransparency gates as C++ every frame
- [ ] Options ShowSoftWaterEdge hides water tracks
close_reason: TerrainVisualImpl::update copies GlobalData.show_soft_water_edge and WaterTransparency.transparent_water_depth into water_tracks.set_render_enabled every flush.

title: InGameUI floating text + HUD message expire/fade
description: C++ InGameUI.cpp updateFloatingText (5030-5077) fades then erases when alpha<=0; addFloatingText gated on getDrawIconUI (4957). HUD messages fade/remove in update (1633-1657) with alternating color1/color2 (2100-2103). Rust replace_floating_texts reset alpha/frame_count; expire must drop text after C++ timeout/fade.

title: [W3DRadar] terrain texture invented ramp; skips TerrainVisual/water/bridge
description:
## C++
`W3DRadar::buildTerrainTexture` (`W3DRadar.cpp:997-1228`) for each 128×128 cell: `radarToWorld2D`, `findBridgeAt` + non-rubble body → `TerrainRoadType::getRadarColor()` at averaged bridge Z; else if underwater, 3×3 sample of `TheWaterTransparency->m_radarColor` interpolated against water table / `m_mapExtent.lo.z`; else 3×3 `TheTerrainVisual->getTerrainColorAt` + `interpolateColorForHeight` using terrain average / hiZ / loZ. Pixels written with world Y orientation.

## Rust
`RadarSystem::refresh_terrain` (`radar.rs:1408-1474`) if 128×128 samples exist paints an invented green-brown elevation ramp `(54,66,46)→(182,166,120)` and hardcoded water `(44,86,140)`, then `interpolate_color_for_height`. If samples are missing (the live default — `new_map` never fed) it fills every texel 139/119/70 brown. No `getTerrainColorAt`, no `WaterTransparency.m_radarColor`, no bridge template color, no 3×3 neighborhood average.

## Evidence
C++ W3DRadar.cpp:1074 / 1144-1178 vs Rust radar.rs:1430-1472.

## Player-visible effect
The LeftHUD radar does not show map tiles, water INI color, or intact bridges. It is a uniform brown plate or a generic height ramp, so players cannot read terrain from the minimap the way ZH does.
close_reason: buildTerrainTexture water INI 3x3 TerrainVisual/bridge hooks

title: [Radar] tryEvent throttle ignores inactive history (4s vs 10s)
description:
## C++
`Radar::tryEvent` (`Radar.cpp:1269-1315`) walks all `MAX_RADAR_EVENTS` slots of the same type. It does **not** require `active`. Distance gate is 250² (note C++ writes the unparenthesized `x - pos.x * x - pos.x` form; intended 2D range is 250). Time gate is `LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND * 10` (300 frames). Events die at 4s (`internalCreateEvent` fade/die) but remain in the ring buffer and still suppress a new ping for the remaining ~6s. Used by `tryUnderAttackEvent` and stealth `tryEvent` callers.

## Rust
`try_under_attack_event_for` (`radar.rs:1323-1343`), `try_stealth_discovered_event` (1631-1648), and `try_stealth_neutralized_event` (1657-1674) all require `event.active`. After `update` clears `active` at `die_frame` (4s, `radar.rs:1063-1066`) a second ping at the same spot is allowed. There is no generic `try_event(type, pos)` matching `Radar::tryEvent`.

## Evidence
C++ Radar.cpp:1285-1301 (type-only) vs Rust radar.rs:1332 `event.active`.

## Player-visible effect
Under-attack / stealth-discovered / stealth-neutralized pings, EVA, and ControlBar glow can retrigger every 4 seconds instead of every 10, so the radar and EVA spam during a prolonged fight.
close_reason: tryEvent type+250sq+10s without active gate

title: [W3DRadar] drawEvents never plays RadarEvent audio or skips FAKE
description:
## C++
`W3DRadar::drawEvents` (`W3DRadar.cpp:546-576`) iterates `MAX_RADAR_EVENTS`. Only `active && type != RADAR_EVENT_FAKE` draw. The first visible frame of a non-beacon event plays `AudioEventRTS("RadarEvent")` then sets `soundPlayed`. Beacons spin the opposite direction at width/10 (`drawSingleBeaconEvent`); generics spin the other way at width/2 (`drawSingleGenericEvent`). Lines are clipped to the radar pixel rect.

## Rust
`draw_radar_in_hud` (`w3d_gadget_draw/hud.rs:320-361`) draws `get_active_events()` triangles via `radar_event_marker` and never inspects `sound_played`, never calls audio, and does not filter `RadarEventType::Fake`. `RadarEvent.sound_played` is stored and xfer'd but no draw/update path sets it or plays `"RadarEvent"`. Fake events created so spacebar can jump still render a marker.

## Evidence
C++ W3DRadar.cpp:554-565 vs Rust hud.rs:320-361 (draw only).

## Player-visible effect
No radar-event chirp when a ping first appears. Script/unit-lost FAKE events (meant to be silent/invisible, spacebar-only) still draw a spinning triangle if they are marked active.
close_reason: drawEvents skips FAKE and plays RadarEvent once

title: Terrain never bakes static sun diffuse

close_reason: generate_geometry already bakes getStaticDiffuse; live shaders/terrain.wgsl multiplies baked vb.diffuse only

title: Water shader/layout mismatch and plane not under Alpine
