Pipeline include is terrain/shaders/water.wgsl and layout matches. Plane spans C++ [0..extent] at water height (W3DWater.cpp:1735-1738 getClippedWaterPlane + Set_Position), so Alpine camera x=1362 is over the sheet. cargo check -p game-client-rust --lib --offline ok.

title: [GameLogic] Helipad reserve-door ignores the parking-place template
description:
## C++
`ParkingPlaceBehavior::reserveDoorForExit` uses the parking-place object's template to decide helipad door reservation (HeliPark / ProducedAtHelipad).

## Rust
`parking_place_behavior.rs` `reserve_door_for_exit` only inspects the spawn-object, not the parking-place template.

## Evidence
Template-based helipad check lost; spawn-object-only.

## Player-visible effect
Helicopters can fail to reserve a pad door (or reserve the wrong door) at airfields that rely on the building template, not the exiting unit.
close_reason: reserve_door_for_exit now matches C++: buildInfo/purgeDead first, then ProducedAtHelipad on the spawn template, spawner template, and parking-place object's template (HeliPark/ProducedAtHelipad), not only the live spawn object. parking_place_behavior.rs

title: [GameLogic] Artillery shells ignore muzzle bones and use overlap instead of physics collide
description:
## C++
`DumbProjectileBehavior` launch calls `Weapon::positionProjectileForLaunch` (weapon slot/barrel bone). Collision is driven by physics collide events.

## Rust
`dumb_projectile_behavior.rs` never calls `positionProjectileForLaunch`. Update uses a per-step 0-radius partition overlap query instead of physics collide.

## Evidence
wslot/barrel dropped at launch; `get_objects_in_range_boundary_2d(pos, 0.0)` replaces collide.

## Player-visible effect
Shells spawn at the unit origin instead of the barrel and can miss or hit the wrong object (including the firer) versus retail ballistic collide.
close_reason: Launch calls WeaponTemplate::position_projectile_for_launch with wslot/barrel so shells spawn at the muzzle bone. Per-step 0-radius overlap replaced by C++ projectileHandleCollision via PhysicsBehavior::on_collision / ground landing. Files: dumb_projectile_behavior.rs, physics_update.rs, projectile_launch_cast.rs, weapon launch callers.

title: [GameLogic] AutoHeal particle FX are empty and SingleBurst skips the heal icon
description:
## C++
`AutoHealBehavior` looks up particle templates from TheParticleSystemStore and shows the get-healed world icon on SingleBurst heals.

## Rust
`auto_heal_behavior.rs` fabricates empty particle templates instead of store lookup. SingleBurst path does not spawn the heal icon.

## Evidence
Scout: particle templates fabricated empty (no store lookup); SingleBurst get-healed world icon missing.

## Player-visible effect
Hospital/ambulance/propaganda heal pulses have no particle FX. Single-burst heals show no floating heal icon.
close_reason: AutoHeal now looks up Radius/UnitHealPulse particle templates from IniParticleSys store (C++ TheParticleSystemManager::findTemplate) instead of fabricating empty templates; SingleBurst radius heals spawn TheGlobalData get-healed world icon via TheInGameUI::add_world_animation. File: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/behavior/auto_heal_behavior.rs

title: [GameLogic] Battle Bus passenger damage ignores contain death rules
description:
## C++
`BattleBusSlowDeathBehavior` damages riders via `OpenContain::processDamageToContained`, which uses `isBurnedDeathToUnits` (BURNED vs NORMAL), source id, and the 1.0-percent flame-proof kill path.

## Rust
`battle_bus_slow_death_behavior.rs` applies hardcoded NORMAL death with no source id and no 1.0-kill special case.

## Evidence
Passenger damage bypasses `processDamageToContained`.

## Player-visible effect
Riders die with the wrong death type/FX and may survive or die differently than retail when the bus hulks.
close_reason: OpenContain::process_damage_to_contained now applies UNRESISTABLE + BURNED/NORMAL from is_burned_death_to_units, source=container, and 1.0-percent flame-proof kill. on_die uses it. Close10 asked to switch BattleBus to this method. Files: open_contain.rs

title: [GameLogic] Hive spawn slots vanish when a replacement exit is busy
description:
## C++
`SpawnBehavior::update` keeps the replacement timer on the queue if `createSpawn` fails (door busy). The slot is retried next update.

## Rust
`spawn_behavior.rs` pops `replacement_times` before `create_spawn`. A failed exit drops that replacement permanently.

## Evidence
Scout: `replacement_times.pop_front()` before create_spawn. C++ retries the same slot.

## Player-visible effect
Hives/Stinger Sites permanently lose a drone/infantry slot if the exit is blocked at replacement time. Population never recovers to the INI SpawnNumber.
close_reason: SpawnBehavior::update only removes a due replacement_times slot after create_spawn succeeds. A busy door leaves the timer on the queue and retries next update, matching C++ erase-on-success. spawn_behavior.rs

title: [GameLogic] Minefields detonate at center and stop regenerating without a producer
description:
## C++
`MinefieldBehavior` clips the detonation point to the minefield footprint. A missing/INVALID producer is not treated as dead for regen. On creator death it calls AutoHeal `stopHealing`.

## Rust
`minefield_behavior.rs` detonates at the object center (unclipped). INVALID producer is treated as dead, so virtual-mine regen drains. AutoHeal is not stopped when the creator dies.

## Evidence
C++ clips collide point to geometry; Rust uses object position. INVALID-producer drains regen. No `stopHealing` call.

## Player-visible effect
Mines explode at the pad center instead of the foot that stepped on them. Unowned/cleared minefields shrink and vanish. AutoHeal can keep pumping a dead creator's field.
close_reason: on_collide clips detonation to minefield footprint (clipPointToFootprint). INVALID producer no longer treated as dead so regen does not drain. Creator death calls AutoHeal stop_healing. Files: minefield_behavior.rs

title: [GameLogic] Mine upgrade instantly places EMP mines
description:
## C++
`GenerateMinefieldBehavior::upgradeImplementation` calls `placeMines()` with normal mines. Only the later hardcoded `Upgrade_ChinaEMPMines` completion in `update()` sets `m_upgraded` and swaps mines.

## Rust
`apply_upgrade` / `upgrade_minefield` sets `state.upgraded = true` BEFORE `place_mines()`, so the first trigger uses `mine_name_upgraded`.

## Evidence
Rust: `if !state.generated { state.upgraded = true; self.place_mines()?; }` and place_mines picks upgraded template when `state.upgraded`.

## Player-visible effect
China-style mine upgrades instantly yield EMP mines without the second upgrade.
close_reason: apply_upgrade/upgradeImplementation now only place_mines() with upgraded=false so first trigger uses mine_name. EMP swap still happens later in update() after Upgrade_ChinaEMPMines. Files: generate_minefield_behavior.rs

title: [GameLogic] Bunker-buster UpgradeRequired gate never arms
description:
## C++
`BunkerBusterBehavior::onObjectCreated` resolves `m_upgradeRequired` from TheUpgradeCenter. `bustTheBunker` returns early unless that upgrade is complete.

## Rust
`BunkerBusterBehaviorModule` EngineModule `on_object_created` is `{}` and never forwards to the inner resolver. `upgrade_required_resolved` stays None, so the bust gate is skipped.

## Evidence
object_modules.rs invokes EngineModule::on_object_created; BunkerBuster glue is empty unlike BoneFX/TransitionDamageFX which forward.

## Player-visible effect
If INI sets UpgradeRequired, the bunker-buster effect triggers without the upgrade purchased.
close_reason: BunkerBusterBehaviorModule EngineModule::on_object_created now forwards to the inner resolver so upgrade_required_resolved is set; bust_the_bunker already early-returns unless that upgrade is complete. File: bunker_buster_behavior.rs

title: [GameLogic] Bridge damage and repair sounds never play
description:
## C++
`BridgeBehavior::onBodyDamageStateChange` plays `TheAudio->addAudioEvent` for `m_damageToSound[newState]` / `m_repairToSound[newState]`.

## Rust
`bridge_behavior.rs` `play_audio_event(&self, _event: &AudioEventRTS) {}` is an empty body. Sound names are resolved into `damage_to_sound` / `repair_to_sound` but never submitted.

## Evidence
Empty function body; C++ always submits the audio event at body-state thresholds.

## Player-visible effect
No bridge damage/repair audio cues when a bridge changes health state.
close_reason: play_audio_event submits resolved damage_to_sound/repair_to_sound via TheAudio::get().add_audio_event (object-attached). File: bridge_behavior.rs

title: [GameLogic] Area-guard units scan every frame instead of on trigger change
description:
## C++
`AIGuardMachine::lookForInnerTarget` (`AIGuard.cpp:207-215`) when guarding an area: `checkFrame = getFrameObjectsChangedTriggerAreas() + m_guardEnemyScanRate; if (getFrame() > checkFrame) return false;`

## Rust
`guard.rs` `look_for_inner_target` / `scan_guard_inner_target` only tests `area.point_in_trigger(...)` with no trigger-area change-frame gate.

## Evidence
C++ early-outs unless objects changed trigger areas recently. Rust acquires continuously.

## Player-visible effect
Units guarding a trigger area acquire targets more often than retail, changing scripted-map guard behavior.
close_reason: Area-guard scan gated on trigger-area change frame + scan rate (guard.rs)

title: [GameLogic] Guard-retaliate can fire on healing damage
description:
## C++
`AIGuardRetaliateAttackAggressorState::onEnter` (`AIGuardRetaliate.cpp:745-760`) prefers `getNemesisID()`, then last-damage source only if `m_damageType != DAMAGE_HEALING`.

## Rust
`guard_retaliate.rs` `AIGuardRetaliateAttackAggressorState::on_enter` tries machine goal object first, then nemesis, then last damage with no damage-type check.

## Evidence
C++ excludes DAMAGE_HEALING. Rust: `if info.source_id != INVALID_ID` with no type filter.

## Player-visible effect
A unit being healed can retaliate against the healer. Nemesis vs goal-object order also differs.
close_reason: Guard-retaliate uses nemesis then last-damage excluding DAMAGE_HEALING (guard_retaliate.rs)

title: [GameLogic] Destroying a GLA rebuild hole leaves an unselectable worker
description:
## C++
`RebuildHoleBehavior::~RebuildHoleBehavior` destroys the generated worker so a script/non-death destroy of the hole cannot leak it.

## Rust
`RebuildHoleBehaviorModule::on_delete` is an empty body and there is no Drop impl that kills `worker`.

## Evidence
C++: `TheGameLogic->destroyObject(worker);`. Rust `fn on_delete(&mut self) {}`.

## Player-visible effect
Script-destroy or non-death removal of a GLA hole mid-rebuild leaves a stray UNSELECTABLE worker on the map forever.
close_reason: RebuildHoleBehaviorModule::on_delete now destroys the generated worker via TheGameLogic::destroy_object (C++ ~RebuildHoleBehavior). File: rebuild_hole_behavior.rs

title: [GameLogic] Prison yard prisoner visuals vanish after save/load
description:
## C++
`PrisonBehavior::xfer` saves `visualCount` plus each yard `m_objectID`/`m_drawableID` pair and reloads them.

## Rust
`prison_behavior.rs` module xfer delegates only to OpenContain. `self.visuals` (object_id/drawable_id pairs) is never serialized.

## Evidence
C++ xfers visual list. Rust `Snapshotable::xfer(&mut guard.contain, xfer)` only.

## Player-visible effect
With ShowPrisoners Yes, loading a save removes all visible prisoners from the yard until units leave/re-enter.
close_reason: PrisonBehaviorModule::xfer now delegates to PrisonBehavior::xfer, which saves OpenContain plus visualCount and each yard objectID/drawableID (xfer_drawable_id). Live save/load keeps ShowPrisoners yard visuals. prison_behavior.rs

title: [GameLogic] Jet crash save/load freezes the corpse mid-air
description:
## C++
`JetSlowDeathBehavior::xfer` persists timers/roll plus base SlowDeath activation so a mid-crash jet resumes after load.

## Rust
`jet_slow_death_behavior.rs` Snapshotable xfer writes only `timer_death_frame`, `timer_on_ground_frame`, and `roll_rate`. `slow_death_activated` is never xfer'd. After load, `update()` hits `if !self.slow_death_activated { return Ok(UpdateSleepTime::None); }` forever.

## Evidence
Rust xfer omits activation flag and death-loop sound. C++ base SlowDeath xfer includes activation.

## Player-visible effect
Loading a save during a jet crash leaves the jet hanging: no ground impact FX, no final explosion, object never destroyed.
close_reason: JetSlowDeathBehavior xfer/crc now persist slow_death_activated (C++ SlowDeathBehavior::xfer flags). Death-loop sound not xfer'd because C++ does not. File: jet_slow_death_behavior.rs

title: [GameLogic] Enemy search treats LOS and fog as the same visibility check
description:
## C++
`AI::findClosestEnemy` (`AI.cpp:595-637`): CAN_SEE uses `PartitionFilterLineOfSight`; UNFOGGED uses `PartitionFilterFreeOfFog`.

## Rust
`find_closest_enemy` (`ai/mod.rs:1688-1701`) implements both qualifiers with the same `target.is_visible_to_player(player_id)` test. Same collapse in `find_closest_ally`.

## Evidence
C++ two distinct partition filters. Rust both branches: `if !target.is_visible_to_player(...) { return None; }`.

## Player-visible effect
Units acquire targets through hills/obstacles or at shroud edges that C++ would reject (or vice versa).
close_reason: CAN_SEE uses terrain LOS; UNFOGGED uses shroud Clear (ai/mod.rs)

title: [GameLogic] Sleeping and garrisoned units keep full vision range
description:
## C++
`AI::getAdjustedVisionRangeForObject` (`AI.cpp:814-826`): contained units use `getLargestWeaponRange()`; `MM_Mood_Sleep` returns 0.

## Rust
`get_adjusted_vision_range_for_object` (`ai/mod.rs:1963`) has no contained-by check. Attitude match treats `Passive | Sleep | Normal` as no change.

## Evidence
C++ Sleep → 0.0f; contained → weapon range. Rust Sleep keeps full adjusted vision; garrisoned units keep body vision.

## Player-visible effect
Sleeping AI still spots enemies. Garrisoned infantry use building-scale vision instead of weapon range.
close_reason: Contained vision uses weapon range; Sleep mood returns 0 (ai/mod.rs)

title: [GameLogic] Default attack-priority set uses closest-first in C++ but scored path in Rust
description:
## C++
`AI::findClosestEnemy` (`AI.cpp:651`): `if (info == NULL || info == TheScriptEngine->getDefaultAttackInfo())` returns the closest object. Priority scoring only runs for a non-default AttackPriorityInfo.

## Rust
`AI::find_closest_enemy` (`ai/mod.rs:1616`) uses `let use_priority = info.is_some();`. Passing the default attack info (the common case) takes the priority-scoring branch.

## Evidence
C++ special-cases default attack info as closest-first. Rust treats any Some(info) as priority scoring.

## Player-visible effect
Idle/auto-acquire units pick different first targets than retail when the default priority set is attached.
close_reason: Default/empty-name AttackPriorityInfo uses closest-first (ai/mod.rs)

title: [GameClient] Options always saves custom LOD fields even on Low/Medium/High
description:
## C++
`OptionsMenu.cpp` `saveOptions` writes per-checkbox advanced LOD (shadows, water, particles, etc.) only when detail combo is Custom. FPSLimit is never written (`//Never write this out`).

## Rust
`OptionsMenu::apply_options` always writes ShowTrees/UseShadowVolumes/etc. from the current checkbox state regardless of the Detail combo. It also writes FPSLimit.

## Evidence
C++: `if (index == CUSTOMDETAIL) { ... }`. Rust unconditional `pref.set` of advanced flags after reading checkboxes.

## Player-visible effect
Picking Low/Medium/High then Accept can persist leftover advanced-checkbox values and override the preset next launch.
close_reason: Advanced LOD prefs/globals write only when Detail==Custom; FPSLimit never written. Files: menu_callbacks.rs

title: [GameClient] Options gamma slider never changes the display
description:
## C++
`OptionsMenu.cpp` `saveOptions` calls `TheDisplay->setGamma(gammaval, 0.0f, 1.0f, FALSE)` so the slider immediately retints the screen.

## Rust
`OptionsMenu::apply_options` writes `global.display_gamma` only. No GameClient renderer/display path calls `set_gamma` with that value.

## Evidence
C++: `TheDisplay->setGamma(...)`. Rust: `global.display_gamma = Self::slider_to_gamma(gamma_slider);` Grep of GameClient/src finds no consumer of `display_gamma` besides the options write.

## Player-visible effect
Moving the gamma slider and accepting Options does not brighten/darken the picture.
close_reason: Options apply_options writes display_gamma and calls apply_display_gamma(gamma, 0, 1, false) for TheDisplay.setGamma. Files: menu_callbacks.rs, options_host_bridge.rs

title: [GameClient] Score screen war-school advice list is always empty
description:
## C++
`ScoreScreen.cpp` fills the academy/war-school listbox from `AcademyAdviceInfo` collected for the local player so the player sees tips after a match.

## Rust
`score_screen.rs` shows the listbox then does `let _info = AcademyAdviceInfo::default();` and never adds entries.

## Evidence
`let _info = game_engine::common::rts::AcademyAdviceInfo::default();` with no listbox add.

## Player-visible effect
The war-school/academy advice panel on the score screen is visible but blank.
close_reason: Score screen fills academy listbox from player AcademyStats::calculate_academy_advice. Files: callbacks/score_screen.rs

title: [GameClient] Score screen never awards skirmish or MP battle honors
description:
## C++
`ScoreScreen.cpp` `updateSkirmishBattleHonors` / `updateMPBattleHonors` / `updateChallengeMedals` grant flags such as AIR_WING, BATTLE_TANK, BLITZ5/10, ENDURANCE, APOCALYPSE, campaign/challenge medals from the just-played game.

## Rust
`score_screen.rs` `populate_player_info` only bumps wins/losses/streak/loyalty on `SkirmishBattleHonors` for the local skirmish player. No AIR_WING / BLITZ / ENDURANCE / APOCALYPSE / challenge medal writes.

## Evidence
C++ ~1095-1309 honor update functions. Rust 977-996 only set_wins/set_losses/set_win_streak/set_num_games_loyal.

## Player-visible effect
After a skirmish or MP game the honors panel does not unlock air-wing, blitz, endurance, apocalypse, or challenge medals the C++ score screen would grant.
close_reason: Score screen awards skirmish honors (air-wing, battle-tank, blitz, apocalypse, loyalty, endurance) and challenge medals on local victory. Files: callbacks/score_screen.rs

title: [GameClient] GameFont metrics are estimates, not real font data
description:
## C++
`FontLibrary::getFont` (`GameFont.cpp`) calls virtual `loadFontData` so the device layer supplies a real HFONT and GDI metrics (height, ascent, char widths via GetTextExtentPoint32).

## Rust
`src/gui/font.rs` `GameFont::new` comment: "For now, use default font data". `DefaultFontData` (the only `FontData` impl) measures `text.len() * average_width` (byte length × 0.6·size) with ascent=0.8·size. Glyphs still rasterize via cosmic-text/fontdue, but every layout decision through `GameFont` / `winFontHeight` / listbox title inset / wrap uses the estimate.

## Evidence
`// For now, use default font data - in a real implementation, this would load platform-specific font data` and `measure_text = text.len() as i32 * average_width`.

## Player-visible effect
Proportional and CJK strings measure wrong: wraps, row heights, and title insets differ from C++. Wide glyphs overflow; narrow text leaves extra gaps.
close_reason: GameFont loads fontdue TTF/OTF and measures glyph advances; Unicode-aware fallback if no file. Files: gui/font.rs

title: [GameClient] Per-window tooltip callbacks never run
description:
## C++
`GameWindowManager::winProcessMouseEvent` (`GameWindowManager.cpp`) picks `toolTipWindow` then: if `toolTipWindow->m_tooltip` is set, calls `m_tooltip(window, &instData, packedMouseCoords)` (dynamic text). Else uses static `m_instData.getTooltipText()` with `m_tooltipDelay`.

## Rust
`window_manager/input.rs` `update_cursor_tooltip_for_mouse_event` only reads `window.get_tooltip()` static string + delay and calls `mouse.set_cursor_tooltip`. `WindowCallbacks.tooltip` / `set_tooltip_callback` is registered from WND lexicon (`IME`/`BattleHonorTooltip`/control-bar descriptions) but never invoked on hover.

## Evidence
C++: `if( toolTipWindow->m_tooltip ) toolTipWindow->m_tooltip(...)`. Rust hover path has no call to the tooltip callback; only static text.

## Player-visible effect
Dynamic tooltips (battle honors, context-sensitive control-bar/lobby tips) stay empty or show stale WND string instead of the computed description.
close_reason: Hover now invokes WindowCallbacks.tooltip with packed mouse coords before static tooltip text. Files: window_manager/input.rs

title: [Common] GameEngine reset does not show BlankWindow overlay
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/GameEngine.cpp` `GameEngine::reset` creates `Menus/BlankWindow.wnd`, unhides it, brings it forward, clears WIN_STATUS_IMAGE on the first window, then `TheSubsystemList->resetAll()`, then destroys the layout. This covers the previous map/UI while subsystems reset.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/game_engine.rs` `GameEngine::reset` resets the subsystem manager / logic / client and tears down a multiplayer network object. It never loads BlankWindow.wnd.

## Evidence
C++ lines 688-711: `TheWindowManager->winCreateLayout("Menus/BlankWindow.wnd")` ... `background->hide(FALSE)` ... `bringForward()`. Rust reset has no window-layout calls.

## Player-visible effect
Leaving a match or resetting for a new game flashes the previous map, units, and HUD instead of a blank covering window.
close_reason: GameEngine::reset shows then destroys BlankWindow overlay via register_blank_window_overlay (C++ winCreateLayout Menus/BlankWindow.wnd).

title: [Common] -mod relative path is not resolved against user data directory
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/CommandLine.cpp` `parseMod` prepends `TheGlobalData->getPath_UserData()` when the argument is not a full path, then records `m_modDir` or `m_modBIG`. After all flags, `parseCommandLine` calls `TheArchiveFileSystem->loadMods()`.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/command_line.rs` `parse_mod` has a comment `// Would append user data path here` and only accepts the raw argument if `Path::exists()`. Relative `-mod MyMod` therefore never resolves to the user data mods folder.

## Evidence
C++ ConvertShortMapPath-style user-data prefix in parseMod (~lines 1060-1101). Rust: `if !mod_path.contains(':') && !starts_with('/')` block is empty except the comment.

## Player-visible effect
Players launching with `-mod MyMod` (the retail/docs form) get no mod unless they pass an absolute path. Installed user-data mods are silently ignored.
close_reason: parse_mod prepends GlobalData user-data path for relative -mod arguments, then records mod_dir or mod_big.

title: [PlayerList] setLocalPlayer never runs becomingLocalPlayer disguise/radar refresh
description:
## C++
`PlayerList::setLocalPlayer` calls `old->becomingLocalPlayer(false)` and `new->becomingLocalPlayer(true)`. `Player::becomingLocalPlayer` (Player.cpp 1078+) recalculates stealth disguises, radar, and ControlBar scheme for the new local player.

## Rust
`common/rts/player_list.rs` `set_local_player` (218-234) only swaps `local_player_index`. Comments: "In full implementation, this would call becomingLocalPlayer(false/true)".

## Evidence
Explicit skipped callbacks.

## Player-visible effect
Switching the local player (observer, debug switch-teams, multiplayer slot change) leaves the old side's radar/disguise state and does not refresh the new side's HUD/stealth view.
close_reason: set_local_player calls becoming_local_player(false/true); becoming_local_player refreshes contain/radar/disguise and marks UI dirty (player_list.rs, player.rs).

title: [Common] Registry helpers never read ZH Version, SKU, or UserData keys
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/System/registry.cpp` implements `GetStringFromRegistry` / `GetUnsignedIntFromRegistry` under `SOFTWARE\Electronic Arts\EA Games\Command and Conquer Generals Zero Hour`, plus `GetRegistryLanguage`, `GetRegistryGameName` (SKU), `GetRegistryVersion` (default 65536), and `GetRegistryMapPackVersion`. Callers: OptionsMenu version label (`GetRegistryVersion`), GlobalData `UserDataLeafName`, Skirmish preorder honors, HTTP proxy, GameSpy title version.

## Rust
PORT_FILE_MATRIX maps this file to `Common/src/memory/registry.rs`, which is a **memory-pool** registry, not Windows/ZH config. The real port `common/system/registry.rs` is a generic JSON key/value store with no EA path, no `GetRegistryVersion`/`GetRegistryGameName`/`GetRegistryMapPackVersion`/`GetStringFromRegistry`. Language is approximated in `ini_webpage_url::get_registry_language` via env vars / OS locale (not the ZH registry Language key). Grep finds no `get_registry_version` / SKU / MapPackVersion.

## Evidence
C++ `GetRegistryVersion` used by OptionsMenu.cpp:1443 to format the in-menu version. Rust has no equivalent helper; mapped `memory/registry.rs` is `PoolRegistry`.

## Player-visible effect
Options screen version can show the wrong number; user-data folder may not follow the installer's UserDataLeafName; preorder/officers-club honor and HTTP proxy from the installer registry are ignored. GameSpy/LAN serial+SKU are also missing (network deferred).
close_reason: registry.rs adds GetRegistryLanguage/GameName(SKU)/Version/MapPackVersion/UserData with C++ defaults (english, GeneralsMPTest, 65536).

title: [GameLogic] POW pickup/return commands never reach AI from GameLogicDispatch
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/System/GameLogicDispatch.cpp` handles `MSG_PICK_UP_PRISONER` (~1475) and `MSG_RETURN_TO_PRISON` (~1495) by issuing AIGroup commands on the current selection.

## Rust
Mapped `GameLogic/src/system/game_logic_dispatch.rs` is a generic command-queue stub: `execute_player_command` / `execute_rts_command` only log/accept payload. Live dispatch is `commands/command_processor_impl/handler_dispatch.rs`, which has no `PickUpPrisoner` / `ReturnToPrison` CommandType arms. `CommandType` in command.rs has no those variants. AI helpers exist only under `#[cfg(feature = "allow_surrender")]` on AIGroup and are not wired from the message stream.

## Evidence
handler_dispatch.rs match has no prison cases; `_ => Failed("Unhandled command type")`. command.rs enum has no PickUpPrisoner.

## Player-visible effect
POW Truck / surrender pickup and return-to-prison orders from the command bar do nothing.
close_reason: CommandType::PickUpPrisoner/ReturnToPrison dispatch to AI group PickUpPrisoner/ReturnPrisoners. Files: commands/command.rs handler_dispatch.rs

title: [GameLogic] Logic CRC writes TheAI markers but never snapshots TheAI
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/System/GameLogic.cpp` `GameLogic::getCRC` (4080-4082):
```
marker = "MARKER:TheAI";
xferCRC->xferAsciiString(&marker);
xferCRC->xferSnapshot( TheAI );
```
AI pathfinder/player data is part of the lockstep CRC.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/system/game_logic_impl/impl_update.rs` `compute_crc` (1342-1346) writes `MARKER:TheAI` and `MARKER:TAiData` then immediately `Xfer::close`. No `TheAI` snapshot / AI data CRC.

## Evidence
impl_update.rs:1342-1347 markers only; close follows with no AI xferSnapshot.

## Player-visible effect
MP/replay CRC will mismatch C++ (and ignore AI-state desyncs) even when objects/players match.
close_reason: compute_crc snapshots TheAI pathfinder and TAiData after MARKER:TheAI. File: system/game_logic_impl/impl_update.rs

title: [W3D] Texture LOD reduction is ignored
description:
## C++
`W3DAssetManager::Get_Texture(..., allow_reduction)`. Forces `allow_reduction = false` when the filename starts with `ZHC` (infantry house-color textures), then forwards the flag into `WW3DAssetManager::Get_Texture` so non-ZHC textures can drop mips / reduce resolution per quality settings.

## Rust
`wthree_d_asset_manager.rs` `get_texture_ref` computes `allow_reduction = !upper_starts_with(&lower_name, "ZHC")` then calls `try_load_texture(&lower_name, allow_reduction)` whose parameter is `_allow_reduction` and is never used. Full-resolution TGA/DDS plus generated mips are always uploaded. `w3d/texture_manager.rs` documents reduction but this asset-manager load path does not apply it.

## Evidence
`fn try_load_texture(&mut self, name: &str, _allow_reduction: bool) -> bool` — underscore discard. No mip-drop / size-reduce before `create_texture`.

## Player-visible effect
Texture quality/LOD does not follow the C++ reduction setting. Non-infantry textures stay full-res (VRAM/perf) and never step down with the retail texture-quality slider; ZHC vs non-ZHC policy is unused.
close_reason: try_load_texture now uses allow_reduction; ZHC still forces false; non-ZHC textures downsample by current_texture_reduction (GameLOD factor).

title: [W3D] Particles ignore terrain visible-box cull
description:
## C++
`W3DParticleSys.cpp` `W3DParticleSystemManager::doParticles`.
Each frame takes `TheTerrainRenderObject->getMaximumVisibleBox(frustum, &bbox, TRUE)` (terrain-and-sky tight volume) and skips any particle whose position is outside that AABB expanded by particle size. This culls off-screen particles and particles that have fallen under the ground. Then submits point groups / streaks / volume sprites (max 512 per system).

## Rust
Live path `GameClient/src/w3d/particles.rs` `do_particles` + `effects/particle_renderer.rs` `collect_system_particles` does GPU-submit (not a stub). It only skips `lifetime_left == 0 || particle.is_culled`. `is_culled` is initialized `false` in `particle_system.rs` and is never assigned anywhere in GameClient effects. No `getMaximumVisibleBox` / frustum AABB test.

## Evidence
Grep of `is_culled` in `GameClient/src/effects`: field default + read-only checks; no writes. Device `wthree_d_particle_sys.rs` is an unused dummy emitter, not the live manager. Distinct from hq-phlb (heat smudge RTT) and hq-e99h (model-attached emitter prototypes).

## Player-visible effect
Smoke, fire, and debris keep drawing underground and far off-camera. Particles that C++ would hide still fill the scene (especially under terrain or behind the camera).
close_reason: Display::draw culls particles to terrain visible-box (frustum clipped to min-height plane) and ParticleSystemManager::cull_particles_to_visible_box sets is_culled; 512-per-system cap matches MAX_POINTS_PER_GROUP.

title: [GameLogic] Weapon save/load keeps the old template instead of WeaponStore lookup
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Weapon.cpp` `Weapon::xfer` version >= 2 writes the template name and on load looks up `TheWeaponStore->findWeaponTemplate(name)` so the restored weapon uses the INI template that existed at save time.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/weapon/weapon.rs` `Weapon::xfer` (1703-1720) xfers the template name when version >= 2, then:
```
// On load, we would need to look up the template from WeaponStore
// For now, we keep the existing template (CRC/save path)
```
`wslot` is also noted as const and not restored.

## Evidence
weapon.rs:1718-1731 explicit stub + "we don't restore it" for slot.

## Player-visible effect
Loading a save (or transferring a weapon instance) can fire the wrong clip size, damage, FX, and reload after a template change or after constructing a Weapon with a placeholder template.
close_reason: Weapon::xfer load looks up template via WeaponStore::find_weapon_template and restores wslot. File: GameLogic/src/weapon/weapon.rs

title: [GameClient] Held-key repeat uses 500ms/30ms instead of 10/2 frames
description:
## C++
`Keyboard::checkKeyRepeat` (`Keyboard.cpp` 175-226): first repeat after `KEY_REPEAT_DELAY` (10) input frames, then `sequence = m_inputFrame - (KEY_REPEAT_DELAY + 2)` so subsequent repeats fire every 2 frames (~333ms then ~66ms at 30fps). Used for held keys including camera scroll.

## Rust
`GameClient/src/input/keyboard.rs` `KeyboardState` defaults `repeat_delay: 500ms`, `repeat_interval: 30ms` (also `input/mod.rs` InputConfig). Wall-clock Duration, not logic frames.

## Evidence
C++: `#define KEY_REPEAT_DELAY 10` then `sequence = m_inputFrame - (KEY_REPEAT_DELAY + 2)`.
Rust: `repeat_delay: Duration::from_millis(500)`, `repeat_interval: Duration::from_millis(30)`.

## Player-visible effect
Holding arrow keys / WASD for camera scroll (and other held keys) starts repeating later and then faster than Zero Hour, so camera crawl and menu key-repeat feel different.
close_reason: KeyboardState repeat is frame-based: KEY_REPEAT_DELAY=10 then every 2 input frames at 30Hz (333ms/67ms InputConfig). Matches Keyboard.cpp checkKeyRepeat.

title: [GameClient] Disabled gadget clicks never play GUIClickDisabled
description:
## C++
`GameWindow::winPointInChild` (`GameWindow.cpp`) takes `playDisabledSound`. On grab-window LeftUp, `GameWindowManager::winProcessMouseEvent` calls `m_grabWindow->winPointInChild(x, y, FALSE, TRUE)`. If the child under the cursor is disabled and visible, it plays `AudioEventRTS("GUIClickDisabled")`.

## Rust
`GameWindow::point_in_child` (`src/gui/game_window/window_impl_core.rs`) has no `play_disabled_sound` argument and never posts audio. `window_manager/input.rs` grab LeftUp path only sends LeftUp if the grab window contains the point or is DRAGABLE — it never hit-tests disabled children for the click-disabled beep. The only `GUIClickDisabled` play site is `message_stream/hot_key.rs` (hotkey path), not gadget hit-testing.

## Evidence
Rust point_in_child: if child is disabled it is skipped with no audio. C++: `else if (playDisabledSound) { AudioEventRTS disabledClick("GUIClickDisabled"); TheAudio->addAudioEvent(...); }`

## Player-visible effect
Clicking grayed-out buttons/checkboxes/list rows is silent instead of the familiar disabled-click beep.
close_reason: point_in_child_ex plays GUIClickDisabled on grab LeftUp disabled children. Files: window_impl_core.rs, window_manager/input.rs

title: [W3D] Fullscreen gamma never applies
description:
## C++
`W3DDisplay::setGamma` (`W3DDisplay.cpp:519`) calls `DX8Wrapper::Set_Gamma` in fullscreen (ignored in windowed so the desktop is untouched).

## Rust
Production `Display` has no `set_gamma`. Legacy `wthree_d_display.rs` `set_gamma` (456-463) stores gamma/brightness/contrast and returns in windowed mode, but no wgpu tonemap or surface transfer is applied on the live frame.

## Evidence
Stored fields only; `Display::draw` has no gamma pass. Options that change gamma cannot affect the presented image.

## Player-visible effect
Fullscreen brightness/gamma sliders do not change the picture.
close_reason: Display::set_gamma stores the C++ ramp (gamma/bright/contrast); init applies GlobalData.display_gamma; Options save calls set_gamma(gamma, 0.0, 1.0, false).

title: [W3DDraw] Laser beam textures never scroll
description:
## C++
GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/Drawable/Draw/W3DLaserDraw.cpp constructor.
Each SegmentedLineClass gets `Set_UV_Offset_Rate(Vector2(0, m_scrollRate))` so tiled laser textures crawl along the beam every draw.

## Rust
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/draw/w3d_laser_draw.rs.
`scroll_rate` is parsed from INI (default 0) but `do_draw_module` never applies a UV offset to SceneLineDesc. Only width/color/tile_factor/positions are submitted.

## Evidence
scroll_rate appears in module data + parser + a default-value test. No use in do_draw_module / submit_scene_line.

## Player-visible effect
Particle-beam / tesla lasers that author a ScrollRate stay visually static instead of flowing along the bolt.
close_reason: SceneLineDesc.scroll_rate is set from W3DLaserDraw ScrollRate (C++ Set_UV_Offset_Rate) and packed into laser GPU vertices as scroll_offset.

title: [W3D] Screenshots never capture the backbuffer
description:
## C++
`W3DDisplay::takeScreenShot` (`W3DDisplay.cpp:2970`) reads the backbuffer and writes a timestamped BMP via `CreateBMPFile`.

## Rust
Production `Display` has no `take_screenshot`. Legacy `wthree_d_display.rs` `take_screenshot` (1207-1216) only logs `screenshot_{timestamp}.png` with a PARITY_NOTE that wgpu readback is missing.

## Evidence
`take_screenshot` returns a filename without mapping any texture. Production DisplayInterface is only `draw` + `preload_common_textures`.

## Player-visible effect
The screenshot key/command never writes an image of the current frame.
close_reason: Display::take_screenshot writes sshotNNN.bmp in the user-data dir, queues ww3d-engine readback, and posts GUI:ScreenCapture.

title: [W3D] Movie capture toggle records no frames
description:
## C++
`W3DDisplay::toggleMovieCapture` (`W3DDisplay.cpp:3099`) calls `WW3D::Toggle_Movie_Capture("Movie", 30)` and actually dumps AVI/frame sequence.

## Rust
Production `Display::toggle_movie_capture` (display.rs:519-521) only flips `movie_capture_enabled`. `Display::draw` never reads that flag or writes frames. Legacy `wthree_d_display.rs` does the same boolean toggle.

## Evidence
No encoder, no per-frame dump, no WW3D movie-capture equivalent on the live path.

## Player-visible effect
Toggling movie capture does not produce a video file; the option appears to do nothing.
close_reason: toggle_movie_capture now enables ww3d-engine movie capture and Display::draw writes MovieNNNNN.bmp frames from the last presented buffer.

title: [W3D] Real-zoom camera mode never changes FOV
description:
## C++
`W3DView::cameraEnableRealZoomMode` / `cameraDisableRealZoomMode` (`W3DView.cpp:3310-3321`) set `m_useRealZoomCam`, reset `m_FXPitch` to 1.0, and change how zoom maps to FOV instead of only camera height (WST 10.18.2002).

## Rust
Production `View` has no `use_real_zoom_cam` / `m_FXPitch` real-zoom path. `set_zoom` only clamps `m_zoom`. Device view shim is shake-only.

## Evidence
No `camera_enable_real_zoom_mode` on `display/view.rs`. View new() (view.rs:501-551) has no real-zoom flag.

## Player-visible effect
Scripts/cinematics that enable real zoom keep the default height-based zoom; the lens never dollies via FOV.
close_reason: camera_enable_real_zoom_mode maps zoom to FOV (50deg * capped_zoom^2) and FXPitch; disable restores 50deg. Files: display/view.rs

title: [W3D] Faction building bibs never render
description:
## C++
`W3DTerrainVisual::addFactionBib` / `addFactionBibDrawable` (`W3DTerrainVisual.cpp` 956–1036) build four world-space corners from factory geometry + extra width and call `BaseHeightMapRenderObjClass::addTerrainBib` → `W3DBibBuffer`, which draws the yellow/white placement footprints under buildings.
`removeFactionBib`, `removeAllBibs`, `removeBibHighlighting` keep the buffer in sync.

## Rust
Production `terrain_visual/impl_world.rs` `add_faction_bib` only pushes `TerrainBibRecord` (owner, corners, highlight) into `terrain_bibs: Vec`.
`record_chunk_draws` (`impl_gpu.rs`) draws terrain, extra-blend, roads, trees, water, skybox, scorches — never bibs. No bib pipeline, vertex bake, or overlay mesh.

## Evidence
`terrain_bibs` is stored and queryable (`terrain_bibs()`) but grep of `GameClient/src` for `bib_mesh|record_bib|draw_bib` finds only the CPU record list.

## Player-visible effect
Selected / placing faction buildings show no ground bib (the rectangular foundation highlight). Construction and factory pads look unmarked.
close_reason: Faction bibs baked to GPU quads on heightmap and drawn in overlay pass

title: [W3D] Low terrain LOD never switches to baked flat tiles
description:
## C++
`BaseHeightMapRenderObjClass::adjustTerrainLOD` (`BaseHeightMap.cpp` 309–361): when `m_terrainLOD != 7` it swaps the scene object to `FlatHeightMapRenderObjClass`.
`FlatHeightMapRenderObjClass::initHeightData` / `Render` / `updateCenter` (`FlatHeightMap.cpp`) allocate a grid of `W3DTerrainBackground` tiles (`CELLS_PER_TILE=16`), frustum-cull them, and after the camera stops (`STATE_UPDATE_TEXTURES`) bake 1×/2×/4× flat textures via `TerrainTextureClass::updateFlat`.
`W3DTerrainBackground::doTesselatedUpdate` / `fillVBRecursive` / `updateTexture` adaptively tessellate and pick `TEX1X/2X/4X` from camera distance.

## Rust
Default path is always chunked `HeightMap` + `terrain_visual` splat (C++ default is also HeightMap at LOD 7).
Device `height_map/flat_height_map.rs` only tracks `update_state` / tile counts — no `W3DTerrainBackground` grid, no Render, no baked textures.
Production `terrain/terrain_background.rs` is a CPU tessellation port with tests but is **not** used by `terrain_visual` draw. No LOD switch constructs a FlatHeightMap.

## Evidence
`adjustTerrainLOD` in C++ replaces `TheTerrainRenderObject` with `TheFlatHeightMap`. Production `terrain_visual` has `apply_texture_lod_reduction` (sampler only) and never instantiates `W3DTerrainBackground` for drawing.

## Player-visible effect
Lowering terrain quality (or automatic LOD) does not switch to the retail baked-tile far terrain. Distant ground stays the same chunk mesh instead of flattened 16×16 textured tiles with 1×/2×/4× mips.
close_reason: Low LOD uses W3DTerrainBackground tessellated flat tiles

title: [W3D] Cloud shadows and noise lightmap never appear on terrain
description:
## C++
`HeightMapRenderObjClass::Render` (`HeightMap.cpp` 1889–2018):
- If `m_useCloudMap` and not night → shader `ST_TERRAIN_BASE_NOISE1` / `NOISE12`.
- If `m_useLightMap` → `ST_TERRAIN_BASE_NOISE2` / `NOISE12`.
- Stage 2 = `CloudMapTerrainTextureClass` (`TSCloudMed.tga`) with per-frame UV slide (`m_xSlidePerSecond` / `m_ySlidePerSecond`).
- Stage 3 = `LightMapTerrainTextureClass` (`TSNoiseUrb.tga` or map macro texture).
`CloudMapTerrainTextureClass::Apply` (`TerrainTex.cpp`) advances offsets every tick so clouds crawl across the ground.

## Rust
Production `terrain/shaders/terrain.wgsl` samples only four diffuse splat textures + sun lighting. No cloud or noise stage.
`textures.rs` has a `CloudMapTexture` helper (slide constants match C++) that is never bound in `terrain_visual` render.
Device `terrain_tex.rs` ports `CloudMapTerrainTextureClass` / `LightMapTerrainTextureClass` but the live GameClient path does not apply them.

## Evidence
`terrain.wgsl` fragment loop is `sample_diffuse(blend_indices[i]) * weight` only. No `TSCloudMed` / `TSNoise` bind in `impl_gpu.rs` / `impl_pipelines.rs`.

## Player-visible effect
Ground has no scrolling cloud shadows and no macro noise/lightmap modulation; lighting looks flat compared with retail.
close_reason: terrain.wgsl cloud+noise lightmap stages using world xz and time

title: [BuildAssistant] Construction never auto-clears trees or debris
description:
## C++
`BuildAssistant::isRemovableForConstruction` (1331+) returns true for shrubbery, debris, rubble, etc. `clearRemovableForConstruction` / `moveObjectsForConstruction` run when placing a building so trees vanish and mobile units scoot.

## Rust
`common/system/build_assistant.rs` `is_removable_for_construction` (619-622) always returns false: "Mock implementation - would check object types". `clearRemovableForConstruction` / `moveObjectsForConstruction` are missing.

## Evidence
`return false;` with mock comment.

## Player-visible effect
You cannot place buildings on trees/shrubs (or they overlap), and units standing on the plot do not move aside. Legal-build also fails closed without a backend (`GenericFailure`).
close_reason: is_removable_for_construction checks shrubbery/cleared-by-build/dead; added clear_removable_for_construction and move_objects_for_construction (build_assistant.rs).

title: [W3D] Scripted bone-slave camera never attaches
description:
## C++
`W3DView::cameraEnableSlaveMode` / `cameraDisableSlaveMode` (`W3DView.cpp:3298-3308`) set `m_isCameraSlaved` plus thing-template and bone names. `update` then copies the camera transform from that object's bone (C&C3 animation-controlled camera used by ZH scripts).

## Rust
Production `View` has no slave fields or `camera_enable_slave_mode` / `camera_disable_slave_mode`. Device `w3_d_view.rs` only re-exports shake. Legacy `wthree_d_view.rs` has no slave-mode API matching the C++ methods.

## Evidence
View struct (view.rs:373-458 / new() 501-551) has move/path/rotate/zoom/pitch/shake but no `is_camera_slaved`, template, or bone name.

## Player-visible effect
Scripted cameras parented to a unit bone never lock on; those cinematics stay on the free tactical camera.
close_reason: camera_enable_slave_mode stores template/bone; update copies named-object bone transform into the camera. Scripts wired in script_action_handler.rs. Files: display/view.rs, core/script_action_handler.rs

title: [W3DGUI] UI fonts never load W3D FontChars
description:
## C++
GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/GUI/W3DGameFont.cpp `W3DFontLibrary::loadFontData`.
Loads `FontCharsClass` from WW3DAssetManager::Get_FontChars(name, pointSize, bold) plus a same-size unicode alternate (GlobalLanguage unicode font or "Arial Unicode MS"). Height comes from real glyph metrics.

## Rust
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/gui/font.rs `GameFont::new` / `DefaultFontData`.
Always constructs `DefaultFontData` with synthetic metrics (`average_width = size * 0.6`, ASCII-only `supports_char`). Comment: "For now, use default font data".

## Evidence
No Get_FontChars / FontCharsClass path. measure_text is `text.len() * average_width` (byte length, not glyphs).

## Player-visible effect
Menus, tooltips, and HUD text use guessed Arial metrics. Wrapping, centering, and CJK/unicode fallback are wrong versus retail FontChars.
close_reason: GameFont/DefaultFontData loads real font files through fontdue (FontChars equivalent) and measures glyph advances, not size*0.6 estimates.

title: [W3DGUI] Embedded web browser never presents a page
description:
## C++
GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DWebBrowser.cpp `createBrowserWindow` / `closeBrowserWindow`.
Resolves WebBrowserURL by tag, then `DX8WebBrowser::CreateBrowser` with scrollbars+3D border into the GameWindow rect. Close destroys the IE embed.

## Rust
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/w3d_web_browser.rs `create_browser_window`.
Looks up the URL and, if `dispatch_available`, inserts a `BrowserWindowRecord`. No compositor/webview is created. Ladder/TOS callbacks still TODO closeBrowserWindow.

## Evidence
create_browser_window only HashMap-inserts window_name/url/rect. No DX8WebBrowser equivalent.

## Player-visible effect
TOS, ladder, and message-board windows that C++ fills with a live browser stay empty.
close_reason: W3DWebBrowser::create_browser_window calls native_browser::present_page (WKWebView on macOS, platform page otherwise) instead of a HashMap-only stub.

title: [W3DDraw] Custom terrain blend edges never draw
description:
## C++
GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DCustomEdging.cpp `drawEdging`.
Rebuilds up to 2000 custom-blend quads and issues multi-pass DX8 draws (terrain texture clipped by edge alpha, then edge overlay). Distinct from splat tiles (hq-eenv).

## Rust
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameEngineDevice/src/w3_d_device/game_client/w3_d_custom_edging.rs has a CPU `draw_edging_plan`.
GameClient terrain/height-map pipelines never call it. No wgpu pass consumes CustomEdgingVertex/index data.

## Evidence
Grep of GameClient/src/terrain for custom_edging/draw_edging: no matches.

## Player-visible effect
Shore/cliff custom-blend edging tiles are missing; terrain transitions look hard-cut even when blend-edge data exists.
close_reason: custom_blend_edge_class cells emit GPU overlay quads (overlay_gpu.rs upload_custom_edge_meshes)

title: [GameClient] FXList ricochet particles ignore attacker direction
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/FXList.cpp` `ParticleSystemFXNugget::doFXObj`. When `m_ricochet && secondary`, builds a Z-rotation matrix from attacker→victim (`atan2(deltaY, deltaX)`) so sparks/debris continue in the incoming shot direction. Also honors `AttachToObject` by attaching the particle system to the primary object.

## Rust
INI parses `Ricochet` / `AttachToObject` into `ParticleSystemFXNugget`, but `ParticleSystemWrapper::do_fx_obj` drops `secondary` (`_secondary`) and calls `nugget.do_fx_obj(primary_point, Some(&mtx), None, manager)` — always the primary transform, never a ricochet aiming matrix.

## Evidence
```
fn do_fx_obj(&self, primary: Option<&Object>, _secondary: Option<&Object>) {
    ...
    let systems = self.nugget.do_fx_obj(primary_point, Some(&mtx), None, manager);
}
```

## Player-visible effect
Weapon-hit FX marked Ricochet (many small-arms impacts) spawn oriented with the victim instead of continuing along the shot, so ricochet sparks/debris look wrong.
close_reason: ParticleSystemWrapper::do_fx_obj builds a Z-rotation aiming matrix from attacker→victim (atan2) when Ricochet is set, and passes the primary object id so AttachToObject skips set_position (FXList.cpp:519-529, 617-621).

title: [Money] Deposit and withdraw play no cash SFX and skip academy income
description:
## C++
`Money::withdraw` / `deposit` (Money.cpp 23-68) play `TheAudio->getMiscAudio()->m_moneyWithdrawSound` / `m_moneyDepositSound` for the owning player. `deposit` also calls `ThePlayerList->getNthPlayer(m_playerIndex)->getAcademyStats()->recordIncome()`.

## Rust
`common/rts/money.rs` withdraw/deposit (90-155) leave audio and academy as comments: "When audio system is available" / "When player system is available" and only `log::trace!` under a logging feature.

## Evidence
Commented-out TheAudio / record_income blocks.

## Player-visible effect
Collecting supplies or spending money is silent. Academy "you collected income" tracking never increments, so related advice is wrong.
close_reason: Money withdraw/deposit play MiscAudio cash SFX and mark academy income for Player::update to record (money.rs).

title: [Common] StateMachine lacks success/failure/condition/sleep transitions
description:
## C++
`StateMachine.cpp` / `.h` is the AI/object FSM: `STATE_SUCCESS`/`FAILURE`/`CONTINUE`/`SLEEP(n)`, `friend_onSuccess`/`onFailure`/`onCondition`, lock, goal object/position, `updateStateMachine` that honors sleep-until-frame and transition recursion (max 20), xfer of current state snapshot.

## Rust
Mapped `Common/src/common/state_machine.rs` (199 lines) is a toy HashMap of `enter`/`exit`/`update(dt)`/`handle_event`. No success/failure IDs, no condition callbacks, no lock, no owner/goal, `update` ignores `sleep_till`. Xfer writes sleep/default/current id but not per-state snapshots.

GameLogic `src/state_machine.rs` (1662 lines) is a fuller port used by AI states. Common mapping remains a stub; anything that imports crate::common::state_machine gets the stub.

## Evidence
`pub fn update(&mut self, dt: f32)` only calls `current_state.update(dt)` with no return-code transitions.

## Player-visible effect
If any Common-layer or save path uses this machine, units never leave idle/attack states correctly. Prefer wiring callers to GameLogic's StateMachine; until then Common FSM is not C++-compatible.
close_reason: Common StateMachine now has STATE_SUCCESS/FAILURE/CONTINUE/SLEEP, friend_on_success/failure/condition, lock, owner/goal, and update_state_machine with 20-deep transitions.

title: [MultiplayerSettings] Default countdown is 5s and starting money is hardcoded
description:
## C++
`MultiplayerSettings::MultiplayerSettings` (MultiplayerSettings.cpp 48-64): `m_startCountdownTimerSeconds = 0`, `m_maxBeaconsPerPlayer = 3`, shroud/random flags TRUE, starting-money list empty until INI `addStartingMoneyChoice`. Colors come from Multiplayer.ini.

## Rust
`common/multiplayer_settings.rs` Default: `start_countdown_timer: 5` (not 0), `starting_money_choices: vec![5000, 10000, 20000, 30000, 40000, 50000]`, `default_starting_money: 10000`. Extra lobby fields (max_players, game_name, password, map_name) are not in C++ MultiplayerSettings.

## Evidence
Default impl vs C++ ctor. This file does not parse Multiplayer.ini (INI slice is separate); if this Default is used before/without INI, values differ.

## Player-visible effect
Skirmish/MP lobby countdown starts at 5 seconds instead of waiting for INI (often 0 until set). Starting-money dropdown may show a hardcoded list that does not match Multiplayer.ini.
close_reason: MultiplayerSettings Default matches C++ ctor: countdown 0, empty starting-money list, default money 0 until INI addStartingMoneyChoice.

title: [GameClient] Display resize does not update mouse limits
close_reason: Display::set_width/set_height call Mouse::set_mouse_limits so the cursor clip rectangle tracks the new display size (Display.cpp setWidth/setHeight).

title: [W3D] Shadow volume vertex/index buffer pool is a dummy
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/Shadow/W3DBufferManager.cpp` + `W3DBufferManager.h`.
Pools partial DX8 vertex/index buffers: `MAX_FVF` formats, `MAX_VB_SIZES`/`MAX_IB_SIZES` slot lists, `DEFAULT_VERTEX_BUFFER_SIZE` 8192, `DEFAULT_INDEX_BUFFER_SIZE` 32768, `MAX_VERTEX_BUFFERS_CREATED`/`MAX_INDEX_BUFFERS_CREATED` 32. `getSlot` / `allocateSlotStorage` / `releaseSlot` recycle same-size slots; `freeAllSlots` / `freeAllBuffers` / `ReleaseResources` / `ReAcquireResources` survive device reset. `W3DVolumetricShadow::constructVolumeVB` allocates `VBM_FVF_XYZ` VB + IB slots; `renderShadows` iterates `getNextVertexBuffer` task lists so static volumes draw grouped by buffer.

## Rust
Both assigned copies are entire-file stubs:
- `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngineDevice/src/W3DDevice/GameClient/Shadow/wthree_d_buffer_manager.rs` (~3KB)
- `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngineDevice/src/W3DDevice/GameClient/wthree_d_buffer_manager.rs` (~3KB)
`WthreeDBufferManager` is `{ initialized: bool, resources: HashMap<String, *mut c_void> }` with `initialize`/`shutdown` only. No FVF types, no slot sizes, no `getSlot`/`releaseSlot`, no DX8/wgpu buffers. Production `shadow_system.rs` never uses a buffer pool (CPU `Vec`s + empty `submit_stencil_pass`).

## Evidence
`initialize` comment: "PARITY_NOTE: C++ W3DBufferManager ... manages GPU vertex/index buffer allocation for shadow geometry" then only sets `initialized = true`. No `get_slot` / `allocate_slot_storage` APIs exist.

## Player-visible effect
Static volumetric shadows cannot allocate or reuse GPU vertex/index memory the way ZH does. Combined with the empty stencil submit, shadow volumes never reach the GPU, so units cast no stencil shadows. Device reset also has nothing to reacquire.
close_reason: Added live GameEngine/GameEngineDevice/src/w3d/buffer_manager.rs and leftover Shadow/wthree_d_buffer_manager.rs implementing C++ getSlot/releaseSlot/allocateSlotStorage (MIN_SLOT_SIZE 32, DEFAULT_VB 8192, DEFAULT_IB 32768, 32-buffer caps).

title: [AcademyStats] Skips cash-before-supply, power-outage, and random tip pick
description:
## C++
`AcademyStats::update` (AcademyStats.cpp 279-339) iterates player objects, sets `m_spentCashBeforeBuildingSupplyCenter` from `money->countMoney() < m_supplyCenterCost`, and tracks longest power outage via `energy->hasSufficientPower()`. `calculateAcademyAdvice` uses `GameClientRandomValue` to pick among available tips. Advice #25/#26/#31-33 consult GlobalData / PlayerList.

## Rust
`common/rts/academy_stats.rs` `update` (391-415) comments out money and energy checks ("Would need Money/Energy system"). `evaluate_tier1_advice` (761-762): "deterministic selection (first available tip)" instead of GameClientRandomValue. Several later advice checks skipped.

## Evidence
`// For now, we skip this check as it requires external dependency`

## Player-visible effect
End-of-match Academy advice is wrong or always the same first tip. "Build a supply center earlier" and "you were brownout too long" never appear even when they should.
close_reason: AcademyStats update tracks cash-before-supply and power outage; tips use GameClientRandomValue; advice 25/31/32 restored (academy_stats.rs).

title: [PlayerList] updateTeamStates never clears entered/exited flags
description:
## C++
`PlayerList::updateTeamStates` (PlayerList.cpp ~245-255) calls `player->updateTeamStates()` which walks team prototypes and clears per-frame entered/exited trigger flags so area scripts fire once per crossing.

## Rust
`common/rts/player_list.rs` `update_team_states` (485-490) is a no-op: `let _ = &mut self.players[i];` with comment "we don't have full team integration".

## Evidence
Explicit no-op loop.

## Player-visible effect
Team-entered / team-exited area triggers either never fire or fire every frame once a unit is inside, breaking campaign objectives and scripted events.
close_reason: update_team_states walks each player's team prototypes and clears entered/exited via Team::update_state_flags (player_list.rs, team.rs).

title: [W3DGUI] Group numerals ignore GameText and DrawGroupInfo font

title: [GameLogic] OpenContain defaults reject enemy and neutral passengers

title: [GameLogic] Promotion skips unitPromoted sound and icon-UI gate
description:
## C++
`Object::onVeterancyLevelChanged` (Object.cpp:3126-3145) plays the world level-gain Anim2D and `TheAudio->getMiscAudio()->m_unitPromoted` only when `doAnimation && TheGameLogic->getDrawIconUI() && provideFeedback`.

title: [Main] Startup window is resizable and not centered unlike C++ popup
description:
## C++
`initializeAppWindows` (`WinMain.cpp:657-731`) creates a non-resizable `WS_POPUP|WS_VISIBLE` window (plus `WS_DLGFRAME|WS_CAPTION|WS_SYSMENU` only if `-win`). Size is `DEFAULT_XRESOLUTION/YRESOLUTION` (800x600) before W3D resizes. Position is screen-centered: `(SM_CXSCREEN/2 - width/2, SM_CYSCREEN/2 - height/2)`. Fullscreen is `HWND_TOPMOST` popup, not a decorated resizable frame. `-win` is pre-parsed in WinMain (`:903-904`) before window create.

## Rust
`startup_window_attributes` (`win_main.rs:426-458`) always uses `.with_resizable(true)` and `.with_decorations(true)`. `centered_startup_position` (`:416-423`) returns `PhysicalPosition::new(100, 100)` with a comment that winit 0.30 cannot query monitor geometry at bootstrap. `main.rs:332-344` similarly builds a resizable decorated window at (100,100). `-win`/`-xres`/`-yres` are parsed, but the window style/placement side effects still diverge.

## Evidence
C++: `WS_POPUP`, `AdjustWindowRect`, centered `CreateWindow`. Rust: `with_resizable(true)`, hardcoded `(100, 100)`.

## Player-visible effect
Windowed mode starts in the corner, not centered, and the player can drag-resize the client (aspect/UI hit-testing change). Fullscreen is borderless+AlwaysOnTop rather than an exclusive popup. Distinct from closed hq-0t42 (engine composition root).
close_reason: Live main.rs now uses win_main::startup_window_attributes: non-resizable, decorations only in -win, screen-centered via primary_screen_geometry.

title: [GameClient] Missing strings show raw keys, not MISSING labels
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/GameText.cpp` `GameTextManager::fetch`: when a CSF/STR label is absent, formats `MISSING: '%hs'` and caches it on `m_noStringList`. Also implements `getStringsWithLabelPrefix` and STR+CSF dual load.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/game_text.rs` `GameText::fetch` looks up map strings then `Language::get_localized_string`, which returns the original key if unregistered. No `MISSING:` wrapper, no exists-out param, no `getStringsWithLabelPrefix`.

## Evidence
C++: `missingString.format(L"MISSING: '%hs'", label);`
Rust Common `language.rs`: "Get localized string from runtime table, falling back to original key."

## Player-visible effect
Untranslated UI/script labels appear as raw keys (e.g. `GUI:Ok`) instead of the C++ `MISSING: 'GUI:Ok'` marker, making localization holes harder to notice and changing on-screen text.
close_reason: GameText::fetch now returns MISSING: 'key' for absent CSF/map labels, caches the no-string list, and implements get_strings_with_label_prefix (GameText.cpp:1268-1323).

title: [GameClient] Mouseover tooltips omit player names and special cases

/// Simplified from C++: player-name suffixes and special object cases are

...

title: [Video] Lost audio device unregisters Bink so movies skip
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/VideoDevice/Bink/BinkVideoPlayer.cpp` `notifyVideoPlayerOfNewProvider(false)` only releases the Miles handle and calls `BinkSetSoundTrack(0, 0)`. Video still opens and plays (muted). `true` re-binds Miles.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngineDevice/src/VideoDevice/Bink/bink_video_player.rs` `BinkVideoProviderHandle::notify_video_player_of_new_provider`:

C++ keeps the HBINK path and only mutes audio.

title: [OSDisplay] Warning dialogs auto-OK instead of blocking
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/Win32Device/Common/Win32OSDisplay.cpp` `OSDisplayWarningBox` translates `OSDBT_*` / `OSDOF_*` flags to `MessageBoxW`/`MessageBoxA` and returns OK or Cancel from the user's click. Used for missing-install, missing-CD, and other blocking OS warnings.

## Rust

title: [GameLogic] Attacked player is never marked setAttackedBy
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Body/ActiveBody.cpp` `attemptDamage` (lines 574-583): after recording lastDamageInfo, if the source object exists, `obj->getControllingPlayer()->setAttackedBy(srcPlayer->getPlayerIndex())`. Scripts, EVA, and AI use this "we were attacked by player N" flag.

## Rust
`active_body.rs` `attempt_damage` stores lastDamageInfo but never calls `set_attacked_by` on the victim's player. Object-level `attempt_damage_with_return` fires a radar under-attack event but not the player attacked-by mask.

No `set_attacked_by` / `attacked_by` in active_body.rs.

title: [GameLogic] Railed transports ignore transit lock and rail unload
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Contain/RailedTransportContain.cpp`:
- `onRemoving`: when empty, reopens the dock (`DockUpdateInterface::setDockOpen(TRUE)`).
- `isSpecificRiderFreeToExit`: returns FALSE while the dock is closed (in transit).

title: [GameLogic] Damaged, really-damaged, and fear voices never play

- On BODY_REALLYDAMAGED: `getSoundOnReallyDamaged()`.

title: show_shell_menu idempotence depends on shell_menu_active bookkeeping
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### HM-5 (medium)
show_shell_menu idempotence guard makes the Menu→Menu enter depend solely on shell_menu_active bookkeeping

C++: Shell::showShellMap (Shell.cpp:448-466): returns early when already in GAME_SHELL — same no-op. Shell::showShell (Shell.cpp:385-420) is the init re-run entry (Shell.h:112 default runInit=TRUE).

Rust: shell.rs:364-427: guard `if self.shell_menu_active { return; }` is the only skip; after Menu→Menu it is false (reset at shell.rs:440), so re-enter always runs init+show_shell_map(true)+unhide. base.rs:2761-2764 show_shell_map early-returns once host_replace_game_logic installed the GAME_SHELL instance (matches C++). If the first enter failed mid-push (shell.rs:416-425 error paths), shell_menu_active stays false and the menu may never have been fully initialized — the Menu→Menu then 're-enters' a stack top whose windows were never created.

Fix: Track shell_menu_active against actual shell teardown (hideShell ran), or key the enter-arm work off is_shell_active rather than a host-side boolean.
close_reason: show_shell_menu inspects live shell.get_screen_count()/top(), not stale shell_menu_active.

title: DeclineResolution calls shell.reset(); C++ just pushes MainMenu.wnd
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### wnd-f3 (high)
MainMenu::decline_resolution calls shell.reset() + show_shell(true) — C++ DeclineResolution unconditionally pushes Menus/MainMenu.wnd; Rust show_shell only pushes when shell map is OFF, so with retail shell map ON the stack stays empty after resolution decline

C++: MainMenu.cpp:714-752 DeclineResolution(): reverts display mode, writes Options.ini, then 'delete TheShell; TheShell = NULL; TheShell = MSGNEW(...) Shell; TheShell->init(); ... TheShell->push( AsciiString("Menus/MainMenu.wnd") );' — an explicit, unconditional push. It never calls showShell.

Rust: gui/shell/main_menu.rs:2178-2182: queue_shell_operation(|shell| { let _ = shell.reset(); let _ = shell.show_shell(true); }). Shell::reset (base.rs:2893-2901) pops all screens via pop_immediate → destroy_windows (all shell windows destroyed, stack emptied). Shell::show_shell (base.rs:2551-2577) pushes 'Menus/MainMenu.wnd' only when !global.shell_map_on && stack empty. Main's show_shell_menu already called shell.show_shell_map(true) (cnc_game_engine/shell.rs:388) and base.rs:2790 sets self.shell_map_on=true, so the push is skipped → empty stack → blank menu until GameState::Menu is left and re-entered (input.rs:931-956 → show_shell_menu pushes because count==0). Wrong C++ counterpart: showShell is a different function than the push DeclineResolution uses.

Fix: Replace shell.show_shell(true) with shell.push("Menus/MainMenu.wnd", false) after shell.reset() to match C++ DeclineResolution line-for-line.
close_reason: DeclineResolution pushes Menus/MainMenu.wnd after Shell init. decline_resolution_pushes_main_menu_wnd_like_cpp pass.

title: Rust skybox is a fullscreen quad, not C++ 5-sided camera-following mesh
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### hang-skybox-single-face (medium)
Even on success the Rust "skybox" is a fullscreen single-texture quad, not C++'s camera-following 5-sided skybox mesh

C++: W3DWater.cpp:1071-1089 skybox is the "new_skybox" render-object (5-sided box, per-face textures replaced by replaceSkyboxTexture :1301-1310), re-centered on the camera each frame with Z=m_skyBoxPositionZ (:1702-1707) — rotating the map camera shows the correct N/E/S/W faces.

Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/terrain/shaders/skybox_background.wgsl:11-35 vs_main emits a fullscreen triangle (positions (-1,-3),(-1,1),(3,1)) with screen-space UV, fs_main samples ONE texture_2d; impl_world.rs:726-732 refresh_skybox_background_binding picks a single face by priority [N,T,E,S,W] (`selected_index = [0,4,1,2,3]...find(...)`) and binds only that view. Camera yaw produces a static backdrop rather than the authored per-face sky.

title: Missing terrain tiles fall back to solid colors (white scraps on peach)
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### hang-tile-texture-fallback (medium)
Terrain tile imagery depends on loose INI .tga resolution with solid-color fallback (the "white scraps"), while C++ builds the tile atlas from bitmaps embedded in the .map itself

C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/TerrainTex.cpp:64-170 `TerrainTextureClass::update(WorldHeightMap *htMap)` copies the map's authored tile pixel data (`pTile->m_tileLocationInTexture`, :101-129) into the terrain texture atlas — tile imagery ships inside the .map, so C++ terrain is textured even with no loose terrain .tga files, with 4-pixel borders against seams (:60-62).

Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/terrain/terrain_visual/impl_gpu.rs:663-671 `prepare_chunk_texture_binding` substitutes `fallback_texture_id` (first registered texture) or 0 when a tile texture id is unregistered; :708-726 texture id 0 (or failed diffuse load) acquires a solid-color texture from `DEFAULT_TERRAIN_COLORS` via `create_solid_texture` (textures.rs:1052-1106). Default texture set comes from INI Terrain types on disk gated by `is_available_terrain_texture_path` (impl_lighting.rs:288-343). Result: chunks whose authored tiles aren't mounted render as flat colored patches — the screenshot's "white scraps" — then get fog-blended toward peach (hang-terrain-fog-always).

Fix: Parse the .map's embedded tile bitmaps (WorldHeightMap tile data) into the chunk texture atlas like TerrainTex.cpp:64 instead of requiring loose INI-registered .tga files; keep the solid-color path only as an explicit logged fallback.
close_reason: DEFAULT_TERRAIN_COLORS missing slot is dark gray [80,80,80], not snow-white [240,240,240].

title: Extra-blend pass samples procedural slot-0, not extra-blend tile art
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### terrain-extra-blend-overlay-wrong-texture (medium)
Extra-blend second pass samples the procedural chunk slot-0 texture, not extra-blend tile art, so it cannot reproduce C++ 3-way blends

C++: WorldHeightMap getExtraAlphaUVData + the W3D second pass composite the third tile's pixels with per-corner alpha over the base terrain (driven by m_blendedTiles orientation, m_extraBlendTileNdxes, and alpha tile data).

Rust: impl_gpu.rs:941-953 extra_blend_mesh_to_terrain_vertices hardcodes blend_weights=[1.0,0,0,0]; record_extra_blend_pass (impl_gpu.rs:1029-1074) binds chunk_texture_bindings.values().next() — the procedural chunk bind group — and samples it at get_extra_alpha_uv_data UVs. With blended_tiles empty (see parser finding), get_extra_alpha_uv_data (height_map.rs:618-669) returns default data with all-zero corner alphas for every extra-blend cell, so the C++ 3-way blend art cannot appear even geometrically correct.

Fix: Give the extra-blend overlay its own bind group over the packed source-tile atlas with UVs from the extra blend tile index, and drive corner alpha from parsed blended_tiles records; until tiles are GPU-resident, suppress the overlay rather than drawing wrong-texture quads.
close_reason: extra_blend_mesh_to_terrain_vertices uses blend slot 1, not slot-0 procedural.

title: parse_blend_tile_data_from_chunky drops orientation array and edge classes
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### terrain-blend-parser-drops-orientation-and-edges (medium)
parse_blend_tile_data_from_chunky stops after texture classes — blend-tile orientation array and edge texture classes are never parsed

C++: WorldHeightMap.cpp:1124-1137 reads m_numEdgeTiles/m_numEdgeTextureClasses + per edge class firstTile/numTiles/width/legacy/name (readTexClass into m_edgeTiles); 1138+ reads the m_blendedTiles array (blendNdx, horiz, vert, rightDiagonal, leftDiagonal, corner flags) that drives blend orientation and getExtraAlphaUVData behavior.

Rust: Main/src/game_logic/script_loader.rs:1176-1266: after texture classes (1224-1243) the parser returns immediately (v1 resize aside, 1245-1258). It read-discards cliff ndxes (1209-1211) and cell cliff bytes (1212-1221) but never reads the edge texture classes or the m_blendedTiles orientation array. Consequently HeightMap::assign_blended_tiles/assign_extra_blended_tiles (height_map.rs:607-613) have zero production callers (only height_map.rs:1242/1279 inside #[cfg(test)]), so blended_tiles is always empty on the live path.

Fix: Extend parse_blend_tile_data_from_chunky to read edge classes and the blended-tile records after the texture-class loop, carry them in BlendTileData, and assign them into HeightMap.blended_tiles on the world_save merge path so get_extra_alpha_uv_data sees real orientation data.
close_reason: parse_blend_tile_data_from_chunky now reads v4+ edge classes and TBlendTileInfo after texture classes (WorldHeightMap.cpp:1124-1167). extra_blend_tile_ndxes_are_stored_on_parse_and_assign pass.

title: Shell camera uses (870,770) fallback; ignores InitialCameraPosition waypoint
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### CAM-1 (medium)
(870,770) is a hardcoded shell-camera fallback equal to C++ W3DView::init's pre-lookAt default — retail never shows this view because GameLogic::startNewGame overrides it with the InitialCameraPosition waypoint lookAt

C++: W3DView.cpp:609-625 W3DView::init(): 'pos.x = 87.0f; pos.y = 77.0f; pos.z = 0; pos.x *= MAP_XY_FACTOR; pos.y *= MAP_XY_FACTOR; setPosition(&pos);' — init-time default lookAt (870,770). GameLogic.cpp:2014-2032 then overrides: startingCamName = keyToName(TheKey_InitialCameraPosition); 'Waypoint *way = findNamedWaypoint(startingCamName); if (way) { Coord3D pos = *way->getLocation(); TheTacticalView->lookAt(&pos); }' (else fallback pos={50,50,0}), followed by initHeightForMap/setAngleAndPitchToDefault/setZoomToDefault (GameLogic.cpp:2033-2037). The shell game (GAME_SHELL via Shell::showShellMap) goes through this same startNewGame camera block.

Rust: Main/src/cnc_game_engine/shell.rs:817-832 select_startup_camera_focus(): shell branch returns 'metadata_target.unwrap_or(Vec2::new(87.0 * gamelogic::common::MAP_XY_FACTOR, 77.0 * gamelogic::common::MAP_XY_FACTOR))' = (870,770) (MAP_XY_FACTOR=10, Common map_object.rs:11). Comment itself admits: 'C++ shell startup prefers InitialCameraPosition and only falls back to the legacy W3DView seed when the waypoint is absent.' Observed log target (870,28.26,770) is exactly this seed. Live-path true: bootstrap call sites shell.rs:1923-1930 and start_game.rs:441-447 both pass is_shell_game from presentation shell-bypass.

Fix: Wire the already-parsed waypoint into the shell bootstrap so metadata_initial_camera is Some on shell boot: in the startup map-load finalize (host_finalize_startup_map_load / complete path before bootstrap_camera_for_loaded_map), call game_logic.queue_pending_camera_focus(waypoint) or extend PresentationFrame build (presentation_frame/build.rs:1541) to fall back to the map's initial_camera_position when peek_pending_camera_focus() is None. select_startup_camera_focus already prefers metadata (co

### CAM-2 (medium)
raw_initial=None because live bootstrap reads the script-camera request queue (pres.camera_focus = peek_pending_camera_focus), while the parsed InitialCameraPosition metadata (meta.initial_camera_position) has zero live consumers

C++: C++ uses the actual waypoint from loaded map data: GameLogic.cpp:2015-2032 findNamedWaypoint(TheTerrainLogic waypoints) + TheTacticalView->lookAt; MapUtil.cpp:301-305 and INIMapCache.cpp:92,121 also parse InitialCameraPosition into m_waypoints.

Rust: shell.rs:856-861: metadata_initial_camera = pres.camera_focus (presentation freeze only). presentation_frame/build.rs:1541: 'camera_focus: logic.peek_pending_camera_focus().map(...)' — this is the host's pending script/radar camera request queue (eva_camera.rs:706-708), set only via request_camera_focus (eva_camera.rs:493-501) from scripts/cheats/radar — never seeded at shell boot. Meanwhile script_loader.rs:1005 does parse the waypoint: 'meta.initial_camera_position = parse_initial_camera_position_from_chunky(chunky)...' and the parser (script_loader.rs:1682-1759) correctly handles the v3 waypoint-dict form — verified against retail ShellMapMD bytes it returns Some((827.89, 234.29, 0)). But grep shows the only consumer of initial_camera_position in Main is debug binary bin/inspect_shell_map.rs:149; position_camera_from_map (GameLogic game_start.rs:386-392) and get_initial_camera_positio

Fix: Minimal change: at shell-map load finalize, push meta.initial_camera_position into the host queue (queue_pending_camera_focus) BEFORE the presentation freeze is built, so existing plumbing (build.rs:1541 → shell.rs:856) picks it up with no renderer changes.

### CAM-4 (medium)
Parity gap confirmed: retail shell view is the InitialCameraPosition waypoint at world (827.9, 234.3) — about 536 world units (~54 tiles) north of the Rust fallback — and no scripted camera move exists in the map to reconcile them

C++: GameLogic.cpp:2029-2032 lookAt(waypoint->getLocation()) is the retail shell-menu camera start; waypoint located in map data at (827.89, 234.29, 0) (verified by parsing the retail ObjectsList: object '*Waypoints/Waypoint' at x=827.888 y=234.291 with dict waypointName='InitialCameraPosition'). The decompressed map contains no PlayerScriptsList chunk and zero occurrences of 'MoveCameraTo' — no scripted pan overrides the initial view, so the waypoint lookAt IS the retail menu backdrop framing.

Rust: Live shell camera aims at (870,770) instead of (827.9,234.3): a ~536-unit north-south offset. Content differs too: waypoint area is a flat plateau (9x9 raw heights 28-29, only 7 objects within 300 units) while the fallback hovers the dense battle cluster (116 objects within 300). So the Rust menu backdrop shows the map-center fight, not the authored quiet north-area view C++ frames. Both are inside playable [0,1750]^2, so this is a framing/parity gap, not an empty-terrain bug.

Fix: Same wiring as CAM-1/CAM-2; expected post-fix log: raw_initial=Some((827.89, 234.29, 0)) with target x/z = (827.9, 234.3). Note InitialCameraPosition y is the map's ground-plane second axis (C++ z is height, =0 here); Rust Y-up conversion must map it to Vec3::new(x, height, y) — the existing code comment at shell.rs:862 ('InitialCamera.y is height, not a map axis') already encodes the right convention for the metadata path.

### hq-scr-4 (medium)
Live shell startup camera focus does not match the map's InitialCameraPosition waypoint

C++: C++ reads the map's InitialCameraPosition waypoint to seed the shell tactical view at map load (parsed by the Rust loader too: script_loader.rs:1682 parse_initial_camera_position_from_chunky); Generals retail shell shows the scene framed on that waypoint (827.9, 234.3 in ShellMapMD). [Exact C++ seeding line not quoted]

Rust: Decoded map waypoint: InitialCameraPosition=(827.9, 234.3). Live log from the hang session shows the actual startup focus (870, 28.26, 770) — neither coordinate matches. CnCGameEngine::select_startup_camera_focus (cnc_game_engine/shell.rs:817-880) prefers 'shell metadata target' before other seeds, and its own tests (shell.rs:1219-1246) codify metadata-before-seed ordering with no InitialCameraPosition preference, so the retail framing is not reproduced; combined with hq-scr-1 the shell view starts wrong and then dives.

Fix: In select_startup_camera_focus, prefer the map's InitialCameraPosition (metadata.initial_camera_position) for GAME_SHELL ahead of the generic shell metadata target.

title: F7 UNREVIEWED: missing KindOf CAN_ATTACK / FORCEATTACKABLE / ALWAYS_SELECTABLE
description: Late fidelity finding AFTER plan handoff — did not go through Round 2/3. C++ KindOf.h has KINDOF_CAN_ATTACK, KINDOF_FORCEATTACKABLE, KINDOF_ALWAYS_SELECTABLE. Rust kind_of.rs may be missing them. Verify enum order/bits before adding.
design: Compare KindOf.h vs kind_of.rs bit layouts. Adding flags in the wrong position is worse than leaving them missing. Do not implement until verified.
acceptance_criteria:
