- [ ] Either closed as already present or promoted with bit-layout-safe plan
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-08-15 HEAD=1df030242 — STALE-PREMISE / already present. Closing.

kind_of.rs is not missing CAN_ATTACK, FORCEATTACKABLE, or ALWAYS_SELECTABLE. All three (and SHRUBBERY / LOW_OVERLAPPABLE) exist at C++ KindOf.h SOURCE-ORDER bit positions. Present since file add fd0795a9b (2026-03-12). Session SHRUBBERY/LOW_OVERLAPPABLE note is also already in-tree.

Side-by-side (KindOf.h source-order vs kind_of.rs):
- CAN_ATTACK: C++ bit 3 = Rust 1<<3 (kind_of.rs:19)
- SHRUBBERY: C++ bit 6 = Rust 1<<6 (kind_of.rs:22)
- ALWAYS_SELECTABLE: C++ bit 57 = Rust 1<<57 (kind_of.rs:73)
- LOW_OVERLAPPABLE: C++ bit 66 = Rust 1<<66 (kind_of.rs:82)
- FORCEATTACKABLE: C++ bit 67 = Rust 1<<67 (kind_of.rs:83)

KIND_OF_BIT_NAMES is a 120-entry exact match of KindOf.h including four ALLOW_SURRENDER names. Rust documents ALLOW_SURRENDER always-on.

Retail compile (ALLOW_SURRENDER undefined, KINDOF_COUNT=116) would shift ALWAYS_SELECTABLE/LOW_OVERLAPPABLE/FORCEATTACKABLE by -4 (53/62/63). That is a known stance (file comment + wave989), NOT "flags missing." Do NOT append. Do NOT reorder. If retail bit alignment is ever wanted, drop/skip the four surrender slots — that is a different M ticket (INI parse, save/load, every mask test).

GameLogic enums.rs KindOf is a semantic enum (not C++ bit layout) and already has CanAttack/AlwaysSelectable/ForceAttackable.
close_reason: STALE-PREMISE: CAN_ATTACK=1<<3, ALWAYS_SELECTABLE=1<<57, FORCEATTACKABLE=1<<67 already in kind_of.rs matching KindOf.h source-order. SHRUBBERY/LOW_OVERLAPPABLE also present. Do not add or reorder bits.

description: C++ FireWeaponWhenDamagedBehavior.cpp:147-195: onDamage fires the reaction weapon whenever its status == READY_TO_FIRE, once per damage event, no time debounce; Weapon::getStatus (Weapon.cpp:2736-2751) const-cast promotes to READY_TO_FIRE as soon as whenWeCanFireAgain <= frame, so with DelayBetweenShots 0 a second qualifying hit in the same or next frame fires again. title: TransitionDamageFX OCL drops C++ damageSource secondary pos (live host)
description:
LEFTOVER IS RIGHT; live contradicts leftover/C++.

C++ (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Damage/TransitionDamageFX.cpp:290-297,338-355): onBodyDamageStateChange resolves damageSource = TheGameLogic->findObjectByID(damageInfo->in.m_sourceID) and creates each state OCL via ObjectCreationList::create(m_OCL[newState][i].ocl, getObject(), &pos, damageSource->getPosition(), INVALID_ANGLE) — the damage-dealer position is the OCL secondary/target.

Leftover (GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/damage/transition_damage_fx.rs:1077-1085,1151-1158,1291): resolve_damage_source_pos models the source position; play_fx_for_state passes let secondary = damage_source_pos.unwrap_or(pos); ocl.create_with_angle(&ctx, Some(object), &pos, &secondary, INVALID_ANGLE, 0).

Live (GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/host_transition_damage_fx.rs:710-731): play_authored_transition_ocl calls ocl.create_with_owner_flag(&ctx, owner_guard.as_deref(), &leftover_pos, &leftover_pos, true, 0) — secondary always == primary. HostTransitionDamageFxEvent carries no damage-source field; callers (Main/src/game_logic/object/pose.rs:805 queue_transition_damage_fx_event -> take_played_transition_event_fx_ocl; Main/src/game_logic/world_tick/ai.rs:421-425 drain) never thread one. Live already snapshots a damage source for the DamageFX path (set_damage_fx_source/peek_damage_fx_source, set at combat.rs:2304) that could supply it.

Effect: OCL nuggets that consume secondary (leftover FireWeaponNugget fires toward it, AttackNugget attacks it, DeliverPayload uses it for formation vectors — GameLogic/src/object_creation_list/advanced_nuggets.rs:605-695) get the bone/loc world pos as their own target instead of the attacker position when a TransitionDamageFX OCL slot fires. Debris-only OCLs ignore secondary, so typical rubble debris is unaffected; fix is to thread peek_damage_fx_source (or last_damage_source) into play_authored_transition_ocl secondary. Note host_bone_fx_damage.rs:702-706 shares this helper (BoneFX side out of scope here).
notes: Acceptance: play_authored_transition_ocl threads the damage-source position as the leftover OCL secondary (falling back to pos when absent), matching leftover transition_damage_fx.rs play_fx_for_state and C++ TransitionDamageFX.cpp:354-355; existing tests keep passing.
close_reason: play_authored_transition_ocl now threads leftover_transition_ocl_secondary into create_with_owner_flag: peek_damage_fx_source leftover object pos, else snapshot pos, else primary (leftover play_fx_for_state / C++ TransitionDamageFX.cpp:354-355).

title: [Transport] onDie kills trapped riders before DieMux and DamagePercentToUnits
description:
## C++
`TransportContain` does not override `onDie`. `OpenContain::onDie` (`OpenContain.cpp:833-851`) is: `dieMux` applicability return → `processDamageToContained(DamagePercentToUnits)` → `killRidersWhoAreNotFreeToExit` → `removeAllContained`.

## Rust
`transport_contain.rs:503-507` `on_die` calls `kill_riders_who_are_not_free_to_exit` *before* `base.on_die`. Base then runs dieMux + damage% (`open_contain.rs:1192-1208`). DieMux-filtered deaths still kill non-exitable riders. Survivors that should take `DamagePercentToUnits` first are already `kill()`'d.

## Evidence
C++ `OpenContain.cpp:833-851` (Transport inherits). Rust `transport_contain.rs:503-507`. Distinct from closed `hq-agluh` (damage% implementation) and `hq-3r0u2` (OpenContain dieMux now present but run *after* Transport's extra kill).

## Player-visible
Battle Bus / airborne transport deaths that DieMux would ignore still destroy trapped riders. When DieMux applies, riders die via `kill()` before the percent-damage pass, so death type/FX do not match C++.
close_reason: transport_contain.rs on_die: DieMux then DamagePercentToUnits then kill_riders then removeAll (C++ OpenContain::onDie order)

title: [Transport] removeFromContain drops exposeStealthUnits so stealth riders stay cloaked

## Rust

Live `TransportContain::remove_from_contain` (`transport_contain.rs` ~1285-1338) discards `expose_stealth_units` (`let _ = expose_stealth_units`) and never `mark_as_detected`. Trait `harm_and_force_exit_all_contained` still passes true into that override.

## Evidence
C++ `OpenContain.cpp:621-633`. Rust Transport override drops the flag; base honors it. Distinct from closed `hq-4hckp` (evac `markAllPassengersDetected`) and `hq-3r0u2` (onDie expose).

close_reason: transport_contain.rs remove_from_contain honors exposeStealthUnits + KINDOF_STEALTH_GARRISON mark_as_detected

title: [Transport] unreserveDoorForExit arms OpenContain door-close C++ never plays
description:
## C++
`TransportContain::unreserveDoorForExit` (`TransportContain.cpp:504-508`) is an explicit no-op. C++ `OpenContain` base is also a no-op (`OpenContain.h:168`). Door-close countdown is armed only inside `exitObjectViaDoor` / `exitObjectInAHurry`.

## Rust
`transport_contain.rs:891-893` delegates to `OpenContain::unreserve_door_for_exit` (`open_contain.rs:1727-1733`), which arms `door_close_countdown = door_open_time` (default 1). `open_contain.rs:636-645` then sets `DOOR_1_CLOSING`.

## Evidence
C++ `TransportContain.cpp:504-508`. Rust `transport_contain.rs:891-893` + `open_contain.rs:636-645,1727-1733`. Callers: `production_update.rs` / `spawn_behavior.rs` exit reservation release.

## Player-visible
A transport that only *releases* an exit reservation (spawn/production abort, not a real unload) plays a one-frame door-close model condition C++ never plays.
close_reason: transport_contain.rs unreserve_door_for_exit is C++ no-op; no OpenContain door-close pulse

title: [FXList] doFXObj fail-open when local player index is invalid
description:
## C++
`FXList::doFXObj` (`FXList.cpp:794-797`) returns when
`primary && primary->getShroudedStatus(ThePlayerList->getLocalPlayer()->getPlayerIndex()) > OBJECTSHROUD_PARTIAL_CLEAR`.

`doFXPos` (`FXList.cpp:784`) is the cell gate: `getShroudStatusForPlayer(local, primary) != CELLSHROUD_CLEAR` returns. `PartitionManager.cpp:3017-3023` treats `playerIndex < 0` / missing cell as `CELLSHROUD_SHROUDED` (fail-closed). Closed `hq-2hak` fixed only the pos path.

## Rust
`fx_pos_cell_is_clear` (`fx_list.rs:588-603`) fail-closes when `player < 0` (hq-2hak).

`fx_obj_is_visible` (`fx_list.rs:605-616`) still **fail-opens**:
- `primary == None` → play (matches C++ `if (primary && …)`)
- `fx_local_player_index() < 0` → **play**
- then compares `get_shrouded_status(player) <= PartialClear`

`fx_local_player_index` (`fx_list.rs:576-582`) is `player_list().read().ok().map(|l| l.get_local_player_index()).unwrap_or(-1)`. `PlayerList` defaults `local_player_index` to `PLAYER_INDEX_INVALID` (`-1`) (`player/list.rs:17`, `player/mod.rs:55`).

Leftover `fxlist_integration.rs` `execute_fx_obj` (`:537-551`) uses the **cell** `CELLSHROUD_CLEAR` gate, not object `OBJECTSHROUD_PARTIAL_CLEAR`.

## Evidence
- C++ `FXList.cpp:794-797` vs Rust `fx_list.rs:605-616`
- Closed `hq-2hak` / `hq-f294` / `hq-x9dh` covered pos / integration pos, not this object-path fail-open
- Distinct from closed `hq-ctjtp` (DamageFX leftover Sound-only)

## Player-visible
While local player is unset (boot, map load, replay/observer edge, lock fail), fogged/shrouded unit death/hit/upgrade FX still play — sounds, particles, lights leak through FOW. Once a valid local index exists the object shroud compare runs.
close_reason: fx_obj_is_visible fail-closes when local player index < 0 (PartitionManager playerIndex<0 shrouded). Leftover execute_fx_obj no longer uses cell CELLSHROUD_CLEAR; fail-closes on invalid local index (FXList.cpp:794-797).

title: [AIPlayer] Host SW targeting ignores radiusCursorRadius
description:
## C++
`ScriptActions::doSkirmishFireSpecialPowerAtMostCost` (`ScriptActions.cpp:4152-4188`) sets `radius = 50`, then `if (power->getRadiusCursorRadius()>radius) radius = power->getRadiusCursorRadius()`, and passes that into `computeSuperweaponTarget`. Large SWs (nuke, particle cannon) therefore sample a grid sized to the real blast cursor.

## Rust
Live crate accepts the caller radius. Live host `try_fire_ready_special_powers` (`Main/src/ai.rs:2644-2645`) always passes `50.0`. Host `compute_superweapon_target` never reads `radiusCursorRadius`.

## Evidence
C++ `getRadiusCursorRadius()` vs host `compute_superweapon_target(..., 50.0, !sneak)`.

## Player-visible effect
Nukes / Particle Cannon / SCUD storms are aimed with a 50wu sample grid. The AI often dumps a city-killer on a dense 50wu pocket instead of the true blast-radius sweet spot.
close_reason: Main/src/ai.rs: SW targeting uses max(50, radiusCursorRadius) from SpecialPower residual table

title: [W3DModelDraw] MinLODRequired never skips extra draw modules
description:
## C++
`W3DModelDrawModuleData::getMinimumRequiredGameLOD` (`W3DModelDraw.h:304`) returns parsed `m_minLODRequired` (INI `MinLODRequired`, `:1184`). `Drawable` ctor (`Drawable.cpp:442-444`) skips a draw module when `TheGlobalData->m_useDrawModuleLOD && newModData->getMinimumRequiredGameLOD() > TheGameLODManager->getStaticLODLevel()`. Options "Extra Animations" maps to `m_useDrawModuleLOD` (`GameLOD.cpp:333`). Extra high-detail `W3DModelDraw` layers are omitted on low static LOD.

## Rust
Live parses `MINLODREQUIRED` into `min_lod_required` (`module_data.rs:131-133`) but `W3DModelDrawModuleData` never implements `get_minimum_required_game_lod` (base `ModuleData` always returns `Low`). `object_factory.rs:1007-1036` instantiates every draw-module entry with no LOD compare. Leftover Device module data does not expose or apply MinLOD either. `use_draw_module_lod` exists on GlobalData (`global_data.rs:104`) and options write it (`menu_callbacks.rs:1040`) — factory never reads it.

## Evidence
C++: `if (m_useDrawModuleLOD && getMinimumRequiredGameLOD() > getStaticLODLevel()) continue`.
Live factory: unconditional `factory.new_module(...)` for every draw entry.
Live module data: parsed `min_lod_required` unused.

## Player-visible
With Extra Animations off / low static LOD, extra high-detail ModelDraw layers (second anim modules, buildup scaffolds, extra FX meshes) still spawn and draw. Low-end option does not drop those modules the way C++ does.
close_reason: get_minimum_required_game_lod on W3DModelDrawModuleData; factory skips extra draw modules when Extra Animations off; leftover min_lod

title: [ChinookAI] Passenger auto-follow retargets every 10 frames, not only idle riders

Also uses `is_passenger_allowed_to_fire(None)` (container-wide) instead of the no-arg C++ check, then does not skip passengers who already have a victim.

## Evidence

title: [GameLogic] Prison bounty cash, score, and floating text diverge
description:

If the prison is `KINDOF_COLLECTS_PRISON_BOUNTY`, `unloadPrisonersToPrison` deposits that sum, `getScoreKeeper()->addMoneyEarned`, and `TheInGameUI->addFloatingText(TheGameText->fetch("GUI:AddCash"), pos, m_prisonBountyTextColor)` above the building.

## Rust

title: [Parking] Live hangar door hold uses ParkInHangars bool not per-stall door
description:
## C++
`reserveSpace` / `purgeDead` / `releaseSpace` call `ProductionUpdate::setHoldDoorOpen(ppi->m_door, true/false)` per reserved stall (`ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:349-351,143-144,414-415`). Each hangar door tracks its own space.

Release only clears hold when `airfield_parked_count == 0` (`airfield.rs:561-567`). Host door residual is a single door-1 cycle (`pose.rs:115-129`).

title: [Physics] Live update never destroys NaN-position objects
description:
C++: PhysicsBehavior::update (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:645-650) checks the integrated translation for NaN after moving the object and calls TheGameLogic->destroyObject(obj) — a corrupted physics state self-cleans instead of poisoning the world.

Rust: PhysicsBehaviorUpdate::update_simple (GameLogic/src/object/behavior/physics_update.rs:767+) integrates pos += vel with no NaN check on the result; only apply_force_with_obj validates INPUT force finiteness (physics_update.rs:331). NaN arising from arithmetic (e.g. mass clamp path in friction `mass_inv = 0` guard asymmetry, division in center-of-mass sin scaling, or a saved-game xfer NaN) propagates into set_transform_matrix forever; the object is never destroyed and calc_sleep_time's is_zero3d comparisons against NaN are all false, so it also never sleeps.

Evidence: grep in physics_update.rs update_simple — no is_finite/is_nan check between pos integration and set_transform_matrix; C++ counterpart at PhysicsUpdate.cpp:645-650.

Player-visible: an object whose physics goes NaN (instead of being removed like C++) permanently vanishes from the visible world while remaining selectable/targetable and never sleeping — leaks simulation time each frame.
acceptance_criteria: update_simple checks pos.x/y/z.is_finite() after integration and destroys the object via TheGameLogic like PhysicsUpdate.cpp:645-650 (DEBUG_CRASH + destroyObject).
close_reason: update_simple checks pos.x/y/z.is_finite() after integration and TheGameLogic::destroy_object_by_id like PhysicsUpdate.cpp:665-669 (NaN translation destroyObject).

title: [WorkerAI] Mine-clearing worker keeps its carried supply boxes
description:
## C++
`WorkerAIUpdate::aiDoCommand` (WorkerAIUpdate.cpp:1042-1050): after dispatching any command, `if (isClearingMines() && m_numberBoxes > 0) { m_numberBoxes = 0; draw->updateDrawableSupplyStatus(maxBoxes, m_numberBoxes); }` — a GLA worker that is carrying supply boxes drops them (visual box count reset) the moment it starts clearing mines, so it does not wander around disarming mines with a crate on its back and the carried state does not leak back into the supply chain.

## Rust
Neither path implements the drop: live host mine-clear engagement (`world_scripts/rebuild_dozer.rs` `find_dozer_bored_mine_target` -> `apply_engagement_decision_aware` -> Attacking; the Command_ClearMines flow in cnc_game_engine) never resets worker cargo/carried-box state, and the GameEngine leftover `supply_system/worker.rs` has no `is_clearing_mines` drop branch in its command handling (`update_drawable_supply_status` only fires on gain/lose box).

## Evidence
- WorkerAIUpdate.cpp:1043-1050 drop-boxes-on-clear-mines tail.
- rebuild_dozer.rs:944-1016 mine target acquire — no cargo/box reset.
- worker.rs gain_one_box/lose_one_box are the only writers of number_boxes; no mine-clear hook.

## Player-visible
A GLA worker ordered (or auto-bored) to clear mines keeps its carried supply box — C++ drops it — so the worker visually ferries a crate while disarming and the dropped-carry transition (drawable supply status) never happens.
close_reason: Live drop_worker_supply_boxes_for_mine_clear zeros stored supplies on ClearMines and bored mine acquire (C++ WorkerAIUpdate::aiDoCommand WorkerAIUpdate.cpp:1043-1050). Leftover WorkerAIUpdate::drop_all_boxes_if_carrying runs after execute_command when is_clearing_mines.

title: [Dozer] Repair docks at structure center within 14 units and floors heal rate at 8.75 HP/s
description:
## C++
Dozer repair is strictly percent-based and docks at the structure perimeter:
heal = maxHealth * RepairHealthPercentPerSecond / LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND per
frame (DozerAIUpdate.cpp:694-699). The dock/approach position comes from
findGoodBuildOrRepairPosition (offset majorRadius/2 + findPositionAround up to
100 away, lines 1836-1882) with arrival tolerance
max(MIN_ACTION_TOLERANCE=70, boundingSphereRadius + 15) in 2D (lines 316-319).

## Rust
Live host (world_objects/support_states.rs repair branch + host_repair.rs):
- Heal rate is dozer_repair_hp_per_sec(max).max(REPAIR_RATE * 0.25), i.e.
max(max_hp * 0.02, 8.75) HP/s. The flat dock rate quartered becomes a FLOOR,
so any structure with max HP < 437.5 repairs FASTER than C++ (a 200 HP
building: 8.75 vs 4 HP/s, over 2x).
- Approach/dock: support_approach_position returns
target_center + direction * min(selection_radius * 0.5, 14) and healing
requires distance to the structure CENTER <= HOST_REPAIR_INTERACT_RANGE = 14.
C++ docks at the sphere edge (~70+) and works from there; Rust must path to
within 14 world units of the center, effectively inside the footprint, and
blocked footprints (block_structure_object_path) make that destination
unreachable for large structures, leaving the dozer re-pathing forever
without healing.

## Evidence
- DozerAIUpdate.cpp:694-699 percent heal; :316-319 tolerance; :1855-1866 dock.
- support_states.rs ~1366-1380: heal floor and INTERACT_RANGE heal gate.
- host_repair.rs:39 HOST_REPAIR_INTERACT_RANGE = 14.0; :63 side_offset =
(selection_radius * 0.5).min(HOST_REPAIR_INTERACT_RANGE).

## Player-visible
Cheap buildings repair more than twice as fast as retail; dozers walk into or
onto the building footprint to repair instead of standing at its edge, and on
large blocked-footprint structures the repair never starts at all.

title: [Dozer] Dozer never backs off to the END dock after finishing construction
description:
## C++
`DozerAIUpdate::newTask` (DozerAIUpdate.cpp:1965-1980) sets the DOZER_DOCK_POINT_END to `position + normalize(position - target) * 5 * PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE_F` — 5 pathfind cells away from the building — and when construction completes `DozerActionDoActionState` moves the dozer there via `TheAI->pathfinder()->adjustToPossibleDestination(...)` + `aiMoveToPosition(&pos, CMD_FROM_AI)` (lines ~610-625). USA/China dozers thus back away from the finished footprint. (WorkerAIUpdate::newTask intentionally leaves END = dock position for workers — dozer-only behavior.)

## Rust
Live host: `world_tick/production.rs` `update_construction` completion path (lines ~254-268) sets the constructing dozer `set_target(None)`, `stop_moving()`, `AIState::Idle` — the dozer stays parked against the building. No END-dock offset exists anywhere in Main. The dormant leftover computes the END dock offset in `dozer_ai_update.rs::new_task` and moves at completion, but without the pathfinder `adjust_to_possible_destination` clamp (goal may sit inside another building).

## Evidence
- DozerAIUpdate.cpp:1971-1978 END offset; :610-625 completion move + adjustToPossibleDestination.
- production.rs:254-268 completion only stops the dozer.
- dozer_ai_update.rs new_task END offset present; handle_build_completion moves to End dock with no adjust.

## Player-visible
USA/China dozers stay wedged against every finished building in packed bases (no 5-cell backup), so they get stuck behind walls/adjacent structures and the next build order pathing often fails, unlike retail.
close_reason: Construction complete paths USA/China dozers to dozer_end_dock_position = dock + normalize(dock-building)*5*PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE_F (C++ DozerAIUpdate::newTask END dock 1992-1998 and DozerActionDoActionState aiMoveToPosition 627-635). GLA workers keep END=dock / stay put (WorkerAIUpdate::newTask).

title: [Display] Letterbox fade leftover shrinks bars; fade-out drops the bottom bar
description:
## C++
`W3DDisplay::renderLetterBox` (`W3DDisplay.cpp` 1987-2033), non-SLIDE_LETTERBOX: bar height is constant `((height - 9/16*width)*0.5)`; only alpha fades via `lbcolor = fade*255 << 24`. While enabled, both top and bottom bars draw. While fading out, the bottom `drawFillRect` is commented out — only the top bar remains, then `m_letterBoxEnabled` is forced FALSE when fade hits 0.

## Rust
Leftover `Display::queue_letterbox_and_filters` (`display.rs` 610-626) multiplies bar height by fade (`* 0.5 * fade`) and draws both bars. Live Main `queue_live_letterbox_and_cinematic_overlays` (`input.rs` 1744-1755) correctly uses constant height + alpha, but still draws both bars during fade-out (does not match the C++ commented bottom bar). Display leftover also paints a fake 24px white mouse square on top of letterbox.

## Evidence
C++ `W3DDisplay.cpp:2003-2022` (bottom fade-out draw commented). Rust Display `bar_height = (...)*0.5*fade`. Main `bar_height = (...)*0.5` with `color.a = fade`, both rects always.

## Player-visible
Display::draw letterbox (startup-movie / dual-world path) grows/shrinks the bars instead of fading alpha. Live cinematic fade-out shows a bottom bar C++ would already have dropped. Fake white cursor box can appear over letterbox on the leftover Display path.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Enable cinematic letterbox and watch the 1s fade-in/out.
2. On Display::draw path, compare bar height vs alpha.

## Acceptance Criteria
Letterbox bars keep constant 16:9 height and fade alpha over 1000ms. Fade-out matches C++ (top bar only unless SLIDE_LETTERBOX). No leftover white cursor quad.
close_reason: Letterbox constant 16:9 height + alpha fade; fade-out top bar only; leftover white cursor quad removed

title: [Production] Warehouse extra crippled/empty gates block Chinooks
description:
## C++
SupplyWarehouseDockUpdate does not override isDockOpen or isClearToEnter. Base isDockOpen is m_dockOpen only. Crippled docks stay "open"; action() returns FALSE only when m_boxesStored==0. AIDock keeps calling action. An airborne docker (Chinook) at a crippled warehouse still collects because setDockCrippled only kills non-airborne inside dockers.

## Rust
supply_warehouse_dock.rs is_dock_open returns !crippled && boxes>0. is_clear_to_enter and perform_supply_transfer also refuse crippled or empty. Trucks cancel/reroute instead of docking a no-op; Chinooks cannot collect from a crippled pile.

## Evidence
C++ DockUpdate.h: virtual Bool isDockOpen() { return m_dockOpen; }
Rust: Ok(!self.is_crippled && self.boxes_stored > 0)

## Player-visible effect
Empty warehouses look closed (collectors give up). Crippled piles block Chinooks that C++ still lets collect.

## Split hint
Keep C++ open/enter semantics; leave empty/crippled checks only in action() and setDockCrippled.
close_reason: supply_warehouse_dock.rs is_dock_open/is_clear_to_enter delegate to base; empty/crippled only fail in action().

Pass offset=true on Default/Queue exit paths and snap the Queue waypoint.

title: [GameEngine.cpp / GameClient.cpp / W3DDisplay.cpp vs Main cnc_game_engine: update order, Display::draw, FPS, l
description:
- TheAudio->UPDATE() runs after client+logic on the live frame instead of before the client
  C++: GameEngine::update order (GameEngine.cpp:735-752): VERIFY_CRC → TheRadar->UPDATE() → TheAudio->UPDATE() (736) → TheGameClient->UPDATE() (737) → propagateMessages → … → TheGameLogic->UPDATE() (752). Audio is drained before this frame's client/logic work (last frame's queued events fire)
  Rust: drive_frame (run_loop.rs:112-192) calls engine.update_with_timing() (client subsystems + host logic tick + HUD + post-presentation residuals) FIRST, then engine.host_update_the_audio() (run_loop.rs:186-192 → cnc_game_engine/audio.rs:168-173, Common THE_AUDIO.update()). The Main AudioManagerSubsystem also updates inside update_runtime_subsystems, but the live Miles-analog THE_AUDIO drain is the last stage of the frame
  One-frame audio timing shift vs retail: sounds queued by this frame's logic are drained/started in the same frame on the live path rather than at the top of the next frame; ordering-sensitive fades/loops observe post-logic state.

- Camera-tracking-drawable residual picks an arbitrary selected drawable and only exists on the disconnected crate path
  C++: GameClient.cpp:594-603: when TheInGameUI->isCameraTrackingDrawable(), TheTacticalView->lookAt(TheInGameUI->getFirstSelectedDrawable()->getPosition()) — deterministic first entry of the selection list
  Rust: update_camera_tracking_drawable (impl_update.rs:186-199) iterates self.drawable_map.values().find_map(… is_selected()) — a HashMap with unordered iteration, so with multi-selection the tracked target is nondeterministic per frame; helper is reachable only from crate GameClient::update, which is disconnected on the live host (residual guards assert !contains('game_client.update()')), and the live InGame tick has no camera-tracking equivalent
  Camera-follow-selected behavior is absent on the live path and, where ported, follows a random selected unit instead of the first selected drawable — C++ gives a stable follow target.

- Fast-time render throttling missing: no timeFast early-out, no 1-of-N render for timeMultiplier>1, no TiVO replay render skip
  C++: W3DDisplay.cpp:1741-1746: when !freezeTime && TheScriptEngine->isTimeFast(), draw updates camera movements, advances syncTime one step, and RETURNS without rendering; 1783-1795: when getTimeMultiplier()>1 a counter returns early so only every Nth frame renders; 1855-1858: in TiVOFastMode replays the render block runs only when frame%30==1
  Rust: Live render() executes the full pipeline every presented frame with dt scaled by visual_speed (input.rs:1421-1435 render_time_delta *= visual_speed; run_loop.rs:630-637 render_frame=true every windowed frame). tivo_fast_mode is consulted only for the soft script FPS limit (start_game.rs:1106-1109), never to skip renders; no multiplier-based frame skip exists in run_loop or render()
  During scripted time-fast cinematics and fast-forward replays the live path pays full GPU cost every frame instead of rendering 1-of-N; behavior is visually similar but the retail render-throttle contract (and its syncTime single-step semantics) is not reproduced.
close_reason: TheAudio UPDATE runs before client+logic; camera tracking follows first selected drawable; time-fast/multiplier/TiVO skip renders.

title: [WW3D2 SceneClass, CameraClass, Light/LightEnvironment, MeshClass render, HLod remaining, DX8Wrapper vs wgpu a
description:
- CameraClass::get_depth returns far−near instead of ZFar
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/Libraries/Source/WWVegas/WW3D2/camera.h:214-217 — `inline float CameraClass::Get_Depth(void) const { return ZFar; }`
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/Libraries/Source/WWVegas/WW3D2/crates/ww3d-renderer-3d/src/rendering/camera_system/camera.rs:525-528 — `pub fn get_depth(&self) -> f32 { self.far_clip - self.near_clip }`
  Wrong value by near_clip for any caller using camera depth as a world-space distance (retail treats Get_Depth as the far-plane distance, e.g. for fog/fade maxima).

- crate SceneClass port: render() applies no fog, runs no visibility/Prepare_LOD pass, builds no light environment, never processes the release list, and has no extra-pass wireframe mode
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/Libraries/Source/WWVegas/WW3D2/scene.cpp:150-186 (SceneClass::Render — DX8Wrapper::Set_Fog(FogEnabled,FogColor,FogStart,FogEnd) before rendering; EXTRA_PASS_LINE/CLEAR_LINE second wireframe pass with ZBIAS 7); scene.cpp:472-541 (Customized_Render — Visibility_Check when stale, On_Frame_Update for UpdateList, builds static LightEnvironmentClass from LightList: Reset+Add_Light+Pre_Render_Update); scene.cpp:556-583 (Post_Render_Processing unlinks and releases objects on the Release list).
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/Libraries/Source/WWVegas/WW3D2/crates/ww3d-renderer-3d/src/scene_system.rs:151-186 — render() only iterates render_order calling pre_render/render/post_render; no fog application (fog fields :52-56 are only exposed via apply_environment_to_render_info which render() never calls), no Visibility_Check/Prepare_LOD, no light-env rebuild from light_list, no release processing (release_list only cleared in clear():187-189 and unregister_all:343-347). PolyRenderType Point/Line/Fill are matched to the identical render call (:168-172) and ExtraPassPolyRenderType does not exist. Note: the live RTS scene (GameEngineDevice/src/w3d/scene.rs) is a separate port of W3DScene.cpp with its own custom-pass modes, so this gap is scoped to the WW3D2 SceneManagerClass path.
  Objects registered for release are never released; scene fog set via Set_Fog_* never reaches the frame unless the caller remembers apply_environment_to_render_info; per-frame visibility + LOD preparation and the LightList→LightEnvironment feed that retail performs inside every SceneClass::Render are missing from the crate scene, and the debug wireframe extra pass cannot be rendered.

- crate MeshClass::render is a no-op stub — C++ per-mesh frustum cull, shadow-alpha base pass, and override-flag handling have no scene-level equivalent
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/Libraries/Source/WWVegas/WW3D2/mesh.cpp:572-733 — MeshClass::Render: skips when outside frustum (CollisionMath::Overlap_Test(frustum,bbox), SKIN meshes exempt), renders base passes unless RINFO_OVERRIDE_ADDITIONAL_PASSES_ONLY, force-renders base pass for alpha meshes during RINFO_OVERRIDE_SHADOW_RENDERING (tree shadows, :636-651), defers to static sort lists when sort_level != NONE, registers additional material passes (Is_Enabled_On_Translucent_Meshes check), adds skins to DX8SkinFVFCategoryContainer, adds DecalMesh under Get_Decal_Rejection_Distance.
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/Libraries/Source/WWVegas/WW3D2/crates/ww3d-renderer-3d/src/rendering/mesh_system_impl/render_obj.rs:37-51 — RenderObjClass::render for MeshClass returns Ok(()) immediately ('actual draw occurs from a higher-level renderer'); special_render (:54-95) likewise returns Ok. The MeshRenderManager path (render_manager.rs render_pass/draw_material_pass/flush_static_sort_lists) implements pass drawing, but nothing reproduces the per-mesh frustum Overlap_Test exemption for skins or the shadow-rendering alpha base-pass special case at scene granularity.
  Through the crate scene, translucent alpha-tested meshes (trees/fences) contribute nothing to shadow/occlusion passes the way retail forces via RINFO_OVERRIDE_SHADOW_RENDERING + alpha shader detection; whether the live cascade fill reproduces this must be re-verified (its tests only cover hidden/decal skipping, render_manager.rs:1736-1783).

- Missing-texture fallback is a procedural checkerboard instead of w3d_missing_texture.tga
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/Libraries/Source/WWVegas/WW3D2/textureloader.cpp:1237-1245 (TextureLoadTaskClass::Apply_Missing_Texture binds MissingTexture::_Get_Missing_Texture()) and texture.cpp:261-267 (TextureBaseClass::Is_Missing_Texture compares against that shared texture); the retail asset is Libraries/Source/WWVegas/WW3D2/RequiredAssets/w3d_missing_texture.tga.
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/Libraries/Source/WWVegas/WW3D2/crates/ww3d-renderer-3d/src/rendering/texture_system/texture_loader.rs:378-382 create_missing_texture builds a checkerboard fallback; asset_texture_loader.rs:132-136 inserts that fallback into the cache for any failed load, so it is reused for every subsequent lookup of that name.
  Any asset the loader cannot resolve renders as a generated checkerboard rather than the retail magenta/black missing-texture TGA, and there is no Is_Missing_Texture-equivalent identity (shared instance) for code that special-cases missing textures.
close_reason: get_depth=ZFar; scene render fog+vis+light-env+extra-pass ZBIAS 7+release; mesh frustum/skins+shadow-alpha; shared w3d_missing_texture.tga

title: [Xfer/Snapshot: GameState, GameStateMap, Object xfer, Drawable xfer, TerrainLogic xfer, Player xfer, ChunkInpu
description:
- Player::xfer unknown upgrade name: Rust warns and consumes a dummy upgrade; C++ throws SC_INVALID_DATA aborting the load
  C++: Player.cpp:4038-4043: findUpgrade fails -> DEBUG_CRASH + throw SC_INVALID_DATA
  Rust: player/snapshot.rs:102-112: log::warn + construct __dummy__ Upgrade and xfer it to consume bytes, continue loading
  Corrupt/modded saves that C++ rejects now load silently with dropped upgrades — divergent failure behavior on bad data.

- GameStateMap::xfer clobbers pristineMapName to empty when re-saving a loaded save; C++ preserves the previously stored pristine map path
  C++: GameStateMap.cpp:331-353: pristineMapName is only overwritten when the current map is NOT in the save directory; on re-saves the member keeps the original pristine path and writes its portable form
  Rust: Common/src/system/SaveGame/game_state_map.rs:420-434: pristine_map_name starts as "" and is only filled when map is outside save dir, then unconditionally stored into save_info.pristine_map_name
  Second and later saves of a loaded game write an empty pristine name (and "" portable path) where C++ writes e.g. "Save\\xxx.map"; pristine-source tracking in the header is lost.

- GameStateMap::xfer save-side non-skirmish branch does not clear skirmish game info; C++ deletes TheSkirmishGameInfo on both save and load when mode != skirmish
  C++: GameStateMap.cpp:396-411: if getGameMode()==GAME_SKIRMISH xfer TheSkirmishGameInfo, ELSE delete TheSkirmishGameInfo (unconditional on mode, runs for save and load)
  Rust: game_state_map.rs:529-545: clear (notify_set_skirmish_payload(None)) only when `xfer.get_xfer_mode() == XferMode::Load`; a non-skirmish save leaves a stale skirmish payload
  Saving a campaign/solo game after a skirmish session retains skirmish slot data that C++ would have destroyed.

- GameState::xfer never refreshes campaign metadata on save; C++ writes current campaign side/mission number or empty side + INVALID_MISSION_NUMBER(-1)
  C++: GameState.cpp:1611-1636 (end of GameState::xfer): reads TheCampaignManager->getCurrentCampaign(); writes campaignSide+missionNumber, else empty side + INVALID_MISSION_NUMBER (= -1, CampaignManager.h:111); saveGame mission name from TheCampaignManager->getCurrentMap() (GameState.cpp:~510-521)
  Rust: Common/src/system/SaveGame/game_state.rs:1069-1082: xfers stale self.game_info.campaign_side / mission_number (defaults ""/0, never -1, no campaign lookup); save_game mission_map_name falls back to pristine_map_name instead of the campaign's current map (game_state.rs:524-531)
  Save header info diverges for every non-campaign save (missionNumber 0 vs -1) and mission saves can record the wrong map name.

- XferLoad::xfer_ascii_string decodes with from_utf8_lossy, replacing non-UTF-8 bytes with U+FFFD
  C++: XferLoad.cpp:157-180: reads raw bytes and AsciiString::set preserves them byte-for-byte
  Rust: Common/src/system/xfer_load.rs:161-179: String::from_utf8_lossy(&buffer)
  Save files containing locale-encoded (non-UTF-8) name/map/template strings are silently corrupted on load instead of preserved; subsequent saves rewrite the mangled names.

- XferSave::xfer_unicode_string length guard uses UTF-8 byte length; C++ checks wide-char count
  C++: XferSave.cpp:280-300: rejects when unicodeStringData->getLength() > 255, where getLength() is the WideChar count; len byte = wchar count
  Rust: Common/src/system/xfer_save.rs:229-247: checks unicode_string_data.len() (UTF-8 bytes) then writes utf16.len() as u8
  Strings with 129-255 wide chars whose UTF-8 encoding exceeds 255 bytes (e.g. accented/non-ASCII) are rejected by Rust but saved fine by C++ — spurious StringError on valid data.

- Object::xfer load clamps out-of-range trigger-area count; C++ throws SC_INVALID_DATA
  C++: Object.cpp:4220-4227: m_numTriggerAreasActive <0 or >MAX_TRIGGER_AREA_INFOS -> DEBUG_CRASH + throw SC_INVALID_DATA (load fails)
  Rust: object_xfer.rs:702: `let trigger_count = (self.num_trigger_areas_active as usize).min(MAX_TRIGGER_AREA_INFOS);` — silently truncates and continues; also leaves num_trigger_areas_active itself at the corrupt value
  Corrupt save data that C++ rejects instead half-loads with clamped trigger-area state; subsequent in-memory count no longer matches the number of entries actually read.

- DataChunkTableOfContents::read 'opened' condition diverges: Rust requires maxId>0 and marks opened on truncated TOCs
  C++: DataChunk.cpp:507-557: m_headerOpened = count > 0 && !s.eof() after reading all entries; also advances m_nextID past maxID
  Rust: Common/src/common/system/data_chunk_io.rs:35-70: early-outs opened=false when count<=0, breaks silently on short reads, then sets opened = max_id > 0 (ignores EOF state, no next_id tracking)
  A truncated/garbage TOC that C++ treats as unopened (isValidFileType false -> legacy path) can be treated as parseable by Rust (or vice versa for all-zero ids), changing map-file compatibility decisions at call sites like SidesList/TerrainLogic map loading.
close_reason: Player unknown upgrade throws; GameState campaign/pristine/skirmish; latin-1 ascii; unicode wchar length; trigger count; TOC opened/next_id

title: [INI parsers: INIObject, INIWeapon, INISpecialPower, INICommandButton, INIMappedImage — field tables, defaults
description:
- CommandButton UnitSpecificSound parsed as a sound FILE path instead of an audio event name
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/GUI/ControlBar/ControlBar.cpp:101 {"UnitSpecificSound", INI::parseAudioEventRTS} — stores an AudioEventRTS whose event name is later resolved against audio event definitions
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/ini/ini_command_button.rs:752-757 sets button.unit_specific_sound = AudioEventRTS::from_sound_file(token) — ini_misc_audio.rs:68 constructs it as a direct sound_file path
  The token (an audio event name like 'RangerVoiceAttackSpecial') is treated as a raw file path, so later event-name lookups or playback resolution cannot match the way C++ does.

- SelectPortrait/ButtonImage names are cleared without ever resolving the Image — C++ resolves to Image* first; post-load resolveNames loop commented out
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/Thing/ThingTemplate.cpp:1278-1288 resolveNames() does m_selectedPortraitImage = TheMappedImageCollection->findImageByName(name) (and buttonImage) BEFORE clearing the name strings; ThingFactory runs resolveNames for templates after INI load
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/thing/thing_template.rs:2758-2767 resolve_names clears selected_portrait_image_name/button_image_name with the findImageByName call left as a comment; the resolved-image fields are typed Option<Arc<FXList>> (1501-1502, wrong type) and always None; the post-load resolve loop in thing_factory.rs:862-864 is commented out, so resolve_names only runs on CreateOverrides loads (thing_factory.rs:719-722)
  There is no getSelectedPortraitImage()/getButtonImage() equivalent: object portraits/cameos are unresolvable from templates, and on override loads the names are destroyed without resolution (C++ destroys the name but keeps the Image). GameClient currently falls back to UpgradeTemplate button-image names (GameClient/src/gui/control_bar/control_bar_impl/types.rs:73-89).

- Object DisplayName stores the raw label instead of translated text (parseAndTranslateLabel)
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/Thing/ThingTemplate.cpp:92 {"DisplayName", INI::parseAndTranslateLabel} — translates the 'OBJECT:xxx' label through TheGameText into a UnicodeString
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/thing/thing_template.rs:2986-2990 sets self.display_name = UnicodeString::from(trimmed) — the untranslated label string
  get_display_name() returns e.g. 'OBJECT:Ranger' where C++ returns localized display text; any UI consumer of template display names shows raw labels.

- OcclusionDelay duration conversion uses round() instead of ceilf
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/INI/INI.cpp:1692-1697 parseDurationUnsignedInt stores ceilf(ConvertDurationFromMsecsToFrames(val)) — always rounds up
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/ini/ini.rs:1980-2001 INI::parse_duration_unsigned_int ends with frames.round().max(0.0) as u32 (also accepts non-C++ 'ms'/'s' suffixes); used by thing_template.rs OcclusionDelay arm (3192-3201)
  For durations that are not exact frame multiples (e.g. 340ms → 10.2 frames), Rust stores 10 where C++ stores 11, so occlusion delays run one frame short; the Main weapon loader's msec_to_logic_frames (ini_template_loader.rs:663-669) and rts/special_power.rs:643-650 both implement ceil correctly, so only the Common ini.rs path diverges.

- Lenient enum fallbacks swallow invalid tokens where C++ aborts the file (Buildable, BuildCompletion, EditorSorting, Geometry, Shadow)
  C++: ThingTemplate.cpp:120/126/130/203-205 parse Buildable/BuildCompletion/EditorSorting/Geometry via parseByteSizedIndexList / GeometryInfo::parse* which throw INI_INVALID_DATA on unknown tokens, aborting the object file load in retail
  Rust: thing_template.rs:3354-3399 parse_buildable_status (unknown → Yes), parse_build_completion (unknown → AppearsAtRallyPoint), parse_editor_sorting (3244-3276, unknown → None), parse_geometry_type (unknown → Sphere), parse_shadow_type (unknown → None) all silently substitute defaults
  Typos or bad tokens in these fields produce wrong-but-quiet defaults instead of the C++ load failure; on valid retail data the result matches, so impact is limited to malformed/custom INI.

- CommandButton Options bit-string edge semantics: no 'NONE' token, +/- mixing allowed, '---DO-NOT-USE---' bit unreachable
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/INI/INI.cpp:879-939 parseBitString32: 'NONE' clears the mask and stops, mixing bare and +/- tokens throws, and every listed name (including index 18 '---DO-NOT-USE---') is settable
  Rust: ini_command_button.rs:789-842 parse_command_field_options: resets only on the first bare token (matches), but 'NONE' is not recognized (errors as unknown), bare/+/- mixing is silently accepted, and '---DO-NOT-USE---' is skipped with `continue` so bit 18 can never be set; 'unused-reserved' is normalized to NEED_TARGET_PRISONER (same bit 3 as C++, correct parity)
  Options = NONE (used to clear a mask, e.g. in override blocks) fails the whole button parse in Rust instead of clearing; mixed-syntax lines that C++ rejects are accepted. Retail data avoids all three forms, so this is an edge-case divergence.

- Common ini_weapon WEAPON_STORE is a divergent parallel store that live loading populates but nothing consumes
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Weapon.cpp:1677-1710 WeaponStore::parseWeaponTemplateDefinition is the single store (per-name lookup, override via newOverride, projectile-name cleanup, debug FireSound validation)
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/ini/ini_weapon.rs:29-145 invents DamageType/AttackType enums ('physical/plasma/hitscan' — not retail DAMAGE_* names), defaults like recharge/rate_of_fire absent from C++; ini.rs:640-656 routes every live Weapon block into this store, shell.rs:1351-1363 loads Weapon.ini into it, but all gameplay reads use the GameLogic store (Main/src/assets/ini_template_loader.rs) — grep shows the Common store has no consumers outside its own tests
  Two weapon databases exist: the live INI dispatch fills the unused Common one (wasted work, misleading state, and its lenient invented parse would mask data errors), while the real store is populated by the separate Main loader — consolidating on the C++-faithful GameLogic parse (weapon_template.rs:2260, currently dead) would fix both this and the dropped-fields blocker.
close_reason: CommandButton UnitSpecificSound is an event name; portraits resolve via MappedImage; DisplayName translates; duration uses ceil; unknown enums abort; Options matches parseBitString32.

title: [GameAudio / GameSounds / GameSpeech / Eva / AudioEventRTS / live Miles-rodio device path (2D/3D play)] 5 mino
description:
- addAudioEvent never writes the chosen sound index back to the caller's event — sequential sound lists never rotate for reused events
  C++: GameAudio.cpp:424: ((AudioEventRTS*)eventToAdd)->setPlayingAudioIndex( audioEvent->getPlayingAudioIndex() ) after generateFilename(), so a caller that re-submits the same AudioEventRTS (persistent ambient/misc events) advances the index; generateFilename's non-random path (++m_playingAudioIndex) % size and random avoid-repeat (AudioEventRTS.cpp:332-348) rely on it.
  Rust: game_audio.rs:647 add_audio_event(&mut self, event_to_add: &AudioEventRts) takes the event by shared reference and only advances playing_audio_index on its internal clone (audio_event.generate_filename()); no writeback exists.
  For events reused across plays (drawable ambient sounds, stored MiscAudio events), sequential (non-AC_RANDOM) Sounds lists always restart at index 0 and random pick cannot avoid repeating the previous file — reduced/incorrect sound variety.

- Level-specific audio event infos never purged on reset
  C++: MilesAudioManager.cpp:444-457 reset() ends with removeLevelSpecificAudioEventInfos() (GameAudio.cpp:865-890 deletes every AudioEventInfo with isLevelSpecific(), i.e. map-authored DialogEvent/AudioEvent overrides), after stopping audio and clearing requests.
  Rust: game_audio.rs:517-556 reset() clears requests/fading/active events but leaves all_audio_event_info untouched; engine AudioEventInfo (audio_event_rts.rs:32-60) has no level-specific flag at all (only the separate DynamicAudioEventInfo type carries is_level_specific, dynamic_audio_event_info.rs:169-171, and it is not stored in the manager registry).
  Map-specific audio event definitions persist into the next map/skirmish; retail deletes them, so stale per-map volumes/limits/filenames can leak between games.

- LowPassCutoff off-screen occlusion never applied — parsed value dropped before reaching the engine
  C++: MilesAudioManager.cpp:1292-1310 initFilters3D(): when m_lowPassFreq > 0 and !isOnScreen(pos), AIL_set_3D_sample_occlusion(sample, 1.0f - m_lowPassFreq) muffles off-screen 3D sounds.
  Rust: ini_audio_event_info.rs:527-533 parses LowPassCutoff into low_pass_freq, but to_engine_info (ini_audio_event_info.rs:265-298) has no field for it and EngineAudioEventInfo (audio_event_rts.rs:32-60) does not carry it; RodioPlaybackHook has no filter path.
  Off-screen 3D sounds play at full fidelity instead of being low-pass occluded per the INI value; positional audio loses its off-screen muffling cue.

- Force-played briefing speech multiplies the speech slider twice
  C++: MilesAudioManager.cpp:2971-3017 friend_forcePlayAudioEventRTS(): AIL_quick_load_and_play with AIL_quick_set_volume(haud, event.getVolume() * getVolume(AudioAffect_Speech), 0.5) — a raw handle outside the manager, volume applied exactly once.
  Rust: game_audio.rs:1493-1545 friend_force_play_audio_event_rts() sets event volume = volume * speech slider, then routes through hook.play(), and RodioPlaybackHook::play computes miles_get_effective_volume() (game_audio.rs:2462-2472) which multiplies the category slider again (speech×speech for briefings, speech×sound for effects).
  Mission-briefing audio plays at squared slider gain (e.g. 55% → ~30%) instead of the retail single application — briefings audibly quieter than retail when sliders < 100%.

- Chat music toggle mutes the flag instead of stopping/resuming the playing stream
  C++: CommandXlat.cpp:4557-4562: if TheAudio->isMusicPlaying() → TheAudio->stopAudio(AudioAffect_Music) (MilesAudioManager.cpp:471-524 stops the music stream now) else TheAudio->resumeAudio(AudioAffect_Music) (unpauses it).
  Rust: GameClient/src/message_stream/meta_event_impl/dispatch.rs:937-945: audio.set_on(false, AudioAffect::Music) / set_on(true, ...) — flips the isOn gate used by add_audio_event only; the currently playing track keeps playing (or never resumes).
  'Stopping Music'/'Resuming Music' command does not actually stop or resume the current track — it only blocks/future-allows new music, so the message lies about the audible state.
close_reason: index writeback, level-specific purge, off-screen low-pass, single speech multiply, music stop/resume

title: [Drawable.cpp + W3D draw modules not already beaded: W3DModelDraw, W3DDependencyModelDraw, W3DOverlordTank/Tru
description:
- hideAllHeadlights never applied — HEADLIGHT sub-objects stay visible in daytime
  C++: W3DModelDraw.cpp:2824-2840 hideAllHeadlights(hide) walks sub-objects and Set_Hidden on any whose name contains 'HEADLIGHT'; called at the end of setModelState (:3157) using m_hideHeadlights which replaceModelConditionState sets from MODELCONDITION_NIGHT (:3162).
  Rust: draw.rs:40/:102 hide_headlights field is assigned in replace_model_condition_state (trait_impl.rs:517-518: hide_headlights = !condition.contains(NIGHT)) but never read; no HEADLIGHT sub-object visibility logic exists anywhere in the draw modules (sub_object_visibility only carries the authored HideShowVec).
  Day-time models keep glowing headlight sub-objects visible; night/day headlight show/hide is stored but has no effect.

- W3DScienceModelDraw hidden latch never recovers after the player acquires the RequiredScience
  C++: W3DScienceModelDraw.cpp:52-70 doDrawModule: while the local player lacks the science it calls setHidden(TRUE) — which only hides the render object (W3DModelDraw::setHidden :1799-1819, no stored latch) — and once the player has the science, doDrawModule proceeds to W3DModelDraw::doDrawModule; recovery happens because setModelState recreates the render object unhidden on any condition-state change.
  Rust: w3d_science_model_draw.rs:156-176 calls DrawModule::set_hidden(&mut self.base, true), which sets base.hidden permanently; W3DModelDraw::do_draw_module early-returns while hidden (trait_impl.rs:30-32) and no code ever clears base.hidden when the science is later acquired (set_model_state does not reset the flag).
  Once a RequiredScience model is hidden for a frame, it stays invisible forever in the Rust port even after the local player researches the science, where C++ would resume rendering (render-object recreation on state change).

- Laser tiling aspect ratio hardcoded to 1.0 (texture never loaded) — Tile factor wrong for non-square textures
  C++: W3DLaserDraw.cpp:136-149 constructor loads the texture and computes m_textureAspectRatio = surfaceDesc.Width/surfaceDesc.Height; doDrawModule :340-346 tileFactor = length/width*m_textureAspectRatio*m_tilingScalar.
  Rust: GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/draw/w3d_laser_draw.rs:516-520 init_lines sets self.texture_aspect_ratio = 1.0 unconditionally (no texture asset load); tile_factor at :745-748 uses that 1.0 ratio.
  Beams authored with Tile=Yes and a non-square texture tile at the wrong density (aspect ignored). Distinct from bead hq-980r (texture scroll never applied) — this is the tiling density computed from texture dimensions.

- W3DModelDraw::preloadAssets not implemented — every wrapper's preload call lands on a no-op default
  C++: W3DModelDraw.cpp:3883-3890 preloadAssets preloads the condition-state models/animations for the time of day; invoked through Drawable::preloadAssets (Drawable.cpp:4725-4730) at map load.
  Rust: impl Module for W3DModelDraw (trait_impl.rs:1-27) overrides only on_drawable_bound_to_object/on_delete/name keys — no preload_assets. Every sibling module delegates into that hole: w3d_dependency_model_draw.rs:175-177, w3d_science_model_draw.rs:137-139, w3d_overlord_tank_draw.rs:125-127, w3d_overlord_truck_draw.rs:95-97, w3d_overlord_aircraft_draw.rs:95-97, w3d_tank_draw.rs:554-556, w3d_truck_draw.rs:590-592, w3d_projectile_draw.rs:236-238, w3d_supply_draw.rs:138-140 all call self.base.preload_assets(...), which resolves to the trait-default no-op.
  Models and animations are never preloaded during map load for the dominant draw module family, so first-appearance streaming hitches / pop-in replace C++ preloading (no wrong frame, but a visible load-behavior gap).

- W3DDependencyModelDraw stealth-imitation only fires when the dependency-cleared flag latches, and doDrawModule skips imitate when enclosing — parity confirmed OK (no gap)
  C++: W3DDependencyModelDraw.cpp:40-98 doDrawModule draws base when cleared, resets flag, then imitateStealthLook from non-enclosing container's drawable; xfer saves m_dependencyCleared (:155-170).

title: [ParticleSys, FXList, GameClientFX, Weather, Snow, DynamicLight, Ripple (particle/FX/weather/light/ray effects
description:
- Particle uplink cannon scorch types off by one — can pick SHADOW_SCORCH, never SCORCH_1
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Include/Common/GameType.h:70-76 — SCORCH_1=0 .. SCORCH_4=3, SHADOW_SCORCH=4; ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:603-604 scorchID = (Scorches)GameClientRandomValue(SCORCH_1, SCORCH_4)
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/behavior/particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:48-49 `const SCORCH_1: i32 = 1; const SCORCH_4: i32 = 4;` used at :1487-1488 game_client_random_value(SCORCH_1, SCORCH_4) → add_scorch
  The cannon's ground scorch decal is chosen from 1..4, so SCORCH_1 never appears and 1/4 of the time it stamps SHADOW_SCORCH (the building-shadow scorch texture) instead of a burn mark.

- StartSizeRate accumulated bonus: applied before sizeCoeff/particleScale scaling and advanced once per burst instead of per particle
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/System/ParticleSys.cpp:1782-1788 — info.m_size = startSize*sizeCoeff*particleScale; THEN info.m_size += m_accumulatedSizeBonus; m_accumulatedSizeBonus += m_startSizeRate.getValue() runs inside generateParticleInfo per particle (each successive particle in a burst grows)
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/effects/particle_system.rs:1966-1969 — size = (start_size.sample() + accumulated_size_bonus) * size_coeff * particle_scale (bonus gets scaled too), and the bonus is advanced once per burst in emit_particles (particle_system.rs:1093-1101), not per particle
  Progressively-growing effect plumes (fires, growing smoke) have wrong per-particle growth timing and wrong magnitude whenever sizeCoeff/particleScale differ from 1.

- Per-particle wind randomness sampled from 0.5..=1.5 instead of C++ 0.7..1.3
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/System/ParticleSys.cpp:1805 — info.m_windRandomness = GameClientRandomValueReal(0.7f, 1.3f)
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/effects/particle_system.rs:1986 — particle_info.wind_randomness = rng.gen_range(0.5..=1.5)
  Wind-swayed particles (WIND_MOTION systems) sway ~43% wider than retail at the extremes.

- tint_all_colors tints the first color key, which C++ deliberately skips
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/System/ParticleSys.cpp:744-752 — 'This tints all but the first colorKey!!!' loop starts at key=1
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/effects/particle_manager.rs:463-470 — `for color_key in &mut self.color_keys` tints all 8 keys including index 0
  House-color tinted particle systems (faction-tinted muzzle flashes/smoke via tintParticleSystemsAllColors) shift their spawn color too, changing the first-frame look of every tinted FX.

- Every particle system delays its first burst by a random BurstDelay
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/System/ParticleSys.cpp:1095-1096 — constructor sets m_burstDelayLeft = 0, so the first update emits immediately and only then schedules m_burstDelay.getValue()
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/effects/particle_system.rs:1334 — `burst_delay_left: info.burst_delay.sample() as u32` in ParticleSystem::new, so emit_particles (particle_system.rs:1085-1089) counts the delay down before the first burst
  Muzzle flashes, explosion puffs and one-shot FX start one BurstDelay late (e.g. BurstDelay 20-40 frames ≈ 0.7-1.3s of dead air after the triggering event).

- IsOneShot systems stop emitting after the first burst — behavior C++ never implements
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/System/ParticleSys.cpp — m_isOneShot is only parsed (INI field :2585), copied (:1082) and xfer'd (:778); no runtime code reads it, so emission continues on BurstDelay cadence until SystemLifetime
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/effects/particle_system.rs:1102-1105 — emit_particles does `if info.is_one_shot { self.is_stopped = true; }` after the first burst
  Any IsOneShot=Yes system with a periodic BurstDelay and SystemLifetime=0 (forever) repeats in retail but fires exactly once in Rust — attached loops like pilot flames can vanish permanently.

- ParticleUpTowardsEmitter orientation is rotated 90 degrees from C++
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/System/ParticleSys.cpp:363-368 with angleBetween (:3390-3416) — angle = signed acos(dot((0,1), dir)) i.e. measured from +Y; for dir=(0,1) the result is 0 so m_angleZ = PI
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/effects/particle_system.rs:246-262 — `let angle_to_emitter = norm_y.atan2(norm_x)` measures from +X; for dir=(0,1) it yields PI/2 so angle_z = 3*PI/2
  Particles flagged IsParticleUpTowardsEmitter (flame tongues, sparks leaning toward their emitter) are rotated a constant +90 degrees versus retail.

- IsEmitAboveGroundOnly parsed but never enforced at emission
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/System/ParticleSys.cpp:2000 — particle creation is skipped when `!m_isEmitAboveGroundOnly || (info->m_pos.z >= TheTerrainLogic->getGroundHeight(info->m_pos.x, info->m_pos.y))` fails
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/effects/particle_manager.rs:1121-1149 can_create_particle_for_system checks use_fx, LOD priority, and count caps but performs no ground-height comparison; is_emit_above_ground_only is only parsed (particle_ini_loader.rs:491-493) and xfer'd (particle_system.rs:619-620)
  Systems meant to only emit above ground (cliff-side vents, under-bridge suppression) spawn particles below terrain where they are invisible or poke through geometry.

- FXList ParticleSystem nugget resolves invented presets before INI templates
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/FXList.cpp:575-578 — reallyDoFX only does TheParticleSystemManager->findTemplate(m_name); no fallback table exists
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/effects/fxlist_integration.rs:596-604 — `let template = if let Some(preset) = particle_presets::get_preset_by_name(&self.template_name) { preset } else if let Some(tmpl) = manager.find_template(...) }`; particle_presets.rs:584-603 defines 12 hand-written templates (SmallExplosion, MuzzleFlash, Fire, DustCloud, ...)
  Any retail particle system whose name collides with one of the 12 invented presets is replaced by approximated parameters (counts, colors, lifetimes) instead of the INI-defined values, silently overriding authored data on the live FXList path.

- SMUD heat-distortion routing: name-prefix hack not implemented; smudges drawn as flat decals
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DParticleSys.cpp:140-166 — systems whose particle type name starts with 'SMUD' (DWORD 0x44554D53) are routed into TheSmudgeManager hardware heat-distortion smudges when getHardwareSupport() && m_useHeatEffects
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/w3d/particles.rs:96-133 collect_smudge_render_items routes only `info.particle_type == ParticleType::Smudge` and renders them via renderer.render_decals (flat decal pipeline); no particle-name prefix check exists
  Retail smudge FX declared as Type=PARTICLE with SMUD*-prefixed textures (the case the C++ hack exists for) render as ordinary alpha particles, and even Type=SMUDGE systems get a gray decal instead of the refraction shimmer over fires/jet exhausts.
close_reason: Particle parity: size bonus per particle, wind 0.7-1.3, tint skips key0, first burst immediate, IsOneShot does not stop, +Y emitter angle, above-ground emit, INI templates not presets, SMUD prefix heat smudges; PUC SCORCH_1=0 by W2ObjMod.

title: [Weapon.cpp, WeaponSet, DamageFX, Armor, ArmorSet, ProjectileStream, FireWeaponUpdate, LockWeapon (PORT_FILE_M
description:
- Laser scatter-miss still damages the intended victim (and hit test uses max scatter, not the rolled value)
  C++: Weapon.cpp:1002-1032: on laser branch, if randomized scatterRadius exceeds primary/secondary damage radius, 'damageID = INVALID_ID' and createLaser targets the ground — the shot misses; comparison uses the POST-randomization scatterRadius (line 979 reassigns it)
  Rust: weapon_instance.rs:1521-1548 ContinuousBeam branch calls inflict_damage_if_requested(source, target_obj_id, ...) unconditionally — damage_id is always the victim; there is no scatter-miss path, and where the private stack compares (weapon_template.rs:837-841) it compares the pre-random max scatter_radius instead of the rolled amount
  Laser weapons with ScatterRadius authored larger than their damage radius never miss in Rust

- ShareWeaponReloadTime not propagated per shot (only on clip reload)
  C++: Weapon.cpp:2655-2667: after every shot, if sourceObj->isReloadTimeShared(), ALL weapon slots get setPossibleNextShotFrame(whenWeCanFireAgain) and setStatus(BETWEEN_FIRING_SHOTS)
  Rust: weapon_instance.rs:300-361 apply_post_fire_state (canonical per-shot bookkeeping) has no shared-reload propagation; sharing only happens in reload_with_bonus (weapon_instance.rs:592-624) on clip reload, setting ReloadingClip
  Multi-weapon units authored with ShareWeaponReloadTime (jets/aircraft) fire all weapons in the same frame instead of sharing one cooldown per shot

- onWeaponBonusChange is a stub — ROF bonus changes never rescale in-flight cooldowns
  C++: Weapon.cpp:1935-1976 Weapon::onWeaponBonusChange: recomputes clip reload / shot delay with the new bonus and rescales m_whenWeCanFireAgain relative to m_whenLastReloadStarted; invoked for all weapons via WeaponSet::weaponSetOnWeaponBonusChange (WeaponSet.cpp:393-403)
  Rust: weapon_instance.rs:821-824 on_weapon_bonus_change: '// Implementation would recalculate timing based on new bonuses' -> Ok(()). weapon_set.rs:1101-1107 dutifully calls it for every slot, so the no-op is on the live call path (implemented only in private weapon.rs:875)
  Picking up a rate-of-fire crate/bonus mid-reload leaves the pending cooldown at the old slower rate until the next clip

- getPercentReadyToFire reports 0.5 during PRE_ATTACK instead of 0.0
  C++: Weapon.cpp:2291-2333 Weapon::getPercentReadyToFire: 'case OUT_OF_AMMO: case PRE_ATTACK: return 0.0f;'
  Rust: weapon_instance.rs:673-674: 'WeaponStatus::PreAttack => 0.5, // Pre-attack is halfway ready' — invented value; feeds getMostPercentReadyToFireAnyWeapon used by AI/jet reload UI
  Weapon-readiness percentages (AI decisions, ammo/readiness pips) read half-ready during aim delays

- chooseBestWeaponForTarget missing Jarmen Kell KILLPILOT/Hero surgical skip
  C++: WeaponSet.cpp:711-719: inside the damage-estimate loop, 'if( weapon->getDamageType() == DAMAGE_KILLPILOT && source->isKindOf( KINDOF_HERO ) && m_curWeapon == PRIMARY_WEAPON && specificSlot == -1 ) continue;' so the snipe weapon is not auto-chosen against vehicles
  Rust: weapon_set.rs:633-860 choose_best_weapon_for_target has no KillPilot/Hero case (the slot-specific path exists separately in action_manager.rs:1688-1705, but auto-choose per-frame is unguarded)
  Hero units with a KILLPILOT primary auto-target vehicles with the snipe weapon instead of requiring the explicit snipe mode

- Canonical is_within_attack_range uses center-to-center distance, ignoring bounding-sphere radii C++ subtracts
  C++: Weapon.cpp:2135-2150 isWithinAttackRange uses ThePartitionManager->getDistanceSquared(source, victim, FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_2D) which subtracts both objects' bounding-circle radii, effectively extending range by the hull sizes; ATTACK_RANGE_CALC_TYPE is 2D (Weapon.cpp:70-75)
  Rust: weapon_instance.rs:406-448 is_within_attack_range computes raw center distance vs template range (no radii); a sibling get_attack_distance (weapon_instance.rs, adds radii) exists but the range gate used by check_can_fire (line ~1352) is the plain center version
  Units must close to center-to-center weapon range against large buildings/units, losing the retail bounding-radius tolerance (visible as units shuffling closer before opening fire)

- Divergent duplicate ArmorSetType enum (Default added, WEAK_VERSUS_BASEDEFENSES/SECOND_LIFE missing) beside the correct body one
  C++: Include/GameLogic/ArmorSet.h:19-30 ArmorSetType: VETERAN=0, ELITE=1, HERO=2, PLAYER_UPGRADE=3, WEAK_VERSUS_BASEDEFENSES=4, SECOND_LIFE=5, CRATE_UPGRADE_ONE=6, CRATE_UPGRADE_TWO=7
  Rust: GameLogic/src/common/types/enums.rs:440-447 ArmorSetType { Default, Veteran, Elite, Hero, Player, CrateUpgradeOne, CrateUpgradeTwo } — spurious Default (colliding with bit 0 = Veteran if used as index), 'Player' naming, and the two missing conditions; the correct 8-value copy lives at object/body/body_module.rs:40-49 and is the one bodies use; common::bit_flags.rs:271-275 has the right bit indices, so the enums.rs variant is a second, wrong convention imported via object_impl_imports.rs:66
  Any code path resolving armor sets through the common::types::ArmorSetType enum cannot represent WEAK_VERSUS_BASEDEFENSES or SECOND_LIFE conditions and misindexes Veteran as Default
close_reason: Implemented C++ Weapon.cpp / ArmorSet parity on the canonical Rust weapon/armor stack

  Rust: gui/ingame_ui/leftover.rs:89-99 create_garrison_hint only pushes an invented HintData line; no drawable notification path exists

  C++: InGameUI.h:371 toggleMessages flips m_messagesOn which only gates postDraw rendering (3429); addMessageText (2061) has no gate — messages keep accumulating while hidden
  Rust: gui/ingame_ui/messages.rs:16-19 add_message_text returns early when !messages_enabled, so messages arriving while 'off' are dropped permanently
  Toggling messages off then on loses every message sent in between; C++ would show them

- InGameUI playMovie/playCameoMovie allocate no video stream/buffer and never decompress frames
  C++: InGameUI.cpp:3874-3898 playMovie opens TheVideoPlayer stream + createVideoBuffer/allocate; update() 1600-1616 decompresses/renders per frame and auto-stops when frameIndex()==0; playCameoMovie 3929-3956 attaches the cameo buffer to ControlBar.wnd:RightHUD via winData->setVideoBuffer; stopCameoMovie 3959-3980 detaches it
  Rust: gui/ingame_ui/leftover.rs:385-409 play_movie/stop_movie/play_cameo_movie/stop_cameo_movie only set an Option<String> flag and call window_video_manager.stop_all_movies(); no stream open, no buffer, no per-frame decompress, no loop-stop, no RightHUD buffer attach (radar movies are rerouted through a separate path in core/subsystems.rs:1560 play_radar_movie)
  The mapped InGameUI pair is a name-flag stub; cameo movie never binds a video buffer to the RightHUD window and nothing in this class ever decodes a frame

- setRadiusCursor drops scatter/continue radii, weapon slot, shortcut most-ready object, and radar coordinate path
  C++: InGameUI.cpp:1172-1274 — radius per type: ATTACK_SCATTER_AREA = scatterRadius+scatterTargetScalar, ATTACK_CONTINUE_AREA/CLEARMINES = continueAttackRange (1218-1227), guard range, specPowTempl->getRadiusCursorRadius(); source object is findMostReadyShortcutSpecialPowerOfType for shortcut commands (1183-1189); decal tinted by the object's controlling player; handleRadiusCursor 1275-1312 maps mouse via TheRadar->screenPixelToWorld when radar on, else screenToTerrain

  Scatter-area/continue-attack radius cursors show wrong radius (or the pending special power's), decal house-color can come from the wrong player, and the decal never follows the cursor over the radar minimap

- objectChangedTeam superweapon re-registration and hiddenByScience computation missing in crate
  C++: InGameUI.cpp:612-651 objectChangedTeam removes/re-adds SW timers per behavior module on team change (and auto-adds at frame 0 for non-commandcenters); addSuperweapon 548-580 computes hiddenByScience = requiredScience && !player->hasScience at add time
  Rust: gui/ingame_ui/impl_update.rs:169-192 add_superweapon_timer accepts a hidden_by_science flag but no caller ever computes it (only snapshot load); grep 'object_changed_team' in Rust finds no InGameUI counterpart
  Crate pair never re-homes superweapon timers when an object changes team and never computes science-hidden state; (live host rebuilds timers per frame from player cooldowns, so this is crate-parity only)

- Diplomacy show animates from the wrong direction/duration and skips C++ open gates and parent defaults
  C++: Diplomacy.cpp ShowDiplomacy 187-266: refuses when isQuitMenuVisible or DisconnectMenu visible; registers WIN_ANIMATION_SLIDE_TOP 200ms; hides both radio buttons; on open shows winSolo (non-MP) or winInGame (MP) and hides the other; radio set to InGame
  Rust: gui/callbacks/diplomacy.rs show_layout 385-424: no quit-menu/disconnect gates; AnimationType::SlideBottom with 500ms; radio buttons never hidden; InGame/Buddies/Solo parents not configured on open (only the radio handler sets them later)
  Diplomacy panel slides up from the bottom over 500ms instead of down from the top over 200ms, can open over the quit/disconnect menus, and opens with undefined parent-pane visibility

- Invented hint types contradict C++ empty attack/force-attack hint stubs
  C++: InGameUI.h:586-596 HintType has only MOVE_HINT/ATTACK_HINT(+DEBUG); InGameUI.cpp:2176-2189 createAttackHint and createForceAttackHint are intentionally EMPTY; begin/endAreaSelectHint (2124-2137) only set m_isDragSelecting + region
  Rust: gui/ingame_ui/types.rs HintType adds ForceAttack/Garrison/Command/AreaSelect variants (marked 'Rust extension'); leftover.rs:40-115 create_attack_hint/create_force_attack_hint/create_garrison_hint push hint entries with 60-frame lifetimes, and begin_area_select_hint pushes an invented zero-coordinate AreaSelect hint with 300-frame lifetime
  Rust records and expires hint data for actions retail deliberately ignores, and models drag-select as a hint rather than the drag-region state C++ uses

- World animations expire while the game is paused
  C++: InGameUI.cpp:5323-5360 updateAndDrawWorldAnimations — the expire check (expire frame reached or PLAY_ONCE_AND_DESTROY complete) sits inside the isGamePaused()==FALSE block, so paused games keep anims alive (they still draw)
  Rust: gui/ingame_ui/world_anim.rs:53-60 — when paused, `expired` still evaluates current_frame >= expire_frame and removes the animation; only the PLAY_ONCE/complete and z-rise branches are pause-gated
  Pausing during a money-pickup/emoticon world animation can delete it early; retail pauses its countdown
