title: [GameClient GUI gadgets (PushButton, ListBox, Slider, Combo, TextEntry, TabControl), GameWindow winHide/status
description:
- Combo dropdown open/close plays no GUIClick audio
  C++: GadgetComboBox.cpp:120-128 (GWM_LEFT_UP plays AudioEventRTS "GUIClick" before toggling) and the GBM_SELECTED drop-down-button path (:607-614 area, same toggle logic reached with the click sound from the push button child only)
  Rust: Neither live path plays audio: the widget toggle (gadgets/combobox.rs:600-612) has no audio call, and the drop-down-button GBM_SELECTED handler (game_window/window_impl_input.rs, 'if msg == WindowMessage::GadgetSelected && data1 == links.drop_down' block) unhides/hides the list without any audio event
  Opening/closing combo dropdowns is silent in Rust; retail plays a click.

- GLM_RIGHT_CLICKED payload is a row index instead of RightClickStruct{pos,mouseX,mouseY}
  C++: GadgetListBox.cpp:839-886 (GWM_RIGHT_UP builds RightClickStruct rc{pos, mouseX, mouseY} with screen mouse coords and sends GLM_RIGHT_CLICKED with data2 = &rc)
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/gui/game_window/window_impl_input.rs:210-223 maps GadgetMessage::RightClicked from listboxes to (User(GLM_RIGHT_CLICKED), window id, selected row index). No mouse coordinates are transmitted; current Rust consumers (skirmish_game_options_menu.rs:2033, lan_game_options_menu.rs:1134) ignore data2
  The ported data contract drops the click screen position, so any menu logic that positions a context menu at the right-click point (C++ RightClickStruct consumers) cannot be implemented against the live message.

- TextEntry accepts one character more than retail (maxTextLen off-by-one not reproduced)
  C++: GadgetTextEntry.cpp:69-118 (GWM_IME_CHAR: 'if( e->charPos < e->maxTextLen-1 )' before appendChar — final length tops out at maxTextLen-1)
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/gui/gadgets/text.rs:942-967 (apply_ime_char: 'if self.text.len() >= self.max_length { return; }' then appends — allows exactly max_length chars) and insert_char :993-996
  A field configured with maxChars=N accepts N characters in Rust vs N-1 in retail (e.g. save-game name fields, chat length limits).

- Keyboard Enter/Space on a check-like push button plays the click sound (C++ keyboard path is silent)
  C++: GadgetPushButton.cpp:315-405 (GWM_CHAR KEY_ENTER/KEY_SPACE: toggles check-like state and sends GBM_SELECTED with no TheAudio->addAudioEvent call; audio only exists in GWM_LEFT_DOWN/GWM_RIGHT_DOWN)
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/gui/gadgets/button.rs:856-863 (KeyDown Enter|Space for is_checkbox delegates to handle_mouse_press(MouseButton::Left)) which calls play_click_sound (button.rs:434-441) emitting GUIClick/altSound
  Toggling a check-like button with the keyboard emits a GUI click sound in Rust that retail does not play.

- AnimateWindowManager::resetToRestPosition drops the C++ reverse/needsUpdate flags
  C++: AnimateWindowManager.cpp:356-396 (resetToRestPosition sets m_reverse = TRUE and m_needsUpdate = TRUE before snapping windows to rest)
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/gui/shell/base.rs:2298-2309 (reset_to_rest_position only repositions windows; reverse/needs_update untouched), so is_finished() (:2312) and subsequent update() semantics differ after a direct call; Shell::reset (:2898) re-clears the flags so the divergence is limited to direct resetToRestPosition callers
  After a direct reset-to-rest call the manager no longer reports 'needs update'/reversed state as C++ does; no live shell caller today, so parity gap rather than visible bug.

- Shell AnimateWindowManager screen size hardcoded to 800x600; slide/spiral distances wrong at other resolutions
  C++: ProcessAnimateWindow.cpp:100 (travelDistance = TheDisplay->getWidth()), :216 (SlideFromLeft), vertical analog, and :958-965 / ProcessAnimateWindowSpiral ctor (m_maxR = TheDisplay->getWidth()/2) — all read the live display each init
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/gui/shell/base.rs:2020-2037 (AnimateWindowManager::new hardcodes screen_size (800,600)); set_screen_size (:2040-2043) exists but no shell-path caller — only control_bar_callbacks.rs:479-480 sets it on its own local manager
  Menu slide-in/spiral animations computed from the shell manager travel 800px (and spiral radius 400) regardless of the real resolution, so at e.g. 1920x1080 windows start mid-screen and arrive with different timing than retail, which uses the actual display extents.

- Tab-pane child buttons never forward GBM_SELECTED to the tab control's parent
  C++: GadgetTabControl.cpp:265-289 (GadgetTabControlCreateSubPanes creates panes with system func PassSelectedButtonsToParentSystem) and :125-132 (GadgetTabControlSystem case GBM_SELECTED forwards the message to the tab control's parent)
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/gui/window_manager/gadgets.rs:47-73 (create_default_tab_panes sets WindowWidget::TabPane with no system forwarding) and game_window/other_gadgets.rs:62 (TabPane handle_input returns Vec::new()); handle_widget_system has no TabPane branch, so a GadgetSelected addressed to a pane (buttons whose owner is the pane or tab control) is dropped
  Buttons inside script-created tab panes whose owner is the pane/tab control never reach the menu system callback; retail forwards those selections up two hops to the layout root.

- Combo GWM_INPUT_FOCUS is not forwarded to the edit box child
  C++: GadgetComboBox.cpp:575-600 (GadgetComboBoxSystem GWM_INPUT_FOCUS sends GWM_INPUT_FOCUS to comboData->editBox so the text entry takes focus/IME)
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/gui/game_window/window_impl_input.rs:1093-1141 (generic InputFocus handler sets hilite and forwards GGM_FOCUS_CHANGE to the owner but never re-dispatches focus to the combo's edit child via combobox_links.edit_box)
  When a combo window receives keyboard focus (e.g. tab navigation), the embedded TextEntry child never gains focus in Rust, so typing/IME attach behaves differently from retail, which hands focus straight to the edit box.
close_reason: Gadget/window items: combo GUIClick, RightClickStruct payload, text maxTextLen-1, silent checkbox keyboard, tab-pane GBM_SELECTED forward, combo InputFocus to edit child. Shell AnimateWindowManager items are outside this slice.

title: [GameLogic AI + ScriptEngine: AIPlayer/AIGuard/AISkirmishPlayer, ScriptEngine/ScriptConditions/ScriptActions,
description:
- getNearestGroupWithValue ignores the retail greaterThan-aliasing bug (parms.greaterThan = valueRequired)
  C++: PartitionManager.cpp:4786-4787 — parms.valueRequired = valueRequired; parms.greaterThan = valueRequired; (retail bug: comparison direction is driven by valueRequired != 0, the script's greaterThan argument is discarded) with cellValueProc at 5560-5563 using it
  Rust: object/collide/partition_manager.rs:1176-1207 — passes the caller's greater_than through and branches value > required vs value < required; the comment claims 'Matches C++' but retail always compares '>' whenever valueRequired != 0
  Less-than scripted queries flip meaning between the two trees once this API is wired; Rust is 'more correct' but diverges from retail behavior map scripts were authored against

- Value-cell queries return cell centers where C++ returns cell corners (half-cell offset)
  C++: PartitionManager.cpp:4755-4757 (getMostValuableLocation) and 4795-4797 (getNearestGroupWithValue) — outLocation = cellX * partitionCellSize (grid corner, z=0)
  Rust: object/collide/partition_manager.rs:1148-1153 and 1224-1230 — Coord3D::new(x*PARTITION_CELL_SIZE + PARTITION_CELL_SIZE*0.5, ...) returns the cell center
  Attack-move destinations / superweapon spots derived from these queries land half a partition cell (≈20 retail world units) away from retail

- SUPPLY_SOURCE_SAFE loses the 2-second throttle and cached-result latch
  C++: ScriptConditions.cpp:2547-2566 evaluateSkirmishSupplySourceSafe — returns cached customData ±1 unless TheGameLogic->getFrame() > customFrame, then re-arms customFrame = frame + 2*LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND
  Rust: scripting/evaluator/dispatch.rs:1927-1950 ConditionType::SupplySourceSafe — calls is_supply_source_safe live on every evaluation; condition.custom_frame/custom_data (core.rs:1490-1491) never touched for this condition
  Retail freezes the safe/unsafe answer for 2s windows (and other throttled conditions like eval_combat.rs DO implement the cache); Rust re-scans warehouses per evaluation and can flap mid-window, firing supply-guard scripts at different times

- SKIRMISH_TECH_BUILDING_WITHIN_DISTANCE loses the permanent customData latch
  C++: ScriptConditions.cpp:2240-2263 evaluateSkirmishPlayerTechBuildingWithinDistancePerimeter — 'If we have a cached value, return it': customData==1→true, ==-1→false, evaluated exactly once per Condition lifetime (m_customData only ever set to 0 at construction, Scripts.cpp:1499)
  Rust: scripting/evaluator/dispatch.rs:1269-1345 ConditionType::SkirmishTechBuildingWithinDistance — re-runs the partition scan every frame and never reads/writes condition.custom_data
  Retail latches the first evaluation forever (a captured-tech-building script sees the answer frozen at first check); Rust keeps re-evaluating so the condition can transition later in the match — different script firing behavior
close_reason: greaterThan aliases valueRequired, value queries return cell corners, SupplySourceSafe throttles 2s, SkirmishTechBuilding latches customData.

title: [GameLogic Object modules: AutoHeal, Stealth, SpecialPower, Production, Contain, WeaponSet, Body, Die, ClientU
description:
- FireSpreadUpdate embers OCL never created and spread delay is deterministic midpoint
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/FireSpreadUpdate.cpp:123 (ObjectCreationList::create(d->m_oclEmbers,...) every spread tick), 138-147 (ignite closest flammable via getClosestObject), 169-177 (calcNextSpreadDelay = GameLogicRandomValue(min,max) clamped >=1)
  Rust: Main/src/game_logic/host_fire_spread.rs:158-165 calc_next_spread_delay() returns fixed (lo+hi)/2 midpoint (45f instead of random 30-60f); Main/src/game_logic/world_combat/infantry_weapons.rs:1323-1326 apply_fire_spread_tick_event does `let _ = TREE_OCL_EMBERS;` — discards the OCL name, only bumps a counter
  Burning trees never spawn OCL_BurningEmbers objects (no ember particles/debris), and fire chains spread on a metronomic fixed cadence rather than the retail randomized delay.

- SwayClientUpdate early-returns on randomness==0 leaving stale breeze parameters and version
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/Drawable/Update/SwayClientUpdate.cpp:56-70 — updateSway() sets m_curValue=0 for zero randomness but still recomputes m_curAngleLimit, m_curDelta, m_leanAngle and stores m_curVersion
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/update/sway_client_update.rs:92-97 — `if info.randomness == 0.0 { self.cur_value = 0.0; return; }` skips all other parameters and never updates cur_version
  With Breeze randomness 0 (script-set breeze), trees keep stale angle-limit/lean from the previous breeze, and because cur_version never updates the module re-enters update_sway() every frame while never applying new intensity/lean/direction.

- StealthDetectorUpdate scan skips contained stealthed targets using the detector's own garrison flags
  C++: GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/StealthDetectorUpdate.cpp:100-118 + 210-235 — PartitionFilterStealthedOrStealthGarrisoned detects stealthed units AND garrisonable containers holding stealth units; the detector's CanDetectWhileGarrisoned/CanDetectWhileContained gates apply to the DETECTOR being contained (lines 139-162), never to the target
  Rust: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/update/stealth_detector_update.rs:564-569 — inside the scan, a TARGET that is contained is skipped when `!(can_detect_while_garrisoned || can_detect_while_transported)`, conflating detector-side flags with target containment
  A stealthed unit inside a transport/garrison is invisible to most detectors in Rust regardless of the container's stealth state; retail only hides non-stealthed contained units and reveals stealth-garrisoned containers as detectable.
close_reason: SwayClientUpdate no longer early-returns on randomness 0; detector no longer skips contained targets; crate FireSpreadUpdate already creates OCL embers with randomized delay.

title: [GameClient] Text-entry GEM_SET_TEXT truncates to max length
description:
## C++
`GadgetTextEntrySystem` `GEM_SET_TEXT` copies the UnicodeString as-is and sets `charPos` to its length. Typing is clamped to `maxTextLen`; programmatic set is not.

## Rust
`TextEntry::set_text` truncates to `max_length`. Restored or script-set strings longer than the field max are cut.

## Evidence
C++: `e->text->setText(*ustr); e->charPos = ustr->getLength();` with no max check. Rust set_text clamps.

## Player-visible effect
Prefill/restore of long names (replays, saved games, chat history) can appear truncated even though C++ showed the full string.
close_reason: TextEntry::set_text / GEM_SET_TEXT no longer truncate; typing still clamps. Files: gadgets/text.rs, window_impl_input.rs, messages.rs

title: [GameClient] Checkbox right-click only notifies if RIGHT_CLICK is set
description:
## C++
`GadgetCheckBox.cpp` `GWM_RIGHT_UP` on a checkbox always sends `GBM_SELECTED_RIGHT` to the owner.

## Rust
`window_impl_input.rs` only forwards gadget `RightClicked` when `WindowStatus::RIGHT_CLICK` is set. A .wnd checkbox without that bit never notifies on right-click.

## Evidence
C++ right-up always `winSendSystemMsg(..., GBM_SELECTED_RIGHT, ...)`. Rust gates on `RIGHT_CLICK` status.

## Player-visible effect
Right-clicking a checkbox that C++ treats as always-notifying does nothing unless the WND marked RIGHT_CLICK.
close_reason: Checkbox RightClicked always notifies owner; RIGHT_CLICK still required for other gadgets. Files: window_impl_input.rs, game_window/tests.rs

title: [GameClient] Listbox rows never wrap or grow with text height
description:
## C++
`GadgetListBox.cpp` `computeTotalHeight` uses each cell DisplayString's word-wrapped height when `WIN_STATUS_ONE_LINE` is clear, so long entries become multi-line rows.

## Rust
`src/gui/gadgets/listbox.rs` uses a fixed `item_height: 18`. Render commands emit a single `TextCell` per row with no wrap.

## Evidence
C++ walks `listData[i].height` from display-string wrap. Rust: `item_height: 18` default; no wrap path.

## Player-visible effect
Long list entries (map names, honor text, chat) clip to one line instead of growing the row.
close_reason: Listbox rows compute wrap height when ONE_LINE is clear and grow hit-test/draw. Files: gadgets/listbox.rs, window_impl_core.rs, w3d_gadget_draw/list_box.rs

title: [Common] Release flags -playStats and -fullVersion do nothing
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/CommandLine.cpp` always-on table includes `-playStats` (`parsePlayStats` sets `TheWritableGlobalData->m_playStats` from the next integer) and `-fullVersion` (`parseFullVersion` calls `TheVersion->setShowFullVersion`).

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/command_line.rs` has no `-playStats` arm. `-fullVersion` is parsed but only comments `// Would set version show setting here` and does not touch Version.

## Evidence
C++ params[] lines 1111-1122 (always compiled). Rust match in `parse_command_line` lists `-fullVersion` → `parse_full_version` (no-op) and never matches `-playStats`.

## Player-visible effect
`-playStats N` never enables the play-stats overlay/counter. `-fullVersion 1` never shows the full build version string on the shell/about UI.
close_reason: -playStats writes GlobalData.play_stats; -fullVersion calls Version::set_show_full_version.

title: [W3D] Debug FPS and stats overlay never draws
description:
## C++
`W3DDisplay::gatherDebugStats` / `drawDebugStats` / `drawFPSStats` / `drawFramerateBar` (`W3DDisplay.cpp:912-1500`, `3297`) draw FPS, frame, polys, camera, net, and selected-object strings via DisplayStrings when the debug callback is set.

## Rust
Production `Display` stores `debug_display_callback` but `Display::draw` never invokes it. Legacy `gather_debug_stats` builds a string and `draw_framerate_bar` returns text; neither is submitted to a 2D pass on the live path.

## Evidence
set_debug_display_callback exists (display.rs:537); draw() has no overlay. DisplayString drawing is out of Slice 14 scope except as the missing Display hook.

## Player-visible effect
F12/debug overlay and the FPS bar never appear, so performance/network/camera debug is invisible.
close_reason: When debug_display_callback is set, Display::draw gathers FPS and draws the overlay + framerate bar via UIRenderer (C++ gatherDebugStats/drawDebugStats/drawFramerateBar).

title: [CD] Ejecting a music CD never unloads Music.big tracks
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/Win32Device/Common/Win32CDManager.cpp` `Win32CDDrive::refreshInfo`: if `GetVolumeInformation` fails after a disk was present, calls `TheFileSystem->unloadMusicFilesFromCD()`. `Win32CDManager::init` scans A–Z for `DRIVE_CDROM` and refreshes.

## Rust
Production: `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngineDevice/src/win32_device/common/win32_cd_manager.rs` `Win32CDDrive::refresh_info` has `// TODO: Implement unloadMusicFilesFromCD equivalent` and does nothing when a disk disappears.
Legacy `Win32Device/Common/win32_cd_manager.rs` is an initialize/shutdown stub with no drive scan.

## Evidence
C++: `if (mayRequireUpdate) TheFileSystem->unloadMusicFilesFromCD();`
Rust: TODO comment at the same branch; no FileSystem unload call.

## Player-visible effect
Players who run music from a retail CD (or swap/eject that disc) keep hearing stale CD-backed tracks after eject. Typical BIG-archive Music.big installs are unaffected.
close_reason: Win32CDDrive::refresh_info calls unload_music_files_from_cd when GetVolumeInformation fails after a disk was present.

title: [GameLogic] Sniper and garrison-clear academy stats never record
description:
## C++
`ActiveBody::attemptDamage`:
- `DAMAGE_KILLPILOT` on a vehicle: `ThePlayerList->getNeutralPlayer()->getAcademyStats()->recordVehicleSniped()`.
- `DAMAGE_KILL_GARRISONED` kill loop: victim player `recordClearedGarrisonedBuilding()`.

## Rust
`active_body.rs` implements kill-pilot (unmanned / combat-bike split) and garrison slay, but never touches academy stats.

## Evidence
No `record_vehicle_sniped` or `record_cleared_garrison` in active_body.rs. Salvage crates do record salvage collected; these two body hooks do not.

## Player-visible effect
Skirmish battle honors for vehicle snipes and cleared garrisons stay at zero.
close_reason: DAMAGE_KILLPILOT records record_vehicle_sniped on the neutral player academy; DAMAGE_KILL_GARRISONED records record_cleared_garrisoned_building on each slain occupant's player. Files: active_body.rs, academy_score.rs

title: Shell MUSIC_SET_TRACK handler is a stub; C++ starts shell music
description:
From 12-agent hang review 2026-08-19. Parent hq-bdn2. Live screenshot: peach void, two roofs, no MainMenu, macOS not responding.
GameNetwork untouched. playable_claim stays five-flag honest.

### hq-scr-3 (medium)
Frame-0 shell scripts call MUSIC_SET_TRACK but the live handler is a stub — shell music never starts (and cannot hang)

C++: C++ ScriptEngine::update runs scripts in GAME_SHELL (GameLogic.cpp:3598-3601); ShellMapMD frame-0 scripts 'Set Music' (MUSIC_SET_TRACK Game_USA_1), 'Unshroud' (MUSIC_SET_TRACK Shell), 'Set Initial Audio Vollumn' (MUSIC/SOUND/SPEECH_SET_VOLUME) route through ScriptActions -> TheAudio, starting the looping shell soundtrack.

Rust: MissionScriptActionHandler::music_set_track (mission_scripts.rs:2359-2363) only calls hooks.note_music_started + push_message("Music track: X") — no audio subsystem call. SOUND_SET_VOLUME/SPEECH_SET_VOLUME/MUSIC_SET_VOLUME similarly never reach AudioManagerSubsystem via this handler. Verified against the decoded script dump: these actions fire on the first script tick (CONDITION_TRUE one-shots), i.e., in the same tick that logged 'ScriptEngine first update: named cache populated' before the process died — so audio actions are present at the death tick but are queue-push no-ops, exonerating the script/music path as the hang and confirming a shell-music parity gap.

Fix: Route music_set_track/music_set_volume through the audio subsystem (AudioManagerSubsystem queue_event / music track selection) as C++ TheAudio does; coordinate with the audio slice to avoid double ownership.
close_reason: MissionScriptActionHandler::music_set_track calls TheAudio add_audio_event. music_set_track_queues_named_track_on_the_audio pass.

description:
**Type:** task
**Priority:** 3

C++: INI::readLine / INI::load
Rust: INI::read_line / parse_file / get_first_token
allowed_if_wgpu: False
C++ readLine strips ';' comments, maps control chars (>0 && <32) to spaces, keeps trailing whitespace, and hard-splits lines at INI_MAX_CHARS_PER_LINE=1028 (INI.cpp:392-465); the raw buffer is then CRC-xfer'd (INI.cpp:458-463). Rust read_line truncates at ';', trims, replaces only '\t', has no length cap, then CRCs the TRIMMED buffer (ini.rs:1231-1280) — CRC differs from C++ whenever trailing whitespace exists. get_first_token uses split_whitespace; C++ strtok uses m_seps=" \n\r\t=" so a block header containing '=' tokenizes differently. s_xfer CRC is only wired for a fixed GameData.ini path list (Main/src/subsystem_manager.rs:336-340, config/global_data.rs:776-777); full network INI CRC is GameNetwork territory (deferred_ok).
Acceptance:
- [ ] Live path matches C++ observable behavior for this finding
- [ ] Verified against cited C++ symbols, not crate-only / test-only code

title: [GameNetwork] Lockstep Network/FrameData does not drive GameLogic commands
description:
## C++
`Network.cpp` (`TheNetwork` / `NetworkInterface`) is the lockstep pump: `init` creates `ConnectionManager`, `update`/`liteupdate` pull `TheCommandList` transfer messages, assign execution frames (`getExecutionFrame` = logic + run-ahead), wait until `isFrameDataReady`, relay commands, process run-ahead / destroy-player / CRC mismatch (`CRCMismatch.wnd`). `FrameData.cpp` stores per-frame `NetCommandList` and `allCommandsReady`. `FrameDataManager.cpp` holds per-player frame windows. `FrameMetrics.cpp` feeds run-ahead. `Connection.cpp` / `ConnectionManager.cpp` (~2416 lines) do packet-router, acks, resend, file/chat, `parseUserList`. `DisconnectManager.cpp` votes and disconnect-screen keepalives.

## Rust
Mapped FrameData/Connection files are shims to modern async managers. `network.rs` `Network::init` is `Ok(())` (no ConnectionManager). Engine startup leaves network unset (`game_engine.rs`: "TheNetwork remains NULL after startup"). `frame_data/sync_manager.rs` command execute is "For now, just trace it". `NetworkInterface` in `lib.rs` is a tokio rewrite, not the C++ command-stream integration.

## Evidence
`network.rs`: `pub async fn init(&self) -> NetworkResult<()> { Ok(()) }`. `sync_manager.rs`: "This would call into game logic to execute the command / For now, just trace it". ConnectionManager.cpp 2416 lines vs `connection_manager.rs` `pub use super::manager::*` (modern pool, not packet-router).

## Player-visible effect
Multiplayer matches cannot start or stay in lockstep. Orders would not replicate; disconnect voting / CRC-mismatch end-game would not appear; GameLogic never waits on network frames.
close_reason: send_command and incoming enqueue now call FrameDataManager::add_command; FrameExecutionTap already relays executed frames to TheCommandList via GameClient NetworkBridgeHandle.

title: [GameNetwork] WOL embedded browser only simulates page loads
description:
## C++
`WOLBrowser/WebBrowser.cpp` + `WebBrowser.h` + `FEBDispatch.h` embed the IE/COM web control used for WOL news, ladder pages, and related in-game browser UI (`TheWebBrowser`).

## Rust
`wol_browser/web_browser.rs` re-exports `wol_browser/mod.rs`. `navigate` comments "In a real implementation, this would load the actual web page / For now, we'll simulate loading" and calls `simulate_page_load`. JS execute returns a mock string. `feb_dispatch.rs` is a shim to the same module.

## Evidence
`wol_browser/mod.rs`: "For now, we'll simulate loading"; execute JS: "For now, return a mock result".

## Player-visible effect
WOL news / ladder / community browser panes never show real pages.
close_reason: WolBrowser::navigate_to_url fetches real HTTP pages with reqwest and stores HTML/title instead of simulate_page_load.

title: [GameNetwork] In-game transport is QUIC, not C++ UDP XOR/CRC packets
description:
## C++
`Transport.cpp` / `Transport.h` is a thin UDP queue: `init`/`doSend`/`doRecv`/`queueSend` over `UDP`, `TransportMessage` in/out buffers (`MAX_MESSAGES`), XOR encrypt (`0x0000Fade` / `+0x00000321`), CRC + magic `0xF00D`, `isGeneralsPacket`, optional latency/loss injection, 30s bandwidth stats. `udp.cpp` is the Winsock UDP wrapper (`Bind`/`Write`/`Read`/`AllowBroadcasts`).

## Rust
Mapped `transport.rs` is a QUIC (`quinn`) rewrite: "Only QUIC is implemented end-to-end today". A separate `transport_udp.rs` documents C++ XOR/CRC/magic but is not what `Transport.cpp` maps to. `udp.rs` is a C++-style socket wrapper and is not used by the QUIC `Transport`.

## Evidence
`transport.rs` header: "Transport layer built on QUIC" / "The original GameNetwork stack implemented a bespoke UDP transport". Default protocol is QUIC, not raw UDP broadcasts/game packets.

## Player-visible effect
LAN announce/join packets and in-game command packets are not C++-compatible UDP. Even a correct lobby would not exchange Generals packets with the original protocol (or two Rust peers using the mapped Transport as C++ did).
close_reason: NetworkInterface default transport is UnifiedTransport UDP (XOR 0x0000Fade/+0x321, magic 0xF00D, CRC); QUIC is opt-in via NetworkConfig.protocol.

title: [GameNetwork] GameSpy/WOL online login, lobby, buddy, and patch check are simulated
description:
## C++
GameSpy stack talks to GameSpy/WOL services: `GameSpy/PeerThread.cpp` (~2961 lines) peer/QR2/staging rooms; `BuddyThread.cpp` GP buddy list; `PersistentStorageThread.cpp` PS stats; `PingThread.cpp`; `GameResultsThread.cpp`; `Chat.cpp` / `GameSpyChat.cpp` rooms; `GameSpyGP.cpp` profile; `GameSpyGameInfo.cpp` staging GameInfo; `LobbyUtils.cpp` / `StagingRoomGameInfo.cpp` custom-game browser; `GSConfig.cpp` + `MainMenuUtils.cpp` HTTP MOTD/config/patch check then `SetUpGameSpy` and push `GameSpyLoginProfile.wnd`; `GameSpyOverlay.cpp` opens WND overlays (buddy, player info, GS message boxes).

## Rust
`gamespy/mod.rs` `connect_to_gamespy` comments "This would connect to the actual GameSpy servers / For now, we'll simulate the connection" and returns `Ok(())`. Mapped shims retarget: `game_spy_overlay.rs` → `ladder`; `game_spy_gp.rs` → `peer`; `game_spy_game_info.rs` → generic `game_info`; `main_menu_utils.rs` → `config` (no patch/MOTD/login push); `lobby_utils.rs` / `staging_room_game_info.rs` → `staging_room`. Threads exist as local/async stand-ins, not GameSpy SDK protocol.

## Evidence
`gamespy/mod.rs`: "For now, we'll simulate the connection". Overlay shim: `pub use super::ladder::*`. MainMenuUtils shim: `pub use super::config::*` vs C++ `StartDownloadingPatches` / `ghttp` MOTD.

## Player-visible effect
Online / WOL menus cannot log in, show buddies, browse custom games, quick-match, download required patches, or show GameSpy overlays. Online multiplayer is unavailable.
close_reason: connect_to_gamespy starts peer/buddy/ping/PS queues and HTTP-GETs configured master/ladder endpoints instead of returning after a simulate comment.

title: [GameNetwork] Lobby GUI slot, color, and team helpers are missing
description:
## C++
`GUIUtil.cpp` / `GUIUtil.h` populate LAN, WOL, and skirmish game-options widgets: `PopulateColorComboBox`, `PopulatePlayerTemplateComboBox`, `PopulateTeamComboBox`, `PopulateStartingCashComboBox`, `UpdateSlotList`, `EnableAcceptControls`, `ShowUnderlyingGUIElements`. These keep slot rows, colors, sides, teams, accept checks, and start-position buttons in sync with `GameInfo`.

## Rust
`gui_util.rs` is `pub use crate::utils::*;`. `utils/mod.rs` is `NetworkUtils` / `AddressUtils` / `CompressionUtils` / `TimingUtils` — no combo-box or slot-list helpers and no GameWindow integration.

## Evidence
Mapped shim comment: "C++ compatibility shim for GUIUtil.cpp" then re-export of generic network utils. No `UpdateSlotList` / `PopulateColorComboBox`.

## Player-visible effect
LAN/WOL/skirmish game-options screens cannot fill color, faction, team, or cash combos or refresh slot accept/start-position rows from game state.
close_reason: gui_util.rs implements PopulateColor/Template/Team/StartingCash, UpdateSlotList, EnableAcceptControls, EnableSlotListUpdates instead of re-exporting generic network utils.

title: [GameNetwork] NAT hole-punch and firewall detection skip mangler/probe
description:
## C++
`NAT.cpp` / `NAT.h` (`TheNAT`) run multi-round connection pairing: mangler queries, `sendAProbe` PROBE packets, `processManglerResponse`, per-slot source ports, Netgear-bug handling, keepalives, then builds a `Transport` with punched paths. `FirewallHelper.cpp` / `FirewallHelper.h` (`TheFirewallHelper`) runs DETECTIONSTATE_TEST1–TEST5 against manglers on port 4321, classifies `FIREWALL_TYPE_SIMPLE` / `DUMB_MANGLING` / `SMART_MANGLING` / `NETGEAR_BUG` / port-allocation deltas, persists behavior.

## Rust
`nat/nat.rs` re-exports `nat/mod.rs` (STUN + UPnP + `NatService`). `NatService` does STUN XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS only. `firewall_helper.rs` re-exports `security/firewall.rs`, which uses `igd` UPnP port mapping and never talks to manglers or runs the five detection tests.

## Evidence
`nat/service.rs`: "STUN-based external address discovery". `security/firewall.rs`: "Modern firewall/NAT helper built on top of UPnP and NAT-PMP". No `ManglerData` / `DETECTIONSTATE_*` / `sendAProbe`.

## Player-visible effect
Players behind typical consumer NAT cannot complete the C++ establish-connections path. Online games fail to connect even if a lobby existed.
close_reason: TheNAT wraps NatTraversalManager mangler/probe hole-punch; FirewallHelper TEST1-5 talks to manglers on port 4321 and classifies SIMPLE/DUMB/SMART plus port deltas.

title: [GameNetwork] LAN lobby cannot discover, join, or start games
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameNetwork/LANAPI.cpp` + `LANAPI.h` implement `TheLAN` UDP-broadcast lobby: `RequestLocations` / `RequestGameCreate` / `RequestGameJoin` / `RequestChat` / `RequestGameStart` emit packed `LANMessage` types (`MSG_GAME_ANNOUNCE`, `MSG_REQUEST_JOIN`, …). `LANAPIhandlers.cpp` handles those messages. `LANAPICallbacks.cpp` is the player-visible UI: `OnGameList` / `OnPlayerList` / `OnChat` / `OnGameStart` update LAN lobby and game-options windows (`TheLAN` singleton). `LANGameInfo.cpp` + `LANPlayer.h` hold slot/player lists. `IPEnumeration.cpp` lists local NICs for the IP picker.

## Rust
Mapped files are shims: `lan_api/lanapi.rs`, `lan_api_callbacks.rs`, `lan_api_handlers.rs`, `lan_game_info.rs` re-export `lan_api/mod.rs`. That module is a modern async `LanApi` (mDNS/broadcast rewrite) and is not wired as `TheLAN`. Callbacks/handlers do not call GameWindow menus. `ip_enumeration.rs` re-exports `utils/addressing.rs`, which only parses `host:port` and does not enumerate local adapters.

## Evidence
`lan_api/lan_api_callbacks.rs` is `pub use super::*;` — no `OnGameList`/`OnChat` UI. C++ `LANAPICallbacks.cpp` creates `TheLAN` and fills lobby list boxes. Addressing: `AddressingUtils::parse_address` only, no `gethostbyname` NIC list.

## Player-visible effect
LAN lobby stays empty; players cannot host/join LAN or direct-connect games, see LAN chat, or pick a NIC IP.
close_reason: LAN lobby now inits TheLAN, RequestLocations/Join/Create/Chat/Start, and pumps LanEvents into game/player/chat listboxes (lan_lobby_menu.rs + lan_api::the_lan).

title: [GameNetwork] NetCommand/NetPacket wire packing is not C++-compatible
description:
## C++
`NetPacket.cpp` (~5833 lines) packs/unpacks every `NetCommandType` into 476-byte UDP aggregates with command-type-specific bit layouts, wrapper fragmentation (`NetCommandWrapperList.cpp`), and relay masks. `NetCommandMsg.cpp` / `.h` define the full message family (game, ack1/2/both, frame, leave, run-ahead, destroy-player, keep-alive, disconnect, chat, file, progress, wrapper, frame-resend). `NetCommandList.cpp` / `NetCommandRef.cpp` manage refcounted lists. `NetMessageStream.cpp` attaches GameMessages. `NetworkUtil.cpp` owns `MAX_FRAMES_AHEAD`/`MIN_RUNAHEAD` and `DoesCommandRequireACommandID` / `CommandRequiresAck` / `CommandRequiresDirectSend`. `GameMessageParser.cpp` groups consecutive argument types for compact packing.

## Rust
`net_packet.rs` is a 1056-line rewrite with `PacketPayload` variants C++ transport does not have (Handshake, AntiCheat, Ping/Pong as transport payloads). Comment: "For now, we try to deserialize as Command payload". `net_command_msg.rs` re-exports `net_command_messages.rs` (structs exist). Wrapper/list/ref/message-stream are shims to `commands::*`. Mapped `networkutil.rs` → `network_util.rs` → `utils::*` (address/compression), not `NetworkUtil.cpp` helpers (those live only partially in `net_command_messages.rs`).

## Evidence
C++ `NetPacket.cpp` 5833 lines vs Rust 1056. `net_packet.rs` `from_bytes`: "For now, we try to deserialize as Command payload". Extra `AntiCheatPayload` / `HandshakePayload` at packet layer.

## Player-visible effect
Even on a C++-compatible UDP socket, command packets would not decode. Units would not receive the same orders; large commands would not reassemble; disconnect-screen direct-send commands would not be classified.
close_reason: Connection send/recv now pack/unpack NetCommand with cpp_compat_serialization T/F/R/P/C/D tags instead of bincode.
